kayâs ayîsiyiniwak mistahi kî-kitimâkisiwak, oskac ôtê ê-ayâcik, nama kêkway ohci kî-pakitinikôwisiwak. ||| The people of old were in a piteous state, when first they lived here on earth. The Higher Powers had put them down here with nothing at all.
nama kêkway ayiwinisa ohci ayâwak; nama kêkway môhkomân. ||| They had no clothes, no knives.
nayêstaw oskan kî-omôhkomâniwak. ||| All they had for a knife was a bone.
nama kêkway ohci ayâwak iskotêw. ||| From the beginning they had no fire.
acosis piko kî-ohci-nipahêwak pisiskiwa, oskana ê-kikamohtâcik wîpisisiwâhk. ||| With merely an arrow they killed animals, fastening bones to their arrows.
nama kêkway; kî-kitimâkisiwak. ||| They had nothing; they were in a piteous state.
kîtahtawê iskotêw kî-osîhtamâsôwak, ômisi ê-tôtahkik; ê-kisitêyik, piyisk êkota kî-otinamwak iskotêw. ||| Presently they made fire for themselves, doing it like this; when it was hot, they got fire from it.
piyisk asiniya ê-pakamahwâcik, ê-wâsaskotêpayiyit, êkotê êkwa kî-ohtinamwak iskotêw ayîsiyiniwak. ||| Also they pounded a stone, and when it sent out sparks, from this, too, the people got fire.
êkwa asiskiy kî-otaskihkowak. ||| Their pots and kettles were of earth.
mîna kî-wâtihkêwak, pahkêkin ê-asiwatâcik, asiniya ê-kisâpiskiswâcik; êwako ohci wiyâs ê-kîsisahkik. ||| Also, they would dig a hole and put in a hide, and heat some stones; in this way they cooked meat.
êkwa kîtahtawê amiskwayâna kî-otayôwinisiwak. ||| Then in time they began to have beaver-pelts for their clothes.
kîtahtawê pêyak kî-pawâtam ê-wî-kapâyit môniyâw-iyiniwa wâpiski-wiyâsa. ||| Then at one time a certain man dreamt that the Canadian, the White Man, would land here.
âcimôw tâyispîhk ta-kapâyit. ||| He told when they would land.
tâpwê ânwêhtawâw; âtiht tâpwêhtâk. ||| Truly, he was not given credence; only some believed him.
êkwa êkotê mâmihk ispiciwak, cîki kihcikamîhk. ||| Then they moved their camp out there to the east, close to the great sea.
"êkwa wîpac kâ-wî-pê-kapâcik!" itwêw; "mâskôc ahpô mitoni kiyipa," itêw ayîsiyiniwa. ||| “Now the time is close at hand when they will land!” he said; “Surely very soon,” he told the people.
tahto kîkisêpâ nitawi-ay-itâpiw mâna nipîhk. ||| Every morning he would go and look out upon the water.
kîtahtawê kâ-pêtisâpahtahk cîmâna. ||| Then at one time he saw boats coming.
ôta ê-pê-takohtêyit, sakicihcênitôwak; atamiskotâtôwak. ||| When the others arrived there, they shook each other by the hand and greeted each other.
cikêmâ êkosi nistam kâ-isi-wâpamât ayîsiyiniw wâpiski-wiyâsa. ||| For, indeed, thus it was that the Indian first saw the Whiteskin.
kahkiyaw kêkway kî-miyik kita-ôh-pimâtisit: môhkomân, pâskisikan, kita-âpacihtât kahkiyaw kêkway pâskisikêwin. ||| They gave him everything to live by: the knife and the gun and all kinds of ammunition for his use.
êkosi êkota ohci kiskinôhamawâw kita-isi-pamihtât pâskisikan. ||| So then he began to be taught how to take care of a gun.
êkota ohci êkwa ati-miyw-âyâwak ayîsiyiniwak. ||| From that time on the Indians were well off.
kîtahtawê êkota ohci piyisk atimwa ayâwêwak, ê-otâpahâcik. ||| At a certain time after this they began to have horses to pull their loads.
ôtê piko nimitaw ayîsiyiniwak okî-ayâwâhtâwâw kayâhtê misatimwa; nama wîhkâc ohci ayâwêw ayîsiyiniw nâtakâm kâ-itapit. ||| And, strangely enough, it was only the people in the south who had horses; the Indian who dwells in the north from that time to this has never had horses.
kîtahtawê osâm êkâ kêkway ê-ayâcik mawimoscikêwin, kîtahtawê pêyak nâpêw otawâsimisa ê-nâ-nipahâpâkwêyit,-- kayâs êsa nama wîhkâc kêkway ôma askîhk ohci ohpikin; ahpô maskosiya kî-kîsitêwa,-- êkwa pêyak nâpêw osâm mistahi ê-miywâtisit, kîtahtawê kâ-wîhtamâkot okîsikowa, "hâw, kika-itohtahitin itê kita-ôh-pimâtisiyan." ||| Presently, because they had no way of worship, presently a certain man whose children had suffered to the point of death from thirst, -- for it seems that of old nothing ever grew from the earth; only grass ripened, -- then a certain man who was very good, was told by the dwellers in the sky, “Now I will take you whence you will have your source of life.”
êkwa tâpwê âpihtâ-kîsikâhk itohtahik mayaw ê-nipât; êkotê ê-pawâtahk, wîhtamâkôwisiw nipâkwêsimôwikamik. ||| Then truly he was taken to the place of the noonday sky, even as he slept; dreaming of that place, he was told by the Higher Powers of the Sun-Dance Lodge.
êwako tahtw-âskiy kita-tôtahkik ayîsiyiniwak kî-miyâwak. ||| The people were given the annual performance of this rite.
êkwa ispî kiskinohamawâw tânisi ta-tôtahk; okîsikôwa kî-kiskinôhamâk. ||| And at the same time he was taught how to perform it; by the dwellers in the sky he was taught.
mâskôc nawac nawac ta-miywâsin kâkikê ta-pakitinamâht ayîsiyiniw; êwako nititêyihtênân. ||| Surely it would be well, if it were always permitted to the Indian; so we think.
tahki kêkway kita-miyo-ohpikin. ||| Crops would always grow well.
namôya maci-kêkway nipâkwêsimowikamik. ||| The Sun-Dance Lodge is not an evil thing.
wiyawâw, "kahkiyaw kêkway maci-kêkway nêhiyawak maci-manitowa atoskawêwak," itwêwak ayamihêw-iyiniwak. ||| To be sure, “The Cree perform all kinds of evil things for the Evil Spirit,” say the missionaries.
namôya niyanân nêhiyaw ôta askihk ohci kiki-pakitinâw; maci-manitôwa mîna manitôw okosisa namôya ohci kiskêyimêw nêhiyaw; mîna maci-manitôw kâ-isiyîhkâsot namôya nêhiyaw kiskêyimêw. ||| On the contrary: the Cree was not put down here on earth with these things; the Cree has never known and does not know an Evil Spirit or a Son of God; and the Cree does not know him who is called the Evil One.
âta kita-kî-tâpwêhtahk nêhiyaw, nawac manitôwa ê-kitimâkêyimikot, êkâ wîhkâc yôtinwa kâ-nipahikot. ||| But rather, well may the Cree believe that the Spirit looks with kindlier pity on him, since he is never killed by winds.
nama wîhkâc nêhiyaw nipahik yôtin. ||| Never is a Cree killed by wind.
nama wîhkâc nipahik nêhiyaw piyêsiwa. ||| Never is a Cree killed by the Thunderers.
nama wîhkâc nêhiyaw nipahik iskotêw. ||| Never is a Cree killed by fire.
êkota ohci nititêyihtênân, nawac nêhiyaw ê-kitimâkinâkôwisit. ||| That is why we think that the Cree is favored by the Higher Powers.
mâskôc ê-kisiwâhât manitôwa, nipâkwêsimowikamik ê-kipihtinahk, êwako ohci mâh-mistahi kâ-ôh-pîkonahkik môniyâw-ôtênawa, nititêyihtênân; mîna iskotêw tahto-kîsikâw kâ-ôh-pîkonahk wâskahikana; tahto-kîsikâw misiwê nikiskêyihtênân ê-saskitêki wâskahikana, mayaw ôtênâhk êtohtêyâhko. ||| Perhaps it is because he has angered the Spirit by putting a stop to the Sun-Dance Lodge, that in such numbers they break up the Canadian's towns; so we think; and that every day fire destroys the wooden houses; every day we learn that everywhere houses have caught fire, every time we go to town.
mîna nipêhtênân tahto-nîpin ê-pîkwâstahki piko itê ôtênawa. ||| And every summer we hear that in many places towns have been destroyed by windstorms.
namôya maci-kêkway kâ-kî-miyikoyâhk manitôw, mawimoscikêwina, nayêstaw kita-isi-nitotamihk miyo-kêkway. ||| It is not an evil thing which the Spirit has given to us, but ways of worship, only that good things may be prayed for.
êkosi nikî-isi-pakitinikonân manitôw ôta askîhk kâ-nêhiyâwiyâhk. ||| Thus did the Spirit set us down here on earth, us who are Cree.
âtiht mâmaskâc mastaw ê-ihtakohki nîmihitôwina êkâ ê-kipihtinahk wâpiski-wiyâs, nanâtohk ê-isi-mêstinikêhk; mâka nipâkwêsimôwin nama kêkway mêstinikâniwa. ||| Strange, that some dances which arose much later are not stopped by the White Man, dances in which various things are used up, while the Sun-Dance involves no waste.
nêhiyawak êkota tahtw-âskiy kî-miyâwak nîso-kîsikâw êkâ kita-mîcisocik, kita-nitotahkik kahkiyaw kêkway kita-miyo-ohpikiniyik, kita-nitotahkik ta-kimiwaniyik. ||| It was given to the Cree, every year, for two days to go without eating, and to pray that all things might grow well, and to pray for rain.
êkosi kâ-isi-pakitiniht ôta askîhk kitimâki-ayîsiyiniw. ||| It was thus that the poor Indian was set down here on earth.
nika-miywêyihtên niya mîna wâhyaw kita-itohtêmakahk pîkiskwêwin, êkâ ê-wâpiyân. ||| I too shall be glad to have my speech go far abroad, I who am blind.
êkosi aspin ê-ohciyân namôya niwâpin. ||| For from the time I was born, I have been blind.
nama wîhkâc askiy niwâpahtên. ||| Never have I seen the earth.
êkosi âskaw piko itê ê-itohtêyân nititohtân; nama wîhkâc niwanihon. ||| Yet when from time to time I mean to go anywhere, I go there; I never get lost.
êkosi êwako pêyak âcimôwin êwako. ||| So much for this, for this one story.
nayêstaw wâpiski-wiyâs maci-manitôwa wiya ê-kiskinôhamâkot wêyôtisiwin, êkosi niyanân mâskôc namôya nikiskêyimikonân maci-manitôwa. ||| Since only the White Man was taught by the Evil Spirit how to acquire wealth, perhaps we others are not known to the Evil Spirit.
êwako ohci kâ-ôh-kitimâkisiyâhk. ||| That is why we are poor.
mistahi ayâw nêhiyaw kisêwâtisiwin; piko itê ê-pîhtokêyit ayîsiyiniwa, kiyâm owêyôtisiwa, asamêw; namwâc ahpô wîhkâc tipahikêhêw. ||| The Cree has much human kindness; wherever it be, if a man, and be he a rich man, enters a dwelling, he gives him food; in no case does he make him pay for it.
kiyâm pêyakwâw kita-mîcisot ê-ayât nêhiyaw, êyiwêhk kaskihtâw wîci-ayîsiyiniwa ê-asamât. ||| Even if the Cree has enough for only a single meal, in some way he manages to give food to his fellow-man.
misiwê ôma askiy nêhiyaw kisêwâtisiwin ê-ayât, êwako piko, kisêwâtisiwin mâwaci ê-ayât, kahkiyaw wîci-ayîsiyiniwa kitimâkêyimêw nêhiyaw. ||| Because, of all this earth, the Cree has most human kindness, because he has more human kindness than all others, the Cree deals kindly with all his fellow-men.
êwako ohci piko isi kâ-tôtâkot môniyâw-iyiniwa. ||| That is why the Canadian has been able to do whatever he pleased to him.
nama wîhkât nêhiyaw kîhkâhtôw; nôtinitôw nama wîhkâc; êkosi êsi-kiskêyihtamân. ||| Never does the Cree quarrel; he never fights; that is as I know it from experience.
namôya nikî-wanihtânân nêhiyaw ôta askihk kâ-kî-isi-pakitiniht. ||| We cannot lose the ways with which the Cree was set down here on earth.
êkwa kayâs êsa pêyak nâpêw ê-manitôwit, kîtahtawê akâmaskîhk ohci nôcihâw. ||| We are told that in ancient times a certain man who had spirit power was persecuted from across the sea.
êkwa kîtahtawê akâmaskîhk kâ-ayâcik ayîsiyiniwak, maci-ayîsiyiniwak, pîwâpisk ohci mâna ayîsiyiniwa ê-osihâcik, ôki wanipahtâkêw-iyiniwak, nîstanaw êhtasicik. ||| At that time across the sea there were some men, evil men, who made men out of iron, did those persecutors, who were twenty in number.
êkwa kotak awa oskinîkiw kâ-kiskêyihtahk ê-wî-kakwê-nipahiht, wawêyîw; asiskîwinisôw; wâpiskâyik asiskiy âpacihtâw. ||| Then another man, a youth, who knew that they were going to try to kill him made himself ready; he painted himself with clay; he used white clay.
êkwa sipwêhtêw; nipîhk êsa waskic pimohtêw, mistahi ê-manitôwit. ||| Then he set out; he walked over the surface of the water, so great was his spirit power.
êkwa ê-takohtêt êkotê ispimihk, wîkiyihk pakicîw ôhi kâ-wî-kakwê-nipahikot. ||| Then, when he arrived up aloft, at the others' dwelling he alighted, at the dwelling of those who were going to try to kill him.
wâpamêwak; "kihiw," itêyimêwak. ||| They saw him; they thought he was an eagle.
"nikostâhtay ana kâ-wî-kakwê-nipahâyâhk;" "ahpô êtokê êwako!" itêw awa kâ-wî-kakwê-nipahât, pîwâpisk ê-macostêhahk ayîsiyiniwa ê-osihât mâna êsa awa maci-ayîsiyiniw. ||| “And did I not fear him whom we were going to try to kill? I should not be surprised if this were he!” said the one who was going to try to kill him, putting iron into the hot fire to make a man, as was that evil person's way.
"êwako ohci kâ-ôh-kî-sâkwêyimoyân, ê-sîhkimiyêk," itêw êsa; "êkwa êwako êtokê awa!" itêw. ||| “This was why I was unwilling, when you urged me,” he told the others; “No doubt this is he!” he told them.
kitimâkêyiminân; pê-pîhtwâ!" itêw êsa. ||| Take pity pn us; come and smoke!” he said to him.
"hâh, namôya ninôhtê-pîhtwân." "kiyâm kipê-miyitinâwâw ta-isi-nipahiyêk," itwêw êsa. ||| “Ho, I do not wish to smoke. If so please you, I have come to let you kill me, as you desire,” he told them.
"hâ, namôya ka-kî-nipahikawin!" itâw; ê-ati-itiht, "kiyâm kitimâkêyiminân!" itik ôhi maci-ayîsiyiniwa; "kiyâm nika-pimâtisinân!" ||| “Oh, it will be impossible to kill you!” he answered him; as he continued to be spoken to in this way, “Please have mercy on us!” he was asked by those evil persons; “Please let us live!”
"namôya!" itêw; "kipê-miyitinâwâw ta-isi-nipahiyêk," itêw. ||| No!” he told them; “I have come to let you kill me,” he told them.
"namôya ka-kî-nipahitinân," itik. ||| “We could not kill you,” they told him.
"hâw, tipiskâki isko nika-pêhon." "êkâ wî-nipahiyêko, êkosi isi nika-kîwân." "mâka kika-aswêyiminâwâw," itwêw. ||| “Well then, I shall wait until dark. If you do not intend to kill me, I shall go home as I am. But I shall be on the lookout for you,” he said.
ê-tipiskâyik êkwa, ê-kîwêt, mosci-pimihâw êkwa. ||| When darkness came and he went home, he merely flew.
ê-wâpahk nitomêw êsa kahkiyaw kâ-mitêwiyit ayîsiyiniwa, kita-osîhtâyit mitêwikamik. ||| On the next day he summoned all the people who took part in the Medicine Ceremony, to have them build a Medicine Lodge.
"êkwa kiyâm pêyak ê-ayât awiyak maskihkiy, kita-itohtatâw," êkosi itêw ayîsiyiniwa; "âhkamêyimok; wîcôhkamawik;" "osâm mistahi kinipahikonawak," itwêw; "kîsihtâyêko ôma kâ-osîhtâyêk mitêwikamik, mîna kahkiyaw kîsihtâyêko, tahto ayîsiyiniwak ka-wî-itohtêcik kîsi-pîhtokêtwâwi, êkospî ka-pê-nitominâwâw," itwêw awa oskinîkiw; "êkwa pîhtokêyâni, nistikwânihk ka-pakamahonâwâw," itwêw awa oskinîkiw; "nika-pimitâcimon, pîhtokêyâni," itwêw; "êkwa mîna nîstanaw atimwak ka-mowâwâwak," itwêw; "êkwa kahkiyaw kika-nîmihitonâwâw," itwêw awa oskinîkiw; "êkwa kî-nipahiyêko, ka-pakocêninâwâw." "ohpimê kika-astânâwâw." "wêskwâhtêmihk ê-askîhtakwâk kika-anâskânâwâw." "êkwa ê-mihkwâk iskwâhtêmihk isi kika-anâskânâwâw." "tâpiskôc nipêwinis kika-isîhtânâwâw," itwêw êsa; "êkotê niyaw iskwâhtêmihk itê isi, sâkâstênohk êkotê isi nika-aspiskwêsimon." "êkwa kapê-tipisk kika-nîmihitonâwâw," itwêw êsa; "ka-mowâwâwak ôki atimwak." "êkwa nîso môhkomâna itakotêwa êtiskwêsiniyân." "kîspin kêkway mihko wâpahtamêko, êkosi nika-sâkohâwak akâmaskîhk kâ-ayâcik ayîsiyiniwak," itwêw êsa. ||| “And please let anyone who has any medicine bring it there,” he told the people; “Work with zeal; help me in what I am doing; too many of us are being killed,” he told them; “When you have finished the Medicine Lodge which you are building, and have completed everything, and when as many persons as mean to go there, have entered the lodge, then you are to come and call me,” said that youth; “And when I enter the lodge, you are to strike me on my head,” said the youth; “I shall be crawling along the ground, when I enter the lodge,” he said; “Also, twenty dogs you will eat,” he said; “And all of you will dance,” said the youth; “And when you have slain me, you will cut me open. Off to one side you will place it. Opposite the doorway you will lay blue mats. And red matting you will lay toward the doorway. You will make something like a small bed,” “And there my body, towards the doorway, facing the direction whence comes the light of day, I shall lie with my head on it. And all night you are to dance,” he told them; “You will eat those dogs. And two knives will hang by my head as I lie. If you see any blood, then I shall be defeating those persons who are across the sea,” he told them.
tâpwê nitawi-osîhtâniwiw mitêwikamik. ||| Accordingly they went and built a Medicine Lodge.
itwêw, "kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwak omaskihkîmiwâwa, mîna mitoni kahkiyaw kî-mêsci-pîhtokêyêko, êkospîhk kika-pê-pêkominâwâw." "pita niwî-nipân," itwêw êsa. ||| He said, “When the medicines of all the people are there, and when all of you, completely and to the last one, have entered the lodge, then you will come and wake me by speech. Meanwhile I wish to sleep,” he said.
tâpwê sôhki atoskêwak ayîsiyiniwak, mitêwikamik ê-osîhtâcik. ||| Accordingly the people worked diligently, building a Medicine Lodge.
êkwa ta-itohtêt pê-nitomâw, ê-kî-kîsihtâwiht. ||| Then he was summoned to go there, when it had been completed for him.
kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwa ê-kîsi-pîhtokêyit, itohtêw. ||| When all the people had gone in, he went there.
"hâw, niwâhkômâkanitik, kiyâm nipakitêyimâw nikosis," itwêyiwa ôhtâwiya; "mayaw pîhtokêci nipahâhkêk," itwêyiwa. ||| “Now then, O my kinsmen, if so please you, I give up my son,” spoke his father; “As soon as he enters, kill him,” he said.
êkosi wiya, "nipahîhkêk!" itwêyiwa. ||| It was his own father who said, “Kill him!”
"ôma ka-isi-sîhkimikoyêk kakwê-tôtamok," itwêyiwa ôhtâwiya, mâka wiya kisêyiniw pêkitêyimât ôhi okosisa. ||| “Try to do this in the way that he has bidden you,” said his father, the old man himself thus offering up his son.
mayaw ê-pîhtikwê-pimitâcimoyit, pakamahomâwa ostikwâniyihk. ||| As soon as the latter crawled into the lodge, he was struck on the head.
kakwêyâhowak oskinîkiwak ômatôwahk wâskikaniyihk ê-yâyikiswâcik. ||| The young men went faithfully to work, slashing him open here at his chest.
êkwa tâpwê pimisimêwak ôma kâ-kî-isi-sîhkimikocik. ||| Then they laid him down in the way he had bidden them.
kahkiyaw êkosi tôtamwak. ||| They did it all in that way.
"hâw, êkwa kahkiyaw nîmihitok!" "êkâ mâ nânitaw mêcimwâci nipahâyêko nikosis!" itwêw awa kisêyiniw kêsêwâtisit. ||| “Now then, all of you dance! Remember that you have not by any means really slain my son!” said the old man, so generous was he.
tâpwê nîmihitôwak kapê-tipisk. ||| Accordingly they danced all night.
ê-pê-wâpaniyik, kîtahtawê kâ-wâpahtahkik mihko môhkomânihkânihk ê-pahpahkikawiyik. ||| As dawn approached, there at one time they saw blood dripping from the blades of the knives.
êkwa tâpwê cîhkêyihtamwak ê-nîmihitocik, nayêstaw atimwa ê-môwâcik. ||| Then truly did they put their heart into the dance, and only dogs they ate.
pîsim ê-pê-sâkêwêt, êkoyikohk natawâpênawâw awa oskinîkiw. ||| When the sun rose above the horizon, they went to view that youth.
êkwa êkota wâpahcikâtêw ê-âpisisihk. ||| There it was seen by all that he returned to life.
kahkiyaw êsa kî-sâkôcihêw anihi nîstanaw ita ayîsiyiniwa. ||| He had overcome all of those twenty persons.
kahkiyaw êsa okî-nâspici-nipâhtâwâw. ||| It appears that they had all gone to sleep beyond hope of revival.
êwako pêyak âcimôwin; êkota ohci namôya êkoyikohk miywâsin mitêwikamik. ||| That is one story; but since then the Medicine Lodge has not been so good a thing as all that.
kahkiyaw kêkway mac-âyisak ahpô ayîsiyiniwak kî-nâ-nipahitôwak, maci-maskihkiya ê-âpacihtâcik, ê-piscipôwihtocik. ||| All kinds of evil beings or person have killed one another, by using bad medicines to poison one another.
piko isi isi-kaskihtâwak êsi-nisiwanâcihitocik kayâs ayîsiyiniwak. ||| The old-time people were able to do all manner of things in the way of destroying one another.
êwako wiyawâw ocipwêwak nîkân kâ-kî-miyikôwisicik mitêwiwin; kêhciwâk kî-itohtêwak mitêwi-manitôwa. ||| It was the Ojibwa who first were given this Medicine Ceremony by the Higher Powers; they went into the actual presence of the Spirit of the Mitewin.
êkota ohci kahkiyaw kêkway nipîhk kâ-otaskîyit, êyakonik mawimostawêwak kâ-mitêwicik; môhkiciwanipêkohk mîna kâ-otaskîyit kahkiyaw mawimostawêwak; mîna tahto kêkway kâ-sâkikihk ôta askîhk, êwakoni kî-kiskinôhamâkôwisiwak kita-isi-mawimostahkik. ||| Since then, those who participate in the Medicine Rite, worship all those beings that have their home in the waters; they worship also that being who has his home in springs; and they were told by the spirits to worship as many things as grow forth out of this earth.
anohc kêyâpic mihcêt kêkway ê-pwâtawihtâcik maskihkîwiyiniwak, kaskihtâwak nêhiyawak omaskihkîmiwâwa ohci; cikêmâ kî-miyikôwisiw nêhiyaw maskihkiy; iyikohk êspîhcâk askiy, kahkiyaw kêkway kâ-wâpahtamihk, niyîpihki kâ-ohpikihk, êspîhcâk askiy, misiwê kî-têpastâwân nêhiyaw omaskihkîm. ||| To this day, many things which the physicians fail of doing, the Cree can do them through their medicines; what wonder, since the Cree was given medicine by the Higher Powers? Over all the extent of the earth, everything that is seen growing forth in the summer time, as far as the earth extends, everywhere the medicine of the Cree was placed within his reach.
misiwê itê itâpiyêko ka-wâpahtênâwâw nêhiyaw ê-kî-miyiht wîsta kita-ohci-pimâtisit. ||| Wherever you may look, you will see that which the Cree, for his part, was given, that he might derive from it his continuance of life.
mîna âpihtaw ê-mâyâtaniyik maskihkiy kî-miyâw. ||| Also, as half of the gift, he was given bad medicine.
wiyawâw êwakoni mitêwak kâ-kî-kiskinôhamâkôwisicik; kahkiyaw kêkway kî-wîhtamâkôwisiwak kit-si-nanâtawihiwâkêcik, ahpô nipîhk kahkiyaw kêkway kâ-ohpikiniyik, kita-pâsahkik kahkiyaw kêkway maskihkiy. ||| Those same Medicine Dancers were the ones to whom it was taught by the Higher Powers; they were shown by the spirits every way of doctoring people, all the things, even, which grow in the water, that they might dry all kinds of medicinal herbs.
ohcitaw nitâyimôtên kayâs nêhiyawak kâ-isi-pimâtisicik. ||| I tell this because I wish to discourse upon how the Cree lived of old.
nimiywêyihtên manitow wiya ê-itêyihtahk, awa nâpêw kâ-pê-natawêyihtahk nêhiyaw tânisi kâ-kî-isi-pimâtisit. ||| I am glad that the Lord had it in mind that this man should come here and desire to know how the Cree used to live.
mitoni mâka kahkiyaw miyo-kanâpanikôwisit ayîsiyiniw, êkwa kayâs nika-âyimôtên. ||| How well the people of old were taken care of, in everything, by the Powers, of that I shall now speak.
nama kêkway wiyasôwêwin ohci-ayâw nêhiyaw; kipahotôwin nama kêkway; nama kêkway maci-ihtiwin; wiyawâw piko ayîsiyiniwak omitonêyihcikaniwâw kî-âpacihtâwak. ||| Originally the Cree had no kind of law; there was no such thing as imprisonment; no such thing as crime; people simply used their own considerate judgment.
ayisk nêhiyaw nama kêkway ohci mâyi-tôtam; namôya ohci mâyi-tôtawêw nêhiyaw kisê-manitôwa. ||| For the Cree did not, by his original nature, do wrong; it is not in the nature of the Cree to do wrong to God.
êkwa nêhiyaw tipiyaw wiya manitôwa kî-kakêskimik; êwako ohci yôspisiwin kâ-ôh-ayât nêhiyaw. ||| The Cree was instructed by God himself in person; that is why the Cree has gentleness.
ayisk kisêwâtisiw, manitôw kâ-kî-pê-kakêskimât ayîsiyiniwa. ||| For he has kindness of heart, since God came and instructed the people.
êkwa mîna piko iskwêwa kî-nâ-naskwêwasimik; êkosi kî-wiyasôwâtêw. ||| At that time only the woman made rejoinders to Him; therefore He pronounced the law for her.
"nama wîhkâc mistahi kita-yahkastêw kitatoskêwin; osâm kinâ-naskwêwasimin." "kiyâm kapê-kîsik atoskêyani, pêyakwan iyikohk kita-ispîhcipayiw kitatoskêwin," kî-itêw êsa manitôw. ||| “Never shall your work show great advance; for you have retorted to me. Let it be that when you work all day, your work will be as far advanced as it was before,” God said to her.
êwakoni piko ôhi pê-mâyasôwâtêw. ||| For her alone He decreed ill.
nâpêwa kî-kiyâmapiyiwa, oskac nêhiyaw ê-osihiht. ||| The man stayed still when the Cree was first made.
êkosi êsa kî-ispayiw, itwêwak kayâs kisêyiniwak, oskac ê-osihât manitôw nêhiyawa. ||| Thus it must have gone, said the old men of yore, when God first made the Cree.
êkosi êsa kâ-ispayik. ||| So that is the way it must have happened.
êkota kî-wîhtamawêw kahkiyaw kêkway maskihkiya, mîna mawimoscikêwin kita-ayâyit. ||| There He told him every kind of medicine, and the religion he was to have.
êkoyikohk wiya manitow ohci nika-pôni-âyimôtên. ||| And at this point I shall cease to discourse of things concerning the Lord.
êkwa niwî-âtayôhkân. ||| Now I shall tell a sacred story.
êwako pêyak âcimowin. ||| And so this is one discourse.
niyanân mîna nitayânân manitôw okiskinôhamâkêwin. ||| We, too, have a teaching of God.
ayisk namôya niyanân n-ôh-nipahânân manitôw okosisa; êwako ohci namôya ninisitawêyimikonân maci-manitôw. ||| You see, not we have ever slain God's Son; that is why the Evil One does not know us.
êwako ohci êkâ kêkway kaskihtâwin kâ-ôh-ayâyâhk. ||| And that is why we have no kind of worldly power.
pêyak, nipâkwêsimôwin. ||| One is the Sun-Dance.
ê-nitotamâht manitôw, kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniw kita-ohpikit ôta askîhk. ||| The Sun-Dance consists of this, that God is entreated that every human being may grow up and thrive here on this earth.
êwako nipâkwêsimôwin, nîso-kîsikâw piko aniki kâ-nîmihitocik nipiy êkâ ê-minihkwêcik, êkwa mîciwin êkâ ê-mîcicik nîso-kîsikâw. ||| The Sun-Dance consists of this, that for two days and no longer the dancers drink no water and for two days eat no food.
mayaw kâ-pôyohk, sêmâk kahkiyaw kîwâniwiw, ê-nitawi-atoskêhk. ||| As soon as it is over, at once all go home and return to work.
namôya wîhkâc ê-kisiwâsihk, êwako mîkiwâhp kâ-âpacihtâcik nêhiyawak. ||| It is never in anger that the Cree use this lodge.
pîsim piyêsiw mostos ohtin, êwakonik nêwo kâ-ôh-nipâkwêsimohk, ê-miyâcik ayîsiyiniwa êwakonik. ||| Sun, Thunderbird, Buffalo, Wind, for these four the Sun-Dance is danced, since they gave it to man.
manitôw otawâsimisa ê-kî-wihât kita-nitotamâht pimâtisiwin, êwakonik âcimostawêwak ôhtâwiyiwâwa manitôwa. ||| Since God appointed these his children, that he might be entreated for life, it is they who convey the message to God their Father.
êkosi êwako ohci kâ-nipâkwêsimohk; namôya ê-mâyâtahk. ||| This, then, is the purpose of the Sun-Dance; not evil.
mistahi mihcêtwâw ohci pimâtisiwak nêhiyawak. ||| In many instances Cree owe their lives to it.
ayis namôya êwakoni piko ê-nitotamawâcik kita-ôh-pimâtisicik; kahkiyaw kita-ohpikit ayîsiyiniw ôta ôma askiy ê-isi-nitotahkik kâ-nipâkwêsimôwinihkêcik. ||| But, in fact, it is not only for themselves that they ask for the power to live; that every human being on this earth may thrive is the prayer of them who celebrate the Sun-Dance.
ê-âhkosit awiyak, asotam ta-wîcihiwêt, ta-nîmihitot, manitôwa ê-nitotamawât. ||| When one is ill, he makes a vow that he will take part in the dance and the prayer to God.
tâpwê âskaw pimâtisiwak êkota ohci nêhiyawak. ||| Truly, often have Cree owed their lives to this.
pîhtwâhêwak êwakoni ôhi kahkiyaw, ôhi pîsimwa mîna piyêsiwa mîna mostoswa mîna ohtina. ||| They cause each of them to smoke, the Sun and the Thunderbird and the Buffalo and the Wind.
êwakoni mîna wâpahtêhêwak cistêmâwa. ||| They show them the tobacco.
awa kâ-wî-nipâkwêsimôwinihkêt, "kitâpahta ôma!" "kitâpam awa, nôhtâ kisê-manitôw, kitawâsimis ê-wî-kanawêyihtamawak kita-pîhtwât!" "miy sôhkisiwin awa kitawâsimis kâ-kanawêyihtamawak cistêmâwa." "kanâci, êkâ kêkway ta-sêkihikocik ayîsiyiniwak." "ita mânokêyâni, kitawâsimisak kâ-wî-mânokawakik, kita-kitâpahtahkik wîkiwâw ta-okimâwihk êkâ awiyak kita-âhkosit;" "kahkiyaw kiyâm kita-miywêyihtamwak ôki kitawâsimisak, tahto kê-pê-nitawâpahkêcik ôma pîsim piyêsiw wîki kâ-wî-osîhtâyân, ohtin mîna." "êyakonik kita-kisêwâtisiwak koyahâkanak, kâ-sôhkahk kipimâcihiwêwin, êwako kita-miyihcik kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwak." "ôma nîpawiyâni nama kêkway kita-sêkihikwak." "wâh-pimohtêci kitawâsimis, pêyâhtik kita-pimohtêw awa piyêsiw, nipiy kita-sâpopatât ohci ôma askiy, êkâ ta-pîkopayik." "kisêwâtotawin; kitimâkihtawin!" "êkosi ê-itwêyân anohc, kahkiyaw ta-miywamahcihohk." ||| He who is about to give the Sun-Dance, “Look upon this thing! Look upon this tobacco, God, my Father, which I shall keep for Thy child to smoke. Give power to Thy child for whom I keep the tobacco. Moderate him, so that mortal men be not frightened by aught. There where I set up the lodge which I am about to erect for Thy children to look upon, let no one be ill; let all Thy children rejoice in it, as many as shall come to look upon this lodge of Sun and Thunderbird which I shall build, and of the Wind. May these Thy appointed creatures be propitious, so that Thy firm gift of life may be given to all men. When here I stand let them not by aught be frightened. When Thy child is about to walk abroad, let this Thunderbird go gently, drenching this earth with rain, that it may not break apart. Be kind to me; hear me with pity! Thus do I now speak, that all may live in health.”
kîspin piyêsiw ê-miyât êwako mîkiwâhp, kâ-mânokêt ayîsiyiniw, mistahi âpacihiwêw. ||| If the Thunderbird gives a man this lodge, and he has set it up, he does much good to people.
kahkiyaw awiya âpacihêw, êkâ ta-nôhtêyâpâkwêyit, ta-miyoskâkoyit nipiy. ||| He does good to each and every one, that they need not thirst and that water may benefit them.
êwako ohci ayîsiyiniwak, pêyak kâ-nipâkwêsimôwinihkêt. ||| This is why; for the sake of mankind is why one gives a Sundance.
pêyakwan pîhtwâwin, pêyak tipiskâw piko ê-nikamohk, sîsîkwanak ê-âpacihihcik. ||| Of similar nature is the Smoking-Lodge, in which the singing lasts only one night and rattles are used.
pêyak wâkayôs êwako nîkân ê-wîhtamâkêt, nêhiyawa ê-wîhtamawât. ||| It was a certain bear who first told of this, revealing it to the Cree.
êkota ohci: pîsim piyêsiw mostos. ||| It is for these: Sun, Thunderbird, Buffalo.
piko itôwahk asiniy apiw pîhcâyihk. ||| Somewhere within the lodge lies a stone.
êyakonik ê-miyihcik cistêmâwa, kita-pîhtwâcik, ê-nitotamâhcik pimâtisiwin. ||| It is they who are given tobacco that they may smoke and are entreated for life.
tâpitawi pîhcâyihk pîhtwâwikamikohk mîcisonâniwiw, minihkwâniwiw nipiy. ||| But also, within the Smoking-Lodge there is eating, and water is drunk.
nôtokêsiwak mânokêwak pîhtwâwikamik, namôya nâpêwak. ||| Old women erect the Smoking-Lodge, not men.
tahto ê-nikamocik, kiyîsi-nikamotwâwi, nitotamawêwak kita-ohci-pimâtisicik. ||| Every time they sing, when they have sung their song, they ask them for the gift of life.
tahto kâ-nikamocik, kahkiyaw êwakonik ê-nitotamâcik. ||| As many as sing, all ask them for it.
âskaw pîhcâyihk mâtôw ayîsiyiniw kâ-pîhtwâwinihkêt. ||| From time to time within the lodge he weeps who is giving the Smoking-Ceremony.
"ôki awâsisak kita-ohpikiwak miyinân, kita-ôh-ohpikinâwasoyâhk!" itwêwak kâ-pîhtwâcik. ||| “Grant us that these children may grow up, grant us the gift of bringing our children to maturity!” say those who smoke.
tahto mîna kâ-nikamocik, kahkiyaw miyâwak cistêmâwa, tahto kâ-nikamocik. ||| As many, also, as sing, all are given tobacco, as many as sing.
âskaw iskwêwak mâtôwak. ||| From time to time the women weep.
"kitimâkihtawinân!" "kitimâkêyim ôki nâpêwak, ê-kitimâkisicik, ê-nitotamâkoyêkok pimâtisiwin." "ôki mîna iskwêwak ta-ohpikihêwak otawâsimisiwâwa kitimâkêyiminân, kisê-manitôw!" "ôki kitawâsimisak kâ-wîci-pîhtwâmihcik miy kita-ôh-kitimâkêyihtahkik kêkway, ta-ohpikîmakaniyik wiyawâw." "êkâ wiya nika-kakwê-sêkihikonân kitawâsimis piyêsiw." "mîna ohtin êkâ wiya ita ê-ayât ayîsiyiniw kakwê-sêkihtâ miywâsin kohpikicikêwin." "êkosi isi kitimâkêyiminân!" ||| “Lend a pitying ear to our prayer! Pity these men, who are pitiable, who implore you for life. And that these women, also, may bring their children to maturity, take pity on us, Lord God! To those children who are given part in the smoking, grant, that they may feel pity for all things, and that their bodies may grow and thrive. Let not Thy child, the Thunderbird try to frighten us. Do not with Wind, there where is mortal man, seek to frighten that good thing Thou hast caused to grow up. Even thus grant us Thy pity!”
ê-pôni-mâtocik ôki iskwêwak, pêyak ê-mâtot, "hay!" itâw, "kitatamihin ê-nitotamâkêstamawiyan pimâtisiwin!" ||| When the women cease to weep, when one has wept, “Thanks!” they say to her; “I thank you for praying for me for life!”
ê-itêyimâcik, ê-mâtoyit, pêskis ê-pîkiskwêyit, "mâskôc ta-kitimâkihtawâw," ê-itêyihtahkik ôki ayisiyiniwak, "hay!" kâ-ôh-itwêcik. ||| Because those people think thus concerning her, when she weeps and at the same time speaks her prayer, because they think “Doubtless she will be heard with pity,” that is why they say, “Thanks!”
êkosi êwako pêyak tipiskâw ê-pôyohk, mayaw ê-kîsikâk, sêmâk kahkiyaw kîwêwak ayîsiyiniwak. ||| Then, when after that one night the ceremony is closed, as soon as day comes, at once all the people go home.
mistahi kîwêhtatâwak mîciwin. ||| They take home much food.
mistahi kîsitêpôw êwako aniki ê-pîhtwât awiyak, pêyak piko omîciwin kâ-miyât, kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwa ta-mîciyit. ||| When anyone of these people thus smokes, he cooks much, for he alone gives them food, that all the people may eat.
mayaw ê-pôyohk, kîwâniwiw nanânis. ||| As soon as the ceremony is over, all go to their various homes.
kotak mîna nîmihitôwin: kikastotinêwak. ||| Another dance still: they dance the Masked-Dance.
êkwa mistikohk tâpisiniyiwa mostoswak waskasîwâhk ohci ê-apisîsisicik. ||| To a pole are fastened the smallest of the hoofs of buffalo.
êyakonik pêyak kîsikâw ê-kîsikâyik piko ê-nîmihitocik. ||| These dancers dance one day, only during daylight.
kahkiyaw mâka kikastotinêwak. ||| All wear a headgear.
namôya nôkwaniyiwa ohkwâkaniwâw; payipisikâtêyiwa otastotiniwâwa ita ê-ohci-kanawâpahkêcik. ||| Their faces are not visible; holes are cut in their headgear, through which they may see.
êwako mîna pêyakwan, wîhtikôhkânisimôwin. ||| This, too, is of the same nature, the Windigo-Dance.
êwako pêyakwan: tahki mîcisôwak; pisisik nâpêwak, namôya iskwêwak. ||| This is alike in both: they always eat; there are only men, not women.
pêyakwan mîna êwako pâh-pêyak piko kâ-miyihcik ayîsiyiniwak, êwako nîmihitôwin, namôya waniyaw, pêyak piko nâpêw. ||| This, too, is a common feature, that only certain individuals are given the gift of holding this dance; not anybody, but only this or that man.
âskaw nisto-mitanaw nîsitanaw nêwomitanaw ihtasiwak ôki kâ-wîhtikôh-kânisimocik. ||| Sometimes the Windigo-Dancers were as many as thirty, twenty, or forty in number.
êyakonik ê-asotahkik kita-ohci-pimâtisicik, wâhyaw ê-ayâyit owâhkômâkaniwâwa. ||| They promised to hold it that they might derive life from it, when their kinsfolk were far away.
"wâpahtihin niwâhkômâkanak, manitôw, kitawâsimisak." "êkospî nika-nîmihâwak." "wâpamaki awa kâ-matwê-âhkosit, kita-pimâtisiw." "êwako mîkiwâhp nika-apîstên." "nika-nîmihâwak ayîsiyiniwak," itwêw. ||| “God, let me see my kinsfolk, Thy children. Then I shall give them a dance. If I look upon him who laments in sickness, let him live. By this lodge I shall take my seat. I shall make the people dance,” he said.
êkoyikohk ê-iskwâk êwako. ||| That is the end of this.
kayâs tâpiskôc simâkanisak nêhiyawak. ||| Of old, like soldiers were the Cree.
namôya kîmôc kî-tôtamwak. ||| They did not act without general consent.
mayaw onîmihitôwak, êyakonik pisisik nâpêwak kayâs, kîspin onîmihitôwak, "namôya ka-mâcînâwâw; namôya ka-mâcîw awiyak," kîspin êkosi ê-itwêcik, awiyak miyâcîci, mênahoci, ôki onîmihitôwak, âta, "kîmôc nitôtên," êtêyihtahki awa kâ-mâcît, têpiskâyiki, têkosihki, wiyâpahki pêhtamwak onîmihitôwak. ||| As soon as these dancers, - they were only men, of old, - as soon as these dancers said, “You are not to hunt; no one is to hunt,” then, if anyone hunted and killed game, then these dancers, even though that hunter would think, “I am doing it in secret,” when at night he has arrived, in the morning those dancers would hear it.
kîkisêpâ wayawîwak; sâkowêwak; nikamôwak. ||| Early in the morning they would go forth; they would whoop; they sang.
awa kâ-kî-mâcît wîki yâyikisamwân, misiwê ê-pîkosamoht. ||| The tent of the one who had hunted would be cut into strips, and all his property cut up.
opâskisikan otinamwân. ||| His gun would be taken from him.
"ayis, nikwêmêsitik, nôhtêhkatêwak nitawâsimisak, kâ-ôh-mâyi-tôtâtakok." "awa pîhtwâhkêk ciscêmâs." "iyikohk kî-nêwo-tipiskâk, êkospî kika-miyitinâwâw isi-miywêyihtamêk," itwêw awa nâpêw. ||| “You see, friends, my children are hungry; that is why I have transgressed against you. Do you keep this tobacco to smoke. In four nights I shall give you that which will please you,” said that man.
kâ-nêwo-tipiskâki pakamahwêw atimwa, ê-nipahât otêma. ||| When the fourth night had come, he clubbed his dog to death; he killed his dog.
pakâsimêw, onîmihitôwak ê-nitawi-asamihcik. ||| He set it to boil, and the dancers were sent for, that they might partake of it.
kâ-kîsi-asamihtwâwi ôki onîmihitôwak, êkwa, "hâw, awa kâ-kî-pîkoswâyahk, nikwêmêsitik, namôya kikisiwâhânaw." "miyihk apasoya, mîkiwâhp; mîna ayiwinisa miyihk." ||| When the dancers had been given it to eat, then, “Now, he whose belongings we have cut to pieces, friends, we have not angered him. Give him tent-poles and a tipi; give him also clothes.”
hâ, êkwa kahkiyaw onîmihitôwak miyêwak ta-âpacihtâyit, pâskisikan môsasiniya mîkiwâhp apasoya. ||| Then all the dancers would give him things to use, a gun, bullets, a tipi, lodge-poles.
êkosi isi miyâw, kîspin êkâya kisiwâsit. ||| With such things he was presented, if he did not get angry.
mâka awa kâ-kisiwâhiht, wîki ê-pîkosamoht, nama kêkway miyâw. ||| But one who was made angry by the destruction of his dwelling, was not given anything.
tâpwê piko kitimâkisiw, kahkiyaw ê-pîkonamoht otayâna otayiwinisa opâskisikan. ||| He was indeed reduced to misery, what with the tearing up of all his implements, his clothes, and his gun.
êkwa pêyak; ocihkomisîsak isiyîhkâsôwak onîmihitôwak. ||| And another; Little Lousy Fellows the dancers were called.
kâkikê wîkiwâw cimatêyiw pîhtêyas, mîkiwâhp, êyakonik onîmihitôwak. ||| Their lodge stood permanently in the center of the camp, the lodge of these dancers.
ôki mîna kotakak sîsîkwanisak isiyîhkâsôwak onîmihitôwak. ||| And another society of dancers was called the Little Rattles.
ê-kîsikâyik nîmihitôwak. ||| They danced by daylight.
iskwêwak naskwahamâkêwak, ê-nikamocik. ||| The women made the chorus as they sang.
êkwa kotakak, mistahi-atimwak. ||| And another society, the Big Dogs.
pêyakwan êkosi isi nîmihitôwak, iskwêwa ê-nikamoyit; namôya ê-nîmihitoyit. ||| They danced in the same way, the women singing, but not dancing.
kotakak mîna onîmihitôwak pihêwak isiyîhkâsôwak. ||| Another society of dancers was called the Partridges.
pêyakwan êkosi ê-tôtahkik. ||| They did like the preceding.
kîspin awiyak mostoswa ê-nipahât, pîkonâw. ||| If anyone killed a buffalo, his possessions were torn up.
ôki kahkiyaw kâ-wîhakik onîmihitôwak pîhtêyas ê-wîkicik, ê-wîhkwêstêki mîkiwâhpa. ||| All these dancers whom I have named, had their lodge in the center, where the other tipis stood in a circle round about.
êwako kahkiyaw pêyakwan êwako wiyasiwêwin, nama awiya kita-mâcît, asêyas piko kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniw ta-mâcît; êwako ê-oyasowâtahkik onîmihitowak, kîkisêpâ pêyak wîhtam, ê-papâ-têpwêt: "êkosi itwêwak onîmihitôwak," ê-itwêt awa ayîsiyiniw, ê-wîhtamawât kahkiyaw awiya. ||| They all had the same rule, that no one was to hunt, except when all hunted in a band; that was the law of the dancers. Early in the morning one would announce it, going about and crying, “So and so say the dancers,” announcing it to every one.
anohc pîtos nîmihitôwin, ê-mîcisohk, kahkiyaw, awâsisak, iskwêwak, kahkiyaw ê-itohtatahk mîciwin, ayâpisîs pêyak askihkohk piko. ||| Today the dancing is different; there is eating. Everyone, children and women, bring food, each one a small amount, in a kettle.
piyis mistahi pîhcâyihk astêw mîciwin. ||| In the end there is a good amount of food in the tent.
namôya pêyak tipiskâw; nôhtaw ê-âpihtâwi-tipiskâk poyonâniwa. ||| Not one night; they stop before midnight.
kayâs nistam ê-ihtakohk ôma askiy, kisêyiniwak wîhtamâkwak kisê-manitôwa. ||| Of old, when this earth first began to exist, the ancient men were told by the Great Spirit, “A church I will give you, by means of which you will succeed in bringing up your successive generations, a church, so that you may pray to the dwellers in the sky for long life and for success in bringing your children to maturity.
"ayamihêwikamik kiwî-miyitinâwâw, kâ-ôh-ohpikihitoyêk, okîsikôwak ta-nitotamawâyêk kinwês kita-pimâtisiyêk, mîna kitawâsimisiwâwak kita-ohpikihâyêkok." "êwako mâmawô ê-sôhki-astâyân ôta askîhk mawimoscikêwikamik ayamihêwikamik nipâkwêsimôwikamik;" "êwako kimiyitinâwâw kita-pimâtisiyêk," itikwak kisê-manitôwa. ||| This is what I establish here on earth for all, the house of worship, the Christian Church, the Sun-Dance Lodge. This I give to you, to be for you a source of life,” they were told by the Great Spirit.
"isko askiy kita-ihtakohk, êwako ta-mawimoscikâkêyêk, miyo-kêkway ta-nitotamêk, êkosi kitisi-pakitinitinâwâw." "êkâya wîhkâc pônihtâk, isko kita-ihtakohk ôma askiy." "miyo-kêkway kâ-wîhtamâtakok;" "nama wiya kêkway ê-mâyâtahk ka-kî-wîhtamâtinâwâw;" "êwako kinwês ê-pimâtisiwiniwik kâ-wîhtamâtakok," itikwak kisê-manitôwa. ||| “That, as long as the earth shall endure, you pray, asking for rightful things, that is the way I set you down to live. Do you never cease from this as long as this earth endures. It is a rightful thing I proclaim to you; no evil thing shall I ever by any possibility proclaim to you. This which I have proclaimed to you is that there be long life,” they were told by the Great Spirit.
êwako ohci êkâ wîhkâc kâ-ôh-pônihtâcik, ayisk kisê-manitow miyo-kêkway ê-itikoyahk, piko awiya êkosi ta-tôtamahk. ||| That is why they never cease from it, since the Great Spirit told us it is a rightful thing, and that every one of us is to practice it.
êkosi kinwês ka-pimâtisinânaw; nama wiya kî-nipinâniwiw. ||| In this wise we shall live long; there shall be no dying off.
mêstanaskowêw isiyîhkâsôw kisêyiniw; êwako otâcimowin. ||| Mestanaskuwew was the name of a man of old; this is his report.
êkota nêhiyawi-masinahikan kâ-kî-miyikot, êkota ohci ta-tâpwêhtamihk, namôya awiyak ta-kî-ânwêhtahk, ê-wâpahtamihk masinahikan anima kâ-kî-miyikot. ||| There the Great Spirit gave him the Cree writing: so that it would be believed, so that no one would be able to disbelieve it, when that writing was seen, which the Great Spirit had given him.
êwako ohci êkâ kâ-kî-pônihtâcik nipâkwêsimôwikamik, êwako mâmawô ê-sôhki-astamâkoyâhk. ||| That is why they cannot cease from the Sun-Dance Lodge, since the Great Spirit founded it for all of us.
"êwako ohci kâ-ôh-wîhtamâtakok nipâkwêsimôwin, nipiy tê-nitotamêk, ta-kimiwahk, kahkiyaw kêkway ôta askîhk ta-miyo-ohpikihk, kâkikê ta-sâpopatât askiy piyêsiw." ||| “It is for this that I proclaim to you the Sun-Dance, that ye may pray for water, so that it rain and that all things on this earth grow well and that the Thunder-Bird may ever drench the earth.”
êwakoni ê-kî-miyât, ta-pamihtâyit askiy, ta-nitotamâmiht, kisêyiniwak ta-nitotamawâcik êkota nipâkwêsimôwikamikohk. ||| To this last he gave the prerogative of being implored to care for the earth, the prerogative that the old men should pray to him there in the Lodge of the Sun-Dance.
êkosi kâ-isi-pakitinât. ||| Thus he created and set him down.
êkwa êkâ kâ-kimiwahk, ê-sâkihtâhk kita-nipâkwêsimoyâhk, mîna êwako ohci mistahi kâ-ôh-yâh-yôtihk; êkosi nititêyihtênân kâ-nêhiyâwiyâhk. ||| And that it does not rain is because it has been forbidden that we dance the Sun-Dance: and it is due to this that there are great storms of wind; so we think who are Cree.
êwako ohci kâ-ôh-ihkihk ê-nisiwanâtisit ayîsiyiniw, ê-kî-sôhki-astamâht omawimoscikêwin, êkwa ê-sâkihtamâht. ||| It is owing to this that the Indian is going to ruin, because his way of worship which was fixed for him is being withheld from him.
kîspin pakitinikâtêk mawimoscikêwin, namôya êkosi ta-ihkin. ||| f his religion is permitted to him, things will not be thus.
tâpwê ôta ê-kî-miyikoyâhk ta-isi-kakîsimototawâyâhk kôhtâwiyinaw. ||| Truly the Father of us all gave it to us that in this place we should implore him.
mâmawô ôhtâwiyimâw ayisk ê-ôhtâwiyihk ê-nitohtâht, kwayask ispayinâniwiw. ||| If he who is the Father of all is worshipped as becomes his Fatherhood, all will go well.
kisê-manitôw namôya ohci wîhtamawêw môniyâsa tânisi ê-kî-isi-pakitinâyit nêhiyawa ôta askîhk. ||| The Great Spirit did not tell the White Man how he placed and instructed the Cree upon this earth.
êwako ohci êkâ kâ-ôh-kiskêyihtahkik. ||| That is why they do not know it.
mâka êwako ohci kâ-ôh-pakitinahk nêhiyawêwin, nêhiyaw omasinahikan, êkota ohci ta-kî-tâpwêhtamihk. ||| But this was why he sent down the Cree writing, the Cree Syllabary, that through it it might be believed.
piko êtokê ê-asawâpit,/ ê-wî-mâtot nîcimos,/ ê-itwêt,/ "âhwiya, nîcimos/ nisâkihâw," ê-itwêt. ||| I wonder if she only looks out, / Near to weeping, my sweetheart, / And says, / “Ah me, my sweetheart, / I love him.”
âhkamêyimo/ ê-pimohtêyan,/ nicîmisim. ||| Hasten / Your walking / My lover.

nipahêwak; kahkiyaw nama awiyak pimâtisiw pêyakosâp aniki ayahciyiniwak. ||| They slew them; not one of those eleven Blackfoot was left alive.
