"êwako ohci nama wîhkâc ka-pôni-okimâwiw," itwêwak sasîwak. ||| “From that time on never will he cease to be chief,” say the Sarsi.
nêhiyawak têkosihkwâwi, "êyâpic okimâwiw kîskihkomân," itwêwak êsa, kêyotêtwâwi nêhiyawak. ||| Whenever any Cree arrive, “Cut-Knife is still chief,” they say, when the Cree come visiting.
êkosi êkwa mistahi kî-okimâwiw wîhkasko-kisêyin. ||| And so Sweet-Grass became a great chief.
êkâ ôma askiy ôma wîwotinaskêyiwin okosisa ôta kî-okimâwiyiwa. ||| And here, on this very land, when the Reserve was assigned, his son was chief.
êwako nâpêw apis-iyinîs kî-isiyîhkâsôw. ||| Little-Man was his name.
nîsitanaw ayiwâk kêkâ-mitâtaht aspin kâ-nipit. ||| It is twenty-nine years since he died.
kîtahtawê mîkiwâhpihk ohci sipwêhtêw, kêkâ-mitâtaht ê-ihtasicik ê-sipwêhtêcik, ê-mostohtêcik, ê-nitonawâcik ayahciyiniwa. ||| At one time he set out from his lodge; nine men were in the party; they went on foot, looking for Blackfoot.
kîtahtawê niyânanwâw ê-tipiskâyik, niyânanwâw ê-kî-nipâcik, mostoswa wâpamêwak. ||| When five nights had passed and five times they had slept on the way, they saw some buffalos.
pêyak awa sipwêhtêw, ê-nitawi-pâskiswât. ||| One man went out to shoot them.
ê-nipahât pêyak, kahkiyaw êkota itohtêwak ê-wiyanihâcik, ê-wî-mîcisocik. ||| When he had killed one, all went there to skin it and cut it up, and to eat.
êkwa ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, omaskisiniwâwa ê-kaskikwâtahkik, ê-mîsahahkik ê-pîkopayiyiki, êwako wîhkasko-kisêyin pasikôw, ê-sipwêhtêt ê-pêyakot. ||| When they had eaten and were sewing moccasins or mending such as were torn, Sweet-Grass arose and went off alone.
êwako ayinânêwosâp ê-tahtopiponwêt awa kâ-sipwêhtêt, ê-wî-kakwê-wâpamât ayahciyiniwa. ||| Eighteen years old was he when he then set out to see Blackfoot. Meanwhile the others stayed where they were.
ôki wiya kotakak apiwak. ê-asawâpit ê-wî-kakwê-wâpahtahk kêkway, ê-ispatinâyik êkota ê-pa-pimisihk, kisiwâk ôta osêhcâyiw; nama kêkway wâpahtam. ||| When he looked out to see what there was to be seen, as he lay there on a rise of the land, close by the land was hilly; he could not see anything.
kîtahtawê kêkway pêhtam ê-pitihkwêyik. ||| After a while he heard something come thudding.
kîtahtawê wâpamêw ê-pê-sâkêwêpayiyit mostoswa mihcêt, kâ-wâpamât ayahciyiniwa mihcêt ê-pê-nawaswâtâyit ôhi mostoswa, ê-wî-nipahâyit. ||| Then he saw a great herd of buffalos come forth and saw a large band of Blackfoot coming in pursuit of the buffalo, to kill them.
namôya kî-tapasîw, wâpamikoci ta-nipahikot. ||| He could not flee, for if they saw him, they would kill him.
kâsôw êkota apisîs ê-sakâsiyik; êkota pimisin, acosisa ê-tahkonahk; nama kêkway pâskisikan. ||| He hid there in a small clump of trees; there he lay, holding his arrows; he had no gun.
ita kâ-pimisihk, kisiwâk ôta pimipayiyiwa mostoswa. ||| Close by the place where he lay came the buffalos.
itê kâ-pê-ohtohtêyit, êkotê misiwê nipahêyiwa mostoswa. ||| Everywhere in yon direction whence they had come, the others had killed buffalos.
êkwa ê-itâpit, misiwê wâpamêw itê kâ-kî-itohtêyit. ||| And when he looked this way, he saw them all going on.
kîtahtawê ê-pimisihk, nâway ê-pê-ihtâyit awa ayahciyiniwa, iskwêwa ê-wîcêwâyit, owîkimâkaniyiwa, pâskisikan ê-tahkonamiyit ôhi nâpêwa, êwakoni otihtik. ||| At last, as he lay there, behind the rest came a Blackfoot with a woman, his wife; the man carried a gun; these came to where he was.
wîhtamawêw owîkimâkana awa iskwêw, ôhi ê-pimisiniyit nêhiyawa. ||| She told her husband that a Cree lay there.
ê-itâpit awa ayahciyiniw, otinam opâskisikan. êkwa awa nêhiyaw kâ-pimisihk acosis ôma otinam, ôhi ayahciyiniwa ê-pimwât; nipahêw. ||| [no translation] Then the Cree who lay there took an arrow like this and shot the Blackfoot, killing him.
âsay mîna êwakoni ôhi iskwêwa pimwêw; mîna êwakoni nipahêw. ||| Then he shot the woman; her too he killed.
êkosi pasikôw; ôhi nâpêwa kâ-nipahât pâskisikan otinam; otêmiyiwa nîso otinêw; têhtapiw. ||| So then he got up; he took the gun from the man he had slain, and his two horses; he mounted.
êkwa awa ayahciyiniwa mihcêt itê kâ-nipahâyit mostoswa, êkotê itohtêw, ê-têhtapit. ||| Where those Blackfoot had killed many buffalos, thither he went, now on horseback.
âta wiya wî-maskamêw; namôya wî-kitâpamêw, ê-kostahk ta-nisitawêyimikot ê-nêhiyâwit. ||| He wanted to rob them, but he did not want to look upon them, fearing they would know him for a Cree.
piyisk miyâskawêw, mihcêt ayîsiyiniwa ê-kî-miyâskawât. ||| At last he passed them; he passed a great many people.
namôya kiskêyihtam kwayask ê-itohtêt pêyak ôhi ayahciyiniwa ê-wiyanihâyit mostoswa. âsay kî-itohtêw. ||| He had unwittingly gone straight to one of the places where the Blackfoot were preparing buffalo.
êkosi"tânisi kî-tôtamân?" itêyihtam, ê-kostât êwakoni. ||| Beyond retreat he had gone there. “What can I do?” he thought, fearing them.
apisîs ohpimê pimohtêw, ê-têhtapit, pêyak ê-sakâpêkinât misatimwa, ayahciyiniwa otêmiyiwa ê-maskamât êwakoni kâ-nipahât. ||| He rode a bit to one side, leading by the bridle the other one of the horses he had taken from the Blackfoot he had slain.
êkwa ôhi kâ-kâh-kitâpamikot nisitawêyimik ê-nêhiyâwit, ê-otinâyit otêmiyiwa; wâpiskisiyiwa; êkosi tapasîw. êkwa têhtapiyiwa. ||| Then when one of the others looked at him, he knew he was a Cree and that he had taken some of their horses; white horses they had; and so he fled.
ê-kîsi-têhtapit awa ayahciyiniw, têpwêw; owîcêwâkana kitâpamik. ||| Then the other mounted. When the Blackfoot mounted, he whooped; his companions looked.
êkosi aniki ayahciyiniwak mihcêt pê-sipwêpayiwak. ||| In this way those Blackfoot started off in a crowd.
êkosi êkwa kâ-tapasît awa nêhiyaw. ||| And so the Cree fled.
êkwa awa kâ-nisitawêyimât nêhiyawa nawaswâtêw ôhi nêhiyawa, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahât. ||| The one who had recognized him as a Cree pursued him to kill him.
êkwa awa nêhiyaw ê-âpasâpamât, "mahti kisiwâk kita-ayât." ôhi kâ-na-nawaswâtikot kisiwâk ayâyiwa, kisiwâk ê-askôkot. ||| When the Cree looked back at his pursuer, “I shall let him get near.” Closer and closer behind him came he who was pursuing.
wâhyaw pâpayiyiwa; wâyonipitêw ôhi kâ-têhtapit ê-môskîstawât ôhi wâhyaw kâ-pê-nakasiwêyit. ||| A long way had the other come; he turned back the horse and attacked the man who had come outdistancing his companions.
kisiwâk ê-osâpamikot, pâskisok. ||| The other saw him near and shot at him.
êkosi tapasîyiwa. êkwa wiya pâskiswêw; nîhciwêpahwêw; nipahêw. ||| Then he shot at the other; he knocked him from his horse, killing him.
âsay mîna êwakoni otêmiyiwa otinêw. ||| This one's horse also he took.
kâ-mihcêticik aniki ayahciyiniwak ê-otihtâcik ôhi kâ-nipahimiht, êkota poyowak. ||| All the other Blackfoot, when they reached the one who was slain, stopped there.
osâm âsay wâhyaw ayâw, ê-tapasît. êkwa owîcêwâkana aspin kâ-kî-nakatât ita kâ-kî-mîcisocik, êwakonik wiya ê-pêhtahkik ê-mâh-matwêwêyik, kî-tapasîwak, ê-mosci-pimipahtâcik, "mâskôc nipahâw", ê-itêyihtahkik,- ôhi kâ-kî-nitawi-ay-asawâpiyit. ||| He was already too far away in his flight Then his companions whom he had left there where they had eaten, when they heard the shots, fled running on foot, thinking, “Perhaps the others have killed him,” - the one who had gone to reconnoitre.
êwako awa kâ-kî-nitawi-asawâpit, êwako nîso nipahêw ayahciyiniwa; nisto misatimwa maskamêw; pêyak pâskisikan; iskwêwa pêyak nipahêw. ||| But he who had gone to reconnoitre had killed two Blackfoot; he had taken three horses from them and one gun; he had killed one woman.
owîcêwâkana miskawêw awa nêhiyaw. ||| That Cree found his comrades.
êkwa âcimôw ôma ka-isi-wâpahtahk, kâ-isi-otinât ôhi misatimwa. ||| Then he told of what he had experienced and of how he had taken those horses.
êkota ayâwak, owîcêwâkana ita ê-miskawât. ||| They stayed there where he found his comrades.
êkwa ê-tipiskâyik, êkota ohci kâwi sipwêhtêwak, ê-itohtêcik ôhi ayahciyiniwa ita ê-wîkiyit, êkwa ê-kimotamawâcik otêmiyiwa. ||| When night came, they set out again, going to where those Blackfoot dwelt, and stole their horses from them. Then they fled.
êkota tapasîwak. kîwêwak; êkwa piyis êkosi isi takosinwak wîkiwâhk. ||| They returned home, and so at last reached their camp.
êwako awa kâ-tôtahk wîhkasko-kisêyin. ||| The one who did thus, was Sweet-Grass.
kîtahtawê ê-ayâcik wîkiwâhk, wawêyîwak, ê-sipwêhtêcik, ayahciyiniwa ê-nitonawâcik, ê-wî-kakwê-kimotamawâcik otêmiyiwa, ahpô pêyakoyici ê-wî-nipahâcik ayahciyiniwa. ||| Once upon a time some people got ready and went forth to look for Blackfoot, to try to steal their horses from them, or, if one was alone, to kill the Blackfoot.
sipwêhtêwak; mitâtaht ayinânêwosâp ihtasiwak nêhiyawak ôki, oskinîkiwak. ||| They set out; eighteen was the number of these Cree, young men.
kîtahtawê sîpiy ê-otihtahkik, êkota ê-kapêsicik, ê-wî-nipâcik tipiskâki, ê-tipiskâyik kisinâyiw, ê-misponiyik. ||| In time, when they came to a stream, they made camp there, to sleep that night. When night came, there was frost, and snow fell.
piyisk wâpan; misponiyiw. ||| Dawn came; it snowed.
"hâw, mâcîk," itêwak oskinîkiwa; "pôni-mâyi-kîsikâki, iyikohk ka-sipwêhtânânaw." "nipahâyêko mostos, namôya ka-nôhtêhkatânânaw." ||| “Now go hunt,” they said to the young men; “When the storm ceases we shall go on. If you kill a buffalo, we shall not go hungry.”
tâpwê pêyak oskinîkiw pasikôw, ê-sipwêhtêt, ê-wî-kakwê-wâpamât mostoswa, ê-mâcît. ||| So a youth arose and set out to look for buffalos, to hunt.
pôti ê-pimohtêt, kâ-wâpamât ayahciyiniwa ê-pêyakoyit. ||| There as he walked along, he caught sight of a lone Blackfoot.
pê-kîwêw owîcêwâkana ita kâ-ayâyit. ||| He came back to his companions.
ê-takohtêt ômisi itêw: "niwâpamâw ayahciyiniw ê-pêyakot," itêw. ||| When he got there he said, “I saw a lone Blackfoot,” he told them.
êkosi wawêyîwak, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahâcik; ati-sipwêhtêwak, ê-itohtêcik ita ka-wâpamimiht. ||| Accordingly they made ready to try to kill the Blackfoot; they set out one after the other and went to the place where the Blackfoot had been seen.
cîki ê-ihtâcik, wâpamêwak misatimwa ê-kîwêtisahwâyit. ||| When they were close by, they saw him driving home horses.
môskîstawêwak, ê-wî-kakwê-maskamâcik ôhi misatimwa. ||| They attacked him, to rob him of his horses.
awa ê-wâpamât nêhiyawa ayahciyiniw, tapasîw, ê-sipwêtisahwât misatimwa. ||| When the Blackfoot saw the Cree, he fled, driving on the horses.
ê-pimipahtât, kisiwâk sîpiy ayâyiw, êkota ê-pinasiwêtisahwât ôhi misatimwa. ||| As he ran along, a river was near there; down to it he drove the horses.
êkota ê-wîkicik ôki ayahciyiniwak. ||| That was the camping-place of those Blackfoot.
êkota ê-sâkêwêcik ita sîpiyihk nêhiyawak, kâ-wâpahtahkik mîkiwâhpa. ||| When the Cree came out upon the river, there they saw the tents.
wawêyîwak ayahciyiniwak, ê-têhtapicik otêmiwâwa, ê-nawaswâtâcik ôhi nêhiyawa. ||| The Blackfoot got ready and mounted their horses, and pursued the Cree.
ê-pimipahtâcik nêhiyawak, kotak ê-pasahcâyik ê-sakâyik êkota ê-itohtêcik, kâ-wâpahtahkik kotaka mîkiwâhpa. ||| As the Cree, in their flight, came to another wooded gully, there they saw some other tents.
mîna êwakoni ayahciyiniwa. ||| These people too were Blackfoot.
êkota ohci tapasîwak. ||| From here again they fled.
mîna êwakoni môskîstâkwak. ||| These people, too, attacked them.
êkwa mihcêtiyiwa, wiyawâw ayinânêwosâp ê-ihtasicik. ||| By this time the others were many, and of them therefore only eighteen.
wâpahtamwak ê-minahikoskâyik; êkota sêskisiwak. ||| They saw a spruce-grove; they fled into it.
"hâw, oskinîkîtik, wâtihkêk," itwêwak ôki nêhiyawak. ||| “Come, young men, dig a trench,” said the Cree.
âsay wâsakâm ayâyiwa ayahciyiniwa. ||| By this time the Blackfoot were all around.
âsay mâci-pâskiswâwak; wiyawâw mîna pâskiswêwak. ||| Now they began to be shot at; and they, too, shot at the others.
wâtihkêwak mistahi ôki oskinîkiwak, êkota ê-apicik wâtihk. ||| Those young men dug a large trench, and they stayed in the trench.
ômisi isiyîhkâtêw ôma wâtihkân: "mênisk" isiyîhkâtêw. ôki kâ-âyimisicik êwakonik ômisi isiyîhkâsôwak: "ê-nâpêhkâsocik" isiyîhkâsôwak, namôya ê-pîhtokêcik wâtihkânihk, êwakonik ê-âhkamêyimocik ê-nôtinikêcik. ||| Such a trench is called “earthwork.” The men who fight so as to be feared are called “braves,” those who do not go into the pit but courageously fight.
piyisk kinwêsk nôtinikêwak. ||| They fought for a long time.
ê-tipiskâyik, kotaka mîna takosiniyiwa ayahciyiniwa, êkoni mîna ê-nôtinikocik. ||| At nightfall some more Blackfoot arrived, and these too joined in the fight against the Cree.
piyis wâsakâm êkota kotawêyiwa, "êkâ ta-sipwêhtêcik," ê-itêyimikocik. ||| Finally they built fires all around, intending to bring it about that the Cree should not leave that place.
namôya nipâwak, ê-nôtinikêcik. ||| They did not sleep for fighting.
âsay mihcêt nipahêwak ayahciyiniwa; wiyawâw nama kêkway nipahikwak ôki nêhiyawak. ||| By now they had killed many Blackfoot; the latter had killed none of the Cree.
piyisk ê-sâkâstêyik, kotaka mîna takohtêyiwa ê-pê-nâh-nâtamâtoyit, ê-pê-wîcihitoyit, ê-wî-kakwê-mêscihikocik. ||| When daylight came, again some other Blackfoot arrived, to relieve the others, and help them try to massacre the Cree.
mâka nama kêkway nipahikwak; cêskwa wiyawâw mihcêt nipahêwak. ||| But they killed none at all of the Cree, while the latter killed many of them.
êwako kapê-kîsik nôtinitôwak, piyisk ê-wî-tipiskâk, nisto piko nôtinikêwak nêhiyawak. ||| They fought all that day, until, toward nightfall, only three of the Cree were still fighting.
ômisi isiyîhkâsôw awa nêhiyaw kâ-âyimisit ê-nôtinikêt: wîhkasko-kisêyin isiyîhkâsôw. ||| This was the name of the Cree who fought most redoubtably: Sweet-Grass was his name.
êkwa kotak mistahi-maskwa isiyîhkâsôw. êkwa kotak napatê-kîsik isiyîhkâsôw; êwako nôhtâwiy. ||| Another was called Big-Bear, and the other was called Half-sky; he was my father.
êkwa ê-tipiskâyik, âsay mîna kotaka takohtêyiwa ayahciyiniwa. ||| Then, at night, still more Blackfoot arrived.
âsay mâka mihcêt nipahêwak ayahciyiniwa. ||| But by this time they had slain many Blackfoot.
êkwa mistahi ê-tipiskâk, nêstosiw mistahi-maskwa; pîhtokêw wâtihkânihk, nîso-kîsikâw, kêkâc nîso-tipiskâw ê-nôtinikêt, kâ-nêstosit. ||| Then, late in the night, Big-Bear got tired; he went into the pit, wearied from having fought two days and almost two nights.
nîso piko êkwa nôtinikêwak nêhiyawak. ||| Then only two Cree were fighting.
wâsakâm kisiwâk ê-pê-itohtêyit ayahciyiniwa, iskotêw ê-tahkonamiyit, êwako ohci ê-pakamahokocik, "ka-kakwê-kîsisôwak," ê-itêyimikocik, piyisk, mistikwa wâsakâm ê-kî-astâcik omêniskiwâhk, piyisk êwakoni saskitêyiwa; mâka namôya kîsisôwak. ||| As the Blackfoot came close from all sides, bearing fire, with which they struck at the Cree, meaning to burn them, at last the sticks which they had placed round their earthwork caught fire, but the Cree were not burned.
kîtahtawê awa napatê-kîsik kâ-isiyîhkâsot êwako ospiskwanihk, ôhi otîhiya êkota, pahkihtiniyiw môsasiniy, ayahciyiniwa ê-pâskisokot; mâka namôya pîkopayiyiwa wasakaya, namôya ê-kî-pikwâhokot; mâka oskan pîkopayiw. ||| Then at one time he whose name was Half-sky, a bullet hit him in the back, here at his shoulder-blade, as the Blackfoot shot at him, but his skin was not broken, he was not pierced by the bullet; but the bone was broken.
êkosi êkwa namôya kî-miciminam pâskisikan. ||| So now he was not able to hold a gun.
ospiton napatê namôya âpacihtâw. ||| He was not able to use his arm on that side.
êkwa pôyôw kâ-nôtinikêt; êkwa pêyakôw wîhkasko-kisêyin ê-nôtinikêt. ||| So he ceased fighting; now Sweet-Grass was alone in the fight.
piyisk kisiwâk êkwa ayâyiwa ayahciyiniwa. ||| At last the Blackfoot were quite near.
kîtahtawê wîhkasko-kisêyin kâ-wâpamât kisiwâk mistikwa ê-cimasoyit, êkota ê-pê-nahapiyit, ê-âkôsimoyit, ê-misikitiyit mistikwa. ||| Then, at one time, Sweet-Grass saw, where a tree stood close by, that a Blackfoot came and crouched near it, shielding himself behind it, behind the big tree.
êkota ohci wâpamêw ê-pê-mihcêtiyit ôhi ayahciyiniwa, êkwa ê-wî-kakwê-otihtinikocik owâtihkâniwâhk. ||| On that side he saw the Blackfoot coming in numbers and making ready to storm them in their trench.
pôti awa ayahciyiniw kâ-nîkânohtêt mistikohk kâ-apit. ||| There, by the tree, sat the Blackfoot who marched in the lead.
awa nêhiyaw itê kâ-ôh-ayât êkotê ohci, awa mistik kayâs êsa ê-kî-kîsisot, wâpamêw ôhi mistikwa, ê-kî-wâsahîhkasoyit. ||| From where he was, that Cree saw that tree, and saw that it had of old been burned, struck by lightning.
êkosi êkwa ôta pâskiswêw mistikwa awa nêhiyaw. ||| So the Cree shot at the tree itself.
ôtê sâpopayiw awa ayahciyiniw; wâskikanihk pahkihtiniyiw môsasiniy; nipahâw. ||| The Blackfoot was pierced to the heart; the bullet entered his breast; he was killed.
êkosi ôhi otôskinîkîma owîcêwâkana kahkiyaw tapasîyiwa, ê-nipahiht ê-okimâwit awa ayahciyiniw. ||| Then his followers and companions all fled, when the Blackfoot chief was slain.
êkosi êkwa pôni-tasinamwak; pôni-nôtinitôwak. ||| Thereupon they ceased firing; they ceased fighting.
kîtahtawê kâ-matwê-pîkiskwêt awa ayahciyiniw ê-nêhiyawêt; "awêniki kiyawâw?" êkosi itwêw. ||| Then the Blackfoot called out, in Cree; “Who are you?” he asked.
"âtiht okimâwak ninisitawêyimâwak." ||| “I recognize some chiefs.”
êkosi ômisi itwêwak nêhiyawak: "nama awiyak okimâw ôta," itwêwak nêhiyawak. ||| Then thus answered the Cree: “There are no chiefs here,” they said.
âta nîso okimâwak nêhiyawak: wîhkasko-kisêyin êwako pêyak okimâw; êkwa kotak mistahi-maskwa, êwako mîna okimâw; mâka namôya wî-wîhtamawêwak. ||| To be sure, two of the Cree were chiefs. Sweet-Grass was a chief, and Big-Bear also was a chief; but they did not want to tell him this.
piyisk awa ayahciyiniw matwê-pîkiskwêw, "tânitahto kinipahikawinâwâw, nêhiyâtik?" êkosi itwêw. ||| Later the Blackfoot called; “How many of you have been slain, O Cree?” he asked.
"nama kêkway," itwêwak nêhiyawak. ||| “None at all,” answered the Cree.
cikêmâ nama kêkway nipahâwak nêhiyawak. ||| And in fact, none of the Cree had been killed.
"kiyawâw mâka?" itêwak nêhiyawak. ||| “And you?” the Cree asked them.
ômisi itwêw ayahciyiniw: "têpakohp mistahi ê-okimâwicik kaskitêwayasitak kâ-nipahâyêkok;" "êkwa mihkoyiniwak nikotwâsik okimâwak kinipahâwâwak;" "êkwa sasîwak nêwo okimâwak kinipahâwâwak; êkwa pîkanôwînawak nîso okimâwak." "namôya mihcêt ôta ayâwak pîkanôwînawak; mâka ôki kotakak kâ-wâh-wîhakik, itôwahk mihcêt okimâwak kinipahâwâwak." "êkoyikohk wî-pôyôwak;" "êkosi kikostikowâwak." êkosi itwêw awa ayahciyiniw. ||| Thus spoke the Blackfoot: “Seven great chiefs of the Blackfoot you have slain; and six Blood chiefs you have slain; and four Sarsi chiefs you have slain, and two Piegan chiefs. There are not many Piegans here, but of those whom I have named, of them you have killed many chieftains. Now they will cease; they fear you now.” Thus spoke that Blackfoot.
êkosi tâpwê pôni-pâskisotôwak. ||| Then really they did cease shooting at each other.
êkwa ôki nêhiyawak pêyak nâpêsis êkota ê-wîcêwât, wâtihkânihk ê-kî-apit awa nâpêsis, "mahti nika-wâpamâwak ayahciyiniwak," itwêw awa nâpêsis. ||| And among those Cree a young lad who was with them and had stayed in the trench, “Let me go look at the Blackfoot,” said this boy.
"êkâ wiya!" itik owîcêwâkana. ||| “Do not!” his comrades said to him.
âhci piko wayawîw wâtihkânihk ohci. ||| Nevertheless he went out of the trench.
kîtahtawê kâ-matwêwêyik; kîpiwêpahwâw, wâwikanihk ê-tawahoht, ê-kaskâwikanêhoht. ||| At once a shot rang out; he reeled over, struck in the spine, the bone shattered.
êkosi otinêwak, ê-ahâcik wâtihkânihk. ||| They got him and laid him in the trench.
"êkosi kâ-kî-ititân; osâm namôya kipa-pêhtên," ê-itâcik ôhi nâpêsisa; "kî-tâpwêhtaman, namôya kâ-kî-tawahokohtayak," itêwak. ||| “This is what I told you; but you did not listen,” they told him; “If you had obeyed, you would not have been wounded,” they said to him.
êkwa kîwêwak ôki ayahciyiniwak. ||| The Blackfoot went home.
êkwa nêhiyawak ay-apiwak êkota, "mâskôc tâpwê kipônihikonawak," ê-itwêcik. ||| The Cree stayed there, saying, “Perhaps they really have given us up.”
kîtahtawê pêyak awa nâpêw, "mahti nika-wâpamâwak; mahti tâpwê kê-kîwêcik," ê-itwêt, ê-sipwêhtêt. ||| Presently one man said, “Let me go look at them; suppose they really will turn out to have gone home,” said he and departed.
pôti namôya wâpamêw, ê-kîwêt. ||| He did not see them; he came back.
nôhtêyâpâkwêwak, nîso-kîsikâw nîso-tipiskâw êkâ ê-minihkwêcik, êkâ ê-mîcisocik, namôya ê-nipâcik. ||| They were thirsty, not having drunk for two days and nights, and having neither eaten nor slept.
êkosi pasikôwak ê-wî-sipwêhtêcik. ||| So they got up to go away.
"ê-wî-nakasiyêk cî?" êkosi itwêw awa nâpêsis. ||| “And are you going to leave me?” asked that boy.
ayisk namôya kî-pimohtêw awa nâpêsis. ||| For he was not able to walk.
"namôya," itik owîcêwâkana; "ê-nôhtêyâpâkwêyâhk." "miskamâhko nipiy ka-pê-nâtikawin," ê-itâcik ôhi nâpêsisa, ê-wayêsimâcik, ê-pê-kîwêcik, ê-pê-tapasîcik. ||| “No,” his companions answered him; It is only that we are thirsty. When we have found water, you will be fetched,” they told him, deceiving him, for they were going to flee for home.
êkosi kahkiyaw pimâtisiwak, wîkiwâhk ê-takohtêcik. ||| So they all stayed alive and reached their village.
awa wîhkasko-kisêyin oskotâkay wâpôwayân nistomitanaw nîsohayiwâk tahtwayak, êkosi nama nânitaw mâ-misiwê ê-pikwâhoht. ||| Sweet-Grass' coat and blanket had thirty-two bullet-holes, but in no spot was he wounded.
namôya kayâs. mâskôc mitâtahtomitanaw askiy. ||| It is not old Perhaps a hundred years.
kîtahtawê ita ê-ayâcik, ê-wîkicik nêhiyawak, mâwacihitôwak ê-sipwêhtêcik oskinîkiwak, ayahciyiniwa ê-nitonawâcik, ê-wî-kimotamawâcik otêmiyiwa misatimwa, kîspin mâka wâpamâtwâwi, pêyakoyici, ta-nipahâcik; êkosi itêyihtamwak. ||| Once where some Cree lived, the young men assembled to go out looking for Blackfoot, in order to steal their horses from them and, if they saw one alone, to kill him; that was their intent.
êkwa kâ-wâpahk, kâ-pimohtêcik, têpakohp tahtwâw ê-nipâcik, êkoyikohk wâpamêwak ayahciyiniwa ita ê-wîkiyit. ||| So on the next day they set out, and when seven times they had slept on the way, they saw some Blackfoot encamped.
êkosi kâsôhtawêwak; namôya wâpamikwak. ||| They hid from them; the others did not see them.
êkwa ê-itohtêcik, ê-tipiskâyik, ê-otihtâcik ita ê-wîkiyit, apiwak êkota, cîki ita kâ-ayâyit. ||| Then, at night, when they went there and reached the others' camp, they sat there close to where the others were.
nîso nâpêwak itohtêwak mîkiwâhpihk, misatimwa ê-kimotamawâcik, ê-nipâyit. ||| Two men went to a lodge and stole the horses while the owners slept.
êkosi owîcêwâkaniwâwa ê-mâh-miyâcik, ômisi itwêwak: "têhtapik; tapasîtân." ||| Then, when they gave them to their comrades, they said, “Mount; let us flee.”
êkosi tâpwê têhtapiwak, ê-wî-sipwêhtêcik. ||| Accordingly they mounted to depart.
nîso oskinîkiwak âtawêyimêwak; pakwâtêwak ê-mâyâtisiyit misatimwa. ||| Two youths were dissatisfied with the horses they had got; they did not like the horses, because they were ugly.
pakitinêwak; namôya wî-tapasîwak. ||| They let them go and would not flee.
"tânêhki êkâ kâ-tapasiyêk?" ||| “Why do you not flee?”
"â, namôya niwî-tapasîn." "kiyawâw tapasîk." ||| “I shall not flee. Go, you others.”
tâpwê tapasîwak ôki kâ-têhtapicik. ||| So those who were on horses fled.
kotakak nîso nâpêwak mîna êwakonik namôya tapasîwak. ||| Two other men also did not flee.
nêwiwak êkwa êkâ kâ-tapasîcik. ||| Thus they were four who did not flee.
"kiwî-wîcêtinâwâw, oskinîkîtik," itwêw awa kisêyiniw pêyak, "mâskôc otinâyêko misatim, ê-itêyimitakok." ||| “I shall go with you, youths,” said one, an old man, “for I think you may perhaps succeed in getting a horse or so.”
êkosi êkwa ôki êkâ kâ-tapasîcik nîso oskinîkiwak itohtêwak, ayahciyiniwa ita ê-wîkiyit. ||| Then the two youths who had not fled went to where the Blackfoot were camping.
otinêwak misatimwa ê-miyosiyit nîsitanaw pêyakosâp. ||| They took twenty-one handsome horses.
êkwa owîcêwâkaniwâwa, nîso ita ê-pêhikocik ôhi kisêyiniwa otihtêwak. ||| Then they went back to where their two companions, one of them the old man, were awaiting them.
miyêw misatimwa ôho kisêyiniwa êwako. ||| The one gave a horse to the old man.
awa oskinîkiw ômisi isiyîhkâsôw: kiyâhkakiyôwêw, kâ-miyât kisêyiniwa ê-miyosiyit misatimwa. ||| The name of the youth was Kiyahkakiyowew, he who gave the old man a fine horse.
êkosi ômisi itwêw awa kisêyiniw: "kitatamihin, wêskinîkiyin." "êwako ohci kâ-ôh-kisâtitân." ||| Then the old man spoke thus: “I thank thee, youth. It was for this I stayed with thee.”
êkosi êwako awa kisêyiniw ômisi isiyîhkâsôw: tawipîsim isiyîhkâsôw. ||| The name of this old man was Tawipisin.
"êkwa tapasîtân," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Now let us flee,” said the old man.
tâpwê têhtapiwak, ê-tapasîcik, ê-wî-kîwêcik. ||| Accordingly they mounted and made for home.
ômisi itwêw awa kisêyiniw: "oskinîkîtik, êkâ wiya pimitisahwâtânik kiwîcêwâkaninawak." "ohpimê itohtêtân." "wiyawâw mihcêt ayâwêwak misatimwa." "wâpahki ta-pimitisahokwak ayahciyiniwa." "âsay wiyawâw wâhyaw ayâtokênik." "kiyânaw kika-atimikonawak." "pimitisahokoyahkwâwi, ohpimê itohtêtân." "namôya ka-wâpamikonawak ayahciyiniwak." ||| Thus spoke the old man: “Young men, let us not go in pursuit of our companions. Let us go in a different direction. They have many horses. Tomorrow the Blackfoot will pursue them. No doubt they are far on their way by now. It is us whom the Blackfoot will overtake. If they pursue us, let us go in a different direction. The Blackfoot will not see us.”
"ahaq," itwêwak oskinîkiwak. ||| “Very well,” said the young men.
êkwa ohpimê itâmôwak. ||| They fled in a different direction.
tâpwê ê-wâpahk kiskêyihtamwak ayahciyiniwak ê-kimotamâhcik otêmiwâwa. ||| As they had foreseen, in the morning the Blackfoot saw that their horses had been stolen from them.
wawêyîwak, ê-âh-awihitocik otêmiwâwa, ê-pimitisahwâcik nêhiyawa, êkwa kapê-kîsik ê-pimipayicik, nêhiyawa ê-wî-kakwê-atimâcik. ||| They made ready, lending one another horses, and went in pursuit of the Cree, riding all day to overtake them.
namôya wâpamêwak nêhiyawa. ||| They had no sight of the Cree.
âhci piko pimohtêwak, ê-wî-kakwê-wâpamâcik nêhiyawa. ||| Still they went on, seeking to get sight of the Cree.
ê-wâpahk êkwa mîna ê-sipwêhtêcik, ê-pimitisahwâcik nêhiyawa, kîtahtawê kâ-wâpamâcik; ita ê-wî-mîcisocik nêhiyawak, pêyak mostoswa ê-nipahâcik, êkota kâ-wâpamâcik ayahciyiniwak ôhi nêhiyawa. ||| In the morning, when again they set out in pursuit of the Cree, suddenly they saw them; where the Cree were about to eat, having slain a buffalo, there the Blackfoot caught sight of the Cree.
mêkwâc ê-mîcisoyit môskîstawêwak. ||| They attacked them while they were eating.
êkwa ôki nêhiyawak pasikôwak, ê-otinâcik misatimwa, ê-têhtapicik, ê-tapasîcik. ||| The Cree jumped to their feet, seized the horses, mounted, and fled.
êkwa âtiht nôtinikêwak; pâh-pâskiswêwak ayahciyiniwa. ||| Some of them fought; they shot at the Blackfoot.
wiyawâw mîna pâh-paskisokwak ayahciyiniwa. ||| The Blackfoot, too, kept shooting at them.
piyisk kinwês nôtinitôwak, ê-pimohtêcik. ||| For a long time they fought each other as they went along.
pêyak nipahâw nêhiyaw. ||| One Cree was killed.
êkosi poyowak ayahciyiniwak, nêhiyawa pêyak ê-nipahâcik. ||| Then the Blackfoot ceased, when they had killed one Cree.
kâ-pôyocik êkosi kîwêwak ôki ayahciyiniwak. ||| The Blackfoot ceased fighting and went home.
êkwa ôki ohpimê kâ-pimohtêcik nêhiyawak, êwako kisêyiniw awa ita kâ-wîcihiwêt, kâwi êkota itohtêwak, owîcêwâkaniwâwa mêskanaw ê-wî-kakwê-wâpahtahkik, ita ê-kî-pimohtêyit. ||| As for those Cree who had gone off in another direction, the party of that old man, they went back to look for the tracks of their comrades.
tâpwê wâpahtamwak ita ê-kî-pimipayiyit. ||| They saw the place where the others had gone by.
"â, oskinîkîtik," itwêw awa kisêyiniw, "namôya êko-tahto ohci ihtasiwak;" "osâm mistahi ôki misatimwak kâ-pimiskanawêcik," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Now, young men,” said the old man, “there were not so many of them as this; too many tracks have the horses made by here,” said the old man.
oskinîkiwak ôki ômisi itêwak: "êko-tahto ôma kâ-kî-otinâcik misatimwa," itêwak ôho kisêyiniwa. ||| The young men answered him, “This is the number of the horses they have taken,” said they to the old man.
namôya wâhyaw ê-ihtâcik, kâ-pê-sâkêwêyit, ê-nakiskawâcik, ê-kîwêyit awa ayahciyiniwa. wâpamikwak êkosi. tapasîwak ôki nêhiyawak. ||| They were not far on their way, when they encountered those Blackfoot coming out from behind a hill on their way home.
môskîstâkwak. ê-sakâyik êkota sêskisiwak otêmiwâwa kiki. ||| Thus they were seen by the others.
wîhkwêskâkwak ayahciyiniwa. ||| The others attacked them.
wâtihkêwak êkota sakâhk, êkota awa kisêyiniw ê-wî-apit wâtihkânihk, êkwa pêyak oskinîkiw. ||| They took refuge with their horses in a wooded place. They stayed in the brush. The Blackfoot surrounded them.
êkwa nîso ôki oskinîkiwak namôya wî-apiwak wâtihkânihk, êkwa ê-pâskisokocik ayahciyiniwa. ||| They dug a pit there in the woods, for the old man to stay in, and the one young man.
pêyak ômisi isiyîhkâsôw: kiyâhkakiyôwêw isiyîhkâsôw; êkwa pêyak pâhpâscês isiyîhkâsôw. ||| The other two young men decided not to stay in the pit when the Blackfoot fired on them.
êwakonik nêhiyawak ê-nôtinikêcik ê-nîsicik. ||| The one's name was Kiyahkakiyowew, the other's Pahpastches.
nîso wâtihkânihk apiwak; êwakonik ê-pîhtâsocik pâskisikana, ôki kâ-nôtinikêcik ê-âpacihtâcik, kâ-tasinahkwâwi kâ-isiwêpinamawâcik ôhi kisêyiniwa, kotak ê-otinahk pâskisikan. ||| Those were the two Cree who fought. Two sat in the pit; they loaded the guns for those who were fighting, the latter tossing the guns, when they had fired them, to the old man, and taking another.
êwakonik ôki oskinîkiwak, kîspin êkâ ê-kostikocik ayahciyiniwa, êwakoni ê-nipahâcik. ||| These young men, whenever a Blackfoot failed to keep at a cautious distance, him they killed.
ôho wiya otêmiwâwa kahkiyaw nipahêyiwa. ||| But the others killed all their horses.
piyisk mihcêt nipahêyiwa ayahciyiniwa. ||| At last they had killed many Blackfoot.
kêkâc ê-tipiskâyik, êkoyikohk pôyoyiwa ôhi ayahciyiniwa, ê-tapasîyit, ê-sêkihâcik. ||| Almost at nightfall the Blackfoot quit and ran away; they had frightened them.
pêyak piko nipahikwak êwakonik ôki. ||| Only one of these men had been slain.
êkwa ê-kî-tapasîyit, êkwa ê-wâ-wâpamâcik otêmiwâwa. awa kisêyiniw kâ-kî-miyiht misatimwa, êwako piko pimâtisiyiwa, êsa ê-kawipitisoyit, oskâtiyihk ê-tâpakwâtahk pîsâkanâpiy ohci awa misatim. êkosi isi otinêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| Then when the others had run away and they looked at their horses, only the horse which had been given to the old man was alive; it had apparently thrown itself down on the ground by getting its foot snagged in the tether.
êkosi sipwêhtêwak, ê-kîwêcik ôki nêhiyawak. ||| Thus the old man took it. So the Cree set out for home.
pêyak piko nipahâw nêhiyaw, ê-nêwicik. ||| Only one of the four Cree was slain.
cikêmâ wiyawâw mihcêt nipahêwak ayahciyiniwa. ||| But certainly they had slain many of the Blackfoot.
êwako ôhi kâ-ôh-pôyocik, ê-sêkihâcik. êkosi isi pimâtisiwak. ||| They ceased fighting when they had frightened them off.
êkosi ê-wâpahk, kapê-tipisk ê-pimohtêcik, ê-wâpahk, ê-otâkosihk, takosinwak wîkiwâhk ôki nêhiyawak. ||| So they saved their lives. On the next day, after marching all night, in the evening these Cree reached their camp.
wiya piko awa kisêyiniw pêyak pêsiwêw ôhi misatimwa. ||| Only the old man brought home his horse.
ôki wiya oskinîkiwak kahkiyaw nipahêyiwa otêmiwâwa ayahciyiniwa. ||| The young men's horses had all been killed by the Blackfoot.
êkosi êkoyikohk âcimowin êwako. ||| That is the end of this story.
âcimôwin kayâs manitowi-kihiw otâcimowin. ||| This is a story Spirit-Eagle told long ago.
êkota ê-kî-wîcihiwêt, mitâtaht ayiwâkês ê-ihtasiyit, ôta ê-nitopayicik, ayahciyiniwa ê-nitopayîstawâcik, êkwa wâhyaw ê-ayâcik ayahciyiniwa otaskiyihk, êkosi kîkisêpâ sipwêhtêwak, ê-waniskâcik. ||| There where he went with a war party of some ten men or more on the war-path against the Blackfoot, when they were far into the Blackfoots' country, they got up one morning and started out.
êkwa kîtahtawê ayahciyiniwak êsa ê-kî-nipahâcik mostoswa, êwakoni itohtêwak. ||| Presently they came to some buffalos which the Blackfoot, apparently, had killed.
êkosi êkwa kotawêwak, ê-wî-mîciwâcik wiyâs, ê-mîcisocik. ||| So they made a fire, for they intended to make a meal, eating the meat.
mostoso-mêya mâwacihtâwak, ê-wî-pônahkik. ||| They gathered buffalo-dung for fuel.
êkwa êkota apwêwak, wiyâs ê-ma-manisahkik, ê-na-nawacîcik, êkwa nîso ê-ispatinâyik ê-wâpahtahkik, ê-wî-nitawi-asawâpicik, nîso ê-sâkêwêcik. ||| There they did the roasting, cutting slices of meat and making preserved meat; two of them, the while, ascending a rise in the land which they saw, to reconnoitre.
namôya isko ê-mîcisocik, êwakonik kâ-nitawâhtâcik-- kîtahtawê âstam ita ê-sakâsiyik misatimwa kâ-sâkêwêyit; kîtahtawê ayahciyiniwa kâ-sâkêwêyit, êkwa ê-itâpicik, mîkiwâhpa ê-sâkamoyiki. ||| They had not yet eaten, when those scouts - suddenly on this side of a small grove some horses came forth; soon a Blackfoot came forth; and when they looked that way, there the tops of some tents showed forth.
êkosi sakâhk itâmôwak; tapasîwak kônihk, sâkahikanis, êkota piko kôna ê-apit, kwayask ita êyakonik nîso êyakonik kâ-nitawâhtâcik. ||| So they fled into the brush; they fled on the snow, straight to a small lake that was all covered with snow, those two scouts.
êkwa ayahciyiniw sâkowêw, nêhi kâ-nâh-nawaciyit ê-wâpamât, êkwa owîcêwâkana ê-nitomât. ||| The Blackfoot gave the war-whoop, when he saw those who were preparing meat, to call his comrades.
êkosi nêki nêhiyawak tapasîwak, mistahi ê-pasahcâyik êkota ê-itâmocik. ||| So these Cree fled, heading for a deep ravine.
ayahciyiniwak wîhkwêskawêwak nêhiyawa, ê-nôcihâcik. ||| The Blackfoot surrounded the Cree in the chase.
êkwa ôki kônihk kâ-kî-kwayasitêcik kisiwâk wâpamêwak ôhi ayahciyiniwa. ||| Those who had gone into the snow, saw the Blackfoot from close by.
êkwa pimipiciwak êkota cîki, iskwêwak ê-nitawi-kapêsicik êkota. ||| They moved their camp close by there; the women went along to camp there.
apisîs piko tawâw, osâm mistahi ê-pasahcâk, êkota pîhcâyihk nêhiyawak ê-ayâcik, ê-nôcihihcik. ||| There was only a small opening, so narrow and deep was the ravine in which the Cree stayed when they were attacked.
êkwa ôki mistahi mâkwaciwak, nipîhk ê-akocihkik. ||| And these men were very cold, lying in the water.
êkosi kôna ê-pakonênâcik, ê-itâpicik, kisiwâk iskwêwa ê-pimohtêyit, mîkiwâhpa kisiwâk ê-cimatêyiki. ||| When they made a rift in the snow and looked out, there were the women walking by and the tents standing near.
êkwa matwê-sâkowêwak ayahciyiniwak. ||| They heard the Blackfoot whooping.
êkwa awa pêyak kâ-akocihk kônihk, osîma pêyak êkota ayâyiwa, manitowi-kihiw osîma. ||| One of the men who were lying in the snow had a younger brother with the other group; Spirit-Eagle's younger brother it was.
"namôya ayîsiyiniwak ê-wî-pimâcihihcik kâ-matwêwêyik." "êkwa itohtêtân;" "nisîm êkota wîcihiwêw," itwêw manitowi-kihiw. ||| “This noise of shooting is not as when quarter is shown. Let us go there; my brother is with them,” said Spirit-Eagle.
êkwa sâyiman ômisi itêw manitowi-kihiwa: "kiyâm êkâ wiya." "osâm nama awiyak ta-âcimôw, mêscihikawiyahko." "mâka pimâtisiyahko, ôma ê-nîsiyahk kika-âcimonânaw, kîkinâhk takosiniyahko." "mâka itohtêyahko, kahkiyaw nipahikawiyahko, nama awiyak ta-âcimôw nêtê mîkiwâhpihk." "kîkinâhk takosiniyahko, kika-âcimonânaw," itwêw sâyiman. ||| Then Solomon spoke thus to Spirit-Eagle: “Better not. For no one will tell the tale, if all of us are slain. But if we live, we two, we shall tell the tale, when we reach our camp. But if we go there and all of us are killed, no one will tell it there at home. When we reach our camp, we shall tell the tale,” said Solomon.
mosci wâpamêwak ayahciyiniwa ê-pâ-pasahkâpiyit, osâm kisiwâk ê-kapêsimostawâcik. ||| Plainly they could see even when a Blackfoot blinked his eyes, so close had they camped to them.
êkwa misatimwa kêkâc pâh-pistiskâkwak, ê-wî-minihkwêyit. ||| And they nearly were stepped on by the horses that came to drink.
aspapiwina kikiskamwak misatimwak; pîsâkanâpiy otâpêwak ê-sakikwêpisocik. ||| The horses had saddles on; they were dragging reins, being all bridled.
ômisi itwêw sâyiman: "têhcipayihotân ôki misatimwak." "ê-mîhkawikicik êtokê kâ-ôh-oyahpisocik." "nama wiya ka-kî-atimikawinânaw." ||| Thus spoke Solomon: “Let us throw ourselves on these horses. No doubt they are bridled because they are swift. They will not be able to catch up to us.”
êkosi ômisi itwêw manitowi-kihiw: "nama wiya nika-kî-nakatâw nisîm." "ôma kâ-mâh-matwêwêyik êkota aspin kî-wîcihiwêw nisîm," itwêw manitowi-kihiw. ||| To this Spirit-Eagle answered thus: “I cannot leave my brother behind. Over yonder where we hear the shots, is where my brother has gone with the rest,” said Spirit-Eagle.
êkwa ê-pôn-âpihtâwi-kîsikâk, kîtahtawê ômisi itwêw sâyiman: "âta niwî-kawacin; âta wiya niya nika-pimâtisin," itwêw, "kiya mâka?" itêw manitowi-kihiwa. ||| When noon had passed, Solomon spoke: “I am almost frozen to death; yet I shall live,” he said; “But as for you?” he said to Spirit-Eagle.
êkosi ômisi itwêw: "niya mîna nika-pimâtisin," itwêw manitowi-kihiw; "kiya nîkân, sâyiman." ||| Then he answered thus: “I too shall live,” said Spirit-Eagle; “Do you perform first, Solomon.”
"êha," itwêw sâyiman; ômisi itwêw sâyiman: "hâw, miscicâkanis, 'kisiwâk kika-osâpamitin, wî-nipahikawiyini,' kikî-isin." "êkwa ohtin, 'kisiwâk kika-osâpamitin wî-nipahikawiyini,' kikî-isin." "kitakohp kinitâhtâmitin;" "ninôhtê-pimâtisin," itwêw sâyiman. ||| “Very well,” said Solomon; thus spoke Solomon: “Come, Coyote, 'From close by shalt thou see me when thou art in danger of being slain,' saidst thou to me. And Wind, 'From close by shalt thou see me, when thou art in danger of being slain,' saidst thou to me. Thy blanket-robe I ask of thee; I long for life,” spoke Solomon.
"êkosi; pasikô," itêw manitowi-kihiwa, "tapasîtân." "êkâ wiya ohci âpasâpi, kâ-osêhcâk awasêwêyini." "kika-askôtin." ||| “So there; arise,” said he to Spirit-Eagle, “let us flee. Do not look behind you when you pass the knoll. I shall come close behind you.”
êkosi manitowi-kihiw sêkisiw kita-pasikôt, osâm kisiwâk ê-ayâyit ayahciyiniwa; mâskôc nistomitanaw tahkoskêwin êkoyikohk mîkiwâhpa ê-ayâyiki, êwako ohci sêkisiw. ||| Then Spirit-Eagle was afraid to stand up, for the Blackfoot were close at hand; because the tents were perhaps thirty steps away was why he feared.
êkwa sâyiman ati-askowêw. ||| Then Solomon kept close behind him.
ê-osêhcâyik kisiwâk êkota kî-âkawêwêwak. ||| They went to where a hill close by cut them off from sight.
êkwa nîpisiya nânitaw têpakohp misit ê-iskwâyiki, êkota kisâtamwak. ||| In a place where the willows were some seven feet high they stayed.
kîtahtawê misi-yôtin; êwakoni sâyiman kâ-kî-nitomât kita-pimâcihikot. ||| Soon a great wind blew; that was the one whom Solomon had called to save his life.
êkwa kotawêwak; êkwa kêtayôwinisêwak, ê-pâsahkik otayôwinisiwâwa. ||| Then they lit a fire; they undressed and dried their clothes.
mistahi mâyi-kîsikâw. ||| It was very bad weather.
êkosi êkwa ê-tipiskâk, misatimwa kimotiwak, ayahciyiniwa otêmiyiwa, aspapiwina ê-kikiskamiyit. ||| So when night came, they stole horses, the Blackfoots' horses, all saddled.
êkwa ôki nêhiyawak kâ-nôcihihcik, "tapasîtân," itwêw pêyak. ||| As for those Cree who were besieged, “Let us flee,” said one.
êkwa ospwâkana oyaskinahêw; miyêw nâpêwa kita-nitonamiyit ê-tawâk ita. ||| Then he filled a pipe; he gave it to a man who was to look for an opening.
takohtêw kâwi: "êkota âta wiya cawâsiw," itwêw. ||| He came back: “Over here is, to be sure, a small opening,” he said.
êkwa oskinîkiwiyinîs otâhk ê-kaskâwikanêhoht, "ê-wî-nitawi-minihkwêyâhk nipiy," itwêwak nâpêwak. ||| And, as a young lad had been shot in the stomach, “We are only going to get a drink of water,” said the men.
êkwa awa nâpêsis ayih acosisa otinam. ||| Then the lad took some arrows.
"nika-kî-sipwêhtân." "pêyak ayahciyiniw nika-nipahâw," itwêw awa nâpêsis kâ-wî-nakatiht. ||| “I shall be able to go. I shall kill a Blackfoot,” said the lad who was to be abandoned.
êkwa nâpêwak ôki tapasîwak. ||| Then those men fled.

êkosi êyâpic anohc nama êskwa takosin. ||| To this day he has not arrived.

manitowi-minahikoskâhk isiyihkâtêw êkota kâ-kî-nôcihihcik. ||| Spirit-Spruce-Grove is the name of the place where they were besieged.
êkwa mistahi kî-manitôwiw sâyiman kâ-ôh-pimâtisicik. ||| Greatly gifted with spirit power was Solomon; through this their lives were saved.

kapêsiwak, ê-nipâcik. ||| They camped and slept.

ayîsiyiniwa iskwêwa wâpamêw; wiyâpamâci owâhkômâkana, "hêy, pêyâhtik, ôma itê kâ-itohtêyan ê-âyimahk!" itik owâhkômâkana. ||| He saw men and women; when he saw his relatives, “Hey, go slow; there is danger where you are going!” his relatives said to him.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpamât êwakoni iskwêyânihk ê-ayâyit ôhi kâ-kî-kîhkâmikot iskwêwa. ||| Presently, at the very end of the town, there he saw that woman who had taunted him.
wîmâskawêw; nânitaw nikotwâsiyiwa iskwêwa. ||| He circled round to avoid her; there were half a dozen women.
"hêy, kiwanisinin, takwahiminânâhtik!" "itê kâ-itohtêyan namôya kêkway kakî-wâpahtên iskwêwak osikâkwaniwâwa!" âsay mîna êkosi itik. ||| “Hey, you have lost your way, Cherry-Tree! Where you are going you cannot gee any women's calves!” she said to him again.
"hêy, tâpwê mâmaskâc kititâw!" itik wîci-iskwêwa awa iskwêw kâ-miyosit. ||| “Why, strangely are you speaking to him!” the other women said to the handsome one.
mihkwêkin kikasâkêw; mihkwâpowêyân akwanahôw awa iskwêw, awa kâ-itwêt. ||| She wore a jacket of red cloth; a red blanket she had for her robe, that woman, the one who had spoken so.
nama nânitaw itwêw awa oskinîkiw kâ-miyosit, ê-kisipiskawât iskwêwa. ||| Not a word said the youth, but went past those women.
êkwa sôhki pimipayiyiwa. ||| He rode on at a good pace.
nâpêwa pisisik wâpamêw. ||| He saw men all along the way.
êkwa wiyâpamâci owâhkômâkana, "pêyâhtik, takwahiminânâhtik! ||| Whenever he saw any of his relatives, “Go slow, Cherry-Tree!
iyinîsi!" itik owâhkômâkana otôtêma. ||| Be careful!” said his relatives, his kinsmen to him.
kîtahtawê kâ-pêhtahk ê-ma-matwêwêyik. ||| Presently he heard the sound of firing.
wâpahtam ê-sakâyik; êwako wâsakâm ayâwak opwâsîmôwak; êkwa ayahciyiniwak sakâhk ayâwak, mênisk ê-ayâcik, ê-osîhtâcik. ||| He saw a wooded place; all round it were the Assiniboine; and the Blackfoot were in the wood, where they had made an earthwork.
âsay âtiht pahkwêyawâwak opwâsîmowak; ayisk kâsôwak ayahciyiniwak. ||| Already some of the Assiniboine had been wounded by bullets; for the Blackfoot were fighting from shelter.
êkwa awa kisêyiniw pêtisâpamêw okosisa, ê-pâpayiyit. ||| Then that old man saw his son riding toward where he was.
nakiskawêw; otihtêw okosisa. ||| He went to meet him; he went up to his son.
"âstam, nikosis!" itêw. ||| “Come here, my son!” he said to him.
êkwa âkawâyihk itohtahêw. ||| Then he led him to a sheltered place.
"hâw, nikosis, nîhtakosî," itêw. ||| “Now, my son, dismount!” he told him.
apiw êkota awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth sat down there.
"nikosis, pêtâ kipâskisikan mîna kipîhtatwân." ||| “My son, give me your gun and your ammunition sack.”
pâskisikan sipwêhtatâw. ||| He carried the gun away.
haw, wâpamêw oskinîkiwa, cîkahikan-pakamâkan ê-ayâyit. ||| He saw a young man who had a tomahawk.
"ôma pâskisikan!" "hâw, oskinîkiw, ôma mêskoc âpacihtâ." "awihin ôma kicîkahikanis," itêw; "namôya ê-nêsowêyimitân, kâ-nitâhtâmitân ôma kicîkahikan; 'mâskôc kisiwâk osâpahkêci,' ê-itêyihtamân, "nikosis."" ||| “Here is a gun! Now, young man, use it in return. Lend me this tomahawk of yours,” he said to him; “Not because I think you l aboard, am I borrowing this tomahawk of yours; but because I am thinking, 'perhaps my son will come to close quarters.'”
"êha; otina; âpacihtâ," itik ôhi oskinîkiwa. ||| “Very well; take it; use it,” the young man answered him.
êkwa okosisa otihtêw. ||| Then he went to his son.
"hâw, nikosis, kêtayôwinisê!" ||| “Now, my son, take off your clothes!”
ôhi kâ-miywâsiniyiki otayiwinisa kêcikonam kahkiyaw êwakoni, ê-mosêskatêt awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth took off all those fine clothes of his, until he was naked.
êkwa ôhtâwiya wâpatoniskinik misiwê wiyawihk, ohkwâkanihk; wêstakaya âpahamiyiwa ôhtâwiya, ospiskwanihk ê-astâyit. ||| Then his father painted him white all over his body and on his face; his father undid his hair for him and placed it at his back.
"hâw, nikosis, ôma kâ-nêyâskwêyâk, êkota kakwê-otihta ê-tâh-tapasîhk, kinwês ka-pimâtisihk, namôya pêyâhtik ê-pimohtêhk." "ômisi kika-ispayihon;" "nânitaw kêkway wâpahtamani, pêyak ôma ohci kika-cîkahên ayîsiyiniwi-mistikwân;" "êkwa kî-tôtaman, kika-otinên tahto kêkway ê-ayât." "kika-pê-kîwân; ôta ka-pê-itohtân." "hâw, nikosis, niyâ!" itêw. ||| “Now, my son, try to reach that point of the woods, where men dodge and flee that life may be the longer, where walking is not slow. Thus you will do; when you see that which I need not name, with this sole weapon you will cut a human head; and when you have done this, you will take as many things as he has. You will come back here; to this place you will come. Now, my son, be off!” he bade him.
êkwa awa môskîstam ôma sakâw. ||| Then he attacked the wood.
kêkâc ê-sêskisit, kâ-pâskiswât, aspin ê-sêskisit. ||| When he had almost disappeared among the trees, he was fired at, and then he went out of sight.
kîtahtawê kâ-pê-matâwisipahtât; pâskisikan pê-tahkonam. êkwa ayiwinisa êkwa ôma misiwê ostikwân. ||| After a time, there he came, running into the open; he held a gun as he came, and clothes, and an entire head.
âsay misiwê mihko wiyâhk ayâyiw. ||| Blood was all over his body.
êkwa ôhtâwiya otihtêw. ||| Then he went to where his father was.

sipwêhtêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| The old man went away.

êkosi nitawi-miyêw okosisa. ||| Thereupon he went and gave it to his son.
êkosi, "hâw, nikosis, tahto-kîsikâw wiyâs kâ-wâpahtamêk, mâka wiya ôma nôtinitowin namôya tahto-kîsikâw." "kisiwâk kakwê-otihta ita kâ-wîkicik." Try to get near the place where they are dwelling. Use this spear,” he told his son; “where men dodge and flee that life may be the longer, - but I shall go with you,” he told his son.
êkwa cîkahikan tahkonam pakamâkan awa kisêyiniw okimâw. ||| Then that old man, the chief, took in his hand a tomahawk.
êkwa nîkânohtêw awa oskinîkiw, nâway ôhtâwiya. ||| In front walked the youth; behind, his father.

tâh-tahkamêw; êkosi isi kahkiyaw mêscihimâwa. ||| He stabbed one after another; he left not one of them alive.
nîkânohtêw; otêma kaskitêwastimwa; wâpowayân paskitastêyiw. ||| He walked in front; his horse was a black horse; a blanket lay across its back.
êkwa kîwêpayiw awa oskinîkiw wîwa kâ-miyosiyit. ||| Then back rode also the youth whose wife was beautiful.
"nitawi-nakiskaw." "ayis iyikohk nitâtiskâk ayîsiyiniw." "tâpiskôc iskwêw niya," itêw owîkimâkana. ||| “Go to meet him. For now a man has outdone me. Like a woman am I,” he told his wife.
êkwa nakiskawêw ôhi oskinîkiwa kâ-kî-nâh-nêpêwimât; ocêmêw ita ê-nakiskawât. ||| Then she met that youth whom she had shamed by her speech; she kissed him where she met him.

ê-tipiskâyik: pê-nitomâw êkota ôhi kâ-kî-nâh-nêpêwimikot. ||| At nightfall he was sent for and invited to the tent of her who had put him to shame with words.
ê-pîhtokêt, "hâ, nisîm, êkota anohc api." ||| When he entered, “Ah, my younger brother, do you now sit here.”
ana ita kâ-apit iskwêw, êkota apiw awa oskinîkiw. ||| Even where that woman sat, there sat that youth.
"haw, nisîm, kimiyitin êwako ana." "ôta pîhtêyask kika-wîkin." "ka-pamihitinâwâw; nika-kîsitêpon," itêw. ||| “Now, O my younger brother, I give you this person here. Here at the center of the village you shall live. l will care for your needs; I shall cook,” he told him.
êkosi tôtam; pamihêw. ||| He did even so; he cared for all his needs.
êkwa tâpiskôc miyosiwak ôki ayîsiyiniwak. ||| And equally handsome were those men.
êkwa nêpâtwâwi, wiyâpaniyiki, kîsitêpôw awa kotak kâ-mêkit wîwa. ||| And when they had slept, of a morning, that other would cook who had given away his wife.
nicawâc ê-kiskêyimiht, kotaka miyâw iskwêwa. ||| When it was known that he had done this, he was given another woman.
nîsokamikisiwak pîhtêyas ociwâma okosâka. ||| They had their two tents in the center of the town, he and his brother, the husband of his wife.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw kâ-miyosit namôya pisikwâtisiw; kiyâm nipâwak pêyak askiy. ||| But that handsome youth was not forward; they slept there, and no more, for a year.
êkwa ê-âkwâ-nîpiniyik, kîtahtawê kâ-mâtot awa iskwêw, êkâ ê-owîcimosihk, âta ê-wîhpêmât ôhi kâ-miyosiyit oskinîkiwa; mâka kiyâmêwisiw; nêpêwisiw, ê-kî-mâh-mâyi-itikot ôhi kâ-wîwit. ||| Then, when summer came again, presently that woman wept, because there was no love-making, even though she slept in one tent with that handsome youth; but he kept his reserve; he still felt shame at the repeated evil words she had spoken to him, she who now was his wife.
nicawâc ostêsa nitomêw. ||| At last he called his elder brother.
"hâw, nistêsê, awa kîwa kiyaskoc kimiyitin." "osâm wahkê-mâtôw." "niya, 'namôya êkotê kîci-iskwêwak ayâwak,' ê-kî-isit, namôya nîci-iskwêw ta-kî-pisiskêyimak, ta-kî-wîwiyân." "aspin kâ-miyiyan, namwâc nôh-owîcimosin." "êwako ohci namôya awâsisa ayâwêw." "êwako pisisik kâ-ôh-mâtot." ||| “Now, O my elder brother, this your wife I give back to you. She is too easily brought to tears. I, to whom she said, 'Not here are your fellow-women,' I cannot fancy my fellow-woman or have her to wife. From the time when you gave her to me, never have I made love to her. That is why she has no child. That is why she weeps all the time.”
"êha, nisîm, mâka êkâ wiya sâkwêyimo;" "ôta nîkihk êkota wîkihkêmo;" "wîwi ana niwîkimâkan." "nama êskwa awâsisa ayâwêw êwako mîna." ||| “Very well, my brother, but do not withdraw your goodwill; stay here in my house; take this other wife of mine. This one too has as yet no child.”
êkosi tâpwê awa kâ-miyosit oskinîkiw kotaka wîwiw ôhi kâ-miyiht. ||| So then the handsome youth took to wife this woman who now was given to him.
kiyipa awâsisa ayâwêwak. ||| Soon they had a child.
êkosi êwako wiya âcimowin; êkoyikohk ê-isko-âcimostâtân. ||| So goes this story; now I have told it you to the end.
kayâs pêyak nâpêw iskwêwasâkay isiyîhkâsôw ayahciyiniw. ||| Of old a certain Blackfoot was named Skirt.
kîtahtawê mistahi ispatinâhk pa-pimisin. ||| Once upon a time he lay on a hilltop.
kîtahtawê wâpamêw iskwêwa ê-wayawiyit, ê-kî-nipahimiht onâpêmiyiwa, ê-kî-nipahikoyit kâhkâkiwacêna. ||| Presently he saw a woman come out of her lodge, a certain woman whose husband had been killed; the Crow Indians had killed him.
êkosi akâwâtêw nâha. ||| And so now this man took a fancy to her.
êkosi wâpamêw ê-otinamiyit cîkahikan. ||| He saw her take an axe. She was carrying her little son.
wîwahoyiwa okosisiyiwa. êkosi sipwêhtêw. ||| So now he went from where he was.

êkosi kâsôhtawêw ana kâ-kitimâkisit ayahciyiniw. ||| Then that woman looked out in every direction from the hilltop.
êkosi ana iskwêw ispatinâhk nanâtawâpiw. ||| Then, when she saw no one, she went away.

êkosi ê-wâpamât, kâsôhtawêw. ay-ati-wâpahtam apisîs ê-sakâsiyik; êkota nahapiw iskwêw ana. ||| As they thus went along, he saw a small clump of trees; there the woman squatted down.
okosisa ohpimê êkota nahahyêw, okosisa. ||| She laid her little son down at one side.
êkosi otinam cîkahikan; êkwa cîkaham asiskiy; êkwa wâtihkêw. ||| Then she took the axe; she chopped at the ground; she dug a pit.
mâna awa nâpêw piyisk kisiwâk otihtêw awa nâpêw. ||| After a time the man had got quite close to her.
êkwa awa iskwêw pasikôw; nanâtawâpiw; êkâ kêkway ê-wâpahtahk, kâwi nahapiw. ||| Then the woman rose to her feet and looked about; when she saw nothing near, she squatted down again.
kwayasitêw, kayâs mahîkhanisisa ê-mônahwât. ||| She went into the pit, digging for old wolflings.
otinêw pêyak; pa-pakamisimêw. ||| She took one up; she flung it on the ground.
êkosi mîna kwayasitêw. ||| Then she went into the pit again.
êkosi awa nâpêw ispahtâw; ê-pê-wayawiyit, kawipayihôw, ê-kâsôhtawât. mîna kâwi kwayasitêw. ||| At that, the man ran to where she was; when she came forth again, he threw himself flat on the earth, hiding from her.
êkosi pasikôw awa nâpêw. ||| Again she entered the pit. At once the man rose to his feet.
wâpamêw, ôta isko, ôtê isi ê-kwayasitêyit, ostikwâniyihk isi. ||| He saw that up to here, up to this point she was in the pit, up to her head.
êkosi êkota wîwiw ôhi iskwêwa. ||| Then he took this woman for his wife.
êkosi awa iskwêw ôtê, miciminêw ôhi nâpêwa. ||| Thereupon the woman took hold of the man here, like this.
êkosi isi wayawîw; êkosi otinêw okosisa; wîwahôw okosisa awa iskwêw. ||| Then she came forth from the pit; she took up her son; the woman carried her son.
êkwa awa nâpêw otinam ocakohpis. ||| The man took his blanket-robe.
ê-sâkêwêt, mîkiwâhpihk nakîw awa nâpêw. ||| When he came to the town, the man stopped by a tent.
"âstam!" itêw iskwêw awa; "âsay kônâpêmimitin." ||| “This way!” that woman said to him; “You are my husband now.”
kîwêhtahik êkwa, pîhtêyask ê-wîkit awa iskwêw. ||| She took him to her lodge; in the center of the camp dwelt that woman.
êkosi isi pîhtokahik wîkiyihk. ||| So she took him into her tent.
êkosi nahapiwak ohtapiwinihk awa nâpêw. ||| Then they took their seats on the settee of the man of the house.
kâsîcihcênik; mîna kâsîhkwênik. ||| She washed his hands and face.
êkosi wayawîw; paspikâpawiw wîkihk. ||| She went out; she stood in the doorway of her tent.

wâpamêw nâpêwa ê-apiyit ohtapiwiniyihk otânisa. ||| She saw the man sitting on her daughter's settee.
êkosi kîwêw awa nôtokêsiw; pîhtokêw wîkihk. ||| Thereupon the old woman went back; she went into her lodge.
wîhtamawêw onâpêma: "kitânisinaw ê-wîtapimât nâpêwa." ||| She told her husband of it: “It is that our daughter is sitting by the side of a man.”
"awînihi?" itwêw kisêyiniw. ||| “Who is he?” the old man asked her.

êkosi êkwa kisêyiniw awa ê-okimâwit, pêyakoyiwa okosisa; êkwa ôhi kâ-otinamâsoyit nâpêwa, êwakoni otânisa. ||| Now, that old man, who was a chief, had one son; and she who had taken that man, she was his daughter.

kinwês êwako ê-wîwit. ||| This was when he had been married for quite some time.

wîhtamawêw okâwiya: "anihi kâ-ayâ-t nimis ayiwinisa êkosi ta-pêtâw nimis." "tânitê aspin nîstâw?" ||| He told his mother his plan: “Those garments which my elder sister is keeping, let her bring them here. But where has my brother-in-law gone?”
"aspin ôtê ê-kî-atimohtêt," itwêw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| “He has gone off and away in this direction,” said the young woman.
