tâpwê miskawêw, itê ê-pimisiniyit. ||| He found him where he lay on the ground.
êkosi êkota nîhtakosîw. ||| So there he dismounted.
êkosi wîstâwa, "waniskâ, nîsta!" itêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| Then to his brother-in-law, “Get up, Brother-in-Law!” said that youth.
êkosi otinamwêw otayiwinisiyiwa ôhi wîstâwa; kotaka ê-miywâsiniyiki postayôwinisahêw ôhi wîstâwa. ||| Then he took his brother-in-law's garments; he put other, handsome ones, on his brother-in-law.
êkwa sîkahwêw ôhi mitoni ê-kinwâyiki wêstakayiyiwa. ||| Then he combed him, for very long was his hair.
kâ-kîsi-sîkahwât wîstâwa, êkwa kâsîhkwênêw. ||| When he had combed his brother-in-law's hair, he washed his face for him.
êkwa ê-kî-kâsîhkwênât, êkwa tômihkwênêw. ||| When he had washed his face, he painted his face for him.
êkosi, "nîstâ, mistahi kisâkihitn." "êkâ wiya ê-nitohtawakik oskinîkiwak, mihcêtwâw ninitotamâkawin, 'nimis awiya miywêyimâci, ta-onâpêmiw,' ê-kî-itêyihtamân." "êkosi kimiywêyimik." "êkâ wiya nêpêwisi." "êkosi êkwa sipwêhtêtân." "êkosi kita-ayâwat nîstâw otêma, ana kâ-kî-nipahiht." ||| Then, “Brother-in-Law, I love you very much. I did not listen when time after time I was besought, for I thought, 'When my sister likes any one, then let her take a husband.' And so she liked you. Do not be ashamed. And now let us depart. You shall now have the horse of my brother-in-law, the one who was slain.”
mistahi miyosiw awa kaskitêwastim kâ-têhtapit awa kâ-kitimâkisit. ||| Very handsome was the black horse which the poor man rode.
tâpwê ê-pimohtêcik awa oskinîkiw, "tâpwê mistahi miyosiw nîstâw!" itêyihtam awa oskinîkiw. ||| As they went along, “Truly, very handsome is my brother-in-law!” thought that youth.
ôhi mitâsa mistahi mîkisak kikamôwak, êkwa ômatôwahk mêstakaya mîna. ||| On those leggings were many beads, and these things, scalps, as well.
miskotâkay mistahi mîkisiyiwa; êwako kikasâkêw awa kâ-wîwit. ||| The coat was heavily beaded; he wore it, who had married the woman.
êkwa nikikwayân êkotôwahk otastotiniw awa kâ-wîwit. ||| And an otterskin he had as his hat, he who had married the woman.
êkosi ê-otâkosik, ê-sâkêwêcik, âsay kîsi-mânokêwân. ||| Then, in the afternoon, when they came in sight of the place, their people had already pitched camp.
ati-nîhtaciwêwak, ê-ati-nîsicik wîstâwa. ||| They came down the slope, the two brothers-in-law.
êkwa awa iskwêw, ê-pêtisâpamât onâpêma, "tâpwê miyosiw ninâpêm!" itêyihtam awa iskwêw. ||| Then that woman, when she saw her husband approaching, “Truly, handsome is my husband!” thought that woman.
êkosi takohtêwak wîkiwâhk. ||| So they came to their tent.
êkosi awa iskwêw wayawîw. ||| Then the woman came out of the tent.
"pîhtokê!" itêw ôhi onâpêma. ||| “Come in!” she said to her husband.
êkwa awa iskwêw âpahwêw ôhi misatimwa. ||| Then the woman unsaddled the horse.
nahapîstawêw onâpêma. ||| She sat down by her husband.
êkosi otinam, ê-asamât, ta-mîcisoyit. ||| She took food and gave him to eat.
êkwa ê-kîsi-mîcisot, ê-tipiskâk, iyikohk wayawîw. ||| When he had eaten, at nightfall, she went out.
wîcêwêw awa iskwêw onâpêma. ||| Her husband went with her.
kîtahtawê piko isi mêtawâkâtâw awa oskinîkiw, ê-ohtêyimiht, okimâskwêwa ê-wîwit. ||| Then at one time, in one way or another, people teased that young man, because they were jealous of his having married a chief's daughter.
"êkâ wiya pisiskêyihta." "mihcêtwâw piko awiyak nikî-nôhtê-wîkimik, mâka nama wiya ê-ohci-nôhtê-onâpêmiyân." "êkâ wiya wîhkâc nitohta piko isi ê-itikawiyan; ê-ohtêyimikawiyan, mihcêt nâpêwak ê-kî-nôhtê-wîkimicik." ||| “Pay no attention to it. Many times more than one of them wanted to marry me, and it was only that I did not want to marry them. Do you never listen when they say foolish things to you, for it is only that you are envied, because many men wanted to marry me.”
kîtahtawê pêhtam, "ayak pîtos-iyiniwak wâpamâwak." ||| Then at one time he heard, “Some foreign folk have been seen.”
êkosi wîstâwa, "êkâ wiya nânitaw ta-itohtêw;" "nisâkihâw nîstâw." ||| Then his brother-in-law said. “Let him not go, you know where; I love my brother-in-law and would keep him.”
êkosi tâpwê nama wiya pakitinik wîwa. ||| Accordingly his wife did not let him go from her.
êkosi kotakak ê-kîskotâtocik, ôta pêmipayitwâwi, "nama êskwa kikîskotâton." "âsay mihcêt kitôskinîkîmak," itik ôhi kâ-pimipayiyit. ||| So then, whenever the others went out to the attack, as they went past there, “Not yet have you gone to the attack. Already many of your men have gone,” they who rode past said to him.
êkwa ê-sîkâwiwiht, "mahti nâs nitêm," itêw ôhi wîwa. ||| Then when some of his people had lost their kin, “Suppose you fetch my horse,” he bade his wife.
"'êkâ wiya ta-sipwêhtêw,' kikî-itik nisîmis," itik wîwa. ||| “'Do not let him depart,' my brother said of you,” his wife replied to him.
"kiyâm nâs nitêm," itêw wîwa. ||| “Just you fetch my horse,” he told his wife.
êkosi nâtêw awa iskwêw ôhi kaskitêwastimwa. ||| So then the woman went and got that black horse.
êkosi wiyahpitêyiwa ôhi otêma; pîhtokêyiwa wîwa. ||| Then she saddled his horse and came into the tent.
êkwa kêtayôwinisêw; nayêstaw kikâsiyânêw awa nâpêw. ||| Then he undressed; he kept on only his breech-clout.
osâwi-asiskiy misiwê wiyawihk sinikohtitâw, misiwê ê-osâwasiskîwastêt êwako. ||| He rubbed ochre all over his body; he covered himself with yellow clay.
êkosi osikosa pêtohtêyiwa. ||| Then his mother-in-law came hither.
"tânêhki kî-oyahpitat ninahâhkisîm otêma?" ||| “Why have you saddled my son-in-law's horse?”
"'wiyahpis,' ê-isit awa," itêw okâwiya awa iskwêw. ||| “Because he bade me saddle it,” the woman answered her mother.
"kikî-kitahamâk kisîmis kita-sipwêhtêt ninahâhkisîm," itwêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| “Your brother forbade you to let my son-in-law depart,” said the old woman.
êkosi awa nâpêw wêstakaya tahtinam; ôta ospiskwanihk asahpitam; wîwa nânapâcihik; tômihkwênik. ||| Then the man undid his hair; he tied it in a knot at the back. His wife tended to him; she painted his face.
êkosi astotin, sihkosiwayân-astotin êwako, êskanak kikamôwak astotinihk. ||| Also a head-dress, a head-dress of weaselskin; horns were fastened on it.
ê-wayawît, ocêmik wîwa. ||| As he left the tent, his wife kissed him.
"nitânis, êkâ wiya ta-iyiwêhôw ninahâhkisîm." "mistahi sâkihik wîstâwa mîna osisa," itêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| “Daughter, do not let my son-in-law throw his life away. His brother-in-law and his father-in-law love him dearly,” said the old woman to her.
êkosi têhcipayihôw otêma. ||| Then he leaped on his horse.
êkosi wâsakâmêw ôma ôtênaw. ||| Then he made the circuit of the town.
"anohc kâ-kîsikâk kika-wîhinâwâw." "pimâtisiyâni, ka-nahihonâwâw, 'iskwêwasâkay' ta-itwêyêk, pimâtisiyâni," itwêw. ||| “On this day you shall speak my name. If I live, you will be content to say 'Skirt,' if I live,” he said.
ê-sâkêwêpayit, atimâpamêw ayîsiyiniwa. ||| As he rode over the hill, he saw the men going yon way.
êkosi êtimâci mâna êkwa, "kikîsiskotâtoh" itik nâpêwa. ||| And so, as he overtook them, “You are going to the attack, are you?” the men would say to him.
ê-osêhcâk atimâpamêw, ê-sâkêwêpayiyit wîstâwa êkwa osisa. ||| From a rise in the land he saw his brother-in-law and his father-in-law riding across a ridge.
ê-ati-atimât osisa, "hâw, ninahâhkisîm, kakwê-pimâtisi!" itik omanâcimâkana. ||| When he overtook his father-in-law, “Now, my son-in-law, try to preserve your life!” said his tabu-person to him.
ê-atimât wîstâwa, "â, nîstâ, mistahi kisâkihitn" itik wîstâwa. ||| When he overtook his brother-in-law, “Oh, my brother-in-law, dearly do I love you!” his brother-in-law said to him.
êkosi kitâpamêw: "hâh, nîstâ, kisâkihitn nîsta!" itêw wîstâwa. ||| Thereupon he fixed his gaze on him: “Oh, my brother-in-law, I too love you!” he told his brother-in-law.
êkosi ati-miyâskawêw wîstâwa. ||| With that he passed his brother-in-law and went on.
pêyak tahki ômisi nâway pâh-pimicipayiyiwa; wâpascimosa têhtapiyiwa. ||| One man always rode about in the rear of the rest; he was mounted on a little white horse.
mayaw ê-atimât, pâskisok. ||| Just as he overtook this man, the latter shot at him.
pêyak ê-ati-nakatimiht nîhciyahkahwêw câpihcicikanis ohci. ||| When one was left behind, he felled him with his spear.
êkosi êtimâci ati-tahkamêw; piyisk kêkâ-mitâtaht nipahêw. ||| Then he would come up to him, and stab him; at last he had killed nine men.
êkoyikohk êkwa tapasîyiwa ôhi wâpascimosa kâ-têhtapiyit. ||| By this time the rider of the small white horse was fleeing.
ita ê-atimât pâskisok; ôta wanôwâhk kitiskahok. ||| When he overtook him, the other shot at him; here on his cheek the other grazed him with a shot.
êkosi isi nawatinamwêw otêmiyiwa. ||| Then he seized hold of the other's horse.
"nîhtakosî!" itêw ôhi pîtos-iyiniwa. ||| “Dismount!” he told the stranger.
êkosi nîhtakosiyiwa. ||| So the other dismounted.
"miyin kipâskisikan!" itêw. ||| “Give me your gunl” he said to him.
"kimôhkomân miyin!" itêw. ||| “Give me your knife!” he told him.
"mîna pîhtasinânêyâpiya!" ||| “And your ammunition-bag!”
êkosi kahkiyaw miyik. ||| So the other gave him everything.
"mîna kitastotin!" mîkwana ê-otastotiniyit. ||| “And your head-dress!” - for the other had a headgear of feathers.
êkosi, "kitêm miyin!" itêw. ||| Then, “Give me your horse!” he told him.
"hâw, awa têhtapi," itêw, ôhi kaskitêwastimwa mîskoc êwakoni ê-miyât; "mistahi mîhkawikiw;" "nama awiyak kika-atimik." "takosiniyani kitaskîwâhk, kita-âcimoyan; êwako ohci'pitanê pimâtisit!' kâ-ôh-itêyimitân." ||| “There, now mount this one,” he told him giving him the black horse in return; “It is very swift; no one will overtake you. When you arrive in your people's country, that you may tell the tale; that is the reason why 'May he live!' is my thought concerning you.”
êwako awa miyêw otastotin, sihkosiwayân-astotin awa ayahciyiniw, êkwa câpihcicikanis. ||| Then he gave him his head-dress, the headdress of weaselskin, did that Blackfoot, and the spear.
awa kâ-pmâtisit kâhkâkiwacên isiyîhkâsôw. ||| he one whose life was spared was called Crow.
êkwa awa ayahciyiniw pê-otihtik wîstâwa. ||| Then that Blackfoot's brother-in-law came up to him.
mistahi pakwâtamiyiwa ôta ê-miswâkaniwit ohkwâkanihk. ||| This brother-in-law was very sorry that he had been wounded in the face.
ati-otinêw kahkiyaw misatimwa awa kisêyiniw, onahâhkisîma tahto kâ-pê-nipahâyit, mîna otayiwinisiyiwa, mîna onîmâskwâkaniyiwa. ||| The old man, as he went along, took all the horses of as many as were the men his son-in-law had slain, and their garments, and their weapons.
êkosi êkwa kahkiyaw kîwêwak. ||| So then they all went home.
ê-wî-takohtêcik, wâhyaw nîkân pimohtêw awa iskwêwasâkay, êwako, ê-ati-sâkêwêcik. ||| When they had almost arrived, then far ahead went Skirt, as they came into view.
namôya kî-âkwaskiskawâw, osâm mistahi ê-tôtahk; âsay kaskihisôw ê-okimâwit. ||| No one was permitted to go ahead of him, on account of the great deeds he had done; he had now won the chieftainship.
êkosi isi kahkiyaw ayahciyiniwak mistahi kostik, ê-wâpamiht, mistahi ê-pâskisoht, êkosi êkâ ê-pikwâhoht. ||| So then he was greatly respected by all the Blackfoot, when it was seen that he had been much shot at and not seriously wounded.
ê-itêyihtahkik kotakak okimâwak, mistahi kostêwak. ||| When the other chiefs thought of that, they greatly respected him.
nama wîhkâc pêtamâsôw ta-mîcit, piko ê-pêtamâht. ||| Never did he need to fetch his food, for always others brought it to him.
êkwa wîstâwa mistahi sâkihik. ||| And his brother-in-law was very fond of him.
êkosi êkwa mistahi okimâwiw. ||| And so he became a great chief.
êkosi ê-nipit, okosisa kî-okimâwiyiwa, êwako ana kotak ôhtâwiya kâ-nipiyit. ||| And then, when he died, his son became chief, the son of the other man who had died.
kaskitêwi-sihkos isiyîhkâsôw. ||| Black-Weasel was his name.
êwako sâkahikan ê-misâk, nimitaw isi wîkiwak opwâsîmôwak, êkota ê-mihcêticik. ||| To the south of that great lake dwelt some Assiniboine, and they were many.
kîtahtawê pêyak awa nâpêw ocawâsimisa âhkosiyiwa. ||| Then at one time a certain man's child fell sick.
âta ê-atoskêmot, ê-nanâtawihimiht, ê-tipahikâkêt otêma mîna wîkiwâw mîna otayiwinisiwâwa, tahki mistahi âhkosiyiwa. ||| Although he employed medicine-men to have the child doctored, and paid out his horse and his tent and his clothes, yet the child remained very sick.
piyisk kahkiyaw mêstinam otayâna; mîna pâskisikan mêkiw, "pitanê pimâtisit nitawâsimis!" ê-itêyihtah. mâka namôya kî-miyw-âyâyiwa. ||| At last he had spent all his belongings; he gave also his gun, thinking, “Would that my child might live!” But they could not get the child well.
piyisk nipiw awa awâsis. ||| Finally that child died.
êkosi êkwa kitimâkisiw awa nâpêw mîna awa iskwêw, pisisik ê-mâtocik, ê-mawîhkâtâcik otawâsimisiwâwa, piyisk kinwêsk. ||| And so then that man and woman were poor, and they were always weeping, lamenting their child, for a long time.
kîtahtawê kîkisêpâ ê-wâpahtahk ê-wî-wâpaniyik, sipwêhtêw awa nâpêw, "nikwatis nika-papâ-ma-mâton," ê-itêyihtah. sipwêhtêw, mostoswayânisa ê-akwanahot, ê-mamêhkocinêt. ||| Then early one morning, when he saw that day was at hand, that man went off, thinking, “Off by myself somewhere I shall go about and weep.” He went away, wrapping himself in a buffalo hide, without his inner garments.
nama kêkway oskotâkay; nama kêkway otâsa; piko otâsiyâna, êkwa omaskisina, êkwa ocahpihcisa, êkota ê-asiwatêyik êkota môhkomân ê-apisâsiniyik. ||| He wore no coat; no leggings; he had only his breechcloth and his moccasins, and his pouch, which contained a small knife. In this guise the Assiniboine set out, because he was in mourning.
êkosi isi sipwêhtêw awa opwâsîmôw, ê-sîkâwit. wâhyawês ê-ayât, ati-mâtôw. ||| When he had gone a ways, he wept as he went on.
êkwa ê-pa-pimohtêt, ôma kâ-misâk sâkahikan êkota sisonê ê-pimi-ma-mâtot, piyisk wâhyawês ayâw. ||| And, as he walked along, weeping by the shore of that big lake, at last he had gone quite far.
namôya wâpahtam mîkiwâhpa. ||| He could no longer see the tipis.
êkwa pôni-mâtôw, ê-ay-ispatinâyik êkota ê-itohtêt, "êkotê ispatinâhk nika-ay-apin," ê-itêyihtah. pîhtaw ê-astâhikot ayîsiyiniwa, êkwa ê-nitawâpamikot, "kiyâm wâpamitwâwi ayahciyiniwak, nika-nipahikwak, iyikohk kâ-mihtâtak nicawâsimis," ê-itêyihtah. êwako ê-wî-ati-âmaciwêt, namôya mistahi ê-ispatinâyik, awasita kotak mistahi ispatinâyiw, êkota kâ-wâpamât, ôma itê kâ-ôh-ayât ohci, ê-ati-âmaciwêyit ayîsiyiniwa, wâpowêyân ê-kikasâkêyit, pâskisikan ê-tahkonamiyit, ê-ati-nîpawiyit mâna, ê-nanâtawâpiyit. ||| Then he ceased weeping, and went to where there were some hills, thinking, “There on a hilltop I shall sit.” Now that he had come here, he began to be frightened by the thought of Blackfoot, who might come and see him, but he thought, “If the Blackfoot see me, let them kill me, so much do I grieve for my child.” As he was on the way, climbing a smaller hill, there rose beyond it another very high one, and there he saw, from the place he had reached, a man climbing up, a man wearing a blanket-robe and holding a gun, who stood still every little ways to reconnoitre.
êkwa wîsta ka-kitâpamêw. ||| Then he, in his turn, kept watching the other.
piyisk kêkâc ê-kîsi-âmaciwêyit, nahapiyiwa, ê-ati-pimitâcimoyit. ||| At last, when the other had nearly reached the top of his hill, he squatted down and went on, crawling.
ê-kîsi-âmaciwêyit, êkota pimisiniyiwa, kâ-wâpamât itâpâkan ê-ayîtisinamiyit, ê-wî-kakwê-wâpamâyit awiya, itê kâ-wîkicik êkotê isi ê-isi-itâpiyit. ||| When he had reached the summit, there he lay, and he saw him turning a spy-glass this way and that, trying to get sight of someone, as he kept looking out in the direction where the Assiniboine were encamped.
mâka namôya nôkwaniyiwa mîkiwâhpa, awasâyihk ê-wîkiwiht. ||| But the tipis were not visible, for they were camping behind a rise in the land.
piyisk kinwêsk kitâpamêw. ||| At last he had watched him a long time.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpamât ê-tapahtiskwêyiyit, namôya ê-nanâtawâpiyit. ||| Presently he saw him lower his head and no longer look about.
"miyâmay ê-nipât," itêyihtam, êkwa kâ-itohtêt. ||| “Doubtless he is sleeping,” he thought, and started to walk in that direction.
ita kâ-kî-ati-âmaciwêyit, êkota ati-ay-itohtêw. ||| He kept walking along where the other had climbed to the hilltop.
"mâskôc ayahciyiniw, ahpô êtokê opwâsîmôw," itêyihtam. ||| “Probably he is a Blackfoot, and yet for all I know, he may be an Assiniboine,” he thought.
ita kâ-kî-nahapiyit ê-ihtât, kâ-wâpamât ê-tapahtiskwêsiniyit. ||| When he came to where the other had squatted down, he could see him lying with lowered head.
namôya nisitawêyimêw. ||| He could not tell who he was.
namôya wâpamêw ohkwâkaniyiw. ||| He could not see his face.
êkwa pêyâhtik pimohtêw, "mâskôc pêkopayici, nika-nipahik," ê-itêyihtahk. piyisk kisiwâk otihtêw. ||| He walked carefully, thinking, “If by chance he should wake up, he would kill me.” At last he got near to him.
ê-kitâpamât, kâ-wâpamât ê-kitôwêhkwâmiyit. piyisk otihtêw. ||| When he looked at him, he saw that he was sound asleep and snoring.
ê-kitâpamât, êkota pâskisikan astêyiw êkwa itâpâkan. ||| At last he came right up to him. When he looked at him, there lay a gun and a spy-glass.
êkwa ê-pakwahtêhoyit wâpahtam, maskisina ê-sêkwasoyit. ||| And he saw that he had extra moccasins tied in his belt.
ê-kitâpamât, ocihcîyiwa ômisi isi ê-nipâyit, "ê-aspiskwêsimot ocihciya," kâ-wâpahtahk ê-kâh-kîskicihcêyit. ||| When he looked at him, as he slept there with his hands like this, “He is resting his head on his hands,” he thought, and then he saw that he had some fingers cut off.
"ayahciyiniw êcika awa!" itêyihtam. ||| He concluded, “And so he is a Blackfoot.”
ê-nanâtawâpit, kâ-wâpamât asiniya. ||| He looked about him and saw a stone.
asêhtêw, ê-otinât asiniya. ||| He walked back and took the stone.
êkwa ê-itohtêt ita kâ-nîpawiyit, ê-nahikâpawistawât, ostikwâniyihk ê-pakamahwât asiniya ohci, nipahêw. ||| Then he went there where the other had stood, and took a good footing close to him, and hit him on the head with the stone, and killed him.
êkosi pâskisikan otinam, mîna itâpâkan, oskotâkayiyiw, omaskisiniyiwa, otâsiyiwa, mîna kaskitêw, mîna môsw-asiniya. ||| hen he took the gun, the spy-glass, his coat, his moccasins, his leggings, and the powder and bullets.
êkâ ê-nisitawêyimât, "mâskôc ahpô nêhiyaw nipisci-nipahâw," ê-itêyihtahk, êkâ kâ-ôh-manisamwât wêstakayiwa. ||| Because he did not know who the other was, and thought, “Perhaps I have by mistake slain a Cree,” was why he did not cut off the other's scalp.
kêkâc âpihtâ-kîsikâyiw; osâm kinwêsk nôcihtâw, ôhi kâ-wî-kakwê-nipahât. ||| It was almost noon; he had been too long killing that man.
êkoyikohk kêkâc ê-âpihtâ-kîsikâyik, takohtêw wîkiwâhk, êkwa ê-âcimot ôma, kâ-isi-wâpamât ayîsiyiniwa, asiniya ohci ê-pakamahwât. ||| When it was almost noon, he reached their camp, and then he told of how he had seen a man and killed him with a stone.
"ninipahâw ê-micimihkwâmit." "êwakoni ôhi kâ-pêtâyân otayâna." "'mâskôc ahpô nêhiyaw,' ê-itêyimak, êkâ kâ-ôh-manisamwak ostikwân," itwêw. ||| I killed him while he slept. These things which I am bringing are his possessions. Because I thought of him, 'perhaps he is Cree,' is why I did not take his scalp,” he said.
ê-kiskinôhahk anima ispatinâw, ispayiwak ê-têhtapicik kotakak nâpêwak. ||| When he had pointed out that hill, other men mounted and rode there.
ê-wâpamâcik, nisitawêyimêwak ayahciyiniwa. ||| When they saw him, they recognized him as a Blackfoot.
êwakonik manisamwêwak wêstakâyiwa, ê-kîwêhtatâcik. ||| These men now cut off his scalp and took it home.
ê-takohtêcik, êkoyikohk êkwa miywêyihtamwak opwâsîmôwak, êkwa ê-nîmihitocik, ê-miyawâtahkik ê-nipahâcik ayahciyiniwa. ||| When they arrived, the Assiniboine were glad, and danced, rejoicing because they had killed a Blackfoot.
kîtahtawê nitawi-sipwêhtêwak, êkwa awa ayahciyiniw ita kâ-pimisihk kâ-nipahiht, kîkway têhtahêwak. ||| Presently they set out for that place, and where that Blackfoot lay who had been slain, they put him up on something.
êkwa ôma ita kâ-kî-pimisihk asiskiy ê-manisahkik, tâpiskôc ayîsiyiniw ê-pimisihk êkosi ê-isi-manisahkik; êkwa awa opwâsîmôw ita kâ-ôh-wâpamât ôhi ayahciyiniwa, êkota mîna asiskiy ê-ati-manisahkik, tâpiskôc ita ê-pimohtêt ayîsiyiniw ê-isi-manisahkik asiskiy. ||| Then they cut away some of the ground where he had lain, cutting it like a man lying there; and there whence that Assiniboine had seen that Blackfoot, there too they went cutting the ground, carving it out like a man walking.
ita mîna ê-ati-nakît mâna, êkota ê-manisahkik asiskiy, piyisk ê-otihtât ôhi ayahciyiniwa. ||| And there where he had stopped on his way, they cut the ground, and finally where he had reached the Blackfoot.
êkwa mîna asiniya kâ-otinât, êkota mîna ê-manisahkik asiskiy. ||| And where he had taken the stone, there too they carved out the ground.
ita ê-tahkoskêt, êkwa mîna ita ê-nîpawit, ôhi ê-pakamahwât ayahciyiniwa, êkosi ê-isi-kiskinawâcihtâcik. ||| Where he stepped, and also where he stood as he killed the Blackfoot, even so they marked it.
ôhi ayahciyiniwa ita kâ-pimisiniyit, ita ê-itiskwêsihk ita kâ-masinahikâsot, êkota ê-ahâcik ôhi asiniya. ||| Where the Blackfoot had lain, there where the head of the image lay, there they placed that boulder.
mâmaskâc êkwêyâk ê-isi-wâpahtahkik ôhi ayahciyiniwa, ê-nipâyit, ê-mosci-pakamahomiht asiniya ohci. ||| It wonderfully resembled their actual experience, the sleeping Blackfoot being struck by a stone held in the hand.
êwako ohci kâ-ôh-masinahwâcik, "kinwêsk ta-nôkwan," ê-itêyihtahkik. tâpwê kinwês kê-nôkwaniyiw êwako. ||| The reason they made the image of him was that they thought, “For a long time let it be visible.” And truly, for a long time this thing was to be seen.
êkoyikohk ê-iskwâk âcimowin. ||| This is the end of the story.
kîtahtawê ê-mihcêticik ayîsiyiniwak, êkwa opwâsîmôwak, êkwa nahkawiyiniwak. ||| Once upon a time there were many of the people, and also of the Assiniboine Sioux and of the Salteaux.
êkosi isi mihcêtiwak, iskwêwak, awâsisak ê-wîcihiwêcik, tâpiskôc ê-pimipicicik. ||| They were numerous, for they had their women and children with them, as they all trekked together.
kîtahtawê êtokê nisto opwâsîmôwak oskinîkiwak ê-sipwêhtêcik, ê-wî-kakwê-wâpamâcik ayahciyiniwa. ||| Then at one time three Assiniboine youths left the band, to try to get sight of Blackfoot.
ômisi isiyîhkâtêw êwako: ê-nitawâhtâcik isiyîhkâtêw. ||| This is called as follows: they went on a reconnaissance, it is called.
ôki oskinîkiwak kâ-nisticik, kîtahtawê mâna ê-sâkêwêcik, kâ-wâpamâcik pêyak ayahciyiniwa, pêyak misatimwa; ê-kitâpamâcik, êsa ôma ê-wiyanihtâkêyit. ||| As those three youths surmounted one hill after the other, presently they saw a single Blackfoot and one horse; when they observed him, it appeared that he was dressing a carcass.
êkwa êwakoni nâciyôstawêwak ôki oskinîkiwak, kisiwâk ê-osâpamâcik. ||| Then those youths crept up to him, and watched him from close by.
atimapiyiwa, ê-wiyanihtâkêyit, ê-mosêskatêyit, ê-kîsopwêyik. môskîstawêwak. ||| He was sitting with his back turned, dressing his game, and he wore scant clothes, for it was a hot day.
iyikohk ê-môsihikocik, kêkâc ê-otihtâcik, pâsici-kwâskohtiw awa ayahciyiniw omostosoma, ê-kwêskipayihot, âsay ôhi pêyak oskinîkiwa kâ-tahkamikot. êkosi ê-otihtinikot, ê-nipahikot, ôma ostikwân ê-pahkwêkisamiyit. ||| [no translation] When he perceived their presence, as they were almost upon him, the Blackfoot jumped over his buffalo-carcass and turned to face them, but already one of the youths had stabbed him.
misatimwa mîna ôhi otinêwak, mîna opâskisikaniyiw, mîna otayiwinisiyiwa. ||| So they seized him and killed him, and cut the scalp from his head.
êkosi namôya awiya kotaka wâpamêwak ôki oskinîkiwak. ||| And they took also his horse and his gun and his clothes.
namôya kiskêyimêwak tânitê ê-ohtohtêt awa ayahciyiniw. ||| The youths saw no one else. They did not know from where that Blackfoot had come.
êkosi kîwêpahtâwak ôki oskinîkiwak, ê-wî-nitawi-âcimocik ôhi ê-nipahâcik ayahciyiniwa. ||| So those youths gallopped back, to go tell of how they had slain that Blackfoot.
tâpwê ita ê-wâpamâcik ayîsiyiniwa owîcêwâkaniwâwa, êkota takohtêwak, ê-âcimocik ê-pêyakoyit ayahciyiniwa ê-nipahâcik. ||| They went to where they saw the people of their band, and told of how they had slain a lone Blackfoot.
"namôya nikiskêyihtên tânitê ê-ohtohtêt awa ayahciyiniw kâ-nipahiht." ||| “I do not know from where he came, that Blackfoot who has been killed.”
êkosi sipwêhtêwak kahkiyaw ôki ayisiyiniwak. ||| So all those people set out.
ê-otâkosiniyik otihtêwak ôhi ayahciyiniwa, ê-wâ-wâpamâcik; êkwa namôya kiskêyihtamok tânitê ê-wîkiyit. ||| Toward evening they came to that Blackfoot and examined him; and they did not know where his camp had been.
ômisi itwêwak: "ka-kiskêyimânawak tânitê wîkitwâwi;" "ka-pêtisâpamânaw nitonâhci awa." ||| They said, “We shall know where they have their camp; we shall see them when they come to look for this man.”
tahki asawâpiwak, ita ê-wâyahcâyik ê-ayâcik ôki nêhiyawak. ||| They kept a continuous look-out, and the Cree stayed in a hollow of the land.
piyisk kêkâc tipiskâyiw; nama awiya wâpamêwak. ||| At last it was almost dark; they saw no one.
ê-wâpahk, âta ê-nanâtawâpicik, nama kêkway wâpahtamok. ||| When day came, although they kept on the watch, they saw nothing.
kîtahtawê ômisi itwêwak ôki nêhiyawak: "mahti nîswayak ta-ispayiwak oskinîkiwak;" "ê-mîhkawikiyit ta-têhtapiwak," itwêwak. ||| Presently the Cree said, “Let young men ride off in two directions; let them ride fast horses.”
tâpwê awihâwak ê-mîhkawikiyit misatimwa. ||| Accordingly they were lent fast horses.
pêyak natimihk isi ispayiw, pêyak âpihtâ-kîsikâhk itêhkê isi. ||| One rode west, and one in the direction of noon.
piyisk wâhyawês ê-ispatinâyik ê-sâkêwêt, êkota ê-ay-apit, ê-nanâtawâpit, kîtahtawê kâ-pê-sâkêwê-têhtapiyit pêyak ayîsiyiniwa. ||| Presently, as he came out over a hill a little ways off, as he stopped there apd looked about, a Blackfoot came riding into view.
piyisk kotaka mîna; piyisk ati-mihcêtiyiwa, êkwa ê-nitonâht awa kâ-nipahiht ayahciyiniw. ||| Soon another; soon there were many of them, looking for the Blackfoot who had been slain.
êkwa pê-môskîstâk awa nêhiyaw. ||| Then they came to attack that Cree.
ômisi isiyîhkâsôw awa nêhiyaw: caciwâsin isiyîhkâsôw. ||| This was the Cree's name: Tchatchiwasin was his name.
êkosi têhtapiw, ê-tapasît. ||| So he mounted his horse and fled.
nisihk iyâpasâpamâci, pôti mihcêtiyiwa, nâh-nâway ê-pâpayiyit. ||| When in a leisurely way he looked behind him, he saw that they were many, riding after him one behind the other.
pêyak wâhyaw pê-nakasiwêyiwa, ê-wâpiskisiyit ê-têhtapiyit. ||| One had far outdistanced the rest; he rode a white horse.
namôya sôhki wî-tapasîw, ê-kiskêyihtahk ê-mîhkawikiyit ôhi kâ-têhtapit. ||| The Cree did not intend to flee fast, for he knew that his mount was fleet.
tahki nahiyikohk pâpayiyiwa. ||| They kept coming toward him, always at about the same distance.
kîtahtawê kâ-pêtisâpamikot owîcêwâkana. ||| Presently his people saw him coming.
wawêyîwak nêhiyawak, kâ-mîhkawikiyit otêmiwâwa êwakoni ê-têhtapicik. ||| The Cree made ready, mounting their swiftest horses.
piyisk kisiwâk pê-ayâw; kisiwâk êkwa pê-askôk ôhi ayahciyiniwa, mâka namôya sôhki ê-tapasît. ||| Presently he had come near; and now the Blackfoot were coming close behind him, but he did not flee fast.
kiskêyihtam kisiwâk ê-ayâyit owîcêwâkana, "namôya nika-kî-atimik misawâc," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He knew that his companions were near, and thought, “In any case they will not be able to catch me in time.”
mwêhci êkwa ê-otihtahk ôma ê-osêhcâyik, êkota kâ-ayâyit owîcêwâkana, êkoyikohk kisiwâk êkwa askôk. ||| By the time he reached the hill where his people were, they were close upon him.
kîtahtawê ka-pê-sâkêwêpayiyit êkwa owîcêwâkana. ||| Then suddenly out into view came his companions.
âsay ôki ayahciyiniwak otêmiwâwa nayawapiyiwa. ||| By this time the Blackfoots' horses were tired.
ê-wâwinipitâcik, ê-tapasîcik ôki ayahciyiniwak, awa wâpastimwa kâ-têhtapit ê-wâwinipitât otêma, ê-tapasît, âsay kisiwâk askôk nêhiyawa. ||| When they pulled them round, to flee, and when the one who rode the white horse pulled it round to run away, the Cree were already close upon him.
ê-pasastêhwât otêma, kâ-pahkisiniyit. ||| When he struck his horse with the quirt, it fell.
nîhcipayiw awa ayahciyiniw. ||| The Blackfoot was thrown.
ê-wî-waniskât, kâ-tâwikipayihikot misatimwa nêhiyawa ê-têhtapiyit. ||| When he tried to get up, the Crees' horses trampled him.
mîna ê-wî-waniskât, âsay otihtinik nêhiyawa, ê-ta-tahkamikot, ê-nipahikot. ||| When again he tried to get up, the Cree were already upon him, and killed him with knife-thrusts.
êkota ohci êkwa, nâh-nâway ê-ati-nipahihcik ayahciyiniwak, piyis mihcêt nipahâwak. ||| From then on, as they overtook and killed one alter the other of the Blackfoot, in the end they had slain many of them.
ayis nayawapiyiwa otêmiwâwa. ||| For the Blackfoots' horses were tired.
ôki piko wâhyaw kâ-kî-nakatihcik ayahciyiniwak, êyakonik piko takohtêwak wîkiwâhk. ||| Only those of the Blackfoot who had been left far behind, only they reached their camp.
êyakonik âcimowak ê-mihcêtiyit nêhiyawa, mîna âsay mihcêt ê-nipahihcik ayahciyiniwak. ||| They told of how the Cree were numerous and that already many Blackfoot had been slain.
êkosi ita ê-tahtakwahcâk, êkota kahkiyaw itohtêwak, ê-wâtihkêcik, iskwêwak mîna wâsakâm ê-apahkwêcik wîkiwâwa ohci, pêyak piko mîkiwâhp ê-osîhtâcik, êkota awâsisak iskwêwak ê-asiwasocik. ||| Then they all went to a flat place in the land and dug a trench, and the women sheltered it all round with covering from their tipis, so as to make one great tent, into which the women and children were placed.
piyis kahkiyaw takohtêwak, tahto êkâ ê-nipahihcik ôki ayahciyiniwak. ||| Soon all the Blackfoot had come there, as many as had not been killed.
êkwa wîhkwêskawêwak ita, êkwa ê-nôtinitocik, kahkiyaw ê-takohtêcik ôki nêhiyawak mîna opwâsîmôwak mîna nahkawiyiniwak. ||| Then they surrounded them there, and they fought, all the Cree and Assiniboine and Salteaux having come there.
pêyak opwâsîmôw, mistahi ê-miyosit oskinîkiw, sihkosiwayâna ê-kikamoyit oskotâkâhk mîna otâsihk, kahkiyaw ê-mîkisiwiyiki otayôwinisa, mîna otastotin sihkosiwayâna ê-kikamoyit, êskana ê-kikamoyit otastotinihk, êwako êkota ê-ayât ôma ê-nôtinitôwiht, namôya nôtinikêw, ê-pêhât ôhtâwiya, câpihcikanis ê-tahkonahk, êkwa cîkahikani-pakamâkan ê-tahkonahk, êkwa napakihkomân, âsay nîso ê-pê-tahkamât câpihcikanis ohci ayahciyiniwa, êkwa pêyak ê-cîkahwât ôma ohci ocîkahikanis, êkosi nisto ê-nipahât, ostikwâniyiwa ôhi pâh-pahki ê-pahkwêkisamwât, "pita nika-miyâw nôhtâwiy," ê-itêyihtahk, otêmiyiwa nîso ê-otinât mîna. ||| A certain Assiniboine, a very handsome youth, with weaselskins on his coat and on his breeches, with beads on all his clothes, and weaselskins also on his toque, and horns, beside, on his headgear, he, staying tight close to the fight, took yet no active part in it, for he was awaiting his father, holding in hand a lance and a tomahawk and a bowie knife; with his lance he had already transfixed two Blackfoot on the way hither, and had tomahawked one, so that he had slain three: taking a part of each one's scalp, in the thought, “Later I shall give them to my father,” and taking also two of their horses.
piyis mihcêtiyiwa owîcêwâkana, ê-takohtêyit. ||| Soon many of his companions had arrived.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpamât ôhtâwiya ita ê-apit ê-pê-itohtêyit. ||| Presently he saw his father coming to where he sat.
"â, nîso nipê-tahkamâwak;" "otêmiwâwa nitôtinimâwa; mîna ostikwâniwâwa nitôtinên." ||| “Oh, two I stabbed on the way; I took their horses; and I took their heads.”
ôhi êwakoni ostikwâniyiwa wâpahtam awa kisêyiniw. ||| The old man looked at the scalps.
"êkwa pêyak ôma ohci nipê-cîkahwâw," itêw ôhtâwiya"êkosi nisto ninipahâwak," itêw. ||| “And one with this I felled as I came,” he told his father; “So that I have killed three,” he told him.
"hay hay hay!" itwêw awa kisêyiniw; "êkosi, nikosis, miywâsin ê-tôtaman, ê-miyosiyan," itêw. ||| “Splendid!” cried the old man; “That is the right way to do, since you are handsome,” he told him.
êkosi êkota ay-apiw, pita ê-pîhtwât awa kisêyiniw. ||| Then the old man sat there a while and smoked.
ê-kî-pîhtwât, "mahti, nikosis, pêtâ kimôhkomân." ||| When he had smoked, “Come, Son, give me your knife.”
otinam awa oskinîkiw, ê-miyât ôhtâwiya. ||| The youth drew it and gave it to his father.
ta-tâsaham ôma môhkomân. ||| He whetted the knife.
"hâ, nikosis, êwako ani kimôhkomân." "ômatôwahk ayahciyiniw namôya tahto-kîsikâw wâpamâw;" "mostos piko tahto-kîsikâw kâ-wâpamiht," itêw. ||| “There, my son, even this is your knife. Such game as the Blackfoot is not seen every day; it is only the buffalo is seen every day,” he told him.
"kah!" itwêw oskinîkiw. ||| “I hear what you say!” said the youth.
êkosi pasikôw, itê kâ-nôtinitôwiht ê-itohtêt awa oskinîkiw. ||| Accordingly he rose to his feet, the youth, and went to the fight.
êkwa ê-kitâpamât, nama awiya wâpamêw ayahciyiniwa. ||| Then when he looked to see them, he saw none of the Blackfoot.
mâka âsay wâh-wâpamêw nêhiyawa, cîki êkotê ê-pimisiniyit, ê-nipahimiht. ||| But already he saw Cree lying near by, Cree who had been slain.
êkota êspahtâw, ê-kwâh-kwâskwêpayihot awa kâ-miyosit oskinîkiw. ||| To that place ran the handsome youth, leaping high as he ran.
cîki ayahciyiniwa kâ-ayâyit, êkota nahapipayihôw. ||| Close to where the Blackfoot were, he flung himself into a crouching position.
mayaw ê-nahapit, pâskisok ayahciyiniwa. ||| As soon as he had squatted down, the Blackfoot shot at him.
kîpiwêpahok, ê-nipahikot. ||| He was hit headlong, and killed.
âsay wîhtamawâw awa kisêyiniw. ||| Already the old man was being told.
ômisi isiyîhkâsôw: mistikwaskihk isiyîhkâsôw awa okosisa kâ-miyosiyit. ||| his was his name: Wooden-Drum was the name of him whose son was so handsome.
"kikosis nipahâw!" itêw. ||| “Your son has been killed!” he was told.
ê-itâpit, kâ-wâpamât okosisa ê-pimisiniyit. ||| When he looked, he saw his son lying there.
itohtêw, ê-ispahtât. ||| He went there, running.
otihtêw okosisa, cîki ayahciyiniwa ita ê-ayâyit. ||| He reached his son, close by to where the Blackfoot were.
otinam okosisa otastotiniyiw, ê-postastotinêt. ||| He took his son's headgear and placed it on his own head.
ê-kîsi-postastotinêt, êkwa ôma cîkahikanis ê-otinahk, âta ê-pâh-pâskisoht, âhci piko apiw, ê-kwêskapit, ê-isi-ohtiskawapit itê kâ-ôh-pâskisoht. ||| Having put on the headgear, he took the tomahawk, and though he was being fired at, yet he stayed sitting there, turning so as to face the fire.
sâsakiciwêpahwâw, ê-nipahiht. ||| He was felled backward and killed.
âsay osîma têpwâtimâwa. ||| Already the cry came to his younger brother.
"mistanikocâsah-kâ-pimwât, kistês nipahâw!" itimâwa osîma. ||| “Shoots-the-Gopher, your elder brother has been killed!” his brother was told.
êkosi awa êkotê itohtêw. ||| Then he too went there.
ê-itâpit, pôti kâ-wâpamât ostêsa êkwa okosisa ê-nipahimiht. ||| When he looked that way, there he saw his brother and his brother's son lying slain.
pasikôw, ê-itohtêt, ê-ati-wayacîwît. ||| He rose to his feet and went there, breaking into a run.
ê-âta-pâskisoht, piyisk otihtêw. ||| Although he was fired at, he went there.
ostêsa otinam ôma cîkahikanis, ê-môskîstawât ayahciyiniwa. ||| He took the tomahawk from his brother, and made for the Blackfoot.
pîhtokêw wîkiyihk, ê-cîkahwât nîso ayahciyiniwa. ||| He entered their camp and felled two Blackfoot.
pê-wayawîw, ê-pê-tapasît, "hahwêh!" ê-pê-itwêt; "nitôtêmitik, nîso nicîkahwâwak nikosis ocîkahikanis ohci," itwêw; "hâw, nitôtêmitik, kakwê-otinihk nikosis têpiyâhk, kiyâm nistês êkotê ka-pimisin," itwêw. ||| He came forth and came fleeing back, crying, “Hyah, friends, I have felled two with my son's tomahawk. So now, friends, try to take up my son's body at least. Let my brother's lie there,” he said.
tâpwê môskîstawêwak oskinîkiwak. ||| Accordingly, the young men made for them.
âta ê-pâskisohcik, otihtêwak ôhi kâ-miyosiyit oskinîkiwa. ||| Although they were shot at, they reached the handsome youth.
otinêwak, ê-kospohtahâcik. ||| They took him up and carried him off.
takohtahêwak owîcêwâkaniwâwa itê ê-ayâyit. ||| They brought him to where their comrades were.
êkosi âhci piko ê-nôtinâcik, ê-pâskiswâcik. ||| Then they kept on fighting the enemy, and shooting at them.
êkwa ôki nêhiyawak cîki ê-pimisihkik, ê-mâtâposihkik êwakonik ê-nâpêhkâsocik, ositiwâhk êkotê âtiht ê-ayâyit owîcêwâkaniwâwa, ôki nîkân kâ-pimisihkik, kâ-ta-tasinahkwâwi, tapahtiskwêyiwak, ôki kotakak ê-tasinahkik, ayahciyiniwa ê-pâ-pâskiswâcik. ||| And where the Cree were lying near there, as the braves lay in a row, with some of their comrades close at their feet, then, whenever those who lay in the front rank had fired, they would duck their heads, and the others would fire, sending a volley at the Blackfoot.
kîtahtawê awa pêyak nêhiyaw otâhk kâ-apit, ositiyihk isi oskinîkiwa, mwêhci ê-wî-tasinahk, kâ-ohpiskwêyiyit oskinîkiwa owîcêwâkana. ||| Then at one time just as a certain Cree in the rear rank was about to fire, the youth, his comrade, who lay by his feet, raised his head.
ostikwâniyihk pistahwêw oskinîkiwa; nipahêw. ||| Thus accidentally he shot the youth in the head and killed him.
pakwâtam ê-pistahwât otôtêma. ||| He was grieved at having shot his friend.
ômisi itwêw: "hahahêy, tâpwê nipakwâtên ê-pistahowêyân!" itwêw, ê-pasikôt, êkota ê-nitawi-nahapit ôhi oskinîkiwa kâ-nipahât. ||| Thus he spoke: “Alas, truly I am grieved at having made a fatal error!” he cried, rising to his feet, and went and sat by the youth he had killed.
namwâc kinwêsk apiw âsay ostikwânihk ê-tawahokot ayahciyiniwa; kîpiwêpahok. ||| He had not been there long, before the Blackfoot sent a bullet through his head; he fell hurtling.
êkosi otinâw, âkawâyihk ê-itohtahiht awa mîna oskinîkiw. ||| So he was taken up and brought to a sheltered spot, and the body of the youth as well.
âhci piko yêhyêw awa ayahciyiniwa ostikwânihk kâ-pâskisokot. ||| He who had been shot in the head by the Blackfoot was still breathing.
nicawâc nipiy ita ê-ayâyik, êkota itohtahâw, êkota ê-pimisihk, ê-akwanahiht wâpowayân. ||| He was taken to where there was water, and there he lay, covered with a blanket.
êkosi isi ohpimê itohtêwak ôki ayisiyiniwak, ôma ê-nôtinitocik kêyâpic. ||| Then the people went off, to fight again.
kîtahtawê kâwaniskât awa nipîhk kâ-pimisimiht, ê-pê-pasikôt, ê-takohtêt otôtêma ita ê-ayâyit, êkota ê-nahapit, "oskinîkîtik, oyaskinahihk!" ê-itwêt; "nika-pîhtwân," ê-itwêt. ||| Then presently he arose who had been laid by the water's edge; he rose to his feet and walked over to his companions, and sat down there, saying, “Young men, fill a pipe. Let me smoke.”
tâpwê ê-kitâpamâcik ôhi ostikwâniyihk kâ-kî-pâskisomiht, namwâc ihtakoniyiw ôma ita kâ-kî-pâskisomiht. ||| Truly, when they looked at him who had been shot in the head, not a trace was there of the bullet-wound.
ê-manitôwit awa nâpêw, ê-nanâtawihisot, êkosi nama takoniyiw ôma ita kâ-pâskisoht. ||| Because that man had manitou power and had cured himself, there was no trace of the gunshot-wound.
piyis wîpac pôyôwak. ||| Soon after that they ceased fighting.
kêkâc mêscihêwak ôhi ayahciyiniwa; wiyawâw mîna mihcêt nipahikwak. ||| They had nearly exterminated those Blackfoot; and on their side, too, many had been slain.
êkosi pê-kîwêwak ôki nêhiyawak, ê-miyawâtahkik, ê-miywêyihtahkik, mihcêt ê-nipahâcik ayahciyiniwa. ||| Then the Cree went home, celebrating their joy at having killed many Blackfoot.
piyis takosinwak wîkiwâhk ôki nêhiyawak. ||| In time those Cree arrived at their camp.
êkoyikohk ê-iskwâk êwako âcimowin. ||| This is the end of the story.
kîtahtawê ayîsiyiniwak ê-wîkicik, kîtahtawê ômisi itwêw pêyak nâpêw; ôhi owîcêwâkana, "ay," itêw, "nawac sipwêhtêtân," itêw, "ka-wîhtamôwacik âtiht ayîsiyiniwak;" "têpakohp kika-ihtasinânaw," itêw. ||| Once upon a time, as some people dwelt somewhere, a certain man spoke as follows; to his comrade he said, “Now then, let us set out; you may tell a few people; seven of us shall go,” he told him.
"kî-nîso-tipiskâki ka-sipwêhtânânaw." "ayahciyiniwak ka-nitonawânawak, miskawâyahkwâwi otêmiwâwa ka-kimotamawâyahk." "mâka wâpamikoyahkwâwi, wî-kakwê-nipahikoyahkwâwi, kiyânaw mîna ka-kakwê-nipahânawak," itêw. ||| “Two nights from now we shall set out. We shall look for Blackfoot, to steal their horses when we find them. And if they catch sight of us and try to kill us, we shall try to kill them,” he told him.
tâpwê ê-kî-nîso-tipiskâyik sipwêhtêwak. ||| Accordingly, after two nights they set out.
awa pêyak nâpêsis ôhtâwiya ê-okimâwiyit, misatimwa itê ê-ayâyit, êkotê ayâw, kâ-wâpamât ê-pimohtêyit ôhi kâ-sipwêhtêyit. ||| A certain young boy, whose father was chief, was where the horses were, and saw them go off who were setting out.
ê-kitâpamât, "miyâmay ê-sipwêhtêcik!" itêyihtam, acosisa ê-ayât awa nâpêsis, kêkâc âta wiya ê-oskinîkit awa nâpêsis; "mahti nika-wîcêwâwak!" ||| When he looked at them, “Surely they are going off!” he thought; at the age of having arrows was the boy, though, indeed, he was close to adolescence; “Oh, do let me go with them!”
itê ê-otâkosiniyik, ê-wî-minahoyit, wîsta êkotê takohtêw. ||| At the place they reached toward evening, as they were about to kill game, he too arrived.
namôya kiskêyimik ôhtâwiya ê-sipwêhtêt. ||| His father did not know that he had gone off.
êkwa ôki nâpêwak kâ-minahocik, kâ-takohtêyit ôhi nâpêsisa, nisitawêyimêwak ôhtâwîyiwa ê-okimâwiyit. ||| And those men, when they had killed game and the boy arrived, recognized him as the chief's son.
namôya nânitaw wî-itêwak. ||| They did not care to say anything to him.
êkosi ê-kîsitêpocik, ê-wî-mîcisocik, miyo-asamêwak ôhi nâpêsisa. ||| So, when they cooked their meal and were about to eat, they gave the boy plenty of food.
"hâw, kitimâkêyimâtân." "kitôkimâminaw okosisa," itwêwak. ||| “Well, let us treat him kindly. He is our chief's son,” they said.
tâpwê êkota nipâwak. ||| Then they slept there.
ê-wâpahk sipwêhtêwak. ||| The next morning they went on.
ita ê-tipiskâyik kapêsiwak. ||| Where they were by dark, they camped for the night.
mwêhci nikotwâsikwâw ê-kî-nipâcik, môhkiciwanipêk ita ê-ayâyik, cîki êkota mostoswa ayâyiwa. ||| When they had slept six nights on the way, near a spring of water were some buffalos.
"hâw, pêyak ta-nitawi-pâskiswêwak." "nipahâci, êkota ka-kapêsinânaw, kika-osîhtâyahk ta-nîmâyahk," itêw. ||| “Now then, let one man go shoot them. If he kills any, we shall camp there and prepare provisions for the march,” the leader told them.
tâpwê pêyak sipwêhtêw, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahât mostoswa. ||| Accordingly one set out to kill buffalos.
cîki ê-sakâyik êkwa itohtêwak ôki kotakak. ||| The others went to a near-by grove.
ê-takohtêcik êkota, âsay ôma kâ-pâskiswât mostoswa. ||| When they got to it, he had already shot the buffalo.
pêhtamiyiwa ayahciyiniwa namôya wâhyaw ê-ayâyit, mitâtaht ê-ihtasiyit, mîna êyakonik nêhiyawa ê-nitonawâcik. ||| The sound was heard by some Blackfoot who were not far from there, ten in number, themselves looking for Cree.
êkwa êyakonik wî-kakwê-wâpamêwak ôhi nêhiyawa. ||| They decided to take a look at the Cree.
pôti wâpamikwak nêhiyawak ôki kâ-wiyanihtâkêcik têpakohp kê-ihtasicik êkwa awa pêyak nâpêsis, êkosi ayinânêw. ||| And there they saw those Cree preparing their carcass, seven of them, with the boy, a total of eight.
tâpwê pê-nâciyôstâkwak ayahciyiniwa. ||| Accordingly the Blackfoot crept up on the Cree.
namôya kiskêyimêwak. ||| The latter did not know of their presence.
mêkwâc ê-wiyanihtâkêcik, nama isko ê-nawacîcik, âsay pâskisokwak ôki nêhiyawak. ||| While they were cutting up the game, before they had begun the roasting, the Blackfoot fired at the Cree.
ôma kâ-sakâyik êkota ê-itâmocik, pêyak pahkisin nêhiyaw, oskâtihk ê-tawahoht, ê-nâtwâpayiyik oskât. ||| As they fled toward the wooded place, one of the Cree fell, his leg pierced by a bullet and broken.
awa nâpêsis nakîw, ê-kisâtât ôhi kâ-kaskatahomiht, ê-têpwêt, "ahâ, nitôtêmitik, wîhtamawâhkêk nôhtâwiy: namôya niwî-nakatâw awa." "kiyâm nîsta nika-nipahikawin," itêw, ê-têpwêt. ||| The boy stopped and stayed by the wounded man, crying, “Hey, friends, tell my father when you see him: I shall not leave this man. I don't care if I too am killed,” he told them, calling to them.
âsay wâhyaw ê-atimipahtâyit owîcêwâkaniwâwa, êkwa âhci piko ê-pâskisokocik ayahciyiniwa, âskaw môskîstawêw, âta wiya ê-pimwât. ||| When their comrades had run far away, and the Blackfoot were still shooting at them, he took the offensive against them from time to time, firing at them.
êkwa awa kâ-kaskatahoht êwako simatapiw, wîsta ê-pâskiswât, wîsta ê-nôtinikêt; mâka nama kêkway kî-nipahêwak, ê-mitâtasiyit, êkwa wiyawâw ê-nîsicik awa nâpêsis. ||| And the man whose bone had been broken sat up, and he too fired at them, joining in the fight; but they did not succeed in killing any of them, for the others were ten, and they only two, one of them a boy.
ayisk owîcêwâkaniwâwa nakatisimikwak. ||| For their comrades had left them behind.
piyisk pôyoyiwa ôhi ayahciyiniwa, ê-kostikocik, ê-sipwêhtêyit. ||| At last the Blackfoot, fearing them, gave up and went away.
êkwa awa nâpêsis iyikohk ê-wâpamât wâhyaw ê-atimohtêyit, êkwa itohtêw môhkiciwanipêkohk, ita ê-tipinawâyik êkota ê-miskahk. ||| Then the boy, as soon as he saw that they had gone far away, went to the spring and found a sheltered place.
êkwa nitawâpamêw ôhi kâ-kaskatahomiht. ||| Then he went to the wounded man.
"â, nimiskên ita ta-ay-ayâyahk," itêw. ||| “Come, I have found a place where we can stay,” he told him.
"â, namôya, nâpêsis! ||| “Oh, no, my boy! Do go home! Your father is chief; he will grieve.
kîwê kiyâm!" "kôhtâwiy okimâwiw; ta-kaskêyihtam." "konita ka-kakwâtakihtân ôta." "namôya mayaw nika-iyiniwîn niskât." "kîwê!" itêw nâpêsisa. ||| You will only suffer here. My leg will not get well so very soon. Go home!” he told the boy.
iyikohk miyo-ayâyani, kîwêyini, êkoyikohk nika-kîwân." "nôhtâwiy iyâcimoci, 'sôhkêyihtâkosiw awiyak, kâ-nakatisimimiht kêsâtâci,' ê-itwêt mâna nipêhtawâw;" "êwako ohci kâ-ôh-wî-kisâtitân," itêw. ||| When you are well and go home, then I shall go home. Whenever my father tells stories, I always hear him say, 'One is counted a brave man, if one stays with those who have been left behind.' That is why I mean to stay with you,” he told him.
êkosi itohtêw awa nâpêsis ôhi wiyâsa; askêkin otinam, êkota ê-otâpêt ôhi oskinîkiwa, sakâhk ê-itohtahât. ||| Thereupon the boy went to where the meat was; he took the hide, and on it dragged the young man to the grove of trees.
ôma ita kâ-tipinawâyik ê-kî-pêsiwât, êkwa wiyâsa awatâw. ||| When he had brought him to the sheltered place, he fetched the meats.
êkwa kotawêw, êkwa ê-kîsitêpot ta-mîcisocik, êkwa mîna nipiy ê-otinahk wînâstakayêpicikanihk, ta-minihkwêyit ôhi nâpêwa. ||| Then he built a fire and cooked, that they might eat, and drew water in the paunch, that the man might drink.
tâpwê minihkwêyiwa, êkwa ê-mîcisoyit. ||| So the latter drank and ate.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, êkwa miscikosa kâ-kîskataham ê-apisâsiniyiki, ôma kâ-pîkopayiyik oskât, êkota ê-tahkopitamwât ôma oskâtiyiw. ||| When he had eaten, he hewed some small sticks to shape, putting a splint on his leg where it was broken.
êkosi ê-kîsi-tahkopitahk, êkwa osîhtâw wîkiwâw nîpiya ohci, êkota ê-ayât, êkwa ê-osîhtât kâhkêwakwa ana nâpêw, êkwa awa nâpêsis tahki ê-asawâpit. ||| When he had tied it up, he built a hut for them of leaves, where the man stayed, preparing dried meat, while the boy always kept a lookout.
kîtahtawê, ayinânêw ê-ihtahto-tipiskâyik êkota ê-ayâcik, kâ-wâpamât ê-niyânaniyit ayîsiyiniwa ê-pêci-âstamohtêyit. ||| Presently, when they had been there eight nights, he saw five men coming toward them.
ê-ka-kitâpamât, âsay mâka ê-otâkosiniyik, pôti ita kâ-ayâcik cîki êkota kapêsiyiwa, ê-osîhtâyit wîkiyiw, tâpiskôc wâskahikan ê-itahâyit mistikwa. ||| As he watched them, as it was evening, he saw them make a camp for the night near to where they were, building a shelter, placing trees in the shape of a wooden house.
êkwa kisiwâk ê-wî-kakwê-osâpamât, ê-wî-kakwê-nisitawêyimât kêko ayisiyiniwa, pôti ayahciyiniwa. ||| And when he made an effort to see them at close range, to see what kind of people they were, he saw that they were Blackfoot.
êkosi itohtêw; êkwa ôhi owîcêwâkana ômisi itêw: "mahti kipâskisikan pêtâ." "ôta kisiwâk mahîhkan ê-ayât, nika-pâskiswâw," itêw. ||| So he went there and said to his companion, “Please give me your gun. I want to shoot a wolf that is close by here.”
êkwa ê-miyikot, êkwa itohtêw. ||| When the other gave it him, he went there.
êkwa ê-pônamiyit, pîhcâyihk ê-apiyit, nâciyôstawêw. ||| The others had made a fire and were sitting indoors; he crept up to them.
êkwa ê-otihtât, isi-niyânaniyiwa, ê-nâh-nawaciyit. ||| When he got near them, they were five, a-roasting of meat.
nawasawâpamôw; tânihi ê-miyohoyit, êwakoni pâskiswêw, ê-sâkowêt. ||| He took careful aim; he shot at those who wore the best clothes, and gave a whoop.
ê-tapasîyit nîso, ê-tâh-tâwikisiniyit mistikohk, osâm ê-sêkihât, êwakoni mîna pimwêw; nipahêw mîna. ||| While two fled, one kept bumping into things, so much had he frightened him; this one too he shot; he killed him too.
êkosi nisto nipahêw. ||| So he had killed three.
ê-kiskêyihtahk ê-tapasîyit; pîhtokêw, otayiwinisiyiwa ê-otinahk, mîna pâskisikan pêyak, pêyak acosisa, pêyak cîkahikani-pakamâkan, êkwa pêyak câpihcicikanis, môhkomâna nêwo, mîna ostikwâniyihk ôta ôma ê-manisamwât. ||| When he saw that they had fled, he went inside and took their garments, and a gun, a set of arrows, a tomahawk, and a lance, and four knives, and he cut off this, on their heads here.
kahkiyaw omaskisiniyiwa otinam, êkwa ê-kîwêhtatât, ôhi kâ-kaskatahomiht wîcêwâkana, ê-pîhtokatât, ê-miyât. ||| He took all their moccasins, and took it all back with him and gave it, when he brought it into their hut, to his wounded companion.
mistahi mâmaskâtamiyiwa, "tânita ê-ohtinaman?" ê-itikot. ||| He was much surprised, and asked him, “Where did you get it all?”
"ê-niyânanicik ôta ê-kapêsicik ayahciyiniwak, nisto ninipahâwak, êkota ôhi ê-ohtinamân," itêw; "kipêhtên êtokê ê-matwêwêk." ||| “Five Blackfoot camped here for the night; I killed three of them and took these,” he told him; “I suppose you heard gunshot.”
"êkota ninîsoyawâwak." "êkwa pêyak osâm êtokê ê-sêkisit, ê-tâh-tâwikisihk, mîna êwako nipimwâw; ninipahâw." "êkosi nisto." ||| That was when I shot two of them. And one, I suppose because he was frightened, bumped into things, and I shot him too; I killed him. That makes three.”
"tâpwê, wêskinîkiyin, namôya kikostâwak!" itik. ||| “Really, young man, you do not seem to be afraid of them!” the other said to him.
piyis êkota ay-ayâwak. ||| Then they stayed there.
namôya êsa ôma wâhyaw ê-wîkiyit. ||| Now, it seems that those others had their camp not far from there.
ôki kâ-tapasîcik ayahciyiniwak takosinwak wîkiwâhk; âcimowak ê-nipahihcik, wiyawâw piko ê-pimâtisicik. ||| Those Blackfoot who had fled arrived at their camp; they told how their comrades had been slain, and that only they were alive.
ê-kî-nêwo-tipiskâyik, kîtahtawê kâ-pêtisâpamât, ê-pâpiciyit ayahciyiniwa. ||| After four nights, there, the boy saw the Blackfoot coming, moving up their camp.
êkwa êkota ohci ka-kitâpamêw, kisiwâk êkota kâ-pê-kapêsiyit, ê-mihcêtiyit. ||| From where he was, he watched them, as they came to pitch camp close by, a great number of them.
êkwa pê-nâtimâwa ôhi kâ-kî-nipahât, ê-kîwêhtahimiht. ||| And those whom he had killed were fetched and taken back.
piyisk ta-ati-tipiskâyiw. ||| At last darkness came on.
iyikohk mistahi ê-tipiskâyik, itohtêw owîcêwâkana. ||| When it was quite dark, he went to where his companion was.
"mahti êkâya pâh-pôna." "kêkway niwâpahtên; mâka namôya nikiskêyihtên kêkway." "mahti nika-kakwê-nisitawihtên," itêw. ||| “You had better not light any fire. I see something; but I do not know what it is. I think I shall go try to hear what it is,” he told him.
êkosi mîna ê-sipwêhtêt, mîkiwâhpihk ê-itohtêt. ||| With that he went off again, and went to the camp.
namôya ê-sakahpitâyit misatimwa; mitâtaht misatimwa otinêw, ê-kimotamawât ayahciyiniwa. ||| They had not tied up their horses; he took ten horses, stealing them from the Blackfoot.
otihtêw owîcêwâkana. ||| He came back to his companion.
"hâw, niwîcêwâkan, tânisi kê-tôtamahk?" "ayahciyiniwak êsa ani kisiwâk kapêsiwak;" "mâka âsay mitâtaht otêmiwâwa ôta nipêsîmâwa!" ||| “Now then, comrade, what shall we do? It seems that Blackfoot are camping close by; in fact I am bringing ten of their horses now!”
"hay hay" itwêyiwa; "tâpwê kitatamihin, niwîcêwâkan!" ||| “Splendid!” said he; “Truly, you delight me, comrade!”
"kika-kîwânânaw, ka-tapasîyahk," itêw; "namôya ka-kî-pimitisahokonawak;" "namôya mihcêt misatimwak," ê-itât. ||| “We shall go home, making our escape,” he said to him; “They will not be able to pursue us; the horses are not many,” he told him.
tâpwê pêyak pê-takohtahêw wîkiwâhk, êkwa ê-wayawîtâcimoyit owîcêwâkana, ê-oyahpitât otakohpisiwâwa ohci, ê-têhtahât owîcêwâkana. ||| Accordingly he brought one of the horses to their hut, dragged out his companion, tied him up with their blanket-robes, and set him on the horse.
"hâ, niwîcêwâkan, kiya kinakacihtân nîkân ohci." "nika-sîhkitisahwâwak misatimwak." "mîna ka-kiskêyihtên tâniyikohk ka-pimipayiyin, kiskât ôma ka-manâcihtâyin," itêw. ||| “Now, comrade, you know how to lead. I shall drive on the horses. Besides, you will know how far to ride without injuring your leg,” he told him.
mistahi miywêyihtam awa oskinîkiw, êkwa ê-sipwê-têhtapit, ê-pê-sîhkitisahwâyit ôhi nâpêsisa misatimwa. ||| The young man was very glad, and rode away, while the boy drove on the horses.
kapê-tipisk pimipayiwak. ||| They rode all night.
ê-kîsikâyik, ê-wâpamât awa oskinîkiw misatimwa, "tâpwê miyosiwak!" itêyihtam. ||| When day came and the young man saw the horses, “Really, they are fine ones!” he thought.
kapê-kîsik pimâmôwak, mîna kapê-tipisk. ||| They fled all day, and again all night.
nîsotipiskwa namôya nipâwak. ||| For two nights they did not sleep.
êkoyikohk ê-wâpamâcik mostoswa, nawaswêw awa nâpêsis. ||| Then, as they saw some buffalos, the boy gave chase.
miywêyihtam awa oskinîkiw, êkota ê-nîhtakosît, ê-wî-wiyanihtâkêcik, ê-wî-mîcisocik. ||| The young man was glad; he dismounted, and they skinned it and cut it up and made ready to eat.
âsay ôtê wîkiwâhk awa nâpêsis êkwa awa oskinîkiw mawîhkâtâwak, "nipahâwak," ê-itihcik, ôhi ka-kî-nakatisimikocik ê-itâcimoyit. ||| Meanwhile, back in their home, this boy and this young man were being mourned; “They were killed,” was said of them, in accordance with the story of those who had abandoned them.
tahki mâtoyiwa ôhtâwiya awa nâpêsis kâ-okimâwi-yit ôhtâwiya. ||| The boy's father, the chief, wept incessantly.
êkwa wiyawâw ê-kîsi-wiyanihtâkêcik, êkwa ê-kîsitêpocik, ê-paminawasocik, iyikohk ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, mîna sipwêhtêwak. ||| But, as for them, when they had cleaned their game, and cooked their meal, and eaten, they went on.
nîswâw ê-nipâcik, kîtahtawê kâ-wâpahtahkik wîkiwâwa. ||| After two nights on the way, presently they came in sight of their camp.
miywêyihtam awa kâ-kî-kaskatahoht. ||| The one who had been wounded was glad.
ispî ê-wâpamihcik, ê-pê-sipwêpayit pêyak oskinîkiw, awîniki ôki êyakonik, "nipahâwak," kâ-kî-itwêt. ||| When they were seen, a young man came to them from the camp; whom did he see, but those of whom it had been said that they were killed!
êkota ohci kîwêpayiw awa, ê-nitawi-wîhtamawât ôhi okimâwa ê-takosiniyit okosisiyiwa mîna ôhi kâ-kî-kaskatahomiht, ê-isi-pêhtahkik, ê-nitawi-nakiskawâcik. ||| Then this man rode back to tell the chief that his son had come home, as well as the man who had been wounded; and when they heard this, they went to meet them.
ê-pêtastimwêyit awa okosisa, okimâwa, awa nâpêsis ôhi kâ-kaskatahomiht niyânan miyêw misatimwa; wiya mîna niyânan ayâwêw misatimwa. ||| That boy, the chief's son, who brought the horses, gave five of them to the man who had been wounded; five horses he kept.
mistahi miywêyihtam awa okimâw. ||| The chief was very glad.
piyisk kahkiyaw awiyak miywêyihtamwak; mîna ayahciyiniwa nisto ê-nipahât awa nâpêsis, miywêyihtamwak ôki ayisiyiniwak, ê-miyawâtahkik, ê-nîmihitocik, awa ohci nâpêsis osâm ê-sôhkêyimiht, "tâpwê nâpêhkâsôw!" ê-itêyimiht, ôhi mîna nâpêwa ê-kaskatahomiht êkâ kâ-wî-nakatât, osâm namôya cêskwa mitoni ê-oskinîkit. ||| Then everyone was glad; also because the boy had slain three Blackfoot those people were glad, and celebrated the outcome with a dance, thinking that boy very brave, thinking of him, “Truly, he is a brave warrior!” especially because he had refused to abandon the wounded man, even though he was not yet full-grown.
êwako anima ohci kâ-ôh-miywêyihtahkik ayîsiyiniwak. ||| That was why those people were glad.
êkoyikohk êskwâk âcimowin. ||| This is where the story ends.
kîtahtawê ê-wîkicik nêhiyawak, mihcêt mîkiwâhpa, mitâtaht ihtasiwak pêyakosâp, iskwêw pêyak; sipwêhtêwak, ê-nitonawâcik ayahciyiniwa, miskawâtwâwi ê-wî-kimotamawâcik otêmiyiwa. ||| Once where some Cree camped in a great camp, ten men and one over, one woman, set out to look for Blackfoot and when they found them to steal their horses.
pêyak mistahi miyosiw awa oskinîkiw; êkwa awa iskwêw mîna êwako miyosiw. ||| One of them, a youth, was very handsome, and the woman, too, was beautiful.
êkwa ôki mitâtaht oskinîkiwak, pêyak awa owîkimâkana ôhi kâ-miyosiyit iskwêwa kâ-wîcêwât. ||| And of those ten young men, of one she was the wife, that beautiful woman, whom he took with him.
kîtahtawê kisiwâsiw; owîkimâkana pakamahwêw, ôma ka-ati-mâna-pimohtêcik, ôhi kâ-miyosiyit oskinîkiwa, "kôwîcimosin," ê-itât owîkimâkana. mayaw kâ-kitâpamâyit, ê-itêyihtahk, âsay pakamahwêw owîkimâkana, namôya ê-owîcimosiyit, konita êkosi ê-itêyihtahk. ||| Then after a time he became ill-tempered; he beat his wife; as they thus marched along, he would say to his wife, of that handsome youth, “You have taken him for your lover.” As soon as it seemed to him that she was looking at the other, he would beat his wife, not that she really had a lover, but from idle suspicion.
nîsosâp tahtwâw ê-nipât, mostoswa ê-nipahâcik, êkota ê-nâh-nawacîcik wiyâs, ê-mîcisocik âsay, oskinîkiwa ôhi pâskiswêwak; nipahêwak. ||| When he had been twelve nights on the march, and they had killed a buffalo and were preserving meat after their meal, they shot and killed that youth.
mîna owîkimâkana pâskiswêwak, ê-kâhkwêyimât. ||| And they shot and killed the man's wife, because he was jealous of her.
êkosi kotak awa, osîma awa oskinîkiw kâ-nipahimiht, ôhi kâ-miyosiyit oskinîkiwa otinêw, ê-kisîpêkinât, ê-wawêsîhât. ||| Then that other young man whose younger brother was he who had been slain, picked up the handsome youth, washed him, and put his finery on him.
mistikwa cimatâw, êkota ê-ahât osîma. ||| He set some sticks upright in the ground and there laid his younger brother.
otinêw ôhi iskwêwa, mîna êwakoni ê-kâsîhkwênât; êkota ahêw, ôhi osîma ita kâ-pimisiniyit. ||| He took the woman too and washed her face; he laid her where his brother lay.
êkosi pasikôw; ôhi nâpêwa kâ-nipahâyit owîkimâkaniyiwa itohtahêw. ||| Then he arose; he took to that place the man who had slain his wife.
ômisi itêw: "wâpam êsi-miyosicik nisîm ôhi iskwêwa." ||| Thus he spoke to him: “Look how beautiful are my brother and this woman.”
êkosi awa kâ-nipahât ôhi oskinîkiwa namôya wî-wâpamêw, ê-pakwâtahk, ê-miyosiyit. ||| Then he who had slain that youth would not look upon him, hating his beauty.
"hâw, êkâ kâh-wî-wâpamacik, namôya tahki ka-kî-kisiwâsin." "ka-mihtâtâw kiwîkimâkan." "êkâ wiya mâto isko ka-takosiniyahk kîkinâhk." "kîspin nôhtaw kimâton, ka-nipahitin kâ-nipahat nisîm." ||| “Very well, since you will not look upon them, you shall not be angry. You shall mourn for your wife. But do not weep until we reach home. If you weep before that, I shall kill you, who killed my brother.”
êkosi itwêw awa oskinîkiw kâ-nipahimiht osîma. ||| Thus spoke the youth whose brother had been slain.
êkosi sipwêhtêwak, ê-nitonawâcik ayahciyiniwa. ||| So they went from there to look for Blackfoot.
pêyakwâw ê-nipâcik, ê-wâpaniyik, wâpamêwak ita ê-wîkiyit ayahciyiniwa. ||| After sleeping once on the way in the morning they saw some Blackfoot encamped.
êkosi ê-tipiskâyik itohtêwak. ||| At nightfall they approached them.
awa osîma kâ-nipahimiht oskinîkiwa, êwako itohtêw mîkiwâhpihk, ê-nipâyit ayahciyiniwa. ||| He whose brother was the youth that had been slain, went to the Blackfoot where they slept in their tent.
otinêw misatimwa, ê-kimotamawât. ||| He took horses, robbing them.
êkosi owîcêwâkana ê-otihtât, mâh-miyêw. ||| When he reached his companions, he distributed them.
"têhtapik; tapasîtân; kîwêtân," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “Mount; let us flee; let us go home,” said that youth.
êwako kapê-tipisk pimipayiwak. ||| All that night they rode.
ê-wâpaniyik êwako âpihtâwi-kîsikâk takohtêwak ôhi ita kâ-pimisiniyit oskinîkiwa êkwa iskwêwa kâ-kî-nipahât ôhi. ||| That noon they reached the place where lay the youth and the woman whom that man had slain.
"hâw, wâpam kiwîkimâkan;" "kêyâpic miyosiw;" "awa oskinîkiw mîna êwako kêyâpic miyosiwak, âta ê-nipicik." ||| “So now, behold your wife; she is still beautiful; she and this youth, still they are beautiful, though they have died.”
êkosi awa kâ-nipahât pakwâtam ta-wâpamât, ê-mihtâtahk ê-kî-nipahât owîkimâkana. ||| Then he who had killed them hated to look at them, regretting that he had killed his wife.
tahki ta-nôhtê-mâtôw; mâka kitahamâk ôhi oskinîkiwa. ||| He was always on the point of weeping, but that youth forbade it.
"êkâya mâto." "ka-nipahitin, mâtoyini." "iyikohk takosiniyahko kîkinâhk, êkospîhk mâtoyini, namôya ka-nipahitin," itwêw awa awa oskinîkiw kâ-nipahimiht osîma oskinîkiwa. ||| “Do not weep. I shall kill you, if you weep. Only when we reach home, then I shall not kill you, if you weep,” said the youth whose young brother had been slain.
nama isko ê-takosihkik wîkiwâhk, mostoswa wâpamêwak. ||| Before they reached their camp, they came in sight of some buffalos.
pêyak nipahêwak, êkota ê-nâh-nawacîcik, ê-mîcisocik. ||| They killed one and stopped to preserve the meat and to eat.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, awa kâ-kî-nipahât owîkimâkana pasikôw; sipwêhtêw, ohpimê ê-nitawi-nahapit, ê-wayawîhtamâtot, ê-tapahtiskwêyit. ||| When they had eaten, he who had slain his wife arose; he went and sat down somewhere, weeping alone, with his head bowed in grief.
êkosi awa kotak oskinîkiw kâ-kî-itât, "mâtoyini, ka-nipahitin", kâ-kî-itwêt, wâpamêw ê-tapahtiskwêyiyit, ê-mâtoyit, ê-itêyimât. ||| Then that youth who had said to him, “If you weep, I will kill you,” saw him with bowed head and, as he thought, weeping.
otinam pâskisikan, ê-nitawâpamât. ||| He took his gun and went to look at him.
ê-wâpamât, tâpwê mâtoyiwa. ||| When he saw him, he was really weeping.
"êkosi kâ-kî-ititân." "nimiywêyihtên, nisîm ê-kî-nipahat, êkwa ê-nipahitân." "â, oskinîkîtik, êkâya pisiskêyimihk." "êkota ta-pa-pimisin." ||| “This is what I told you. I am glad to kill you who killed my brother. Come, young men, pay no attention to him. Let him, lie here.”
êkosi sipwêhtêwak; kîwêwak. ||| So they departed; they returned home.
nîswâw ê-nipâcik, takohtêwak wîkiwâhk; misatimwa pêsiwêwak. ||| After two nights on the way they reached their camp; they brought home the horses.
êkwa ê-âcimocik ê-nâh-nipahitocik wiyawâw, namôya ayahciyiniwa ê-nipahikocik, mistahi owâhkômâkaniwâwa mihtâtikwak awa kâ-miyosit oskinîkiw awa mîna iskwêw kâ-nipahihcik. ||| And when they told of how they had done killing among themselves, and that it was not the Blackfoot who had done killing among them, then greatly their relatives mourned for that handsome youth and for the woman who had been slain.
kayâs mostoswak, paskwâwi-mostoswak, nânitaw mitâtaht tipahikan, êkoyikohk askiy nama kêkway nôkwan, ê-akoskahkik paskwâwi-mostoswak. ||| The old-time buffalos, for a distance of some ten miles the earth was not visible, as the buffalos covered it.
êwako âcimôwin namôya kayâs, mâskôc niyânano-mitanaw askiy êkospî ôma iyikohk ê-mihcêticik mostoswak. ||| This story is not old, perhaps fifty years ago it was, when the buffalos were so many.
nâpêwak niyânan êwakonik ê-âcimocik ê-wâpamâcik, piko ê-pimohtêcik ôki nêhiyawak, akohpa ômisi ê-wêpinahkik, ê-tawitisahwâcik mostoswa; êkwa ôtê nâway kâwi ômisi ê-pê-tipwayâyit ê-misihtawayâyit. ||| Five men they were who told of it, having seen it when they were out for a walk, these Cree.
êkwa mitâtaht tipahikan êkoyikohk isko ê-ayâcik paskwâwi-mostoswak, iyikohk ê-mihcêticik, êkâ ê-tawâyik ita kâ-pimohtêcik. ||| They shook their blankets like this, to drive the buffalos apart, and behind them the herd closed in again.
êkoyikohk isko, mitâtaht tipahikan isko mihcêtiyit mostoswa, ê-wâpamâcik nêhiyawak kayâs, nânitaw niyânano-mitanaw askiy. ||| And for a distance of ten miles there were buffalos so numerous that there was no opening where they walked.
êwako pêyak âcimowin. ||| Ten miles in length was the herd of buffalos which these Cree saw of old, some fifty years ago.
pêyak nâpêw powâmêkan isiyîhkâsôw; êwako kâ-wâpamât ôhi mostoswa. ||| One man was called Powamekan; he saw these buffalos.
êkwa pêyak nâpêw tâmpêsin isiyîhkâsôw. ||| And one man was called Tampesin.
êkwa pêyak wataniy isiyîhkâsôw. ||| And one was called Bird-Tail.
êkonik ê-wâpamâcik iyikohk ê-mihcêtiyit paskwâwi-mostoswa. ||| They saw the herd of buffalos that was so great.
kîtahtawê opwâsîmowak mihcêtiwak; mîna mîkiwâhpa mihcêtinwa. ||| Once upon a time there were many Assiniboine Sioux; and there were many tents.
pêyak opwâsîmôw oskinîkiw mistahi kitimâkisiw. ||| One Assiniboine, a young man, was very poor.
nama awiya owâhkômâkana pimâtisiyiwa. ||| None of his kinsfolk were living.
"tâpwê nikitimâkisin," itêyihtam. ||| “Truly I am wretched,” he thought.
êkwa wîwa, nôtokêsiwa kêkâc, kakwêcimêw: ||| Then he asked his wife, who was nearly an old woman:
"awiyak cî kiwâhkômâkan pimâtisiw, kôhtâwiy kikâwiy kisîm kistês kimis?" "nama awiyak cî pimâtisiw?" itêw. ||| “Are any of your kinsfolk alive, your father, your mother, your younger brother or sister, your elder brother, your elder sister? Is none of them alive?” he asked her.
êkwa ômisi itik: "mitoni nama awiyak." ||| She answered him, “They are all gone.”
"êkwa tâpwê kikitimâkisinânaw." "âhkamêyimo ê-atoskêyan." "niya mîna nika-âhkamêyimon, ôta kâ-wîkihkêmoyahk kita-atoskawâyahkok ta-pamihâyahkok, ôma ita kâ-wîkihkêmoyahk." ||| “Then truly we are pitiable. Take heart and work. I too shall take courage, and we shall work for the people here among whom we dwell.”
ê-piponiyik êkwa atoskêwak. ||| In winter then they worked.
ê-miyoskamik ê-âhtokêwiht, êkwa papâmohtêw. ||| In spring, when his people moved camp, he walked about.
matokahpihk pôti miskam: mîkwana êkwa pîwâpiskwa. ||| In an abandoned lodge he found something: some feathers and some pieces of metal.
êkwa kîwêhtatâw; owîkimâkana miyêw. ||| He took the things home and gave them to his wife.
"nah ôhi kanawêyihta," itêw. ||| “Take these things and save them up,” he told her.
êkwa manimisâskwatwêw; ahcâpiya mîna osîhêw; nîsitanaw niyânanosâp osîhtâw acosisa. ||| Then he gathered spruce-wood; he made a bow and twenty-five arrows.
êkwa pîhtatwâna kaskikwâtêw. ||| Then he sewed a quiver.
êkwa ispatinâhk itohtêw, ê-wîhkwêstêyiki mîkiwâhpa ê-kitâpahtahk. ||| Then he went to the top of a hill and looked at the lodges which stood in a circle.
wâpahtam mîkiwâhp pîhtêyas ê-cimatêyik. ||| He saw a single lodge which stood in the center.
itêyihtam, "wêyôtisiw nâha." "mahti nika-nitawi-kakwêcimâw;" "nika-nitawi-atâmâw atimwa pêyak ôhi ohci nîpisisa," itêyihtam. ||| He thought, “That man is rich. Suppose I go ask him; I shall buy a dog from him with these arrows,” he thought.
itohtêw ê-otâkosiniyik, mihcêt ê-wâpamât atimwa, otâpânâskwa, atimo-otâpânâskwa. ||| He went there in the evening, and saw a great many dogs and sleds, dog-sleds.
êkwa ê-pîhtokêt, pôti apiyiwa nâpêwa. ||| When he entered the lodge, there sat a man.
"tawâw, oskinîkiw", itik; "hâw, ta-mîcisôw." ||| “Come in, young man,” said the other to him; “Come, let him eat.”
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, miyêw. ||| When he had finished his meal, he gave the things to the other.
"ôhi ohci kâ-pê-itohtêyân acosisa, 'mâskôc pêyak miyici,' ê-itêyihtamân, kâ-ôh-pîhtokêyân." ||| “I have come here on account of these arrows, thinking perhaps he would give me a puppy;' that is why I have come to our tent.”
"êha, kika-miyitin." ||| “Yes, I shall give you some.”
têpakohp ihtasiyiwa. ||| There were seven of them.
"âsay pâhkwâpiwak ôki acimosisak;" "êwakonik kimiyitin; êkwa okâwiyiwâwa, acimosisak okâwiyiwâwa." "kitatamihin ôhi kâ-pê-miyiyan." ||| “These puppies have already opened their eyes; I give you these; also the dam, the puppies' mother. I thank you for having come and given me these things.”
êkwa iskwêwak postamôhêwak kiskânakwa ôhi kâ-atâwêwiht. ||| Then the women harnessed the female that had been sold.
kêkâ-tipiskâyiw âsay. ||| It was already close to night.
kîwêhtahêw; nayômêw acimosisa kahkiyaw. ||| He took them home, carrying all the puppies.
pimitisahok ôhi kiskânakwa. ||| The bitch ran behind him.
owîkimâkana kitotêw, "pê-wayawî!" ||| He called to his wife, “Come out!”
"sakahpis." "ôhi otawâsimisa kita-nôhêw." ||| “Tie her up. Let her suckle these puppies of hers.”
sakahpitêw. asamêw ôhi atimwa. ||| She tied her up and fed her.
ohpikihêw otawâsimisa. ||| The dog brought up its young.
âsay mîna kotaka kîskikaham misâskwatwa. ||| Then again he cut some spruce-sticks.
kêyâpic êko-tahto, nîsitanaw niyânanosâp âsay mîna osihtâw. ||| Again the same number, twenty-five, he made.
ê-kîsihtât, âsay mîna ispatinâhk itohtêw. âsay mîna kitâpahtam mîkiwâhpa. ||| When he had finished them, again he went to the hill-top and looked down at the tents.
"nêki mihcêtiwak ê-atoskêcik iskwêwak," itêyihtam; "êkotê nika-kiyokân," itêyihtam awa kâ-kitimâkisit opwâsîmôw. ||| “Down there are many women at work,” he thought; “There I shall visit,” thought the poor Stony.
kiyokêw ê-otâkosiniyik, ê-pimiwitât ôhi kâ-kî-osîhtât acosisa. ||| He made his visit at dusk, carrying along the arrows he had made.
ê-takohtêt mîkiwâhpihk, "tawâw," itik ôhi nâpêwa. ||| When he came to the tent, “Come in,” said the man to him.
pîhtokêw; âsay mîna asamâw. ||| He entered; this time too he was given food.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, "hâw, oskinîkiw! ||| When he had eaten, “Now, young man, it is not your habit to go a-visiting.
nama wîhkâc kikiyokân." "kâ-pê-kiyokêyan kîkway êtokê ê-pê-nitawêyihtaman?" ||| No doubt you have called here with something in mind.”
"ôhi ê-pimiwitâyân ê-pê-atâmitân, kîspin kitayân." "'ayâwak iskwêwak mihkihkwana mâtahikan cîkahikan kiskiman môhkomân,' ê-itêyihtamân, "mahti nika-nitawi-atâmâw," kâ-itêyihtamân." ||| “It is that I have come to trade you these things which I am carrying with me, if you have the trade. 'The women have hide-flatteners, hide-scrapers, hatchets, files, and knives,' was my thought; 'Suppose I go buy them from him,' was my thought.”
"ahaq, ihtakonwa," itik ôhi nâpêwa. ||| “Yes, these things are here,” said the man to him.
kahkiyaw miyik tahto kâ-pê-atâmât. ||| He gave him all the things he had come to buy.
kîwêhtatâw wîkiwâhk. êkwa miyêw owîkimâkana. ||| He took them home and gave them to his wife.
"nahi ôhi; kiya ôhi âyâ; nahastâ; kanawêyihta;" "osâm mistahi kikitimâkisinânaw," itêw owîkimâkana. ||| “Here, take these things; do you keep them; put them away and take care of them; we are altogether too destitute,” said he to his wife.
"êha," itik, "kitatamihin," itik owîkimâkana. ||| “Yes,” his wife answered him; “Thank you.”
âsay mîna otinam misâskwatwa; âsay mîna nîsitanaw niyânanosâp osîhtâw. ||| Again he took some spruce-sticks; again he made twenty-five.
âsay mîna ê-otâkosiniyik ê-wîhkwêstêyiki mîkiwâhpa kitâpahtam: pôti pîhtêyask cimatêyiw mîkiwâhp. ||| Again at nightfall he looked at the tents standing in a circle. There in the center stood a lodge.
itêyihtam: "nâha okimâw manitôwiw; nihtâ-nanâtawihiwêw," itêyihtam. ||| He thought: “Yonder chief has spirit-power; he is a great healer.”
itohtêw; ê-otâkosiniyik pîhtokêw. ||| He went there; at nightfall he entered.
ê-itâpit askotâskopisonihk, pôti wâpahtam pâskisikana nisto. ||| When he looked at the wooden beams along the wall, there he saw three guns.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, miyâw pâskisikan pêyak, ê-atâwêt ôhi ohci acosisa, êkwa kaskitêw pîhcipihkwâna ê-sâkaskinêyit, êkwa môsasiniya nîsitanaw, êkwa cahkisêhikana nîso, êkwa kêtahikana nîso. ||| When he had eaten, he was given a gun, which he bought with those arrows, also some gun-powder, a powder-horn full of it, twenty bullets, two flints, and two ramrods.
"kitatamihin, oskinîkiw, ôhi kâ-miyiyan," itêw. ||| “I thank you, young man, for giving me these,” he said to him.
"êkosi kanawêyihta," itêw owîkimâkana. ||| “So do you save these things,” he told his wife.
âsay mîna osîhtâw acosisa nîsitanaw, "êwakoni nika-ayân," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| Again he made twenty arrows, “These I shall keep,” being his plan.
êkwa ôki acimosisak misikitiwak; êkwa âsay takwâkin; âsay mitoni misikitiwak. ||| Now those puppies had grown up and it was autumn; they were already quite big.
êkwa awa iskwêw nakayâhêw. ||| The woman broke them to harness.
pâ-pîmakâmêpitêw ôhi acimosisa. ||| She hitched up those young dogs.
êkwa kêkâc pipon. êkwa mitoni kisin. ||| Then it was nearly winter, and very cold.
kêkâc ê-pipohk, paskêpiciwak ê-nîsicik owîkimâkana awa kâ-kitimâkisit. ||| When it was nearly winter, the two, the poor man and his wife, moved camp away from the others.
sakâw otihtam ê-ihkatawâyik, wâsakâm ê-sakâyik, mihta ê-mihcêniyiki, mîna mostoswa ê-mihcêtiyit. nipahêw pêyak mostoswa. ||| He came to a wood with an open space in the middle with woods all round, where there was plenty of fuel and where the buffalos were many.
êkwa osîhtâw wîki, mîkiwâhp, mihtikowâhp ê-misâyik. ||| He killed a buffalo. Then he built his dwelling, a large wooden house.
êkwa kahkiyaw otinam wiyâs. ||| He took all the meat.
êkwa tahto-kîsikâw mâcîw; tahto-kîsikâw minahôw. ||| Then every day he hunted; every day he made a killing.
atimwa âpacihêwak ayinânêw; kahkiyaw otinamwak wiyâs. ||| They used the eight dogs; they took all the meat.
mîna wanihikêw mistiko-wanihikana, mahîhkana ê-nôcihât, nanâtohk atâwâkana ê-nipahât wanihikanihk. ||| Also he trapped with wooden traps, trying for wolves, and killed all kinds of fur-bearing beasts in his traps.
pêyak kîsikâw âskaw mitâtaht ayiwâkês nipahêw mahîhkana. ||| Often he killed more than ten wolves in a day.
mihcêt osîhtâw cêsipicikana, wiyâs êkota ê-akotât, wiyâs ê-akotât cêsipicikanihk. ||| He built many drying-frames, on which he hung his meat. The woman, too, worked bravely.
êkwa awa iskwêw âhkamêyimôw. kêkâc wiyâpaniyik pôni-atoskêw, mistahi ê-atoskêcik. ||| It would be almost dawn when they quit work, so busy were they.
âsay ati-kâ-kîsopwêyâyiw. ||| The warm weather was already coming on.
"mahti êkwa nika-osîhâw otâpânâsk," itêyihtam. ||| “I suppose I had better make a sled now,” he thought.
osîhêw atimo-otâpânâskwa, ê-pasahwât mistikwa, napakitâpânâskwa ê-osîhât. ||| He built a dog-sled with split trees, a flat dog-sled.
ê-kî-kîsihât, takohtêw. ||| When he had finished it, he tied it up.
êkota napakâhtikohk ahêw mostoswayâna mîna mahîhkaniwayâna, nanâtohk atâwâkana. ||| On the boards of it he put buffalo-robes, wolfskins, and all kinds of furs.
sipwêhtêw, ê-itohtêt wâskahikanihk, otatâwêwa ê-nitawâpamât. ||| He went off to see the trader in his house.
"haw, pîhtoka; asam kitêmak," itik okimâwa. ||| “Well, bring them in; feed your dogs,” said the agent to him.
pîhtokahêw wâskahikanihk, ê-asamât. ||| He brought them into the shed and fed them.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw kâ-kitimâkisit, "awîna ita ê-ayât ê-pê-wâh-ohci-sipwêhtêyan?" itik. ||| Then they asked the poor young man, “Who is there at the places you come from?”
"niya piko êkwa niwîkimâkan." "mistahi nitayân wiyâs wiyinwa pimiya atâwâkanak." "nitawêyihtamani wiyâs, kika-miyitin." ||| “Only my wife and I. I have a great deal of meat, fats, grease, and fur. If you need meat, I can give you some.”
"êha, ninitawêyihtên mîcim tahto ê-ayâyan;" "kahkiyaw nika-otinên," itik; "tâniyikohk otâpânâskwak?" ||| “Yes, I want all the food you have. I can take it all,” the other told him; “How many wagonloads is it?”
"pêyak, nîso, mitâtaht otâpânâskwak." ||| “One, two, ten wagonloads.”
mistahi kititwân." "ahpô ôtênaw ê-otihtamân, nama wîhkâc mitâtaht sâkaskinêwak otâpânâskwak." ||| You are saying a great deal. Even when I come to a town, there are never ten loads.”
"êkwa ê-pêyakoyan, kiwîkimâkan ê-nîsiyêk, mistahi kâ-nitawêyimacik otâpânâskwak." ||| “For you and your wife alone that is quite a few sleds.”
"êha," itêw, "nôhtaw." "wiyâs piko mitâtaht otâpânâskwak kâ-nitawêyihtaman." "tahto kêkway atâwâkana mêstawatâtwâwi kôskinîkîmak, êkoyikohk nika-pê-itohtân ta-pê-otinikêyân." "anohc wiya pêyakwasâkay kika-miyin, kaskitêwêkin êkwa pêhpêsâpowayân." "êkwa kiya! ||| “Yes,” answered the other, “and that is not all. It is for meat alone that I need ten sleds. When your helpers have carted away all the furs, then I shall come to take my pay.
pêyakwayôwinis wêmistikôsiwi-ayôwinisa, astotin, êkwa kiya kiminihkwêwin kâ-miywâsik, êkwa pêyakonisk mihkwêkin, êkwa cistêmâw;" "iyikohk ê-wî-miyiyan." "itâp pê-otinikêyâni êkota ka-wîhtamâtin." ||| Today just give me one dress-length, black cloth and striped cloth. And one suit of your white-man's clothes, a hat, and some of your own good liquor, one fathom of red flannel, and some tobacco; that is all you need to give me. When I come back to collect, I shall tell you the rest.”
kîwêw. owîkimâkana otihtêw. pêyakwâw nipâw; owîkimâkana otihtêw. ||| He went home to his wife, sleeping one night on the way.
"kakwêyâho;" "ôma osihtâ kita-oskotâkâyan," itêw. ||| “Stick to your work; make yourself a dress of this,” he told her.
kakwêyâhow ê-kaskikwâtahk awa iskwêw oskotâkay ôma kaskitêwêkin, otâsa mîna awa iskwêw, wanakwaya mîna. ||| The woman worked busily, sewing a dress for herself out of the black broadcloth, as well as some gaiters and sleeves.
postayôwinisêw awa iskwêw. ||| She put on her new clothes.
"hâ, pakwahtê ôma," itêw owîkimâkana, "ôma wâpowêyân." ||| “Good, now wear this round your waist,” he said to his wife, “this robe.”
ê-kîsi-postayôwinisêt awa iskwêw, êkwa awa nâpêw postayôwinisêw, wêmistikôsiwi-ayôwinisa; astotin, postastotinêw. ||| When the woman had dressed up, the man also dressed up in white-man's clothes, and put on his hat.
âsay namôya kitimâkisiwak. ||| Now they were no longer poor.
otinam; oyâkanihk iskotêwâpoy sîkinam, êkwa êwako ê-minihkwêcik. ||| He took the whiskey and poured it into a bowl and then they drank it.
"ay, êkoyikohk; pôni-minihkwêtân;" "osâm kika-atoskânânaw;" "ta-takosinwak ayîsiyiniwak, wêmistikôsiwak, ê-wî-pê-nâtahkik wiyâs." "âhkamêyimo ê-atoskêyan." "âhkamêyimo êkwa tâpwê kita-atoskêyan;" "niya mîna nika-âhkamêyimon ta-nipahtâyân atâwâkana." ||| “There, that will do; let us stop drinking; we have too much work ahead; some people are coming, Frenchmen, to fetch meat. Set bravely to work. We are altogether too poor, having no kinspeople. It was for this I bought the dogs, to be our beasts of burden. tâpwê ê-kî-nisto-tipiskâyik nikotwâsik otâpânâskwa takosiniyiwa. ||| Accordingly, three days later six sleds arrived.
"pisisik wiyâs pêtâhkêk;" "atâwâkanak pêyak otâpânâsk ka-pêsiwâwâwak, niyânan otâpânâsk wiyâs êkwa." ||| “Bring only meat; one load of fur you will bring, and five loads of meat.”

êkwa nêtê wâskahikanihk takosinwak. ||| They arrived yonder at the trading-house.
