"êkwa nânitaw nîsitanaw otâpânâskwak ta-sipwêhtêyân kahkiyaw nika-pêtân tahto kâ-ayâcik mîciwin ahtaya mîna." ||| “Perhaps twenty sleds will be filled. There is much meat, grease, and fat. No doubt you will think it a great deal for one man to give you in fur and various kinds of food. He has grown rich, all by himself with his wife. The firewood where they live looks like a town, as one approaches. Never are all the sleds full, and there are the six sleds all loaded. If I go off with some twenty sleds, I can bring all the meat they have and the furs.”
"hâ, êkosi ê-isi-wâpahtaman?" ||| “So that is the way you fared?”
"nîsitanaw otâpânâskwak ka-sipwêhtahâwâwak." "kîspin sâkaskinêci, kahkiyaw sâkaskinêtwâwi, tâpiskôc mihcêt ôtênawa ê-wâpahtamân nika-itêyihtên." "hâw, sipwêhtêk." ||| “You will go off with twenty sleds. When they are all full, I shall think I am beholding many villages. Very well, be off.”
êkwa sipwêhtêwak nîsitanaw otâpânâskwak. ||| So twenty sleds started out.
"kahkiyaw pêtâyiw pôsihtâyêko ta-pê-sipwêhtêwak." "mahti nika-wâpamimâwa owîkimâkana mistahi kâ-atoskêyit." ||| “When you have loaded it all, let them set out and come here. I should like to see his wife who does so much work.”
takosinwak; êkwa kahkiyaw otâpânâskwak sâkaskinahêwak. ||| They arrived; and all the sleds were loaded full.
êkwa awa otêma atimwa awa opwâsîmôw ayinânêw kahkiyaw otâpahêw, atâwâkana ê-pôsihât, ê-otâpêyit. ||| In addition the Stony hitched up all his eight dogs and loaded the sled with fur and took it.
namôya sêmâk sipwêhtêw. ||| He did not set out right away.

"hâ, kiya kitayiwinisa nêwo ayiwinisa ayîsiyiniwak ta-postiskahkik ê-kaskitêwâki." "êkwa, kîspin kitayâwâw, pêyak misatim." "êkotôwahk ê-nitawêyimakik." ||| “Of your clothes, four suits for men to wear, black suits. And, if you have one, a horse. That is what I want.”

"haw, pêyak kâ-nitomat misatim, wiyâs kâ-miyiyan." "êkoyikohk têpipayiw wiyâs, ôki misatimwak kâ-otinacik." "êwako kita-ohci-atamiskâtân." "â, êkosi." "êkwa kîkway wâh-otinaman ayiwinisa?" ||| “Now you asked for one horse for the meat you gave me. That meat pays for these horses you have just taken. Therefore you shall not need to be bashful when you come here. I shall greet you first of all, no one else, only you. A chief's coat I shall give you, and a flag; these I give you as presents. "nêwo ayîsiyiniwak ta-postiskahkik." "êkwa kiya kiminihkwêwin." "êkwa mihkwêkin nêwinisk êkwa kaskitêwêkin nêwinisk." "êkwa cistêmâw." "êkwa pâskisikêwin." "êkwa nanâtohk kêkway, wâpamona, oyamanak." nâtakâm itohtêw, ê-nitawi-kîskikahahk apasoya. ||| He went into the forest and cut tent-sticks.

"êkota ayâw." "kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwak ayâwak êkota." ||| “He is over there. All the people are over there.”

sipwêhtêw; kîwêpayiw; kahkiyaw nêwo nitomêw ôhi ayîsiyiniwa. ||| He went away; he rode back; he called all four of those men.
"nêma kâ-osêhcâk, kâ-awasitêk nêma, êkotê ê-ohci-nitomikawiyêk." ||| “Yonder hill, just beyond it, that is from where the invitation comes to you.”

otihtêwak ôhi kâ-kitimâkisiyit. ||| They came to that man who had been poor.
"mistahi ê-kî-kitimâkisit awa kâ-isinâkosit kâ-wêyôtisit," itêyihtamwak ôki okimâwak nêwo. ||| “He who was so very poor, here he is looking like this, a wealthy man,” thought those four chiefs.

"êha, kika-okimâwin." "tahto kâ-tipêyihtamân mîkiwâhpa kahkiyaw kimiyitin, ta-tipêyihtaman," itik kahkiyaw ôhi nêwo okimâwa. ||| “So be it; you shall be chief. As many tents as are under me, I give them all to you to command,” he was told by each of those four chiefs.
ê-otihtahk ê-wîhkwêstêyiki mîkiwâhpa, pîhtêyask nitawi-mânokêyiwa ôhi okimâwa, ê-atoskâkot. ||| When he came to where the tents stood in a circle, those chieftains set up a lodge in the center, doing the work for him.

mitoni ninikotwâsinân, ê-sipwêhtêyâhk. ||| There were six of us who set out.
wiyâpahtamâhko mîkiwâhpa, nikâsowânân, êkâ ta-wâpamikoyâhkok ayahciyiniwak, ê-pimohtatâyâhk ôtê ohci ayiwinisa, ê-nitawi-wîtaskiyâhk wâhyaw awasâpisk. ||| When we saw any tipis, we hid from the people, lest the Blackfoot see us. We were carrying garments with us, from here, for we were bound on an embassy far beyond the Rocky Mountains.
piyisk nôtihtênân asinîwaciy, têpiskâki piko ê-pimohtêyâhk, êkâ awiyak ta-nôtinikoyâhk, ê-wî-kakwê-takohtêyâhk itê kâ-itohtêyâhk. ||| At last we came to the Rocky Mountains, walking the while only at night, lest anyone fight with us, for we meant to reach our destination.
piyisk awasâpisk nitakohtânân. ||| At last we arrived beyond the Rockies.
êkotê piyisk mînisa miywâsinwa, iyikohk ê-takohtêyâhk. ||| The berries were ripe by the time we arrived.

piyisk kinwês âkawâyihk nikâsonân. ||| For quite a while we stayed in hiding.
êkosi kîtahtawê êkwa nikaskihtânân pîhtêyask ê-cimatêk mîkiwâhp, ê-okimâwit kinêpikoyiniw. ||| Then in time we managed to gain the tipi which stood in the center, that of the Snake who was chief.
nipîhtokânân, ê-tipiskâk. ||| We entered when it was dark.
ê-pîhtokêyâhk, waniskâw awa okimâw. ||| When we entered, the chief arose from his couch.
êkosi apisîs piko pônasiwak. ||| So they made only a small fire.
wîwa nayêstaw nistiwak, ê-nîsôskwêwêt. ||| With his wives, they were only three, for he had two wives.
êkosi pêyak wayawîw awa, ê-atotak, niwîcêwâkan; êkosi otinam; kahkiyaw pîhtokatâw ayiwinisa ôhi ê-pimohtatâyâhk, ê-nitawi-mêkiyâhk, mîna nanâtohk akohpa. ||| So then I bade one of my companions go out; he took the things; he brought in all the things we carried with us to give away, and all kinds of blanket-robes.
êkosi isi pakitinamawâw awa kâ-pîhtokawâyâhk. ||| Then they were set down before him whose tent we had entered.
êkosi wîwa kitotêw; wayawiyiwa. ||| Then he spoke to his wives; they went out.
kîtahtawê pîhtokêyiwa wîwa. ||| Presently his wives came in.
wîhkâc pê-pîhtokêyiwa ôhtâwiya. ||| At times his father came in.
êkosi ka-kitotêw ôhtâwiya; ati-wayawiyiwa. ||| So then he spoke to his father; the latter would go out.
êkosi ê-pîhtokêyit ôhtâwiya, wa-wayawîwak ôki iskwêwak, kotakihk ê-itohtêcik. ||| In this fashion, when his father came in, his wives would go out, and go to some other place.
êkosi kotakak okimâwak pâh-pîhtokêwak. ||| Then other chiefs began to come in.
êkosi mitoni sâkaskinêwak. ||| The tent became crowded.

"kîspin kî-pê-maci-nôcihtâcik, kitêmiwâwak tahto kâ-miyosicik ka-kimotamâkawinâwâw; êkosi mîna niya nika-nipahikwak." "âsay kayâhtê ê-nipâyân, kayâhtê kotawêwak." "êkosi nikoskonikwak." "êkâ ohci ôhi kâ-astêki ê-pê-nitawi-miyicik ayiwinisa, mîna môsw-asiniya, mîna kaskitêw." "êkosi kinitawêyimitinâwâw ta-miyo-otôtêmiyêk." "êkosi kê-wâpahk ta-pê-nitawi-okwêmêsiyêk kinitotamâtinâwâw." "hâw, êkosi êsi-wîhtamâtakok," itêw otôskinîkîma; "êwako ohci kâ-ôh-nitomitakok." ||| Then that chieftain spoke: “Now then, although I was unwilling, you made me chief. Accordingly, I now ask of you not to overstep that which I shall tell you. Had they come here with evil designs, you would have been robbed of as many of your horses as are handsome; and likewise, me they would have killed. Without my knowledge, and while I was yet asleep, they made a fire. Then they awakened me. Their purpose was to come give me these things that lie here, garments, and bullets, and powder. Accordingly, I ask of you that you be good friends. Tomorrow I shall call upon you to come here and make friends with them. There, this is what I had to say to you,” he said to his followers; “It was for this that I summoned you.”
"hâw, ôma kâ-itwêyan namôya nika-kî-miyâskênân kipîkiskwêwin," itik ôhi otôskinîkîma. ||| “Now, this which you have spoken we shall not by any chance transgress, this speech of yours,” his followers answered him.
"êkosi mâka kêkwayak ôki?" ||| “But now, what sort of men are they?”
êkosi kakwêcimêw awa okimâw. ||| Thereupon the chief asked them.
wîhtamawêw pêyak awa nâpêw, êwako ciwayân kâ-itiht: "nêhiyawak niyanân," itêw; "êkosi ôhcitaw ê-pê-nitawâpamitâhk." "'wâhyaw askîhk kiyâm nika-wâpahtênân,' ê-itêyihtamâhk, êwako ohci ôta kâ-wâpamiyâhk," itêw. ||| One of those men, the one whose name was Tehiwayan, told him: “We are Cree,” he told him; “And we have come with the express purpose of visiting you. 'We shall see much of the earth,' was our thought, and therefore you see us here,” he told him.
êkosi nitawi-kawisimôwak ôki okimâwak. ||| Then those chieftains went home to bed.
êkwêyâk êwako kitotêw awa ôhtâwiya. ||| Only then did he address his father.
êkosi ati-wayawiyiwa. ||| Thereupon the latter went out.
ê-kî-kîwêyit ôhtâwiya awa okimâw, êkwêyâk êkwa pîhtwâwak. ||| When the chief's father had gone home, only then did they smoke.
êkosi pîhtokêyiwa wîwa awa okimâw, ê-pêtâyit ta-mîcisocik ôki kâ-nitawi-wîtaskîcik. ||| Then the chief's wives came in, bringing food for those to eat who had come to make a treaty.
êkosi ê-kî-mîcisocik, wayawîwak; wîcêwêwak ôhi okimâwa. ||| When they had eaten they left the tipi; the chief went with them.
sipwêhtêwak; nâtêwak otêmiwâwa mîna kotaka ayiwinisa. ||| They went from there; they fetched their horses and their other things.
êkosi ê-takohtêcik, sâ-sakahpitêwak otêmiwâwa. ||| Then, when they came back, they tethered their horses.
êkosi isi pâh-pîhtokatâwak ôki iskwêwak ôhi nêhiyawa kêkway ê-pê-miyikocik. ||| Then those women began to bring into their dwelling the things which the Cree had given them when they came.
êkosi isi pîhtokêwak kahkiyaw ôki nâpêwak. ||| Then all those men went into the tent.
êkosi êkwa kawisimôwak. ||| So then they went to bed.
ê-wâpahk, waniskâwak. ||| When day broke, they got up.
ê-kî-mîcisocik, nahascikêwak ôki iskwêwak. ||| When they had eaten, the women put the dwelling in order.
êkosi wayawîwak; ôhtâwiya awa okimâw pîhtokêyiwa. ||| Then they went out; the chief's father entered.
wîhtamawêw ê-ta-têpwâtimiht kotaka okimâwa. ||| He told him of the arrival of other chiefs who had been summoned by calling.
kahkiyaw mitoni sâkaskinêwak ôma mîkiwâhp. ||| When all were there, they entirely filled that tent.
kîtahtawê kotak okimâw nitawi-nitomâw. ||| Presently one more chief was sent for.
êkosi êkwa wî-nipahêw êwako nicawâc awa okimâw. ||| Then this chief thought it best to kill them.
"hâw, nikwêmê, nîsta kika-nipahin." "wî-nipahatwâwi, nîsta ka-nipahin." ||| “Now then, my brother in arms, you will kill me too. If you are to kill them, you will kill me too.”
êkosi nitomâw kotak iskwêw ê-nêhiyawêt. ||| Then a woman was called who spoke Cree.
pê-itohtêw êkota; pîhtokêw. ||| She came there; she came into the tent.
êkosi kakwêcimâw awa nâpêw nêhiyaw. ||| Then that one Cree was questioned.
namôya ê-pê-nipahtâkêyân, mîna namôya ê-nôhtê-kimotiyân." "'mahti nika-nitawi-pîhtwân; mîna nika-nitawi-mîcison,' ê-itêyihtamân," itwêw awa nêhiyaw. ||| It was not for murder that I came here, and not because I wanted to steal. 'Suppose I go and smoke; suppose I go and eat,' was what I had in mind,” said that Cree.
êkosi ê-wîhtamâht awa okimâw. ||| Then that chief was told this.
êkosi êkwa okwêmêsa misatimwa nîso miyêw ê-mîhkawikiyit, kiyâm êkâ ta-pisiskêyimâyit ôhi kâ-nôhtê-nipahâyit. ||| Thereupon he gave his friend two swift horses, that he might cease to mind those whom he desired to kill.
êkosi isi miyêw cistêmâwa, môsasiniya, kaskitêw, mîna ayiwinisa. ||| Then likewise he gave him tobacco, bullets, powder, and garments.
kapê-pipon êkotê ayâwak ôki nêhiyawak. ||| Those Cree stayed there all winter.
mitoni misatimwa mihcêt miyâwak. ||| They were given very many horses.
êkosi ê-nîpihk, wawêyîwak. ||| Then, when summer came, they made ready to depart.
êkwa pê-wîcêwêw okwêmêsa kinêpikoyiniwa. ||| The Snake who was the Cree leader's friend accompanied him a ways.
iyikohk wâhyaw ê-pê-ayâcik, êkoyikohk kîwêyiwa okwêmêsa. ||| When they had gone quite a ways on the hither journey, only then did his friend go back.
niyânanomitanaw ayiwâk nikotwâsik miyikwak misatimwa. ||| The others had given them fifty-six horses.
êkosi êkwa, "wâpamaci ayahciyiniw, wî-nipahiski, wêpinâhkanik ôki misatimwak kâ-miyikawiyêk." "mistahi mâh-mîhkawikiwak êkonik." "piko kîwê- tapasîhkêk." "êkosi ta-miywâsin, takosiniyani kitaskîhk." ||| And so then, “If you see Blackfoot and they want to kill you, give rein to these horses that have been given to you. They are very swift. Simply flee for home. In this way you will easily reach your country.”
êkosi têpiskâki iyikohk, pimohtêw, êkâ ta-wâpamikot ayahciyiniwa. ||| Then only at night did he march, so as not to be seen by the Blackfoot.
iyikohk kêkâc ê-piponiyik, êkoyikohk takosin. ||| When it was almost winter, he arrived.
pêyak ayahciyiniwa ê-kimotamâkocik, atimêwak. ||| One Blackfoot had stolen horses from them, and him they overtook.
êkosi êkoni maskamêwak. ||| They took them away from him.
êkosi ê-wî-nipahikocik, nipahêwak. ||| Then, when he tried to kill them, they killed him.
êkota ohci kâ-kî-ihtakohk kiyôtêwin wîtaskîwin, êkâ ta-kimotamâtocik otêmiwâwa. ||| So began the mutual visiting and the alliance and the agreement not to steal each other's horses.
êkoyikohk pêyak pipon, iyikohk êsa ê-kî-sipwêhtêt, pîtos-iyiniwa otaskiyihk ê-kî-ayât. ||| It was one year from the time when he had set out on his visit to the foreigners' country.
"tâpwê nisâkihikwak kinêpikoyiniwak," kî-itwêw êwako kisêyiniw: "'pitanê êkâ wîhkâc maci-wîcêhtocik, wiyâpahtotwâwi,' nikî-itwân mâna, ispî ê-okimâwiyân." "êwako ohci nanâtohk ayîsiyiniwak kâ-ôh-kî-sâkihicik: namôya wîhkâc n-ôh-nipahtâkân." "kâkikê nikî-ayân ayahciyiniwak otaskîwâhk." "êkosi kiyîwêyâni nitaskîhk isi, nikî-mâna-pîkiskâtâwak ayahciyiniwak." "êwako ohci, kwayask ê-itâtisiyân, kâ-ôh-kisêyinîwiyân." "'êwako ani kakwê-ayâk, nitawâsimisitik, êwako.'" "'kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniw ka-miyo-wîcêwâwâw,' nikî-itâwak mâna nitawâsimisak." ||| “Truly, the Snake people were fond of me,” said that old man; “'Would they might never deal wrongly with each other, when they see one another,' I used to say, when I was chief. That is why all kinds of people loved me: I never killed people. All the time I was in the Blackfoots' country. And when I went home, they would always regret my departure, the Blackfoot. Because I was of decent and righteous character, is why I reached old age. 'That is the way you must try to be, my children, even thus. You must deal rightly with every human being,' I always told my children.”
ispî kâ-omikîhk êwako âcimowin. ||| This story took place at the time of the smallpox.
êkwa kîtahtawê nâ kisêyiniw âhkosiw, ita ê-kapêsicik. ||| A certain old man took sick where they were encamped.
êkwa otâpâsôw, ê-pimipicicik. ||| He was driving his team, for they were on the trek.
êkwa ita ê-kapêsicik, êkota mistahi âhkosiw kisêyiniw ana. ||| And then, there where they camped, that old man became very sick.
ômisi isiyîhkâsôw awa kisêyiniw: pitikwayasit isiyîhkâsôw. ||| This was the old man's name: Club-Foot was his name.
êwako mistahi kâ-âhkosit. ||| He was the one who fell very sick.
êkwa nêwâw ê-tipiskâk, êkwa pimisin; wî-nipiw. ||| For four nights he lay there; he was at the point of death.
êkwa êkota piciwak ôki kotakak ayîsiyiniwak; mâcika nakatâwak pêyak mîkiwâhp. ||| Then the other people there moved camp; as was to be expected, that family was abandoned there.
pêyak nôtokêsiw êkwa oskinîkiskwêw pêyak; êwako êkâ kâ-wâpit awa oskinîkiskwêw; mistahi kitimâkisiw. ||| An old woman and a young woman; and this young woman was blind; she was pitiable indeed.
êkwa namôya kî-nahastâwak. ||| They were not able to arrange their house.
ê-nipit êkota wîkimêwak; êkota awa kisêyiniw pimisin. ||| When the old man died, they stayed there with him; there lay the old man.
êkwa nîso-tipiskâw wîkimêwak. ||| For two nights they stayed with him.
êkwa awa nôtokêsiw âhkosiw. ||| Then the old woman took sick.
êkwa nîso-tipiskâw êtataw pimâtisiw. ||| For two nights she barely lived.
âsay kêkâc ê-wâpahk, namôya pimâtisiw; nipiw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| When it was almost dawn, she was no longer alive; the old woman had died.
êkwa êkota pêyakôw êkâ kâ-wâpit oskinîkiskwêw, okâwiya kâ-nipiyit. ||| Then that blind young woman was alone there, she whose mother had died.
êkwa êkota, "tânisi nika-tôtên?" êkosi itêyihtam; "namôya nika-sipwêhtân;" "nîsta ôta nika-nipin," itêyihtam. ||| Then, “What shall I do?” she thought; “I shall not go away from here; I too shall die in this place,” she thought.
"misawâc nika-nipin, nîsta." ||| “In any case I too shall die.”
êkwa okâwiya ôhi kîtahtawê, "hâw, nitânis, sipwêhtê; niya!" "anohc sipwêhtê," ê-itikot, ê-cîpayamatisôstawât; "niyâ, sipwêhtê!" ||| Then suddenly her mother said to her, “Now, my daughter, depart from here; go! Depart even now!” she said to her, speaking as the spirit of one departed to one still alive, “Go, leave!”
misatimwak nisto âh-ayâwêw, pêyak mistacimosis; nêwo. ||| She had three horses and one foal; four.
hâw, "êha, nika-sipwêhtân," itwêw. ||| “Very well, I shall depart,” she answered.
"tânitê êtokê mêskanaw?" "nama niwâpin;" "nama nikiskêyihtên," êkosi itêyihtam. ||| “But where, I wonder, is the road? I am blind; I do not know,”
êkwa misatimwa takosiniyiwa. ||| The horses came to where she was.
êkwa êkota otinêw ôhi misatimwa. ||| Then she took hold of those horses.
êkwa ta-tahkopitêw: êkwa aspapiwin, wiyahpicikêw. ||| She hitched them up; she took a saddle and harnessed them.
êkwa apisîs îwahikanisa êkota aspapiwinihk tahkopitêw. apisîs pimîs. ||| A little chopped meat she tied there to the saddle, and a bit of fat.
otinêw ôhtâwiya ocistêmâwi-maskimotisiyiw; asiwatâw. ||| She took her father's tobacco-pouch; she put it into her garment.
maskihkîwâpoy otinam, mîna askihkosa, wiyâkanis. êkwa kâ-sipwêhtêt. ||| She took some tea, and a small kettle, and a cup, and set out.
"tânisi êtokê nika-pimâtisin?" itêyihtam; "namôya niwâpin." ||| “I wonder how I shall keep alive”, she thought; “I am blind.”
sipwêhtêw; misatimwa sakâpêkinêw. ||| She set out; she led the horses on the lines.
êkwa mêskanaw nitonam. ||| She sought the road.
êkwa osita ohci mêskanaw ê-nitonahk, piyisk miskam mêskanaw. ||| Seeking the road with her feet, at last she found it.
"mâskôc nika-nipin," itêyihtam. ||| “No doubt I shall die,” she thought.
êkwa ê-pimohtêt wâhyaw itohtêw. ||| She walked a long ways.
êkwa ômisi ê-têhtapit. ||| So then she mounted a horse.
misatimwak sipwêhtêwak; pimipahtâwak. ||| The horses set out; they trotted on.
pêyak kîsikâw kinwês pimipahtâwak misatimwak. ||| On the first day the horses trotted quite a long time.
piyisk kiskêyihtam: "tipiskâw êkwa." kiskêyihtam: "sakâw; ôma mêskanaw, sakâw." itohtêw sakâhk; êkota kapêsiw. ||| At last she knew that night was at hand. She knew that there was a grove of trees: “Here is the road, here the grove.” She went into the wood; there she camped.
ê-wâpahk êkwa sipwêhtêw; nitonam mîna mêskanaw. ||| At daybreak she set out again; again she sought the road.
ômisi mîna osita, mêskanaw nitonam. ||| Like this, with her feet, she sought the road.
sipwêhtêw, mêskanaw; pimipahtâwak misatimwak. ||| She set out on the road; the horses trotted along.
nama kêkway nipiy ôta ayâw; nôhtêyâpâkwêw. ||| She had no water; she was thirsty.
kîtahtawê- misatimwa, pimipahtâwak misatimwak,- nipiy miskam. ||| Presently - the horses were trotting along, - she found some water.
minihkwêwak êkwa êkota misatimwak mîna ana iskwêw. ||| Then the horses and that woman drank there.
êkwa âsay mîna têhtapiw; êkota mistatimwak mêskanaw êkwa miskamwak. ||| Then she mounted again; the horses found the road. The horses trotted along.
pimipahtâwak misatimwak. ê-tipiskâk nipâw; mîna kapêsiw. ||| When night fell she slept; she camped again.
kîtahtawê misatimwak, "brrr!" wî-tapasîwak. ||| Suddenly the horses went, “Brrr!” They wanted to run away.
otinêw; âsay mîna têhtapiw. ||| She took them; she mounted one.
nama kêkway mêskanaw. ||| The road was not there.
"nama kêkway mêskanaw êkwa;" "tânitê êtokê êkwa?" ||| “This isn't the road; where can the road be?”
itê mîna ê-tipiskâk kapêsiw. ||| Then again when night fell, she camped.
êkota nipâw; nipiy êkota ayâyiw, sâkahikan. ||| There she slept; there was some water, a lake.
ê-wâpahk, sipwêhtêw. ||| At daybreak she went from there.
nama kêkway âsay mîcisôwin. ||| By this time she had nothing to eat.
isi-pimohtêw; têhtapiw. ||| She went on, riding.
"tânitê êtokê?" itêyihtam. ||| “Whither, I wonder,” she thought.
mêkwâc ê-pimohtêt, kîtahtawê nipiy pahkopêwak ôki misatimwak. ||| As she went along, presently the horses were going into water.
wâhyaw êkwa itêyihtam. ||| She thought it a long ways.
ôma ê-sipwêhtêt, ôma ispatinâw kiskêyihtam, ê-âmaciwêt, mistahi ê-ispatinâyik. ||| Here when she set out, she knew that it was a hill, that she was going up a high hill.
tahkohcâyihk pêyakwanohk nîhtakosîw. ||| On top of the hill in a place, she dismounted.
kîtahtawê misatimwak ôki sêkisiwak, "prrr!" wî-tapasîwak. ||| Presently the horses grew frightened; “Brrr!” They made to run away.
"mâskôc nika-pakamahok ayahciyiniwak; nika-nipahikwak," itêyihtam. ||| “Perhaps the Blackfoot will strike me down; they will kill me,” she thought.
kîtahtawê ayîsiyiniwa, "wâhwâ!" itik; "kikitimâkisin," itik. ||| Presently some people said to her, “Dear me! You are in a sorry state.”
"hâw, kika-pimâtisin," itik, nêhiyawa ê-miskâkot. ||| “There, your life is saved,” they told her, for some Cree had found her.
mistahi pakwâtam ana nâpêw ê-kitimâkisiyit ôhi iskwêwa. ||| That man was greatly disturbed at the woman's plight.
êkosi isi otihtahêw kisiwâk mîkiwâhpa, ê-kîwêhtahât. ||| So he took her to some tents that were close by, he took her home with him.
takosin mîkiwâhpihk. ||| He arrived at the camp.
awa nâpêw mistahi miyo-ayâw. ||| That man was very well off.
"hâ, nama kêkway cistêmâw," itêw. ||| “I haven't any tobacco,” he said to her.
awa iskwêw otinêw cistêmâwa; miyêw ôhi nâpêwa ôhi, maskihkîwâpoy mîna. ||| The woman took the tobacco; she gave it to that man, and the tea as well.
êkota, "mistahi kitatamihin," itwêw awa nâpêw ê-miyiht cistêmâwa. ||| Then, “You are doing me a great kindness,” said the man when he was given the tobacco.
êkwa êkota kî-pimâtisiw ana iskwêw. ||| And there that woman was able to live.
êkosi êkoyikohk ôma âcimowin ê-iskwâk. ||| So that is the end of this tale.
nikî-wâpamâw ana iskwêw; mîna nâpêw ana ninisitawêyimâw kâ-kî-miskawât. ||| I saw that woman; and I knew the man who found her.
kêtahtawê êsa iskwêw mistahi kiyiskwêw, êkwa ê-onâpêmit piko awiya nâpêwa oskinîkiwa, êkwa ê-âyimisit. ||| Once upon a time, the story goes, a certain woman was very silly; she would consort with any man or youth, and she was very troublesome.
kêtahtawê wâpamik owîkimâkana kotaka; misi-pakamahok. ||| Once her husband caught her with another man and gave her a sound beating.
apisîsiyiwa ocawâsimisa; nayômêw êwakoni. ||| She had a small child, which she carried on her back.
kêtahtawê kâwi kîwêw; kotaka wîwiyiwa onâpêma; kisiwâsiw. ||| After a while she went back home; her husband had taken another wife; she was angry.
sipwêhtêw awa nâpêw; kotaka iskwêwa sipwêhtahêw. ||| The man went away; he took the other woman along with him.
êkwa nawaswêw awa iskwêw. ||| Then that woman ran after them.
tâh-têpwâtêw, "niwî-wêpinâw awa kicawâsimis!" itêw. ||| She kept calling to him, “I'll throw away your child!”
âhci piko sipwêhtêw nâpêw. ||| The man went away just the same.
wâhyaw mitoni ê-ispatinâk, wêpinêw êkotê ocawâsimisa iskwêw awa. ||| Far away on a hill that woman abandoned her child.
êkwa ocawâsimisa nakatêw, ispatinâhk ê-wêpinât, ê-apisîsisiyit. ||| She left her child, abandoning it on a hill, a baby.
"mahîhkanak nitasamâwak awa iskwêsisa." ||| “To the wolves I feed this little girl.”
êkwa nêtê kîwêpahtâw. ||| Then she ran back yonder.
mêkwâc wîkiwâhk ê-apit, onâpêma takohtêyiwa. ||| As she stayed there in their house, her husband arrived.
"tâniwâ nitânis?" itik. ||| “Where is my daughter?” he asked her.
misi-pakamahok mitoni. ||| He gave her a terrible beating.
sipwêhtêw; nâtêw otânisa. ||| She went off; she went to fetch her daughter.
kotaka ayîsiyiniwa miskawêyiwa. ||| Other people had found her.
"tâniwâ?" itik onâpêma. ||| “Where is she?” her husband asked her.
âsay mîna mitoni misi-pakamahok. ||| Again he gave her a terrible beating.
êkwa awa iskwêw pimitisahwêw onâpêma. ||| The woman pursued her husband.
pê-kîwê kiyâm!" itêw onâpêma. ||| Please come home!” she said to her husband.
êkwa iskwêw kotaka nâpêwa otihtik. ||| Then another man came to where that woman was.
konita itêw, "namôya nimihtâtâw." "nimiywêyihtên ê-sipwêhtêt." "nawac kiya mistahi kisâkihitin," itêw; "nêma ê-miywêyihtamân." "êkwa ka-sipwêhtânânaw nîkinâhk." "ka-nipânânaw." ||| She told him all kinds of things, “I am not sorry about him. I am glad he is gone. I love you much more,” she told him; “This is the kind of thing I like. Now let us go off to my house. We shall sleep there.”
takohtêwak wîkiwâhk iskwêw. ||| They came to the woman's house.
êkwa ê-tipiskâk, nâpêw awa sipwêhtêw. ||| Then, after dark, the man went away.
pêyakohkwâmiw awa iskwêw. ||| The woman slept alone.
nîpâtipisk kîwêyiwa onâpêma. ||| During the night her husband came home.
êkwa pimisiniyiwa wayawîtimihk; kâh-kitotik. ||| He lay outside the tent; he conversed with her.
"pîhtokê," itêw; "kayâs kâ-sipwêhtêt niwîkimâkan." ||| “Come inside,” she told him; “My husband went away long ago.”
êkwa awa onâpêma ôhi ê-takosiniyit. ||| But it was her husband who had arrived.
êkwa, "namôya," itwêw nâpêw; "ahpô êtokê kiwîkimâkan ta-takosin," itêw. ||| So now, “No,” said he; “Your husband may come, for all I know,” he told her.
"namôya," itwêw iskwêw, "aspin wâhyaw ê-atimohtêt." ||| “No,” said the woman; “He has gone far away.”
nikostâw kiwîkimâkan." ||| I am afraid of your husband.”
"kiyâm pîhtokê!" itwêw iskwêw. ||| “Do come in!” said the woman.
awa nâpêw, "hâ," itwêw, "nika-pîhtokân." ||| “Well,” said the man, “I shall go in.”
êkwa mâh-mâsihêw iskwêw. ||| Then the woman lay with him.
"ahpô êtokê kinâpêm ta-takosin." "êkâya sôhki pâhpi; ta-takosin kinâpêm; ka-pakamahokonaw." ||| “Your husband may come any minute. Do not laugh aloud; your husband will be coming; he will beat us.”
"namôya," itwêw iskwêw; "namôya." "wâhyaw aspin; namôya ta-takosin." ||| “No,” said the woman; “No. He is far away; he will not be coming.”
âhci piko mâsihêw nâpêwa ôhi. ||| Still she lay with that man.

êkwa mitoni ê-môhcôwiyan, kâ-mihkwâsikêw!" "kinipin êkwa." "sôskwâc êkwa kinipahitin." ||| So you really are as crazy as all that, Red-Glow! This is the end of you. Without delay now I shall kill you.”
tâpwê piko otihtinêw; kipihkitonênêw. ||| And really he seized her; he began to choke her.

mistahi kakwê-kwâpatahwêw. ||| He beat her as if to knock the insides out of her.
êkosi isi piyis pônihêw. ||| Then at last he left her alone.
ê-wâpaniyik tâni mîna oka-isinâkosih! ||| When morning came, you would have wondered what she ever had looked like.
tâpiskôc askihk ohkwâkan. ||| Her face was like a kettle.

"nitawi-naskwahamâkê, kâ-mihkwâsikêw." ||| “Go join in the singing, Red-Glow.”
"mâka wîpac pê-kîwêhkan," itâw. ||| “But come home early,” he told her.

piyis nâpêw kisiwâsiw. ||| At last the man got angry.

pê-takopayiyiwa ôtê. ||| He rode up to where she was.

"namôya." "kiyâm postasâkê." ||| “No. Put on your blouse.”
êkwa nâpêw mâkwêyimôw. ||| Then the man began to be worried.

êkwa iskwêw âhkosiw mitoni. ||| Then the woman was very sick.

"wiya kiwîkimâkan; namôya niya." "kêtahtawê ê-tipiskâk, âsay ê-kawisimoyân, kâ-pê-koskonit, 'kiwî-nipahikonaw; sipwêhtêtân,' ê-isit." "nisêkimik." "tâpwê nimihtâtên, nisîm, ê-tôtamêk." "êkosi kika-osîmimitin." "nâtitisahohkok nitêmak," itêw otôskinîkîma. ||| “Truly I am sorry, Brother, at what you two have done. So now I shall have you as my younger brother. Go drive my horses hither,” he bade his followers.
wîpac pêtisahwêyiwa. ||| Quickly they drove them there.
nawasonêw ê-mîhkawikiyit nîso otêma; kîwêhtahêw. ||| He picked out two of his swiftest horses; he brought them to his tent.
êkwa otayiwinisa ê-mîkisiwiyiki, êkwa opâskisikan, opîhtatwâna miyêw. kiki nîso omîhkawikiwi-atimwa ôhi okosâka; mâka êkosi ê-otinât ê-osîmit. ||| Likewise of his beaded clothes, and a gun of his, and an ammunition-bag he gave to him, together with two swift horses, to his fellow-husband; thus, in spite of rivalry, he accepted him and made him his brother.
kîwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth went home.
"âta wiya namôya kinipahik!" itâw. ||| “So he did not kill you, after all?” he was asked.
êkwa wiya nêwo miyêw ostêsa masinasowi-atimwa. ||| Then he gave his elder brother four brindled horses.
êkwa mîna pêyak ayahciyiniw otôtamôwin, kîhyawêma kîpa êsa ê-kî-kwêskêyihtahk, anohc mistahi ê-kî-kisiwâsit. ||| This was another of the Blackfoot's ways, that he changed his mind exceedingly fast, when but now he had been very angry.
êwako mîna mitoni kayâs ê-kî-ihkihk tôtamôwin, ahpô awiya kâ-kitâpamâyit wîwiwâwa ayahciyiniwak, âsay ê-kî-âsitêyimâcik wîstawâw. ||| This too was a very old custom of theirs, that if anyone so much as looked at the Blackfoots' wives, at once they suspected him.
êwako pônipayiyiw; wîstawâw miywêyihtamwak awahkânisak, ê-pôni-kîskikotêcik. ||| This has stopped; the poor slaves are glad that their noses are no longer being out off.
kêsinâ mâna kî-wawiyasinâkosiwak. ||| They surely must have looked funny.
tânikâ kî-wâpamâyahkok; mistahi êtokê ka-pâhpinânaw. ||| I wish we could have seen them; we should have laughed a great deal.
êwako pêyak kêhcik kêkway ê-ihtakohk, isi-nôtiniskwêwêwin. ||| But this is a thing which no longer exists, this kind of fighting one's wife.
pêyak êwako ê-kîsi-âtocikâtêk otisi-iyinihkêwin. ||| This is one of their customs that people tell of.
nitâmisoyiwa owîkimâkana. ||| A man's wives gathered berries.
kâ-nakiskawâyit oskinîkiwa, nâpêsisa, êkwa kâ-âsitêyimât. ||| When they met a youth or even a boy, he became jealous of him.
"miyâmay kônâpêmin êwako oskinîkiw!" itêw. ||| “I can tell that youth is your man!” he said to her.
"namôya," itik; "konita ê-nakiskawak." ||| “No,” she answered him; “I only met him by chance.”
ohcitaw kônâpêmin," itêw. ||| You say that just because he is your man,” he told her.
acosisa tahkonam awa ayahciyiniw. ||| That Blackfoot took some arrows.
ê-nakiskawât owîkimâkana êkwa pêyak nâpêsisa ê-wîcêwâyit, nîkân owîkimâkana pa-pî-pimwêw. ||| When he encountered his wife and a boy who was with her, first he shot arrow after arrow into his wife.
êkwa nâpêsisa mîna, mîna êwakoni pimwêw; nipahêw. ||| Then the boy, too, him too he shot; he killed him.
êkwa oskinîkiwa nitonawêw; papâ-têhtapiw sakâhk. ||| Then he looked for the young man; he rode about in the woods.
êkwa, "êkây awiyak ta-otinêw ôhi kâ-nipahimak," itwêw. ||| Then, “No one is to take up the bodies of those I have killed,” he said.
owîkimâkana êkwa kotaka nâpêsisa, êwakoni mîna ê-nipahât, êkwa êkota pimisinwak, ohci ôhi awiya wî-otinâyici, ê-wî-nipahât. ||| His wife and the boy he had slain with her would lie there then, because if anyone were going to take them up, he would kill him.
êwako mîna pêyak ayahciyiniw otôtamôwin; maywês ihtakohk wiyasôwêwin êwako kâ-kî-ispayik; mêkwâc paskwâwi-mostoswa ê-ohtâpanihocik ayîsiyiniwak, ayahciyiniwak, mîna pwâsîmowak, sasîwak, kinêpikoyiniwak, kâ-otaskîwikamikowak, nahkawiyiniwak, êwako anima kâ-kî-ihkihk. ||| This too was a custom of the Blackfoot; before there was any law was when this took place; when the people were still living on buffalo-flesh, - the Blackfoot and the Assiniboine, the Sarsi, the Snakes, the Earth-Lodge People, the Salteaux, - that was when this took place.
aya pêyak âhcî ê-kî-sôniyâwokimâwit ôta nêhiyânâhk, êkwa pêyak âpihtawikosisân pôl kapinêt, êwako pîhtokêwak minihkwêwikamikohk. ||| A certain man named Archie, who was Indian Agent here in the Cree country, and a halfbreed, Paul Caplette, entered a tavern.
êkosi, "mitoni cî kinisitohtên nêhiyawêwin?" itêw awa kaplêt, sôniyâw-okimâw ê-itât. ||| Then, “Do you understand the Cree language very well this Caplette asked him, asked the Indian Agent.
"â, mitoni ninêhiyawân!" itik. ||| “Why, I speak Cree very well!” the other answered him.
"hâ, kîspin kinêhiyawân, kîspin mitoni kwayask kinisitohtên nêhiyawêwin, wanwêhkâtâni, kika-minahâwak ôta tahto kâ-ayâcik pîhcâyihk âpihtawikosisânak." "mâka kîspin êkâ wanwêhkâtâni, niya nika-minahiwân." "kêkway anima: 'ahpônâni kîwâc,' kêkway anima êwako?" ||| “Well then, if you speak Cree, if you understand the Cree language very well, then, if I speak so that you cannot understand me, you will treat to drinks as many halfbreeds as are in here. But if I do not put you at a loss by my speech, then I shall stand the drinks. What is this: 'With nary a fail,' what is this?”
êkosi, "â, konita ê-osîhtâyan, 'osâm ninihtâ-nêhiyawân,' ê-itêyihtaman!" itik awa kisêyiniw kaplêt. ||| Then, “Oh, you are just making it up, because you think you speak Cree so well!” said the other to old man Caplette.
"â, êkosi minahiwê!" itêw awa kaplêt. ||| “Ho, so now stand the drinks!” Caplette answered him.
êkosi awa sôniyâw-okimâw isiwêpinêw napakihtakohk niyânanwâpisk. ||| Thereupon the Indian Agent threw five dollars on the bar.
nânitaw niyânanosâp êkota pîhcâyihk ê-ayâyit, êkoni kahkiyaw ê-minahât, nayêstaw nikotwâsik sôniyâs ayiwâkipayiw anihi niyânanwâpisk. ||| As there were about fifteen men in the place, when he had treated them all, only six bits were left of that five dollars.
"hâ, namôya kîhtwâm ka-wanwêhkawin kêkway!" "êkoyikohk'nîsta ninêhiyawân,' nititêyihtên, konita kâ-wanihcikêyân." ||| “Well, you will never put me at a loss again: Because I thought 'I too speak Cree,' is why I lost my money for nothing.”
"ê-pîtosi-nêhiyawêyan, namôya mihcêtin nêhiyawêwin." "pêyak kêkway mihcêtwayak isiyîhkâtêw, mitoni ta-nisitohtamihk nêhiyawêwin." "'pêyak kêkway ninisitohtên,' kitêyihtên, pêyak kêkway pîkiskwêwin nêsitohtamani nêhiyawêwin." ||| “Because you talk a foreigner's Cree, the Cree language is poor and of small extent. But each thing has many names, when the Cree language is well understood. You think, 'I understand the name of one thing,' when really you understand only one word.”
êkosi mistahi pâhpiwak. ||| At that they laughed much.
ê-wîhtamâht ana osîkinikêw kêkway ohci kâ-minahiwêt awa, mistahi pâhpiw mîna êwako. êkosi kîsihtâwak êwako. ||| When the bartender was told why this man was standing treat, then he too had a hearty laugh So they finished this.
êkosi wayawîwak êkwa. ||| Then they went out of the place.
mînakôs isiyîhkâsôw otâcimowin kâ-wî-âtotamân. ||| Minakos is the name of him whose story I am going to tell.
mitâtaht nîsosâp nâpêwak wawêyîwak, ê-wî-nitopayicik, opwâsîmôwak, ayahciyiniwa ê-wî-nitopayîstawâcik. ||| Twelve men made ready to go on the war-path, Assiniboine, to make war on the Blackfoot.
wâhyaw ê-ihtâcik, kîtahtawê pêtisâpahtamwak ê-mâyi-kîsikâyik; sakamo pê-kitoyiwa, kâh-kitoyiwa piyêsiwa. ||| When they had gone a long way, at one time they saw a storm coming; unceasingly the Thunderers were coming with repeated noise.
êkwa kisiwâk ê-pê-mâyi-kîsikâyik, ocistikosiwak. ||| When the storm came near, they made a shelter.
apiwak, opâskisikaniwâwa ê-cimatâcik; êkwa akotâwak otakohpiwâwa; êkota pîhcâyihk ayâwak. ||| They stayed in one place, fixing their guns upright in the ground; over them they hung their blankets; they stayed underneath there.
asê-takosinomakaniyiw, yêkaw pisisik êkotowahk ohci kâ-kimiwaniyik. ||| It came backwards; a downpour of sand was the rain.
êkosi pasikôwak; sipwêhtêwak âsay mîna. ||| Then they arose; they set out again.
êkosi êkwa kotak mîna pêtisâpahtamwak. ||| Then they saw another thing coming.
âsay mîna nahapiwak. ||| Again they sat down.
takopayiyiw ê-mâyi-kîsikâyik. ||| The storm overtook them.
apisîs wâh-wâyawis nipiy pahkihtiniyiw, êkwa pisisik kinosêwa êkotôwahk ohci nayêstaw ê-kimiwahk. ||| A few scattered drops fell, for this was a rain of fishes and of nothing else.
ômayikohk êtokê ispapiwak, êkosi, pêyak misit. ||| So deep they lay on the ground, like this, a foot deep.
pasikôwak êkwa; sipwêhtêwak. ||| Then they arose; they went on.
kîtahtawê mostoswa wâpamêwak; osâm kayâs kâ-mîcisocik. ||| Presently they saw a buffalo; it was very long since they had eaten.
pêyak oskinîkiw: "nitawi-nipa; mîcisôhâhkahk nipahaci." ||| One youth was told, “Go kill it; let us eat, when you have killed it.”
nipahêw ê-pâskiswât; takohtahêw kahkiyaw êkota. ||| He killed it with a shot; he brought them to that place.
wiyanihtâkêwak, askêkin misiwê ê-otinahkik. ||| They skinned it, taking the hide entire.
êkwa pakocênêwak; êkwa otakisiya wayawîpitamwak. ||| Then they cut it open and drew out the entrails.
êkota itâmihk, ôtê otêhihk ana mostos, kî-pê-itiskwêpiw kisêyiniw, mitoni ê-wâpistikwâtit, ê-pêyakwaniyik oskîsik, ê-tapahtâskwêpit. ||| Inside there, by the heart of that buffalo there sat facing them an old man with white hair and only one eye, his head bowed forward.
"mâskôc namôya kwayask kiwî-ispayinânaw." "nama wîhkâc êkosi ihkin." ||| “Perhaps we shall not fare well. Never has such a thing happened.”
nakatêwak; namôya mowêwak. ||| They left it there; they did not eat it.
êkosi kîtahtawê mostoso-mêskanaw êkwa mitimêwak, kâ-ati-mâh-mîsiyit êsa mostoswa. ||| Then soon they followed the trail of the buffalo, where these had left their tracks.
kîtahtawê kîsitêyiw otêhi-wîhkwâhk pimiy. ||| Suddenly the fat in the heart-bladder grew hot.
êkosi sêkisiwak, osâm mâmaskâc ê-isi-wâpahtahkik. ||| They were frightened at seeing this astounding thing.
namôya otinamwak; nakatamwak. ||| They did not take it with them, but left it.
êkwa ê-mêkwâ-pimohtêcik kisâstêyiw; nôhtêyâpâkwêwak. ||| Then, as they marched along, the weather grew hot; they became thirsty.
nama kêkway nipiy kî-miskamwak. ||| They could not find any water.
êkwa atimwa pêyak wîcêwêwak, omaskisiniwâwa ê-otâpêyit; paskêpahtâw awa atim, ê-nôhtêyâpâkwêt. ||| They had a dog with them to carry their moccasins; this dog left the trail in its thirst.
kîtahtawê ê-itâpicik, kî-minihkwêyiwa. ||| Soon when they looked, it had drunk.
"yâ, minihkwêw atim; miskam nipiy." "kinôhtêyâpâkwâhtânaw!" "ispahtâ; nitawâpahta," itêw oskinîkiwa. ||| “Why, the dog has drunk; he has found water. Perhaps it is over with our thirst. Run down there; go and see,” the leader told a young man.
êkwa ispahtâw; atim ôta takopahtâw; kawipayiw êkota, ê-kawipêt. ||| He ran thither; the dog came running; it reeled over, falling from what it had drunk.
êkwa oskinîkiw têpwêw; "iskotêwâpoy!" itwêw. ||| The young man called out; “Whiskey!” he said.
êkwa kahkiyaw ispahtâwak. ||| Then all ran to the place.
êkwa ê-miyâhtahkik, tâpwê iskotêwâpoy. ||| When they smelled it, really it was whiskey.
namôya wî-minihkwêwak; kostamwak. ||| They would not drink; they were afraid of it.
"namôya wîhkâc êkosi ihkin." "mâskôc namôya kwayask kiwî-ispayinânaw." "kiyâm kîwêtân," itwêw kâ-nitopayiwinihkêt. ||| “Never has the like of this happened. Perhaps we shall not fare well. We had better go home,” said he who had made the war-party.
ana wiya atim kî-kawipêw: êwako piko ê-kî-minihkwêt, osâm ê-nôhtêyâpâkwêt. ||| As for the dog, it died of what it had drunk, it alone having drunk in its thirst.
kayâs kîtahtawê nêwo nêhiyawak sipwêhtêwak; mitoni mîhkawikiyiwa otêmiwâwa, ê-nitawi-kimoticik misatimwa. ||| Once upon a time, long ago, four Cree set out; their horses were very fleet, and they went to steal horses.
nama wiya kî-kimotiwak. ||| They did not succeed in stealing any.
kîtahtawê pêyak oskinîkiwa kîminatêwak. ||| Then at one time they attacked a young man from ambush.
êkosi êkwa maniswêwak ostikwâniyiw. ||| Then they scalped him.
êkosi tapasîwak; êkotê konita itê kâsôwak; kotakihk sipwêhtêwak. ||| Then they fled; they hid somewhere or other; they went off to another place.
tâpwê wâpahtamwak ê-mihcêtiniyiki mîkiwâhpa. ||| They saw a village of many tents.
êkosi êkota kimotiwak. ||| There, then, they stole.
ma-mitoni kâhcitinêwak misatimwa. ||| They managed to lay their hands on many horses.
êkosi ê-tipiskâk tapasîwak. ||| Then they fled in the night.
kapê-tipisk pimâmôwak. ||| All night long they rode in flight.
ê-wâpahk, ita kôh-kimoticik, kâwi êkota takosinwak. ||| At daybreak they arrived again at the place where they had stolen horses.
êkosi misatimwa wêpinêwak. ||| So they let the horses go.
sêmâk nawaswâtâwak, ayahciyiniwa ê-nawaswâtikocik. ||| At once they were pursued, by the Blackfoot they were pursued.
êkosi ê-mîhkawikiyit otêmiwâwa, êkosi nakasiwêwak. ||| But as their horses were fleet, they outdistanced their pursuers.
êkosi ê-kiskêyihtamiyit êkâ ta-kî-atimikocik, pônihikwak. ||| When the others knew that they could not overtake them, they quit them.
êkosi ati-ka-kîwêwak. ||| So they went on towards home.
mwêhci nêwâw ê-kî-nipâcik, kîkisêpâ minahôwak. ||| When they had been exactly four nights on the way, in the morning they killed game.
êkota nâh-nawacîwak. ||| There they prepared meat.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, sipwêhtêwak. ||| After their meal, they went on.
êkwa kisinâyiw, kêkâc ê-piponiyik, kêkâc. ||| It was cold, for it was nearly winter.
kîtahtawê wâpahtamwak mîkiwâhp. ||| Presently they came in sight of a tent.
ê-tipiskâk itohtêwak. ||| When night fell, they approached it.
êkota ê-takohtêcik, wâpamêwak misatimwa nîso, ê-nipahcikâsoyit. ||| When they reached it, they saw two horses that had been killed.
ê-wâpaniyik itohtêwak. ||| In the morning they went there.
pîkonamwak mîkiwâhp. ||| They broke open the tent.
ê-pîhtokêcik, ayîsiyiniwa pimisiniyiwa ê-nipiyit, ayahciyiniwa. ||| When they entered, there lay a man who had died, a Blackfoot.
otinêwak ê-tâpiskawâyit pîwâpiskominisa mihcêt, otakohpiyiwa mîna. ||| They took a great number of metal beads which he had as a necklace, and his blanket-robes.
mitoni mosêskatênêwak nâpêwa êsa. ||| They must have stripped the man completely.
êkosi isi sipwêhtêwak. ||| Thereupon they departed.
kîtahtawê wâhyaw ê-ayâcik, kâ-matwê-sâkowêyit. ||| Presently, when they were quite a ways, there he came a-whooping.
êkosi êkwa ê-âpasâpicik, wâpamêwak, ê-pê-nawaswâtikocik. ||| When they looked back, they saw him coming in pursuit of them.
êkosi êkwa tapasîwak; tahki kisiwâk askôkwak. ||| They fled; he kept close upon them.
piyisk nayawapiyiwa otêmiwâwa. ||| At last their horses went out of breath.
kîtahtawê têpwâtikwak, "pêtâk kâ-maskamiyêk!" ||| Then at one time he called to them: “Bring here what ye have robbed from me!”
âhci piko namôya wî-miyêwak. ||| Still they did not want to give him the things.
sôhki sôhki êkwa tapasîwak. ||| With all their might they fled.
kîtahtawê wêpinam otakohpiyiwa, pêyak ê-nayawapiyit otêma. ||| Presently one whose horse was winded threw away a blanket of the man's.
ê-âpasâpit, ê-pê-otihtamiyit, otinamiyiwa. ||| When he looked back, the other came up to it and took it.
âhci piko pê-pimitisahokwak. ||| Still he came chasing them.
êkoyikohk mitoni wî-atimik awa kâ-nayawapiyit otêma. ||| By this time he had almost overtaken the one whose horse was out of breath.
êkosi têpwâtêw owîcêwâkana. ||| So the latter called to his companions.
"wâh-wêpinamok anihi kâ-kî-otinamêk," itêw owîcêwâkana. ||| “Throw away all the things you took,” he cried to his companions.
tâpwê wâh-wêpinamiyiwa kahkiyaw. ||| Accordingly they threw away everything.
nayêstaw pîwâpiskominisa namôya wêpinêw pêyak, osâm ê-miywêyimât. ||| Only one did not throw away the metal beads, because he liked them too much.
êkosi ê-âpasâpit, kâ-wêpinahkik anihi ê-pê-otihtamiyit, otinamiyiwa. ||| When he looked back, the other reached the things they had thrown down and took them.
âhci piko pê-pimitisahokwak. ||| He still kept after them.
mitoni ê-wî-atimikocik, êkoyikohk oskinîkiw awa kâ-ayâwât pîwâpiskominisa kiskêyihtam ê-nayawapiyit otêma. ||| When he was very close upon them, the youth who had the metal beads perceived that his horse was out of breath.
kiskisopayiw; pîwâpiskominisa otinêw, ê-wêpinât. ||| He took thought; he laid hold of the metal beads and threw them down.
ê-otihtâyit matwê-sâkowêyiwa, "namôya misawâc takî-maskamiyêk niwawêsîhona!" ||| When the other reached them, he whooped aloud, “Not after all will ye be able to despoil me of my fineries!”
êkosi pônihikwak. êkosi kîwêyiwa. ||| Thereupon he quit them, and they returned home.
pêyak nikî-wâpamâw kisêyiniw; êwako ê-kî-âcimot kisêyiniw ômisi itwêw, "nika-âcimon," itwêw. ||| A certain old man whom I am old enough to have known, used to tell this story. “I shall tell of what I have seen,” he would say.
kîtahtawê pêyak nâpêw wî-sipwêhtêw, ê-wî-nitonawât ayahciyiniwa. ||| At one time a certain man was going to set out to look for Blackfoot.
niwîhtamâk( itwêw awa kisêyiniw). ||| He told me of his purpose (said this old man).
niwîcêwâw; ayinânêw nitihtasinân oskinîkiwak ê-nitopayiyahk. ||| I went along; eight was the number of us young men who went on the war-path.
kîtahtawê ê-pa-pimohtêyâhk, êkwa wâhyaw ê-ayâyâhk, kîtahtawê ê-apiyâhk, ê-pîhtwâyâhk, pêyak oskinîkiw ê-sipwêhtêt, ê-wî-sâkêwêt ispatinâhk, ê-wî-kakwê-wâpamât ayahciyiniwa, ê-nitawâhtât awa kâ-wî-nanâtawâpit ispatinâhk ohci, ê-itâpit, wâpamêw mostoswa nêwo. ||| Presently as we marched along, after we had gone a great distance, then once, as we sat smoking, a young man left camp to reach the crest of a hill, to look out for Blackfoot, and when this scout reconnoitred, as he looked yon way, he saw four buffalo.
owîcêwâkana wâwâstahamawêw. ||| He signaled to his companions.
êkosi pasikôwak, ê-itohtêcik ôhi oskinîkiwa. ||| Accordingly they rose to their feet and went to where that young man was.
ê-otihtâcik, "tânisi?" itêw. ||| When they reached him, “How is it?” the leader asked him.
"â, konita ôta ê-ayâcik mostoswak." ||| “Oh, merely that there are some buffalo here.”
"â, kakwê-nipahihkok," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Very well, try to kill them,” said that old man.
pêyak oskinîkiw sipwêhtêw ê-wî-pâskiswât, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahât. ||| A young man set out to shoot them.
êkwa ê-nâciyôstawât ê-apiyit, cîki ê-ihtât, kâ-wâpamât wâkayôsa ê-nâciyôstawâyit ôhi mostoswa. ||| Then, when he crept up to them and was crouching now quite near, he saw a bear stealing up to these buffalo.
êkosi pê-kîwêw awa oskinîkiw, ê-kostât ôhi wâkayôsa, ê-âcimostawât owîcêwâkana. ||| Thereupon the young man came back, afraid of the bear, and told his companions the story.
"wâkayôs nâciyôstawêw ôhi mostoswa," itêw owîcêwâkana. ||| “A bear is stealing up to these buffalo,” he told his com panions.
"mahti kitâpamâtân tânisi kê-tôtahk ôho wâkayôs," êkosi itwêwak. ||| “Let us go see how this bear will do,” they said.
tâpwê pasikôwak, ispatinâsihk ê-nahapicik, ê-kitâpamâcik. âsay cîki ayâw wâkayôs ôhi takwahinâwa. ||| So they arose and seated themselves on a small eminence of the ground to watch the animals.
kîtahtawê pasikôw awa takwahinâw pêyak, ê-ati-sipwêhtêt, ê-itohtêt ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| By this time the bear had got close to the bull buffalos.
pasikôw awa wâkayôs, ê-otihtikot ôhi takwahinâwa. ||| Suddenly one bull arose, left the others, and went up to the bear.
nôtinitôwak. namôya kinwês nôtinitôwak. ||| When the bull came near, the bear also rose.
mayaw ê-nipahiht kotak pasikôw. ||| Not long did they fight. The bull was killed.
mîna êwako ê-itohtêt ôhi ita kâ-nipahimiht. mîna êwako nôtinitôwak. kiyipa mîna êwako nipahik wâkayôsa. ||| As soon as it had been killed, another rose and went to where the first one had been killed.
kotak mîna pasikôw, ê-itohtêt, ê-wî-nôtinât wâkayôsa. ||| This one, too, fought with the bear. Soon it, also, was killed by the bear.
nôtinitôwak; mîna êwako nipahik. kotak awa pasikôw, ê-kisiwâsit. ||| Then another still rose up and encountered the bear and fought with it.
âsay mîna itohtêw ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| They fought; this one, too, the bear killed.
mîna êwako nôtinitôwak; nipahik. ||| Then the remaining one rose up, angry.
mêscihêw awa wâkayôs ê-nêwiyit takwahinâwa. ||| It, too, went up to the bear.
ita kâ-kî-apicik ôki takwahinâwak, êkota ohci pasikôw osk-âyîsis. ||| It, too, fought; the bear killed it. The bear killed all four of the bulls.
êwako êkota pâh-pimicipayiw, ê-kisiwâsit, ê-môskîstawât ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| Then from that place where those four bulls had been there arose a young buffalo.
kisiwâk ê-otihtât, êkota kawipayihôw. ||| It ran along angrily toward the bear, to attack it.
ê-pasikôt, ayîsiyiniw isinâkosiw, câpihcicikanis ê-tahkonahk. ||| [no translation] When it got up, it had the form of a man holding a lance.
êwako êwakoni kostêw awa wâkayôs. ||| The bear was afraid of this one.
ê-wî-tapasît, môskîstawêw awa ayîsiyiniw. ||| When it tried to escape, the man attacked it.
tahkamêw ôhi wâkayôsa; nipahêw. ||| He stabbed the bear and killed it.
êkosi êkwa kawipayihôw; ê-pasikôt, pôti êwako mostosis. ||| Then he flung himself on the ground; when he arose, there was again that young buffalo.
êkosi tapasîw awa mostosis; tâpwê piko nimitaw isi-tapasîw. ||| So the young buffalo ran away; it made for the open prairie.
êkosi êkwa ôki oskinîkiwak itohtêwak, ê-nitawâpamâcik ôhi mostoswa kâ-nipahimiht. ||| Thereupon the young men went to the place to look at the buffalos that had been killed.
ê-takohtêcik, ê-wâ-wâpamâcik, kahkiyaw awa wâkayôs ê-kaskikwênât, êkwa awa wâkayôs ospiskwanihk nôkwaniyiw êkota ê-tahkamikot ôhi mostosisa, tâpiskôc ayîsiyiniw ê-kî-tahkamât. ||| When they got there and examined them, it appeared that the bear had broken the necks of them all, and in the bear's back they could see the place where the buffalo-calf had stabbed it, exactly as though a man had made the wound.
êkwa êkota ôki oskinîkiwak wiyanihêwak. ||| Then the young men skinned them and cut them up.
"ka-mîcisonânaw," êkosi itwêwak. ||| “We shall eat,” they said.
tâpwê kotawêwak, ê-nawacîcik, ê-mîcisocik. ||| Accordingly they built fires to prepare parched meat and to eat.
êkwa awa kisêyiniw ômisi itwêw: "oskinîkîtik, kayâs nôhcîn;" "nama wîhkâc ômisi nitisi-wâpahtên." "mêskoc namôya kiwî-miyopayinânaw;" "mâskôc kika-nipahikonawak ayahciyiniwak." "kiyâm kîwêtân." "ka-miywâsin kîwêyahko," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| Then the old man spoke as follows: “Youths, I am an old man; never have I seen anything like this. Perhaps we shall not fare well; perhaps the Blackfoot will slay us. We had better go back. It will be better if we go home,” said the old man.
"ahaq," itwêwak oskinîkiwak. ||| “Very well,” said the young men.
êkota pêyak tipiskâw ayâwak. ||| They stayed there one night.
ê-wâpahk, sipwêhtêwak, ê-kîwêcik. ||| In the morning they set out for home.
piyisk takosinwak wîkiwâhk. ||| At last they reached their camp.
"êwako ohci kâ-ôh-pê-kîwêyâhk, 'mâskôc namôya nika-miyopayinân,' ê-itêyihtamâhk, ê-isi-wâpahtamân, kâ-ôh-pê-kîwêyân." ||| “That is why we have come home, 'Perhaps we shall not fare well,' was our thought, so it seemed to me; that is why I turned back.”
êkosi êwako âcimowin. ||| So much for this story.
nîsôtêwi-mostos, êwako ê-wâpahtahk ôma âcimowin; niya nisis êwako kisêyiniw. ||| Twin-Buffalo, he is the one who had this experience; my mother's brother was this old man.
êkwa kotak nâpêw mâmaskâc êsa kî-miywêyihtam ê-mihkosihot. ||| Now, there was another man, the story goes, who greatly liked to wear red clothes.
pêyakwâw ê-wawêsît, mihkosiyiwa opakwahtêhona; êkwa asikanêyâpiy opîhtasinânêyâpîw; êkwa mihkwêkinwêtâsa kikitâsêw; êkwa mihkokwana otastotinihk itamoyiwa. ||| Once when he dressed up, his belt was red, and red yarn he had for his ammunition-bag; he wore red flannel breeches; a red feather was on his hat.
êkwa nisto-pipon isiyîhkâtêwa kayâs ayîsiyiniwak ê-kî-wiyâhtâcik; êkotôwa mîna ê-kikiskahk ê-mâcît. ||| And 'three-year' were called some things which the old-time people wore; one of these also he had on, as he hunted.
êkwa itê nipahêw pêyak mostoswak; wiyanihêw. ||| Then over there he killed a buffalo; he set about skinning and cutting it up.
mêkwâc ê-wiyanihât, kêtahtawê ê-tasot, pôti ôhi ôta kâ-nîpawiyit ayîsiyiniwa, nîpiminâna ê-tahkonamiyit, namôya ê-nîpîwiyiki. ||| While he was cleaning it, at one time, as he straightened up, there stood a man holding some cranberries without leaves.
namôya wî-otinam; kostêw, pêyak piko oskîsikoyiw oskahtikoyihk ê-oskîsikoyit. ||| He did not want to take them; he feared him, for he had only one eye, on his forehead.
tâpiskôc kâ-wâwiyêyâki êkoyikohk êspîhcâyik oskîsikoyiw; êwako ohci kâ-ôh-kostât. ||| Like a round dish, so big was that man's eye; that was why he feared him.
mêkwâc ê-pimâmot, kêtahtawê kâ-otihtât ominahôwina; pôti ôhi kêyâpic êkota kî-nîpawiyiwa. ||| As he fled, lo, he came again to the game he had killed, and there was that person standing again.
kêtahtawê mîna kâwi êkota kâ-takopahtât. ||| Soon again he came running to that place.
nêwâw ê-takopahtât êkota, êkwa namôya kiskisiw. ||| When he had ran into that place four times, he fainted.
kêtahtawê ê-wâpaniyik, kîkisêpâ kiskisiw, kêkâc ê-nipit, ê-kipitonêhpisot opîhtaskatêwâna. ||| When day broke, he came to his senses, almost dead, his mouth tied shut with the thongs of his powder-horn.
mostâpêkasêw mitoni; nama kêkway kikiskam. ||| He was all naked; he had not a thing on his body.
ê-takosihk kîsitêpowân. ||| When he arrived, a ceremonial meal was prepared for him.
kî-âcimot ê-isi-wâpahtahk, "mahti niya nika-otinên," itwêyiwa kotak ayîsiyiniwa. ||| When he had told his experience, “Why, I should have taken them,” said the other people.
êkwa âtiht, "sâkôtêyimik êkâ tita-otinahk," itwêwak âtiht ayîsiyiniwak. ||| And some, “That person frightened him out of taking them,” said some people.
êkosi wiya êwako ê-itâcimohk. ||| That is the way this is told.
kêtahtawê êsa êkwa iskwêw awa nihtâ-nôcihcikêyiwa onâpêma. ||| Once upon a time, the story goes, there was a woman whose husband was a great hunter.
kêtahtawê onitopayiwa mawîhkâtik iskwêw. ||| Once a war-party asked her for help.
miyik wêpinâsona ta-kosâpahtahk; otinam. ||| They gave her cloth-goods that she might use the medium's tent; she accepted the gift.
ospwâkana miyik ê-saskahamâkot. ||| They gave her a pipe with a ceremonial offering of tobacco.
"mihcêt misatimwak ka-otinâwâwak," itêw. ||| “You will take many horses,” she told them.
êkwa iskwêw wîsâmâw ta-wîcihiwêt. ||| The woman was invited to go along.
êkwa sakâhk pimipiciw. ||| She camped from place to place in the woods.
piyis nama kêkway mîciwak. ||| At last they had nothing to eat.
nîso otawâsimisa êkwa osîma pêyak êkwa onâpêma êkwa wiya; niyânaniwak. ||| Her two children, her younger sister, her husband, and she; there were five of them.
nama kêkway mîciwak. ||| They had nothing to eat.
kêkâc nipahâhkatosôwak. ||| They were nearly dead of hunger.
kêtahtawê iskwêw awa onâpêma môwêw. ||| Then that woman ate her husband.
êkwa êkota ayâw; piyisk kitamwêw. ||| She stayed there; in time she ate his entire body.
otawâsimisa mîna pêyak kitamwêw; piyis mîna kotaka. ||| Then she ate up one of her children; then the other.
osîma piko iskwamêw. ||| Her sister alone she spared.
êkwa osîma wâposwa piko ê-môwâyit, mistahi piko êkwa micihcîsa iskwastam. ||| Her sister ate only rabbits and left only the fore and hind paws uneaten.
êkwa ê-sipwêhtêt, wîcêwêw osîma, ê-sipwêhtêcik, kotaka ayîsiyiniwa ê-nitonawât, ê-wî-môwât. ||| Then the woman went from there, with her sister she went from there, to seek other people whom she might eat.
nitawi-takosin ôhtâwiya okâwiya ostêsa ita ê-ayâyit. ||| She headed for the place where her father and mother and older brothers were staying.
kêtahtawê kiskêyihtam ayîsiyiniwa kisiwâk ê-ayâyit. ||| Presently she knew that some person was near.
"ka-kakwêcimik," itêw osîma, "'awîna kâ-mîcisot?' kika-itik." "'wiya awa nisîm,' kika-ititin." "'cî?' ititâni, "êha," kika-itwân." "êkây êkosi wî-itwêyini, ka-nipahitin." ||| “He will ask you,” she told her sister, “'Who has been eating here?' he will ask you. 'Why, my sister here,' I will say of you. When I ask you, 'Isn't that so?' you will answer, 'Yes.' If you do not speak thus, I will kill you.”
"êha," itwêw iskwêw; "êkosi nika-itwân," itwêw. ||| “Yes,” said she; “I shall speak thus.”
êkwa pêhôwak maskwamiyihk. ||| Then they waited on the ice.
kêtahtawê kâ-pêtisâpamâcik wîcimosa. ||| Presently they saw her sweet-heart coming.
"awîna kâ-mîcisot?" itikwak. ||| “Who has been eating here?” he asked them.
"wiya awa nisîm," itwêw iskwêw awa. ||| “Why, my sister here,” said that woman.
"cî," itêw, "nisîm?" ||| “Isn't that so, Sister?” she asked the other.
"mahti mâka," itêw awa nâpêw wîcimosa, "kêkway kâ-nîmâyêk?" itêw. ||| “But let me see, then,” said that man to his sweetheart, “what supplies are you carrying?”
kêkway natonamwêw: pôti ôma awa omisimâw ayîsiyiniw micihciya nîmâw, êkwa kotak wâposwa. ||| He looked to see what they had: behold, the older sister had a store of human hands, the younger of rabbit's paws.
"kiya kika-nipahitin," itêw; "kitawâsimisak êkwa kiwîkimâkan kikitamwâwak." "kinisiwanâtahkamikisin." ||| “As for you, I shall kill you,” he said to her; “You have eaten up your children and your husband. You are a horrible being.”
êkwa kîwêhtahêw; takohtahêw wîkiwâhk. ||| He took the women home with him; he brought them to his lodge.
êkwa tihkisamwak wâkayôsi-pimiy. ||| Then they melted bear's-grease.
êwako êkwa pâh-pâkomohêwak. ||| In this way they made her vomit repeatedly.
mistahi kapê-ayi pâkomohêwak. ||| They kept her vomiting for a long time.
kêtahtawê kâ-pâpayihâyit miskwamiya. ||| Presently she threw up some ice.
êkwa âpahkawisiyiwa. ||| Then she came back to her natural self.
êkwa iskwêw ê-kiskisit ômisi itwêw: "nitawâsimisak nikitamwâwak mîna niwîkimâkan." "êkosi êkwa nipakwâtên;" "kiyâm nipahik," itwêw. ||| When she regained her memory, she spoke thus: “I have eaten my children and my husband. I cannot bear it; please slay me,” she said.
"âhci piko êkâ nipahiyêko nika-mêscihtân ôtênaw." "nama awiyak nika-sâkôcihik." ||| “In spite of everything, if you do not slay me, I shall destroy everyone in the village. No one will overcome me.”
piyis êkwa, "êha," itâw. ||| At last, “Very well,” she was told.
ê-ati-mêstihkasot nitonikâniwiw. ||| When in time she had burned up, a search was made.
êkwa miskawâw êkota asinîs ê-miyosit. ||| There a beautiful little stone was found.
êkwa êwako wâtihk nitawi-asiwahâw. ||| Then they went and placed it in a pit.
êkosi isi piciwak ayîsiyiniwak; nakatamwak. ||| Thereupon the people moved camp; they left it behind.
kîhtwâm ê-nîpihk pê-ispiciwak; takopiciwak êkota. ||| The next summer they came there again to camp; the band arrived there.
êkwa pimihkân osîhtâwak ê-wîhkohtocik. ||| They made pemican and held a feast.
êkwa nitawâpahtamwak; pôti ôma êkota wâtihk ohci tapasîyiwa wâkayôsa. ||| Then they went to look at the thing; lo, there from out the pit fled a bear.
êwako awa iskwêw kâ-kî-nipahiht, ê-kwêskimot. ||| This was none other than the woman who had been slain; she had changed to this form.
êsa mîna sipwêhtêpayiw ê-pêyakot, ê-nêpêwimikot oskinîkiskwêwa, ê-wî-kakwê-isîhkawât, "osâm tâpwê wiya êkâ êhtakohk kâ-ocikihkwêyan, ka-nôcîhkawin," ê-itikot. ||| Another young man went off alone, because a young woman had taunted him to shame when he paid court to her, saying to him, “Truly, if it were not that you are pock-marked on your face, you might woo me with success.”
êkwa sipwêtatwêmôw, tahki nayêstaw ê-mâtot. ||| At that he went off weeping, and wept off alone all the time.
êkwa kêtahtawê kâ-miskawât ayîsiyiniwa. ||| Then presently he found some people.
"tânêhki ôma kâ-ôh-mâtoyan?" ||| “Why are you weeping like this?”
"ê-nêpêwimit iskwêw, 'tâpwê wiya êkâ ihtakohk kâ-ocikihkwêyan, ka-isîhkawin,' ê-isit." ||| “Because a woman has taunted me to shame, saying to me, 'Truly, if it were not that you are pock-marked in your face, you might woo me.'”
"hâw, nôsisê, mahti êyiwêhk nika-kotêyihtên." ||| “Why, grandchild, let me at any rate see what I can do for this.”
êkwa tihkisam pimiy, wâkayôsi-pimiy; wiyâkanihk astâw. ||| Then he melted some fat, bear's-grease; he put it in a bowl.
êkwa tahkopitam maskosiya. ||| Then he tied up some herbs.
"hâw, êkwa matotisitân!" itêw. ||| “Come, now let us take a sweat-bath!” he told him.
êkwa kêtayôwinisêw oskinîkiw. ||| Then the youth took off his clothes.
pîhtokêwak êkwa matotisânihk, pimiy mîna ôma, masko-pimiy. ||| Then they entered the sweat-lodge, with that fat, that bear's-grease.
akwanahamwân omatotisâniwâw. ||| Their companions covered their sweatlodge for them.
êkwa êkosi ê-sîkahasiniyêt kisêyiniw, ê-pôh-pôtâtât oskinîkiwa, piyis namôya ta-ihtakoniyiw ôma kâ-ocikisiyit. ||| Thereupon, when the old man poured the fat on the stone, and kept blowing on the youth, at last the pock-marks on his face began to disappear.
piyis ê-mêstinahk pimiy ôma, mîna kîhtwâm pîhtokatâwân. ||| When he had used up that fat, some more was handed in to them.
êwako ê-mêstinahk, âsay nama kêkway ihtakoniyiw ocikisiwin. ||| When he had used this up, his pock-marks were gone.
êkwa ê-pâskît, namôya kakêtihk ta-kahkâpêwiw oskinîkiw. ||| And when he opened the lodge, whole and without flaw in body was the youth.
"êkwa ka-kîwân, nôsisê," itik ôhi kâ-kî-nitawihikot; "êkwa sipwêhtê; iskwêw ana kâ-kî-kîhkâmisk ka-nahâpason, wî-pê-itohtêci kisiwâk," itik omosôma. ||| “Now you will go home, my grandchild,” he was told by him who had doctored him; “Now depart; your sense of smell will tell you when that woman who insulted you is coming near,” his grandfather told him.
kiskinôhamâk ta-ispinêmât. ||| He taught him how to scold her.
"wahwâ!" itwêwak ayîsiyiniwak; "mistahi miyosiw oskinîkiw kâ-kî-sipwêhtêt." ||| “Dear me!” said the people; “Very handsome is the young man who went away.”
êkwa awa iskwêw kâ-kî-pakwâtât maskisinihkêsiw, ê-wî-nitawi-miyât. ||| Then the woman who had scorned him made some moccasins to give him.
êkwa ê-kîsihtât, itohtêw. ||| When she had finished them, she went there.
kêswân oskinîkiw wayawîw; wâpamêw. ||| Just then the youth was going out of his tent; he saw her.
pê-âkwâskâk iskwêwa. ||| The woman came to head him off.
"nah ôhi êyiwêhk," itik. ||| “Here is a little present for you,” she said to him.
otinam; kwâhciwêpinam. ||| He took them and flung them aside.
"hêy, nika-wî-nipin," itwêw iskwêw awa. ||| “Oh dear, I wish I were dead,” said the woman.
"namôya niya êkosi nôh-itwân, ê-kîhkâmiyan," itêw oskinîkiw. ||| “I did not say anything like that when you insulted me,” the youth told her.
êkwa kîwêw awa oskinîkiskwêw; nêpêwisiw. ||| Then the young woman went home; she was ashamed.
têpiskâyiki nitawâpamêw. ||| Of a night she would go to see him.
"pê-wîhcêkan," itwêyiwa, kisiwâk êtohtêci. ||| “A nasty smell is coming this way,” he would say whenever she came near.
nama nânitaw isi kî-wâpamêw oskinîkiwa. ||| She was not able to have any converse with the youth.
mîna êwako otâcimôwiniwâw ayahciyiniwak, ê-kî-mamâhtâwisicik kayâs ayahciyiniwak, mêkwâc paskwâwi-mostoso-wiyâs ê-mîcicik. ||| This too is a Blackfoot story, of how the Blackfoot of old had mystic power, when they used to eat buffalo-meat.
êyakonik otôtamôwiniwâw mîna ayahciyiniwak kâ-kîsihtâyân. ||| That of which I have just finished telling is another custom of the Blackfoot.
mâmaskâc kîpa êkâ ê-ihtakoniyik ocikihkwêwin. ||| It is wonderful that in a short time the pock-marks disappeared from his face.
wiya êwako nikîsihtân âcimôwin. ||| So now I have finished this story.
kîtahtawê iskwêw otawâsimisa wîcêwêw, ê-nâtahkik mînisa. ||| Once a woman went with her children to get berries.
sîpîhk êkota ê-âpahwâcik misatimwa; êkota ê-wî-kapêsicik. ||| At the river they unharnessed their horses, planning to camp there.
êkosi êkwa sipwêhtêwak, ê-pimohtêcik, mînisa ê-wî-otinahkik. ||| Then they went from there, on foot, to take berries.
ê-wâpahtahk awa iskwêw mînisa, êkota otinam. ||| Where the woman saw berries, she took them.
kotaka wâpahtam; êkotê itohtêw. ||| She saw some more; she went there.
kîtahtawê kêkway kâ-wâpahtahk, ostikwâniyiw ê-wâpahtamwât. ||| Suddenly she saw something; she saw some creature's head.
"misi-kinêpik!" itêyihtam. ||| “A great serpent!” she thought.
otinêw asiniya ê-pakamahwât, ê-nipahât. ||| She took a stone and struck it so as to kill it.
êkosi mistik otinam, ê-itohtêt ê-pakamahwât; nipahêw, kâ-wâpamât tâwayihk oskahtikoyihk otêskana ê-kikamoyit, ê-pêyakoyit. ||| Then she took a stick and went up to it and beat it; she killed it; and then she saw that in the middle of its forehead it had a single horn.
êkwa ê-otihciyit kinêpikwa, tâpiskôc sôniyâw ostikwân êsinâkwaniyik. ||| And the serpent's head looked like bright metal.
namôya wâpamêw tâni iyikohk ê-iskosiyit ôhi kinêpikwa kâ-nipahât. ||| She could not see how long this serpent was which she had killed.
mitoni ê-sôhkêyimot awa iskwêw, kâ-nipahât ôhi kinêpikwa. ||| Very brave was this woman, to have slain that serpent.
êkosi sipwêhtêw, ê-âmaciwêt. ||| So she went from there, up the bank.
êkota kâ-wâpahtahk ê-misâyik wâti. ||| There she saw a great cave.
"mâskôc êwako awa kinêpik wîki," itêyihtam. ||| “No doubt the lair of that serpent,” she thought.
êkosi sipwêhtêw, ê-itohtêt otawâsimisa, ê-âcimostawât ê-nipahât. ||| Then she went from there to where her children were, and told them of how she had killed it.
êkosi ôki oskinîkiskwêwak namôya wî-wâpamêwak, ê-kostâcik. ||| Then those young women did not care to see it, for they were afraid of it.
êkosi êkoyikohk êwako âcimowin. ||| That is the end of this story.
ôtê sîpîhk ayâwak nêhiyawak. ||| By yonder river some Cree were staying.
kîtahtawê manêsiwak cistêmâwa mîna kaskitêw mîna kaskitêw mîna môsasiniya. ||| Then at one time they ran short of tobacco and gunpowder and bullets.
nîso nâpêwak,- ômisi isiyîhkâsôw awa nâpêw: kaskitêwi-maskwa isiyîhkâsôw; kotak nâpêw kwâskwintôwân isiyîhkâsôw; ê-ociwâmihtocik, awa kwâskwintôwân osîmimâw,- êwakonik sipwêhtêwak, pahkêkinwa ê-pimiwitâcik. ||| Two men, - this was the one man's name: Black-Bear was his name; the other man was called Toss-Aloft; they were brothers, and Toss-Aloft was the younger, -- they started out, taking along some hides.
pêyak piko misatimwa wîcêwêwak, ê-nayahtamiyit pahkêkinwa mîna omaskisiniwâwa, ê-mostohtêcik. ||| They took only one horse, which carried the hides and their moccasins, and they walked.
ê-otihtahkik sîpiy, âsowahamwak. ||| When they came to the river, they forded it.
pakâsimôw awa ostêsimâw kaskitêwi-maskwa, ê-sakâpêkinât misatimwa nipîhk, osoyihk ê-tahkopitahk mihtos, êkota ê-micimît kwâskwintôwân, ê-âsowahahkik. ||| The older one, Black-Bear, went into the water, leading the horse by the bridle; at its tail he had tied a raft, to which Toss-Aloft held fast as they crossed.
pihkohôwak, ê-kapâcik. ||| They came to the other side and went ashore.
ê-kî-wîwahâcik otêmiwâwa, êkwa sipwêhtêwak, ê-pimohtêcik. ||| When they had re-loaded their horse, they set out again, walking.
nîswâw ê-nipâcik, takohtêwak wâskahikanihk, nisto-kîsikâw ê-pimohtêcik. ||| After two nights on the way, they reached the post, having tramped three days.
êkosi okimâwa wâpamêwak, ê-itâcik, "cistêmâw, êkwa kaskitêw, môsw-asiniya, êkwa cahkisêhikana ê-pê-nâtamâhk, ê-manêsiyâhk," itêwak. ||| So then they saw the trader and told him, “Tobacco and gunpowder and bullets and flints we have come to get, for we have run short,” they told him.
"êha," itikwak, ê-miyikocik cistêmâwa, konita ê-miyikocik, namôya ê-atâmâcik. ||| “Very well,” he told them, and gave them tobacco, as a present, not as part of their purchase.
êkosi êkwa kotaka miyikwak cistêmâwa, kaskitêw, môsw-asiniya, cahkisêhikana, papakiwayânasâkaya, mîna mihkwêkin, mîna kaskitêwêkin, môhkomâna, oyamana, wâpamona. ||| Then, besides, he gave them other tobacco, powder, bullets, flints, shirts, and red flannel and black broadcloth and knives, paint, and mirrors.
ôhi ohci opahkêkinomiwâw ohci mistahi miyikwak. ||| For their hides he gave them many things.
nîso-tipiskâw ê-kî-ayâcik, kî-sipwêhtêwak, ê-pê-kîwêcik, ê-nayahcikêyit otêmiwâwa pêyak. ||| When they had been there over two nights, they left to come home, their one horse carrying the load.
nîswâw ê-kî-nipâcik, otihtamwak ita kâ-kî-ohci-âsowahahkik. ||| When they had slept twice on the way, they reached the place where they had forded on their journey out.
têpâpahtamwak wîkiwâwa ita kâ-kî-ohci-pê-sipwêhtêcik. ||| They were in sight of their camp from which they had gone on their journey.
êkwa êkota sisonê sîpîhk ayâwak, ê-âpahwâcik ôhi otêmiwâwa, pita ê-mîcisocik. ||| Then they stopped there by the bank of the river, unharnessing their horse and eating a meal before they went on.
êkwa ê-kî-mîcisocik, osîhtâwak mihtos, êkota ê-astâcik ôhi kâ-pêtâcik. ||| Then, when they had eaten, they built a raft, on which they placed the things they had brought with them.
êkwa otêmiwâwa osoyiyihk tahkopitam ôma mihtos. ||| Then the one tied the raft at the horse's tail.
"hâw, êkwa, nisîm!" itwêw awa ostêsimâw. ||| “There, Brother!” said the elder.
namôya wî-pahkopêw awa osîmimâw. ||| The younger could not make up his mind to go into the water.
piyisk otinam awa ostêsimâw mihkwêkinos. ||| At last the elder brother took a piece of red cloth.
êkwa mistikosa kîskataham, ê-mâh-masinahahk. ||| Then he cut off some twigs, and marked them.
êkosi awa kwâskwênitôwân ê-miyiht, otinam; pakastawêham sîpîhk. ||| When Toss-Aloft was given this, he accepted it; he threw it into the river.
"hâw, êkwa, nisîm!" itwêw kaskitêwi-maskwa, ê-pahkopêt, ê-pakâsimot. ||| “So, there now, come, Brother!” said Black-Bear, wading into the water.
êkwa awa osîmimâw micimîw mihtotihk. ||| Then the younger brother held on to the raft.
kêkâc tâwakâm apisîs ê-miyâskahk, kîtahtawê awa ostêsimâw itâmihk nipîhk kêkway kâ-miskonahk. ||| When he had got a bit past the middle of the stream, the elder brother suddenly felt something under the water.
kiskêyihtam: maci-pisiskiwa. ||| He knew what it was: an evil beast.
êkota nakâsin awa misatim, ê-tâwikiskawât ôhi itâmihk nipîhk kâ-ayâyit. ||| There the horse stood still, as it struck with its foot the creature that was under the water.
namôya wâpamêwak; piyisk awa nâpêw êkotê ispayihôw, ositihk ohci ê-wî-kakwê-miskawât ôhi itâmihk kâ-ayâyit. ||| They could not see it; at last that man bent over that way, trying to find with his foot the creature that was below.
ê-miskoskawât, êkota nakêstiw, ê-ocipitât ôhi otêma. ||| When he had found it with his foot, he stood still and drew the horse toward him.
êkosi ati-sipwêhtêw. ||| So then he started to go on.
awa osîmimâw nâway kâ-ayâ-t, ê-miskoskawât, sêkisiw. ||| When the younger brother, who was in the rear, felt the creature with his foot, he grew frightened.
ômisi itwêw: "nistêsê, nistêsê!" itwêw. ||| “Brother, Brother!” he cried.
"êkâ wiya nânitaw itwê!" itwêw awa ostêsimâw; "kinâpêwin, nisîm!" itêw. ||| “Do not say a word!” said the elder; “You are a man, Brother!” he told him.
êkosi kêkâc ê-kapâcik, kîtahtawê êkotê ispayiwak, tâpiskôc ê-ocipitikocik ôhi kâ-kî-miskoskawâcik. ||| But then, when they had almost reached the shore, suddenly they moved in the other direction, exactly as if they were being pulled back by the creature they had stepped upon.
âsay mîna awa osîmimâw, "nistêsê, nistêsê!" itwêw. ||| Again the younger brother cried, “Brother, Brother!”
"êkâ nânitaw itwê, nisîm!" itwêw awa ostêsimâw, âhci piko ê-yâhyânahk awa ostêsimâw. ||| “Do not say a word, Brother!” said the older one, swimming against the pull.
âsay mîna kiskêyihtam ê-asêpayit. ||| Again he perceived that he was moving backwards.
âsay mîna osîma ma-mawimoyiwa, "nistêsê, nistêsê!" ê-itwêt. ||| Again his brother entreated, crying, “Brother, Brother!”
ê-kitâpamât osîma, kâ-wâpamât misi-kinêpikwa ê-môskipêyit. ||| When he looked at his brother, he saw a Great Serpent emerge from the water.
ômisi itwêw awa ostêsimâw: "hahâw, nimosô, piyêsiw, 'kîspin kêkway sêkihikoyani, kisiwâk kika-osâpamitin,' kikî-itwân; êwako ohci nama kêkway kâ-ôh-kostamân," itwêw awa ostêsimâw. ||| Thus spoke the elder brother: “Now then, 0 my grandfather, Thunderer, 'If by anything you should be frightened, from close by I shall be looking at you,' you said; that is why I fear nothing,” said the elder brother.
kiyipa âsay pêhtawêw piyêsiwa, ê-kitoyit. ||| In a moment he heard a Thunderer roaring.
âta ê-âhkamêyimot ê-yâhyânahk, piyisk pahpahkipêstâyiw, ê-wî-kimiwaniyik; mâka tahki kitoyiwa piyêsiwa. ||| When nevertheless he swam with all his might, soon there fell scattered drops of a coming rain; meanwhile unceasingly roared the Thunderer.
kîtahtawê mistahi pêhtâkosiyiwa. ||| Presently he made a great noise.
tâpiskôc ê-matwêwêyik itihtam; aspin êkwa nama kiskêyihtam. ||| The man heard it like the report of a cannon; that was the last he knew.
kîtahtawê iyikohk ê-kiskêyihtahk, pôti pâhkwahcâhk kâ-pimisihk awa ostêsimâw. ||| After a time, when he came to his senses, there lay that elder brother on the dry land.
êkwa ê-nanâtawâpit, namôya wâpamêw osîma, mîna otêma, mîna ôhi kâ-kî-wâpamât misi-kinêpikwa. ||| When he looked about him, he did not see his brother, or the horse, or the Great Serpent which he had seen.
"mâskôc môwik nisîm," itêyihtam. ||| “Perhaps it has eaten my brother,” he thought.
ê-pasikôt, ê-âmaciwêt, kâ-wâpamât osîma, tahkohcâyihk ê-papâmitâcimoyit osîma. ||| When he rose to his feet and walked up the slope, there he saw his brother, crawling about at the top of the bluff.
êkotê kâ-wâpamât otêma ê-ma-mîcisoyit, kêyâpic osoyiyihk ê-tahkopitêyik ôma mihtos. ||| And there he saw his horse grazing, with the raft still tied at its tail.
"hay hay!" itwêw; "pimâtisiw nisîm!" ê-itwêt. ||| “Splendid!” he cried; “My brother is alive!”
ê-otihtât, pasikôyiwa osîma. ||| When he came up to him, his brother arose.
ê-ati-itohtêcik otêmiwâwa, ê-otihtâcik, âpihkonamwak ôma osoyiyihk kâ-tahkopitêyik. ||| Then they went on to where their horse was, and, when they got to it, untied the thing that was tied to its tail.
êkwa ôhi kâ-kî-pôsihtâcik êwakoni ê-wâpahtahkik, nama kêkway wanihtâwak. ||| When they looked at the things that they had loaded on there, they missed nothing.
êkosi namôya kiskêyihtam kîkwaya ê-kapâwêpinikocik; ayisk namôya wâpamêw awiya kâ-tôtâkocik. ||| And so he did not know by what sort of being they had been thrown ashore; for he had not seen anyone do that to them.
êkosi wawêyîwak, ê-wiyahpitâcik otêmiwâwa, ê-nayahtahâcik ôhi kâ-pêtâcik, ê-ati-kîwêcik. ||| So they made ready, harnessing their horse and loading it with the things they had brought, and went on towards home.
kisiwâk ê-ihtâcik, ômisi itwêw awa ostêsimâw: "nisîm, niya nika-âcimon ôma kâ-isi-wâpahtamahk, kâ-isi-kiskêyihtamahk tânisi ê-ispayiyahk," itwêw awa ostêsimâw; "kika-nitohtawin, ita kiyâskiyâni ayiwâkês wî-itâcimoyâni," itwêw. ||| When they were near, the elder brother said: “Brother, I shall tell of what we have seen, of the experience we have gone through,” said the elder one; “You will hear me, if at any point I try to lie or exaggerate,” said he.
"ahaq," itwêw awa osîmimâw. ||| “Very well,” said the younger.
piyisk takohtêwak wîkiwâhk. ||| At last they came to their camp.
êkwa ê-kî-pîhtokêcik, êkwa nitomêw nâpêwa, ê-pîhtokêt, ê-mâh-miyât cistêmâwa, "hâw, kîstawâw ta-pîhtwâyêk!" ê-itât. ||| Then when they had entered, he called the men, and as they entered, gave each of them tobacco, saying to them “There, that you too smoke!”
"pêskis ê-wî-âcimostâtakok tânisi ispayiyâhk awa nisîm ôta sîpîhk," itwêw. ||| It is because at the same time I wish to tell you how my brother here and I fared by this river,” he said.
"ahaq," itik ôhi ayîsiyiniwa. ||| “Very well,” said those people to him.
êkwa âcimôw ôma êkâ kâ-wî-pahkopêyit osîma, piyisk anihi kâ-miyât osîma; êwako âcimôw. ||| Then he told how his brother had been unwilling to wade in and how he had at last given his brother those objects; he told of that.
piyisk kâ-pahkopêcik, tânisi kâ-isi-kiskêyihtahkik, êwako âcimôw, piyisk êkâ ê-kiskêyihtahk, pâhkwahcâhk ê-ayâcik. ||| He told of what they had perceived when they finally went into the water, and of how in the end he had lost consciousness, and how they had got to the dry land.
itwêwak ôki ayîsiyiniwak, "niwâpahtênân mistahi êkotê ê-mâyi-kîsikâk, mîna mistahi ê-kitocik êkotê piyêsiwak," itwêwak. ||| Said those people, “We saw that there was a great storm over yonder, and that the Thunderers made a great noise there,” said they.
"mâskôc êwakonik ê-kapâwêpinikoyâhkok," itwêw awa ostêsimâw. ||| “No doubt it was they who threw us ashore,” said the elder brother.
nimosôm awa kaskitêwi-maskwa. ||| This Black-Bear was my grandfather.
kîtahtawê ôki ayîsiyiniwak ê-mihcêticik, mîkiwâhpa ê-mihcêtihki, kîtahtawê pêyak awa ê-okimâwit namôya awiya owîkimâkana. ||| Once upon a time, in a place where there were many people and many tents, one of the chiefs had no wife.
mitoni miyosiw. kotak okimâw nîso ayâwêw iskwêwa owîkimâkana; êkosi pêyak miyosiw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| [He was very good-looking.] Another chief had two wives; one of them was a beautiful young woman.
awa kâ-môsâpêwit okimâw kimotamawêw ôhi okimâwa owîkimâkaniyiwa; wanihêw awa owîkimâkana. ||| The chief who was unmarried abducted this wife of the other chief's; he could not find his wife. Although he looked for her, he could not find her.
iyâta-nitonawâci, wanihêw. awa okimâw, iyâta-wîsta-nitonawâci, âhci kâtêw, ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa ê-kâtât. ||| The other chief, although he too looked for her, merely changed her hiding-place, for he was keeping the young woman in hiding.
têkohtêci mîkiwâhpa, "nîsta namôya nimiskawâw," itwêw. ||| When he came back to the tents, “I, too, cannot find her,” he would say.
piyisk ômisi itêyihtam awa okimâw: "â, nika-nitopayin; ayahciyiniwak nika-nitonawâwak," itêyihtam; "ôki kotakak oskinîkiwak kâ-nâpêhkâsocik nika-wîcêwâwak," itêyihtam awa okimâw; "kinwêsk nika-sipwêhtân; pêyak askiy nika-sipwêhtân." "êkosi nika-kî-isi-ayâwâw awa iskwêw kâ-kimotiyân," itêyihtam. ||| At last this chief thought, “I shall go on the war-path; I shall look for Blackfoot,” he thought; “I shall take with me some of these young men who are braves,” thought this chief; “I shall go away for a long time; for a year I shall go away. In this way I shall be able to have the woman I have stolen,” he thought.
piyisk nitomêw oskinîkiwa, ê-wîhtamawât ê-wî-nitopayit, ayahciyiniwa ê-wî-nitonawât. ||| At last he called a young man and told him that he was going on the war-path, to look for Blackfoot.
ôhi mâna ê-wîcêwât pêyak oskinîkiwa, "nikwêmê," ê-itâhkômât, wîhtamawêw. ||| A certain young man with whom he used to go about, whom he called “my brother-in-arms” by way of relationship, to him he told his plan.
"hâw, kâ-ôh-nitopayiyahk, kisîmak âtiht ta-wîhtamawacik âskaw; namôya ka-mihcêtiyahk," itêw. ||| “Now, I am calling you that you may here and there tell some of your juniors that we are going on the war-path; it is not my plan that we be many,” he told him.
"mâka pita wâskahikanihk ka-itohtânânaw, kika-atâwêyahk môsw-asiniya êkwa kaskitêw êkwa ayiwinisa, êkâ kita-isi-nôhtêpayiyahk kêkway, pêyak askiy ka-kakwê-ayâyahk," itêw. ||| “But first we shall go to the fort, to buy bullets and powder and clothes, so that we may not run short of anything, as we plan to stay a year,” he told him.
"wâpahki ka-mâhiskênânaw," itêw. ||| “Tomorrow we shall go to the trading-post,” he told him.
tâpwê ê-nâ-nipâwiht, nitawâpamêw ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa, ê-nitawi-wîhtamawât ôma ê-itêyihtahk. ||| Accordingly, when all the people were asleep, he went to see that young woman, to tell her of this which he had planned.
tâpwê ê-wâpahk mâhiskamok, ê-atâwêt môsw-asiniya êkwa kaskitêw, ayiwinisa, mîna mihkwêkin, kaskitêwêkin. ||| Then, on the next day, they went to the trading-post and he bought bullets and powder, and clothing, and red flannel cloth and black broadcloth.
ê-takosihkik wîkiwâhk, nitomêw okimâw, ômisi ê-itât: "awa, okimâtik, wâpahki pita nika-nitonawâwak mostoswak, tânitê ihtâtwâwi, êkota tâh-ispiciyêk," itêw otiyinîma; "niwî-papâmâcihon," itêw. ||| When they arrived at the camp, he called the chiefs, and said to them, “Well now, Chiefs, tomorrow I shall go look for buffalo, so that you may move camp to wherever they are,” he told the chiefs; “I mean to roam about,” he told them.
