"êwako kâ-ôh-nitomitakok." "nika-nîsotipiskwân," itêw. ||| “That is why I have called you. I shall stay out two nights,” he told them.
tâpwê,- ê-nîpihk ôma,- kâ-wî-sipwêhtêt, ê-kâh-kawisimôwiht, wiyahpitêw nîso otêma. ||| And so, - this was in summer-time, - when he was ready to set out, when all the people had gone to bed, he saddled two of his horses.
êkosi ê-sipwêhtêt, ê-sipwêhtahât ôhi iskwêwa, wâhyaw ê-itohtahât, itê ta-kî-isi-sipwêhtêt. ||| Then he set out, taking that woman away with him, leading her far off in the direction which he was going to take.
tâpwê wâhyaw ê-ayât, ê-pasahcâyik, ê-sakâyik, môhkiciwanipêk ê-ayâyik, mostoswa nipahêw pêyak, êkota ê-nakatât ôhi iskwêwa wiyâsa mîna. ||| Then, when he was far away, in a wooded ravine where there was a spring, he killed a buffalo, and there he left that woman with the meat.
"hâw osîhtâ kâhkêwakwa," itêw ôhi iskwêwa, ê-kîwêt; "êkâya wîhkâc sâkêwê," itêw; "êkâya kaskêyihta; nika-takosinin," itêw. ||| “Now then, prepare dried meats,” he told her, as he left for home; “Do not ever go out into the open,” he told her; “And do not feel lonely; I shall come here,” he told her.
tâpwê ê-kî-nîso-tipiskâyik, êkosi ê-takosihk mîkiwâhpihk. ||| As he had said, after two nights he arrived in camp.
"ôtê isi nâtakâm isi ispicihkêk." "ôtê wiya kâ-itohtêyân nimitaw nama kêkway mostoswak," itêw. ||| “Move your camp this way, toward the north. Over this way where I have been, toward the south, there are no buffalo,” he told them.
êkosi ê-tipiskâk sipwêhtêwak. ||| Then at nightfall they set out.
nistomitanaw ihtasiwak. ||| They were thirty in number.
mistahi ayiwinisa sipwêhtatâwak. ||| They took much baggage with them.
pêyakwâw nôhtaw kapêsiwak; mîna ê-wâpahk, ê-âpihtâ-kîsikâyik, kâ-otihtahkik ôhi ita iskwêwa kâ-kî-nakatât. ||| Once they camped before they got there; on the next day, at noon, they came to where he had hidden the woman.
"nikwêmê, ispisohtê." "nêma kâ-ispatinâ-k, êkotê pêhîhkan." "pita ôma kâ-sakâk nika-kîskatahên misâskwatwa nîso, ta-ôh-kanâcihtâyân nipâskisikan," itwêw. ||| “My brother-in-arms, go on ahead. At yonder hill wait for me. I mean to stop and cut two saskatoon sticks in this grove, to clean my gun,” he said.
êkosi ê-ati-sipwêhtêt, ê-pinasiwêt, sakâhk otihtêw ôhi kâ-kî-kâtât iskwêwa. ||| So off he went, down into the gully, and to the woman he had hidden.
"mwêhci êkwa nikaskêyihtêh," itwêyiwa. ||| “I was just beginning to feel lonely,” she said.
êkosi êkota kîskataham misâskwatwa. ||| So then he out the saskatoon sticks there.
"wawêyî," itêw; "ôta ôma pimohtêwak oskinîkiwak." ||| “Make ready,” he told her; “Over yonder the young men are on the march.”
ê-sâkêwêcik, kê-wâpamâcik ispatinâhk ê-apiyit, ê-pîhtwâyit. ||| When they came into view, they saw the others there on the hilltop, smoking.
êkwa ôki oskinîkiwak ê-pê-sâkêwêyit ê-wâpamâcik, "awiya awa pê-wîcêwêw," itêwak otôkimâmiwâwa. ||| And those young men, when they saw them come forth, “He comes with someone,” they said of their chief.”
"â, iskwêwa miyâmay!" itwêwak. ||| “Why, surely, it is a woman!” they said.
kisiwâk ê-pê-ayâyit, nisitawêyimêwak ôhi iskwêwa. ||| When they had come near, they recognized that woman.
"êwako awa kayâs ka-wâh-wanihiht ita kâ-miskawât!" itêwak. ||| “It is that person who has been lost for this long time, whom now he has found here!” they said of her.
ê-pê-takohtêyit, awîna ôhi êwakoni kâ-kî-wanihimiht! ||| When they arrived there, yes, it was none other than the woman who had been lost!
"wâhyaw wiya ana kimiskamâson, nikwêmê!" ||| “Truly, you have made a good find in a far-away place, Brother!”
"êha, kêswân nimiskawâw êwako ôma kâ-sakâk," ê-itwêt, "hâ, nikwêmê, tâpwê kimiyopayin!" itêw. ||| “Yes, by chance I found her in this grove,” he said, and, “Ha, Brother, truly, you are fortunate!” he answered him.
êkosi êkwa sipwêhtêwak. ||| Thereupon they went from that place.
ita ê-kapêsicik, ômisi itwêw: "â, nisîmitik, êkâ wiya kêkway kita-atoskâtam awa iskwêw." "kiyawâw ka-paminawatâwâw awa iskwêw," itêw. ||| Where they encamped, he said, “Now, Brothers, this woman is by no means to work at anything. It is you who will provide for her,” he told them.
"hâ, tâpwê nama wiya tita-atoskêw!" itwêwak, ôhi iskwêwa. ||| “Very well, she shall not do any work!” they said, of this woman.
êkosi miyêw ôma mihkwêkin, "kaskikwâta, kita-oskotâkâyan," ê-itât, "mîna kita-otâsiyan ôma," itêw ôhi iskwêwa. ||| Then he gave her that red cloth, saying to her, “Sew it for your skirt and for your leggings.”
êkosi tâpwê ka-kaskikwâtisow awa iskwêw. ||| Accordingly that woman sewed clothes for herself.
tâpwê miywâsiniyiwa otayôwinisa. ||| Truly, excellent were her clothes.
êkosi nistomitanaw pêyakosâp ihtasiwak. ||| So now their number was thirty-one.
tâpwê ê-wâpaniyik, ê-sipwêhtêcik, namôya wâhyaw ê-ihtâcik, mostoswa wâpamêwak. ||| The next day, when they set out, they had not gone far, when they saw some buffalo.
êkosi, "minahok!" itêw; êkota ka-nîmâwinihkêyit itêw otôskinîkîma. ||| Then, “Make a killing!” he told the others; he told his followers to prepare food there for their journey.
êkota mîna kapêsiwak. ||| Then they pitched camp there.
ê-wâpahk, ê-sipwêhtêcik, kâ-pêhtahk ê-ma-matwêwêyik; mâka namôya kiskêyihtam tânitê kâ-matwêwêyik. ||| On the next day, as they set out, he heard some shots; but he did not know whence the noise came.
âhci piko ê-pimohtêcik, sîpiy wâpahtamwak. ||| They kept on walking and came to a river.
"minahok!" itêw; "minahoyêko, sîpîhk ka-itohtatânânaw wiyâs." "êkota ka-kapêsinânaw." "kika-osîhtânânaw nîmâwina, pêskis êkota ohci kita-ay-asawâpiyahk ôma kâ-mâh-matwêwêk." "mâskôc ayahciyiniwak," itêw ôhi otôskinîkîma. ||| “Make a killing!” he told them; “When you have killed some, we shall take the meat to the river. There we shall camp. We shall prepare a store of meat, and at the same time reconnoitre from there as to that shooting. Perhaps it was Blackfoot,” he told his followers.
êkosi sipwêhtêwak nîso oskinîkiwak, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahâcik ôhi mostoswa. ||| Then two young men went off to try to kill some of those buffalo.
tâpwê pâskiswêwak nîswâw; nîso nipahêwak. ||| They fired twice at them; they killed two.
êkosi ê-wâpamâcik ê-nipahâyit, êkotê itohtêwak. ||| When they saw that the young men had killed them, they went there.
ê-otihtâcik, "hâw, mitoni kahkiyaw kakwê-otinamôhkêk wiyâs." "ôma sîpîhk kâ-sakâk, êkota ka-kapêsinânaw, ta-nîmâwinihkêyêk," itwêw; "nika-ispisi-itohtânân." ||| When they got to them, “Now then, try to take every bit of the meat. In that wooded spot by the river we shall camp, and there you will prepare the meat,” he said; “We others will go on ahead.”
êkosi ôki oskinîkiwak wiyanihtâkêwak. ||| So then those young men skinned and cut up the carcasses.
êkwa ôki sîpîhk ôki kâ-takohtêcik, êkota nakîwak, ê-otinakik mistikwa, ê-osîhtâcik wîkiwâwa. ||| And those who went to the river, stopped there and gathered sticks and set up their tents.
nîso osîhtâwak, nîpiya ohci ê-apahkwêcik wîkiwâwa. ||| They built two, covering them with leaves.
êkwa ôki oskinîkiwak wiyâsa âwatâwak. ||| And those young men brought in the meats.
êkwa âsay wâpamikwak kotaka ayîsiyiniwa, ôhi kâ-kî-pêhtahkik ê-tasinamiyit, êwakoni kâ-wâpamikocik. ||| Now, by this time they had been seen by the other people; those whom they had heard firing, by, them they had been seen.
ê-wâpamikocik, "ayahciyiniwak!" itêyimikwak otôtêmiwâwa. ||| When they were seen by the others, “Blackfoot!” these people, their fellow-tribesmen, thought of them.
êkosi ka-kâsôhtâkwak, wiyawâw ê-osîhtâcik onîmâwiniwâwa. ||| Accordingly the others hid from them, while they prepared their dried meats.
êkwa ôhi kotakak kâ-mihcêticik itohtêwak. ||| Then those others, who were many in number, went toward them.
êkwa ôki cîki âsay ayâwak, ê-nipâyit otôtêmiwâwa. ||| By this time these people had come close to where their fellow-tribesmen were sleeping.
piyisk otihtêwak, ê-nipâyit. ||| At last they reached them, as they slept.
namôya nisitawêyimêwak. ||| They did not recognize them.
êkosi isi ôhi wîkiyiwa ê-wîhkwêkâpawicik, ê-pâskiswâcik. ||| And so they surrounded their tents and opened fire on them.
ê-pîkiskwêcik, ôki kâ-nipâcik, pêyak kâ-pêhtahk otôtêmiwâwa ê-pîkiskwêyit, kâ-têpwêt, "niyanân!" ê-itwêt. ||| When they spoke, one of those who were sleeping there, heard that it was their fellow-tribesmen speaking, and shouted, saying, “It is we!”
pêyak ê-wî-wayawiyâmot, otihtinik pêyak, ê-tahkamikot môhkomân ohci. ||| When one of them fled out from a tent, one of the others seized him and stabbed him with a knife.
êkoyikohk kâ-pêhtahkik, kâ-kiskêyihtahkik otôtêmiwâwa ê-pisci-pâskiswâcik. ||| Only then did they hear and learn that by mistake they were firing on their own tribesmen.
kitôtêminawak!" itwêw. ||| Our fellow-tribesmen!” he cried.
kêkâc kahkiyaw nipahêwak. ||| They had killed nearly all of them.
mitâtaht piko namôya nipahâwak; mâka kahkiyaw miswâwak. ||| Only ten were not killed; but all were wounded.
êkwa ê-kotawêcik, kâ-nisitawêyimâcik otôtêmiwâwa. ||| Then, when they made a fire, they recognized their fellow-tribesmen.
awa okimâw iskwêwa kâ-wîcêwât, nipahâw ôhi kiki iskwêwa kâ-kî-kwâsihtwâkêt. ||| That chief who had the woman with him, had been killed, together with the woman he had abducted.
êsa awa kê-tahkamiht namôya nipiw. ||| The one who had been stabbed did not die.
pîhtokahâw, kwayask ê-pimisimiht, "mâskôc ta-nipiw," ê-itêyihtamoht. ||| He was taken into a tent and carefully laid down, for, “No doubt he will die,” his people thought.
êkosi ôki kotakak kâ-misohcik, "nama wiya ta-kî-nipiwak," ê-itêyimâcik êwakoni, "ka-sipwêhtahânawak; ka-kîwânânaw," itwêwak, ê-pakwâtahkik otôtêmiwâwa mihcêt ê-nipahâcik. ||| But as for those others who had been wounded by shots, thinking of them, “They are not likely to die,” they said, “We shall take them away with us; we shall return home,” for they were down-hearted at having killed so many of their tribesmen.
êkosi sêmâk nakatêwak, osâm ê-pakwâtahkik ê-tôtawâcik owâhkômâkaniwâwa, ê-kîwêcik. ||| So immediately they left the slain, too much depressed at what they had done to their fellow-tribesmen, and went home.
êkwa awa kâ-tahkamiht êkota pimisin pîhcâyihk. ||| The one who had been stabbed lay there within.
niyânan pîhcâyihk êkota ita kâ-pimisihk êkota pimisiniyiwa ôhi oskinîkiwa ê-kî-nipahimiht. ||| Inside there where he lay, lay five of the young men who had been slain.
"misawâc wîsta ta-nipiw," ê-itêyimikot, kâ-ôh-nakatiht. ||| Because they thought of him, “In any case he too will die,” was why he had been abandoned.
piyisk wâpaniyiw, êkota ê-pa-pimisihk. ||| At last dawn came, as he lay there.
piyisk kapê-kîsik pa-pimisin. ||| He lay there all day.
namôya minihkwêw nipiy; namôya mîcisôw. ||| He drank no water; he did not eat.
"mâskôc nîsta nika-nipin," itêyihtam. ||| “No doubt I too shall die,” he thought.
mâka ita kâ-pimisihk, opâskisikan êkota astêyiw, êkwa pîhcasinânisa, môsasiniya ê-asiwatêyik, êkwa kaskitêw ê-asiwatêyik. ||| But where he lay, there was his gun, and his ammunition-bags, with bullets in them, and with powder.
piyis kêkâc tipiskâyiw. ||| At last it was almost night.
kîtahtawê kâ-pêhtahk kêkway, ê-pa-pimisihk, ê-matwê-pê-pimohtêyit awiya. ||| Presently he heard something, as he lay there, the sound of someone walking hither.
"mâskôc wîsta pêyak apisîs ê-pimâtisit," itêyihtam, "ôta kotakihk mîkiwâhpihk," itêyihtam. ||| “Perhaps someone else who has a bit of life left in him,” he thought; “there in the other tent,” he thought.
kâ-pê-paspiskwêyiyit, ê-kitâpamât, pôti wâkayôsa ê-kitâpamikot. ||| When the other pushed his head into the doorway, and he looked at him, there was a bear looking at him.
"êkosi êcika ani kê-nipahit, maywês nipiwaki!" itêyihtam. ||| “And so this creature will kill me if I do not die soon enough for him!” he thought.
êkotê iskwâhtêmihk isi ê-pimisiniyit ôhi oskinîkiwa kâ-wayawîhtahât awa wâkayôs, ôhi oskinîkiwa ê-nitawi-môwât ohpimê, ômisi itêyihtam awa: "nîsta nika-môwik!" itêyihtam. ||| When the bear had taken out of the tent the young man who lay nearest the doorway, going off somewhere to eat him, then he thought, “He will eat me too!”
namôya kî-nipâw awa oskinîkiw. ||| The young man could not sleep.
piyisk wâpaniyiw; namôya nipâw. ||| Finally day broke; he had not slept.
mitoni ê-kîsikâyik, âsay mîna kâ-pê-takohtêyit ôhi wâkayôsa; âsay mîna pê-paspiskwêyiyiwa, ê-kitâpamikot, wîsta ê-kitâpamât. ||| When it was full day, again there came the bear; again it stuck its head into the doorway and looked at him, and he, in turn, looked at it.
ayisk namôya kî-waskawîw, mistahi ê-wîsakêyihtahk ôma ita kâ-tahkamiht. ||| For he could not move, what with the great pain of his knife-wound.
itê isi ê-isi-sâwahtot, êkotê nîso pimisiniyiwa oskinîkiwa; êwakoni mîna pêyak kâ-wayawîtâpêyit ôhi wâkayôsa, aspin mîna êwakoni ê-nitawi-môwâyit. ||| Near his feet lay two young men; one of these, again, the bear dragged out of the tent, and went away to eat him.
"êkosi êcika ani kahkiyaw kê-kitamokoyâhk" itêyihtam êwako. ||| “And so it turns out that it will eat us all up!” thought he.
kapê-kîsik pa-pimisin. ||| All day he lay there.
kêyâpic namôya minihkwêw; mîna namôya mîcisôw wiya. ||| Again he did not drink; and he did not eat.
nama kêkway wâpahtam ta-mîcit; cikêmâ ôhi kâ-nipahikocik, êwakonik ê-manêsicik mîciwin, kahkiyaw otinamwak ôhi kâ-kî-nîmâwinihkêyit; êkosi kâ-kîwêcik wiya êwakonik. ||| He saw nothing to eat; for, indeed, they who had killed them, being in want of food, had taken all the provisions which the others had prepared; and so they had gone home.
êkwa awa aspin kâ-wayawîhtahât oskinîkiwa, piyisk kapê-kîsik nama kêkway wîhkâc môsihtâw awa miswâkan. ||| After that creature had taken that youth out of the tent, the wounded man noticed nothing more all day.
iyikohk ê-tipiskâyik, âsay mîna ka-pê-paspiskwêyiyit wâkayôsa, iyâyaw ê-kitâpamikot mâna, kinwêsk ê-kitâpamikot mâna, kâ-pê-pîhtokêyit. ||| When it was getting dark, again the bear came sticking its head under the door-flap, looking at him eagerly, as before; when, as before, it had looked at him a long time, it came into the tent.
kotaka mîna ôhi oskinîkiwa aspin mîna ê-wayawîhtahâyit, kêyâpic nîso pimisiniyiwa. ||| When, again, it had taken out another of those youths, two still lay there.
"âta wiya kêyâpic ôhi nîso ta-môwât, nama mayaw niya ta-môwit!" itêyihtam êwako kapê-tipisk. ||| “I hope he will first eat these two, before he eats me!” he thought all that night.
ê-wâpaniyik, mitoni ê-kîsikâyik, âsay mîna kâ-pê-takohtêyit wâkayôsa, êkwa ôhi itê kâ-pimisihk ôhi oskinîkiwa êkoni wayawîhtahêyiwa. ||| When day came, and it had grown quite light, again the bear arrived, and that youth who lay there, him it dragged out of the tent.
"â, êkwa nêhi kâ-pimisiniyit, otâkosiki êwakoni ta-wayawîhtahêw, êkwa niya wâpahki kîkisêpâ kê-môwit!" itêyihtam, ê-pa-pimisihk. ||| “Yes, now, in the evening, he will take out the one who lies over yonder, and tomorrow morning he will eat me!” he thought, as he lay there.
"êkwa mâskôc ahpô nôhtaw nika-nipin!" itêyihtam. ||| “But perhaps and as likely, I shall die before then!” he thought.
êkosi êwako kapê-kîsik pa-pimisin. ||| Thus he lay there all that day.
namôya kî-waskawîw êkwa. ||| He still was unable to move.
piyisk ê-ati-ta-tipiskâyik, "â, kêkâc êkwa mâna kâ-takohtêt wâkayôs!" itêyihtam. ||| At last, as darkness approached, “Yes, and now it is near to the time when the bear always comes!” he thought.
mitoni iyikohk ê-tipiskâyik, êkoyikohk kâ-takohtêyit; mâka mîna ê-pê-paspiskwêyiyit, iyâyaw kitâpamik. ||| When it had got quite dark, then it came; again it came sticking its head into the doorway, and eagerly looked at him.
ê-kî-kitâpamikot, ôhi oskinîkiwa kâ-wayawîtâpêyit aspin. ||| When it had looked at him, it dragged out that young man, and off it went.
"hâ, êkwa niya wâpahki kê-nipahit, êkâ cêskwa nipiwaki!" itêyihtam. ||| “Yes, and now tomorrow he will kill me, if I do not die before he comes!” he thought.
piyisk mistahi ati-ta-tipiskâyiw; mâka namôya kî-waskawîw, namôya ê-maskawâtisit. ||| At last it got darker and darker; he could not move; he had not strong life in him.
piyisk ati-wa-wâpaniyiw. ||| At last day began to come.
"pîhtaw êcika ani êwako kê-kitimahit, maywês nipiwaki ta-nipahit, ta-môwit!" ê-itêyihtahk; "kîkisêpâ pê-itohtêci êkwa niya kê-nipahit!" itêyihtam. ||| “And so now I must expect it; he will give me a painful death, killing me because I did not die for him in time, that he may eat me!” he thought; “When in the morning he comes, it is I this time whom he will kill!” he thought.
piyis ati-ka-kîsikâyiw. ||| At last day grew bright.
êkwa asawâpamêw ka-pê-takohtêyit. ||| He watched for it to come.
piyis ispi-kîsikâyiw; nama takohtêyiwa. ||| At last it was high day; the creature did not come.
mitoni ê-âkwâ-kîsikâyik, kîtahtawê kâ-pêtwêwêtâhtamiyit. ||| When it was full noon, presently it came, breathing audibly.
"êkwa niya kê-môwit!" itêyihtam. ||| “Now he will eat me!” he thought.
ê-pê-paspiskwêyiyit, âsay mîna kitâpamik; wîsta ka-kitâpamêw. ||| When it thrust its head into the doorway, again it looked at him; he, too, kept looking at it.
kinwêsk kitâpamik; piyis pîhtokêyiwa. ||| For a long time it gazed at him; at last it came inside.
"â, êkwa niya kê-wayawîhtahit" itêyihtam, kêyiwêhk ê-kostât, âta namôya ê-maskawâtisit. ||| “Yes, now he will take me out with him!” he thought, fearing it, even though there was but little life in him.
pôti akâmâyihk nêtê kâ-pimohtêyit, itê ê-itiskwêsihk, êkota kâ-nîpawiyit. ||| But it walked along the far side of the tent, and stood in the direction of his head, as he lay.
êkwa namôya kî-waskawîw. ||| He was not able to move.
kîtahtawê êkota kâ-nahapiyit, ocihciya ômisi ê-itastât wâkayôs, êkota ê-aspiskwêsimot, ê-apit, âskaw ê-kitâpamât ôhi oskinîkiwa. ||| Presently the bear sat down there, placing its fore paws like this, and leaning its head on them, as it sat there, gazing at that young man.
ê-pôn-âpihtâwi-kîsikâyik, kîtahtawê tâpiskôc ê-ati-miywamahcihot kâ-itêyihtahk awa oskinîkiw. ||| When the day was past noon, then at one time it seemed to that young man as if he were feeling better and better.
mâskôc awa niwî-kitimâkêyimik," itêyihtam. ||| Perhaps this creature means to take pity on me,” he thought.
êkosi, "namôya êtokwê awa!" itêyihtam awa oskinîkiw, ê-pa-pimisihk. ||| And so, “Perhaps not he!” thought the youth, as he lay there.
ê-otâkosiniyik, pasikôw awa wâkayôs. ||| Towards nightfall, the bear arose.
ê-wî-môwit êkwa" itêyihtam awa oskinîkiw. ||| Now he will eat me!” thought the youth.
ê-kî-sâ-sîpiyit, ati-wayawiyiwa. ||| It stretched itself, and went out of the tent.
nama mayaw pîhtokêyiwa. ||| It did not come in again just then.
"hâw, mâskôc pîhtokêci, êkwa nika-môwik!" itêyihtam. ||| “Yes, no doubt when he comes in, then he will eat me!” thought he.
kîtahtawê pîhtokêyiwa; kêyâpic êkota nahapiyiwa. ||| Presently it came into the tent; it sat down in the same place as before.
êkosi, "â, namôya êsa ani êtokê niwî-nipahik!" itêyihtam. ||| Then, “Why, it really does not seem that he is going to kill me!” he thought.
êkosi kîtahtawê tâpiskôc ê-nôhtê-nipât itêyihtam. ||| Then presently he felt as if he needed to sleep.
pôti kâ-waskawît êkwa awa oskinîkiw, ê-akwanahisot, êkwêyâk ê-waskawît, aspin kâ-nakatiht, niyânanwâw ê-tipiskâyik. ||| And then that young man moved, putting the cover over himself; it was the first time he had moved, from the time he had been abandoned, for five days and nights.
êkosi aciyaw piko nipâsiw. ||| And so he dozed for a little while.
piyis ê-pêkopayit, âsay kâ-wî-wâpaniyik, tâpiskôc ê-miyomahcihot itêyihtam. ||| Then, when he woke up, it had already dawned, and he felt quite well.
piyisk mitoni kîsikâyiw. ||| At last it was full daylight.
ê-isi-âkwâ-kîsikâyik, kîtahtawê kâ-pasikôyit, ê-wayawiyit. ||| When high day had come, presently the bear rose to its feet and went out.
iyikohk ê-pîhtokêyit, kêyâpic êkota nahapiyiwa. ||| When it came back in, again it sat down there.
ê-kitâpamât, ômisi itik; pîkiskwêyiwa: "'ninipin,' kitêyihtên." "namôya kika-kî-nipin," kâ-itikot. ||| When he looked at it, it spoke to him as follows, speaking like a man: “'I am dying,' you think. You shall not by any chance die,” it said to him.
"ayâ, matwân cî ê-tâpwêt?" itêyihtam. ||| “Alas, I wonder if he speaks true?” he thought.
"êha, kika-pimâtisin," kâ-itikot. ||| “Yes, you will live,” it told him.
"ahpô piko ta-nipahâhkatosoyân," itêyihtam. ||| “Perhaps only to die of starvation,” he thought.
êkosi êkota pa-pimisin; mitoni êkwa wâh-waskawîw ospitona oskâta mîna. ||| So he lay there; but now he kept moving his arms and logs quite freely.
mâka mistahi nêstosiw; osâm kinwêsk ê-pimisihk, êwako ohci kâ-ôh-nêstosit, êkwa mîna mistahi ê-kî-wîsakêyihtahk, mâka ati-miywamahcihôw, ôma ê-itikot ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| But he was very tired; he was tired because he had lain so long, and also because he had suffered so much pain. But he felt better and better, now that that bear had said this to him.
kapê-kîsik êkota ê-apiyit, ê-otâkosiniyik, kêkâc ê-tipiskâyik, kâ-nôhtê-waniskât. ||| When it had sat there all day, toward evening, when darkness had almost fallen, he felt a desire to get up.
tâpwê waniskâw, ê-simatapit. ||| He raised himself and sat up.
ê-kî-simatapit, kâ-pasikôyit, ê-wayawît. ||| When he sat up, the bear rose to its feet and went out of the tent.
iyikohk mistahi ê-tipiskâyik, pîhtokêyiwa, kêyâpic êkota ê-nahapiyit. ||| When darkness had come, it entered and sat down again.
ê-kî-nahapiyit, kâ-nôhtêhkwasit, ê-nôhtê-nipât. ||| When it had sat down, he began to feel sleepy and to long for sleep.
mayaw ê-kawisimot, sêmâk nipâw. ||| As soon as he lay down, he went to sleep.
namwâc ohci pêkopayiw. ||| He did not wake up again.
iyikohk ê-pêkopayit, âsay ispi-kîsikâyiw. ||| When he woke up, it was already high day.
waniskâw, ê-simatapit. ||| He raised himself and sat up.
"êkosi êcika ôma ê-wî-pimâtisiyân!" itêyihtam. ||| “And so I am going to live, after all!” he thought.
êkosi kîtahtawê kâ-otinahk opîhtasinânisa, ê-nôhtê-sipwêhtêt. ||| Then presently he took his ammunition-bags, meaning to go away.
"matwân cî ôma nika-kî-pasikôn?" ê-itêyihtah. ||| “I wonder if I shall be able to get up on my feet?” he thought.
ê-kî-otinahk opîhtasinânisa, êkwa pakwahtêhôw, ôma oskotâkay, wâpowayân ê-oskotâkât. ||| When he had taken his ammunition-bags, he fastened his belt round his coat, which was a blanket-robe.
êkwa sêkwasôw opîhtasinânisa; êkwa omaskisina otinam, êwakoni mîna ê-sâ-sêkwasot. ||| He fastened the ammunition-bags under his belt; then he took his moccasins, fastening them, too, under his belt.
ê-kî-otinahk opâskisikan, kâ-pasikôyit ôhi wâkayôsa, ê-pê-âhci-tahkoskêyit. ||| When he had taken his gun, the bear rose to its feet and took a few steps toward him.
kisiwâk ê-nîpawiyit, ê-kitâpamikot, "â, isko awa ta-pasikôwak!" itêyihtam. ||| When it stood close and looked at him, “Well, it seems I am to get up for him!” he thought.
êkosi ê-wî-pasikôt, namôya kî-pasikôw. ||| When he tried to get on his feet, he was unable.
nicawâc ômisi isi wâwikaniyihk micimîw, ê-pasikôt. ||| He needs held fast to the bear's back, as he rose to his feet.
ê-nîpawit, konita na-namipayiw, osâm kinwêsk ê-pimisihk. ||| When he stood up, he reeled this way and that, because he had lain so long.
êkosi âhci tahkoskêyiwa; wîsta âhci tahkoskêw, ê-micimît ôhi wâkayôsa wâwikaniyihk. ||| Then the bear took a step; he too took a step, holding fast to the bear's back.
namôya êkwa kostêw, "mâskôc niwî-pimâcihik," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He did not fear it now, thinking, “Perhaps he means to help me to live.”
piyis wayawîhtahik, êkwa ê-sipwêhtêt. ||| At last it led him out of the tent, and he started off.
nânitaw nêmitanaw tahkoskêwin êtokê ê-itohtêt, nêstosiw. ||| When he had walked about forty steps, he was tired.
namôya sêmâk sipwêhtêyiwa. ||| It did not start off at once.
iyikohk wiya ê-itêyihtahk ê-âhcikâpawit, êkoyikohk kâ-wî-sipwêhtêyit. ||| Only when he decided to move ahead from where he stood, only then did it move on.
mîna namôya wâhyaw itohtêw, âsay mîna ê-nêstosit. ||| Again he had not walked far, when he was tired.
mîna êkota kinwêsk nîpawiw, ê-ay-itâpit. ||| Here too he stood for a long time, looking this way and that.
êkoyikohk êkwa pôn-âpihtâwi-kîsikâyik. ||| By this time it was afternoon.
piyisk ê-ay-âhtohtêcik, iyikohk ê-otihtahkik ôma ita kâ-kî-pê-pinasiwêcik, âsay pahkisimoyiwa, ê-wî-tipiskâyik. ||| At last, as they kept walking a little ways at a time, when they reached the spot where they had come down the bank on their way hither, the sun had already set, and darkness was at hand.
ita ê-pasahcâyik, êkota ê-ati-itohtêcik, mistahi nêstosiw, pîhtaw ê-nôhtêhkatêt mîna ê-nôhtêyâpâkwêt. ||| From their walk along the river-bottom he had become very tired, and now he was hungry and thirsty besides.
mistahi ê-tipiskâyik, kêkâc kîsi-âmaciwêwak. ||| By the time it was entirely dark, they had almost climbed to the top of the bluff.
ê-nîpawit, nakiyiwa. ||| When he stood still, the bear halted.
wîsta êkota nahapiw. ||| He too sat down there.
ê-kîsi-mitoni-nahapit, pasikôyiwa, ê-îkatêhtêyit. ||| As soon as he had got himself into a comfortable position, it rose to its feet and walked off to one side.
aspin êkwa wiya nôhtêhkwasiw. ||| At that moment he felt sleepy.
"nicawâc mahti nika-nipân," itêyihtam. ||| “Now I had better sleep,” he thought.
iyikohk ê-wâpaniyik, pêkopayiw. ||| At daybreak he awoke.
ê-kîsikâyik, kîtahtawê kâ-pêtisâpamât pêtâstamohtêyit. ||| When daylight had come, presently he saw the bear walking toward him.
pê-takohtêyiwa; kisiwâk nahapiyiwa. ||| It came up to him; it sat down close by him.
êkoyikohk mistahi nôhtêyâpâkwêw. ||| By this time he was very thirsty.
êkwa kâ-pasikôt, ê-nêstohtêt, êkwa êkâ ê-kisiskâhtêt, "mâskôc têhtapiyân nikâh-kisiskâhtân," itêyihtam. ||| When he had risen to his feet, as from weariness he could not walk well or fast, “Perhaps if I ride I shall go faster,” he thought.
ê-apiyit êkwa ômisi isi pâsitâhkoskêw, ê-nîpawit. ||| Where the bear sat, he stepped straddling it, like this, as he stood.
kâ-pasikôyit, nisihkâc êkosi êkwa miyo-apiw, ê-têhtapit. ||| When it rose to its feet, he sank gently into a comfortable sitting position, riding on its back.
êkosi isi ê-sipwêhtêyit, ê-ati-âmaciwêyit, êkwa ê-ayîtâpit, ê-têhtapit ôhi wâkayôsa, ê-kîwêhtahikot, itê kâ-kî-ohtohtêcik êkotê, itêhkê ê-isi-kîwêhtahikot. ||| And so it set out, climbing the rest of the bluff, he the while looking about him, as he rode the bear, which was taking him home, in the very direction from which he and his party had come.
namôya wâhyaw ê-ihtât, kâ-miskahk nipiy. ||| When he had not gone far, he found water.
êkosi êkota cîki nipîhk nahapiyiwa, êkwa ê-nîhtakosît, ê-minihkwêt, mîna ê-kâsîhkwêt. ||| Accordingly the bear stopped by the water, and he dismounted and drank and washed his face.
wîsta minihkwêw awa wâkayôs. ||| The bear, too, drank.
mitoni ê-kîsi-nânapâcihisot, mîna êkota pê-nahapiyiwa. ||| When it had carefully cleaned and arranged itself, it came back and sat down there.
âsay mîna têhtapiw; êkosi êsi-pasikôt, ê-sipwêhtêt. ||| Again he mounted it; then it arose and started off.
kêkâc mitoni miyo-ayâw; itêyihtam, ê-pa-pmohtêt, ê-têhtapit. ||| He was close to feeling very well, it seemed to him, as he went along on his mount.
kapê-kîsik êwako pimohtêw. ||| All that day he went ahead.
iyikohk ê-tipiskâyik, nakiyiwa, ê-nahapiyit. ||| When it grew dark, the bear stopped and sat down.
êkosi êkwa nîhtakosîw, ohpimê ê-nahapit. ||| So then he dismounted, and sat down a little ways off.
"hâw, ôta nika-nipân," ê-itêyihtahk, pasikôyiwa, ê-ati-sipwêhtêyit. ||| “Well, I shall sleep here,” he thought, and at that the bear rose to its feet and went away.
êkosi wiya kawisimôw; na-nipâw. ||| So he lay down for the night and slept.
iyikohk ê-pêkopayit, pôti sâsay kîsikâyiw, osâm kinwêsk ê-nipât, kiyipa kâ-wâpamât ê-pêci-âstamohtêyit, pê-takohtêyit. ||| When he woke up, he saw that it was already day, for he had slept long; at once he saw the bear coming towards him; it came up to him.
"mâskôc êkwa nika-kî-pimohtân," itêyihtam. ||| “Perhaps now I shall be able to walk,” he thought.
mâka mistahi nôhtêhkatêw; êkwa mîna nôhtêyâpâkwêw. ||| But he was very hungry; and he was thirsty again.
ê-pasikôt, ê-ati-sipwêhtêt, pasikôyiwa, ê-âkwaskiskâkot, ê-âkwaskohtâyit. ||| When he rose to his feet and started to go on, the bear rose to its feet and headed him off, walking round in front of him.
"isko awa ta-têhtapiyân mîna!" ê-itêyihtahk, nicawâc têhtapiw. ||| “It seems he wants me to ride him again!” he thought, and needs mounted.
êkosi ê-sipwêhtêyit. ||| Then the bear started off.
namôya wâhyaw ê-ihtât, nipiy wâpahtam. ||| He had not gone far, when he saw some water.
êkosi êkota itohtêyiwa, êkota ê-nakiyit, ê-minihkwêt, mîna ê-minihkwêyit. ||| It went there and halted, and he drank, and it drank, too.
iyikohk mîna ê-kî-ka-kâsîhkwêt, âsay mîna pasikôw, ê-wî-sipwêhtêt; êkota mîna pê-nahikâpawiyiwa. ||| When he had washed his face, he rose to his feet to go on; again it came there and stood, ready for him.
nicawâc mîna têhtapiw, ê-sipwêhtêyit, ê-pa-pimi-têhtapit kapê-kîsik. ||| So he needs mounted again, and it set out, and all day he rode on.
piyis nîso-kîsikâw âsay ê-têhtapit, ê-otâkosiniyik, kâ-wâpamât mostoswa. ||| At last, when he had ridden two days, toward evening, he saw some buffalo.
"nika-kakwê-minahon," itêyihtam; "ninôhtêhkatân," itêyihtam. ||| “I shall try to make a killing,” he thought; “I am hungry,” he thought.
tâpwê nîhtakosîw, ê-ati-sipwêhtêt; pôti kâ-nahapiyit ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| Accordingly he dismounted and went off; the bear, he saw, sat down.
wiya ati-sa-sipwêhtêw. ||| He kept going ahead.
piyis kisiwâk otihtêw ôhi mostoswa. ||| At last he got near the buffalo.
piyisk pâskiswêw; pêyak nipahêw. ||| At last he took a shot at them; he killed one.
hâ, miywêyihtam, "êkwa kê-mîcisoyân!" ê-itêyihtahk. ||| Oh, he was glad, thinking, “So now I shall eat!”
mêkwâc ê-wiyanihtâkêt, kâ-pê-takohtêyit wâkayôsa. ||| While he was preparing it, the bear came up to him.
êkwa ê-kîsi-wiyanihtâkêt, kotawêw, ê-kîsitêpot, ê-wî-mîcit. ||| When he had finished his butchering, he made a fire and cooked his meal.
iyikohk ê-kîsisahk wiyâs, ita ê-miywâsiniyik asamêw ôhi wâkayôsa, wîsta ê-mîcisot. ||| When he had cooked the meat done, he gave the best parts of it to the bear, and he too ate some.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, êkoyikohk ati-ta-tipiskâyiw. ||| When they had eaten, darkness was falling.
nêstosiw; pa-pimisin. ||| He was tired; he lay down.
iyikohk mistahi ê-tipiskâyik, êkwa mîna kotaka wiyâsa kîsisam, ê-wî-osîhtât ta-nîmât. ||| When night had come, he cooked some more meat, to make provision for his journey.
tâpwê mistahi kîsisam. ||| He cooked much of it.
êkoyikohk ê-nôhtê-nipât; kawisimôw. ||| By this time he felt the need of sleep; he lay down for the night.
iyikohk ê-pêkopayit, âsay âkwâ-kîsikâyiw, êkwa mîna ê-wî-kakwê-mîcisot. ||| When he awoke, it was already bright day, and again he felt like eating.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, kotaka mîna kîsisam wiyâsa. ||| When he had eaten, he cooked some more meat.
iyikohk mistahi ê-kîsikâk, "êkoyikohk êtokê nika-sâkohtân ta-nayahtamân," ê-itêyihtahk, êkoyikohk ispi-kîsikâyiw. ||| When full daylight had come, “This much perhaps I shall be able to carry,” he thought; and by this time it was high day.
wawêyîw, ê-wî-sipwêhtêt. ||| He made ready to go.
ê-nayahtahk onîmâwin, ê-wawêyît, ê-ati-sipwêhtêt, ay-âkwaskiskâk ôhi wâkayôsa, ê-kisâtamiyit wiyâsa. ||| When he took his provisions on his back, and got ready and was starting off, the bear kept getting in his way and keeping close to the meat.
piyisk nicawâc kâwi wâyonîw, wiyâsa ê-otihtahk. ||| At last he was forced to turn back and go to where the meat was.
wiyâsa ôhi ê-sakâpîhkâtahk, êkwa ôma askêkin ê-aciwisahk, ê-kîsi-mâh-manisahk, ôhi wâkayôsa têhtastâw wâwikaniyihk. ||| He tied the meat up in a bundle, and cut the hide into small pieces, and when he had out off every bit, he placed it on the bear's back.
kwayask nîpawiw awa wâkayôs, êkwa ê-wîwahât ôhi wiyâsa. ||| The bear stood still, while he loaded the meats on its back.
iyikohk ê-kîsi-wîwahât, êkwa êkosi êkwa ê-sipwêhtêt, êkwa ê-pimi-wîcêwât ôhi wâkayôsa, mistahi ê-nayahtamiyit wiyâs. ||| When he had loaded it, then he started off, walking along with the bear, which was carrying a great load of meat.
ita ê-otihtahk nipiy, êkota nîhtinamawêw ôhi wiyâsa, êkota ê-minihkwêt, "ôta nika-ayân; ôhi wiyâsa nika-pâsên," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| Where he came to some water, there he took the meats from its back, and drank, thinking, “Here I shall stay; I shall dry these meats.”
êkota kotawêw, kâhkêwakwa ê-osîhtât. ||| He built a fire there, and prepared dried meat.
kapê-kîsik êkota ayâw, ê-ka-kisâtikot wâkayôsa. ||| He stayed there all day, the bear keeping near him.
piyis tipiskâyiw; êkota mîna nipâw. ||| At last night came; he slept there.
ê-wâpaniyik, kapê-kîsik osîhtâw okâhkêwakoma, tahki ê-kotawêt, ê-pâsahk okâhkêwakoma, piyis kapê-kîsik. ||| When morning came, all day he made his dried meat, building fires to dry his meats, until the day had passed.
iyikohk ê-tipiskâyik, êkoyikohk kîsihtâw okâhkêwakoma; êkoyikohk mîna tipiskâyiw. ||| By nightfall he had finished his dried meats; by this time it was dark.
iyikohk ê-nôhtê-nipât, êkoyikohk kawisimôw. ||| When he felt the need of sleep, he lay down.
iyikohk ê-pa-pêkopayit, âsay wâpan. ||| When he awoke, day was dawning.
êkwa ma-mîcisôw; mîna awa wâkayôs mîcisôw. ||| Then he ate; the bear ate, too.
êkoyikohk ê-ka-kîsi-mîcisocik, êkoyikohk wawêyîw, ê-wî-sipwêhtêt. ||| When they had eaten, he made ready to depart.
êkwa mîna nayahtahêw otêma wâkayôsa onîmâwina. ||| Then again he loaded his provisions on the back of the bear, his animal of use.
êkosi êkwa ê-sipwêhtêt, ê-ati-wîcêwât ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| So then he set out, the bear going with him.
êkwa sâsay êkwa miyo-ayâw ôma kâ-kî-tahkamiht ita. ||| By this time he had recovered from the wound where he had been stabbed.
ayis êwakoni ôhi wâkayôsa ê-wîcihikot, kiyipa kâ-ôh-miyo-ayât. ||| Of course it was because that bear helped him that he got well so quickly.
êkosi ôma êkwa kâ-pa-pimohtêcik, kâh-kiyipa nakîw ê-mîcisot; osâm kinwêsk namôya kî-mîcisôw. ||| Then, as they thus walked along, every little while he stopped and ate; he had gone too long without food.
êkwa mistahi ê-kî-wîsakêyihtahk, nawac kawâhkatosow awa oskinîkiw; êkwa ê-miyomahcihot, êwako ohci kâh-kiyipa kâ-ôh-nôhtêhkatêt. ||| Also, because, he had suffered so much pain, that youth was badly worn down; so now, when he had got well, it caused him to get hungry at frequent intervals.
piyis tâpwê nisto-kîsikâw ê-pimohtêt, âsay namôya ayâw kâhkêwakwa. ||| At last, when he had tramped three days, he had no more dried meats.
piyis wâpamêw ê-wîsakêyihtamiyit wâwikaniyiw ôhi wâkayôsa, osâm mistahi ê-kî-nayôhtamiyit kinwêsk kâhkêwakwa, êkwa wiya mîna ê-kî-têhtapit kinwês; êwako ohci kâ-ôh-wîsakêyihtamiyit wâwikaniyiw. ||| He saw now that the bear was suffering in its back, from having carried so much dried meat for such a long time, and from his having ridden it so long; from all this its back was sore.
êkwa wiya pimiwitâw ôhi okâhkêwakoma, piyis mîna nîso-kîsikâw ê-nayahtahk kâhkêwakwa; namôya mâka mistahi âta wiya êkwa kâ-pimiwitât. ||| So then he carried his dried meats; he carried them on his back for two days; but there was not much for him to carry now.
kîtahtawê sîpiy êkwa kâ-otihtahk. ||| Presently he came to a river.
ê-otâkosiniyik, ôma sîpiy ê-sâkêwêt, êkota ê-sakâyik, êkota kapêsiw. ||| Towards evening, when he came forth into sight of that river, there in a wooded place, he camped.
êkwa ê-kotawêt, ê-wî-mîcisot, âsay êsa ôma kotaka ayîsiyiniwa ê-wâpamikot; wiya namôya wâpamêw. ||| Then, when he made a fire to prepare his meal, some people there saw him; but he did not see them.
êkosi ôma ita kâ-kotawêt, kâ-ay-apit, mêkwâc ê-mîcisot, kîtahtawê kâ-pasikôyit wâkayôsa, sîpîhk isi itêhkê ê-itâpiyit. ||| So then, when he had built a fire, and was sitting there eating, presently the bear got up and looked in the direction of the river.
"wah, kêhcinâ kêkway ê-môsihtât!" itêyihtam. ||| “Why, he must have noticed something!” thought he.
âstawinam ôma otiskotêm. ||| He extinguished his fire.
ê-kî-âstawinahk, kîtahtawê kâ-simaciyit ôho wâkayôsa, ê-itapiyit tahki êkotê, tâpiskôc kêkway ê-wâpahtamiyit; piyis pê-itohtêyiwa ita kâ-apit. ||| When he had put it out, presently the bear got up on its hind legs and kept looking over there, as if it saw something; at last it came to where he sat.
tâpiskôc ê-wî-tapasiyit, itêyihtam, ê-kitâpamikot ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| It seemed to him as if it wanted to flee, the way the bear kept looking at him.
pasikôw, ê-ati-sipwêhtêt. ||| He got up and went from that place.
sêmâk ita ê-pasahcâyik, êkota ati-itohtêyiwa, mitoni ê-kisiskâhtêyit, tahki sisonê sakâhk ê-ati-itohtêyit. ||| At once the bear made for the gully, walking very fast, keeping always along the edge of the woods.
piyis ê-otihtahk mistahi ê-sakâyik, êkota sêskisiyiwa. ||| At last, when it came to where the woods were dense, it went into the brush.
wîsta sêskisiw; piyis ita ê-kaski-sakâyik, êkota kâ-nahapiyit. ||| He too went among the trees; finally, where the woods were densest, it sat down.
wîsta êkota nahapiw. ||| He sat down there, too.
kîtahtawê êkotê kâ-ohtohtêcik tahki âh-itâpiyiwa ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| Soon the bear began to look repeatedly in the direction whence they had come.
kîtahtawê kâ-pêhtahk ê-matwê-kâ-kîskosîwiht. ||| Presently he heard some people whistling.
"miyâmay ayîsiyiniwak!" ê-itêyihtahk, kâ-ati-samaskisiniyit ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| “Plainly, human beings!” he thought, as the bear lay close to the ground.
tâpiskôc ê-kostâciyit itêyihtam. ||| It seemed to him exactly as if the bear were frightened.
iyikohk ê-âkwâ-kîsikâyik, êkoyikohk sipwêhtêw. ||| When it was full daylight, then he departed.
êkwa piyis ê-tipiskâyik, kapêsiw sîpîhk. ||| At last, when night came, he camped by the river.
êkwa êkota ê-nipât, ê-wâpaniyik, iyikohk âsowaham ôma sîpiy. ||| There he slept, and on the next day, crossed the river.
êkwa mitoni êkwa miyw-âyâw. ||| By this time he was very well.
nistwâw ê-nipât, êkoyikohk kotak sîpiy otihtam. ||| After three nights, he reached another river.
êkosi kisiwâk êkwa êkota wâskahikan ê-ayâyik, wîstâwa êkota ê-ayâyit, kihci-môhkomâna, wîstâwa êkota ê-ayâyit, kihci-môhkomâna ê-owîstâwit, osîma ê-onâpêmiyit. ||| Now close by this place was a trading-post, where his brother-in-law lived, an American, for he had an American, his younger sister's husband, as his brother-in-law.
êwako ohci, ê-kiskêyihtahk êwako, ita kâ-ôh-itohtêt, kâ-ôh-isi-kîwêt. ||| For this reason, because he knew this, he had taken this way toward home.
âsay kî-pêhtamiyiwa ê-nipahihcik. ||| They had already heard that those people had been killed.
"aspin apisîs pimâtisiw; 'mâskôc ta-nipiw,' ê-kî-itiht," itâcimostâmâwa owâhkômâkana. ||| “The last that was seen of him, he was scarcely alive; 'No doubt he will die,' was said of him,” was the story his relatives were told.
mîna ôhi osîma âsay kî-pêhtamiyiwa. ||| His sister, too, had heard it.
êkwa osîhtâw ita ê-wî-pôsit, ôma sîpiy ê-wî-âsowahahk. ||| So now he made that on which to embark, so as to cross this river.
ê-kîsihtât, êkwa ê-pôsit, êkwa ê-pimiskât, ê-âpasâpit, êkoyikohk tawâyihk sîpîhk ê-ihtât, kâ-pê-pahkopêyit ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| When he had finished it, and embarked, and paddled across, as he looked back, just as he was in the middle of the stream, into the water went the bear.
ita ê-kapât, êkota cîki kapâyiwa. ||| Close by where he landed, it came ashore.
âsay mâka nama kêkway ayâw ta-mîcit. ||| By this time again he had nothing to eat.
ayis ôhi wâkayôsa mâh-mistahi asamêw; êwako ohci kâ-ôh-kitâcik onîmâwiniwâwa. ||| For he had always given the bear much to eat; that was how they had used up their supplies.
êwako ôma kâ-kapâcik ê-ministikôwiyik. ||| That place where they came ashore was an island.
êkosi êkota tahkohcâyihk namôya wâhyaw kâ-ayâyit ôhi wîstâwa. ||| And not far from there, at the top of the bank, was where his brother-in-law lived.
êkwa sakâhk êkota apiw mîna awa wâkayôs. ||| He stayed there in the woods, with the bear.
"tânisi awa nika-kî-isi-paskêwihâw?" "mâskôc awa tita-akâwâtik ôhi kihci-môhkomâna," itêyimêw, "ta-nôhtê-nipahikot," itêyihtam. ||| “How shall I manage to part from this creature? Most likely this American will want to eat him,” he thought of the bear; “He will want to kill him,” he thought.
kîtahtawê ômisi kâ-itikot, êkwêyâk ê-kitotikot ôhi wâkayôsa, "hâ, nikwêmê, ê-kitimâkisiyan, ê-wî-nipiyan, 'kêhcinâ nika-nipin,' ê-itêyihtaman, "kêhcinâ nika-môwik," ê-itêyimiyan, "nicawâc nika-kakwê-pimâcihâw," kititêyimitin, "kitimâkisiw," ê-itêyihtamân." "'pimâtisici, nika-wîkimâw, otôtêma otihtâci,' kititêyimitin," kâ-itikot. ||| Presently it spoke thus to him, speaking to him only now: “Well, Brother, when you were in misery and were about to die, and 'Surely I shall die,' was your thought, and, 'Surely he will eat me,' was your thought concerning me, then, 'Suppose I try to make him live,' I thought about you, for, 'He is to be pitied,' I thought. 'If he lives, I shall stay with him, when he goes to his fellows,' I thought concerning you,” it said to him.
"hâ, nikwêmê, nisâkwêyimon!" "ôki wêmistikôsiw awa kâ-wî-otihtak kika-nipahik." "êkwa mîna nitôtêmak otihtakwâwi, kîskwêwak oskinîkiwak; kika-nipahikwak." "namôya nika-kî-kostikwak oskinîkiwak; kika-nipahikwak." "namôya kinôhtê-tako-wîcêtin," itêw. ||| “Oh, Brother, I cannot do that! These people, this Frenchman to whom I am going, will kill you. And when I reach my fellow-tribesmen, the young men are reckless; they will kill you. It is unlikely that I can bring the young men to respect my wishes; they will kill you. I do not want to have you with me when I arrive where the others are,” he told it.
ohcitaw kiwî-papâ-wîcêtin," itik. ||| Even so, I want to go about with you,” it answered him.
"â, nikwêmê, ôta ayâ." "nika-itohtân awa wêmistikôsiw." "osâm ninôhtêhkatân." ||| “Well, Brother, stay here. I am going to that Frenchman's. I am hungry, you see.”
"niya mîna ninôhtêhkatân," kâ-itwêyit. ||| “I too am hungry,” it said.
êkosi ati-pasikôw, ê-nakatât ôhi wâkayôsa, ê-âsowahahk ôma apisîs ê-nipîwisiyit; ministikohk ayisk kâ-nakatât. ||| Then he arose, and left the bear, and crossed the bit of water that lay between; for it was on an island that he left the bear.
ê-kîsi-âmaciwêt, kisiwâk ayisk kâ-ayâyik ôma wâskahikan, êkota ê-itohtêt, cîki ê-ihtât, kâ-pê-wayawiyit ôhi wêmistikôsiwa. ||| When he had climbed the bank, he went to the house, for it was right by there. When he came near, that Frenchman came out.
ê-wâpamikot, nîpawiyiwa, ê-kitâpamikot. ||| When he saw him, he stood still and looked at him.
piyisk cîki ê-ihtât, mitoni nisitawêyimik. ||| At last, when he had come closer, the other fully recognized him.
pîhtokêyiwa; kiyipa mîna pê-wayawiyiwa, osîma asici ê-pê-nakiskâkot, "hây hây!" ê-pê-itwêyit osîma, ê-atamiskâkot, wîstâwa osîma mîna ê-itikot, "'kayâs nipahik otôtêma,' kikî-itikawin," itik wîstâwa. ||| He went into the house; at once he came out again, and he and his sister came to meet him, his sister crying, “Splendid!” as they greeted him, his brother-in-law and his sister both saying this to him. “'Long ago he was killed by his fellow-tribesmen,' they said of you,” his brother-in-law told him.
pâhpiw; "kiwâpamin ôma; namôya ê-nipahikawiyân, kâ-wâpamiyan," ê-itikot. ||| He laughed; “You see me here; since you see me, it cannot be that I have been killed,” he told him.
"hâw, pîhtokêtân," itik. ||| “Come, let us go indoors,” they said to him.
"nipêwin êkota api," itik; "kinêstosin êtokê," itik. ||| “Sit there on the bedstead,” they told him; “You must be tired,” they told him.
êkosi ê-ati-paminawasoyit osîma, ta-miyo-mîcisot, ê-itêyimikot, êkwa wiya ê-âcimostawât wîstâwa ôhi iyikohk ê-kwatakihtât, ê-itêyihtahk. ||| Then his sister went on to cook, meaning that he should eat well, while he told his brother-in-law of his sufferings, as they seemed to him.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, sêmâk wâpowayân, papakiwayânasâkay, ospwâkana, ciscêmâsa, kocawâkanisa ê-miyikot wîstâwa, "ômatôwahk namôya ka-kî-miyitin; namôya ka-miywêyimâw," ê-itikot; "kisîm ta-kaskikwâtam ta-otâsiyan," itik. ||| When, they had eaten, at once his brother-in-law gave him a blanket, a shirt, a pipe, tobacco, and matches, and said to him, “These things here I cannot give you; you would not like them; your sister will sew something into leggings for you,” he told him.
êkwa êkota ay-ayâw, tahki ê-miyo-mîcisot, ita kâ-ay-ayâ-t. ||| Then he stayed there, eating good food all the while he was there.
ê-kîkisêpâyâyik, wayawîhtatâw nanâtohk ê-wîhkicisiyit pahkwêsikana, ê-nitawi-asamât wâkayôsa, maywês waniskâyit wîstâwa. ||| Early in the morning, he took out of the house all kinds of tasty cakes, and went to feed the bear, before his brother-in-law had got up.
pôti kêyâpic êkota ayâyiwa. ||| The bear, he found, was still there.
êkwa ê-kîwêt, ê-pîhtokêt, kiyipa waniskâyiwa êkwa wîstâwa. ||| When he went back, as he entered the house, soon his brother-in-law got up.
ê-wâpamikot, "wa, tâpwê mistahi kitânawêw!" itêyihtamiyiwa. ||| When he saw him, “Why, really, he does consume a big amount of food!” was the other's thought.
êkosi kapê-kîsik êkota ay-ayâw. ||| So then he stayed there all day.
êkoyikohk mîna ê-tipiskâyik; âsay mîna wiyâkanihk mistahi astâyiwa mîciwin. ||| It grew dark; again the other put a great deal of food into a dish.
"niyôhtêhkatêyini, ka-mîcisoyin; mitoni kisîhkacin," itik wîstâwa, "osâm mistahi ê-pimohtêyan," ê-itikot. ||| “This is so that you may eat whenever you get hungry; you are too thin,” his brother-in-law said to him, “because you tramped so much,” he told him.
tâpwê iyikohk mîna ê-nipâyit, êkoyikohk wîsta nipâw. ||| So then, when the others went to sleep, he too slept.
kîkisêpâ ê-pêkopayit, "hâ, nika-nitawi-asamâw," itêyihtam. ||| In the morning, when he awoke, “There, I shall go feed him,” he thought.

iyikohk ê-waniskâyit wîstâwa, "tâpwê mistahi mîcisôw nîstâw!" "tânisi awa tiyôtahk?" "namôya êkoyikohk ta-kî-kitât!" piyisk kapê-kîsik ay-ayâw. ||| Then he stayed there all day.
iyikohk mîna ê-tipiskâyik, "ahâw, niwîkimâkan, mahti mistahi astâ êkwa mîciwin, kistês kâ-mîcit mâna." It must be that he uses it for something or other; he could not possibly eat up as much as is always at his place.”
"êha," itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Yes,” said the woman.
tâpwê ê-wî-kawisimocik, mistiyâkanihk êkotowihk êkwa astâw mîciwina, êkota ê-nitawi-pakitinamwât ita mâna kâ-nipâyit ostêsa. ||| Accordingly, when they were about to go to bed, she put food into a huge dish and went and set it down for her brother where he always slept. ed, and then they all got up and went about their day's work.
piyis mistahi ê-tipiskâyik, êkwa ê-kawisimocik, namôya wî-nipâw awa wêmistikôsiw, ê-kanawêyimât wîstâwa. ||| Then, when it was deep night, and they had gone to bed, that Frenchman did not go to sleep, but watched his brother-in-law. At last day broke.
piyisk wâpaniyiw. kîtahtawê kâ-matwê-wayawiyit wîstâwa. ||| Presently he heard his brother-in-law go out of the house.
ê-tawinahk, wâpamonâpiskohk ohci kâ-wâpamât, ê-atimohtêyit, wiyâkan ê-tahkonamiyit, sîpîhk ê-itohtêyit, aspin ê-âkawêwêyit. ||| He opened the door, and with a mirror he saw him, as he went off holding the dish, and made for the river, disappearing round a bend. He kept on the lookout for him.
tahki asawâpamêw. nama mayaw pê-sâkêwêyiwa. ||| It was quite a while before he came back into view.
iyikohk ê-pê-sâkêwêyit, pôti nama kêkway mîciwin pêtâyiwa, nayêstaw wiyâkan. ||| When he came into view, there, he was bringing no food at all, only the empty bowl.
iyikohk ê-pîhtokêyit, êkoyikohk itohtêw, êkwa ê-kotawêt, êkwa ê-paminawasot, êkwa kahkiyaw waniskâwak, êkwa ê-âh-atoskêcik. ||| When the other came in, he went there and built the fire and cooked, and then they all got up and went about their day's work.
piyis, "mahti nika-itohtân." "tânisi awa tiyôtahk nîstâw?" itêyihtam, ê-itohtêt. ||| Finally, “Suppose I go there. What can my brother-in-law be doing?” he thought, and went there.
pôti sîpiy ê-otihtahk, ati-mitihtêw ita ê-mostâwahkâyik, wîstâwa ê-pâ-pimohtêyit, piyis sakâhk. ||| When he came to the river, he followed the other's tracks on the bare sand, where his brother-in-law had walked, and then into the woods.
kîtahtawê kâ-otihtahk ita êsa mâna kâ-sîkihtitâyit ôhi mîciwina, kâ-mâtâhât wâkayôsa. ||| Presently he came to where, evidently, the other had been in the habit of pouring out that food, and there he found the tracks of a bear.
êkosi isi kîwêw awa wêmistikôsiw. ||| So then that Frenchman went back home.
"êcika awa wâkayôsa ê-pê-nâh-nitawi-asamât!" itêyihtam. ||| “So it is a bear he has always gone off here to feed!” he thought.
iyikohk ê-takohtêt, wîhtamawêw owîkimâkana. ||| When he got back, he told his wife.

I have been down to the place where he feeds it; but I have not seen the bear,” he told her; “So now, do you put a great deal into the bowl, that the bear may stuff itself,” he told her.
êkosi awa iskwêw nêwo êsinâkwaniyik papakiwânêkin nâh-nîso tipahikan iyikohk miyêw ostêsa. ||| Then that woman gave her elder brother four pieces of cotton cloth, all of the same pattern, of two yards each.
"haw, kâ-nâh-nitawi-asamat ôma miyâhkan ôhi," itêw ostêsa; "mîna ôhi nitawi-asam." "kikî-wâpamik kîstâw kâ-nitawi-âh-asamat," itêw ostêsa. ||| “Now, give these to him you always go to feed,” she told her elder brother; “And give him this to eat. tâpwê nitawi-asamêw, kâ-tapasiyit. ||| And really, he went to feed it, and, there, it had run away.
êkwa mitihtêw; ita êkosi ê-paskwâyâyik, êkota miskawêw. ||| Then he tracked it; there where the open country began, there he found it.

He will kill you in the end, if you do not go away,” he told it.
"êha," itik; "â, nikwêmê, kâkikê kisîwâk ohci kika-kanawêyimitn." "kika-okimâwin," itik; "ayisk kisâkwêyimon ta-papâ-wîcêtân," itik. ||| “Very well,” it answered him; “Now, Brother, for all time to come, from close by I shall be guarding you. You will be a chief,” it told him; “It seems that you are unwilling to have me go about with you,” it told him.
êkwa kîwêw êkwa wîstâwa wîkiyihk wêmistikôsiwa. ||| Then he went back to his brother-in-law, the Frenchman's house.
êkota êkwa wâkayôs awa sipwêhtêw. ||| Then the bear went away from there.
êkwa êkota wîstâwa wâskahikanihk ayâw, mitoni ê-miyo-ayât. ||| And he stayed there in his brother-in-law's trading-post, and was very well.
êkosi itêw wîstâwa: "ninôhtê-kîwân," itêw. ||| Then he said to his brother-in-law, “I want to go home,” he told him.
êkosi miyik misatimwa pêyak êkwa aspapiwin. ||| Then the other gave him a horse and a saddle.
êkosi êkwa ê-wâpahk wawêyîw, kahkiyaw kêkway êkwa ayiwinisa ê-miyikot. ||| Then at day-break he got ready, and they gave him all kinds of useful things.
êkosi êkwa sipwêhtêw êkwa, ê-kîwêt. ||| So then he set out, to go home.
nistwâw ê-nipât, êkoyikohk wâpahtam mîkiwâhpa. ||| When he had slept three times, he came in sight of the camp.
êkota ê-takosihk, pôti ôhtâwiya okâwiya êkota ayâyiwa; wâpamêw. ||| When he arrived, there were his father and mother; he saw them.
"tâpwê mistahi nimiywêyihtên nikosis ê-pimâtisit!" "'nipahâw,' ê-kî-itwêhk, kâ-sisikoci-miywêyihtamân ê-wâpamak nikosis!" itik. ||| “Truly, very glad am I that my son is alive! When it had been said, 'He was killed,' truly it is a joyful surprise to see my son!” he said to him.
kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwa ê-atamiskâkot, ê-miywêyihtamiyit ê-pimâtisit, êkosi êkota ohci êkwa kihtêyihtâkosiw awa oskinîkiw. ||| All the people greeted him and were glad that he was alive, and so, from that time on, they all thought a great deal of this young man.
êkosi tâpwê mwêstas iyikohk êsa kî-okimâwiw. ||| Accordingly it really turned out later that he became a chief.
êkosi êkoyikohk ê-iskwâk êwako âcimowin. ||| And so this is the end of the story.
kîtahtawê wêmistikôsiwak mâhamwak êkota wîcihôwin. ||| At the time of which I shall tell, the White Men were going down the river for the Hudson's Bay Company.
êkwa kayâs ê-mâhamoht oskinîkiw pêyak wîcihiwêw. ||| And when thus, long ago, they went down stream, a certain young man joined the Indians who were going along.
êwako ê-pê-kîwêyit owîcêwâkana, kisâtam mâmihk, ê-wîwit êkotê, ê-otinât iskwêwa. ||| Then, when his companions went home again, he stayed in the east, for he had taken a woman to wife there.
mwêhci ê-nisto-pipohk, êkoyikohk kâ-sipwêhtêt, ê-masinahikêt mac-ôhôw. ||| Three years later Bad-Owl hired himself out to the Whites and went away from there.
nêtê ita ê-âywêpicik mâna, êkotê ê-askamâkocik omaskêkôwa pêyak. ||| Down yonder, at a place where they always stopped to rest, a certain Swampy Cree was awaiting their arrival.
mitâtasiyiwa owîkimâkana awa kisêyiniw, omaskêkôw, ê-manitôwit. ||| That old man, that Mushkago, had ten wives, for he was of manitou nature.
kostik sakâw-iyinîsa, osâm ê-manitôwit, mêyosiyici iskwêwa, sôskwâc ê-otinât. ||| The Bush People feared him because he was of manitou nature: whenever there was a pretty woman, at once he would take her for himself.
êkâ tiyâpwêhtâkoci, sêmâk nipahêw. ||| If people resisted him, at once he would kill them.
piyisk êkota ohci kostâw. ||| In time thus, he came to be feared.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw, "kêhcinâ wâpamâci ôhi niwîkimâkana nika-maskamik awa kâ-manitôwit. ||| Then that young man thought, “Surely, if he sees my wife, that manitou person will take her away from me.
osâm miyosiw niwîkimâkan," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| For my wife is beautiful.”
âsay ocawâsimisiwak nâpêsisa; tahkopisoyiwa. ||| By this time they had a child, a boy; he was still in the swaddling bag.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw, "êkoyikohk mâna kâ-takosihkik ayîsiyiniwak natimihk ohci," itêyihtam; "mahti nika-kakwê-wâpamâwak." "kîhkîhk awiyak nêhiyaw ta-masinahikêw," itêyihtam. ||| Then the young man thought, “This is the time when the people from the west always arrive. I had better try to see them. Surely some Plains Cree will be in the river-gang,” he thought.
pôti tâpwê wâpamêw owâhkômâkana nêhiyawa, âtiht êkota nêhiyawak ê-atoskêcik, êwako pêyak mac-ôhôw. ||| And really it turned out that he did see some of his Plains Cree kinsmen, for a number of Cree were working with the gang, and one of them was Bad-Owl.
êkwa ôki omaskêkôwak êkota ayâwak, awa ka-manitôwit kisêyiniw ê-pakosêyimot kîkway ta-miyiht, astisa ê-miyiht mâna, êhtasiyit owîkimâkana kiyikaw âtiht ayiwinisa ê-miyimiht, ôki wêmistikôsiwak ê-miyâcik, ê-kostâcik, ê-mac-âyiwiyit ôhi omaskêkôwa. ||| And those Swampy Cree were there too, and the old man who had manitou power was there, hoping to be given something, for always he was given gloves, and each and all of his wives were given clothing; the White People gave him these things, because they feared him, for an ugly customer was that Mushkago.
kîtahtawê kâ-pê-mâsihât awa omaskêkôw. ||| Then at one time that Mushkago came to seize her.
êkota ayâw mac-ôhôw; sisonê sîpîhk ita ê-kîskatâwahkâyik, cîki êkota ayâw. ||| Bad-Owl was there; on the steep bluff at the edge of the river, close by there he was staying.
kîtahtawê ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa kâ-wâpamât, "mâ kîhkîhkan! ||| Presently, when he saw that young woman, “Dear me, it must come in spite of anything!
kiwâpamitin, piko ta-wîkimitân!" itêw. ||| I have seen you, and now there is nothing but I must marry you!” he said to her.
namôya cêskwa pê-pakosihtâw kêkway, kita-miyiht. ||| He had not yet come to beg for things.
iyâyaw ôhi iskwêwa wî-kakwê-otinêw, ê-wî-kîwêhtahât. ||| He was too intent on taking the woman for himself and taking her home with him.
ê-pê-kîwêcik, ôma iyikohk kâ-wâpamâcik. ||| Then on the way home, this far from them, they saw him.
êkosi awa iskwêw mawimôw. ||| At that the woman began to wail.

pasikôw, ê-ati-nâtât. ||| He rose to his feet and made for him.
mêkwâc maskawisîw awa mac-ôhôw. ||| In those days Bad-Owl was strong.

otinam mac-ôhôw cîkahikan. ||| Bad-Owl picked up an axe.
ê-pê-kapâyit, "kikisiwâhitin cî?" itêw. ||| When the other came to land, “Have I made you angry?” he asked him.
"êhâw, nitôtêm, namôya kikisiwâhin! ||| “Yah, Fellow-Tribesman, you have not made me angry!

As now you go on your river voyage, you will continue to be on your guard as you go along. And if you pass the things that will be on your way, also, you will be on your guard; you will see my servant. And if you pass this, there where you camp you will see my little pet beast. And if you pass him, then yonder you will look out for my servant; and this last one you will not pass,” he was told by that Mushkago who was a manitou.
katisk ê-nêyâyik ê-awasêwêskahkik, kîtahtawê kêkway pahkihtiniyiw ospiskwanihk. ||| As soon as they had passed the first sharp bend in the river, suddenly something fell on his back.
ômisi ê-tôtahk, pôti ôhi amiskosîsa. ||| When he did like this, it turned out to be a beaver-bug.
tahki kâh-kiyipa otihtikôw kêkway, awa omaskêkôw ê-itisahahk. ||| Unceasingly, at short intervals things reached him, things which the Swampy Cree had sent.

nama wî-naskwâw awa mac-ôhôw. ||| Bad-Owl did not care to retaliate.

êkwa awa otatâwêw, "mac-ôhôw, nimâkohik awa kâ-wî-otihtikoyahk." "kîspin sâkohtâyini, pêyakwasâkay mihkwêkin kika-miyitin, êkwa ôma iskotêwâpoy," itêw. ||| Then the trader said, “Bad-Owl, I dread this which is about to come upon us. "êha." "namôya ana pisiskiw; pistôs ana." "êkosi nikî-wâpamâw." ||| “Very well! That is no beast; it is a whirlwind. I have seen the like of it.”
