"êha, nitôtêm, kâwi kika-miyitin, êkâ wîhkâc kîhtwâm êkosi ta-tôtaman;" "kôskinîkîmak nika-mêsci-pakamahwâwak." "'mâka pita pêyakwâw nika-wâpamâw.'" "'êkâ wî-tôtahki ôma kê-isi-kitotak, mahti nîsta êkospî kiyâm nitêma kita-wâpamêw, ta-mâsihikot,' kikî-itêyimitin." "mâka awa kiwîkimâkan kâwi kika-ayâwâw." "piko wâh-itâhpihiskik kôskinîkîmak, ka-itâhpihikwak ôki kôskinîkîmak." "êkwa okîskwêwak ita ê-kî-otinacik kita-isi-kîwêwak." "kîspin êkâ tôtamani, kika-misi-wanâcihitin." ||| “Very well, Fellow-Tribesman, I will give her back to you, on condition that never again you do as you have done. I shall strike down your helpers to the very last one. 'I shall give him one more interview. If he is not willing to do as I shall tell him, then let him in turn see my familiar beasts and wrestle with them,' is what I thought concerning you. But now you shall again have this wife of yours. In whatever way your followers may feel inclined to laugh at you, they will laugh at you. And these women are to go back from wherever you have taken them. If you do not do so, I shall destroy you beyond redemption.”
"êha, nitôtêm, nika-tôtên;" "ninôhtê-pimâtisin." "pêyak piko nika-miywêyimâw awa kâ-kî-otinat." "êkwa ôki kotakak ta-kîwêwak owâhkômâkaniwâwa." ||| “Yes, Fellow-Tribesman, I will do so; I wish to live. I am fond only of the one you took. These others may go back to their relatives.”
"osâm mihcêt kikanawêyimâwak." "misawâc nika-pêhtên, kîhtwâm nipahtâyêko." "êkosi kitisi-kitahamâtin, êkâ ta-maci-nôcihtâyan." ||| “You have altogether too many wives. I shall not fail to hear of it, if you do any more killing. And so now I forbid you to exercise any more evil arts.”
"êha, nitôtêm, nika-tôtên anima kâ-itwêyan;" "osâm ninôhtê-pimâtisin, mîna awa niwîkimâkan ê-sâkihak." "kika-wâpamâwak kita-kîwêcik." ||| “Yes, Fellow-Tribesman, I shall do this which you say; I want to live, and I love this wife of mine. You will see that they go home.”
wayawîwak, nanânis ê-isi-kîwêcik ôki kotakak iskwêwak, êkota ohci êsa kâ-kî-kostikot omaskêkôwa awa mac-ôhôw. ||| They went out of the tipi, and those other women went to their several homes, and all because evidently the Mushkago feared Bad-Owl.
êkoyikohk êskwâk âcimôwin. ||| That is the end of the story.
nêhiyaw pêyak, osîma oskinîkiwa. ||| A certain Cree had a younger brother, a mere youth.
awa ostêsimâw pêyakoyiwa okosisa. ||| The elder brother had one son.
mistahi âhkosiyiwa, ê-apisîsisit awa nâpêsis. ||| This little boy fell very sick.
êkwa atoskêmôw, ayîsiyiniwa ê-atotât. ||| The man sought medical aid, employing people to use their power.
"mâskôc awa kâ-sâkihak nikosis kita-nipiw," itêyihtam. ||| “Perhaps my beloved son is to die,” he thought.
kîtahtawê awa oskinîkiw, ostêsa ê-sêkisiyit, "mahti, nistêsê, wâpatonisk miyin," itêw ostêsa. ||| Then at one time that youth whose brother was in fear, said to him, “Come, Brother, give me some white paint-clay.”
piyisk misiwê wâpatonisk astêw. ||| Then he put the white clay all over his body.
âta ê-âhkosiyit okosisiwâwa, otinêw, ê-wayawîhtahât awa oskinîkiw. ||| Although their son was ill, the youth took him up, and carried him out of the tent.
ê-pîhtokahât ôhi awâsisa, miyw-âyâyiwa. ||| When he brought the child in again, he was well.
êkosi kîtahtawê wîwiw; tâpiskôc wîwiwak ostêsa. ||| Then, in the course of time, he took a wife; he took his wife from the same family as had his elder brother.
"hâw, nisîm, atâwâkanak nôcihâtân; paskêpicitân," itêw osîma. ||| “Come, Younger Brother, let us go in pursuit of furs; let us move camp away from the band,” he said to his younger brother.
âsay otawâsimisiwak awa oskinîkiw; misikitiyiwa, ê-pimitâcimoyit. ||| The youth and his wife had by this time a child; it was of a size to be crawling about.
kîtahtawê ê-mâcîcik, êkwa awa iskwêw nikohtêw. ||| Then at one time, as they were hunting, that woman gathered wood.
kîtahtawê ê-tipiskâyik, êkâ ê-takosihk, nitonikêwak ostêsa. ||| Presently, as darkness fell and she did not arrive, the youth and his brother searched.
namôya miskawêwak; namôya mâtâhêwak. ||| They did not find her; they did not come upon her tracks.
"mâskôc nipiw sisikoc," itêyihtamwak. ||| “Perhaps she suddenly died,” they thought.
êkwa ostêsa saskahamawêw. ||| Then he offered his elder brother a lighted pipe.
"nistêsê, kakwê-kiskêyim kîtim." "kikosisinaw mistahi mâtôw," itêw. ||| “My, elder brother, try to know about your sister-in-law. Our son is crying much,” he told him.
"nisîm, ôta omêskanaw awa nîtim piko niwâpahtên, êkota ôma kâ-nitonikêyahk." "namôya nânitaw nitisi-wâpahtên ta-misi-wanâtisit awa nîtim ka-wanihâyahk." ||| “My younger brother, here I see only the path of my sister-in-law, even there where we made search. Not in any way do I see that my sister-in-law whom we have lost has gone to her ruin.”
wiyaskinahêw awa ostêsimâw. ||| The elder brother filled a pipe.
êkwa miyâw ospwâkana. ||| He gave the other the pipe.
"nisîm, êwako ana pîhtwâ." "kakwê-miskaw nîtim." "namôya misi-wanâtisiw." "mâskôc kêkway kikiskêyihtên," itêw osîma. ||| “My younger brother, smoke this. Try to find my sister-in-law. She has not been destroyed. Perhaps you have some mystic power,” he said to his younger brother.
êkwa pîhtwâw awa oskinîkiw. ||| Then the youth smoked.
êkwa itohtêw ita kâ-nikohtêyit owîkimâkana. ||| Then he went to where his wife had gathered wood.
êkwa ê-pipohk; ômayikohk osita kaskitênam; êkwa ôhi ocihciya kaskitênam awa oskinîkiw. ||| It was winter; he blackened his feet, here; and he blackened his hands, the youth.
êkwa itohtêw; ê-otihtahk owîkimâkana ita ê-kî-nikohtêyit, nitonikêw. ||| Then he went there; when he came to where his wife had gathered firewood, he searched.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpahtahk ita ê-kî-nîpawiyit owîkimâkana; ita ê-tahkoskêyit êkota nîpawiw. ||| Presently he saw a place where his wife had stood; upon the imprints of her feet he placed his feet, as he stood.
ita ê-ayîtiskêyit, êkota tahkoskêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| Upon the imprints of her feet, as she had gone, step after step, the youth placed his feet, as he walked.
pahkêkin akwanahôw; êwako piko mosêskatêw. ||| He had a skin wrapped round him; but for this garment he was unclothed.
êkwa tahkoskêw ita ê-kî-tahkoskêyit owîkimâkana. ||| Then he made his steps wherever his wife had set foot.
kîtahtawê êkota ohci ê-itâpit, pôti ôma tâpiskôc pîsimwêyâpiy isinâkwaniyiw omêskanaw awa iskwêw, nayêwac ê-pimakocihk. ||| Presently, as he looked on ahead, lo, there, like a rainbow looked the trail of that woman, as she had left the ground and floated through the air.
ohpîw awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth took off from the ground.
nayêwac pimakocin, tâpiskôc ê-pimihât. ||| He floated through the air as though he were flying.
pôti wâhyaw ê-ayât, pôti minahikwâhtikwa ê-nawêyâskosiniyit, êkota êsa kâ-nipâyit, namôya tâpwê ê-nipât, ê-owîcimosit anihi kâ-sipwêhtahikot. ||| Behold, when he had gone a long ways, where a pine tree lay across the path, there she must have slept, - not that she had really slept, but where she had taken for her lover him who had abducted her.
êkota ohci ohpiyiwa. ||| From there she had again risen aloft.
ohpîw wîsta, êkwa ê-pimakocihk nayêwac. ||| He too rose aloft, gliding again through the air.
kîtahtawê kâ-ati-nîhtakociniyit. ||| Presently she had again gone down to the ground.
ati-nîhtakocin wîsta. ||| He, too, at that point, went down to the ground.
kîtahtawê mohcihk êkwa ati-pimohtêyiwa, ê-sêskisiyit minahikoskâhk. ||| Then she had walked on, on the earth, and had gone into a wood of pines.
pôti kâ-wâpahtahk wîstêpahkwayikamik ê-mâyâtaniyik, ê-misâyik. ||| There he beheld a large and ugly tent of old leather rags.
kotak wâpahtam ê-apisâsiniyik. ||| He saw another and smaller one.
pôti ôhi kî-apiyiwa wêskwâhtêmihk; kotaka nâpêwa pimitakâm apiyiwa. ||| Lo, there they sat, opposite the doorway; another man sat across the lodge from them.
kiki-apiyiwa owîkimâkana, ê-wîtapimâyit pâkahkosa. ||| There sat his wife, sitting by the side of a bony spectre.
awa pimitakâm kâ-apit, êwako tapahtiskwêyiw kotak pâkahkos, ê-ostêsit awa pâkahkos kâ-kimotit iskwêwa. ||| That other bony spectre who sat aross the lodge, lowered his head; and he was the elder brother of him who had stolen the woman.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw pimohtêw, pâskisikan apasôhk ê-takopitêyik, ê-wâpihtakâyik; "pâskisikan pôti ôma! ||| Then that youth walked over to where a gun hung from the lodgepole; it looked like a bleached stick; he thought, “So this is a gun!
wîsta nika-otinên ôma pâskisikan; nîsta êwako nika-ayân!" itêyihtam. ||| From him, in turn, I shall take the gun; I, in turn, shall have it!”
êkwa ê-otinahk, pimakocin awa iskwêwa kâ-kimotit pâkahkos, ê-pâhpit. ||| As he took it, that bony spectre who had stolen the woman, came reaching for it, with a peal of laughter.
"nikosâk, pakitina ôma nipâskisikan!" "ê-sâkihtâyân ôma nipâskisikan!" "kîwinaw kîwêhta!" itwêw awa pâkahkos. ||| “My follow-husband, let go of this my gun! I love this gun of mine! Take back our wife!” said the bony spectre.
âsay kikî-otinâw, ê-mêkwâ-sâkihak nîsta." "kêkway ê-sâkihtâyan niwî-otinên." "êwako ohci kipâskisikan kâ-ôh-pê-nâtamân." "nîsta ê-sâkihak mêkwâc kîwa, kikî-pê-nâtâw." "êkosi namôya ta-kî-wîwiyân." ||| That is why I have come to take your gun. When I loved her who is your wife, you came and took her. So now I cannot have her to wife.”
"â, nikosâk, kiyâm miyin nipâskisikan; mistahi nisâkihtân!" itwêw awa pâkahkos. ||| “Oh, Fellow-Husband, please, give me my gun; I prize it too highly!” cried the bony spectre.
"namôya ka-kî-miyitin." ||| “I shall not by any chance give it to you.”
"ahpô nama wîhkâc kêkway ka-pwâtawihtân." "ka-nihtâ-nipahtân kêkway pisiskiwak." "tahki ka-wîcêtin." ||| “If you wish, never will you fail of any game. You will be good at killing every kind of beast. Always I shall go at your side.”
"namôya!" itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “No!” said the youth.
êkwa awa ostêsimâw wayawîw, ôhtâwiya ê-nitawi-nitomât. ||| Then that elder one went out of the tent to call his father.
pôti awa kisêyiniw pâkahkos pîhtokêw. ||| The old man Koshtchey entered.
"hây, nitawâsimisak kî-nîpawîstâtowak." "âta nôton, 'êkâ wiya êkotôwahk iyinito-ayisiyiniw ohtin iskwêw,' nikî-itâw awa nikosis; "manitôwiwak iyini-ayisiyiniw," nikî-itâw mâna, wiyîhtamawaki kêkway, âhci piko kâ-tôtahk, kâ-katâc ê-onâpêmiyit kâ-maskahtwêt awa nikakêpâtisîm, êkâ ê-tâpwêhtawit." "- nikosis, êkosi awa ê-tâpwêt, awa kikosâk kâ-isi-wîhtamâsk." "kapê-tipisk ka-nikamohitinân, tânisi ta-tôtaman." "kiyâm niya kitimâkihtawin." "mistahi nisâkihtânân nipâskisikaninâna." "êwako awa ostêsimâw kiciwâm ninahihtâk;" "tânisi ê-itak tôtam, awa kikosâk ê-kakêpâtisit, kâ-nitawi-kimotamâsk kiwîkimâkana." "êkosi anihi ê-tâpwêt, ôma kâ-itisk." ||| “Alas, my children have stood facing each other! Although often, 'Do not take a woman of the common, mortal men,' I said to my son; 'Of manitou nature are real men,' though I told him more than once, when I instructed him, yet none the less he did so, robbing, as if none other would serve, one who had a husband, this stubborn fool of mine, who does not heed my words. - My son, even thus he speaks true, this thy fellow-husband, in what he has told thee. All night we will teach thee songs and how to do. Pray, hear me with pity. We greatly prize our guns. This one here, your kinsman now, obeys my word; as I tell him, he does, while he, your fellow-husband is foolish and stubborn, and thus has gone and stolen your wife from you. But in this he spoke true which he told you.”
"êha." "êkâ wiya kiyâski." "awa nika-kîwêhtahâw kîwinaw," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “Very well. Do not speak false. I shall take home with me this wife of ours,” said the youth.
"pêyakotipiskwa piko ôta nika-ayânân; wâpahki nika-kîwânân awa kistim." ||| “One night only we shall stay here; tomorrow your daughter-in-law here and I shall go home.”
"hâ, niciwâ, kitatamihin, ê-tâpwêhtawat kôhtâwiyinaw." "ê-atamihiyan, nama wîhkâc ayîsiyiniw ka-kîhikon." "iyâhkosici, kika-pimâcihâw; ahpô awâsis, iskwêw, nama wîhkâc ka-kîhikon kita-pimâcihat." "hâw, niciwâ, êkosi niya kitisi-miyitin." "kikosâk minahôwin kiwîhtamâk, ta-wahkê-nipahtâyan kêkway pisiskiwak." ||| “There, Kinsman, I thank you for having lent ear to him who is now your father as well as ours. Because you have done me this favor, never shall mortal man be lost to you. Whenever one is sick, you shall restore him to life; be it a child, a woman, never shall he be beyond your power of restoring him to life. There, brother, this is my gift to you. Your fellow-husband promised you the killing of game, of every kind of beast.”
"êkwa niya, nikosis, mâhtâhitôwin kika-isiyîhkâtên; êwako niya kimiyitin." "pimiy asamîhkan, takosiniyani kîkiwâhk." "êkota cîki kâ-wîkiyêk nîso môswak kimiyitin, kita-asamiyan, êkota ohci pimiy kita-otinaman." "êkosi awa kiciwâm kâ-itwêt, êkosi nîsta kitisi-miyitin." ||| “And I, my son, Potlatch you will call it; this is what I give to you. Give me fat to eat, when you arrive at your home. Close by to where you dwell, two moose I give you, that you may feed me, that you may take the fat from them. And even as your brother said, even such a gift I too am giving you.”
êkwa nikamohik okosâka. ||| Then his fellow-husband taught him songs.
ê-kîsi-nikamohikot, ê-wâpaniyik, wayawîwak owîkimâkana awa oskinîkiw. ||| When he had been taught the songs, and day had come, the youth and his wife went from that tent.
pâkahkos wayawîw mîna, ê-wîcêwât okosâka. ||| The bony spectre, too, went out, to escort his fellow-husband.
"hâw, nikosâk, êkâya kotaka nâpêwa kita-ayâwêw kîwinaw." "kêtiski-ayîsiyinîwiwin kimiyitin." "mîna kikosisinaw ta-kêtiski-ayîsiyinîwiw." "tâpwê êkâ wiya wîhkâc kita-mâmawîhitow kîwinaw; nikâhkwêyihtaskin." ||| “Very well, Fellow-Husband; let not our wife have dealings with other men. I give you a full span of life. And our son, too, shall live a full span of life. But see to it that our wife never be guilty of adultery; I am jealous in marriage.”
êkosi kîwêwak owîkimâkana. ||| So he and his wife went home.
takohtêwak wîkiwâhk. ||| They reached their dwelling.
posko-kîsik mâcîw awa oskinîkiw. ||| That same day the youth hunted.
nîso nipahêw môswa ê-wiyinoyit; kahkiyaw otinam pimiya oskanihk ohci, êkwa êwako ê-asamât ôhtâwiya, ociwâma, okosâka. ||| He killed two fat moose; he took all the marrow from the bones, and made of it an offering to his adoptive father and brother and to his fellow-husband.
êkwa aspin ê-ispayik namôya âcimôw awa oskinîkiw. ||| And the youth did not tell of what had happened from the time he went away.
namôya kakwêcimêw osîma awa nâpêw. ||| That man did not question his younger brother.
"tânisi êtokê tiyôtahk awa nisîm, kâ-pêsiwât owîkimâkana!" "kêhcinâ manitôwiw awa nisîm!" itêyihtam awa ostêsimâw. ||| “I wonder how my younger brother did, to bring back his wife! Surely my younger brother has manitou power!” thought the elder brother.
êkwa ôho okosisiwâwa tânitahto askiy ê-wî-ohpikiyit, kîtahtawê ê-kwâpikêt awa iskwêw, kotaka nâpêwa kâ-kitotât, ê-mâmawîhitot. ||| Then when that son of theirs, after I know not how many years, was nearly grown, then at one time, when that woman was fetching water, she had converse with another man, and committed adultery.
ê-kîwêt, awiya kâ-pakamahokot otihtimanihk. ||| As she went home, someone struck her on the shoulder.
êkosi sêmâk âhkosiw. ||| Then at once she became ill.
mayaw ê-âhkosiyit, awa nâpêw atoskêmôw, ta-nânapâcihimiht owîkimâkana. ||| As soon as she fell sick, that man called in doctors, that his wife might have treatment.
êkota ohci kiskêyihtam ê-pakamahomiht owîkimâkana. ||| In this way he learned that his wife had been struck.
"nikî-kâh-kitotâw êwako ana oskinîkiw." "êkosi ê-pê-kîwêyân, êkota kâ-pasastêhokawiyân nitihtimanihk; êwako ohci kâ-âhkosiyân." ||| “I had been having a talk with that young man. Then, as I was coming home, I was struck with a stick or switch on my shoulder; from that I am sick.”
piyisk kêkâc nipiw awa iskwêw mihcêtwayak ê-atoskêmohk. ||| At last that woman was close to death, though many kinds of doctoring were tried.
piyisk awa awa oskinîkiw kâ-wîwit ostêsa miyik ospwâkana, kita-pîhtwât. ||| At last the youth whose wife she was, was given a pipe by his elder brother, that he smoke.
"kakwê-nânapâci nîtim, nisîm." "nama nânitaw âsay kî-tôtawâw." ||| “Try to treat my sister-in-law, Younger Brother. All kinds of treatment have already been given her.”
"hâw, ôma kâ-sakâk êkota osîhtâk têsipicikan," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “Very well, over in that grove set up a scaffold,” said the youth.
êkosi osîhtâwân têsipicikan. ||| Accordingly a scaffold was built for him.
êkwa ê-tipiskâyik, êkotê itohtahâw awa iskwêw kâ-âhkosit. ||| Then, at nightfall, the sick woman was taken there.
ê-kîwêcik, namwâc cêskwa otihtam awa wîkiwâw, awa oskinîkiw, awa mîna ostêsimâw, âsay ita wîtimwa kâ-akociniyit, êkota âsay kâ-matwêwêyik, ê-sâkowêwiht. ||| When they went back home, that youth with his elder brother had not yet reached their dwelling-place, when already, from where the latter's sister-in-law lay high on the scaffold, there came the report of a gun, and they heard shouting.
"nikosâk, kîwinaw pê-nâs; âsay pimâtisiw," itâw. ||| “My fellow-husband, come get our wife; already she is cured,” he was told.
itohtêw kâwi awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth went back there.
kahkiyaw pêhtawâw awa pâkahkos tânisi ê-itwêt. ||| Everything was heard which that bony spectre said.
pôti wêtihtât owîkimâkana, âsay nîhtakosiyiwa. ||| When he reached his wife, she was already climbing down.
ê-takohtêt wîkiwâhk, âsay miyo-ayâw awa iskwêw, mistahi kâ-kî-âhkosit. ||| When she reached their dwelling, she was already well, sick as she had been.
êkosi êkota ohci kiskêyimâw awa oskinîkiw ê-mamâhtâwisit. ||| So then from this the youth was known to have magic powers.
êkosi awa ê-pimâtisit awa iskwêw. ||| Thus this woman was restored to life.
êkosi êkwa awa oskinîkiw mâhtâhitôwinihkêw. ||| And then that youth arranged a potlatch ceremony.
êkosi kostâw êkwa, ê-manitôwit ê-itêyimiht. ||| And then he was feared, because he was thought to have spirit power.
namôya awiya nôcîhkamâk. ||| And his wife was not wooed by any man.
êkwa êkota kâ-ohcipayik nêhiyawak ê-mâhtâhitocik. ||| And from this it came that the Cree have the potlatch.
êkoyikohk iskwâw âcimowin. ||| Here ends the story.
pêyak nâpêw kotokwaskisin isiyîhkâsôw. ||| A certain man was called Crooked-Moccasin.
êkwa kîtahtawê kîkisêpâ sipwêhtêw, ê-mâcît, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahât pisiskiwa. ||| Once upon a time he set out in the morning, to hunt, meaning to kill some game.
wâpahtam mitoni kîkisêpâ ê-mihcêniyiki mîkiwâhpa. ||| Early in the morning he saw a great many tipis.
êkwa ê-pimohtêt mêkwâc, kîtahtawê paskwâw wâpahtam; wâsakâm sakâyiw. ||| As he walked along, presently he saw an open meadow; round about were woods.
"êwako nika-taskamohtân," ê-itêyihtahk, kîtahtawê ka-wâpamât ayîsiyiniwa ê-pê-matâwisiyit. ||| “I shall walk across this,” he was thinking, when he saw a man come into the open.
nîmipâskisikanêyiwa. ||| That person was carrying a gun.
tawâyihk paskwâhk ê-pimohtêt awa kotokwaskisin, "nâha kotak ayîsiyiniw," itêyihtam, "kêhcinâ nika-têpâskiskawâw," itêyihtam. ||| As Crooked-Moccasin was walking in the middle of the meadow, “Yonder man,” he thought, “surely I shall meet him as our paths cross,” he thought.
pôti tâpwê têpâskiskawêw. ||| It really turned out that he encountered the other at the point where their ways crossed.
sêmâk wîhik: "yahô, kotokwaskisin! ||| At once the other called him by name: “Yoho, Crooked-Moccasin!
kêswân êtokê nêkiskotâtoyahk!" ||| It is by chance, I suppose, that we meet!”
êkosi ômisi itik, pêskis ê-pâhpit awa kâ-nakiskâkêt; ê-kitâpamât, awîna awa, pâkahkos awa kâ-pâhpit; ômisi itêw: "kotokwaskisin, kakwê-sâkohitotân!" "kipâskisikaninawa astwâtotân; awiyak sâkohihci kita-otahwâw opâskisikan." ||| Then the other spoke thus to him, and at the same time he laughed, who had encountered him; when he looked at him, why, that person who laughed was a Bony Spectre. This he said to him: “Crooked-Moccasin, let us try to overcome each other! Let us put up our guns as a stake; whoever is overcome will lose his gun.”
"namôya," itêw kotokwaskisin; "namôya ê-papâ-mâsihkêyân," itêw. ||| “No,” Crooked-Moccasin told him; “I am not going about wrestling,” he told him.
"namôya, kotokwaskisin; kiyâm mâsihitotâk." "awiyak sâkohihci kita-otahwâw opâskisikan," itwêw awa pâkahkos. ||| “No, Crooked-Moccasin; please, let us wrestle. Whichever is defeated will lose his gun,” said the Bony Spectre.
namôya ê-papâ-mêtawêyân; pisiskiw ê-wî-kakwê-nipahak," itêw ôhi pâkahkosa. ||| I am not going about to engage in matches; I want to kill game,” he told the Bony Spectre.
"hâ, kiyâm mâsihitotân." "ta-miywâsin, awiyak opâskisikan otahohci." "sâkohiyani, nîso kika-ayân pâskisikana." "pêyak nama wîhkâc ka-patahikâhkân, nipâskisikan otahoyani." "êkwa niya otahotâni, nôhtâwiy nika-miyâw ayîsiyiniw opâskisikan." "ê-nôhtê-wâpahtahk, kâ-ôh-pê-nakiskâtân." "'nika-kakwê-otahwâw opâskisikan,' ê-itêyimitân, êwako ohci kâ-ôh-pê-nakiskâtân." ||| “Oh, please, let us wrestle. It will be fine, when one of us loses his gun. If you defeat me, you will have two guns. With one you will never miss the mark, if you win my gun from me. And if I win yours, I shall give my father a human being's gun. Because he wants to see one, is why I have come here to meet you. 'I shall try to win his gun from him,' was my thought concerning you, owing to which I have come here and met you.”
"hâw, wêsâ kitisimin!" ||| “Well, you urge me too much!”
astâw opâskisikan awa kotokwaskisin; awa mîna pâkahkos. ||| Crooked-Moccasin put down his gun; so did the Bony Spectre.
otihtinitôwak, ê-wî-kakwê-kawiwêpinitocik. ||| They grappled, trying to throw each other.
mwêhci ê-nayawît awa kotokwaskisin, âcikêhwêw; pakamisiniyiwa, ê-kawiwêpinât ôhi pâkahkosa. ||| Just as Crooked-Moccasin was tiring, he tripped the other; he threw the Bony Spectre, who fell hard on the ground.
pâhpiw awa pâkahkos. ||| The Bony Spectre laughed.
"nitaka kiskât nipiswahên," itik ôhi pâkahkosa; "êkwa êyâpic pêyakwâw!" itik. ||| “By chance I stumbled over your leg,” the Bony Spectre said to him; “Come, once more!” he said to him.
otihtinitôwak; âsay mîna mâsihitôwak. ||| They grappled; they wrestled again.
kêyâpic ê-wî-nayawît, âcikêhwêw pâkahkosa; âsay mîna kawiwêpinêw. ||| Once more, as he was about to give out, he tripped the Bony Spectre; again he threw him.
âsay mîna pâhpiw awa pâkahkos. ||| Again the Bony Spectre laughed.
"kotokwaskisin, nitaka nipiswahên kiskât, kâ-ôh-sâkohiyan." "êyâpic pêyakwâw!" itik, pêskis ê-pâhpit awa pâkahkos. ||| “Crooked-Moccasin, by chance I stumbled over your leg; that is how you got me down. Once more!” the Bony Spectre said to him, and laughed.
êkwa ômisi itêw: "êha, namôya êkwa kika-âstêtâmosininânaw." ||| Then he said to him, “Yes, but this time we shall not stop for a rest.”
âsay mîna mâsihitôwak. ||| They wrestled again.
piyisk mîna nayawîw awa ayîsiyiniw. ||| At last the mortal man again grow tired.
mîna ê-nayawît, âsay mîna âcikêhwêw; âsay mîna kawiwêpinêw. ||| Again, as he wearied, he tripped the other; again he threw him to the ground.
âsay mîna pâhpiw awa pâkahkos. ||| Again the Bony Spectre laughed.
"nitaka kiskât nipiswahên, kâ-ôh-sâkohiyan." "êyâpic pêyakwâw!" itwêw awa pâkahkos. ||| “By chance I tripped over your leg; that is how you got me down. Once more!” said the Bony Spectre.
âsay mîna otihtinitôwak. ||| Again they grappled.
âsay mîna ê-nayawît awa kotokwaskisin, âsay mîna âcikêhwêw. ||| Again, as Crooked-Moccasin was tiring, he tripped the other.
sâkohêw; kawiwêpinêw. ||| He overcame him; he threw him.
êkwa pâhpiw awa pâkahkos. ||| Then the Bony Spectre laughed.

"êwako nipahikêhkâci: kotak mîna êkota ohci kita-ayisiyinîwiw." ||| “There, Crooked-Moccasin, twice a full span of human life you have here won from me. Already five times the full span have mortal men so far stayed on this earth. Thus it is that I say twice. When you in your present person leave the earth, another will take up mortal life where you leave off. When he dies of old age, still another will from that point on live a human life.”
nama kîkway wâpahtam awa kotokwaskisin. ||| Crooked-Moccasin saw nothing.
otinamiyiwa kîkway ê-tâpiskamiyit. ||| The other took something from round his neck.
"ôma mîna pêyak ê-otahoyan, miyêtawêyini kita-âpacihtâyan." "namôya wiya ayîsiyiniw ka-kakwê-kitimahâw, têpiyâhk êkâ kêkway ta-mêskoskaman, kînikâw ohtiskawinamâski ana kê-wîci-mêtawêmat." "êkwa ôma nipâskisikan." "awa kêtiskâwi-kêtiski-ayisiyinîwit, âpihtaw âpihtâwi-ayisiyinîwici êwako awa, kiyi-otihtikoyêk wêmistikôsiw." "êwako awa kita-wâpamêw ta-mihcêtiyit wêmistikôsiwa." "êkospî ôma kika-âpacihtân." ||| “Here is another thing which you have won from me, to use when you engage in contests. You will not, indeed, try to destroy people, but, only so that you need fear nothing, if he draw a sharp weapon against you, with whom you are playing. And here is my gun. When he who lives the full span of mortal life is halfway through his human course, then the Frenchman will come to where you are. He will see the Frenchmen grow many. At that time you will use this thing.”
otinamiyiwa ostikwâniyihk, awîna ôma, mêstakaya ê-kinwâyiki. ||| He took it from his head, and it was nothing other than a long hair.
"nanâtohk kita-isi-mêtawêw; êkota kîsta kika-âpacihtân." "êkwa kîwêyani, ôta ohci ka-kîwân." "kâ-wîkiyan âstamita kâ-sakâk, kotak âscam-itahîs apisîs sakâsin." "êkota kika-ohtinên kita-asamiyan." Now, when you go home, go directly home from here. In the wood that is this side of where you dwell, a bit to this side is a small clump of trees. From there you will get that with which to feed me. In that place are moose; I give them to you. You are too pitiable; you all are too pitiable who are mortal men. Give me an offering of fat,” the Bony Spectre told him; “And yes, take home this gun of mine; for you have won it from me.”
kîwêw awa kotokwaskisin. ||| Crooked-Moccasin went home.
awa mîna pâkahkos mîna êwako sipwêhtêw. ||| The Bony Spectre, too, went away from there.
nama kêkway opâskisikan; ayis otahwâw. ||| He had no gun; he had lost it playing.

kotaka mîna pâskiswêw; mîna êwakoni nipahêw. ||| He shot also the other and killed it.

tâpwê osihtâwân pimiy. ||| Accordingly the fat was prepared for him.

êkosi êkwa ôma mêkwâc kâ-nitohkêmot, êwako ohci nêwo-tipiskâyiw, ôhi kâ-kî-mâsihât pâkahkosa. ||| And then when he invited his guests, it was four nights from the time when he had wrestled with the Bony Spectre.

mahti nika-wâpahtên manitowi-pâskisikan," itwêw awa pêyak kisêyiniw, "kahkiyaw kita-wâpahtamahk," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| Let me see the spirit being's gun,” said a certain old man, “that all may see it,” said old man.

êkwa, "hâw, piko itwêyêko nika-tôtên." "nikiskinôhamâk êkâ wîhkâc kita-patahamân kêkway, piyâskisamâni." "nama wîhkâc nika-pîhtâson." "sôskwâc tamâkonamân, êkosi kita-isi-matwêwêk." ||| Then, “Now, whatever you say, I shall do so. He instructed me so that I shall never miss a mark when I shoot. I shall never need to load it. "hâw, kiyâm astâ." "nama wîhkâc êkotowahk ayâw ayîsiyiniw." "osâm kika-misi-wanâcihtân." "kiyâm nitawi-astâ," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Well then, you had better put it away. Never has mortal had the like of it. You will work too much destruction. You had better put it down,” said the old man.
ê-sîhkimiht kotokwaskisin kiyâm kita-astât, tâpwêhtam. ||| When Crooked-Moccasin was urged to give it up, he obeyed.
êkosi nitawi-astâw; nîpisîhkopâhk akotâw. ||| So he went to put it away; he hung it up in a willow grove.
ômisi itwêw: "awa, nîci-pakês! ||| He spoke thus: “Come, my opponent at play! This gun I give back to you.
ôma pâskisikan kâwi kimiyitin." "anihi wiya kotaka êwakoni namôya kimiyitin, kêtisk ayîsiyinîwiwin kâ-otahotân." "osâm kostamwak nitôtêmak ôma kipâskisikan." "anihi mîna kitayôwinisa kâ-otahotân, êwakoni mîna namôya kâwi ka-kî-miyitin; ôma piko kipâskisikan, êwako piko kâ-miyitân." ||| But those other things I do not give you, the full span of life which I have won from you. nama awiya wâpamêw; konita pâ-pîkiskwêw. ||| He saw no one; he continued to speak into space.

êwako âcimowin kayâs. ||| This is an ancient tale.
êwako kisêyiniw nipahikêhkâw. ||| This old man died of age.
êkota, ôma niya, kisêyinîwici ayîsiyiniw, êwako pêyak kêtisk ayisiyiniw; kotak ta-nihtâwikiw. ||| Here, when even as I, a man grows old, that is one full span of life; another will be born.
êkoyikohk isko kêtisk ayisiyiniwiwin; nama êskwa ihtâw êwako. ||| So long is a full span of life; not yet does he exist.
kêyâpic kinwêsk kitayân askiy; kêyâpic nama mayaw ta-pêkopayiw. ||| Still for a long time the earth will be; not yet for a while will it go to pieces.
êkoyikohk êwako êskwâk âcimowin. ||| That is the end of this story.
kîtahtawê ôki nêhiyawak ôta,- pêhonân isiyîhkâtêw,- êkota ê-wîkicik, pêyak awa oskinîkiw ê-miyosit, êkwa ôhtâwiya ê-okimâwiyit, pêyakow; nama awiya wîtisâna. ||| Once upon a time when some Cree were staying right here, - Place-of-Waiting-for-Each-Other (Battleford) it is called, - there was a certain handsome youth whose father was chief, and he was an only child; he had no brothers or sisters.
êkosi kitimâkêyimâw. ||| So he was tenderly cared for.
namôya atoskêw ta-mâcît; namôya: piko pisisik ê-mêtawêt, wiyâkan mistikoyâkan êwako ê-mêtawâkêt; "ê-pakêsêt," isiyîhkâtêw êwako mêtawêwin. ||| He did no work in the way of hunting; instead, he always played, and what he played with was a cup, a wooden bowl; the cup-game this game is called.
mâka mistahi sâkihtâw ôma mistikoyâkan, êkâ kâ-mêtawêt piko ê-pîmakâmêskahk ôma, ahpô ê-nipât âskaw ê-kikiskahk. ||| He was very much devoted to this wooden bowl; when he was not playing, he wore it on a strap round his shoulder, and even when he slept he sometimes kept it on his person.
kîtahtawê ôma êkota ê-wa-wîkicik, kâ-pâpiciyit wâhyaw ohci sakâw-iyinîsa, mâka ê-macihtwâyit, ê-manitôwiyit. ||| Then at one time, as they made a long stay here, one of those Bush-Fellows moved his camp here from afar, and he was one who practised evil, and a manitou person.
êkwa ê-âh-atâwêyit, atâwêwikamikohk itohtêwak ê-nisticik oskinîkiwak. ||| Then, when he was doing his trading, three young men went to the trading-post.
kîtahtawê kâ-pîhtokêyit oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| Presently some young women came into the house.
êkwa ôhi kisêyiniwa pôti nisto otawâsimisiyiwa, mistahi atâwâkana ê-pîhtokahâyit. ||| It appeared that they were the old man's three daughters, and they were bringing a great store of furs into the post.
sêmâk ôhi osîmimâwa akâwâtêw awa kâ-mêtawêsit. ||| At once he who was addicted to that game took a fancy to the youngest woman.
"tâpwê miyosiw, nîscâs!" itêw ôhi kâ-wîcêwât. ||| “Really, she is beautiful, Cousin!” he said to those who were, with him.
"nîscâs, tâpwê mistahi nitakâwâtâw awa iskwêw" itêw. ||| “Cousin, really, I very much desire this woman!” he said to them.
âyimisiwak ê-macihtwâcik sakâw-iyiniwak; kitisi-pêhtênânaw mâna." "tânêhki êwako kâ-akâwâtat?" When people want to give you women to wife, you do not accept,” said the one to his cousin.
"â, nîscâs, mâka nitakâwâtâw!" itêw. ||| “Oh, Cousin, but I am in love with her!” he answered him.

"hâ, mâka êkwêyâk nitakâwâtâw iskwêw!" itwêw. ||| “Oh, but it is only now that I long for any woman!” he said.
nika-kakwêcihkêmon pita," itwêyiwa; "ê, kikitimâkêyimitin mâka, nikosis, piko ta-atâwêyân," itêw. ||| Let me first inquire,” said his father; “But I love and cherish you, my son, and there is nothing for me to do but buy her,” he told him.
êkwa nitomêwak oskinîkiwi-sakâw-iyinîsa, ê-kakwêcimâcik, mahti ta-onâpêmiyit. ||| Then they called in a young Bush-Fellow and asked him whether those girls had husbands.
"namôya onâpêmiwak." "omisimâw ana nîswâw onâpêmiw; êkwa ana tastawêyas pêyakwâw onâpêmiw; ana osîmimâw namôya cêskwa onâpêmiw." That oldest one has twice been married; and the middle one has been married once; the youngest one has never had a husband. Three sons-in-law he has had, and each time, when off they went to camp by themselves, and then in spring were seen again, to our surprise their son-in-law was not with them. And so it is not known in what way they destroyed them. When they are asked, they will not tell,” he told them.

"wiya tipêyimêw otawâsimisa ninôtokwêm; wiya kî-âyimihik ê-wî-ohpikihât," itêw; "mahti kiyi-itêyihtahk; nika-wîhtamawâw," itêw. ||| “Hoho, Fellow-Tribesman, as for me, I shall be glad to have an animal like the Plains Cree. Truly there where we others dwell, there is a lack of horses,” he told him; “I cannot at this time tell you anything, Fellow-Tribesman. It is my wife who has decision over her children; it is to her they gave trouble when she labored to bring them up,” he told him; “Let us see what she thinks; I shall tell her of this,” he told him.
êkosi konita ay-âcimôwak. ||| Then they conversed of other things.
iyikohk ê-kîwêt awa sakâw-iyiniw, ê-pîhtokêt, "yahah, nôtokêsiw, kâ-nitomit awa paskwâw-iyiniw, ê-nitotamawit kitânisinawa." "pêyak misatim kiwî-miyikawinânaw;" "mâka kiya ê-tipahitân, ê-kî-âyimihiskik, ê-wî-ohpikihacik kitawâsimisinawak," itêw. ||| When the Bush Cree went home, and entered his tent, “Yah, Wife, this Plains Cree invited me to ask me for our daughter. We are to be given one horse; but it is by you I shall guide myself, since it was to you our children gave trouble when you labored to bring them up,” he said to her.
"nâh, êkosi mâna mâka kê-mêkiyahk!" "wiyâyêpac wiya otôtêmiyahk!" itwêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| “Goodness, do let us give her, then! We ought to be glad to have him in our family!” said the old woman.
êkosi ê-wâpaniyik, "kisâkamisikê, nôtokêsiw; nika-nitawi-nitomâw paskwâw-iyiniw," itêw. ||| So, the next morning, “Prepare hot water, Wife; I am going to invite the Plains Cree,” he told her.
tâpwê nitawi-nitomêw. ||| So he went and invited him.
ê-wâpamât awa kisêyiniw, pôti mistahi miyosiyiwa ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| When that old man saw her, he saw that the young woman was very beautiful.
"ta-kî-êcik-âni-miywêyimât nikosis!" itêyihtam. ||| “No wonder, I see, that my son fell in love with her!” he thought.
êkwa ê-kî-mîcisocik, "nitôtêm, anima kâ-kî-isiyan tipiskohk, miywêyihtam awa ninôtokwêm;" "têpêyimôw pêyak otânisa ta-ayâyit paskwâwiyinînâhk, ê-itwêt." ||| Then, when they had eaten, “My fellow-tribesman, my wife is pleased with that which you said to me last night; she is content that one of her daughters stay in the Plains Cree country, she says.”
êkosi awa kisêyiniw nanâskomôw. ||| Then that old man gave thanks.
"tâni êwako êtokê mâka, nitôtêm?" itêw. ||| “But which one is it, Fellow-Tribesman?” he asked him.
"â, tâni ana êwako wêsîmimâwit, êwako kâ-nôhtê-wîcêwât nikosis," itêw. ||| Oh, the one who is the youngest; she is the one whom my son desires to take to wife,” he told them.
"êkosi mâna mâka, nitôtêm, otâkosiki ta-itohtêw nitânis." "pita kêkway ta-kî-kaskikwâtasiw," itêw. ||| “So then, Follow-Tribesman, this evening my daughter will go there. First she will have to do a little sewing,” he told him.
êkosi kîwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| Then the old man went back home.
ê-pîhtokêt, "hâ, nikosis, kimiyikawin ana kâ-nitawêyimat," itêw okosisa. ||| When he entered the tipi, “Well, my son, the one you love is given to you,” he said to his son.
iyikohk ê-otâkosiniyik, êkoyikohk pê-wîcêwêw otânisa awa nôtokêsiw, ê-pê-nayahtahkik ayiwinisa, kiki ocayânisa awa oskinîkiskwêw; ayis anohc piko mistahi atâwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| When evening came, that old woman came with her daughter, and they carried a burden of clothes and the young woman's belongings; for, only a short time before, that old man had traded much at the post.
êkosi pîhtokêw awa, tita-isi-miyikot awa oskinîkiw, ê-kaskikwâtamoht; kayâhtê miyohôw wiya, ôhtâwiya ê-okimâwiyit. ||| So she entered, and they gave the youth what had been sewn for him; they were surprised at the fine clothes he wore because his father was a chief.
tâpwê mêkiw pêyak misatimwa; tâpwê wîkimêw. ||| As he had promised, he gave one horse; really, he took her to wife.
piyisk kinwêsk wîkiwak. ||| They camped there for a long time.
piyisk kotakak ayîsiyiniwak pâh-piciwak, mîna kayâs kâ-nakatiht awa kisêyiniw sakâw-iyiniw, otôtêma ê-kî-piciyit, ê-ka-kisâtât otânisa. ||| After a while the other people, one by one, moved camp, until it was long since the old Bush Cree had been left as the last, staying on with his daughter after his fellow-tribesmen had moved away.
kîtahtawê nitomêw awa otihtâwâwa. ||| Then at one time he called his daughter's father-in-law.
ê-pîhtokêyit, ê-kî-ma-mîcisocik, "yôh, nitihtâwâw, êkoyikohk ôma kâ-ispîhtâwahk, êkwa mâna niyanân kâ-mâci-nôtatâwâkanêyahk," itêw; "ninôhtê-nâtakâsin; êkwa êkoyikohk kinwêsk ê-kisâtitân," itêw; "êkosi mâka niya mîna kiyipa kê-piciyân;" "êkoyikohk nîsta ê-ihkêyihtamân, kayâs kâ-nakacipicistawicik nitôtêmak," itêw; "êkosi ômisi nititêyihtên," itwêw awa kisêyiniw sakâw-iyiniw; "nitihtâwâw, pita nâtakâm ninôhtê-isi-wîcêwâw ninahâhkisîm, ta-kiskinôhamawak sakâwi-mâcîwin, nôcihcikêwin," itêw; "itâp nîpinisiyâhko, êkoyikohk kiyâskociwâw ka-pamihikowâw kistimiwâw," itêw. ||| When the latter had entered, and when they had eaten, “Now, my fellow-father-in-law, the time has come now when we others always go out to hunt for furs,” he told him; “I want to go to the Bush Country; this is as long as I can stay with you,” he told him; “So now I too shall soon move camp; I think it long enough now, since long ago my fellow-tribesmen have moved camp and left me behind,” he told him; “And so this is my idea,” said the old Bush Cree; “Fellow-Father-in-Law, for a while I should like to take my son-in-law along to the North Country, to teach him the woodland way of hunting and getting furs,” he told him; “When we come back to summer camp, then you, in return, will have the service of your daughter-in-law,” he told him.
âta pakwâtam; mâka kostêw ôhi otihtâwâwa, "mâna oka-nitawi-misi-wanâcihoh!" ê-itêyimât okosisa. iyikohk ê-kîwêt, wîhtam ê-wî-piciyit. ||| To be sure, he disliked the plan; but he feared this man, his son's father-in-law, thinking of his son, “If only he does not go to his destruction!” When he came home, he announced that the others were going to move camp.
"pita nistim ta-nitawâpamêw, ta-wîhtamawât, ta-pêhikoyêk," itêw. ||| “My daughter-in-law had better first go see them and tell them to wait for you,” he told them.
êkosi wayawîw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| So then the young woman left the tipi.
"â, nikosis, âyiman itê kâ-nahâhkapiyan." "kipêhtênânaw ê-macihtwât, ê-manitôwit kimanâcimâkan." "mahti pita pônihtâ kimêtawêwin." "itâp iyikohk takosiniyini ôtê, kika-ma-mêtawân," itêw; "awahê êkâ wiya kakwê-kisiwâ kimanâcimâkan." "âhkamêyimo, isko kaskihtâyan, kîkway ta-kakwê-nipahtâyan," itêw okosisa; "âta ani kisâkihitin; mâka nikostâw kimanâcimâkan, ê-manâ-kisiwâhak," itêw. ||| “Oh, my son, it is a dangerous place where you are to stay with your wife's people. We hear that your father-in-law is a sorcerer and a person of manitou power. Do for a time give up your game. When you come back here, you may play as much as you like,” he told him; “Do your utmost not to anger your father in-law. Gather your energies, as far as you are able, and make an effort to kill things,” he told his son; “I hate to let you go; but I fear your father-in-law, and should dread to displease him,” he said to him.
tâpwê wawêyîwak, ê-wî-picicik. ||| Accordingly they made themselves ready to move camp.
tâpwê nîswayak isi sipwêhtêwak. ||| And so in two different directions they went from there.
êkwa awa sakâw-iyiniw sipwêhtahêw onahâhkisîma. ||| The Bush Cree took his son-in-law away with him.
â, miywêyihtam awa kisêyiniw. ||| Oh, the old man liked that.
iyikohk nâtakâm ê-ayâcik, êkoyikohk ati-mâh-mâcîw awa kisêyiniw, ê-wîcêwât onahâhkisîma, ê-kiskinôhamawât tânisi tita-isi-mitihtâyit pisiskiwa. ||| As soon as they were in the wooded country, the old man kept hunting as they went on, taking his son-in-law with him and teaching him to track the game.
piyisk nakacihtâw awa oskinîkiw. ||| In time the young man became skilled.
hâ, pêyakôw êkwa, ê-mâh-mâcît, môswa ê-mâcîtotawât, nanâtohk pisiskiwa ê-nôcihât. ||| So now he went alone, as he continued to hunt, hunting moose and pursuing all kinds of game.
êkâ miyâcîci, kîtahtawê mâna, "mêtawêtân!" ê-itikot owîkimâkana, mîna ôhi wîtimwa ê-pakêsêcik, piyisk miywêyihtamwak ôki oskinîkiskwêwak. ||| When he was not hunting, presently always, “Let us play!” his wife would say to him, and then they, as well as his sisters-in-law, would play the cup-game, until, in time, those young women became fond of it.
âta wiya namôya tahki iyisâc ê-pônihtât mâna awa oskinîkiw. ||| Indeed, the young man was always loth to cease from it.
piyisk ê-ati-piponiyik, "hâh, êkoyikohk ôma êspîhtâwahki, êkotê kâ-mâwacîhitohk," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| Then, in time, as the winter went on, “Now then, the time has come when the band assembles over yonder,” said the old man.
êkoyikohk ayâwak nîmâwin. ||| By this time they had food for the journey.
tâpwê pâpiciwak ita ê-ayâcik kotakak sakâw-iyiniwak. ||| They came to where the other Bush People were staying.
â, miywêyimâw awa paskwâw-iyiniw, êkotê ê-takosihk. ||| The Plains Cree was liked when he came there.
cîhkêyimik oskinîkiwa, mâka ê-itikot, "âyiman anihi!" "tânêhki ita kâ-ôh-nahâhkapiyan?" "mistahi ana âyimisiw." "âta, 'namôya mistahi nânitaw nitôtên,' kâ-itêyihtamiyit awiya, âsay ê-misi-wanâcihât awa kisis." "mîna nistwâw kî-onahâhkisîmiw; ati-misi-wanâcihêwak," itêw, ôhi ê-itikot oskinîkiwa; "awahê kakwê êkâ wiya kisiwâ kisis;" "âyimanohk ôma kâ-wîkihkêmoyan, ana ana mîna kîtim omisimâw ê-wîcôhkamawât ôhtâwiya, ê-macihtwâyit, ê-manitôwicik." ||| Another young man became his friend, but he told him, “It is a hard thing! Why are you staying here with your wife's people? He is really a hard man to be with. Even though one thinks, 'I am doing nothing serious,' before one knows it, this father-in-law of yours has done for him. He has had three sons-in-law before you; one after another they have destroyed them,” he told him, that youth told him; “Be on your guard and try not to incur your father-in-law's displeasure; it is in a dangerous place you are, staying with your wife's people, for that oldest sister-in-law of yours, too, makes common cause with her father in his bad magic, and both have manitou power.”
êkosi êkwa êkota ayâwak, iyikohk ê-mâwacîhitocik, ê-mihcêtisicik, nanâtohk ê-âh-isi-wîhkohtocik, mîna ê-nîmihitocik. ||| So there they stayed, when the band had assembled in great number, inviting one another to all manner of feasts, and dancing religious dances.
wiya oskinîkiw kîtahtawê pêyak cîhkêyimik oskinîkiwa, pisisik ê-kiyokâkot. ||| In time a certain other young man became fond of this youth and constantly visited him.
mâka ôhi wîtimwa tahki mawinêhok, ê-pakêsêcik. ||| His sisters-in-law kept bothering him to play the cup-game with them.
ayis namôya mâcîwak: ôma ê-otami-wa-wîhkohtowiht. ||| For they did no hunting, but were busy with feasting one another.
piyisk awa oskinîkiw kâ-ôh-kâ-ka-kiyokêt, êwako mîna kiskêyihtam ê-mêtawêt, piyisk ê-wîhtamawât kotaka oskinîkiwa ê-ayât awa paskwâw-iyiniw pakêsêwiyâkan. ||| After a time that young man who kept visiting them had, he too, learned the game, and in time told the other young men that the Plains Cree had a bowl for the cup-game.
kîtahtawê mâna pîhtokêyiwa oskinîkiwa, ê-wî-kiskinawâpahtamiyit ôma omêtawêwin, ê-kiskinôhamawât; piyisk kiskêyihtamiyiwa; piyis mâna nitomâw êkotê ê-mêtawêcik, ê-kiskinôhamawât oskinîkiwa; piyisk kâ-kapê-kîsik mêtawêw, nêtê kâ-kîsi-miywêyihtahk pisisik kâ-kî-mêtawêt. ||| Presently some young man would always be coming into the tipi, to learn that game of his by looking on, and he would teach it to him; in time the other would learn it; in time he would be invited to come where they were playing and teach it to the young men; presently he was playing all day and every day, with the same addiction that had kept him always a-playing in his home off yonder.
êkosi êkwa tôtam, pisisik ê-mêtawêt. ||| That was what he did, he played all the time.
piyis êkwa âskawi-piciwak kotakak. ||| The time came when the others, at intervals, moved camp.
piyis êkwa nâh-nôhtêhkatêwak; ayis ôma kâ-wâh-wîhkohtocik mistahi mêscipayihtâwak mîciwin. ||| By and by, too, they began to go hungry; for in their feasting one another they had used up much food.
kîtahtawê êkwa awa kisêyiniw tânitahto kîsikâw êkwa êkâ kêkway tâpwê ê-mîcit, ê-kisâtât onahâhkisîma, pisisik ê-mêtawêyit, kîtahtawê nîsotipiskwa ê-mêtawêyit, êkoyikohk kisiwâsiw awa kisêyiniw. ||| Then at one time, when for I know not how many days that old man had not eaten anything to speak of, as he stayed there with his son-in-law who did nothing but play, then at one time, when the latter had been a-playing for two days and nights, at last the old man lost patience.
ômisi itwêw: "êkoyikohk kinwêsk ê-isîtôwihak paskwâw-iyiniw, kâ-nôhtêhkatêyahk." "kika-picinânaw," itêw; "omêtawêwin ta-mîciw." "iyikohk minahoyâni, namôya kika-asamâwâw." "wîsta nipahtâci kîkwaya, êkoyikohk ta-mîcisôw," itêw onahâhkisîma. ||| Said he: “Long enough now have I supported the Plains Cree, seeing that now we are starving. Let us move camp,” he told the others; “Let him eat that toy of his. When I kill game, you are not to feed him. When he kills something, then he can eat,” he said of his son-in-law.
ê-kîkisêpâyâyik, mistahi pakwâtam awa oskinîkiskwêw ê-itimiht owîkimâkana. ||| When morning came, that young woman was greatly distressed by what had been said concerning her husband.
êkosi êkwa ê-wawêyîwiht kiskêyihtam. ||| So then he learned that his people were getting ready to leave.
kâ-mêtawêwiht kiskêyihtamwak kâ-mêtawêcik. ||| Where they were gaming, the players learned of it.
"piciwân êkwa wîkiwâw paskwâw-iyiniw," itâw. ||| “The Plains Cree's people are moving their camp,” he was told.
"êhêhêy haha" itwêyiwa ôhi sakâw-iyiniwa; "nitôtêm, âyimisiw ana; namôya ani okisêwâtisiwiniw." "kîspin kêkway kâ-kisiwâhikot, âyimisiw." "namôya kisêwâtotam kîkwaya." "âsay ani ê-kisiwâhat, êkâ kâ-ôh-pê-wîhtamâkawiyan ê-wî-picit." "sôskwâc, kîspin kêkway kikiskêyihtên, kakwê-âhkamêyimo." "manitôwiw ani!" itik ôhi nâpêwa. ||| “Dear me!” said that Bush Cree; “Fellow-Tribesman, he is a dangerous person; he has no kindliness at all. If anything angers him, he is dangerous. He has no kindliness toward anything. You have already incurred his displeasure: that is why you were not sent the message that he is about to break camp. Without delay, if you have any knowledge beyond the common, try to gather your energies. He is a manitou person, I tell you!” that man said to him.
"êkosi nikitimahik." "nama kêkway nikiskêyihtên." "nama kêkway nipawâtên." "êkosi sôskwâc nika-nipahik," itwêw. ||| “If that is the case, he has done for me. I have no mystic knowledge. I have not dreamed anything. If it is as you say, he will soon kill me,” said he.
êkosi êkwa ê-kî-nêwo-tipiskâyik, êkoyikohk sipwêhtêw. ||| So then, when four nights had passed, he went away.
hâh, otihtam êsa ê-kî-kapêsiyit. ||| He came to a place where the others evidently had camped.
nîswâw ê-kapêsiyit, êsa kâ-minahoyit. ||| When he had passed two of their overnight camping places, he saw where they had killed game.
ê-takohtêt, ê-otâkosiniyik, pôti wiyâsa kâ-wâpahtahk. ||| When he overtook them, at nightfall, there he saw the meat.
"êkosi êcika ani kê-mîcisoyân! ||| “So now I shall get a meal!
ninôhtêhkatâh!" itêyihtam. ||| I am hungry enough!” he thought.
mâka ômisi kî-itwêw awa kisêyiniw: "iyikohk kêkway nipahtâci paskwâw-iyiniw, ta-mîcisôw." "âta takohtêci, êkây asamâhkêk." "misawâc nika-kiskêyihtên, kîmôc asamâyêko," itwêw. ||| But the old man had spoken thus: “When the Plains kills anything, then let him eat. Even though he arrives, do not give him food. I shall be sure to know it, if you feed him secretly,” he said.
mâka kahkiyaw kostik otawâsimisa owîkimâkana. ||| All feared him, his children and his wife.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw kâ-pîhtokêt, wâpahtam kâhkêwakwa ê-akotêyiki. ||| When the young man entered, he saw the pieces of parched meat hanging.
piyis namôya wâpahtam ta-wî-kakwê-asamiht, ê-ka-kâmwâtapiyit owîkimâkana. ||| At last he did not see that there was any intention of feeding him, and his wife sat silent and gloomy.
piyisk, "nitawâsimisitik, mahti kâhkêwakwa nawacîk, ta-kawisimôwi-mîcisoyahk," ê-itât, tâpwê nawacîwak ôma kâhkêwak. ||| In time, “Children, roast some dried meat for our bedtime meal,” he said to them, and so they roasted a piece of dried meat.
êkwa ê-mîcisocik, namwâc asamâw. ||| Then, when they ate, he was given no food at all.
ê-âta-asamimiht owîkimâkana, nama wî-mîcisoyiwa, "kiyâm nîsta nika-nipahâhkatoson," ê-itêyihtamiyit. ||| His wife was given some, but she would not eat, thinking, “Let me too starve.”
"yahô, nitânis, mîciso! ||| “Hoho, Daughter, eat!
namôya ka-kî-kisîstên mîciwin!" itwêyiwa. ||| You cannot go without food!” said the other.
tâpwê mîcisôw; namôya asamêw onâpêma, ê-kostât ôhtâwiya. ||| Accordingly she ate; she did not give her husband food, for she feared her father.
piyisk êkosi isi kawisimôwak. ||| At last they went to bed, even so.
ê-kîsi-kawisimocik, ocêmêw owîkimâkana awa iskwêw. ||| When they had gone to bed, the woman kissed her husband.
"niwîkimâkan, mâskôc kêkway kikiskêyihtên." "âhkamêyimo, kêkway ta-kakwê-nipahtâyan kêkway." "ê-kitahamât ôma nôhtâwiy êkâ ta-asamikawiyan, êkosi ê-kostâyâhk kahkiyaw." "âta nipakwâtên ê-tôtâkawiyan, ê-sâkihitân." "ôki ôki nimisak iyâta-onâpêmitwâwi, êkosi ê-tôtâhcik ôma kâ-wî-tôtâkawiyan, ê-nipahâhkatosocik." "êkwa ê-manitôwit nôhtâwiy, namôya awiya wîhkâc ê-sâkôcihikot." "kisâkihitin." "kakwê-minahôstamâso," itik. ||| “My husband, perhaps you have some mystic knowledge. Summon your forces, that you may kill something. The fact is that my father has forbidden your being given any food, and we all stand in fear of him. To no avail am I distressed at what is being done to you, for I love you. When these my elder sisters here had husbands, this was done to them which is about to be done to you, and they died of hunger. Because my father is a manitou person, he is never defeated by anyone. I love you. Try to kill some food for yourself,” she told him.
"êhâ, êkosi ana kê-nipahit kôhtâwiy! ||| “Oh, if that is so, then your father will kill me!
namôya kêkway nikiskêyihtên," itêw. ||| I have no mystic knowledge,” he told her.
êkosi mâtôw awa oskinîkiskwêw, ê-itikot owîkimâkana. ||| Then the young wife wept, when her husband said this to her.
kîkisêpâ mîna ê-mîcisôwiht, namôya asamâw. ||| In the morning, when again the family ate, he was not given food.
êkosi isi ê-kîsi-mîcisôwiht, "piko ta-piciyahk!" itwêyiwa. ||| When in this way his people had eaten, “We must move camp!” said that other.
êkosi wawêyîw, ê-mâcît. ||| So then he went out of the tent and hunted.
iyâta-kîkway-wâpahtahki, wâh-nipahtâci, kîkway pêhtam, ê-tapasîyit ôhi kâ-wî-nipahât. ||| Although he would get sight of things, whenever he was about to kill them, he would hear something, and the creature he was going to kill would run away.
ahpô wâposwa piyâskiswâci, namôya nipahêw. ||| Even though he shot at nothing more than a rabbit, he did not kill it.
êkosi piyis mâna aspin itê kâ-ispiciwiht ê-itohtêt, têkohtêci, êkosi ê-ay-apit, namôya asamâw. ||| When then at last he would go to where his people had moved the camp, when he arrived, and sat there, he was not given food.
âta tahto-kîsikâw ê-mâcît, mâka nama kêkway kî-nipahtâw. ||| Although he hunted every day, he did not succeed in killing anything.
iskâniyê kêwâhkatosot. ||| How weak he grew with hunger!
piyis mâna mistahi nîpâhtêw, êkwa ê-kawâhkatosot. ||| At last he took to walking much in the dark, so far gone with hunger was he.
kîtahtawê êkwa namôya kî-mâcîw, êkwa ê-kawâhkatosot, pêciwihci, ê-apit matokahpihk, wîhkâc iyikohk mâna ê-sipwêhtêt. ||| Then in time he became unable to hunt, for the weakness of hunger, and when they moved camp he would sit on the deserted site, able only at intervals to move himself from the spot.
kîtahtawê ê-pîhtokêt, pahkisin êkwa, ê-nêsôwâhkatosot. ||| Then at one time, as he came into the tipi, he fell to the ground, exhausted by starvation.
