"yâ, nisîm, êkosi mâna itâcimâwak pâkahkosak." "êkotôwahk êtokê," itwêw awa ostêsimâw. ||| “Oho, Brother, this is what they tell of the bony spectres. Such they must be,” said the elder.
kîtahtawê kisiwâk mîna kâ-pê-matwêwêyik, âsay mîna ê-pê-sâkôwêyit. ||| Presently again, from near by came the sound of a shot, and again someone's whooping.
êkoyikohk pêhtamwak ê-pê-yôtiniyik. ||| Then they heard the coming of a rush of wind.
kwayask sêkisiw awa osîmimâw, ê-kostât pâkahkosa. ||| The younger was properly frightened, fearing the bony spectres.
ôta ê-tako-yôtinipayiyik, kâ-wâpamâcik akâmiskotêw ê-apiyit pâkahkosa, konita ê-wî-pâhpiyit, mâ-mîskoc ê-kitâpamikocik. ||| When the gust of wind reached them, there they saw, sitting at the far side of the fire, a bony spectre, smiling a hollow smile and looking now at one, now at the other.
sêkisiw awa osîmimâw; nama kî-waskawîw. ||| The younger one grew frightened; he could not stir from the spot.
awa ostêsimâw, êwako tahki kâh-kiyipa ê-kitâpamikot, kîtahtawê, "miyâmay waskawîw," ê-itêyimât, âsay osîma ê-isikâtêsiniyit, kâ-nahapiyit pâkahkosa, ê-yâsipitâyit otâsiyâna awa oskinîkiw, ê-wî-sisikotiskênikot, awa ostêsimâw kâ-otihtinât. ||| The elder, at whom the thing kept gazing every little while, suddenly thought, “Surely, he is about to make a move,” - and already at his younger brother's feet, as he lay, sat the bony spectre, and was drawing off the youth's breech-clout, to leap upon him by surprise; and the elder brother laid hold of the creature.
pita ta-mâsihkêw!" "pisisik mâna kâ-âcimihcik êkosi ê-wî-tôtahkik, ôma kâ-wî-tôtâsk!" itêw osîma. ||| Let us give him a fight! That which they are said always to be wanting to do, he is now about to do to you!” he told his brother.
"yâ, awas, êyisiyinîwiyin! ||| “Faugh, go away, mortal man!
pakitinin!" itêw pâkahkos. ||| Let go of me!” the bony spectre said to him.
ohcitaw kiwî-kakwê-maskamitin pâskisikan!" itêw. ||| I am bound to try to take away your gun!” he told it.
nîsôhkawêwak, ê-mâsihâcik. ||| The two attacked it and wrestled with it.
"namôya kiwî-ohci-pakitinitin!" itêw, ê-kiskêyihtahk ê-sâkohât. ||| “I will not let you go!” he said to it, when he knew that he had it fast.
nîsôhkawêwak, ê-mâsihâcik. ||| They both grappled with it and wrestled with it.
"hâw, êyisiyinîwiyin, kiyâm pakitinin!" "ahpô kika-wêhcihâwak pisiskiwak; kimiyitin, mitoni ta-minahoyan," itêw. ||| “Come, mortal man, do let me go! If you like, you may have easy play with game animals; I give you the gift of killing much game,” it told him.
kinihtâ-kakwê-cîsimâwâw ayîsiyiniw," itêw. ||| Such as you are given to cheating mortal men,” he told it.
"ahpô kêtisk kâ-ayisiyinîwinâwâw awa kisîm." "pakitinin!" ||| “If you like, you shall have full length of life, you and your younger brother here. Let me go!”
namôya kiwî-pakitinitin!" ||| I will not let you go!
"kiyâm kitimâkihtawin! ||| “Take pity on my words! Let me go!
pakitinin!" "ahpô kiwâhkômâkan mistahi iyâhkosici, êtotikawiyini, kika-pimâcihâw," itik. ||| If you like, whenever your kinsman is sorely ill, and you are called to aid, you shall restore him to life,” it told him.
osâm kinihtâ-kakwê-cîsimâwâw ayisiyiniw." "pakitinitâni, namôya ta-kî-ispayiw anima kâ-isiyan," itêw. ||| Such as you are too much given to cheating mortal men. If I let you go, that which you say to me will not come to pass,” he told it.
êkoyikohk mâka êkwa wî-wâpaniyiw. ||| But by this time dawn was near.
kiskêyihtam êkâ ê-pakitiniht pâkahkos. ||| The bony spectre knew that it would not be freed.
kîtahtawê kâ-miskonahk kêkway ê-pîmakâmêskamiyit ôhi pâkahkosa. ||| Presently the one felt with his hand something which that bony spectre wore across its shoulder.
tahki sâkihtâyiwa êwako. ||| It was always holding fast to this object.
"nisîm, kêkway awa mistahi kâ-sâkihtât, ê-pîmakâmêskahk." "kakwê-maskamâtân," itêw. ||| “Brother, there is something to which this creature anxiously clings, something which is slung across its shoulder. Let us try to get it away,” he told him.
"yâ, êkâ wiya, êyisiyinîwiyan! ||| “Oh, do not, mortal man!
mistahi anima ê-sâkihtâyân!" ||| I prize it so highly!”
kîtahtawê kâ-nisitawêyihtahk awa oskinîkiw. ||| Suddenly that youth recognized it.
miyâmay ôma pakêsêwiyâkan, kîscâsinaw otôyâkan!" itêw osîma. ||| Surely this is a bowl for the cup-game, our cousin's bowl!” he told his brother.
êkwa tâpwê, "yâhâ, awasitik, êyisiyinîwiyan! ||| So then, “Oho, be off, mortal man!
mistahi anima ê-sâkihtâyân!" ||| I prize this thing too dearly!”
nisitawêyihtamwak wîscâsa opakêsêwiyâkaniyiw. ||| They recognized their cousin's gaming-bowl.
"hâh, nisîm, êkâya pakitinâtân!" "iyây-ihkinokwê, awa pâkahkos kâ-kanawêyihtahk kîscâsinawa opakêsêwiyâkan!" itêwak. ||| “Come, Brother, let us not lose hold of him! What strange thing may it be, that this bony spectre is possessed of our cousin's gaming-bowl!” they said of it.
piyis êkwa ê-wâpaniyik, namôya êkwa wî-waskawîw awa pâkahkos. ||| When at last day broke, that bony spectre no longer tried to move.
êkwa wêwêkahpitêwak wâpowayânihk, "nisîm, ka-kîwêhtahânaw," ê-itât osîma. ||| Then they wrapped it tightly in a blanket, and, “Brother, let us take him home with us,” said he to his younger brother.
ayis êkwa kîsikâyiw. ||| By this time it was day.
êkwa awa ostêsimâw ê-nayômât pâkahkosa, ê-kîwêhtahâcik, piyis ê-wî-takohtêcik, êkota ayiwêpiwak. ||| Then the elder brother carried the bony spectre on his back, and they took it home with them, until, when they were almost at their destination, they halted.
"hâ, nisîm, kîwê." "wîhtamaw kôhtâwiyinaw: anima kâ-wîkiyahk kwêskâhtik ta-mânokêwak anima konita kâ-astêk apahkwâson; mitoni isi ta-anâskêwak maskosiya; mîna mistahi kita-astâwak mihta." "êkâya wîhtamawâhkan awa ê-pêsiwâyahk," itêw; "kakwêcimiski, êkâya wîhtamaw," ê-itât osîma; "êkwa anima mihkwêkin wêskwâhtêmihk kita-anâskêwak; êkwa pêyak wâpowayân êkota mîna ta-astâwak." "iyikohk kîsihtâtwâwi, ka-pê-wîhtamawin;" "mâka êkâ wiya ta-pê-itohtêwak kôhtâwiyinaw; êkâ wiya nika-kakwê-wâpamikwak," itêw. ||| “Now, Brother, go home. Tell our father this: at the other side of the grove from where we camp, let them build a tipi with the tent-coverings of whatever kind they have; let them cover the ground well with grass; and let them place there a large supply of firewood. Do not tell him that we are bringing this being,” he told him; “If he asks you, do not tell him,” he told his brother; “And let them spread this red cloth on the ground opposite the entrance; and there let them lay also one blanket-robe. When they have completed this, you will come and tell me; but do not let our father and the others come here; they are not to try to see me,” he told him.
êkosi kîwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| So the youth went home.
ê-takohtêt, "tâniwâ kistês?" itik ôhtâwiya. ||| When he arrived, “Where is your elder brother?” his father asked him.
"awa, ôta kisiwâk aspin ê-apit." "mâka ômisi ê-itwêt: 'anima kâ-wîkiyahk kwêskâhtik êkota ta-nitawi-mânokêwak,' ê-itwêt," itêw ôhtâwiya; "'kîsi-mânokêtwâwi, mistahi ta-astâwak maskosiya, mîna ta-anâskêcik kâ-anâskasoyahk.'" "'êkwa wêskwâhtêmihk ta-anâskêwak mihkwêkin; mîna pêyak wâpowayân êkota tita-astâwak,' ê-itwêt nistês" itêw ôhtâwiya. ||| “Oh, quite near here he was stopping when I left him. But this is what he says: 'At the far side of the grove from our camp they are to go and set up a tipi,' he says,” said he to his father; “'When they have set up the tipi, they are to place there much grass, and they are to lay on the ground those things which we use as mats. And opposite the entrance they are to use red cloth as a rug; and one blanket-robe they are to place there,' says my older brother,” said he to his father.
"ê hê hê hê ha ha!" itwêw awa kisêyiniw; "mâna nânitaw otisi-misi-wanâcihoh nikosis!" itwêw. ||| “Alas, alas!” cried the old man; “It looks as though my son had come to some grief!” he cried.
"namôya!" itwêw awa osîmimâw; "kiyâm kakwêyâhok," itêw ôhtâwiya. ||| “No!” said the younger brother; “Try to do the work quickly,” he told his father.
tâpwê wawêyîwak, ê-nitawi-mânokêcik ôki iskwêwak, awa kisêyiniw maskosiya ê-manisahk, ê-wî-anâskêcik. ||| Accordingly they made ready, the women going and setting up the tent, and the old man mowing grass to use on the floor.
"ahaw, sâsay êkwa, nikosis!" itêw. ||| “There, it is ready, my son!” he told him.
"â, nôhtâ, kiyawâw kahkiyaw êkâ wiya pê-itohtêk; mîna êkâ wiya kakwê-pê-itâpik," itâw. ||| “Now, Father, all of you, do not come there; and do not try to look,” he told him.
êkosi ê-nitawi-wîhtamawât ostêsa, êkosi kîwêhtahêw awa pâkahkosa; pîhtokahêw, wîkiwâhk ê-ahât, ôma ita mihkwêkin kâ-anâskêwiht. ||| Then he went and told his elder brother, and he brought home the bony spectre; he brought it into their tent and laid it there where the red cloth had been placed as a rug for him.
êkosi pa-pimisin awa pâkahkos, ê-akwanahiht, êkwa ê-nâtahk ta-mîcicik awa oskinîkiw. ||| So there lay the bony spectre, covered with a rug, while the youth went to get something for them to eat.
kîtahtawê êkwa ê-wî-wâpaniyik, "nisîm, mahti nâta pimiy," itêw, "êkwa wiyâkan, êkwa askihk." ||| Then, towards dawn, “Brother, go fetch some fat,” he told him, “and a bowl, and a kettle.”
êkwa êwako ê-pêtât, ê-tihkisahk ôma pimiy, êkosi wiyâkanihk sîkinam, ê-tahkikamastât êwako. ||| When he had brought them, he melted the fat and poured it into the bowl, and set it to cool.
"nâha, pâkahkos, ôma minihkwê!" "kimiywêyihtên pimiy; kititikawinâwâw mâna," itêw. ||| “Here, Bony Spectre, drink this! You are fond of fat, they always say of the like of you,” he said to it.
namôya wî-otinamiyiwa. ||| It would not take it.
piyis waniskânêw, êkwa otôniyihk ê-akonahk ôma wiyâkan, "minihkwê!" ê-itât. ||| At last he raised it from where it lay and held the bowl to its lips, and said to it, “Drink!”
tâpwê piyisk minihkwêw. ||| At last it really did drink.
"êkoyikohk mistahi minihkwêw," ê-itêyimât, pôni-minahêw. ||| When he thought, “Now it has drunk much,” he stopped giving it to drink.
kîhtwâm mîna minahêw. ||| Once more he gave it drink.
kîtahtawê ê-mêkwâ-apit awa pâkahkos, kâ-pwa-pwâkomipayit pisisik ê-kaskitêwâkamiyik. ||| Then soon, as the bony spectre sat there, it vomited, bringing up nothing but a black liquid.
"nisîm, mahti mîna pêyakwâw nâta pimiy," itêw. ||| “Brother, once more, fetch some fat,” he told him.
âsay mîna pêtâw, mîna êwako ê-tihkisahk; ê-minahât, âsay mîna pwâkomoyiwa. ||| Again he brought some, and this too he melted, and gave the creature to drink, and again it vomited.
êkwa mitoni askîhtakwâyiw kâ-pâpayihtâyit. ||| This time very green was that which it threw up.
êkwa ê-pakaskihk ê-osâwâkamiyik. ||| This time, something bright yellow.
êkosi êkwa pônihêw, kâwi ê-pimisihk. ||| Then he left it alone, and it lay down again.
kîtahtawê ê-otâkosiniyik, ômisi kâ-itwêt awa pâkahkos: "nîscâs, mahti pêyakwâw minahin pimiy; miyâmay kiwî-pimâcihin," kâ-itwêt awa pâkahkos. ||| Presently, toward evening, thus spoke that bony spectre: “Cousin, pray once more give me fat to drink; for it is plain that you mean to restore me to life,” said that bony spectre.
"hâw, nisîm, pêyakwâw nâta pimiy." "êkâ wiya wîhtamaw kôhtâwînaw," itêw. ||| “Come, Brother, once more fetch some fat. Do not tell our father,” he told him.
tâpwê pêtâw pimiy, êwako mîna ê-tihkisahk, ê-minahât mîna. ||| Accordingly, he brought fat, and this, too, they melted, and gave to that person to drink.
kitâyiwa, mîna ê-pwâkomoyit. ||| He drank it all, and vomited again.
êkwa wâpiskâyiw ê-pâpayihtâyit. ||| This time, white was that which he throw up.
ê-kîsi-pwâkomoyit, "nîscâs, mitoni êkwa nikiskisin." "niya ôma, nîscâs, ê-papâ-pâkahkôwiyân!" itêw wîscâsa. ||| When he had done vomiting, “Cousin, now I am fully conscious. It is I, my cousin, who have been going about in the form of a bony spectre!” he told his cousin.
êwako kâ-kî-nipahâhkatosot oskinîkiw kâ-miyosit. ||| He was none other than that handsome youth who had starved to death.
êkosi êkwa awa osîma, "hâ, nisîm, tahto kâ-ayât kôhtâwiyinaw maskihkiya ta-pakâhtâwak," itêw osîma; "êkâya wîhtamaw." "mistahi ôma ê-wî-miywêyihtamahk, pimâcihâyahko kîscâsinaw," itêw. ||| Then said the one to his brother, “Come, Brother, let them set to boil as many medicinal herbs as our father has. Do you tell him this. Greatly now we shall rejoice, if we restore our cousin to life,” he said to him.
tâpwê nitawi-sîhkimêw ôhtâwiya. ||| So he went to make the request of his father.
tâpwê pakâhtâw maskihkiya awa kisêyiniw. ||| Accordingly, the old man set the medicines to boil.
ê-kîsihtât, êwako ôma ohci mîna ê-minahâcik wîscâsiwâwa, êkosi tâpwê pimâtisiyiwa. ||| When he had finished this, again, they gave to their cousin to drink, and now truly he lived.
êkwa asamêwak, êkwa wîstawâw ê-mîcisocik. ||| Then they gave him food, and they, too, ate.
"nîscâs, tâpwê nimiywêyihtên, ê-pimâtisiyân, ê-wâpamitakok!" "piko ê-itwêyan nika-tôtên, ê-pimâcihiyan." ||| “Cousin, truly, I am glad to live and look upon all of you! Whatever you say I will do, for you have restored me to life.”
kiya nawac piko ê-itwêyan nika-tôtênân." "nama wîhkâc kêkway ka-nâtên," itêw wîscâsa. ||| Rather, whatever you say, we others will do. Never shall you go for anything,” he told his cousin.
iyikohk ê-miyoskawiyit, êkwa, "nîscâs, êkwa cî kâh-wâpamikwak nôhtâwiy nikâwiy mîna nimis?" itwêyiwa. ||| Then, when he was quite well, “Cousin, may my father and mother and sister see you now?” he asked.
"êha, nika-pê-wâpamikwak." ||| “Yes, let them come and see me.”
êkwa nitawi-wîhtamawêwak. ||| Then they went to tell them.
"nôhtâ, 'tânisi ôki êtahkamikisicik?' kitêyihtên." "ôma kâ-mâciyâhk pâkahkos ê-kî-otihtikoyâhk, êwako ê-pê-kîwêhtahâyâhk;" "nîscâs opakêsêwiyâkan ê-ayât pâkahkos, kâ-kî-pê-kîwêhtahâyâhk." "êwako ana ê-mâh-minahiht pimiy, iyikohk ê-âpahkawisit, êkwa maskihkiya kâ-pakâhtâyan, êkwani mîna ê-mâh-minahâyâhk." "êkosi êkwa, 'nipê-wâpamikwak,' ê-itikoyêk, êwako êsa ana, "kî-misi-wanâcihâw", kâ-kî-itiht nîscâs, êsa ana ê-pâkahkôwit." "mâka êkwa kâwi êkwa âpisisin," itêw. ||| “Father, 'What are these persons trying to do?' you are thinking. That time when we were hunting, a bony spectre came where we were, and we brought it home here with us; because the bony spectre had our cousin's gaming-bowl, we brought it home with us. Then, when it was given repeated drinks of fat, when he came to himself, that was when you set medicines to boil, and these, too, we gave him to drink. And so now, 'They may come and see me,' he says to you, for he turns out to be none other than that cousin of mine, of whom it was said, 'He has been destroyed;' it appears that he has been in the form of a bony spectre. But now he has come back to his natural state,” he told him.
êkosi êkwa ê-ati-wayawît, ôki ôki ê-itohtêcik, tâpwê wâpamêwak. ||| Then, as he left the tent, these people went there and really, they saw him.
nisitawêyimêwak, ê-atamiskawâcik. ||| They recognized him, and welcomed him.
êkosi êkota ay-ayâwak. ||| So there they all stayed.
kîtahtawê mâna, "nîscâs, ôta kisiwâk ayâwak môswak. ||| Often, in the time that followed, “Cousin, some moose are close by.
nitawi-nipa," ê-itwêt awa kâ-kî-pâkahkôwit, êkosi ê-nitawi-nipahâcik ôhi, piyis kiyipa tâhcipôw. ||| Go kill one,” he would say who had been a bony spectre, and they would go kill one, and so finally, he soon recovered his flesh with good fare.
êkosi êkwa pê-sipwêhtêwak, êkwa ê-kîwêhtahâcik wîscâsiwâwa. ||| So then they set out to come here, to bring their cousin home.
piyis ê-nîpiniyik, takosinwak ôta pêhonânihk. ||| At last, in spring, they arrived here at Battleford.
namôya ita ê-wîkiwiht wî-kapêsiwak, êkâ ta-wâpamimiht ôhi, mîna êkâ ta-pêhtahk nâha kisêyiniw kâ-kî-nipahâhkatosohât. ||| They did not care to camp where the people were staying, lest he be seen, and lest the old man hear of it who had starved him.
êwako ohci kâ-ôh-kâtâcik ôhi wîscâsiwâwa. ||| For this reason they kept their cousin concealed.
piyisk pê-sipwêpiciwak. ||| At last they moved their camp and brought it here.
namôya êkota ayâyiwa osisiwâwa. ||| Their uncle was not there.
kâwi kâ-kîsi-miyosit awa oskinîkiw, êkosi isi miyosiw. ||| That youth was now again as handsome as he had formerly been.
êkwa ê-pê-nimitâsipicicik, kîtahtawê wâpamêwak ayîsiyiniwa. ||| Then, as they came trekking into the open country, presently they came in sight of people.
ê-kakwêcihkêmocik, osisiwâwa namôya wâhyaw âcimimâwa ê-wîkiyit. ||| When they asked, their uncle was said to be camping not far from there.
awa ostêsimâw ispayiw, ê-nitawâpamât osisa. ||| The older brother rode there, to see his uncle.
mâtoyiwa osikosa, âsay ê-kiskisiyit okosisiyiwa. ||| His aunt wept, remembering her son.
"êkâ wiya mâto, nisikosê," itêw. ||| “Do not weep, my aunt,” he said to her.
êkosi miyik osisa miskotâkay ê-mîkisiwiyik, sihkosiwayâna ê-kikamoyit, mîna mitâsa. ||| Then his uncle gave him a beaded jacket with weaselskin tassels, and breeches.
"ôma wiya miskotâkay nânitaw ka-kî-itâpacihtân," itêw osisa, "nîscâs tita-oskotâkât," ê-itêyihtahk; "hâ, nisisê, kisiwâk ôma ôta niwîkinân." "ê-pê-nitomitân, wâpahki ta-pê-ispiciyan," itêw. ||| “As for this jacket, you will have use for it,” he told his uncle, and his thought was, “My cousin shall have it.” -- “Now, uncle, we are camping close by here. I have come to invite you to move your camp there tomorrow,” he told him.
namôya wîhtamawêw ê-pimâtisiyit wîscâsa. ||| He did not tell him that his cousin was alive.
êkosi isi kîwêpayiw. ||| Thereupon he rode back.
âcimostawêw wîscâsa. ||| He told his cousin what he had done.
"niwâpamâwak kôhtâwiy." "wâpahki ôta ta-pâpiciwak," itêw; "namôya niwîhtamawâwak ê-pimâtisiyan," itêw. ||| “I have seen your father and his people. Tomorrow they will move their camp here,” he told him; “I did not tell them that you are alive,” he told him.
êkwa tâpwê ê-wâpaniyik pâpiciyiwa. ||| Then really, the next day, the others came with their camp.
mâtôwak ê-wâpamâcik. ||| They wept when they saw them.
"yâ, nicâhkos, êkâya mâtok!" itêw ocâhkosa. ||| “Oh, Sister-in-Law, do not weep!” said the woman to her sister-in-law.
êkwa wêskwâhtêmihk pimisin awa oskinîkiw, ê-wêwêkisihk. ||| Opposite the entranceway lay that youth, wrapped in a covering.
"hâw, ôta ta-pê-pîhtokêw nisis êkwa nisikos," itêw. ||| “Now then, my uncle and aunt are to come inside here,” he told them.
pîhtokêwak, êkotê ê-isi-sâwahtoyit okosisa. ||| They entered and stood at the foot-end of their son's couch.
"nisisê, tânisi ka-itêyihtên, wâpamat nîscâs?" ||| “Uncle, what would you think, if you saw my cousin?”
"nitihkwâ, nika-miywêyihtên, kîscâs wâpamak ita ê-pimisihk," itwêw awa okimâw. ||| “Nephew, I should be glad to see the place where your cousin lies,” said that chief.
"hâ, nîscâs, waniskâ!" itêw. ||| “Come, Cousin, arise!” he bade him.
ê-waniskâyit, awîna ôhi, êwakoni okosisa wâwiyak! ||| When he arose, who was it but, incredibly, his son!
kêkâc kipatâhtam awa kisêyiniw, iyikohk ê-miywêyihtahk, ê-wâpamât okosisa. ||| The old man almost choked with emotion, so happy was he, when he beheld his son.
êkosi mistahi miywêyihtamwak. ||| So they rejoiced greatly.
êkosi ê-wâpaniyik, ispiciwak pêhonânihk. ||| Then, on the next day, they moved their camp to Battleford.
mâka namôya wîhtamwak ê-pimâtisiyit ôhi oskinîkiwa, ê-kostâcik nêhi kisêyiniwa, "mâskôc pêhtahki, mîna nika-misi-wanâcihikonân," ê-itêyihtahkik. tâpwê kapêsiwak. ||| But they did not make it known that that youth was alive, for they feared yonder old man, thinking, “Perhaps, if he hears this, he will destroy us all.” So they pitched camp.
ê-wâpahk, sakâw-iyinîsak kâ-pâpicicik, awîna ôhi, êkwa kâ-ayâyit ôhi kâ-kî-nipahâhkatosohikot, êkwa ê-wî-mâhiskamiyit. ||| The next day some Bush Folk came camping there, and, behold, among them was the one who had starved him, coming to trade at the post.
"nîscâs, mahti nitawâpahkêk, mahti kê-wâpamâyêk niwîkimâkan," itêw. ||| “Cousin, pray, go look if you can see my wife,” he told them.
tâpwê itohtêwak ôki oskinîkiwak. ||| So those young men went there.
nawac kiyipa kâ-pê-pîhtokêyit ôhi sakâw-iyiniwa, wâpamikwak wîscâsiwâwa owîkimâkaniyiwa. ||| That Bush Cree had come and entered before them, and their cousin's wife saw them.
kêyâpic namwâc wawêsiyiwa, kêyâpic ê-mihtâtât awa owîkimâkana, nîso-pipon aspin kâ-nipahâhkatosoyit, kâ-itêyihtahk, owîkimâkana. ||| Even now she had not put on any ornaments, for she was still grieving for her husband, who had, so far as she knew, starved to death two years before.
mayaw ê-wâpamât ôhi oskinîkiwa, sêmâk tapahtiskwêyiw awa oskinîkiskwêw, ê-pahpahkikawâpit, owîkimâkana wîscâsiyiwa ê-nisitawêyimât. ||| As soon as she saw those youths, the young woman bowed her head and wept, because she recognized her husband's cousins.
êkwa awa kisêyiniw, "ê hê hê hêy ha ha!" itwêw; "ita oka-kî-miywêyihtêh ninahâhkisîm, wîscâsa kî-wâpamât, êkâ katawa kâ-kî-ay-ispayiyâhk!" itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| And that old man cried, “Dear me, dear me! How happy my son-in-law would have been to see his cousins, unlucky as we have been!” said that old man.
êkosi kiyipa ati-wayawîwak ôki oskinîkiwak, wîscâsiwâwa ê-wî-âcimostawâcik. ||| At that those youths quickly went out, to go tell their cousin.
"nîscâs, niwâpamânân nitawêmânân." "kêyâpic namôya nânapâcihow." "tâpwê êsa kikî-mihtâtik." "mayaw ê-nisitawêyimikoyâhk sêmâk pahpahkikawâpiw," itêw. ||| “Cousin, we have seen our kinswoman. Even now she wears no finery. It seems that truly she has been grieving for you. As soon as she recognized us, she shed tears,” he told him.
iyikohk ê-pimi-kîwêyit, êkwa kâ-itohtêt awa nôtokêsiw, ostima ê-nitawi-wâpamât, "nitawi-nitom," ê-itât awa oskinîkiw okâwiya. ||| As soon as they went on home, that old woman went there to visit her daughter-in-law, for, “Go see her,” that youth had said to his mother.
ê-pîhtokêt, "hêy hêy hêy hi hi!" itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| When she entered, “Dear me, dear me!” cried that old man.
mâtôw awa oskinîkiskwêw, osikosa ê-wâpamât. ||| The young woman wept, when she saw her mother-in-law.
awa wiya kisêyiniw, "êhêhêy hi hi!" kâ-itwêt; "oka-kî-miywêyihtêh ninahâhkisîm, ita ta-kî-wâpamât okâwiya ôhtâwiya, iyikohk kâ-kî-kîsinâcihikôwisiyâhk, ê-misi-wanâtisit ninahâhkisîm," itwêw. ||| But the old man cried, “Dear me, dear me! How glad my son-in-law would have been, to see here his mother and his father, cruelly deprived as we have been by powers above our control, in my son-in-law's destruction!” he said.
namôya ê-kiskêyihtahk ê-pimâtisiyit awa kâ-itwêt kisêyiniw. ||| The old man said this not knowing that the other lived.
"ê-pê-nitomak awa nistim, ê-wî-wâpamikot osisa," itêw. ||| “I have come to invite my daughter-in-law here, for her father-in-law wishes to see her,” she told them.
wiyâyêpac kinôhtê-wâpamik nitihtâwâw!" itêw. ||| It is gratifying that my fellow-father-in-law wishes to see you!” he said to her.
wâhyawês ê-ihtâcik, "nisikosê, konita aniki kâ-mihtâtâmôwi-kîskwêcik, kikosisa wiyawâw aniki ê-misi-wanâcihâcik." "ahpô ôma wâh-mâtoyâni, nôhcihikwak," itwêw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| When they had gone a ways, “Mother-in-Law, it is but in pretense that those people carry on as though they were grieving, for it is they who destroyed your son. Even when I would weep, they stop me,” said the young woman.
"â, nistim, êkâ wiya âtota kiyâm!" itêw. ||| “Oh, Daughter-in-Law, please, do not speak of that!” she told her.
êkosi pîhtokêwak wîkiwâhk. ||| So they entered their dwelling.
ê-atamiskawât osisa, mâtôw. ||| When she greeted her father-in-law, she wept.
"kiyâm api, nistim." "êkâya mâto," itêw. ||| “Be quiet, Daughter-in-Law. Do not weep,” he told her.
êkwa ê-kî-mîcisot, "kîwê êkwa, nistim." "mistahi ta-tipiskâw," itêw. ||| Then, when she had eaten, “Go home now, my daughter-in-law. It is getting very dark,” she told her.
êkotê awa oskinîkiw askamawêw. ||| There that young man was lying in wait for her.
êwako ohci kâ-ôh-itât awa nôtokêsiw, êkosi ê-kî-itikot okosisa. ||| That was why the old woman had said this to her, for her son had bidden her so.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw ita ê-pimisihk, ê-pimohtêyit, pasikôw, ê-miciminât. ||| Then, where the young man lay, as she walked by, he arose and seized hold of her.
"kiyâm pakitinin!" "aspin niwîkimâkan kâ-misi-wanâtisit, namôya wîhkâc êkosi nititêyihtên, kotak nâpêw ta-nitawêyimak," itêw. ||| “Do let me go! Ever since my husband came to grief, I have never had the feeling of wishing for another man,” she said to him.
"hâ, namôya ka-kî-pakitinitn!" "niya ôma, niwîkimâkan! ||| “Oh, I shall not let you go! It is I, my wife!
nipimâtisin ôma!" "êwako anima ita kâ-kî-nakasiyêk, êkosi anima nikî-pê-sa-sipwêhtân," itêw. ||| I am alive! From that place where you left me behind, I have come here,” he told her.
"êkwa nôhtâwiy wîkiwâhk itohtêtân pita, kâ-ôh-pê-wayawiyan," itêw. ||| “Then let us but go to my father's dwelling, from which you have even now come,” he told her.
"mâcikôtitân ôma ita nipakêsêwiyâkan!" itêw. ||| “Look, here is my bowl for the cup-game!” he said to her.
êkoyikohk tâpwêhtam awa oskinîkiskwêw, konita ê-mâtot, ê-oy-ocêmât onâpêma, êkwa ê-kîwêhtahikot. ||| Then the young woman believed it, and wept without grief, kissing her husband again and again, as he took her back to his dwelling.
ê-pîhtokêcik êkwa, tâpwê mitoni nisitawêyimêw onâpêma. ||| When now they entered, she did indeed fully recognize her husband.
êkosi êkwa êkota ayâwak. ||| So there they stayed then.
iyikohk ê-wâpaniyik, ka-kaskikwâsôw, ê-miyât awa iskwêw ostima ta-otayôwinisiyit. ||| The next day she spent at sewing, for that woman gave her daughter-in-law things to wear.
iyikohk ê-âkwâ-kîsikâyik, pê-nâtik omisa. ||| At noon, her elder sister came to get her.
kâsôw awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth hid himself.
namôya wâpamik wîtimwa. ||| His sister-in-law did not see him.
kêyâpic kaskikwâsoyiwa. ||| His wife kept on sewing.
"ta-pê-kîwêyan êkwa!" itêw. ||| “You are to come home now!” she told her.
"nistim pita ta-kîsikwâtam ocayôwinisisa." "kîsikwâtahk itâp ta-kîwêw," itêw. ||| “My daughter-in-law is first to sew her garments. When she has finished sewing them, she will come home,” she told her.
iyikohk ê-tipiskâyik, êkwa kîwêw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| When darkness was failing, then the young woman went home.
wîcêwêw owîkimâkana. ||| Her husband went with her.
ê-pîhtokêt awa iskwêw, nâwayês kâ-pîhtokêyit onâpêma. ||| When she entered the tipi, her husband went in behind her.
sêkisiw awa kisêyiniw. ||| The old man was frightened.
"ninahâhkisîm, kiyâm nika-pimâtisin!" itêw. ||| “My son-in-law, please let me live!” he said to him.
"yâ, nimanâcimâkan, namôya nânitaw kititêyimitin, ê-kî-âta-tôtawiyan;" "nama nânitaw nititêyihtên!" ||| “Oh, my father-in-law, I bear you no grudge at all, even though you did that to me; I do not think anything of it!”
tahto kêkway ê-miywâsiniyik ê-kî-atâwêt awa kisêyiniw, kahkiyaw miyêw onahâhkisîma, mîna ê-iskonât atâwâkana, nikikwayâna, pahkêkinwa, ê-miyât. ||| As many fine things as that old man had bought at the trading-post, all of them he gave to his son-in-law, as well as the furs which he had kept out for himself; otterskins, and cured buffalo hides he gave him.
"kiyâm nika-pimâtisin, ninahâhkisîm!" itêw. ||| “Pray let me live, my son-in-law!” he said to him.
"êkosi namôya nânitaw nititêyihtên," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “I tell you, I think nothing at all of it,” the youth answered him.
êkosi ê-ati-pasikôt, ê-kîwêcik owîkimâkana, ocayânisiwâwa ê-kîwêhtatâcik, mistahi mâkwêyimôw awa kisêyiniw, onahâhkisîma ê-nisitawêyimât. ||| Then he rose to his feet, and he and his wife went home, taking their belongings with them; and greatly worried was that old man, having recognized his son-in-law.
êkwa ê-kawisimocik, "niwîkimâkan," itwêw awa oskinîkiw, "tânisi, kimiywêyihtên cî ê-owôhtâwîyan?" ||| Then, as they went to bed, “My wife,” said that young man, “Tell me, are you glad that you have a father?”
nikisiwâhik ana, mâna ê-kî-kitimahisk, ê-kî-kakwâtakihisk." "nawac kiya nimiywêyihtên ê-wâpamitân," itêw. ||| He made me hate him, when he made you miserable and tormented you. I am far more glad that I can lay eyes upon you,” she told him.
"hâw, tâni ana mîna êkosi isi nôcihtât tâpiskôc kôhtâwiy?" itêw. ||| “Now, which ones have followed the same ends as your father?” he asked her.
"nikâwiy ana wiya miyo-pimâtisiw, êkwa ana kâ-askôwiskawak." "nimis wiya ana omisimâw, kâ-itâtisit nôhtâwiy, êkosi itâtisiw," itêw. ||| “As for my mother, she is a good person, and so is the sister to whom I am next in age. But as for my oldest sister, she is of the same character as my father,” she told him.
êkosi ômisi itêyihtam awa oskinîkiw: "hâw, anohc ôma kâ-wî-nipât, kayâhtê namôya ta-kî-waskawîw;" "ta-nipôwisiw awa kisêyiniw!" "mîna namôya ta-nihtâwêw!" "iyikohk takwâkiki, ta-pwâna-waskawîw!" "êkosi êkota mîna kiyipa otânisa ka-pwâna-waskawiyiwa, anihi omisimâwa!" itêyihtam, êkwa ê-kawisimot. ||| Then that youth thought, “Now, tonight when he sleeps, let him suddenly lose the power of moving his limbs; let that old man be paralyzed! And let him lose the power of speech! Until autumn comes, let him be unable to stir a limb! And also let his daughter soon lose the power of movement, that eldest one!” he thought, and lay down to sleep.
kîtahtawê ê-wâpaniyik, namôya waskawîw ana kisêyiniw, ê-nipôwisit. ||| Then, in the morning, that old man could not stir, and was paralyzed.
êkwa namôya nihtâwêw. ||| Also, he could not speak.
pê-nitomâw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| That young woman was sent for.
"pê-nitawâpam kôhtâwiyinaw!" "tânisi êtokê isi-ayâw!" "kayâhtê nipôwisiw; namôya mîna pîkiskwêw," pê-itêw awa osîma. ||| “Come, see our father! What can be the matter with him? Suddenly he has become paralyzed; and he does not speak,” one came and told her sister.
"namôya niwî-nitawâpamâw," itêw omisa. ||| “I do not care to go and see him,” she told her elder sister.
iyikohk awa oskinîkiw, "mahti nitawâpamâtân kôhtâwiy," itêw. ||| But the young man, in turn, said to her, “Let us go see your father.”
ê-pîhtokêt, mayaw ê-nisitawêyimât awa kisêyiniw onahâhkisîma, konita ê-cîpitonêyit, "nika-atamiskawâw," ê-itêyimât onahâhkisîma. ||| When he entered, as soon as the old man recognized his son-in-law, he helplessly twitched the muscles of his face, thinking of his son-in-law, “Let me greet him.”
"yahôw, tânisi êkwa tiyôtahk kisêyiniw, konita kâ-ca-cîpitonêyit sakâw-iyiniw omanitôwiw?" itêw. ||| “Why, what is the old man doing, twisting his face that silly way, the manitou Bush Cree?” he asked him.
êkwa ôki oskinîkiskwêwak ê-kakîsimototawâcik wîtimowâwa ta-kakwê-pimâcihâyit ôhtâwiyiwâwa, "namôya nânitaw nika-kî-tôtên, êkâ mâ manitôwiyân." "wiya kôhtâwiyiwâw manitôwiw, kahkiyaw awiya ê-itikot sakâw-iyiniwa," itêw, êkosi ê-ati-wayawît, ê-kîwêt. ||| Then, when those young women implored their brother-in-law to try to restore their father to life, “I cannot do anything, since of course I have no manitou power. It is your father has manitou power, as all the Bush Cree say of him,” he told them, and with that left the tent and went home.
iyikohk ê-takwâkiniyik, nipiw awa kisêyiniw. ||| When autumn came, the old man died.
êkosi mîna kiyipa otânisa nipiyiwa. ||| Likewise his daughter soon died.
êkosi êkoyikohk êskwâk âcimôwin. ||| Now, this is the end of the story.
pêyak êsa nâpêw kaspwân isiyîhkâsôw. ||| A certain man, the story goes, was called Gaspard.
itôwahk nawac piko kâ-môhcôwicik, kisâstaw êkotôwahk êsa awa awa nâpêw. ||| Of the kind that are more crazy than anything else, of that kind, to all appearance, was that man.
êkwa mistahi kitimâkêyimik ostêsa. ||| His elder brother was fond of him and cared for him.
êkwa kîtahtawê âhkosiyiwa. ||| Then at one time the elder brother took sick.
êkwa wiya kaspwân nama wîhkâc êsa atoskêw. ||| But as for Gaspard, he never worked.
êkwa piko awâsisa nayêstaw piko ê-mêtawâkêt, êwako piko nayêstaw ê-isi-atoskêt. ||| He only played with the children, that was the only kind of work he did.
nama kêkway kotak êwako piko ê-atoskâtahk, awâsisa piko ê-otaminât. ||| At nothing else he worked, only at amusing the children.
nîsiyiwa ostêsa ocawâsimisiyiwa. ||| His brother had two children.
kîtahtawê ostêsa ôki maci-ayîsiyiniwak ê-mihcêticik nipahêwak êwakoni anihi. ||| Presently those evil men, who were many, killed that elder brother of his.
êkwa wiya piko kaspwân kâ-isiyîhkâsot êkwa mistahi ê-kihtimit. ||| Then there was left only that Gaspard, who was so lazy.
kêyiwêhk pamihêw awa iskwêw wîtimwa; mistahi kitimâkêyimêw. ||| That woman took such care as she was able of her brother-in-law; she treated him with most pitying kindness.
êkwa piko awâsisa nayêstaw ê-otaminât. ||| And all he did, even now, was to amuse the children.
mistahi mâna pakwâtam awa iskwêw, êkâ wîhkâc ê-atoskêyit ôhi wîtimwa. ||| The woman was very much dissatisfied because her brother-in-law never worked.
ahpô nama wîhkâc nikohtêw awa kaspwân, osâm mistahi ê-kihtimit, êkwa piko wîtimwa ê-atoskêyit. ||| That Gaspard never even gathered firewood, for he was too lazy; his sister-in-law did all the work.
êtataw nawac piko êsa asamisôwak. ||| They had barely enough to eat.
kîtahtawê ômisi itêyihtam, ê-wî-mâcîwiht: "mahti nika-wîcihiwân!" itêyihtam êsa awa iskwêw; "mâskôc wî-wêpihihci nîtim," itêyihtam êsa. ||| Presently, when the people were about to go on a hunt, she thought, “I had better go along!” thought the woman; “Perhaps my brother-in-law will be aroused to some activity,” she thought.
tâpwê êkosi isi isi-wîcêwêw. ||| So accordingly she took him along.
êkwa nama kêkway âhci piko awa kaspwân, piyisk âta ê-wâh-wanihikêwiht. ||| But Gaspard still did nothing at all, even though the people were trapping.
piyisk êkosi isi isi-piciwân. ||| Finally their band moved camp.
nitawâc namôya awa iskwêw wî-piciw. ||| The woman needs determined not to move.
ayisk namôya wîtimwa wî-atoskêyiwa. ||| For her brother-in-law would not do any work.
êkwa awa iskwêw wâkayôsa miskawêw. ||| Then the woman found a bear.
mistahi ê-wiyinoyit, êkota ohci mistahi mâwacihtâw pimiy. ||| As the beast was very fat, she took a great amount of grease from it.
êkwa wâposwa ê-nâ-nipahât, piyisk mistahi mîsihtâw. ||| And since she also kept killing rabbits, finally she had a big store of food.
êkwa kîtahtawê kîkisêpâ namwâc wî-mîcisôw awa kaspwân. ||| Then at one time Gaspard would not eat anything in the morning.
mâmaskâtam awa wîtimwa êkâ ê-wî-mîcisoyit awa iskwêw. ||| The woman was surprised that her brother-in-law would not eat.
"tânêhki ôma êkâ o-wî-mîcisot?" itêyihtam êsa. ||| “Why does he not want to eat?” she thought.
âsay mîna namôya mîcisôw ê-âpihtâ-kîsikâyik. ||| At noon again he did not eat.
piyisk ê-tipiskâyik namôya mîcisôw. ||| Then, in the evening, he did not eat.
êkwa mistahi pakwâtam awa iskwêw ê-wâpaniyik mîna ê-asamât, namôya wî-mîcisoyiwa. ||| The woman greatly disliked this. In the morning, when again she gave him food, he would not eat.
piyisk mîna tipiskâyiw, êkâ ê-wî-mîcisot. ||| Night came, and still he would not eat.
"tânêhki ôma?" itwêw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| “What is the matter?” said the young woman.
êkwa, "nîtim, êkâya nânitaw itêyihta." "namôya ê-âhkosiyân," itwêw êsa awa kaspwân. ||| Then, “Sister-in-Law, do not worry about it. It is not that I am ill,” said Gaspard.
"kêhcinâ," itêyihtam awa iskwêw, "ê-akâwâsit," itêyimêw ôhi wîtimwa. ||| “Surely,” thought the woman, “he must be falling in love with me,” she thought of her brother-in-law.
êkwa kîtahtawê ômisi itwêw: "nîtim, êkâya êkosi itêyimin." "konita êkosi kitêyihtên," itwêw êsa. ||| Then presently he spoke thus: “Sister-in-Law, do not think that of me. You are mistaken in thinking that,” he said.
êkwa kîtahtawê nêwo-kîsikâw namôya êsa mîcisôw. ||| Then presently, for four days he had not eaten.
ôta ômisi êsa itwêw: "nîtim," itwêw êsa, "ana oskinîkiskwêw ôta kâ-kî-ayât wîhtikôwiw." "piko kita-kakwêyâhoyan ta-tapasîyahk," itwêw êsa; "anohc kâ-tipiskâk kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwa êkotê kâ-ayâyit ta-mêscihêw," itwêw êsa; "wâpahki tipiskâki ôta ta-takohtêw," itwêw êsa; "tapasîtân kiyâm," itwêw êsa awa nâpêw. ||| Then he spoke as follows: “Sister-in-Law,” he said, “that young woman who was here has become a Windigo. The only thing for you to do is to hurry preparations that we may flee,” he said; “This very night she will kill all the people who are staying over there,” he said; “Tomorrow night she will arrive here,” he said; “Let us flee, do,” said that man.
tâpwê ê-wâpaniyik mayaw mâci-wawêyîwak. ||| Then in the morning, at once they began to make ready.
"têpiyâhk kicawâsimisak ita ta-pôsihacik pêyak piko otâpânâsk sipwêhta." ||| “Take along at any rate one sled, so that you can at least let your children ride.”
tâpwê nêwo atimwa êsa wiyahpitêw. ||| Accordingly she harnessed four dogs.
êkwa ôhi wêwêkinêw otâpânâskwa, têpiyâhk êkosi isi ê-isi-tapasîcik. ||| She covered the sled, and with nothing more they went.
âsay êkwa mâmaskâtêw awa iskwêw wîtimwa pêyâhtik ê-pa-pimohtêyit; êkwa wiya mitoni sîhkimik sôhki kita-pakamahwât atimwa. ||| It was not long before the woman was wondering at the way her brother-in-law slowly walked along; for at the same time he was urging her to beat the dogs to a good pace.
"êkâya manâtaskâsin," itwêw awa kaspwân. ||| “Do not worry about leaving me behind,” said Gaspard.
tâpwê sôhki tapasîw awa iskwêw, âhci piko kâ-pa-pmohtêyit ôhi wîtimwa. ||| Really, the woman fled with speed, while her brother-in-law merely strolled along.
mâmaskâtam, âhci piko ê-pa-pmohtêyit pêyâhtik. ||| She wondered at the quiet way he ambled on.
êkwa itêw, "kisiwâk êkwa pê-ayâw." "kahkiyaw êkwa anihi kâ-kî-piciyit kitamwêw," itwêw awa nâpêw. ||| Then he told her, “Now she has come near. She is eating up all those who moved camp,” said that man.
mistahi pakwâtam awa iskwêw. ||| The woman was greatly distressed.
"êcika awa ê-manitôwit!" itêyimêw êsa wîtimwa; "êwako êcika awa êkâ kâ-ôh-wî-atoskêt!" itêyihtam êsa awa iskwêw. ||| “So it seems that he has manitou power!” she thought of her brother-in-law; “So that is why he will never do any work!” thought the woman.
êkwa ati-tipiskâyiw. ||| Darkness was falling.
ê-ati-tipiskâyik, âhci piko pimâmôwak. ||| When it grew dark, they nevertheless went fleeing on.
"nîtim, êkwa kîkinaw pê-otihtam," itwêw êsa. ||| “Sister-in-Law, now she has reached our dwelling,” he said.
êkwa tâpwê tapasîwak. ||| Then truly they fled.
"pita aywêpi; mîcisôw." ||| “Stop and rest; eat.”
êkwa tâpwê mîcisôw awa iskwêw. ||| So then the woman ate.
mayaw ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, atimwa ê-kî-asamât, tapasîwak. ||| As soon as they had eaten, after feeding the dogs, they went on in flight.
êkwa tâpwê ê-ati-wâpaniyik, misi-sâkahikan otihtamwak. ||| Then, as dawn came, they reached a large lake.
"wêpinik atimwak," itêw wîtimwa. ||| “Turn the dogs loose,” he told his sister-in-law.
tâpwê awa iskwêw wêpinêw atimwa. ||| So the woman turned the dogs loose.
êkwa wîtimwa nayômêw êkwa ocawâsimisa. ||| Then he took his sister-in-law and the children on his back.
pêyak awa iskwêw nayômêw; êkwa awa nâpêw tahkonêw wîtimwa mîna nayômêw. ||| The woman took one on her back; the man took hold of his sister-in-law, and bore her on his back.
êkwa kâ-pêtisâpamâcik miskwamîhk ê-pê-pmohtêyit ôhi iskwêwa. ||| And then they saw that woman come walking toward them over the ice.
kîtahtawê, "sôhki tapasî, nîtim." "âsay kikitimâkêyimin!" itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| Then, soon, “Flee with all your might, Brother-in-Law. You have taken pity on me!” said the woman.
kîtahtawê wâskahikana atâwêkamik ita ê-ayâyik otihtamwak. ||| Presently they came to some wooden houses of a trading post.
ômisi itwêwak: "awa iskwêw wîhtikôw nipê-mâkohikonân!" itwêw êsa; "mistahi nîtim manitôwiw," itwêw êsa; "kiyâm sîhkimihk; mâskôc ahpô kita-nipahêw wîhtikôwa," itwêw êsa. ||| They spoke thus: “We have been driven here by that Windigo woman!” she said; “My brother-in-law has great manitou power,” she said; “Do ask him; perhaps he will even kill the Windigo,” she said.
tâpwê otatâwêw wiya tipiyaw itohtêw. ||| Then the trader came in person.
ômisi itêw anihi nâpêwa: "kitimâkêyiminân, kaspwân!" "osâm nika-mêscihikonân wîhtikôw." "iyikohk âpihtaw ôta kêkway ê-astêk ka-miyitin." ||| He said to that man, “Take pity on us, Gaspard! The Windigo will destroy us all. Half of the goods that are here I will give you.”
"âta wiya êkoyikohk kêkway mistahi ôta astêw atâwêkamikohk." ||| “Then all the goods, as many as are here in the trading post.”
"êha," itwêw awa kaspwân, "mâka iskwêwi-ayôwinisa nîswâyihk osîhtâk," itwêw êsa; "kakwêyâhok," itwêw êsa. ||| “Very well,” said Gaspard, “but make two suits of women's clothes,” he said; “Hurry up,” he said.
tâpwê kakwêyâhowak nîswâyihk iskwêwi-ayôwinisa ê-osîhtâcik. ||| So they hastened to make two suits of women's clothes.
tâpwê êkosi isi wawêyîw. ||| So he dressed himself.
"kîkway mîna?" itik ôhi otatâwêwa. ||| “What else?” the trader asked him.
"nîso mîna akwanânak ninitawêyimâwak," itêw êsa, "nîso mîna tâpiskâkanak, êkwa cîkahikanis." ||| “I need also two shawls,” he told him, “and two necklaces, and a hatchet.”
tâpwê kahkiyaw miyâwak. ||| They were given everything.
êkwa ê-kî-miyihcik, âhci piko natomêw sênapâna. ||| When the things had been given to them, he called for ribbons beside.
êkwa postayôwinisêwak. ||| Then they put on the clothes.
"pê-askôwin, nîtim," itêw êsa. ||| “Follow close behind me, Sister-in-Law,” he told her.
tâpwê pê-askôwêw awa wîtimwa iskwêw. ||| So the woman followed close behind her brother-in-law.
mayaw ê-otihtâcik, samaskipayihôw maskwamîhk awa oskinîkiskwêw kâ-kî-wîhtikôwit. ||| As soon as they came to where she was, that young woman who had turned into a windigo throw herself flat on the ice.
kâsôw; kâtâw ohkwâkan. ||| She hid herself; she hid her face.
"kipê-nitomitin, nicâhkos!" itêw êsa awa kâ-nitawi-nipahât. ||| “I have come to invite you, my gossip,” he who had come to kill her said to her.
namwâc êsa wî-kitotik ahpô. ||| She would not even speak to him.
namwâc ahpô wî-kitâpamik. ||| She would not so much as look at him.
"tânisi awa êtahkamikisit?" "mistahi ôma namôya kwayask kitôtên, mihcêt ayîsiyiniwak ê-kitamwacik!" itwêw êsa. ||| “How is this person carrying on? You do very wrong to eat up many people!” he said.
êkwa pasikôw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| Then that young woman rose to her feet.
"namôya mâka misawâc ka-kî-sâkôcihin!" itwêw êsa. ||| “Nevertheless, You will not be able to overcome me!” she said.
sêmâk ê-ati-têpwêt, ômisi itêw awa wîtimwa: "nîtim, kiyâm kiya pakama!" "osâm nimacêyimâw!" itwêw êsa. ||| At once he called out and said to his sister-in-law, “Sister-in-Law, please, do you strike her down! I think her of too little account!” he said.
tâpwê awa iskwêw pakamahwêw êsa ôhi wîhtikôwa. ||| Accordingly the woman struck down that Windigo.
êkwa ômisi itêw: "nîtim, kwayask âcimôhkan ê-isi-nipahâyâhk." ||| Then he told her, “Sister-in-Law, do you then tell aright the tale of how we killed her.”
êkosi êkwa awa oskinîkiw kâ-kihtimit, êkosi êkwa miyâci-atoskêt. ||| And after that this youth, who had been so lazy, began to work.
ê-kî-nipahât, mâci-nikohtêw. ||| When he had killed that person, he began to gather fire-wood.
mayaw kîkisêpâ kîsi-piminawasôw. ||| Early in the morning he had his cooking done.
mâmaskâtam awa iskwêw, êkwa ê-mâc-âtoskêyit; okihtimiyih! ||| The woman wondered at his now beginning to work; he had been so lazy!
êkwa mîna êkosi mîna mâcîw awa. ||| And then, too, he began to hunt.
nama wîhkâc êkwa apiw. ||| Now he never sat at home.
"kiyâm niya nika-onâpêmin!" itêyihtam êsa awa iskwêw. ||| “Let me be the one to have him for my husband!” thought that woman.
"matwân cî nika-pakwâtik?" itêyihtam êsa. ||| “Can it be that he will reject me?” she thought.
kîtahtawê ê-apiyit, "nîtim, kitimâkêyimin." "kiyâm niya wîkimin; êkâ wiya pîtos awiyak wîkim," itwêw êsa awa iskwêw. ||| Then, at one time, when he was at home, “Brother-in-Law, take pity on me. Do marry me; do not marry anyone else,” said that woman.
"tâpwê, nîtim, âta êsa kwayask kititwâh." "namôya cêskwa ta-kî-wîwiyân," itêw êsa wîtimwa; "kîspin wîwiyâni, wîpac nika-nipin," itwêw êsa awa nâpêw kaspwân. ||| “Truly, Sister-in-Law, you have spoken like a good woman. But I cannot yet a while take a wife,” he told his sister-in-law, “If I take a wife, I shall soon die,” said that man, Gaspard.
êkwa âsay mîna kîhtwâm kakwêcimêw wîtimwa. ||| Then again she questioned her brother-in-law.
"tâpwê kikitimahin, nîtim, êkâ wîkimiyin," itwêw êsa awa iskwêw; "'tâpwê êtokê ê-kitimâkêyimât ôhi otawâsimisa?' kititêyimitih!" itêw êsa wîtimwa. ||| “Truly, you cause me sorrow, Brother-in-Law, by not marrying me,” said that woman; “'I wonder if he really loves the children!' I have been thinking of you!” she said to her brother-in-law.
"êha, nîtim, nikitimâkêyimâwak; êwako ohci kâ-ôh-pamihtâtân," itêw êsa. ||| “Indeed, Sister-in-Law, I love them; that is why I am supporting them for you,” he told her.
"êha, nîtim, têpiyâhk aciyaw wîkimitâni!" itwêw êsa. ||| “Oh, Brother-in-Law, if I could be married to you for even a little time!” she said.
tâpwê wîwiw nicawâc wîtimwa. ||| So he needs took his sister-in-law to wife.
ê-mâci-piciwiht, ati-sêmâk-wîcihiwêwak. ||| When the people began to move camp, they went along at once.
kâh-kisiwâhtwâw; mistahi nihtâ-minahôw; mîna ê-nihtâ-wanihikêt, mitoni nanâtohk atâwâkana misiwê nâh-nipahêw. ||| He was the object of many people's anger; he was very good at killing game; and he was a good trapper, too, and continued to kill many furred things of all kinds.
maci-ayîsiyiniwak oyasowâtêwak êsa, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahâcik. ||| Some evil men decided to try to kill him.
"osâm mistahi nikitimahikonân kaspwân," nitawi-itwêwak wîkiwâhk. ||| “Gaspard is making us too poor,” they said in their lodge to which they had gone.
takohtêw awa kaspwân, kahkiyaw êsa kâ-piciwiht, "tânêhki kâ-ôh-picicik?" ê-itwêt. ||| Gaspard came and saw that all his band had moved camp and asked, “Why have they moved camp?”
wîhtamawâw mistahi ê-kisiwâhât. ||| He was told that he had greatly angered them.
tâpwê nêwo ôki mistahi ê-manitôwicik kisiwâsiwak. ||| And really, four who had great manitou power were angry.
itwêwak, "ohcitaw kika-nipahânaw!" itwêwak; "namôya ka-kî-pwâtawihânaw!" itwêwak maci-ayîsiyiniwak. ||| They said, “By all means, let us kill him! Not by any chance can we fail of him!” said the evil men.
nêwiwak êsa, mistahi ê-manitôwicik. ||| They were four, who had great manitou power.
tâpwê mâci-osîhtâwak êsa, ê-wî-kosâpahtahkik, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahâcik. ||| And so they set about building that which they would use for the medium's work, meaning to try to kill him.
tâpwê âta ê-pê-nitomiht, opawâkaniyiwa ê-nitomikot, namôya tâpwêhtam. ||| Truly, though he was summoned from his home, though their dream spirit summoned him, he gave no heed.
nêwo-tipiskâw tahto-tipiskâw ê-kosâpahtahkik ôki maci-ayîsiyiniwak, namôya kî-itohtêyiwa. ||| For four nights every night those evil men used the medium's tent, but he did not go there.
iskwêyâc êkwa ômisi êsa itêw nôtokêwa pêyak ê-ayâwâcik: "nôhkô, pêsiw kitihkom," itêw êsa; "êkotôwahk nika-ôh-nipahâwak," itwêw êsa. ||| At the end of this time he spoke thus to a certain old woman whom they had with them: “Grandmother, give me a louse of yours,” he said to her; “With such I shall kill them,” he said.
tâpwê nôtokwêw awa nitonawêw êsa, ê-misikitiyit otihkoma mayaw ê-miskawât. ||| So the old woman looked for one, and straightway found a large one of her lice.
ocihcîhk êsa ahêw awa nâpêw. ||| The man set it on his hand.
tâpwê mayaw êkwa ê-pê-nitomikot ôhi pawâtâkana, itohtêw. ||| Then, as soon as those dream spirits came and summoned him, he went there.
pîhtokêw kosâpahcikanihk. ||| He went into the medium's tent.
êkwa tâpwê mawinêhok ôhi. ||| Then truly they sought fight with him.
ômisi êsa itêw: "kikitimâkisinâwâw kâ-wî-kakwê-nipahiyêk," itwêw êsa; "namôya kikî-nipahinâwâw," itwêw êsa; "mistahi nimanitôwin," itwêw êsa. ||| Thus he spoke to them: “You are pitiable, you who mean to kill me,” he said; “You cannot kill me,” he said; “I have great manitou power,” he said.
hâw, pakitinêw ihkwa. ||| There, he set down the louse.
"kita-wî-nipahik awa maci-ayîsiyiniw ôhi ihkwa!" itwêw êsa. ||| “Let this evil man be killed by this louse!” he said.
tâpwê maci-ayîsiyiniw êsa nipahik ôhi ihkwa. ||| Then truly, the evil man was killed by the louse.
misiwê otônihk pîhtokêyiwa; êkosi isi nipahik, ê-kipwatâmoskâkot ihkwa. ||| It went into his mouth and down his throat; and so the louse killed him by stopping his windpipe.
"tânisi êkwa kâ-manitôwit?" itwêwak êsa; "tânisi?" ||| “Why, what is the matter with the manitou man?” they asked; “What is it?”
"kipatâmoskâk ihkwa!" itwêwak êsa. ||| “A louse choked him!” they said.
namwâc êsa kî-nahinâw, êkosi ê-isi-wêpiniht, osâm mistahi ihkwak ê-ayâcik. ||| It was not even possible to bury him, and he was merely left there, for there were too many lice.
âsay mîna kîhtwâm ê-tipiskâk kotak awa maci-ayîsiyiniw, êwako wî-kakwê-nipahêw. ||| When the next night came, the second evil man tried to kill him.
âsay mîna êwako sîhkihkêmôw, kosâpahcikan ta-osihtâwiht. ||| This one, too, gave instructions that they build a medium's lodge for him.
tâpwê osîhtâwân kosâpahcikan. ||| So a medium's tent was built for him.
mayaw ê-kîsihtâwiht, âsay mîna pê-natomâw. ||| As soon as they had finished it for him, again he was summoned.
âsay mîna ôhkoma nitotamawêw, kotaka ta-miyikot ihkwa. ||| Again he asked his grandmother to give him a louse.
tâpwê awa nôtokêsiw mîna kotaka nitonawêw otihkoma. ||| So the old woman looked for another of her lice.
âsay mîna êwakoni nitawi-ohci-nipahêw. ||| He went and killed this one, too, with it.
maci-ayîsiyiniwa kahkiyaw mêscihêw. ||| He killed off all the evil men.
nêwo-tipiskâw tahto-tipiskâw ê-osîhtâyit êsa kosâpahcikan, kahkiyaw êsa aniki maci-ayîsiyiniwak ihkwa êsa kî-mêsci-nipahikwak, nêwo maci-ayîsiyiniwak. ||| Having for four nights every night set up a medium's tent, all those evil men were killed off by lice, four evil men.
êkwa nitawi-mawimostawêwak ôhi kaspwâna. ||| Then they went to entreat Gaspard.
"kiyâm kitimâkêyiminân! ||| “Pray, take pity on us!
kiyâm êkâya niyanân nipahinân!" itwêw êsa. ||| Pray, do not kill us, too!” the spokesman said.
"tâpwê namôya kiyawâw kâ-kisiwâhiyêk," itwêw êsa kaspwân; "ayâwihkok ôki kâ-wî-miyiyêk," itwêw êsa. ||| “Really, it is not you who made me angry,” said Gaspard; “Keep those things you mean to give me,” he said.
kîtahtawê mîna kotakak ôki maci-ayîsiyiniwak mastaw êhtakocik. ||| Presently, there came into being, later, some more evil men.
ayisk wiya êkwa okimâwiw awa kaspwân. ||| Now, by this time, this Gaspard was the chief.
pê-nitomâw ê-mâmawôpicik ôki ayîsiyiniwak, êkota ohci pê-nitomâw. ||| They sent for him. From where those people were sitting in assembly, he was sent for.
"wîhtikôw kiwî-otihtikonaw," itwêwak ôki nâpêwak. ||| “A Windigo is coming to where we are,” said those men.
êwako ôma ohci kâ-ôh-mâmawôpicik, êkwa ê-pê-nitomiht awa kaspwân. ||| That was why they were sitting in council, and why Gaspard was sent for.
"namôya kita-kî-takohtêw anohc wiya kâ-pipohk." "kîhtwâm pôni-ocêhtowi-kîsikâki, êkospîhk ta-takohtêw." "kiyâm kita-pônêyihtamok." ||| “He cannot arrive this winter. When New Year's Day has passed again, then he will arrive. Let them think no more about it.”
êkosi tâpwê namôya takohtêw wîhtikôw. ||| And really, the Windigo did not come.
piyisk êkosi namôya na-nâkatôhkêwak. ||| In time they ceased from their alertness.
piyis mîna niyîpihk êkwa ê-ati-takwâkihk, mâci-wawêyîwak omâcîwak. ||| Then, when summer had passed and autumn was coming on, the hunters began to make ready.
"nika-wîcêwâwak," itwêw êsa kaspwân; "anohc ôma kâ-pipohk, êkwa kâ-wî-takohtêt wîhtikôw," itwêw êsa; "âta wiya namôya nikêhcinâhon ta-kî-nipahak." "nawac piko nikostâw," itwêw êsa kaspwâl. ||| “I shall go with them,” said Gaspard; “This winter is when the Windigo will come,” he said; “To be sure, I am not certain that I shall be able to kill him. Rather, in fact, I fear him,” said Gaspard.
tâpwê êsa wawêyîw wîsta. ||| And so he too got ready.
kâ-mâci-piciwiht, êkotê ê-ay-ayâcik, tahto-tipiskâw ayîsiyiniwak ôki kostâcîskâkwak wîhtikôwa, tahki êsa ê-mâmawôpicik. ||| When the band started to move, then off in that place where they were, every night those people were frightened for the coming of the Windigo, and would always sit assembled.
mwêhci ê-âpihtâwi-piponiyik, ê-ati-tipiskâyik, wîsâmêw wîwa. ||| Exactly in the middle of winter, one night, as darkness came on, he asked his wife to go with him.
ômisi êsa itêw: "anohc êkwa kâ-wî-tipiskâk wîhtikôw kâ-wî-takosihk." "kîstanaw nitawâpitân," itêw êsa wîwa. ||| He said to her, “In this very night that is now at hand, is when the Windigo will arrive. Let us too be on the lookout,” he told his wife.
tâpwê wawêyîw awa iskwêw. ||| So the woman dressed up.
itohtêwak, wiyawâw mîna ê-nitawâpicik. ||| They went there, that they too might watch.
mayaw ê-pîhtokêcik mistahi miywêyihtamwân. ||| As soon as they entered the tipi, all the people were very glad.
ômisi itêw ôhi nâpêwa: "âhkamêyimok!" "anohc êkwa, kêkâc wâpahki, wîhtikôw wî-takosin," itwêw êsa. ||| He said to those men, “Do your best! Tonight, just before dawn, the Windigo will arrive,” he said.
sâsay êkwa pêhtamwak ayîsiyiniwak mosis wîhtikôwa ê-matwê-yêhyêyit. ||| By this time the people heard plainly the loud breathing of the Windigo.
êkwa ômisi itwêw: "acosisa osîhtâk mitoni ê-apisâsiki." ||| Then he said, “Make some very small arrows.”
ê-kîsihtâwiht, miyâw. ||| When they had been finished for him, he was given them.
tâpwê kêtayôwinisêw; osâwasiskîwastênisôw. ||| Then he took off his clothes; he painted himself with ochre.
êkota êsa sêmâk kwêskimow, êsa ê-apiscâwâsisiwit. ||| Then, all at once, he changed his form, turning into a little child.
mitoni mâmaskâtamwak êsa ôki nâpêwak êkota kâ-ayâcik, apisc-awâsisa ê-wâpamâcik, ê-kwêskimowit kaspwân. ||| Those men who were there were greatly amazed when they saw the little child into which Gaspard had transformed himself.
êkosi isi ati-isi-ohpiskâw, ê-nitawi-nakiskawât wîhtikôwa. ||| Thereupon, in that form, he rose into the air, to go and encounter the Windigo.
mistahi êsa kinosiyiwa ôhi wîhtikôwa, kahkiyaw êsa mistikwa ê-ayiwâkiskawâyit, iyikohk ê-kinosiyit. ||| That Windigo was very tall, so tall that he overtopped all the trees.
tâpwê nakiskawêw; ê-atimapiyit êsa otihtêw. ||| Really, he met him; he came upon him as he sat facing yon way.
"kîkway ôta ê-osîhtâyan?" itêw êsa; "kîkway kiyi-osîhtâyan?" ||| “What are you doing here?” he asked him; “What is it you mean to do?”
"anohc kâ-tipiskâk kahkiyaw kiwî-kitamotinâwâw!" itik êsa. ||| “Tonight I mean to devour you all!” the other told him.
mâci-têpwêwak, ê-nôtinitocik, mistikwa mîna êkwa ê-pâh-pahkwacipitâcik, ê-ohci-pâh-pakamahotocik. ||| They began to whoop, as they fought, tearing up trees with which they beat each other.
êkosi mistahi ohtêyihtamwak oskinîkiwak. ||| Then the young men were very envious.
"tânisi êtokê ka-kî-isi-nipahânaw?" Let us try to kill him in this way,” said those young men; “'Let us tell one another by what means each of us can be killed,' we will say to him,” said the young men.
tâpwê tahto-tipiskâw mâna ê-mâh-mâmawôpicik, tahto ôki kâ-pawâmicik wâh-wîhtamâtôwak. ||| Accordingly, every night, as they sat assembled in their usual way, they told one another their dreams.
kîtahtawê êsa wîsta kâ-itohtêt. ||| Then at one time he too went there.
"namôya konita ta-kî-pîhtokêyan," itik ôhi oskinîkiwa; "tânitowihk kiya êkâ kâ-ôh-kî-nipahikawiyan?" itik êsa. ||| “You cannot come in without paying the price,” the young men said to him; “To what manner of thing is it due that you cannot be killed?” they asked him.
"nama wîhkâc nika-nipahikawin," itwêw êsa; "pêyak kêkway sîpâ misitihk kêkway kita-ohtinamihk kita-mâhtakoskâkoyân." ||| “I shall never be killed,” he said; “There is but one thing: if something taken from under one's foot surmounted me.”
mayaw ê-tipiskâyik, nitawi-astâwân sîpâ itôwahk kâ-tahkoskâtamihk mâna asâmihk ohci. ||| As soon as night had come, they went and placed on him the kind of thing that is stepped on underneath, from a snowshoe.
êkosi êsa kî-nâspici-nipâw. ||| Thereupon he never awoke from his sleep.
êkota êsa kî-nipahâw kaspwân, osâm mistahi ê-kî-manitôwakêyimot. ||| So at this point Gaspard was killed, because he had thought himself too much of a manitou.
tahkohc otakohpihk ê-astâwiht anima, kâ-nipahikot asâmêyâpiy. ||| When that thing was placed on top of his blanket, he was killed by the snowshoe strap.
êkoyikohk ê-mêscihtâyân, ê-kîsihtâyân. ||| Now I have told it all, now I have finished it.
kîtahtawê pêyak awa nâpêw, ê-nîsicik owîkimâkana, ita ê-wîkicik. ||| Once upon a time there was a man who lived alone somewhere with only his wife.
kâ-nipahât mostoswa, ê-takohtêt wîkiwâhk, ê-wîhtamawât owîkimâkana, wawêyîw awa iskwêw, ê-wî-nâtahk wiyâsa. ||| When he had killed buffalo, as he arrived at their tipi and told his wife, the woman would make ready to fetch the meat.
astis manipitam, ê-macostêhahk iskotêhk. ||| She would pull out a dried sinew and scorch it in the fire.
papêtikohkahtêw astisis. ||| The sinew would shrivel up small.
"ômisi isi ta-kisiwâkiwiw, kâ-wî-nâtamân wiyâsa!" itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Even thus let it be near whence I am to fetch the meats!” she would say.
êkosi ê-wayawît, ê-sipwêhtêt, ê-nâtahk wiyâsa, tâpwê kisiwâk otihtam, ê-otinahk, ê-kîwêhtatât. ||| Thereupon, when she left the tipi and went forth to fetch the meat, she would in fact come to it close by, and take it and bring it home.
"wâ," itêyihtam awa nâpêw, "tâpwê kâh-kiyipa pêtâw wiyâsa," itêyihtam. ||| “Dear me,” thought the man, “truly she is always quick about bringing the meat,” thought he.
êkosi kîtahtawê kiskêyihtam wîwa ê-misikitiyit, ê-pwâwiyit. ||| Then presently he know that his wife was big with child.
pêyakwanohk ayâw; namôya wî-mâcîw, "kiyâm ta-miyopayiw," ê-itêyimât owîkimâkana; "êkâ ka-misi-wanâcihât ôhi awâsisa watâhk kâ-asiwasoyit," itêyihtam awa nâpêw. ||| He stayed right there; he did not care to hunt, thinking of his wife, “Pray that it may go well with her, that she may not lose the child that is in her womb,” thought the man.
pôti kîtahtawê âhkosiyiwa owîkimâkana, ê-wî-wâpamâcik ôhi awâsisa. ||| Presently, there, his wife fell ill, for they were about to see their child.
tâpwê ê-tipiskâyik, pahkisiniyiwa. ||| And indeed, when darkness came, she was forced to her couch.
mistahi miywêyihtam awa nâpêw ê-otawâsimisiyit wîwa êwakoni. ||| The man was very glad that his wife had given birth to a child.
êwako êkwa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| And this child was Wisahketchahk.
êkosi kanawêyimêwak, ê-ohpikihâcik. ||| So they cared for him and brought him up.
piyis misikitiw awa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| In time this Wisahketchahk grew big.
âsay mîna ocawâsimisiwak. ||| Again they had a child.
mîna êwako nihtâwikiw. ||| This one, too, was born.
osîmisiw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk had a little brother.
êkwa êkota ay-ayâwak. ||| So they lived in that place.
piyisk misikitiwak ôki awâsisak. ||| In time those children grew big.
êkwa pisisik mâcîw awa nâpêw. ||| And that man did nothing but hunt.
êkwa awa iskwêw ê-nikohtêt mâna, na-nama-mayaw takohtêw awa iskwêw. ||| Now, when that woman gathered firewood, she had a way of not coming back on time.
"namôya êkwa atoskêw êkoyikohk," itêyimêw owîkimâkana awa nâpêw, osâm kâh-kinwêsk ê-nikohtêyit; "tânisi awa tiyôtahk?" itêyimêw; "mahti nika-kakwê-kiskêyimâw kêkwayi ê-otamihikot;" "osâm kâ-kapê-kîsik nikohtêw." ê-itêyimât owîkimâkana. ||| “Now, she does not work as long as this,” thought the man of his wife, when again and again she took too long about gathering wood; “What is it she does?” he thought of her; “I had better try and find out what sort of thing delays her; she is all day gathering firewood,” thought he of his wife.
kîkisêpâ wawêyîw, ê-wî-mâcît, ê-sipwêhtêt, êkwa itê kâ-nikohtêyit owîkimâkana, êkotê ê-itohtêt. ||| The next morning he made ready to go hunting and set out and went to where his wife got firewood.
êkota kâsôhtawêw owîkimâkana. ||| There he hid from his wife.
kîtahtawê kâ-pêci-âstamohtêyit, ê-pê-nikohtêyit. ||| Presently she came walking that way, at her task of getting firewood.
ê-pê-takohtêyit êkota sakâhk, kâ-wâpamât ê-misikitiyit mistikwa ê-kîskipayiyit. ||| When she arrived there in the grove, he noticed a large cleft tree.
êkota nîpawiyiwa owîkimâkana, ê-kêtayôwinisêyit, ê-mosêskatêyit. ||| By it his wife took her stand, and took off her clothes until she stood naked.
otinam mistik awa iskwêw, ôhi mistikwa kâ-misikitiyit ê-pa-pakamahwât awa iskwêw. ||| She took up a stick and began to beat that large tree.
ômisi itwêw: "ninâpêmitik!" itwêw, kâ-wâpamât awa nâpêw mihcêt ê-wayawiyit mistikohk ohci kinêpikwa. ||| This was what she said: “O my husbands!” she said, and then the man saw a great many serpents come forth from the tree.
êkosi nahapiw awa iskwêw, ê-pimisihk, misiwê êkota ê-papâmâhtawêyit ôhi kinêpikwa awa iskwêw wiyawihk. ||| At that the woman lay down flat and those serpents climbed this way and that all over her body.
piyisk namôya wâpamêw owîkimâkana, osâm misiwê ê-ayâyit kinêpikwa. ||| Soon he could no longer see his wife, for the serpents were all over her.
êkosi isi sipwêhtêw awa nâpêw, wâhyaw ê-nitawi-nipahât mostoswa. ||| Thereupon that man went away; he went far away and killed a buffalo.
ê-kîwêt, nôhtaw tipiskâyiw. ||| It was dark before he got home.
piyis takohtêw; mistahi nîpâhtêw wîkiwâhk. ||| At last he arrived; in deep darkness he came home from his tramp.
êkosi ê-wâpahk, "ninêstosin," itwêw awa nâpêw; "namôya niwî-mâcîn," itêw owîkimâkana. ||| Then, the next morning, “I am tired,” said the man; “I am not going to hunt,” he told his wife.
wawêyîw awa iskwêw, ê-wî-nâtahk wiyâsa. ||| The woman made ready to fetch the meat.
otinam astis, ê-macostêhahk. ||| She took a sinew and scorched it.
"ômisi ta-isi-kisiwâkiwiw kâ-wî-nâtamân wiyâsa!" itwêw awa iskwêw, ê-ati-wayawît. ||| “Even thus let it be near whence I am to fetch the meats!” she said, going out of the tent.
awa nâpêw otinam ôma astisis kâ-kî-macostêhamiyit owîkimâkana, ê-sîpêkipitahk, "ta-wî-pîhcâyiw kâ-nâtahk wiyâsa!" ê-itât owîkimâkana, cikêmâ ê-kisiwâsit. ||| The man took the little bit of sinew which his wife had scorched, and stretched it long, saying, of his wife, “Let it be far whence she fetches the meats!”
"hâw, hâw, nitawâsimisitik, namôya êsa ôyâ kwayask ê-tôtahk kikâwiyiwâw, kâ-kinwêsk kâ-nikohtêt." "nikî-wâpamâw tânisi ê-tôtahk; nipakwâtên." "tapasîk," itêw, "niwî-nipahâw kikâwiyiwâw," itêw. ||| “Come, my children, it seems that your mother who has left has been acting in no becoming way, when always so long she was at gathering firewood. I have seen what she did; it is hateful to me. Flee,” he told them; “I am going to kill your mother,” he told them.
"hâw, nitawâsimisitik, ôta kwayasitêk; tapasîk!" itwêw. ||| “Come, my children, go into this hole; flee!” he said.
êkwa ôki nâpêsisak êkota pîhtokêwak. ||| Then those boys went in there.
kâwi êkota astâw apasoy, ê-tapasîyit otawâsimisa. ||| He put back the tent-pole, and his children fled.
êkwa awa nâpêw otinêw askihkwa êkwa cîkahikan, ê-sipwêhtêt, ê-itohtêt ôhi mistikwa kâ-kî-pa-pakamahwâyit owîkimâkana. ||| Then that man took a kettle and an axe and went, off, going to that tree which his wife had struck.
ômisi itwêw, ê-otinahk mistik, ê-pa-pakamahwât ôhi mistikwa: "ninâpêmitik, nitakohtân!" itêw. ||| Taking up a stick of wood and repeatedly striking the tree, he said, “O my husbands, I have come!”
pôti ê-pê-wayawiyit kinêpikwa, cîkahwêw; nipahêw, êkota askihkohk mihko ê-ati-sîkinahk; wiya ôhi wêpinêw. ||| Then, look you, when the serpents came forth, he hacked them with the axe and killed them, but always poured the blood into the kettle; what was left of them he threw away.
piyê-wayawiyici, ati-nipahêw, askihkohk tahki ê-astât mihko. ||| He kept killing them as they came forth, and always put the blood in the kettle.
piyis kahkiyaw nipahêw ôhi kinêpikwa. ||| At last he had killed all of those serpents.
êkosi kîwêw; kîwêhtatâw ôma mihko. ||| Thereupon he went home; he took the blood home with him.
êkwa ê-ay-apit, piyisk kêkâc tipiskâw; êkoyikohk kâ-takohtêyit owîkimâkana, ê-pêtâyit wiyâs. ||| As he sat there, at last it began to grow dark; only then did his wife arrive, bringing the meat.
ômisi itwêw awa iskwêw: "tâpwê wâhyaw kikî-nipahâw mostos!" itwêw awa iskwêw; "kêsiskaw nika-nikohtân; osâm kiyipa ta-tipiskâw," itwêw. ||| Thus spoke that woman: “Truly far off did you kill the buffalo!” she said; “First I shall get firewood; soon it will be dark,” she said.
"cêskwa!" itwêw awa nâpêw; "pita mîci," itêw owîkimâkana; "ôma ê-kî-osîhtâyân mihko ta-mîciyan," itêw. ||| “Wait!” said the man; “First eat this,” he told his wife; “Eat this blood which I have prepared,” he told her.
"namôya; osâm nipapâsêyihtên ê-wî-nikohtêyân," itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “No; I must hurry and get my firewood,” said the woman.
"kêsiskaw mîciso; kayâs kâ-kî-mîcisoyan," itêw owîkimâkana. ||| “First eat; it is a long time since you have eaten,” he said to his wife.
"êha," itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Very well,” said the woman.
pîhtokêw, ôma mihko ê-otinahk, ê-minihkwêt. ||| She went into the tipi and took the blood and drank it.
tâpwê ê-wîhkasiniyik awa!" itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| Truly this creature's blood tastes good!” she said.
"kinisitospitên cî?" itêw awa nâpêw. ||| “Do you recognize the taste of it?” the man asked her.
"êha; mihko mâka ôma," itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Yes, why, this is blood,” said she.
"kinâpêm-mihko!" itêw awa owîkimâkana. ||| “Your husband's blood!” he said to his wife.
"nâ, mâkw awa nika-kakwâhyakihikoh!" itwêw awa iskwêw, ê-ati-wayawît, ê-itohtêt ôhi mistikwa. ||| “Heavens, but he has frightened me!” cried the woman, as she left the tent and went to that tree.
mistik ê-otinahk, ê-pa-pakamahwât ôhi mistikwa, "ninâpêmitik, nitakosinin!" itwêw awa iskwêw, pêyak ê-apisîsisiyit kâ-pê-wayawiyit. ||| Taking up a stick and beating at the tree, “O my husbands, I have come!” called the woman, and one tiny little one came out.
kisiwâsiw; êkwa kîwêw. ||| She was angry; she went home.
êkwa awa nâpêw cîkahikan otinam, kisiwâk ê-pê-ayâyit owîkimâkana. ||| Then that man took an axe, as his wife came near.
ômisi itwêw awa iskwêw: "kikisiwâhin kâ-mêscihacik ninâpêmak!" itwêw. ||| Thus spoke the woman: “You have angered me by killing all my husbands!” she cried.
ê-wî-pîhtokêyit, kâ-cîkahwât owîkimâkana; kîskikwêtahwêw owîkimâkana. ||| As she was about to enter the lodge, he struck his wife with the axe; he chopped off his wife's head.
êkosi ê-tapasît, hâ, ispimihk ê-itohtêt. ||| Then he fled; way up aloft he went.
"hâw, ayîsiyiniw cêskwa ôtê nîkân tita-ohpikiw;" "'kâ-misikitit acâhkos,' tita-itwêwak." "niya êwako," itwêw awa nâpêw. ||| “Now, off in the future man will grow into being; 'The Great Star,' they will say. That will be I,” said the man.
êkwa awa iskwêw ostikwân tihtipipayiyiw, ê-nitonawât onâpêma. ||| Then that woman's head went rolling, as she sought her husband.
piyisk kiskêyihtam tânitê ê-itohtêyit onâpêma. ||| At last she perceived whither her husband had gone.
"hâw, niwîkimâkan, kikî-sâkihtân; ka-osôkanin!" "pimitisa kinâpêminaw, nisôkan!" ||| “There, my husband, you were fond of them; you shall have buttocks! Go follow our husband, 0 my buttocks!”
êkwa awa ôma ostikwân ôma tihtipipayiw, ê-nitonawât otawâsimisa. ||| Then that head went rolling, as she sought her children.
"miskawakwâwi, nika-mêscihâwak kitawâsimisak," itêw owîkimâkana. ||| “If I find them, I shall kill off your children,” she called to her husband.
misiwê nitonikêw awa tihtipistikwân. ||| That Rolling Head searched everywhere.
piyisk miskam ita kâ-kwayasitêyit otawâsimisa, êkwa ê-pimitisahwât. ||| At last she found the place where her children had gone into the ground, and she started in pursuit of them.
wâhyaw kî-wayawîwak ôki awâsisak, ê-tapasîcik. ||| Far off those children had emerged and gone on in their flight.
êwako, ôki nâpêsisak, wîsahkêcâhk êwako âskaw ê-nayômât osîmisa. ||| As to those boys, Wisahketchahk from time to time would carry his little brother on his back.
piyisk kisiwâk ayâyiwa okâwiyiwâwa, ôhi tihtipistikwâna. ||| At last quite near was their mother, that Rolling Head.
"nitawâsimisitik, pêhik! ||| “My children, wait for me!
nika-nôhâw kisîmis," itêw. ||| I want to suckle your little brother,” she called to them.
piyisk awa awâsis mâtôw. ||| Soon that child cried.
"nistêsê, pêhâtân kikâwiyinaw!" itwêw. ||| “Big Brother, let us wait for our mother!” he said.
ê-wî-nipahikoyahk ana kikâwiyinaw!" itêw. ||| Our mother there wants to kill us!” he told him.
"nitawâsimisitik, pêhik!" tahki ê-itât, piyisk kisiwâk ê-ay-ayâyit, "hâw," itwêw wîsahkêcâhk, "sîpiy ôta ta-wî-ayâw!" ||| “My children, wait for me!” it kept saying to them, and at last had come very near, when, “Here,” said Wisahketchahk, “Let there be a river here!”
ê-itwêt, âtakâmakisin, kâ-wâpamât cahcakiwa. ||| When he spoke thus, there was a stream blocking his path, and there he saw a crane.
"âsowahohinân, cahcakiw;" "nikâwiyinân ê-wî-nipahiyâhk," itêw. ||| “Take us across the water, Crane; our mother wants to kill us,” he said to it.
"êha," itikwak; "hahâw, nôsisimitik!" ||| “Very well,” it told them; “Come, my grandchildren!”
âsay kisiwâk pê-ayâyiwa okâwiyiwâwa. ||| By this time their mother had come very close.
êkosi nayômikwak, ê-wî-âsowahamiyit. ||| The crane took them on its back and was about to cross the water.
âsay êkota okâwiyiwâwa kâ-takohtêyit. ||| Their mother arrived.
"cahcak, pêsiw nitawâsimisak;" "nikaskêyihtên ê-wî-nôhâwasoyân." ||| Crane, bring me my children; I am sad with longing to suckle my child.”
"êkâya tâpwêhtaw, nimosô!" itêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “Do not believe her, Grandfather!” Wisahketchahk told it.
pihkohôw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk was taken across.
êkwa awa cahcakiw êkotê isicimêw. ||| Then the crane swam back yonder.
"âstam!" itwêw awa tihtipistikwân; "âsowahohin;" "nikaskêyihtên ê-wî-nôhâwasoyân." "ahpô kika-wîkimitin," itêw. ||| Come here!” cried that Rolling Head; “Take me across the water; I am sad with longing to suckle my child. If you like, I will even lie with you,” she told it.
"ahaq," itwêw awa cahcakiw; "hâw, ka-nayômitin." ||| “Very well, said the crane; “Come, I will take you on my back.”
"êkâya waskawî; nikâ-kîtimihkawisin," ê-wîsakêyihtahk ospiskwan. ||| “Do not move; my spine is very sensitive,” meaning that it had a pain in its back.
osâm pêyâhtik ê-pimohtêt, "kisiskâhtê!" itêw awa tihtipistikwân; "ninôhtê-nôhâwasowâh awa!" ômisi ê-ispayihot, ê-nâh-namipayihot. ||| When it went too slowly, “Go fast!” the Rolling Head cried at it; “I am in distress with the need of suckling this child!” and it threw itself about like this, bobbing up and down.
kwêtipipayihow awa cahcakiw; pakastawêpayiw awa tihtipistikwân. ||| The crane winced and ducked; into the water went that Rolling Head.
ômisi itwêw awa cahcakiw; "hâw, cêskwa nîkân ôtê ayîsiyiniw kita-ohpikiw;" "'namêw' kika-isiyihkâtikwak," itêw ôhi tihtipistikwâna. ||| Thus spoke the crane: “There, off in yon future time man will come into being; 'Sturgeon,' they will call you,” it said to that Rolling Head.
êkwa tâpwê mistahi mâtôw awa wîsahkêcâhk osîmisa, ê-wâpamât okâwiya ê-pakastawêhomiht. ||| Then truly Wisahketchahk's little brother wept much, when he saw his mother thrown into the water.
"nisîmis, êkâya mâto; ê-kî-wînipahikoyahk kikâwiyinaw," itêw osîmisa. ||| “Little Brother, do not weep; it is because our mother wanted to kill us,” he told his little brother.
êkota ay-ayâwak sîpîhk, ê-ma-mêtawêhât osîmisa. ||| There they stayed by the river, and he amused his little brother by making him play.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpamât kisêyiniwa, ôsihk ê-pê-pimiskâyit. ||| Then at one time he saw an old man who came paddling a canoe.

ê-ohpiwêpinât awa awâsis pâkahacôwânisa, êkotê pahkisiniyiwa. ||| When the child threw his little ball up into the air, there it fell.
otinêw, ê-ati-sipwêcimêt. ||| He took it and started to paddle away.
êkwa tâpwê mâtôw awa nâpêsis. ||| Then truly that little boy cried.
"nimosô," itêw awa wîsahkêcâhk, "pê-kapâwêpin nisîmis opâkahacôwânisa!" "êkwani ohci okîskowêmohikoh!" itêw. ||| “Grandfather,” Wisahketchahk called to him, “Throw my little brother's ball back here to the shore! That is what would make him stop crying!” he told him.
"â, nôsisê, pê-nâs!" ||| “Yes, Grandchild, come fetch it!”
êkosi ê-wî-nâtât, otapoyiwa êkota ê-ati-mitimêyâhtawêt wîsahkêcâhk, kâ-pôsiwêpahokot ôhi kisêyiniwa. ||| When, accordingly, Wisahketchahk came to fetch it, and was climbing out by holding on to the paddle, the old man threw him down into the canoe.
êkosi ê-ati-sipwêhtêyit, ê-nakatâcik osîmisa. ||| Then he started off, so that they left Wisahketchahk's little brother behind.
êkwa tâpwê mistahi mâtoyiwa. ||| The child wept bitterly.
"nimosô, kikitimahânaw nisîmis! ||| “Grandfather, we are making my little brother unhappy!
namôya tâpwêhtam awa kisêyiniw. ||| The old man paid no heed.
kîtahtawê awa awâsis kâ-mâtot itwêw: "nistêsê, tâpwê kikitimahin kâ-nakasiyan!" itwêw; "nicawâc nika-mahîhkaniwin," itwêw awa awâsis, ê-ati-sipwêpahtât. ||| Presently that child that was weeping cried out: “Big Brother, truly you are making me unhappy by leaving me! All I can do is turn into a wolf,” cried the child, and ran away from there.
mahîhkaniwiw; "ôhôwôwô" â, êkosi êkwa êkoyikohk êwako âtayôhkêwin. ||| He turned into a wolf. “Ohowowo!” There, that is the end of this sacred story.
kêtahtawê wawêyîw wîsahkêcâhk; sipwêhtêw. ||| Once upon a time Wisahketchahk got ready and went forth.
êkwa mostoswa wâpamêw. ||| Then he saw a buffalo.
"cêskwa, nisîm!" itêw. ||| “Wait a bit, Little Brother!” he said to it.
êkwa nakîwak ôki mostoswak. ||| Then the buffalo stopped.
"mâ, kitapwêsin," itêw. ||| “Why, you are all hot!” he said to it.
êkwa watâyihk isi-sâminêw. ||| Then he felt its belly.
êkotê ohci tahkamêw môhkomân. ||| He stabbed it from there with his knife.
pa-pimisin, êkwa wiyâsa ê-pimastât, ê-wî-mîcisot. ||| He lay there, having placed the pieces of meat along the ground, intending to eat.
êkwa ayih oskana cîkaham, pimiy ê-osîhtât; wîhkwâhk asiwatâw. ||| And the bones he broke, to make fat; he put it into the bladder.
êkwa itohtêw sîpîhk. ||| Then he went to the river.
wâpamêw ayi wacaskwa. ||| He saw some muskrats.
"âstam, nisîmitik," itêw; "ta-tahkâw ôma ayi." ||| “Come here, Little Brothers,” he said to them; “I want this stuff to get cool.”
osoyiyihk tahkopitam. ||| He tied it to the tail of one.
sipwêhtêw sîpîhk wacask, pimiy anima ê-tahkatiniyik, ê-papâmiskât. ||| Then the muskrat went off into the river, so that the fat cooled off as it swam about.
"êkâya sêkimin, nistêsê," itwêw wacask. ||| “Don't call out and frighten me,” said the muskrat.
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk askamawêw sakâhk. ||| Then Wisahketchahk watched it from the brush.
sîpîhk sisonê ê-kwêskosimât, sêkimêw wacaskwa. ||| From the bank of the stream he whistled at the muskrat and frightened it.
tapasîw wacask; koskopayihtâw ôma pimiy; êkwa sîpîhk pimâhotêw. ||| The muskrat fled; it spilled the fat; the fat floated on the water.
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk pimipahtâw sîpiy ôma ayi ê-sâ-sôpahtahk pimiy, sîpîhk. ||| Then Wisahketchahk ran and lapped up the fat from the river.
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk kisiwâsiw. ||| Angry was Wisahketchahk.
"ayîsiyiniwak'pîstêw' ta-itwêwak êkwa ôma pimiy." "niya askiy kâ-kî-osîhtâyân;" "kîhkîhk ka-nakiskâtin, wacask; kîhkîhk ka-nakiskâtin, niya askiy kâ-kî-osîhtâyân!" ||| “Mortal men will call this fat 'foam.' It was I who created this earth; in spite of all, I shall meet you, Muskrat, I who created this earth!”
êkwa sipwêhtêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Then Wisahketchahk went away.
êkosi misi-sakâw wâpahtam. ||| Then he saw a big forest.
êkwa piponiyiw; kawaciw mitoni. ||| Now it was winter; he was very cold.
wâpahtam mîkiwâhpa; awâsisa mâh-mêtawêyiwa. ||| He saw some tents; children were playing there.
"âstam, nisîm," itêw, "tâni anima ayi okimâw wîki?" ||| “Come here, Little Brother,” he said to one; “Which is the chief's tent?”
kiskinôhamâk; itohtêw. ||| The boy pointed it out to him, and he went there.
êkwa nâpêw awa, "tawâw, nistêsê!" ||| The man there called, “Come in, my elder brother!”
asamâw okiniya, pimihkân. ||| He was given wild quinces to eat, in the form of pemican.
"êkâya kêtayôwinisê, nistêsê;" "kîkisêpâ nipicinân." ||| “Do not undress, Brother; early in the morning we move camp.”
âhci piko kêtayôwinisêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| In spite of the warning, Wisahketchahk undressed.
akotâw ê-pâsahk otayiwinisa. ||| He hung up his clothes to dry.
kîkisêpâ mitoni ohpahowak pihêwak. ||| Early in the morning a great many partridges flew up.
wîsahkêcâhk kônihk waskic nipâw. ||| Wisahketchahk was sleeping on the snow.
êkwa kisinâyiw mitoni. ||| And it was very cold.
mistikohk akotêw awa ayiwinisa. ||| On a tree hung those clothes of his.
êkwa wî-nipahaciw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk was almost frozen to death.
kisiwâsiw; waniskâw; pihêwak ôki piciwak. ||| He was angry; he arose; those partridges had moved camp.
kisiwâsiw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk was angry.
"nika-nitonawâwak pihêwak, niya askiy kâ-kî-osîhtâyân!" ||| “I shall look for the partridges, I who created the world!”
êkwa sipwêhtêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Then Wisahketchahk went away from there.
kêtahtawê ê-pimohtêt, ê-nîpihk, kêkway?- pihêsisa wâpamêw wacistwanihk. ||| hen, at one time, as he was walking along, in summer, what was that? -- some young partridges he saw in a nest.
"tânisi êsiyîhkâsoyêk, pihêsisitik?" ||| “What is your name, young partridges?”

sîpîsisihk wîsahkêcâhkwa askamawêwak; âyîtawakâm sîpîsisihk apiwak. ||| By a brook they lay in wait for Wisahketchahk; on both banks of the little stream they sat.

aciyaw wâpahtam ôma sîpîsis. ||| Soon he saw the brook.
"nêwâw nika-pê-wâpahtên ôma." "êkota nika-pâsic-ôhpîn." ||| Four times I shall run at this brook. Then I shall jump across.”
êkwa kî-sipwêhtêw; asêhtêw; êkwa wayacîwîw, sîpîsisihk ê-ispahtât. ||| Then he walked off; he walked back; he took a running start, heading for the brook.
tâpiskôc ê-wî-pâsic-ôhpît, pôyôw. ||| At the very point of jumping across, he halted.
âsay mîna wayacîwîw. ||| Again he took a running start.
"êkwa nika-pâsic-ôhpîn," itwêw. ||| “Now I shall jump across,” he said.
êkwa môskîstam êkwa. ||| So now he made for it.
mwêhci ê-ohpît, misahci ohpîwak pihêwak. ||| ust as he jumped, up went the partridges.

kêtahtawê akwâyâhokôw. ||| In time the water carried him to the bank.
pa-pimisin sisonê nipîhk. ||| He lay there by the water's edge.
êkwa waniskâw; ocahpihcisa nitonawêw. ||| hen he got up; he looked for his tobacco-pouch.

kêtahtawê ê-itâpit, nipîhk akohciniyiwa. ||| Then once, as he looked that way, it lay there in the water.

kisiwâsiw, ocahpihcisa ê-wanihât. ||| He was angry at having lost his tobacco-pouch.
kêtahtawê itâpiw; ispimihk wâpamêw ê-akociniyit. ||| Then at one time he looked that way; he saw it hanging up aloft.
"cê, macastimwak!" itêw, "tâpwê nikisiwâhikwak." ||| “Bah, the dirty dogs!” he said of them; “They surely have angered me!”
sipwêhtêw êkota ohci. ||| He went away from there.
êkwa wâpamêw misahkamik sîsîpa. ||| Then he saw a great many ducks.
wî-tapasîwak sîsîpak. ||| The ducks started to flee.
"cêskwa: nisîmitik," itêw. ||| “Wait a bit, Little Brothers!” he called to them.
"namôya, nistêsê." "osâm kiwî-nipahinân." ||| “No, Big Brother. You mean to kill us.”
nayahcikêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk carried something on his back.
kêtahtawê sâkahikan; mitoni misikamâw. ||| There was a lake; it was a very big lake.
