"âyiman, nisîmitik." ||| “It is hard, Little Brothers.”
êkwa mâwacihêw nanâtohk sîsîpa niska. ||| He assembled all kinds of ducks and geese.
sôskwât êkwa pîhtokêw, êkwa sîsîpak misahkamik, ê-wî-nîmihitocik. ||| Then at once he entered, and all the ducks were to dance.
"ka-pasakwâpinâwâw ka-nîmihitoyêk." ||| “You will close your eyes for this dance of yours.”
"êha," itwêwak sîsîpak. ||| “Yes”, said the ducks.
nîmihitôwak êkwa sîsîpak; mâka pasakwâpiwak. ||| Then the ducks danced; but they had their eyes closed.

kêkâc ê-mêscihât, pêyak awa apisîsisiw napatê piko pasakwâpiw. ||| When he had nearly finished all of them, one little fellow held only one eye shut.

nîso piko isi-tapasîwak; pimâtisiwak nîso piko. ||| Only two of them thus escaped; only two got away with their lives.

"namôya kêkway nipêtân nîmihitôwin." "mitoni nikî-nôhtêhkatân." "tâpwê môhcôwiwak sîsîpak." "mistahi nika-mîcison êkwa." ||| I was very hungry. Truly, foolish are the ducks. Now I shall have plenty to eat.”
"pita nika-pimohtân." "mwêstas nika-mîcison." ||| “First I shall take a walk. Afterwards I shall eat.”
kêtahtawê ê-pimohtêt, wâpamêw mahkêsîsa. ||| As he was walking, he saw a fox.
"ê, cêskwa, nisîm," itêw; "kikakwê-nakatonânaw." "awiyak nakasiwêci, sîsîpa kahkiyaw ta-môwêw," itêw. ||| “Hey, stop a bit, Little Brother!” he said to him; “We shall have a race. Whichever wins will eat all the ducks,” he said to him.
niwîsakêyihtên niskât; namôya, wîsahkêcâhk." ||| I have a sore leg; no, Wisahketchahk.”
"asiniyak niskâtihk nika-tahkopitâwak." "êkosi ka-nakacipahin." ||| “I shall tie some stones to my leg. That way you will outrun me.”
"êha," itwêw mahkêsîs. ||| “Very well,” said the fox.
êkwa tahkopitêw asiniya oskâtihk wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Then Wisahketchahk tied some stones to his leg.
êkwa sipwêhtêwak mitoni. ||| Then they started off at a great rate.
namôya kî-kisiskâhtêw wîsahkêcâhk; osâm kosikwatiwak asiniyak. ||| Wisahketchahk could not go fast; the stones were too heavy.
têtipêwêwak ispatinâw. ||| They ran round a hill.

mahkêsîsa kisiwâhik. ||| He was angry at the fox.
"niya askiy kâ-kî-osîhtâyân!" "ka-miskâtin!" ||| “It is I created the earth! I will find you!”
sipwêhtêw; nitonawêw mahkêsîsa. ||| He went from there; he looked for the fox.
kêtahtawê ê-pa-pimohtêt miskawêw, ê-nipâyit timaskâhk. ||| hen at one time, as he walked about, he found him sleeping in the tall grass.
"tânisi kê-tôtawak?" "pakamahwaki nika-nisiwanâcihâw askêkinos." "nika-owahpihtisin." "nitawâc nika-pasisamawâw." ||| “What shall I do to him? If I club him, I shall spoil the hide. I shall have it for a tobacco-pouch. I had better stifle him by building a fire round him.”

êkwa mahkêsîs kisiwâk ê-pê-kwâhkotêyik pasikosipahtâw. ||| When the blaze came close, the fox jumped to his feet.
êkwa miywêyihtam, ê-pasikosipahtâyit. ||| He was glad when the other jumped to his feet.

êkwa pâhpiw, "mistahi nipahîhkaswâw," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He laughed, thinking, “I am certainly killing him with this fire!”
êkwa ê-âstawîyik, nama kêkway mahkêsîs. ||| But when the fire subsided, there was no fox.
"cêê, wînikonêwi-mahkay!" "tânitê kî-itâmoyan?" "ôhcitaw ka-miskâtin," itêw. ||| “Miserable foul-breathed fool! Where could you escape? All the more surely will I find you!” he said of him.
kêtahtawê ê-pa-pimohtêt, pêhtam ê-matwê-pâh-pâhpihk. ||| Then once, as he walked along, he heard loud and repeated laughter.

êkwa mistikw ê-ocipitât, kâwi ôh-pahkihtiniyiwa oskîsikwa. ||| Then, when he pulled at the bush, his eyes fell from it, back into place.

âsay mîna wîsakêyihtam. ||| Again he was in pain.
âsay mîna sakâhk itohtêw. ||| Again he stepped into the brush.

êkwa âta ê-ocipitahk, nama kêkway. ||| But then, though he tugged at the bush, they were not there.
mahkêsîs awa kwâsihtâw oskîsikoyiwa wîsahkêcâhkwa. ||| That fox had stolen Wisahketchahk's eyes.
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk âh-ocipitêw kapê-kîsik. ||| Then Wisahketchahk kept tugging at the tree all day.

pônihêw êkwa mahkêsîs awa. ||| Then the fox left him alone.
kêtahtawê tâwikisin. ||| Then at one time he bumped into something.

"namôya êkotôwa kâ-nitawêyimak." ||| “That is not the kind I want.”
"kêkway ê-itikawiyan?" ||| “What are you called?”
"êkotôwa kâ-nitawêyimak." ||| “That is the kind I want.”

nêtohtahki, wâhyaw kâ-matwê-nipâkwêsimôwiht. ||| Whenever he listened, far off was the noise of the Sun-Dance.

"nisîmitik, kiyâm kitimâkihtawik." ||| “Little Brothers, please grant me what I beg.”

kîtahtawê kwêskîmow; kâwi ayîsiyinîwiw; pasikôw; misiwê ostikwân ôma sipwêhtatâw. ||| Suddenly he changed his form; he turned back into human shape; he arose; he carried off the whole head.
kikamoyiw wâwâskêsiwistikwân ostikwânihk. ||| The deer's-head was fastened over his head.

nama kêkway isi-wâpiw. ||| He could not see at all, the way he was fixed.

pahkopêw, ê-wî-pakamahwât wâwâskêsiwa. ||| She went into the water to club the deer.

wîsahkêcâhk tapasîw. ||| Wisahketchahk ran away.
pônâmôw; êkota ohci êkwa sipwêhtêw. ||| He stopped in his flight; then he again made off from that place.
pimohtêw, kâ-wâpamât niska. ||| As he walked along, he saw some geese.
wî-tapasîwak niskak. ||| The geese tried to get away.
"cêskwa, nisîmitik!" ||| “Wait a bit, Little Brothers!”
"nisîmitik, nîsta nika-niskiwin," itêw. ||| “Little Brothers, I too shall be a goose,” he said to them.
"êkwa, nistêsê, ayîsiyiniwak wâpamatwâwi, ohpimê ka-pimihân," itêw. ||| “And now, Big Brother, whenever you see people, off to one side you will fly,” one said to him.
êkwa mîcisôwak êkota sâkahikanihk. ||| Then they ate, there in the lake.
kêtahtawê ohpahôwak. ||| Presently they flew up.
nîkâniw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk was in the lead.

nôhtêhkatêw; nama kêkway mîciw. ||| He was hungry; he had nothing to eat.
êkwa nicawâc wî-kakwê-minahôw. ||| He decided to try and kill some game.
wâpamêw mostoswa nêwo; nama nânitaw isi kî-nipahêw. ||| He saw four buffalos; he had no way of killing them.
kêtahtawê oyahpitam mistikwa, ayîsiyiniwa ê-osîhât, tâpiskôc ê-mâsihitoyit; êkwa mostoswa itohtêw. ||| Soon he tied up some sticks, arranging them like men wrestling; then he went to where the buffalo were.
"cêskwa, nisîm," itêw, "nêki ayisiyiniwak kâ-mâsihitocik, 'takwahinâwak wîhcêkisiwak,' ê-itwêt pêyak ana, êkwa kotak ana, "namôya," ê-itwêt, "nawac iyâpêsisak," ê-itwêt," "êwako ohci kâ-nôtinitocik;" "mâka ê-wî-miyâmitakok." ||| “Wait, Little Brothers!” he called to them; Those men are wrestling over there, because one of them said, 'Bulls stink,' and the other said, 'No. young steers are worse,' that is the reason they are fighting; but I have come to smell you.”
êkwa otinam kîmôc omôhkomân. ||| Then secretly he took his knife.
êkwa sîpâ ê-isiniskêyit, ê-wî-miyâmât takwahinâwa, tahkamêw; nipahêw. ||| Then when he hold his arm out under the bull, to smell him, he stabbed him; he killed him.

"konita ê-osîhtâyân, nama awiyak ayîsiyiniw!" ||| “When I just made the thing, and there isn't any man there!”
"mistahi nika-mîcison êkwa." ||| “Now I shall eat a plenty.”
êkwa wiya pahkwêkiswêw. ||| Then he skinned them.
osîhtâw êkwa wiyâsa. ||| And he prepared the meat.
êkwa ê-kî-kîsihtât, pa-pimisin. ||| When he had got it ready, he lay there.

pê-takopahtâw êkota mahîhkanis. ||| A young wolf came running up.
"awas," itêw; "niwiyâsima mâka mîna ka-wîhkohkân," itêw. ||| “Get out,” he said to him; “You'll be inviting people, as usual, to dine on my meat,” he said to him.
ostikwân piko waskawinam. ||| All he could do was turn his head.

"nika-minahon êkwa." ||| “Now I shall kill game.”

"tâni êkosi kôh-wî-itwêyin?" "kikî-osahamawin ê-wî-minahoyân." ||| “Why are you bound to cry out like that? You drove off my game when I was going to bag it.”

êkwa otinam câpihcikanis; pîkohtitâw. ||| Then he took his spear; when he landed it, it broke.

"mâskôc kotak wâpamaki, nika-nipahik," itêyihtam êkwa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “Perhaps if I see another one, it will kill me,” thought Wisahketchahk.

êkwa wîsahkêcâhk tapasîw. ||| Then Wisahketchahk ran away.

êkwa asamik; mîcisôwak. ||| Then they gave him food; they ate.
"hâw, nôtokêsiw, wêpâhtakahikê," itwêyiwa osîma; "nistês onôhtêhkatâh." "nitomâtânik mostoswak," itwêyiwa. ||| “Come, Old Woman, sweep out the tent,” said Wisahketchahk's younger brother; “My big brother has been going hungry, you know. Let us call some buffalo,” said he.
tâpwê wêpâhtakahikêw. ||| Accordingly, she swept.
êkwa oyaskinahêw, ê-pîhtwâcik. ||| Then he filled the pipe, and they smoked.
ê-kîsi-pîhtwâcik, êkwa otinêyiwa sîsîkwana. ||| When they had smoked, he took a rattle.
"hâ, nistêsê, kîsta kika-nikamon." ||| “Now, Big Brother, you too are to sing.”
êkwa nikamoyiwa, sîsîkwana ê-âpacihâyit. ||| Then the other sang, using the rattle.
â, kahkiyaw nikamôwak, piyisk kinwês; piyisk pôyowak; kawisimôwak; nipâwak. ||| They all sang, for a long time; at last they ceased; they went to bed; they slept.
ê-wâpahk kîkisêpâ, ê-wayawît awa kisêyiniw, kisiwâk wâpamêw mostoswa. ||| In the morning early, when the old man went outside, he saw the buffalo close by.
ômisi itwêw: "wâ, nistêsê, kisiwâk ayâwak mostoswak!" itwêyiwa, ê-otinâyit sîsîkwana. ||| He said, “Hullo, Brother, the buffalo are close by!” and as he spoke, he took up his rattle.
"â, nisîm, nîsta êtokê nika-itohtân," itêw. ||| “Oh, Brother, don't you suppose I could go there, too?” he asked him.
"namôya," itik, ê-wayawiyit, ê-itohtêyit pîhtokahân. ||| “No,” the other told him, and went out of the tent, to the buffalo-close.
êkotê ê-itohtêyit, âkawâyihk ohci kitâpamêw, kâ-wâpamât iskwâhtêmihk ê-nahapiyit ôhi osîma, ê-nikamoyit. ||| When the other went there, he watched him from behind something, and there he saw his little brother seat himself and sing.
mayaw ê-pêhtahkik ôki mostoswak, sêmâk pê-sipwêhtêwak, ôhi kisêyiniwa ê-môskîstawâyit. ||| As soon as those buffalo heard it, at once they started off in that direction, going straight for the old man.
awa kisêyiniw ômisi itwêw: "îtawiyaw pimohtê!" itêw ôhi mostoswa. ||| Then the old man spoke as follows: “Walk along at both sides!” he said to the buffalo.
tâpwê âyîtaw pimohtêyiwa, ê-pîhtokêyit pîhtokahânihk. ||| And really, they walked past on either side of him, and entered the buffalo-pound.
êkosi êkwa acicisiniyiwa ôhi kisêyiniwa, ê-kitâpamât awa wîsahkêcâhk osîma, ê-pwêkitoyit. ||| Thereupon that old man got down on all fours with his head to the ground, and, Wisahketchahk all the while watching his younger brother, broke wind.
akâwâtamawêw, ê-wâpamât ê-tôtamiyit osîma. ||| He envied his younger brother for what he saw him do.
êkosi kîwêw awa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| So the Wisahketchahk went back to the tipi.
ê-apit, kâ-pê-pîhtokêyit osîma, "hâ, nistêsê, mistahi êkwa ka-mîcisonânaw; mihcêt ninipahâwak mostoswak," ê-itikot. ||| As he sat there, his brother cam in, and, “Ho, Big Brother, now we shall eat a plenty; I have killed many buffalo,” he told him.
"hay hay hay!" itwêw wîsahkêcâhk; "hah, kimôhkomân otina; nitawi-wiyanihtâkêtân," ê-itikot. ||| “Splendid!” said Wisahketchahk; and the other said to him, “Come, take your knife; let us go do the butchering.”
tâpwê kahkiyaw itohtêwak, ôki mîna iskwêwak. ||| So they all went there, the women too.
ê-takohtêt, mihcêt mostoswa wâpamêw, ê-pimisiniyit. ||| When he got there, he saw many buffalo lying there.
wa-wiyanihtâkêwak; kahkiyaw wiyanihêwak; êkwa âwatâwak wiyâsa. ||| They cleaned one after the other; they cut them all up; then they carried off the meat.
âpihtaw miyik wiyâsa; êkwa mistahi ayâw mîciwin, êkwa owîkimâkana ê-osîhtâyit kâhkêwakwa. ||| He gave him half the meat; so now he had plenty of food, and his wife set about making dried meat.
mâka mîna akâwâtamawêw ôma kâ-isi-nipahâyit. ||| But still he envied the other his way of killing them.
nôhtê-sipwêhtêw; êkwa oyaskinahêw otôspwâkana, ê-pasikôt, ê-miyât ôhi osîma. ||| He wanted to go away; so he filled his pipe and rose to his feet, and gave it to his little brother.
mâtôw wîsahkêcâhk; ômisi itwêw: "nisîm, kitimâkêyimin;" "kitakâwâtamâtin kitisi-minahôwin," itwêw wîsahkêcâhk, ê-mâtot. ||| Wisahketchahk wept; he spoke as follows: “Little Brother, take pity on me; I long for you power of killing game in this way,” said Wisahketchahk, weeping.
piyisk, "ahaq," itik. ||| At last the other said, “Yes,” to him.
êkosi êkwa ê-nahapit, ômisi itik: "hâw, nistêsê, iyikohk wî-sipwêhtêyini;" "misawâc mêkwâc mistahi kitayânânaw wiyâs," ê-itikot. ||| When accordingly he had sat down, the other said to him, “Now, Big Brother, wait until you are ready to leave; for the present we have in any case a great deal of meat,” the other told him.
"hâw, nisîm, ôtê pimohtêwak nitawâsimisak," itêw; "anohc kâ-kîsikâk, 'êkotê kika-wâpamitin,' nikî-itikwak." "êkosi anohc ka-sipwêhtêyân," itêw. ||| “Well, Little Brother, over yonder my children are walking along,” he told him; “With reference to this very day, 'In that place I shall see you,' I told them. So now is when I must leave,” he told him.
"nâh," itik owîkimâkana, "mistahi ôma wiyâs kitayânânaw; mâka kitawâsimisinawak êkota ka-pêhikonawak." ||| “Nonsense,” his wife said to him, “Here we have all this meat; after all, our children will wait for us over there.”
"misawâc niwî-miyik ominahôwin nisîm." "wâpamâyahkwâwi kitawâsimisinawak, êkotê mihcêt nika-nipahâwak mostoswak," itwêw. ||| “What matter, since my brother is going to give me his hunting-power? When we see our children, I shall kill plenty of buffalo over there,” said he.
"ahaq," itik owîkimâkana. ||| “Very well,” his wife answered him.
êkosi ômisi itik osîma: "hâw, nistêsê, kâ-wî-miyitân nitisi-minahôwin!" ||| Then his younger brother spoke to him as follows: “Now then, Big Brother, I shall give you my power of killing game in this way!”
êkwa wayawîwak, ohpimê ê-itohtêcik. ||| Then they left the tipi and walked off to one side.
"hâ, nistêsê, ôta nahapi!" ||| “There, Brother, sid down here!”
nahapiw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk sat down.
êkosi êkwa isisin; nêtê ôtê osîma êkosi isi acicisiniyiwa, ê-kitâpamikot. ||| So he crouched down that way; over at this end his brother crouched in the same way, and kept looking at him.
"nistêsê, kitâsiyân wîhkwatin!" ||| “Big Brother, pull aside your breech-clout!”
"ômisi ispita kâskitoya!" ||| “Pull your buttocks like this!”
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk êkosi ispitam sôhki; sôhki êkosi ê-tôtahk, pwêkitoyiwa. ||| Then Wisahketchahk stretched them hard; when he had done it properly, the other broke wind.
sêmâk wiya wîsahkêcâhk kwâskwêkocin. ||| At once Wisahketchahk flew up into the air.
wâhyaw pahkisin; wîsakisin. ||| Far off he fell; he had a bad fall.
pasikôw, ê-itohtêt, "hâw, pêyakwâw, nistêsê!" ê-itikot. ||| He got up and walked back, and, “Fall, once more!” said the other to him.
âsay mîna acicisin, âsay mîna ê-pwêkicitikot. ||| Again he crouched down, and again the other broke wind at him.
êkwa êkota kinwês nipahisin. ||| Then for a long time he lay there as though dead.
êkosi êkwa pasikôw, ê-ati-sipwêhtêt. ||| Then at last he rose to his feet, and went to leave.
"hâ, êkwa, nôtokêsiw, sipwêhtêtân!" ||| “There, come, Old Woman, let us go.”
wâhyaw ê-ihtâcik, "hâw, nôtokêsiw, matwân cî tâpwê ê-miyit kaskitêw?" itwêw; "mahci ôma sakâw nika-kotahâskwâtên." ||| When they were far from there, “Well, Old Woman, can it be that he really has given me the power?” said he; “Suppose I take a trial shot at this grove of trees.”
"êkâ wiya!" itik owîkimâkana; "ka-wiyakihtân." "kika-ôh-mîcisohtânaw!" ||| “Don't!” his wife said to him; “You will waste it. Didn't you say we were to get our food from it?”
"ô, mâskôc nikakwê-cîsimik." "kiyâm nika-kotahâskwân." ||| “Well, perhaps he was trying to fool me. Do let me make a trial shot.
âhci piko kotahâskwâtam ôma sakâw. ||| Undeterred, he made a trial shot with that grove of trees as his target.
kahkiyaw mistikwa kawiwêpaham. ||| He knocked over all the trees.
"kâh, tâpwê êsa ani nimiyik ominahôwin nisîm!" ||| “What do you think of that! So my little brother did really give me his way of killing game!”
êkosi mîna âhci piko sipwêhtêw. ||| Then he set out again, as before.
namôya wâhyaw ê-ihtât, kâ-wâpamât ê-misikitiyit asiniya. ||| He had not gone far, when he saw a big stone.
"êhâ, nôtokêsiw, mahci nika-kotahâskwân," ê-itwêt, "êkâ wiya!" itik owîkimâkana. ||| “Hey, Old Woman, suppose I do some target-shooting,” he said, and “Do not!” his wife told him.
âhci piko pwêkicitêw asiniya. ||| Over he protest he broke wind at the stone.
iyawis kwâskwêwêpahwêw; pîkopayiyiwa asiniya. ||| He knocked it bodily into the air; the stone flew to pieces.
"nhâ, nôtokêsiw, kapêsitân;" "ninôhtêhkatân," itêw. ||| “Well, Old Woman, let us pitch camp; I am hungry,” he said to her.
"kîkwayi tê-mîciyahk?" itik. ||| “What are we to eat?” she asked him.
"ka-osîhtânânaw pîhtokahân; kika-nitomânawak mostoswak," itêw. ||| “Let us build a buffalo-pound; we shall call some buffalo,” he told her.
ê-kîsi-mânokêcik, êkwa ta-osîhtâwak pîhtokahân, êkwa ê-tipiskâyik, ê-nikamocik, ê-nitomâcik mostoswa. ||| When they had set up their tipi, they went about building the pound, and them, after dark, they sang to call the buffalo.
ê-wâpahk kîkisêpâ, kâ-wâpamât mostoswa. ||| Early in the morning he saw the buffalo.
êkwa sipwêhtêw, iskwâhtêmihk ê-nahapit awa wîsahkêcâhk, êkwa ê-nikamot, "îtawiyaw pimohtêk!" ê-isi-nikamot, mayaw ê-pêhtâkot mostoswa, pê-sipwêpayiyiwa. ||| Then he set out, and sat down in the entrance-way, this Wisahketchahk, and began to sing, “Walk along at either side!” When he sang thus, as soon as the buffalo heard him, they started running toward him.
kisiwâk ê-ayâyit, "tâwâskikan!" ê-itwêt, tâwikipayihik mostoswa. ||| When they were near, he said, “Square in the chest!” and the buffalo ran right into him.
êkwa kitâpamik owîkimâkana. ||| Then his wife saw him.
ê-kitâpamikot owîkimâkana, ê-ispahtâyit, pîkonamiyiwa ôma opîhtokahân. ||| When she saw him, she ran there, and broke down his enclosure.
kahkiyaw wayawiyiwa, ê-tapasîyit. ||| All the buffalo ran out.
êkoyikohk êkwa waniskâw, ê-âpisisihk. ||| Only then he got up, having returned to his senses.
êkwa acicipayihôw, ê-pwêkitot. ||| Then he threw himself down on all fours and broke wind.
nama kêkway nipahêw; ayisk kî-mêstinam kâ-kotahâskwêt. ||| He killed nothing; for he had wasted it in target-shooting.
"atimo-kisêyiniw!" itik owîkimâkana, êkâ kêkway ê-nipahtât, ê-kîhkâmikot. ||| “Dog of an old man!” his wife said to him, when he killed nothing, and she began to scold him.
"hâ, nôtokêsiw, kiyâm kiya kîwêpahtâ;" "nisîm ispahtâ;" "nitawi-nitotamaw anima kâ-kî-isi-miyit kita-ôh-mîcisoyahk otisi-minahôwin." ||| “Well, Old Woman, please, do you run back; run to my little brother's; go ask him for some of that game-killing power that he gave me, so that we may use it to get food.”
êkwa tâpwê kîwêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| So the old woman went back.
nêtê ê-takohtêt, "hâw, nîtim, mistahi ê-ma-mâyinikêt kistês, ê-mêstinahk kâ-kî-miyat kita-ôh-minahot, ê-kâ-kotahâskwêt." "êkwa mîna kinwêsk nipahik mostoswa, 'tâwâskikan!' ê-itwêt, "ê-wanitonâmoyân," ê-itwêt." "'piko ôma anohc itohtê; nitawi-nitotamaw nisîm otisi-minahôwin,' ê-isit, kâ-pê-sipwêhtêyân." ||| When she arrived over yonder, “Well, Brother-in-Law, I have come because your brother, who always makes a bad mess of things, has used up in target-shooting that which you gave him for killing game. And, besides, the buffalo knocked him silly for a long time, because he said, ‘Square in the chest!’ and then he said, ‘It was a slip of the tongue.’ ‘Just you now go there; go ask my brother for some of his way of killing game,’ he told me, and that is why I have come here.”
"ahaq, nîtim, ka-miyitin nîswâw kita-ôh-minahoyan," itêw; "â, âstam!" ||| “Very well, Sister-in-Law, I will give you wherewith twice to kill game,” he told her; “Now, come here!”
"nâ, nîtim, ôta acicisini!" ||| “So then, Sister-in-Law, get down on all fours here!”
"ôhi ômisi ispita kâskitoya!" ||| “Stretch out your buttocks like this!”
tâpwê êkosi ê-tôtahk, ê-pwêkicitikot, wâhyaw pahkisin. ||| And really, when she did that way, and he broke wind at her, far off she fell to the ground.
kîhtwâm mîna êkosi ê-tôtâkot, ê-pwêkicitikot, kinwês kinwêsk nipahisin awa nôtokêsiw. ||| When he did it to here a second time and broke wind at her, for a long, long time the old woman lay senseless.
iyikohk ê-âpisisihk, kîwêw. ||| When she came back to life, she went back.
ê-takohtêyit, awa wîsahkêcâhk, "niwîkimâkan, kimiyik cî?" ||| When she arrived, Wisahketchahk, “Wife, did he give you any?”
"atimo-kisêyiniw, ê-âyimaniyik êcika awa!" itik. ||| “Dog of an old man, and so it is a difficult thing, as it turns out!” she answered him.
êkwa osîhtâwak ôma kâ-kî-pîkonamiyit pîhtokahân. ||| Then they build up the buffalo-pound which she had pulled down.
ê-kîsihtâcik, êkwa ê-tipiskâyik, êkosi kâ-nikamocik, ê-nitomâcik mostoswa. ||| When they had got it in shape, and night came, they sang to call the buffalo.
tâpwê ê-nipâcik, ê-wâpahk, kîkisêpâ, kâ-wâpamât mostoswa. ||| And really, when they had slept, early the next morning, there he saw the buffalo.
êkwa itohtêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| Then the old woman went over there.
"îtawiyaw pimohtê!" itwêw. ||| “Walk along at either side!” were her words.
êkwa acicisin ôwa nôtokêsiw, ê-pwêkitot. ||| Then the old woman got down on all fours and broke wind.
kahkiyaw nipahêw mostoswa. ||| She killed all the buffalo.
mistahi miywêyihtam wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk was very glad.
êkwa ê-awatâcik wiyâs, "hâw, nôtokêsiw, pakâhtâkohkê." "kî-mîcisoyahko, kâhkêwakwa ka-osîhtânânaw," itêw owîkimâkana. ||| Then, when they carried in the meat, “Well, Old Woman, boil it in the kettle. When we have eaten, we shall prepare jerked meat,” he told his wife.
"êha," itwêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| “Yes,” said the old woman.
tâpwê ê-kî-mîcisocik, êkwa osîhtâwak kâhkêwakwa. ||| And so, when they had eaten, they made jerked meat.
akâwâtamawêw ôma kâ-nipahâyit mostoswa owîkimâkana. ||| He envied his wife the way she had killed the buffalo.
êkwa isîhtâw kâhkêwakwa awa wîsahkêcâhk, ê-ati-akotât mistikohk. ||| And so Wisahketchahk prepared dried meat, hanging it on a tree.
piyisk ê-tipiskâyik, "hahâw, êkâya nipâ, nôtokêsiw; kakwê-kîsihtâ kiwiyâsima," itêw. ||| When at last it grew dark, “Now, Old Woman, do not go to sleep; try to finish preparing your meats,” he told her.
tâpwê kapê-tipisk pânisâwêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| And so that old woman spent the whole night curing meat.
piyisk nôhtêhkwasiw. ||| At last she was sleepy.
"êkâya nipâ, niwîkimâkan!" itêw. ||| “Don't go to sleep, Wife!” he told her.
piyisk nipâw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| Finally the old woman fell asleep.
"waniskâ, niwîkimâkan! ||| Even when he said to her “Get up, Wife!
kipânisâwâh!" iyâta-itâci, namôya pêkopayiyiwa; nipâyiwa. ||| Don't forget your meat-curing!” she did not wake up; she was asleep.
"nika-kimotamawâw," itêyihtam, ôma kâ-ôh-nipahâyit mostoswa. ||| “I will steal it from her,” he thought, meaning that with which she had killed the buffalo.
piyisk oskotâkâsiyiw owîkimâkana ohpinamwêw, ita kâ-ôh-pwêkitoyit êkota ê-itâpit. ||| Finally he lifted up his wife's petticoat, and looked at whence she broke wind.
kâ-wâpahtahk ôma kâ-ôh-pwêkitoyit, êkwa miscikos otinam, ê-wî-otâskwahamawât, ê-wî-kimotamawât. ||| When he had caught sight of that from which she broke wind, he took a little stick, meaning to take it from her by means of the stick and to steal it from her.
mayaw ê-waskawiwêpahahk, kâ-pêkopayiyit, ê-pwêkitoyit. ||| Just as he began to twitch the stick, she woke up and broke wind.
mêtoni wâhyaw itakocin awa wîsahkêcâhk, ê-pistahokot owîkimâkana. ||| Off and away, to a great distance, Wisahketchahk went flying, when his wife thus accidentally shot him.
itê ê-pahkisihk, kinwês nipahisin. ||| There he fell to the ground, for a long time he lay as if dead.
"atimo-kisêyiniw kâ-môhcôwit, kâ-wiyakihtât!" itwêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| “Dog of an old man, crazy fool, to waste it like that!” cried the old woman.
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk ômisi itwêw: "'ê-ati-pasikôt kiwîkimâkan, kotahâskwâtâhkan,' ê-kî-itisk cî nisîm?" ||| Then Wisahketchahk said, “‘When your husband is in the act of getting up, use him as a target for your shots,’ is that what my brother told you to do?”
"namôya; ayisk kimôhcôwin," itik owîkimâkana. ||| “No, you are crazy, that is all,” his wife answered him.
aya êsa ôhi sikâkwa ôhi kâ-mâh-miyikocik ta-minahocik. ||| It appears that he was the Skunk, he who gave them the power of killing game.
êkosi êkwa êkoyikohk êwako âtayôhkêwin. ||| And so this is the end of this sacred story.
kayâs kîtahtawê-- êkwa nitâtayôhkân-- kîtahtawê yâhki pêyak nâpêw pêyakokamikisiw, wîwa êkwa nîso otawâsimisa. ||| Once upon a time, long ago -- I am now telling a sacred story -- once upon a time, of old, a certain man dwelt in a lone lodge with his wife and his two children.
kîtahtawê mâna sêpwêhtêci, owîkimâkana wawêsiyiwa. ||| Then presently, whenever he went away, his wife put on her finery.
namôya kiskêyihtam tânêhki ohci ê-wawêsiyit owîkimâkana. ||| He did not know why his wife put on her finery.
kîtahtawê konita sipwêhtêhkâsôw, ê-mâcît; êkwa kâsôw, "mahti kê-tôtahk," ê-itêyimât. pôti êkwa kâ-wâpamât mistikwa ê-pa-pakamahwâyit, êkwa ka-pê-wayawiyit kinêpikwa, kâ-wâpamât owîkimâkana ê-owîcimosiyit, sêmâk mistahi kisiwâsiw. ||| So then at one time he merely pretended to go away to hunt; he hid himself, thinking of her, “let me see what she will do.” And then he saw her beating a tree, and a serpent came out, and he saw that his wife had it for a lover, at once he was very angry.
mistikwa ê-pakamahwâyit wîwa, "ninâpêm, êkwa nitakohtân!" itwêyiwa. kisiwâsiw mistahi. ||| When his wife struck the tree, she said, “My husband, now I have come!” He was very angry.
ohtêyihtam; ayisk osâm nawac sâkihimâwa kinêpikwa. ||| He was jealous; for the serpent was loved more than he.
êwakoni ôhi kâ-wî-âtayôhkâtimak wîsâhkêcâhk okâwiya mîna ôhtâwiya. ||| Those of whom I mean to tell the sacred story were Wisahketchahk's mother and father.
êkwa awa nâpêw mistahi kisiwâsiw; nama kî-nipâw. ||| So now that man was very angry; he could not sleep.
ômisi itêw wîwa: "wâhyaw niwî-isi-mâcîn," itêw wîwa. ||| He said to his wife: “I am going far away to hunt.”
tâpwê mitoni wâhyaw isi mâcîw. ||| He really went very far away to hunt.
"tânêhki kâ-ôh-katikoniyan?" itik owîkimâkana. ||| “Why did you stay out over night?” his wife asked him.
"wâhyaw nikî-isi-mâcîn," itêw; "mâka kiya kika-nâtên wiyâsa," itêw wîwa. ||| “I have been far off to hunt,” he told her; “But you, are to fetch the meat,” he told his wife.
"êha," itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Very well,” said she.
mayaw ê-sipwêhtêyit wîwa, oskotâkayiyiw otinam, ê-postiskahk. ||| As soon as his wife had gone, he took her skirt and put it on.
itohtêw ôhi kinêpikwa ita kâ-asiwasoyit mistikohk. ||| He went to where that serpent was inside the tree.
"ninâpêm, nitakohtân!" itêw kinêpikwa. ||| “My husband, I have come!” he said to the serpent.
tâpwê pê-wayawiyiwa. ||| Really, it came out.
môhkomân ohci kîskikwêsâwâtêw; kîwêhtahêw ôhi kinêpikwa; mîcimâpoy osîhtâw. ||| He cut through its neck with a knife; he took the serpent home; he made a broth.
êkwa kâtêw otawâsimisa. ||| Then he hid his children.
cikêmâ maywês askiy ihtakohk, nanâtohk isi kîsi-kaskihtâwak. ||| One must keep in mind that before the earth existed they had many kinds of power.
kâh-kotâwinêw otawâsimisa askîhk. ||| He plunged his two children into the ground.
êkwa awa iskwêw mistahi kahkiyaw kêkway kaskihtâw, ahpô kahkiyaw kêkway êsa ê-pîkiskwâtahk, êkosi êsa ê-naskwêwasimikot. ||| And that woman, too, had great power for all things, and could talk even to every kind of thing and accordingly receive answer from it.
êkwa kahkiyaw kêkway mîna nâpêw pîhcâyihk ôta kâ-ihtakoniyik kitahamawêw êkâ kêkway kita-wîhtamâkoyit. ||| And then the man forbade every object that was in their dwelling to tell her anything.
takohtêyiwa êkwa wîwa. ||| Then his wife arrived.
asamêw kinêpikwa kâ-kî-mîcimâpôhkâkêt. ||| He gave her the serpent to eat which he had cooked into broth.
"hwâ, kêkway ôma," itwêw awa iskwêw, "mistahi kâ-wîhkasik?" ||| “Oh, what is this,” asked the woman, “which tastes so good?”
"kinâpêm kinêpik omihko, êkotôwahk ohci kâ-osîhtamâtân," itêw. ||| “The blood of your husband, the serpent; from it I have made this for you,” he told her.
kisiwâsiw awa iskwêw. ||| The woman was angry.
"nama cî tâpwê ahpô êkosi ê-tôtaman?" itêw êsa. ||| “It is not true, is it, that you have done even this?” she asked him.
itohtêw itê mâna kinêpikwa kâ-nitawi-wâpamât awa iskwêw. ||| So she went to where she was in the habit of visiting the serpent.
êkwa pakamahwêw mistikwa. ||| Then she struck the tree.
namwâc kinêpikwa pê-wayawiyiwa. ||| The serpent did not come out.
mistahi kisiwâsiw, konita ê-pê-mawîhkâtât. ||| She was very angry, as she came back, loudly bewailing it.
ê-pê-pîhtokêt, onâpêma kîskikwêtahok. ||| When she entered the dwelling, her husband cut off her head.
êkosi isi ohpiskâw awa nâpêw, ê-tapasît. ||| Then he rose into the air, to flee.
"nitawâc ôta kîsikohk nika-nitawi-otaskîn." "nika-acâhkosiwin!" itwêw, ê-ati-isi-ohpiskât. ||| “I shall needs go dwell there in the sky. Let me be a star!” he said, as he rose higher and higher.
êkwa awa iskwêw, kîtahtawê tôhkâpîmakan ôma pisisik mistikwânis. ||| And that woman, that severed head presently opened its eyes.
êkwa kîtahtawê kâ-pîkiskwêt ôma ostikwân. ||| Then presently that head spoke.
"â, nitôyâkan, tâniwêhkâk?" ||| “Come my dish, where are they?”
sôskwâc kahkiyaw kakwêcimêw otâpacihcikana. ||| Without delay, she asked all her utensils.
kahkiyaw mitoni kâh-kitotam, ê-kakwêcihtahk. ||| She spoke to every single one in turn, questioning it.
pôti asiniya kâ-wîhtamâkot askîhk ê-kî-kotâwinâyit onâpêma. ||| At last a stone told her that her husband had sunk them into the earth.
nêwo kêkway kî-miyêw otawâsimisa awa nâpêw, ispîhk ê-sipwêtisahwât, sîpiy kita-osîhtâyit, êkwa iskotêw, êkwa asinîwaciy, êkwa sakâw, okâminakasîwi-sakâw. ||| Four things that man had given his children, at the time when he started them off; that they might make a river, fire, a mountain of stone, and a forest; a forest of thorn trees.
êkwa têpwêw awa ostikwânis awa. ||| Then that head began to call.
"nitawâsimisitik, pêhik!" "kikitimahinâwâw kâ-nakasiyêk!" itwêw. ||| “My children wait for me! You are making me wretched by leaving me!” it cried.
tahki têpwêw awa iskwêw. ||| That woman called all the time.
êkwa awa nâpêsis itâmaskamik kâ-isi-tapasît, wâhyaw ohci wâpahtam ôma pisisik mistikwân ê-pîkiskwêmakaniyik, ê-nayômikot ostêsa. ||| And that little boy who was fleeing under ground, from afar he saw that severed speaking head, as he was being carried on his elder brother's back.
ômisi itêw: "nistêsê, nama kêkway kikâwiyinaw." "ostikwân piko kâ-pîkiskwêmakahk," itwêw. ||| He said to him, “Big brother, our mother is not there. It is only a talking head,” he said.
otinêw ôhtâwiya kâ-kî-miyikot, iskotêw nêhiyawak kâ-ôh-osîhtâcik; wêpinêw nâway isi. ||| He took that which his father had given him, that from which the Cree make fire; he threw it behind him.
"ôta iskotêw ta-wî-ayâw!" itwêw. ||| “Let there be fire!” he said.
tâpwê mistahi nakânikôw awa, wâhyaw ohci iskotêw ê-isi-kwâhkotêyik. ||| And really that being was entirely brought to a stop, when far and wide the fire blazed.
ayis pisisik ostikwân pimohtêmakaniyiw. ||| For it was but a severed head which went along.
êwako piko nêhiyaw kâ-isiyîhkâsot êsa mac-âyisa ê-kî-wîcihikot, pisisik ostikwân kâ-ôh-tihtipipayiyik. ||| Because he, at any rate, who is called Indian was helped by evil beings, was why that severed head could roll along.
piyisk miyâskam iskotêw. ||| Finally it passed by the fire.
êkwa nawaswâtêw sâsay mîna otawâsimisa. ||| Then it again pursued its children.
kahkiyaw saskitêyiwa wêstakaya. ||| All its hair was aflame.
êkwa mîna kîtahtawê ê-ay-itâpit ana kâ-nayômiht awâsis, "namôya kikâwiyinaw, nistêsê! ||| Then presently when again that child looked about, who was being borne by the other, “It is not our mother, big brother!
kiyâm sôhki tapasîtân!" itêw. ||| Let us flee with all our might!” he told him.
âsay mîna kîhtwâm otinam ôhtâwiya kâ-kî-miyikot okâminakasîwi-waciy kita-osîhtât. ||| Again he took that which his father had given him that he might make a hill of thornberry-trees.
tâpwê âcisin awa ostikwân kâ-tihtipipayiyit. ||| That Rolling Skull was really blocked.
êkwa atotêw misi-kinêpikwa, kita-kâh-kîskamâyit okâminakasiya, kita-tawinamâkot, sôskwâc kita-pimohtêt. ||| Then it bade a Great Serpent to bite through the thorn-trees and make a passage through for it, that it might go unchecked.
tâpwê kaskihôw sôskwâc ê-pimohtêt. ||| And so it managed to go on, unchecked.
êkwa âsay mîna wâhyaw ê-itâmocik, âsay mîna pêtisâpamêw ostikwân ê-pê-tihtipipayiyit awa awâsis kâ-nayômiht. ||| Then, when again they had fled a long ways, again that child who was being carried saw the Skull come rolling.
âsay mîna kâ-kî-miyikot ôhtâwiya asinîwaciy kita-osîhtât âsay mîna nâway isiwêpinam. ||| And again, he threw behind them that which he had been given by his father that he might make a mountain of rock.
mistahi misi-ispayiw asinîwaciy. ||| Vastly that rock crag extended.
nama kî-kaskihôw awa ostikwânis ta-pâsitohtêt. ||| That Skull-Being could not manage to go across it.
kwayask atotêw amiskwa ta-pîkwamâyit ôhi asiniya, ê-pîwâpiskôwiyiki wîpitiyiwa. ||| At once it employed a beaver with iron teeth to bite the rock into pieces.
êkwa kaskihôw sâsay mîna. ||| Then it was able to go on.
âsay mîna nawaswâtêw otawâsimisa. ||| Again it pursued its children.
âsay mîna pêtisâpamêw awa awâsis kâ-nayômikot ostêsa. ||| Again that child who was being borne by his elder brother saw it coming.
êkwa mîna sîpiy kita-ôh-osîhtât kâ-kî-miyikot ôhtâwiya ôtê nîkân pisci isiwêpinam. ||| Then that which his father had given him that he might make a river, he threw it, by mistake, on ahead.
ati-itwêw awa awâsis. ||| The child kept crying its cry.
mâtôwak êkwa, ê-kostahkik ta-nipahikocik ôma mistikwân ka-tihtipipayiyik, okâwiyiwâwa ostikwâniyiw. ||| Then they wept in terror that the Rolling Skull would kill them, their mother's skull.
êkwa ê-mâtocik, "êkâya mâtok! ||| Then as they wept, “Do not weep!
kika-pihkohitinâwâw!" itikwak misi-kinêpikwa. ||| I will take you to safety!” a Great Serpent said to them.
êkwa akâmihk ê-kî-takohtahikocik, kâwi âsowaham awa kâ-kî-âsowahohât ôhi awâsisa. ||| When he had brought them to the far shore, he crossed back, who had taken the children across.
ê-wâpamât êkotê awa mistikwân kâ-tihtipipayit, ômisi itwêw: "âsowahohin niya mîna!" itêw. ||| When the Rolling Skull saw him, it said, “Take me across, too!” it said to him.
"êkâya mâka papâsêyihta," itik. ||| “But do not be impatient” he told it.
pôsiw ospiskwaniyihk. ||| It rode on his back.
mwêhci tâwayihk nipîhk ê-ayâcik, "misi-kinêpik, wêsâ kipêsiskân!" itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| Just when they were in the middle of the stream, “Great Serpent, you are going all together too slowly!” said that woman.
"'namêw' kika-isiyîhkâson!" itik awa ostikwân awa kâ-tihtipipayit. ||| “‘Sturgeon’ will be your name!” he told that Rolling Head.
êkwa ôki nâpêsisak papâmâcihowak, mistahi ê-kwatakihtâcik. ||| Then those boys wandered about, suffering many hardships.
êwako awa otawâsisîwihtay wîsahkêcâhk. ||| That boy was Wisahketchahk in his childhood.
êkospîhk êkwa sipwêhtêwak, osîmisa ê-wîcêwât. ||| Then they departed from there, he with his little brother.
pâkahatôwânisa osîhtamawêw, ta-mêtawâkêyit. ||| He made a ball for him to play with.
kîtahtawê cîki sîpîhk ê-pa-pimohtêcik, êwako ostêsimâs, "âstam!" kâ-itikot kisêyiniwa otôsiyihk ê-pôsiyit. ||| Then at one time, as they were walking by the river, the elder boy was told, “Come here!” by an old man in a canoe.
ê-pôsit, êkosi isi isi-kwâsihik. ||| When he stepped into the canoe, this person carried him off.
êkwa awa kâ-apisîsisit awa nakatik. ||| They left the smaller boy behind.
ê-ati-isi-mâtot, "nistêsê, nitawâc niya nika-mahîhkaniwin!" itwêw awa nâpêsis osîmimâs. ||| Then as he began to weep, “Big brother, now I shall have to turn into a wolf!” cried that little boy, the younger one.
êkosi êwako piko kî-otinâw wîsahkêcâhk, êkwa êkotê wîkiyihk ê-takohtahikot ôhi kisêyiniwa. ||| Thus only Wisahketchahk was taken, and the old man brought him over yonder to his dwelling.
kwatapinik otôsiyihk; namôya ahpô wî-kîwêhtahik. ||| He put him under his canoe as he tipped it on the beach; he did not even care to take him home.
takohtêw wîkiwâhk awa kisêyiniw, nîso otânisa. ||| The old man went to his abode, to his two daughters.
"nitawâsimisitik, nipêsiwâw kita-isi-onâpêmiyêk," itwêw êsa; "nitawi-wâpamihk," itwêw. ||| “My children, I have brought someone for you to marry,” he said; “Go look at him,” he said.
wayawîw ê-omisimâwit, ê-nitawi-wâpamât. ||| The older girl went out of the tent and looked at him.
mistahi êcika awa ê-mâyâtisiyit. ||| Why he was very ugly!
"namôya ta-kî-onâpêmiyân awâsis!" itêw. ||| “I cannot marry a child!” she said of him.
"â, kêyiwêhk miyosiw." "mâskôc ahpô osâm mistahi ê-mâtot," itwêw êsa. ||| “Oh, he is handsome enough. Perhaps it is only because he has been weeping too much,” he said.
êkwa itohtêw osîmimâw. ||| Then the younger sister went there.
awa oskinîkiskwêw kîwêhtahêw anihi awâsisa, ê-kî-kâsîhkwênât. ||| This young woman brought the lad home, after washing his face.
pamihêw; tâpwê onâpêmiw êwako. ||| She took care of him; she really took him for her husband.
êkwa pakwâtêw awa omisimâw, wâwâc mâna ohcitaw ê-tôtahk awa awâsis, ê-mîsît otanâskâniyihk. ||| The elder sister disliked him, and all the more so as the child wantonly played tricks, [no translation]
ê-kî-nêwo-tipiskâyik mâka ômisi itêw: "mahti matotisânihkê; nika-osîhtân niyaw," itwêw. ||| On the fourth night, however, he said to them, “Do you build a lodge for the steam-bath; I shall make my body,” he said.
tâpwê matotisânihkêwân, ê-osîhtât wiyaw. ||| Accordingly a sweat lodge was built for him, and he made his body.
êkwa mistahi miyosiw ê-âhcihisot. ||| Then he was very handsome, when he had made himself over.
akâwâtêw êkwa awa kâ-kî-pakwâtât. ||| Then she who had disliked him conceived a passion for him.
âta kêtotâci, namwâc ahpô nôhtê-kitotik. ||| But even though she plied him with speech, he did not care to have her so much as speak to him.
êkwa awa kêsêyinîwit sîhkimik otânisa ôhi omisimâwa isi-kakwê-nipahât. ||| Then the old man was urged by that elder daughter of his to try and kill him.
êkwa tâpwê, "ahaq, nika-kakwê-nipahâw," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| And really, “Yes I shall try to kill him,” said the old man.
"tânitê êtokê nika-kî-ohtinên miscikosa ê-miywâsiki?" itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “I wonder where I can get good little arrow-sticks?” said the youth.
êkwa, "nika-itohtahâw ninahâhkisîm," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| Then, “I shall take my son-in-law to such a place,” said the old man.
êkwa tâpwê itohtahêw ê-ministikôwiyik. ||| And so he took him to an island.
ômisi itwêw awa kisêyiniw: "nipawâkan, êwako ana kitasamitin!" itwêw. ||| Thus spoke the old man: “My dream guardian, I feed you this man!” he said.
mayaw otati-sêskisihtay awa oskinîkiw, ka-pê-môskîstâkot wâkayôsa, itôwahk kâ-wâpiskisicik. ||| Hardly had the youth gone into the brush, when out came a bear at him, one of those who are white.
"'nika-nipahâw,' cî ôma ê-itêyihtaman?" itêw awa; "nama ka-kî-nipahin," itwêw; "ayisk nîsta kôpawâkanimitin," itwêw. ||| “‘I shall kill him,’ is that what you are thinking?” said he; “You cannot kill me,” he said; “For I, too, have you as my dream spirit,” he said.
tâpwê nipahêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth really slew it.
âsiskawêw ôhi kisêyiniwa; waskic nipîhk ati-pimohtêw. ||| He outdistanced the old man; he walked along the surface of the water.
ê-kîwêt awa kisêyiniw, kâ-wâpahtahk wâkayôs ostikwân ê-akotêyik otiskwâhtêmihk; mâka wiya kisêyiniw mawîhkâtêw opawâkana, ê-nipahimiht. ||| When the old man went home, there he saw the bear's head hanging over the doorway; the old man bewailed his dream guardian who had been slain.
âsay mîna kîtahtawê ê-ay-ayâcik, ômisi itwêw awa oskinîkiw: "tânitê êtokê nika-ohtinâwak mîkwanak ê-miyosicik, nîpisisa kita-ohci-osîhtâyân?" ||| Presently, as they dwelt there, the youth spoke thus: “I wonder where I can get pretty feathers to make my arrows?”
"ôtê ôma kâ-asinîwacîwik, êkotê mistahi miyosiwak mîkwanak." "êkotê nika-itohtahâw," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Over yonder amid the rocky cliffs, there the feathers are very fine. I shall take him there,” said the old man.
tâpwê sipwêhtahêw êkotê isi. ||| Really, he led him off to go there.
êkosi êkotê ê-takohtahât, piyêsiwa ê-owacistwaniyit. ||| And so he brought him there where the thunderers had their nests.
"hâw, nipawâkanitik, êwako ana kitasamitinâwâw!" itêw. ||| “Come, my dream guardians, I feed you this man!” he said to them.
âsay mîna kahkiyaw nipahêw ôhi piyêsiwa. ||| Again, he killed all those thunderers.
âsay mîna, "tânitê êtokê nika-kî-ohtinên nîpisiy ê-miywâsik, kita-osîhak?" ||| Once more, “I wonder where I could get a good osier to make my bow?”
êkosi sâsay mîna kisêyiniw, "nika-itohtahâw itê ê-miywâsiniyik nîpisiya." ||| Then again, the old man: “I shall take him where the willows are good.”
âsay mîna, "ê, nipawâkan, êwako kitasamitin!" itêw misi-kinêpikwa. ||| Again, “Come my dream Guardian, this one I feed to you!” he said to a great serpent.
âsay mîna awa oskinîkiw kâ-asamimiht misi-kinêpikwa nipahêw. ||| And again, the youth slew the Great Serpent to whom he was being fed.
ostikwâniyiw kîwêhtatâw. ||| He took home its head.
âsay mîna kisêyiniw nâway takohtêw. ||| Again the old man was the second to arrive.
mawîhkâtêw mîna opawâkana. ||| He grieved over this dream spirit, too.
"misi-kinêpik, nipawâkan!" itwêw. ||| “Great Serpent, my dream guardian!” he cried.
êkwa namôya kî-kiskêyihtam tânisi êkwa kita-kî-isi-kawatimât ta-kî-isi-nipahât, ahpô ta-kawatimât. ||| Then he did not know how he could freeze him to death, to kill him, but by freezing him.
êkwa ômisi itwêw: "mâcîtân, nitêhkwâ!" itêw. ||| So he said, “Let us hunt my nephew!” he said to him.
ê-tipiskâyik iyikohk, nipahêwak môswa. ||| At night fall, no sooner, they killed a moose.
piko ta-nipâyahk!" "kimisi-kawâtâpâwânânaw!" ||| We shall have to sleep out! We are soaked through to the bone!”
"pâsêtân kitayiwinisinawa!" itêw. ||| “Let us dry our clothes,” he said to him.
tâpwê pâsamwak, mitoni mistahi ê-pônahkik minahikoskâhk. ||| So they dried them, feeding up a huge fire in a cedar-grove.
mayaw ê-kiskêyimât onahâhkisîma ê-nipâyit, otinamwêw otayiwinisiyiwa kâ-kî-akotâyit. ||| As soon as he knew that his son-in-law slept, he took the latter's clothes from where he had hung them.
"kêkway kâ-saskitêk?" "kitayiwinisa mêstihkahtêwa!" ||| “What is burning? Your clothes have burned up!”
"hâh, ayisk kiwî-kakwê-nipahin!" "-- itâp nika-môsôwin!" itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “Hah, of course, for you are trying to kill me! - So then I shall turn into a moose!” said the youth.
nitomêw, ê-ati-sipwêhtêt awa kisêyiniw kisinwa. ||| As the old man went away, he called the cold.
tâpwê mistahi kisinâw. ||| And really, it grew very cold.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw kîwêw. ||| Then that youth went home.
âsiskawêw osisa; môsôwiw, ê-kîwêt. ||| He outdistanced his uncle; he was in the form of a moose, as he went home.
êkwa, "tânêhki?" itik wîwa. ||| Then, “Why thus?” his wife asked him.
"kôhtâwiy ê-wî-kakwê-nipahit, kahkiyaw nitayiwinisa kî-mêstihkasam." ||| “Because your father is trying to kill me, he burned up all my clothes.”
têkohtêt awa kisêyiniw, apiyiwa onahâhkisîma. ||| When the old man arrived, his son-in-law sat there.
"tânêhki mîna kâ-ôh-mêstihkasamwat kitihkwatim otayiwinisa?" itik otânisa. ||| “Why now did you burn up your nephew's clothes?” his daughter asked him.
"hâ, ê-kîskwêhkwasiyân," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Oh dear, because I was walking in my sleep,” said the old man.
"mahti pêyakwâw âsay mîna!" itêyihtam awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Let me try once more!” thought the old man.
"ninahâhkisîm, mahti mâcîtân!" itêw. ||| “My son-in-law, let us hunt!” he said to him.
"namôya ta-kî-kîwêyahk!" itêw sâsay mîna. ||| “We shall not be able to go home!” he said to him, again.
iyikohk ê-tipiskâyik, nipahêwak môswa. ||| Not before nightfall they killed a moose.
"kiyâm ka-kapêsinânaw," itwêw awa kisêyiniw; "kika-pâsênânaw kitayiwinisinawa,"-- "kîhkîhk êkosi nika-kakwê-isi-nipahâw," ê-itêyihtahk awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Let us camp,” said the old man; “We shall dry our clothes,” for, “In spite of all, I shall try to kill him this way,” thought the old man.
êkwa akotâwak ê-kî-pônahkik otayiwinisiwâwa. ||| Then, after feeding up a fire, they hung up their clothes.
mayaw ê-nipâyit, awa oskinîkiw nîhtinam kahkiyaw otayiwinisa. ||| As soon as the other slept, the youth took down all of his own garments.
êkwa kisêyiniw waniskâw. ||| Then the old man got up.
pasakwâpiw, konita ê-kîskwêhkwasîhkâsot. ||| He squinted from under his eyelids, pretending to walk in his sleep.
wiya kêsêyinîwit kêhciwâk otayiwinisa kahkiyaw mêstihkasam. ||| The old man himself burned up all his own clothes.
"kêkway kâ-kîsitêk?" itêw. ||| “What is that burning ?” he asked him.
"ôhi niya kâ-astêki nitayiwinisa," itwêw awa oskinîkiw; "kiya êtokê kêhciwâk kitayiwinisa kâ-pônaman," itêw ôhi kisêyiniwa; "ayisk êkosi kikî-tôtawin; nîsta mâka êkosi isi ki-ka-isi-nakatitin." ||| “Here are my clothes, lying here,” said the youth; “I daresay it is your own clothes you have put into the fire,” he said to the old man; “But seeing that you did it to me, I too shall now leave you, as you left me.”
itâp êtokê nika-môsôwin!" itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| I suppose I shall then turn into a moose!” said the old man.
nama kaskihtâw kita-môsôwit. ||| But he did not succeed in turning into a moose.
nitomêw kisinwa awa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk called the cold.
nipahêw ôhi kisêyiniwa. ||| He killed the old man.
mâcika êkwa nôtokêsiw nêpahimiht onâpêma mistahi kisiwâsiw. ||| Of course the old woman now was very angry, when her husband had been killed.
"kika-nôtinitonânaw!" itêw onahâhkisîma; "ahkâmasiniy êkotôwahk nêwâw ka-nimahotin;" "êkota kê-pakamahotân!" itwêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| “We shall fight!” she said to her son-in-law; “With this pounding stone four times I shall threaten you; then I shall strike you!” said the old woman.
nêwâw ê-nimahwât nâpiwa, otinamiyiwa; ostikwân ohci pîkwatahamiyiwa. ||| When for the fourth time she held it over Napiw as if to strike, he took it; he smashed her head with it.
êkosi êkwa awa kotak oskinîkiskwêw, mîna êwako nipahik. ||| Thereupon that other young woman, her, too, he killed.
êkosi kahkiyaw ê-nipahikocik. ||| So he killed them all.
macikah ayâwak êkota wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Of course Wisahketchahk and the other stayed there.
êkwa sipwêhtêw, ê-pêhtahk osîma kâ-kî-mahîhkaniwiyit ê-nipahikoyit itâmi-nipîhk kâ-otaskîyit nanâtohk misi-pisiwa mîna misi-kinêpikwa. ||| Then he set out, for he heard that his little brother who had turned into a wolf had been slain by the various Great Panthers and Great Serpents that dwell under water.
"tânisi êtokê nika-tôtên itâmi-nipîhk kita-itohtêyân?" ||| “I wonder what I shall do to go under the water!”
kâ-wâpamât osîma, ita ê-kî-nipahcikâsoyit, nipîhk mâna ê-ay-itâpi-t, ê-okimâwiyit kinosêwa otiskwâhtêmiyihk ê-akociniyit, mistahi pakwâtam. ||| When he saw, as he always looked into the waters, his little brother, where he had been slain by them all, hanging over the doorway of the Chief Fish, he was filled with grief and hate.
kîtahtawê itohtêw; nitawi-pimwêw ôhi kâ-okimâwi-yit kinosêwa. ||| Presently he went there; he went and shot with an arrow that Chief Fish.
papâmohtêw êkosi isi. ||| Then he wandered about.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpamât ayîkisa. ||| Presently he saw a frog.
"hâ, ninitawi-nipiskêyân," itwêw awa ayîkis. ||| “Why I am going to doctor by breathing,” said the frog.
"tânisi kâ-itôtaman, wî-nipiskêyani?" itwêw awa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “What do you do, when you are breath-doctoring?” asked Wisahketchahk.
ê-kî-wîhtamâkot, nipahêw ôhi. ||| When it told him, he killed it.
naspitamohisow; osîhisôw ta-ayîkisiwit. ||| He turned himself into its form; he made himself to be a frog.
itohtêw êkwa kâ-kanawêyihcikâsoyit kâ-mihkosiyit mahîhkaniwayâna. ||| He went to where they kept the Red Wolfskin.
mayaw ê-pîhtokêt, "tawîstâhk! ||| As soon as he entered, “Make way for this person!
êwako êkwa kâ-wî-pê-pimâcihât ôhi wîsahkêcâhkwa kâkî-pimwâyit," itâw. ||| This is the one who has come to cure him whom Wisahketchahk has shot with an arrow,” was said of him.
ê-isi-tôtawât ôhi kâ-nitawi-nânapâcihât, êkwa tâpwê sôhki kihcitânam ôma acosis. ||| When he was treating him whom he had come to tend, then, truly, with a vim he thrust in that arrow.
"kêkway itahk ayîkis kê-nipiskêt!" "mistahi ôma kikisiwâhinâwâw, nisîm ê-kî-nipahâyêk!" itwêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “What is that about a frog would be breathing on wounds! Rather you have angered me much by killing my little brother!” cried Wisahketchahk.
"kikisiwâhâwak maci-pisiskiwak!" itik manitôwa; "wî-iskipêw askiy." "kahkiyaw pâh-pêyak pisiskiwak otina, nanâtohk kâ-papâmihâcik." "ê-misâk ôsi osîhtâ," itik. ||| “You have enraged the evil beasts!” the Lord told him; “The earth will be flooded. Take one of every beast, and of all those who fly. Build a great canoe,” He told him.
êkospîhk êsa maywês iskipêk ôma askiy, kahkiyaw kêkway êsa okî-môtohtâwâw pisiskiwak. ||| At that time, we are told, before this earth was flooded, all kinds of animals ate each other.
ahpô paskwâwi-mostoswak kî-môwêwak ayîsiyiniwa, iyâta-ayâ-yici. ||| Even the buffalo ate men, no matter where they were.
êkosi kî-ispayiw êsa. ||| That is the way things were.
kahkiyaw pâh-pêyak otinêw wîsahkêcâhk nâh-nîso ohci, pêyak nâpêw-âyisa, kiskisîsa. ||| Wisahketchahk took one of every kind, in pairs one male and one female.
kahkiyaw kâ-papâmihâyit, mîna ôta askîhk misiwê kâ-papâmohtêyit, kahkiyaw nâh-nîso ohci otinêw. ||| Of all who fly and of all who walk about this earth, of each he took two.
êkosi osîhtâw ê-misâyik ôsi. ||| Then he built a great canoe.
êkosi kî-wani-tipiskâyiw êsa. ||| Then deep darkness came.
êkosi kahkiyaw atâhkwak namôya ohci ihtakôwak. ||| All the stars ceased to be.
misiwê kî-iskipêyiw askiy, ê-kî-kîsihtât ê-misâyik ôsi. ||| Everywhere the earth was flooded, when he had finished the great canoe.
êkwa misiwê ê-iskipêyik, kahkiyaw asinîwaciya ê-ayiwâkipêyiki, êkwa papâmâhokowak. ||| Then, when the flood was everywhere, and all the mountains of rock were submerged, then they drifted about.
piyisk wî-nipahâhkatosôw. ||| At last he nearly starved to death.
wîwa nipahâhkatosoyiwa. ||| His wife starved to death.
êkwa ômisi kahkiyaw kêkwaya nipîhk kâ-otaskîyit mac-âyisa ê-wî-kakwê-nipahikot, iyâta-pê-itohtêyici ê-nipahât, piyisk kahkiyaw kêkwaya kostik. ||| Then, when all the creatures that dwell in the water, the evil beings, tried to kill him, when in vain they came there, and he slew them, then at last all creatures feared him.
êkwa kîtahtawê kisê-manitowa kâ-pakicîtotâkot. ||| Presently God descended to him.
ômisi itik: "kîspin êkâ kî-kâhcitinamani asiskiy, êkosi namôya wîhkâc kita-ihkipayiw ôma nipiy," itik. ||| Thus He spoke to him: “If you cannot scrape up some earth, then never will these waters recede,” He told him.
nêmitanaw êskotôskwanêhk ita ê-pâhkwâsik; misiwê êsa kî-iskipêpan. ||| It was forty cubits to the bottom; the flood had covered all.
"êkwa tânisi kê-tôtamân?" itêyihtam âta wiya. ||| “Now how am I to do?” he thought, none the less.
ayisk kahkiyaw kî-pôsihêw pisiskiwa. ||| But he had all the beasts on his ship.
kîtahtawê atotêw mâkwa, ta-kakwê-otinamiyit asiskiy. ||| Presently he bade the loon try to take up some soil.
pôti namwâc kî-kaskihtâyiwa. ||| It turned out quite unable.
kîtahtawê mîna atotêw nikikwa. ||| Then he presently he employed the otter.
namwâc kaskihtâyiwa. ||| It was entirely unable to do it.
kahkiyaw tahto kâ-nihtâ-kôkiyit âta ê-atotât, namwâc kî-kâhcitinamiyiwa asiskiy. ||| Although he employed all, as many are good divers, they could not at all scrape up any earth.
kîtahtawê wacaskwa atotâw. ||| Then in time he sent the muskrat.
nama mayaw mitoni takohtêyiwa. ||| It was a long time coming back.
êwakoni apisîs kî-kikamoyiw asiskiy. ||| A little earth was sticking to it.
âsay mîna kîhtwâm sihkimêw. ||| Again he bade it go.
nêwâw sipwêhtisahwêw kita-nâtamiyit asiskiy. ||| Four times he sent it off to fetch earth.
"êkoyikohk!" itik manitôwa. ||| “It is enough!” the Spirit told him.
êkota ohci kî-miyikôwisiwak ayîsiyiniwak nêhiyawak, oskac askiy ôta ê-ayâcik. ||| Thus it was that the Indians were given this by the spirit powers, that first the they had an earth here.
êkosi kahkiyaw nipiy nama takon êkwa kahkiyaw. ||| For then all the water ceased to be.
êkosi sipwêhtêw êkota ohci wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Then Wisahketchahk went away from here.
êkwa wiyasôwâtêw ayîsiyiniwa kita-owîcêwâkaniyit, ê-wî-osihât manitôw. ||| Then the Spirit decreed that he was to have man as a companion, and decided to create man.
asiskiy ohci osihêw nîso ayîsiyiniwa. ||| He made two human beings of earth.
êkwa maywês âpâhkawihât nâpêwa, ospikêkaniyiwa iskwêyânihk pêh-pêyak ohci otinamwêw, êkwa kâ-âpâhkawihât. ||| Then before He brought the men to life from each of them He took the lowest rib, and then He brought them to life.
nistam ê-pîkiskwêt ayîsiyiniw, ê-kî-osihiht, "nipiy!" kî-itwêw êsa. ||| When man first spoke, after being created, we are told that he said, “Water!”
kîhtwâm ê-pîkiskwêt, "nimîciwin!" kî-itwêw êsa. ||| When he spoke again, we are told that he said “My food!”
kahkiyaw kêkway nama kêkway ohci kostikwak. ||| They were feared by all creatures, for no cause.
"omihtikôs" kî-isi-wihâw nistam nâpêw. ||| “Dug-out-canoe” the first man was named.
nêwo kî-ayâwak, pâh-pîtos ê-isi-wâhkôhtocik. ||| Four of them dwelt there, being in different wise related, so as to make a family.
êkota êkwa kî-sipwêhtisahwâw nistam kâhkâkiw, kahkiyaw askiy ê-wâsakamêt. ||| Then from there the raven was first sent out to make a circuit of the earth.
pôti nicawâc kî-asênâw. ||| In the outcome he was needs rejected.
êkwa kihiw kî-sipwêhtisahwâw. ||| Then the eagle was sent out.
êkota ohci nama wîhkâc êsa kî-nipiwak ayîsiyiniwak. ||| In the time that began then, people never died.
pêyâhtik kî-kâmwâci-pimâtisiwak, piyisk ê-ati-mihcêticik. ||| They lived quietly and undisturbed, until at last they came to be many.
kî-miskamwak tânisi ê-isi-pimâcihocik. ||| They found how to keep themselves alive.
êkota ohci kâ-pê-ohpikihitot nêhiyaw, ayîsiyiniw. ||| From that time to this in successive generations has come the Cree, the Indian.
nanâtohk ayîsiyiniw kahkiyaw ninisitohtên ôma kâ-nitawêyihtâkwahk âcimôwin. ||| Of all the different peoples I understand this story which is desired.
nêhiyaw tânisi ê-isi-pimâtisit, ê-kî-pê-isi-ohpikihitocik nêhiyawak, kahkiyaw nikiskêyihtên. ||| Of how the Cree lived, as the Cree have come down through the generations to this time, all of this I know.
mîna wâpiski-wiyâs ôta kâ-pê-takohtatât ayamihâwin, kahkiyaw mîna êwako nikiskêyihtên, tânisi ê-pê-isi-wîhcikâtêyik. ||| And of the Christian worship which the white man has brought here with him, of this, too, I know all, of how it has been announced to this time.
ôhcitaw nitâtayôhkâtên nistam ayîsiyiniw, tânisi ê-kî-isi-osîhcikâsot nêhiyaw. ||| I have chosen to tell the sacred story of how the first man was created, the Indian.
mâskôc êkotôwahk kâ-nitawêyihcikâtêk, mâskôc ê-nôhtê-kiskêyihtamihk nêhiyaw opimâtisiwin, ê-itêyihtamân, kâ-ôh-isi-âtayôhkêyân. ||| Because I have thought that doubtless this is what is desired, that doubtless people wish to know of the life of the Indian, that is why I tell this sacred story.
nîswâw mitâtahtomitanaw askiy ê-kî-ispayik, êkospîhk êsa okî-nipahikoh wâkayôsa êwako nistam ayîsiyiniw, êsa ê-kî-nipit. ||| When twice a hundred years had gone by, at that time, this first man was killed by a bear, and so he died.
êwako niyanân kâ-nêhiyâwiyâhk onipiwa ocahcâhkoyiwa ta-kanawêyimât kî-itasôwâtik êsa manitôwa. ||| Then, we are told, he was assigned by the Spirit to care for the souls of the dead of us who are Indians.
matwân cî kêyâpic êkosi ispayiw; namôya nika-kî-itwân. ||| I question if it is still so; I cannot say.
ayisk osâm ninisiwanâcihisonân. ||| For too greatly we are destroying ourselves.
kî-kitahamawâw ayîsiyiniw êkâ kita-ayamihât; êwako ohci kâ-itwêyân. ||| The Indian was forbidden to practise the Christian Religion; that is what I mean.
"nêhiyaw kâ-isiyîhkâsot piko kâ-itak: êkâya ayamihâhkan! ||| “I say this only to him who is called Indian: thou shalt not worship in Christian wise!
namôya kiya kâ-miyitân." "nitawâsimisa ohcitaw nimiyâw wâpiski-wiyâs, kita-kakwâtakihot, wiya ê-kî-nipahât nitawâsimisa," kî-itwêw êsa manitôw. ||| Not to thee do I give this. I give my son to the white man, that he may suffer for having slain my Son,” said the Lord.
êkoyikohk êwako pêyak pîkiskwêwin. ||| So much for this discourse.
kîtahtawê sipwêhtêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Once upon a time Wisahketchahk set out.
kîtahtawê wâpamêw osk-âyîsisa wacistwanihk pihêsisa. ||| Presently he saw some young partridges in a nest.
"nisîmitik, pihêtik, tânisi êsiyîhkâsoyêk?" ||| “My little brothers, partridges, what is your name?”
"âta kiwîhinân, 'pihêwak' kâ-itwêyan; êkosi piko ê-isiyîhkâsoyâhk." ||| “But you just did name us, when you said, ‘partridges’; that is the only name we have.”
"namôya!" itwêw wîsahkêcâhk; "kahkiyaw kêkway nîswayak isiyîhkâtêw." ||| “No!” said Wisahketchahk; “Everything has two names.”
"namôya," itik; "êkosi piko, 'pihêwak,' ê-isiyîhkâsoyâhk." ||| “No,” they told him, “For we have only this name, ‘partridges’.”
mâ-mitonêyihtamok;" "kotak mîna wîhôwin kitayânâwâw." ||| Take thought upon it; you have some other name besides.”
êkosi awa ostêsimâs ômisi itêw: "âta wiya mâna nikâwiy nôhtâwiy, 'okoskohiwêsîsak' kitisiyîhkâsonânaw, êkwa"pihêwak";" "kinîsoyîhkâsonânaw, nititikonân mâna." ||| Thereupon the oldest of them said to him, “To be sure, my mother and father do say to us, ‘Little Startlers,’ we are called; and ‘Partridges’; we have two names.”
nitakis ôki koskohiwêcik!" itêw, ê-mîsît ostikwâniyihk, ê-pîwêyimât; "nama ta-kî-koskohiwêyêk!" itêw; "nama awiyak ka-kî-sêkihâwâw!" itêw. ||| Fine ones these are to startle anyone!” he said to them, [shitting on their heads] to show his contempt; “You couldn't startle anybody!” he told them; “You will never scare anybody!” he told them.
êkwa ôki pihêwak ê-kîwêcik, awîna ôhi otawâsimisiwâwa! ||| Then, when those partridges came home, what had happened to their children!
"tânêhki ôma, nitawâsimisitik, kâ-ôh-isinâkosiyêk, ê-wîhcêkisiyêk?" itikwak okâwiyiwâwa ôhtâwiyiwâwa mîna. ||| “Why is this, children, that you look like this [no translation]?” their mother and their father asked them.
"wiya ana wîsahkêcâhk ê-kakwêcimikoyâhk, 'tânisi êsiyîhkâsoyêk, nisîmitik, pihêtik?' ê-itikoyâhk, êkâ ê-wîhtamawâyâhk, "âta kosa kiwîhinân," ê-itâyâhk, "namôya; kahkiyaw kêkway nîsoyîhkâtêw," nititikonân." "piyisk niwîhtamawâw, 'okoskohiwêsîsak nitisiyîhkâsonân,' ê-itak, "nitakis ôki koskohiwêcik," kâ-itikoyâhk, ê-mîsît nistikwâninâhk." "êkosi aspin kâ-sipwêhtêt, ê-pâhpit." ||| “Why, when that person Wisahketchahk asked us, ‘What is your name, little brothers, partridges?’ and we did not tell him, but said to him ‘but you have just spoken our name,’ then he said to us, ‘No; everything has two names.’ At last I told him, saying to him, ‘Little Startlers we are called,’ whereupon he said of us, ‘Fine ones these are to startle anyone,’ [no translation] With that he was off and away, laughing.”
"hâw, niwîkimâkan, sipwêhtê." "mâka mîna sîpîsis otihtahki, êkota ka-wawiyasihânaw, 'nitakis ôki sêkihiwêcik,' kâ-itât kitawâsimisinawa; kanôhkawâtân." ||| “Well, wife, come away. When he comes to the creek again, we shall make him a laughing-stock for saying to our children, ‘Fine ones these, to startle anyone.’ Let us attack him.”
tâpwê pihêwa mawîhkâtêwak, ê-mâwacihitocik. ||| Accordingly they appealed to the other partridges, and all assembled.
êkwa kîtahtawê kâ-wâpahtahk sîpîsis ê-sakâyik. ||| Then presently he came to the creek in the woods.
êkwa âyîtaw âyîtawakâm pihêwak apiwak êkota, ê-kâsocik. ||| And there on both sides, on both banks sat the partridges in concealment.
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk otihtam sîpîsis. ||| Then Wisahketchahk reached the creek.
êkosi ê-wâpahtahk, mostoswayâna akwanahôw; êkwa pahkêkin oskotâkay; êkwa pahkêkin otâsa. ||| When he came to it there, he had on a buffalo robe; and leather was his coat; of leather were his breeches.
êkwa ômisi itwêw: "mahti"- sôhki pîkiskwêw- "iskêkâni osk-âyi astotin astwâtohk, osk-âya ayiwinisa, 'awiyak âsowakamêyohpîci, kita-ayâw ôhi,' itwêhk." "nistwâw nika-nômiskên; êkota nêwâw mwêhci nika-ohpîn," itwêw. ||| Then he spoke as follows: “Come” and loudly he spoke - “I have a feeling that a new hat has been put up as a prize, and new clothes, and it has been announced, ‘If anyone jumps to the far shore, he shall have these.’ Three times I shall stop short; then, the fourth time, I shall jump,” he said.
nitohtâk ôhi pihêwa; mâka namôya wâpamêw. ||| The partridges listened to him; but he did not see them.
"aciyaw nika-wêpikâtân," itwêw; âcimostawêw tânisi ê-wî-tôtahk. ||| “For a short while I shall exercise my legs,” he said; he simply told them what he meant to do.
êkwa wâhyaw nîpawiw; otakohpa ôta ahêw; tâpiskawêw. ||| Then he stood a ways off; he put his blanket-robe here, like this; he put it round his neck. Then he came on a running start; at the bank of the creek he stopped with a jump.
êkwa pê-wayacîwîw; sisonê sîpîsisihk naki-kwâskohtiw. ||| “Tut tut, I shall get my tobacco-pouch all wet, if I don't make it,” he said; “I'll throw it across.”
otinêw wahpihcisa; namôya kanawâpamêw, ômisi ê-isiwêpinât; akâmihk pahkisiniyiwa. ||| He took his tobacco-pouch; he did not keep his eye on it as he flung it; like this it fell somewhere on the other bank.
ê-wêpinât, pêyak pihêwa kâ-ohpahoyit. ||| When he threw it, one of the partridges flew up.
"yôho, mâna tâpwê nika-koskowihikoh!" itwêw. ||| “Tut tut, really, he came very near startling me!” he said.
"êkwa piko nistwâw!" ||| “Now only three times more!”
mîna âsay nôhcimihk itohtêw. ||| Again he went away from the water.
namôya kiskêyihtam itê wahpihcisa kâ-isiwêpinât. ||| He did not know the exact spot to which he had tossed his tobacco-pouch.
êkwa pê-wayacîwîw; nakîw. ||| Then he came with a running start; he stopped.
êkwa piko nîswâw," itwêw. ||| Now only twice more!” he said.
êkwa nîso ohpihâyiwa. ||| Then two of them flew up.
"yôho, mâna nika-sêkihikohtayik ôki pihêwak okoskohiwêsîsak!" ||| “Tut tut, they came mighty near scaring me, these partridges, these little startlers!”
âsay mîna pê-môskîstam ôma sîpîsis. ||| Again he came running at that creek.
êkwa anohc êkwa nika-ohpîn." "iskêkâniya osk-âya astwâtohk astotin ayiwinisa, 'awiyak âsowakamêyohpîci nika-miyâw,' itwêhk." "êkwa mâka niwî-ohpîn," itwêw. ||| Now this time I shall jump. Without doubt a new hat has been put up as a prize, and new clothes, with the statement, ‘If anyone jumps across the water, I shall give him these.’ But now I shall jump,” he said.
êkwa sipwêhtêw; êkwa êkotê sâkowêw: "êkwa niwî-ohpîn;" "niwî-otinên osk-âya;" "niya nika-ayân;" "niwî-ohpîn!" "namôya êkwa niwî-nakîn!" itwêw; âcimostawêw ôhi kâ-kâsôhtâkot. ||| Then he was off; and then he shouted: “Now I am going to jump; I am going to take the new clothes; I, I shall have them; I am going to jump! This time I shan't stop!” he cried; he gave it all away to them who were hiding from him.
êkwa pê-wayacîwîw, ê-pê-sâkowêt. ||| Then he came with a running start; he came a-shouting.
mitoni kisiwâsiw pisisik. timîw ôma sîpîsis. ||| He kept himself in a high state of excitement.
ôma ê-ohpît âyîtawakâm pihêwa kâ-ohpîyit, ê-pitihkoyit. ||| [no translation] When he jumped, up went the partridges from both banks with a whirr.
sêkisiw; tâwakâm pahkisin. ||| He was scared; he fell into the middle of the water.
ôhi kâ-manâcihtât omaskisina, otâsa kâ-tâpiskahk, kahkiyaw sâpopatâw, otakohpa. "cê! ||| Those moccasins of his, which he treated with such care, his breeches, which he had round his neck, he got them all drenched, and his blanket-robe.
macastimwak kâ-koskowihicik, kâ-sâpopatâwak nitayiwinisa!" itwêw. ||| “Bah! Those dirty dogs startled me and made me get my clothes all wet!” he cried.
"hah, nika-pîhtwân!" "kî-pîhtwâyâni, êkoyikohk ta-pâstêwa ôhi nitayiwinisa," itwêw. ||| “Ha, I shall have a smoke! When I have smoked, these clothes of mine will be dry,” he said.
êkwa ê-nitonawât wahpihcisa, nama miskawêw. ||| Then, when he looked for his tobacco-pouch, he could not find it.
"tânitê ôma, nahpihcis êsi-wanihak?" ||| “Where can it be that I lost my tobacco-pouch?”
nitonawêw nipîhk, êkwa êkâ ê-miskawât. ||| He looked for it in the water, but he did not find it.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpamât ê-akociniyit. ||| Then all at once he saw it lying in the water.
maci-ahpihcis awa kâ-kâsôhtawit!" "nikaskêyihtêh ê-wî-pîhtwâyân!" ||| This nasty tobacco-pouch has been hiding from me! I was getting sad for want of a smoke!”
akohciniyiwa; otinêw; nama kêkway. ||| It lay there in the water; he reached to take it; there was nothing.
piyisk ômayikohk; nama kêkway. ||| At last as far as this; nothing.
"â, ê-tapasît awa nahpihcis!" itêyihtam; "nicawâc kinwês kîmîw." ||| “Oho, and so this tobacco-pouch of mine is running away!” he thought; “It has been away a long time, for all I could do.”
êkwa ômisi ê-tôtahk, piyisk nahapiw. ||| Then, when he reached like this, at last he was in a sitting position.
nêtê mohcihk kâskatâwahkinikêw; nama kêkway. ||| Way out he was scratching up gravel from the bed of the stream; nothing.
itâpiw; "êwako awa nahpihcis!" itwêw, "mahti êkwa nika-otinâw," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He looked there; “There is my tobacco-pouch!” he cried; “Now do let me take it,” he thought.
êkwa ômisi ê-tôtahk, ôta ê-akohcihk ôta, "nika-ati-ômisi-itiskwêyin," ê-itêyihtahk, pôti ôhi ispimihk ôta mistikohk kî-akociniyiwa. ||| Then, when he did like this, there where, by this time, he lay in the water, thinking, “I will turn my head like this when I reach,” why, there, up aloft in a tree there, hung that thing.
maci-ahpihcis awa kâ-wâh-wanihak, kâ-kaskêyihtamihit!" "niwî-pîhtwâwâh!" "êcika awa ita ê-akocihk!" itwêw; "nicawâc namôya awiyak," itwêw, ê-otinât, "nicawâc kika-nahihon, êkâ kita-âpatisiyan." ||| There is that nasty tobacco-pouch I kept losing till it made me miserable! As if I hadn't been longing for a smoke! And so, there it hangs!” he cried; “Since you won't have it otherwise, be absent,” he said, taking it; “Since you won't have it otherwise, I'll teach you how to be of no use.”
nama kêkwaya ôhi otôspwâkana wahpihcisa mîna. ||| Gone was his tobacco-pouch, and his pipe as well.
nama iskwa pâstêyiwa otayiwinisa. ||| His garments were not yet dry.
kîtahtawê sâpopêyiwa otakohpa; kosikwatiyiwa. ||| Now his blanket was drenched through; it was heavy.
osâm ê-kîsopwêyik, ê-pimohtêt, pôti osâm ê-pwâwihât ôhi otakohpa, ê-kisâstêyik, pôti kâ-wâpamât asiniya ê-misikitiyit. ||| And as the weather was very hot, as he walked along, he could hardly carry that blanket-robe of his, in the hot sun, when there he saw a big stone.
ê-otihtât, "hâw, nisîm," itêw ôhi asiniya, "kimiyitin awa nitakohp," itêw. ||| When he came up to it, “Now, brother,” he said to that stone, “I give you this blanket of mine,” he said to it.
kâ-akwanahât, ati-sipwêhtêw; mosêskatêw. ||| When he had covered it, he went away; he went naked.
êkwa namôya wâhyaw ê-ihtât, kâ-pê-nôkwaniyik ê-wî-kimiwaniyik, ê-pê-kâh-kitoyit piyêsiwa. ||| Then, when he had not gone far, there came signs of rain; as the Thunderers sounded their approach.

kîwêpahtâw; takohtêw; otinêw. ||| He ran back; he came to the place; he took it.
"nipê-nâtâw awa nitakohp," itwêw. ||| “I have come to get my blanket here;” he said.
"yahah, mâka mîna nika-wî-pimitisahok awa kâ-kî-miyak nitakohpa!" itwêw, ê-itât ôhi asiniya. ||| “Dear me, but now this fellow to whom I had given my blanket will come and chase me!” he said, speaking of that stone.

"yahah, omîhkawikîh awa!" itêw; "isi cîkâhtaw!" ||| “Dear me, he runs fast, this fellow!” he said of it; “It's a close shave, this!”
piyisk kisiwâk; wayacîwîw. ||| At last it was near; he ran hard.
kîsopwêyiw; kîpa nayawapiw. ||| It was hot weather; soon he was tired.
"mahti êkâ ê-kî-pê-âmaciwêt awa kâ-watakamisit, nitakohpa ê-kî-awihak!" ||| “Let's hope that he won't be able to come up the hill, this dangerous person to whom I lent my blanket!”
êkwa tâpwê mîhkawikiyiwa. ||| Truly, it went fast.
itê ê-sakâyik itâmôw. "mahti kita-âtisin awa kâ-watakamisit!" ê-itwêt. ||| He fled to a wooded place, “Let's hope that dangerous character will be blocked!” he said.

âsay wîsahkêcâhk sêkisiw; êkwa wayacîwîw. ||| By this time Wisahketchahk was thoroughly frightened; he ran with all his might.
"osâm êkâ awiyak ta-kî-itâmoyân, kayâs nôhtâwiy ê-kî-nipit," itwêw; "ta-kî-nâtamawit nama awiyak," itwêw. ||| “And there is no one I can flee to, for my father died long ago,” he said; “There isn't anyone could help me,” he said.

ositihk mâhtakoskâk ôhi asiniya. ||| The stone came down on his foot and held him fast.

pê-âhtapiyiwa oskâtihk; êkwa mâhtakoskâk. ||| It moved farther up, onto his leg; it held him fast with its weight.
"âstamita nawac, nisîm!" ||| “Farther up this way, brother!”
"namôya!" itik; "kîspin itahk êpiyâni, nama wîhkâc nitâhtapin," itik. ||| “No!” it answered him; “If I sit down anywhere, I never change my seat,” it answered him.
êkosi êkwa nama kî-pihkohow, kahkiyaw kêkway pêmohtêyici êkota, manicôsa, "kakwê-pihkohin, nisîm!" ê-itât, "namôya! ||| So now he could not get himself free, and whenever any creature, even a worm or a beetle, went by, “Try and get me free, little brother!” he would say to it, but “No!
nikostâw!" ê-itikot. ||| I am afraid of him!” it would answer him.

nikostâw osâm!" kî-itâw; "pêyakwanohk kita-apit, ita êpici," itik nanâtohk ôhi kêkway. ||| I fear him too much!” he was told; “Let him stay where he is, when he takes his seat anywhere,” those different creatures said to him.
kîtahtawê pîskwa kinwês kâ-kitoyit; ê-kitoyit, kâ-cîpipayiyit. ||| Then at one time the mosquito hawk gave a long, repeated cry; when it cried, the stone moved with a jerk.
"yôhôn, pakâhkam awa asiniy kostêw êwakoni," itêyihtam; "nisîm, âstam!" ||| “Hoho, plainly this stone fears this one creature,” he thought; “Little brother, come here!”

kakwê-pihkohin;" "nitiskiskâk awa asiniy." "kika-isi-miyosiyan kika-isîhitin, kîspin pahkwatinaci awa asiniy." ||| Try to get me free; this stone is killing me with its weight. I will make you beautiful, if you move this stone away.”

êkwa ispâhkêpayihow awa pîskwa; êkotê ohci pê-môskîstawêw ôhi asiniya; pwêkicitêw. ||| Then the mosquito hawk soared up into the air; from there it came attacking that stone; [no translation].
kêyâpic nama kî-pihkohôw awa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Even yet Wisahketchahk could not get himself free.

iyikohk kita-ispîhcâw." ||| It ought to be only as long as this.”

êkwa pakwâtam awa pîskwa ê-misâyik otôn. ||| The mosquito-hawk hated having a big mouth.
kisêyiniw sipwêhtêw, êkwa ê-piponiyik. ||| The Old Man set out, and it was in winter.

mihcêtokamikisiyiwa, mihcêt mîkiwâhpa. ||| Those people had many tents, many were the lodges.
ê-ati-takohtêt ispatinâhk, awâsisa, "okiyôtêw!" itik. ||| When he arrived at the hill, the children said of him, “A visitor!”

ha, itohtêw êkotê, pîhtêyas ê-cimatêyik. ||| So he went to the tent that stood in the center. He entered.
"pahkwêsikanâpoy," itêyihtam. ||| “Porridge,” he thought.
"ôta ta-pê-mîcisôw" itâw, ê-nitomiht. ||| “Let him come and eat over here,” someone said to him, inviting him.
êkwa mwêhci ê-wî-mîcisot, âsay mîna kotakihk kotaka ê-nitomikot. ||| Then, just as he was about to begin eating, again he was invited by others to another tent.

"â, nistêsê, kîpa mâna piciwak ôki ayîsiyiniwak kîkisêpâ!" ||| “Ho, big brother, these fools always break camp very early of a morning!”
"pisinê nîtim kotawêci, êkota nika-pêkopayin," itêyihtam. ||| “As soon as my sister-in-law kindles the fire, I shall wake up,” thought he.
kêtayôwinisêw, "wêtinahk nika-nipân," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He took off his clothes, thinking “I do want to sleep in comfort.”

"cê, wînikonêwi-mahkayak!" ||| “Bah, the filthy brutes!”
êkwa postayôwinisêw. ||| Then he put on his clothes.
"nama kîhtwâm nika-wayêsihikwak!" ||| “They shan't fool me again!”

mîtosiskâhk, ita ê-sîpêyâyik, awâsisa ê-tatwêwitamiyit, ê-sôskwaciwêyit, mistahi tahtakosiw kôna, awâsisa ita ê-mêtawêcik, ê-kîskwêcik. ||| He went to a poplar-grove, to where there was an open place among the trees, where some children were playing noisily, sliding down a hill. Very hard and smooth was the snow where the children were playing and raising a rumpus.
mwêhci ê-otinahk, "hâw, nipê-nitomâw kistêsinaw; ta-pê-mîcisôw nîkihk," itâw. ||| Just as he took it, “Hullo, I've come to invite our big brother; he is to come eat at our hose,” he was told.

"hâw, nîtim, ita kâ-wîkihkêmoyân, êkota itohtâtân ôma kâ-asamiyan pimihkân," itwêw. ||| “Well, sister-in-law, let us take the pemmican over to where I am visiting for the night,” he said.
"â, nisîm, mistahi ninêstohtân;" "ê-timikonik osêtinâhk niwî-nipân." ||| “Now, little brother, I am tired from my long tramp; I want to sleep on the deep snow, on the hillside.”
"nistêsê, wîpac wî-piciw awa okimâw!" ||| “Big brother, the chief here means to move camp promptly!”
âsay miskâkaniyiw itê ê-wî-âywêpihk. ||| They had already found the place to stop to rest.
"pita êkota ê-wî-mîcisohk, maywês mîciso ê-wî-picihk." ||| “Wait and eat at the place where we are planning to eat, before we move on.”
"â, nisîm, kotawêci nîtim, âsay nika-waniskân," itêw osîma. ||| “Oh, little brother, when my sister-in-law kindles the fire, I shall get up all right,” he told his younger brother.
êkosi kêcikonam omaskisina otâsa mîna oskotâkay, ê-aspiskwêsimot. ||| Accordingly he took off his moccasins, his breeches, and his jacket; using them all for a pillow.

êkotowihk kâ-pîhtokêt, itâmihk kônihk ê-sîpâyâkonakihiht. ||| For such they were whose tents he had entered, and he had been led to go deep under the snow.

wîsahkêcâhk mistahi kitimâkisiw; nama wiya kêkway otayôwinis ê-wîkicik, ê-ayâcik. ||| Wisahketchahk was very poor; he had not even clothing in his house, where he dwelt with his family.

êkwa wîsahkêcâhk nama kêkway ayâw atâwâkan. ||| But Wisahketchahk had no furs to sell.
kotakak ayîsiyiniwak mistahi ayâwak; atâwêwak êkonik mistahi ayiwinisa; êkwa wîsahkêcâhk nama kêkway. ||| The other people had many; they bought many clothes, but Wisahketchahk none at all.

"kîspin miyiyani, kiyipa nika-ayân." ||| Then he spoke to the Frenchman as follows: “Won't you let me have credit? I haven't any furs. But in a short time I shall have a good many with which to pay my debt.” Thus Wisahketchahk spoke to the Frenchman: “You will not need to pay anything. If you give me credit, in a short time I shall have them. “Very well,” the Frenchmen “What do you want, Wisahketchahk?”

êkota mistahi ayôwinis otinam. ||| Then he took a great deal of clothing.

êkwa miyik maskihkiy, piscipôwin. ||| So the other gave him some medicine, poison.
êkwa kîwêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Then Wisahketchahk went home.

êkwa êkota piscipôwin astâw pimîhk; êkwa apisâsin oyâkanis, sîkinam êkota pimiy. ||| Then he put the poison into the fat; and into a small dish he poured the fat.

kîtahtawê wâpamêw mahîhkana pêyak. ||| Presently he saw a wolf.
"â, nisîm, âstam!"- ôhi mahîhkana. ||| “Hey, brother, come here!” to that wolf.
"â, namôya!" itwêw mahîhkan, "ê, kiwî-nipahin osâm!" ||| “Oh dear, no!” said the wolf; “Why, you want to kill me!”
ê-wî-masinahikêhitin." ||| I want to employ you.”
"tânisi ê-wî-isi-masinahikêhiyan." ||| “How do you want to employ me?”
"ê-wî-atoskahitân ka-papâ-nitomacik mahîhkanak mîna mahkêsîsak, kahkiyaw kâ-miyosicik mahkêsîsak." "ôta nika-apin ispatinâhk, ê-wî-kakêskimitakok, ê-miywâsihk âcimôwin ka-wîhtamâtakok." ||| “I want to give you the work of going round and summoning the wolves and foxes, all the good-looking foxes. I shall be sitting here on this knoll, ready to preach to you, to tell you good tidings.”
êkwa tâpwê awa mahîhkan sipwêhtêw, ê-nitomât mahîhkana mîna mahkêsîsa. ||| So that wolf went off to call the wolves and foxes.
tâpwê pêtohtêwak mihcêt mahîhkanak. ||| Indeed, many wolves came.

ômisi itêw: "nisîmitik, ayamihâwin kâ-nitohtamêk ta-otinamêk;" "êkosi êkwa namôya awiyak ka-nipahikowâwak, ayamihâyêko." "mâka êkâ tâpwêhtamêko, ka-nipahikowâwak." But if you do not believe, someone will kill you. Look upon these things, these here!” As the wolves and foxes looked at those pieces of fat, “Now, then, if anyone eats this which I shall place between his teeth, long will he live,” spoke Wisahketchahk.
êkwa kahkiyaw, "niya, niya!" itwêwak mahîhkanak, ê-miywêyihtahkik kinwês ka-pimâtisicik. ||| Then all the wolves cried, “I, I!” glad that they were to live long.
