mîciw awa mahîhkan; êkosi êkwa sipwêhtêw. ||| A wolf would eat it; then he would go.
pâh-pêyak ê-saskamohât wâsakâm, mîna mahkêsîsa, kahkiyaw mêstinam ôma pimiy. ||| He placed it in their mouths, one by one, round the circle, the foxes' too, using up all the fat.
"êkosi kinwês ka-pimâtisinâwâw, nisîmitik, ôma kâ-otinamêk ayamihâwin." ||| “So now long shall you live, brothers, now you have accepted this faith.”
tâpiskôc ayamihêwiyiniw wîsahkêcâhk, ê-miyât mahîhkana ayamihâwin. ||| Just like a priest was Wisahketchahk, as he gave religious instruction to the wolves.
kîtahtawê ê-apit mêkwâc wîsahkêcâhk, kahkiyaw kwâskwêpayihoyiwa mahîhkana, ê-pahkisiniyit, ê-piscipoyit, kahkiyaw ê-nipiyit. ||| Presently, as Wisahketchahk sat there, all the wolves leaped up in the air and fell down, poisoned, and they all died.
"maci-kakêpâtisak ôki!" "nika-ôh-ta-tipahikâkêwâh!" itêw êsa ôhi mahîhkana wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “These stupid fools! I surely did need something to pay my debts with!” Wisahketchahk must have said to those wolves.
êkwa wiyanihêw, ê-kîwêhtahât, êkwa mahkêsîsa mîna kahkiyaw. ||| Then he skinned them and took their skins home, and all the foxes' too.
mahîhkana ayamihâwin kâ-kiskinôhamawât, kahkiyaw nipahêw. ||| Having taught the wolves religion, he killed them all.
êkosi kahkiyaw tipaham omasinahikêwina, ê-wayêsimât mahîhkana. ||| In this way he paid all his debts, by deceiving the wolves with talk.
kêtahtawê pimohtêw wîsahkêcâhk; mâka mîna nôhtêhkatêw. ||| Once upon a time Wisahketchahk was walking along; as usual, he was hungry.
kîtahtawê wâpamêw mostoswa nîso, takwahinâwa pêyak, pêyak iyâpêsisa. ||| Presently he saw two buffalos, a bull and a young steer.
ômisi itêyihtam: "tânisi nika-nipahâwak?" itêyihtam. ||| This is what he thought: “How shall I kill them?” he thought.
ê-wâpamikot, wî-tapasîyiwa. ||| When they saw him, they wanted to run away.
miywâsin âcimowin ka-âcimostâtinâwâw." ||| I shall tell you a good story!”
cêskwa nîpawiwak mostoswak; namôya tapasîwak. ||| Soon the buffalos stood still; they did not run away.
êkwa takohtêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Then Wisahketchahk walked up to them.
ômisi itêw: "ayisiyiniwak ê-itwêcik, 'takwahinâw wîhkimâkosiw; miyosiw,' ê-itwêcik, kotakak ayisiyiniwak ômisi itwêwak: "iyâpêsis miyosiw; wîhkimâkosiw," ê-itwêcik, ê-kî-kîhkihtocik." "êwako ohci wî-kisiwâsiwak." "'mahti cêskwa niya nika-wâpamâwak; awîna wîhkimâkosiw,' nititwân, kâ-pê-nitawâpamitakok," ê-wî-wayêsimât ôhi mostoswa. ||| This is what he said to them: “Some men said, ‘The bull smells good; he is beautiful,’ but then some others said, ‘The young steer is beautiful; he smells good,’ and so they quarrelled. On this account they were getting quite angry. ‘Just wait a bit, while I go look at them to find out which smells better,’ said I, and so I have come to see you,” he spoke to deceive those buffalos.
tâpwê tâpwêhtam awa mostos. ||| The buffalos really believed him.
êkwa tâhkinêw; ômisi isi miyâhtam ocihciy; kotaka mîna ôhi ôtê. ||| So he touched one; he smelled his hand like this; and then the other one.
ômisi itêw: "kiya kiwîhkimâkosin; kiya kimiyosin," itêw iyâpêsisa. ||| He said to him, “You, you smell good; you, you are handsome,” he said to the young steer.
miywêyihtam iyâpêsis ê-miyosit, ê-itêyihtahk. ||| The steer was glad to think himself beautiful.
omôhkomân tahkamêw watâyihk. ||| He stabbed him in the belly with his knife.
tânita kê-wîhkimâkosit!" "ninôhtêhkatêwâh!" ||| How should he smell good? It is hungry I was!”
nipahêw; nipiw awa iyâpêsis. ||| He killed it; the young steer died.
êkosi ê-pahkisiniyit, ê-nipiyit, itohtêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| So when it fell down dead, Wisahketchahk walked up to it.
êkwa nika-mîcison," itwêw. ||| Now I shall eat,” he said.
êkwa wiyanihêw, ê-pahkwêkiswât. ||| Then he cut it up, stripping off the hide with his knife.
êkwa ômisi itwêw wîsahkêcâhk: "wiyin nika-ayân," itwêw. ||| Then thus spoke Wisahketchahk: “I shall have the fat meat,” he said.
ôma ospiton, wîsahkêcâhk ospiton"namôya!" itwêw, "niya nika-ayân wiyin," itwêw. ||| His arm, Wisahketchahk's one arm, said, “No! It is I shall have the fat meat,” it said.
kotak ospiton: "namôya! ||| His other arm said, “No!
êkosi pîkiskwêwak, tâpiskôc nisto ayîsiyiniwak, ê-pêyakot wîsahkêcâhk. ||| So they spoke, as if they were three persons, though there was only Wisahketchahk.
kisiwâsiw âsay awa; awa mîna kisiwâsiw. ||| The one had already grown angry; now the other, too, got into a rage.
"namôya kika-ayân wiyin; niya niwî-ayân." ||| “You shan't have the fat meat! I, I shall have it!”
wîsahkêcâhk ômisi pîkiskwêw: "êkâ wiya, nisîmitik!" "konita kiwî-kisiwâsinâwâw wiyâs ohci." ||| Wisahketchahk spoke thus: “Don't, little brothers! Needlessly you are growing angry over this meat.”
ohcitaw ê-âsponisit." ||| He simply insists on being selfish.”
"â, êkâya nânitaw itwê!" "kika-tahkamitin." ||| “Oh, keep still! I'll stab you.”
"â, nîsta ka-tahkamitin." ||| “Oho, it's I who will stab you.”
namôya ta-miywâsin ta-nipahitoyêk wiyâs ohci." ||| It wouldn't do for you two to kill each other for the sake of this meat.”
konita mâka kisiwâsiw. ||| But he got into a foolish rage.
môhkomân ômisi tahkamêw; ôma ospiton tahkahtam. ||| With his knife he stabbed him like this; he stabbed that arm of his.
kwêski miyisôw ômisi môhkomân. ||| Across to the other side he handed himself the knife, like this.
kotak mîna ospiton tahkahtam. ||| He stabbed his other arm, too.
êkosi êkwa pahkihtin môhkomân; nipahêw ospitona. ||| And so then the knife fell down; he had killed his arms.
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk nîpawiw, ospitona ômisi. ||| There stood Wisahketchahk, with his arms like this.
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk namôya mîcisôw; sipwêhtêw; nakatam wiyâs. ||| And Wisahketchahk did not eat; he went away; he left the meat.
ayis ospitona âhkosiw; nipiyiwa ospitona; namôya kî-miciminam môhkomân. ||| For he was sick in his arms; in fact, his arms had died; he was not able to hold a knife.
êkosi êwako âtayôhkêwin. ||| Thus goes this sacred story.
kîtahtawê ê-pimohtêt wîsahkêcâhk,- nôhtêhkatêw mâka mîna,- ê-pimohtêt, kâ-wâpamât sîsîpa, êkwa niska mihcêt, sîsîpa. ||| Once upon a time, as Wisahketchahk was tramping along as usual he was hungry as he was tramping along, he saw some ducks and many geese, ducks.
êkosi ômisi itêyihtam: "tânisi ka-isi-nipahakik?" itêyihtam. ||| Then this was what he thought: “How shall I kill them?” he thought.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpahtahk sâkahikanis, êkota sisonê nipîhk kâ-wâpahtahk asisiya. ||| Presently he saw a little lake, and by the water's edge some weeds.
otinam, ê-titipinahk. ||| He took them and rolled them up.
mistahi tahkopitam, ê-nayahtahk, ê-sipwêhtêt. ||| He tied up a great bundle of them, took it on his back, and went off.
sîsîpa ita kâ-ayâyit, êkota cîki ê-pimohtêt, kâ-wâpamikot sîsîpa. ||| When he came walking close to where the ducks were, they caught sight of him.
ômisi itwêwak sîsîpak: "hâ, kistêsinaw!" itwêwak; "kêkway kâ-nayahtahk?" êkosi itwêwak. ||| The ducks said, “Ho, our big brother! What is that he's carrying on his back?” they said.
"mahti nika-kakwêcimâw," itwêw awa sîsîp. ||| “Suppose I ask him,” said one duck.
"nistêsê, kîkway kâ-nayahtaman?" ||| “Big brother, what is that you're carrying on your back?”
âhci piko pimohtêw; tâpiskôc êkâ ê-pêhtawât, âhci piko pimohtêw. ||| He kept right on walking; just as if he had not heard, he kept on walking.
âsay mîna sîsîp ômisi itêw: "nistêsê, kîkway kâ-nayahtaman?" ||| Again the duck asked him, “Big brother, what is it you're carrying on your back?”
êkoyikohk nîpawiw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Only then did Wisahketchahk stand still.
"mâ," itwêw, "kîkway kâ-nayahtaman?" ||| “Say,” it said, “what is it you're carrying?”
"wâ, pasakwâpisimôwina!" itwêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “Why, Shut-Eye Dances!” said Wisahketchahk.
"kêkway pasakwâpisimôwin?" itwêw sîsîp. ||| “What is a Shut-Eye Dance?” said the duck.
wîsahkêcâhk ômisi itwêw: "nîminâna," itêw. ||| Wisahketchahk spoke thus: “A saltatory rite,” he told the other.
"nîmihinân," itwêw sîsîp; "nika-pasakwâpisimonân!" ||| “Do you give us a dance,” said the duck; “Let us dance the Shut-Eye Dance!”
"hay hay!" itwêw wîsahkêcâhk; "â, miywâsin ê-kitimâkinawiyêk, nisîmitik!" "nama awiyak nitâpwêhtâkoh, tê-nîmihitocik, kayâs ê-kî-asotamân ta-nîmihitôwinihkêyân," itwêw wîsahkêcâhk; "êkosi pê-kapâk." ||| “Splendid!” cried Wisahketchahk; “Oh, it is fine that you have taken pity on me, little brothers! No one has given heed to me until now, and danced, when long ago I had pledged myself to give a ritual dance,” said Wisahketchahk; “So then, come ashore.”
ta-sipwêhtêwak êkwa sîsîpak mîna niskak. ||| Off went the ducks and geese.
ômisi itwêw wîsahkêcâhk: "maci-kakêpâtisak, ninôhtêhkatêwâh!" "mistahi nika-mîcison!" itêyihtam wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Thus spoke Wisahketchahk: “Hopeless ninnies, I've been starving! I shall have a big meal!” thought Wisahketchahk.
ê-apit, êkota takohtêyiwa. ||| They came to where he sat.
"â, âstamitik, nisîmitik!" itwêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “Ha, come here, little brothers!” said Wisahketchahk.
êkwa ê-sipwêhtêt, ê-sakâyik ê-itohtêt, mihta ita ê-mihcêniyiki, êkota takohtêw. ||| Setting out and making for a clump of trees, he came to where there was plenty of wood for a fire.
"hâ, nisîmitik, otinamok mihta," itwêw. ||| “Ha, little brothers, take up some faggots,” he said.
tâpwê otinamwak mihcêt, êkwa ê-osihtâcik wîkiwâw, êkota ê-apahkwêcik ôho asisiya. ||| Accordingly they took up a plenty and built themselves a lodge, which they thatched with those weeds.
apisâsiniyiw iskwâhtêmis. ||| The little doorway was very small.

wêskwâhtêmihk êkosi ômisi itapiyiwa, êyakonik niskak. ||| Accordingly these, the geese, sat like this, at the far end, facing the door.
nêtê iskwâhtêmihk, êyakonik ê-apisîsisicik êkota apiwak. ||| Over at the other end, by the door sat the little fellows.
êkwa kipaham ôma iskwâhtêm awa wîsahkêcâhk, "êkâ ka-wayawîcik," ê-itêyihtahk. êkwa mâtôw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Then that Wisahketchahk blocked up the doorway, thinking “So that they can't get out.” Then Wisahketchahk wept.
"nisîmitik, kinanâskomitinâwâw, ê-kîsihtâyêk ôma mîkiwâhp." "êkâ awiyak ê-kitimâkinawit, kiyawâw kâ-kitimâkinawiyêk," itwêw, ê-mâtot. ||| “Little brothers, I thank you for having built this lodge. When no one took pity on me, it was you who pitied me,” he spoke, weeping.

"kîspin manitôw nipêcimâw, 'hweh hweh hweh!' nika-itwân;" "êkota sôhki ka-nîmihitonâwâw, pêhtawiyêko, êkosi itwêyâni." ||| Thus spoke Wisahketchahk: “Now, little brothers, here in the centre I shall stand; I shall sing. When I sing, you will dance; [sic] you will close your eyes. Not until I cease singing will you open your eyes. When I summon the spirit-power, I shall say, ‘Hwe, hwe, hwe!’ then you will dance with all your might, when you hear me call thus.
êkwa mistik tahkonam wîsahkêcâhk, nîpiya ê-kayâsâyiwiyiki ê-takopitêyiki, ômisi ê-isiwêpinahk, ê-sêwêpayiyiki, tâpiskôc sasawihyâkan, ôhi nîpiya. ||| Then Wisahketchahk took hold of a branch that had old leaves on it which rustled when he swung it, like this, just like a bell, those leaves.
ômisi itwêw: "pasakwâpisimôwina nipêciwitân!" êkosi itwêw, ê-nikamot. ||| These were his words: “Shut-Eye Dances I bring here!” were the words of his song.

êkosi ê-ati-wâsakâmêt, tahki ê-nikamot, ê-ati-kîskikwêpitât niska ôhi mîna sîsîpa kâ-misikitiyit. ||| In this way he kept on circling round, singing all the while, and, as he went, wringing the necks of the geese and of the big ducks.
nêtê iskwâhtêmihk ê-nîmihitot sihkihp, êwako ê-pêhtahk kêkway, ê-napatê-tôhkâpit, ê-nîmihitot, kâ-wâpamât wîsahkêcâhkwa ê-ati-nipahâyit. ||| Over yonder by the door danced Hell-Diver, and when he heard something or other, and opened one eye as he danced, there he saw Wisahketchahk killing one after another.
"îyahâ!" itwêw, "mâka mîna kimêscihikonaw wîsahkêcâhk!" itwêw. ||| “Yah!” he cried, “It's the same old story, Wisahketchahk is killing us off!”
ê-tôhkâpicik kotakak, ômisi itwêw wîsahkêcâhk: "kêkway ôma ita kê-pêtâyân nîmihitôwin, kakêpâtisicik?" wayawîyâmowak kotakak, ê-tapasîcik. ||| They fled out of doors, the others, trying to get away.
êkosi wayawîw wîsahkêcâhk, ê-pâhpit, ê-miywêyihtahk, "mistahi nika-mîcison," ê-itêyihtahk. êkosi pîkonam ôma wîki, ôhi mihta ê-otinahk, ê-kotawêt, ôhi ê-wî-nawacît nîpin-âya. ||| Thereupon Wisahketchahk went out of the lodge, laughing and rejoicing, thinking, “I shall eat a plenty.” So then he tore up that lodge of his, taking the faggots and building a fire to roast those summer creatures.
êkosi ê-nawacît, kahkiyaw nawacîw. ||| He roasted them whole.
êkosi osâm mistahi ê-pônahk, apwêsiw. ||| Having made too big a fire, he began to feel hot.

tâpwê wâhyawês ê-itohtêt, kâ-wâpamât mahkêsîsa ê-wîsakêyihtamiyit oskâtiyiw, ê-watiskâyit, êkâ ê-kî-pimohtêyit, ê-wî-tapasîhikot. ||| And so when he had walked a little ways, there he saw Fox, who had a pain in his leg, and was limping and could not walk properly, as he tried to run away from him.
"cêskwa, nisîm!" itêw. ||| “Wait a moment, little brother!” he called to him.
"wâ, namôya" itik; "osâm mâka mîna nânitaw kiwî-tôtawin," itik. ||| “Dear me, no!” the other answered; “You are only going to play me some new trick,” he said to him.

"êkota mihcêt ninipahâwak niskak mîna sîsîpak, êkota ê-nawacîyân," ê-itât; "mistahi ka-mîcisonânaw," itêw; "mâka pita ka-kakwê-nakatonânaw." "nêma wâhyaw kâ-ispatinâ-k êwako ka-têtipêwêpahtânânaw." ||| “Over there I have killed a lot of geese and ducks, and there I am roasting them,” he told him; “We shall have plenty to eat,” he told him; “But first let us race. Let us run around that hill not far from here.”
kiwâpamin êkâ ê-kî-pimohtêyân, ê-wîsakêyihtamân niskât," itwêw mahkêsîs. ||| You see I can't walk, with my sore leg,” said Fox.
ômisi itwêw wîsahkêcâhk: "asiniyak niskâtihk nika-tahkopitâwak," itwêw. ||| Wisahketchahk spoke thus: “I shall tie stones to my leg,” he said.

asiniya otinêw wîsahkêcâhk, ê-tahkopitât oskâtihk. ||| Wisahketchahk took some stones and tied them to his leg.

mayaw ê-âkawêwêt wîsahkêcâhk, kîwêpayiw awa mahkêsîs, namôya ê-wîsakêyihtahk oskât, ôma kâ-pikihtêyik ê-ispayit. ||| As soon as Wisahketchahk was out of sight behind the hill, that Fox turned back, and his leg was not sore at all, as he made for the rising smoke.

kitamwêw kahkiyaw. ositiyiwa piko ôhi niska êkwa sîsîpa, êkoni piko iskotêhk astâw, "ta-wâpahtahk wîsahkêcâhk," ê-itêyihtah. êkosi tapasîw, "nika-kisiwâhâw," ê-itêyimât wîsahkêcâhkwa. ||| Only the feet of those geese and ducks, only those did he put into the embers, thinking, “Let Wisahketchahk see them.” Then he made for safety, thinking of Wisahketchahk, “He will be angry at me.”
êkwa wîsahkêcâhk iyikohk ê-takohtêt mistahi apwêsiw; ayisk mistahi pimipahtâw. ||| Then, when Wisahketchahk arrived, he was very hot; for he had had quite a run.

namôya wâhyaw ê-ihtât, kâ-wâpamât, ê-na-nipâyit, mitoni ê-mistatayêyit; ayisk kî-kîspoyiwa. ||| He had not gone far, when he saw him taking a nap, his belly all big; for he had eaten a hearty fill.

na-nitohtâk, ôma ê-itât. ||| The other was listening to what he said about him.
êkosi kotawêw, wâsakâm ê-saskahahk maskosiya. ||| So then he made a fire, setting fire the grass round about.
êkwa ê-kwâhkotêyik, waniskâw awa mahkêsîs. ||| When the blaze came, Fox got up.
"heq," wîsahkêcâhk ômisi itwêw; "hiheq, mahti mîna kitamok niniskimak!" itêw. ||| “Ha,” said Wisahketchahk; “Haha, just you eat up my geese again!” he said to him.

piyisk namôya wâpamêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| At last Wisahketchahk could see him no more.
kwâskwêpayihôw awa mahkêsîs, iskotêw ôma ê-pâsici-kwâskohtit, ê-tapasît. ||| Up leaped Fox, jumping across the flame, and making for safety.
namôya wâpamêw wîsahkêcâhk, ê-tapasîyit. ||| Wisahketchahk did not see how he ran away.
piyis misiwê pasitêyiw, êkota ê-wâskâhtêt wîsahkêcâhk. ||| At last there was a big fire, and Wisahketchahk kept walking round it.
"tâpwê nikitimahâw, ê-nipahîhkaswak mahkêsîs," itwêw wîsahkêcâhk; kâ-wâpahtahk pihko ê-astêyik, mostoso-mêy ita ê-kî-astêyik, "tâpwê nikitimâkîhkaswâw!" ê-itwêt; "mahti ka-iskohkasot, nika-môwâw, iskohkasoci," ê-itêyihtah; ôma pihko ê-wî-otinahk, "kâ-kîsisot iskotêw êsa ôma êwako mahkêsîs," ê-itêyihtah, ê-cîsihot. ||| “I have surely put an end to Fox; burning him to death,” said Wisahketchahk; and when he saw the ashes lying, where there had been buffalo-dung, “Surely I have burned him to a sorry end!” said he; “I shall eat what is left of him, if there is any of him left from the fire,” he thought; and he was going to take up the ashes there, thinking, “And this must be Fox, burned up in this fire,” as he deceived himself.
êkoyikohk namôya kiskêyihtam ê-kî-tapasîyit. ||| Even now he did not know that the other had got away.
êkosi êkoyikohk êwako âtayôhkêwin. ||| And so this is the end of this sacred story.
ê-ta-tahkiskawât sihkihpa, "hâw, ôtê nîkân ayîsiyiniw kita-ohpikiw;" "ka-wâpamik ôma kâ-nanâpotôkanêskâtân." "'sihkihp' kika-isiyihkâtikwak." "namôya ka-miyosin;" "osâm kikisiwâhin ê-wîhtaman, ê-tôhkâpiyan," itêw. ||| When he kicked Hell-Diver, “Now then, ahead in future time mortal man will grow up; he will see here on you where I have kicked your rump crooked. ‘Hell-Diver,’ they will call you. You will not be handsome; too much have you angered me by telling this and by opening your eyes,” he told him.
kîtahtawê êsa sa-sipwêhtêw; ayisk misiwê kî-tôtam wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Once upon a time he went from place to place; for Wisahketchahk did all kinds of things.
ahpô kî-kaskihtâw ê-onôtinikêwokimâwit. ||| He even managed to become a captain of soldiers.
kêtahtawê sipwêhtêw êsa. ||| Once upon a time, the story goes, he set out.
kîtahtawê wâskahikan kâ-otihtahk. ||| Presently he came to a wooden house.
"ay, ay-api, ay-api, nistêsê!" ||| “Ha, stay a while, stay a while, big brother!”
nitonikêyiwa iskwêwa, ê-asamikot. ||| A woman looked for something to give him to eat.
hô, namwâc kêkway wâpahtam kita-otinamiyit mîciwin. ||| Ho, he saw nothing at all in the way of food that she could take.
sôskwâc tâpiskwêkanêkinwa otinêyiwa, ôta mîcisowinâhtikohk êsiwêpinâyit. ||| At once she took out a shawl and threw it on the table.
wâpahtam êkota nanâtohk mîciwina. ||| There he saw all kinds of food.
mâka mîna itêyihtam wîsahkêcâhk; "nika-kimotin," itêyihtam. ||| In his usual way, Wisahketchahk thought, “I shall steal it,” he thought.
mâ-mitonêyihtam tânisi ta-isi-nôhtê-nipâyit ôhi ka-pê-kiyokawât. ||| He kept revolving in his mind how he could make his hostesses want to sleep.
ômisi itwêw: "hâw, kiyawâw, nisîmitik, nêwo-tipiskâw kika-âcimostâtinâwâw." ||| He said, “Now, in return, my little sisters, for four nights I will tell you stories.”
"hâ, tâpwê, nistêsê, nimiywêyihtênân ê-âcimohk!" itik ôhi iskwêwa. ||| “Oh, indeed, big brother, we like story-telling!” those women said to him.
nama wîhkâc wâpamêw ta-kîsitêpoyit. ||| He never saw them do any cooking.
"nika-kimotamawâw, nipâci, otâpiskwêkanêkinwa," ê-itêyihtahk êsa wîsahkêcâhk, êkwa âcimôw kapê-tipisk. ||| “When she goes to sleep, I shall steal her shawl from her,” thought Wisahketchahk, and told stories all night.
namôya ohci nipâyiwa. ||| But they did not go to sleep.
âsay mîna kapê-kîsik âcimôw. ||| All the next day he told stories.
kîhtwâm mîna ê-tipiskâyik, âsay mîna kêyâpic namwâc nipâyiwa. ||| When another night came, again they did not sleep at all.
"mâna êkâ nika-kî-kimotamawâhtayik!" ||| “Could it be that I should be unable to steal it from them!” When he had told stories for exactly four nights and days, then those young women went to sleep. He searched where they kept their things; he stole it from them. So then he went off with it; he fled.
nêwo-tipiskâw pimipahtâw. ||| For four days and nights he ran.
êkwa kîtahtawê kâ-pêhtahk ê-matwê-cîkahikêwiht. ||| Then at one time he heard someone noisily chopping wood.
"ohcitaw kika-otihtitin," itêyihtam êsa. ||| “I shall do my best to reach you,” he thought.
âsay mîna ê-wâpaniyik, âhci piko pêhtam. ||| When the next day broke, he still heard it.
êkwa piyisk nêwo-tipiskâw tâpiskôc pêyakwan iyikohk ê-matwê-cîkahikêyit, nêwo-tipiskâw mwêhci ê-pimohtêt, êkoyikohk wâpamêw kîkisêp, ê-matwê-wâskahikanihkêyit. ||| And at last, when he had heard the other chopping away for four days and nights, apparently always at the same distance, and when he had walked four days and nights, then at last, in the morning, he saw him, noisily working at a wooden structure.
namwâc kêkway wâpahtam kita-osîhtâyit mihta, âta nêwo-kîsikâw ê-pêhtahk. ||| He saw no wood at all with which that person could build anything, though he had heard the noise of it for four days.
nîso piko mihta kiyastêyiwa. ||| Only two sticks lay there.
"wâ, nisîm, kayâs ohci, nêwo-tipiskâw aspin, kâ-pêhtamân ê-nikohtêyan!" ||| “Dear me, little brother, for a long time, ever since four nights ago, I have heard you chopping!”
ê-âta-kitotât, namwâc ahpô wî-kitâpamik. ||| Although he spoke to him, the other would not so much as glance at him.
kapê-kîsik piko isi âta ê-isi-kitotât, ahpô namwâc wî-kitâpamik. ||| Although through the day he addressed him in all manner of ways, he would not even look at him.
nitawâc êkwa, ê-wî-tipiskâyik, aspin ê-astâyit cîkahikaniyiw, ê-âta-nawaswâtât, namôya kiskêyimêw ê-pîhtokêyit. ||| And then, at nightfall, when the other laid down his hatchet and was off and away, he needs ran after him, but he could not make out into what place he had disappeared.
namôya miskawêw; wanihêw. ||| He could not find him; he had lost him.
misiwê papâmitâcimôw, "nisîm, kikitimahin!" ê-papâ-itwêt, ê-papâmitâcimot, ê-wî-kakwê-ka-kitotikot, ê-nitawêyihtahk ta-kitotikot. ||| He crawled about, and, “Little brother, you are making me desperate!” he kept crying, to make the other speak to him; desiring to have the other address him.
piyisk êtokê nêstohkwasiw. ||| At last he must have gotten sleepy from weariness.
sâsay mîna kayâhtê ê-waniskât, kî-nâ-nâtwâhinihtêyiwa. ||| When he awoke, there was the other already a-splitting of logs.
âsay mîna kapê-kîsik âta, "nisîm!" piko isi ê-ati-itât, nama wî-ka-kitotik. ||| Again, though all day he kept saying to him, “Little brother!” he would not talk to him.
âsay mîna ê-tipiskâyik, aspin âta ê-kîwêyit, ati-miciminêw; ê-ati-pîhtokêyit wîkiyihk, êkota ohci wanihêw. ||| When the next night came, when the other made off to go home, he held fast to him, but when he went into his dwelling, from that point he lost him.
âsay mîna kapê-tipisk papâmitâcimôw, ê-nitonawât; piyisk mîna mohcihk êkosi isi nipâw. ||| Again he crawled about all night, looking for him; at last he again slept right there on the bare ground.
kîkisêpâ ê-waniskât, âsay mîna kî-nikohtêyiwa mîna kîhtwâm. ||| In the morning, when he got up, this time, too, the other had already started working at his wood.
"anohc êkwa ôhcitaw kika-kitosin!" itêyihtam êsa mâka mîna wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “Now today I will see to it that you talk to me!” thought Wisahketchahk as before.
âsay mîna kapê-kîsik âta ê-kitotât, nama kî-kitotik. ||| Again, though he talked to him all day, he could not make the other address him.
âsay mîna ati-kîwêyiwa. ||| Again the other went home.
mistahi êkwa pakwâtam. ||| He was very much annoyed.
"ahpô ôma!" itêyihtam; "kêhcinaw apiw!" "cîpay êkâ kâ-wî-ka-kitosit!" itêyihtam êsa. ||| “Maybe it is this!” he thought; “Surely he is at home here! He is a dead man, this person who will not converse with me!” he thought.
tâpwê mâhtakoskam oskan, êkota ê-miskahk. ||| Accordingly, he threw his weight on that bone and held it down.
êkwa kîkisêpâ kayâhtê ê-pêkopayit, "awas, wîsahkêcâhk! ||| Then, in the morning he was awakened by the other saying to him, “Get away Wisahketchahk!
nimiywêyihtêh ê-cîkahikêyân!" kâ-itikot, kayâhtê ê-mâtakoskawât. ||| I was having a pleasant time at chopping!” for he was holding him down by the weight of his body.
"cêskwa, nisîm!" itêw; "nisîm, mistahi kikakwâtakihin, âta nêwo-kîsikâw ê-kitotitân, êkâ ê-kitosiyan." ||| “Wait a bit, little brother!” he told him; “Little brother, you were tormenting me terribly, by not talking to me, when for four days I addressed you.”
"hâw, nistêsê," itik, "ôta ê-kî-nipahisoyân," itik; "êwako." ||| “Well, brother,” the other told him, “It is because in this place I killed myself,” he told him; “That is the way of it.”
"tânêhki mâka êkâ kêkway kâ-ôh-kaskihtâyan, tahki ê-nikohtêyan tahto-kîsikâw?" ||| “But why is it you accomplish nothing, when you are always a-chopping every day?”
"ôta kayâs ê-kî-pahkwêkahamân nisit," itik êsa. ||| “It is because of old in this place I chopped off my foot,” the other told him.
"êha," itwêw awa cîpay; "tânitê mâka kî-ohtinamân mîciwin?" itêw wîsahkêcâhkwa. ||| “No,” said the dead man; “Where could I get any food?” he said to Wisahketchahk.
"asamikawiyan cî mâka, kika-mîcison?" ||| “But if you were given something to eat, would you eat?”
"êha, nika-mîcison, kîspin asamiyin," itwêw êsa awa cîpay. ||| “Yes, I would eat, if you gave me food,” said the dead man.
"hâw, nisîm, kika-asamitin!" ||| “Very well, little brother, I shall give you something to eat.”
êkwa ôma kâ-kî-kimotit tâpiskwêkanêkin otinam, ê-taswêkiwêpinahk. ||| Then he took the shawl he had stolen and spread it out.
atôspowinâhtikohk pôti kahkiyaw kêkway wâpahtam. ||| Look you, on a table he saw all kinds of things.
tânispîhk êtokê omîcisohtay awa cîpay! ||| I wonder when that corpse had last eaten!
ayisk wîsahkêcâhk kâ-isiyîhkâsot kahkiyaw awiya kî-wayêsimêw. ||| For he who was called Wisahketchahk deceived everyone.
mistahi nâspic atamihêw ê-asamât. ||| He entirely won him over by giving him the food.
"hâ, mistahi kitatamihin, wîsahkêcâhk, ôma kâ-asamiyan!" ||| “Hah, you greatly oblige me, Wisahketchahk, giving me food like this!”
"hâ, nisîm," itêw, "niya nipapâmâcihon." "nama nânitaw nika-itâpacihtân ôma tâpiskwêkanêkin." "kiya nama nânitaw ka-kî-ohtinamâson ta-mîciyan," itêw ôhi cîpaya. ||| “Oh, little brother,” he told him, “as for me, I am travelling about. I shall not have any use for this shawl. But you would not have any resource from which to get anything to eat,” he told the dead man.
"êha," itwêw awa cîpay, "mistahi kitatamihin, wîsahkêcâhk!" "êkwa nama wîhkâc nika-nôhtêhkatân, wîsahkêcâhk." "mahti nimistikowatihk osâwi-sôniyâw êkota miskawaci, otinâhkan," itwêw awa cîpay. ||| “Yes,” said the dead man, “I thank you very much, Wisahketchahk! Now I shall never be hungry, Wisahketchahk. Go see; if you find any gold in my wooden box, just take it,” said the corpse.
tâpwê wîsahkêcâhk ê-sîhkimiht, nitonikêw osâwi-sôniyâwa. ||| According [sic] as he was bidden, Wisahketchahk looked for gold.
"wîsahkêcâhk, kakwê-iyinîsi mâka! âta wiya kimôhcôwin." "ôta kwêski-sakâhk namôya wâhyaw okimâw mêkwâ kwâpahwêw sôniyâwa." "êwako ki-ka-itohtân." "ki-ka-na-nitawâpamâw." "ômisi kika-itâw: 'niyanân tâpwê miyosiw kâ-kwâpahwâyâhk osâwi-sôniyâw,' kika-itâw;" "'kiya mistahi mâyâtisiw.'" "'kêkâc pisisik nipiy kikwâpahên,' kika-itâw;" "'niyanân osâwi-sôniyâw pisisik nikwâpahwâw,' kika-itâw;" "'êkwa kiya kêkâc pisisik nipiy kikwâpahên.'" "'nawac ita sôniyâw kâ-ohtinak kîsta pê-itohtêyan,' kika-itâw." "êkwa wâhyaw pê-itohtahaci, kika-nipahâw." "'kâ-isinâkosit awa okimâw, êkosi nika-wî-isinâkosin!' kika-itwân." "itâp ka-naspitawâw." ||| “But, Wisahketchahk, be sensible! After all, you are a crazy fellow. At the other side of these woods a chief is now digging gold. You will go where he is. You will go see him. You will say to him, ‘The gold we others are digging is really fine,’ you will say to him; ‘Yours is very poor. You are scooping up almost nothing but water,’ you will say to him; ‘But as for us others, I scoop up pure gold,’ you will say to him; ‘And you, you are scooping up almost nothing but water. You had better come over yourself to where I get gold,’ you will tell him. And when you have led him far off, you will kill him. ‘As the chief looked, so I shall look!’ you will say. Then you will resemble him completely.”
êkosi sipwêhtêw, ê-kî-kakêskimikot wîsahkêcâhk ôhi cîpaya, êkwa okimâwa ê-wî-nitawi-nipahât. ||| Then Wisahketchahk set out, as he had been directed by the dead man, to go and kill that chief.
tâpwê namôya wâhyaw ê-itohtêt, sîpîsis otihtam, ê-mêkwâ-kwâpahwâyit sôniyâwa. ||| And really, he had not gone far, when he came to a brook where the latter was digging for gold.
"tâpwê kiya mistahi mâyâtisiw sôniyâw kâ-kwâpahwat," itwêw wîsahkêcâhk; "êkwa niyanân mistahi miyosiw sôniyâw;" "osâwi-sôniyâw piko nitotinânân." ||| “Truly, the metal you are digging up is very poor,” Wisahketchahk told him; “But our metal is very fine; we get nothing but gold.”
"tânitê mâka mahti?" itik; "itohtahin." "mahti nika-nitawâpahtên," itik. ||| “Now, where is that, pray?” the other asked him; “Take me there.
kêkway â wâpahtêhêw. ||| Let me go see it,” he told him.
"niyanân osâwi-sôniyâw piko nitotinânân," itik. ||| He showed him some. “We get nothing but gold,” he told him.
êkwa tâpwê sipwêhtahêw; ita ê-âyimaniyik ati-ay-itohtahêw. ||| So then he led him away; he led him on into rough places.
êkwa wâhyaw ê-ayâcik, mistikwa nîso ê-cimasoyit, êkota ê-sêkoyit, ostikwâniyihk pakamahwêw; nipahêw. ||| Then, when they had gone quite a ways, as the other got between two trees that stood close, he hit him on the head and killed him.
"êkosi nika-wî-naspitawâw awa okimâw!" itwêw êsa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “So now I want to resemble this chief!” said Wisahketchahk.
tâpwê, ayisk wîcihik ôhi cîpaya; tâpwê naspitawêw êsa ôhi okimâwa. ||| And really, for he was being helped by that Deadman, really, he looked exactly like the chief.
"êkwa mahti sêmâk nika-kîwân." "mahti êsinâkosiyit wîwa," itêyihtam. ||| “Now I shall go straight home. Let me see what his wife looks like,” he thought.
aciyaw piko kwâpahwêw sôniyâwa. ||| He dug for gold but for a short while.
wawêyîw; êkosi isi kîwêw. ||| He dressed up; right then he went home.
wâhyaw ohci pêtisâpamik ôhi kâ-nipahât wîwiyiwa. ||| From afar the wife of him whom he had killed saw him coming.
"tânisi kâ-ôh-pê-kîwêyan nama wîhkâc nôhtaw kipê-kîwân." "iyikohk nîsosâp tipahikan mâna kâ-pê-âpihta-kîsikâw-mîcisoyan." "mistahi kîtahtawê kimôhcôwin!" ||| “Why are you coming home? You never come home before the regular time. It is always twelve o'clock that you come home to eat dinner. You are acting very crazily, all of a sudden!”
âta wiya êsa nisitohtawêw. ||| He did somehow understand what she was saying.
êkwa êkosi isi kîwêw. ||| So he went right back.
mîna nitawi-itohtêw. ||| He went back where he had come from.
aciyaw pê-otihtik ôhi kâ-kî-kiskinôhamâkot cîpaya. ||| Soon the Deadman who had instructed him came to where he was.
"kêhcinâ wîpac kika-nipahikawin!" "osâm mistahi pakahkam kiwî-môhcôwin!" "namwâc ahpô kikiskêyimâw pîsimôhkân!" itik. ||| “Certainly you will soon get yourself killed! It is evident that you will act too crazily! You do not even know the clock!” he told him.
êkwa wâpamêw pîsimôhkâna, êkwayâk kâ-nisitawêyimât. ||| Then he looked at a clock, making his first acquaintance with it.
êkwa kîwêw, nîsosâp tipahikan ê-ispayiyik. ||| Then he went home, when twelve o'clock had come.
âsay mîna nitawi-atoskêw, mîna ê-nitawâpamât sôniyâwa. ||| Then he went back to work, to look for gold.
êkwa wîpac pôni-atoskêw. ||| He quite work after a short time.
"tâpwê kîtahtawê mistahi kimôhcôwin," itik ôhi owîkimâkana, "êkwa wâh-wîpac ê-pê-kîwêyan!" itik. ||| “Really, all of a sudden you have gone altogether insane,” that wife of his said to him, “Coming home early all the time like this!”
"hâh," ômisi itwêw; "kîtahtawê wâh-wîpac kêkway niwâh-wani-kiskisin," itwêw. ||| “Why,” he said, “my memory has become very short, all of a sudden.”
êkwa ê-otâkosiniyik, masinahikan kâ-pîhtokatâyit. ||| Then, in the evening someone brought in a letter.
kâ-kiskisit anihi cîpaya kâ-kî-kitimâkêyimikot, êkwa wayawîw. ||| Remembering that Deadman who had befriended him, he went out of the house.
"wahwa, mistahi kimôhcôwin!" itik; "êkosi êcika ana wîpac kê-nipahikawiyan!" ||| “Alas, you are a crazy fool!” he told him; “And so it appears you will soon be killed!”
sâ-sâminamiyiwa ohkwâkana, oskîsikwa, otôn: nisitawinam masinahikan. ||| The other touched his face, his eyes and his mouth: he could read.
êkwa ê-wâpahtahk, masinahikâtêyiw, wâpahki ê-wî-pê-nôtiniht; ayisk onôtinikêwa ôhi okimâwa kâ-nipahât, êkwa wâh-wîpac êsa mâna ê-pê-nôtinimiht. ||| Then, when he read it, it was written that tomorrow people were coming to fight him; for that chief he had killed had been at war, and had been attacked, it seemed, every little while.
masinahikêw; âcimostawêw otiyinîma. ||| He wrote; he told his followers the news.
tâpwê, "wawêyîk, iyinitik." "kiwî-pê-nôtinikonânaw wâpahki." "nipêyitisahamâkawin," itêw, "masinahikana." ||| “Get yourselves ready, men. Tomorrow they are coming to fight us. Letters have been sent to me.”
tâpwê kîkisêpâ takohtêyiwa kâ-pê-nitopayîstâkocik. ||| And really, in the morning they arrived who were coming to make war against them. But as for Wisahketchahk, of course, he merely looked on in his useless way.
mâka wiya wîsahkêcâhk mâka mîna ka-kitâpahkêw konita. ||| Presently that woman said to him, “Truly, you are entirely foolish! Your men will all be killed,” she told him; “You ought to order your clothes to be taken out for you to put on, and your horse to be saddled.”
tâpwê wîsahkêcâhk sîhkihkêmôw otêma ta-wiyahpitimiht. ||| So Wisahketchahk ordered his horse to be saddled.
postayôwinisêw; nitawi-nôtinikêw. ||| He put on his clothes; he went and fought.
mistahi mâka mîna môhcôhkâsôw. ||| Of course he carried on in a crazy way.
kahkiyaw êsa mêscihêw ôhi kâ-pê-nôtinikêyit. ||| He killed all those who had come to fight.
êkosi pêyak piko kîwêtisahwêw, masinahikan ê-kî-osihtât. ||| He sent only one back home, having written a letter.
nêtê ê-takohtatâcik, ômisi itwêwak otiyinîsiwak: "mâka mîna êtokê wîsahkêcâhk!" itwêwak. ||| When he arrived over there, the wise men said, “Doubtless this is Wisahketchahk, up to his old tricks!”
masinahikan osîhtâw: "kîspin kiya wîsahkêcâhk, kiwî-nipahitin sôskwâc." "osâm misiwê kitisîhcikân." ||| He wrote a letter: “If you are Wisahketchahk, I shall kill you without delay. You are cutting up altogether too much.”
pôti êkwa ê-pêtamâht wîsahkêcâhk, ayamihtâw. ||| When it was brought to Wisahketchahk he read it.
"kiya êtokê mâka mîna, wîsahkêcâhk, ôma kâ-tôtaman," itâw. ||| “Doubtless it is you, Wisahketchahk, up to your old tricks, who are doing all this,” he was told.
tapasîw; namôya ahpô awiya wâpahtêhêw ôma masinahikan; êkosi isi ê-isi-tapasît. ||| He fled; he did not even show anyone this letter; he fled just as he was, at once.
nêwo-tipiskâw pimâmôw. ||| He ran four days and nights.
kîtahtawê ê-misâyik sâkahikan ê-otihtahk, "êkosi kâ-kî-ititân, 'wîsahkêcâhk mâka mîna êtokê kiya,' kâ-kî-ititân," itik ayîsiyiniwa, ê-nakiskawât sisonê sâkahikanihk; "hâw, wîsahkêcâhk, ka-mêtawânânaw!" itik. ||| Then, when he came to a big lake, “I told you so, ‘Doubtless you are Wisahketchahk, up to your old tricks,’ I told you,” said a man to him, whom he met by the shore of the lake; “Now, Wisahketchahk, let us have a contest!” he said to him.
êkwa tâpwê kakwêcimêw tânisi kita-isi-mêtawêcik. ||| So he asked him in what way they were to contend.
"waskic nipîhk ka-pimohtânânaw," itik. ||| “We shall walk on the surface of the water,” the other told him. “Very well,” said Wisahketchahk.
tâpwê ati-sipwêhtêw awa wîsahkêcâhkwa kâ-mawinêhwât. ||| Accordingly he started out who had challenged Wisahketchahk.
namwâc ahpô wayiskam nipiy. ||| He did not even ripple the water as he stepped.
akâmihk ê-kî-takohtêt, êkotê ohci têpwâtêw wîsahkêcâhkwa. ||| When he reached the other side, from there he shouted to Wisahketchahk.
"haw, mwêhci tâwakâm ayâci wîsahkêcâhk, êkota nitawi-kihtâpayiw;" "mâka namôya niwî-nipahâw." "êkota nipîhk ta-mêcimwâci-nahapiw!" ||| “Now, when Wisahketchahk is right in the middle of the water, he will sink under water; but I do not mean to kill him. Let him sit down there for good, there in the water!”
tâpwê itâmi-nipîhk êkotê nahapiw, itamihk nipîhk. ||| And really, there he sat down, under water.
kahkiyaw kêkway ê-atotât, nama wiya tâpwêhtâk. ||| When he called every kind of being to help him, they did not heed him.
kahkiyaw, "nikostânân kâ-tôtâsk," itik. ||| Everyone told him, “We fear him who is doing this to you.”
kîtahtawê mâkwa kâ-têpêyimot kita-otinât wîsahkêcâhkwa. ||| At last the loon consented to take Wisahketchahk from where he was.
kîtahtawê wîsahkêcâhk, "hah, mahti nika-osîhtân; osâm kîtahtawê nikâ-mâkohikon kêkway," itêyihtam. ||| Once upon a time Wisahketchahk thought, “Well, suppose I make some arrows; sometime something or other will drive me to close quarters.”
osîhtâw misâskwat; osîhtâw acosisa. ||| He prepared a saskatoon willow; he made some arrows.
"kêkway kê-kînikâk êkota kita-astâyân," itêyihtam. ||| “I ought to put something sharp on here,” he thought.
kîtahtawê miskam mistik, mihta ôma tâpiskôc. ||| Presently he found a stick of wood, like this faggot here.
napakihtak osîhtâw; tâpihtitâw mihcêt. ||| He made flat slivers of wood; he put them as tips on many arrows.
"êkosi!" itêyihtam; "nika-ôh-minahon kita-mîcisoyân," itêyihtam; "â, kîsâc mîna câpihcikanis nika-osîhtân;" "êwako mîna nika-osîhtân," itwêw. ||| “There!” he thought; “With these I shall kill game and have something to eat,” he thought; “Why, to be the better prepared, I shall make also a spear; this too I shall make,” he said.
ê-kîsihtât, "â, mîna napakihkomân nika-osîhtân;" "osâm miywâsin awa mistik kita-ôh-osîhtâyân," itêyihtam. ||| When he had finished it, “Why, I shall make a broad-bladed knife, too; for this piece of wood is very good to make it of,” he thought.
osîhtâw môhkomân, napakihkomân. ||| He made a knife, a broad-bladed knife.
êkwa ê-wâpahtahk onîmâskwâkana, "pitanê môskîstawit, môskîstâkawiyân!" itêyihtam; "osâm miywâsinwa ninîmâskwâkana;" "nama kêkway nika-kostên," itêyihtam. ||| Then, when he looked upon his weapons, “I just wish he I just wish someone would attack me!” he thought; “For my weapons are very good; I shan't be afraid of anything,” he thought.
ê-kî-kîsihtât, sipwêhtêw. ||| When he had finished them, he started out.
pasahcâhk akâmihk êkotê wâpamêw wâkayôsa. ||| At the other side of a ravine he saw a bear.
hâ, kiskêyihtam ê-macihtwâyit. ||| Ha, he knew him for an ugly customer.
"â, nika-kisîmâw, têpwâtak; êkosi nika-nipahâw; nika-mowâw," itêyihtam. ||| “Ho, I shall make him angry by calling to him; then I shall kill him; I shall eat him,” he thought.
êkwa ômisi itêw: "awêna nâha?" têpwêw, "kâ-wâpikiskicêt!" ||| Then he called to him: “Who is that creature over there?” he shouted, “That white-rumped one!”
ê-pêhtahk awa wâkayôs, kisîmâw. ||| When the bear heard that, he was angered.
"mahti tânitê kâ-têpwêhk!" itêyihtam. ||| “Let me see from where this shouting comes!” he thought.
kîhtwâm ê-mônahikêyit, "mahti nika-kakwê-wâpamâw awa kâ-isit," itêyihtam. êkwa sîpâ ômisi tôtam, ê-wâtihkêt; ôtê osâpiw. ||| When the other was back at his digging, he thought, “Let me try and see him who is saying this to me.” Then down underneath there, he did like this, as he dug his pit; from here he looked forth.
pôti kâ-pimi-sâkiskwêt. ||| Sure enough, there he was, sticking out his head.
"awîna nâha kâ-wâpikiskicêt!" itêw. ||| “Who is that white-rump over there? Pshaw!” he called to him.
hâw, wâpamêw ayîsiyiniwa; môskîstawêw. ||| Well, he saw a man; he made for him.
êkwa awa wîsahkêcâhk pîmakâmêpitêw opîhtatwâna. ||| Then that Wisahketchahk pulled round his quiver by the strap.
kisiwâk ôta ê-pê-nakiyit, pimwêw. ||| When the other came to a halt close by, he shot an arrow at him.
nâtwâhtin ôma mistik. ||| That stick of wood fell broken as it struck.
wîpisisa piyisk mêstinam. ||| Soon he used up all his arrows.
"êha, kâ-pa-pêyakonîmâskwêwinêhk kî-ayîhtiyân, ka-kî-wawânihih!" itêw. ||| “Yes, yes, if I were the kind of person who carries only one weapon, you would be the finish of me!” he called to him.
otinam câpihcikanis; tahkamêw. ||| He took his spear; he jabbed at him.
ê-tahkamiht awa wâkayôs, "mam!" itwêw. ||| When the bear was hit with the spear, “Mum!” he went.
"kâ-pa-pêyakonîmâskwêwinêhk kî-ayîhtiyân, ka-kî-wawânihih!" itêw. ||| “If I were the kind of person who carries only one weapon, you would be the finish of me!” he told him.
tahkamêw ôma ohci napakihkomân mistik kâ-kî-osihtât; nâtwâhtiniyiw. ||| He made a stab at him with that flat knife which he had made out of a piece of wood; it broke lengthwise under the impact.
êkosi êkwa sêkihik, "manitôwiw!" ê-itêyihtahk. "nika-nipahik!" itêyihtam; "nicawâc nika-tapasîn," ê-nâtâmototahk ita ê-sakâyik. ||| At this, he grew afraid of the other, thinking, “He is supernatural!” “He will kill me!” he thought; “I had better run away,” and he headed in panic for the woods.
mitoni kisiwâk askôk, ê-tâwatiyit. ||| The other was close at his heels, with gaping jaws.
iyâpasâpici, kisiwâk askôk. ||| Whenever he glanced back, the other was close upon him.
nîpisiya ê-asaskitêyiki, êkota itâmôw. ||| He fled to where some willows stood in a clump.
êkwa kâsispôkocin awa wâkayôs. ||| The bear just missed as he jumped.
têtipêwêpayihôw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk dashed round the trees.
kapê-kîsik êkota wâsakâmêtisahok. ||| All day long the other chased him round and round.
kîtahtawê nêyawapitwâwi, âyîtaw nîpawîstâtôwak. ||| Presently whenever the were out of breath, they would stand facing each other, at either side.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpamât êskana, ita kâ-pâh-pimipahtât êkota ê-môskatâwahkiskawât. ||| Then at one time, he saw a horm from over which he had kicked loose the ground as he ran by.

"pakahkam awa wâkayôs kostêw," itêyihtam awa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “Plainly this bear is afraid of it,” thought Wisahketchahk.
awa mîna wâkayôs nayawapiw. ||| The bear, too, was out of breath.
nicawâc tahkiskawêw wîsahkêcâhk ôhi kâ-kostimiht êskana. ||| Wisahketchahk tried kicking that horm, which was an object of fear.
piyisk pahkwaciwêpiskawêw. ||| At last he knocked it lose with his foot, as he passed.
nicawâc ê-wîmâskawâyit, "kostêw!" itêyihtam awa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| When the other with plain intent made a circuit round it, “He is afraid of it!” thought Wisahketchahk.
"pakahkam awa kostêw!" itêyihtam. ||| “Plainly he fears it!” he thought.
nicawâc ostikwânihk akonêw, ômisi ê-itât ôhi wâkayôsa: "hwhw!" ê-itât, kâ-wâki-kwâskohtiyit. ||| He tried holding it on his head and saying “Hwoo!” to the bear, and there, the latter jumped off at an angle.
"mahti nika-môskîstawâw! nayawapiw!" ê-itêyimât. ||| “When he thought of the other, “Suppose I go for him!
môskîstawêw; tapasîyiwa. ||| He is tired!” he attacked him; the other ran away.
iyâpasâpiyici ôhi wâkayôsa, kisiwâk askôwêw, "hwhw!" ê-itât. ||| Whenever the bear glanced back, he was close upon him, saying, “Hwoo!”
êkosi mâna wî-kakwê-mîhkawikiw. ||| So he tried to run faster and faster.
piyisk wâpamêw wîsahkêcâhk ôhi wâkayôsa, pîstêw otôniyihk ê-ohcikawiyik. ||| At last Wisahketchahk saw the foam dripping from the bear's mouth.
piyisk awa wâkayôs, "kiyâm nika-wêpahok!" itêyihtam. ||| At last the bear thought, “Well, he might as well toss me on his horn!”
kawipayihôw êkwa awa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| And the bear threw himself flat on the ground.
ohtiskawapîstawêw ômisi ê-itinât êskana, ê-wî-nipahatâhtamiyit, mayaw kâ-itâpamikoci, "whw!" ê-nimisîwihât. ||| He sat down facing him, holding out the horn at him, like this, while the other was almost dead, puffing for want of breath, and every time the other looked at him, he threatened him, going “Hwoo!”
"pakahkam kostêw!" itêyihtam; "namôya awa wîhkâc ta-waniskâw, nakatimaki ôhi nitêskana," itêyihtam. ||| “Plainly he is afraid of it!” he thought; “He will never get up, if I leave this horn of mine here,” he thought.
mistahi kititêyimison, ayîsiyiniw miyâkohaci." "nîsta nitayân kêkway kita-ôh-nipahitân." ||| You think a great deal of yourself, when you drive a man to close quarters. But I, too, have something with which I can kill you.”
tâwatiw wâkayôs, ispî ê-pê-itisinimiht ôhi êskana, wîpita ê-sâmahamoht. ||| The bear had his mouth gaping, and the horn was stuck out at him till it touched his teeth.
"cacêmâsinwa ôhi kîpita!" itêw wîsahkêcâhk. ||| “Those teeth of yours are very short!” Wisahketchahk told him.
"hâw, nitêskan, wêpahwâhkan awa cacêmapicîs wâkayôs!" "wêpahwâhkan, mayaw waskawîci ôta ohci." "kanawêyim ta-waskawît." "konita nôtamihik;" "nikiyôtêwâh!" "mêyâkwâm, nitêskan;" "kinisitohtên ôma!" "wêpahwâhkan!" ||| “Now, my Horn, be ready to toss this stubby-tooth bear! Toss him as soon as he stirs from this spot. Watch his slightest move. He has delayed me for no reason; I was going visiting! Look sharp, my Horn; you understand what I say! Be ready to toss him!”
êkosi cimahêw ôhi êskana êtiskwêsiniyit. ||| With that, he stuck the horn upright in the ground toward the bear's head, as he was lying.
"wêpahwâhkan, nitêskan!" "niwî-sipwêhtân." "wâpam awa wâkayôs!" "misawâc kika-wêpahok." "êkosi kika-nipahik, mayaw waskawîyani!" ||| “Be ready to toss him, my Horn! I am going away from here. Watch this bear! - You cannot avoid his tossing you. So then, he will kill you, as soon as you budge!”
êkosi cimahêw êkota. ||| So he stuck it upright there.
ê-kî-piponiyik, kîhtwâm ê-nîpiniyik, "mahti nika-nitawâpamâw nisîm," itêyihtam. ||| When winter had passed and summer had come again, “Suppose I go have a look at my little brother,” he thought.
kî-sîkwâhkatosoyiwa ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| That bear had starved to death.
êkosi kâ-kî-ititân:" "misawâc kî-waskawîyan, sêmâk ka-kî-nipahikoh awa nitêskan!" ||| That is what I told you: certainly, if you had budged, at once this Horn of mine would have killed you!”
êkosi êkoyikohk êskwâk âtayôhkêwin. ||| That is the end of this sacred story.
"nisîm!" ê-wâpahtahk pâwistik; "nisîm!" ||| “Little brother!” when he saw the rapids; “Little brother!”
"'tâpwê nisîpwêwêmon!' kitêyihtên." "kimawinêhotin, awîna kiyipa kê-kihtimit," itêw. ||| “Truly, I keep long at my noise!” you think. I challenge you to see which of us will weary first,” he told it.
iyikohk ta-pôni-askîwik, êkoyikohk nikî-itik kôhtâwînaw ta-kîskowêyân," itik. ||| When the green earth ceases to be, only then did Our Father tell me to cease from my noise,” it told him.
"â, mâka kiwî-mawinêhotin!" ||| “Oh, but I mean to challenge you!”
ômisi itêyihtam: "pipohki ta-kîskowêw," ê-itêyimât. ||| He thought, “In winter it will stop”; that was what he thought of it.
êkota nahapiw êkwa wîsahkêcâhk, ôma ê-pêhtâkwaniyik. ||| Then Wisahketchahk sat down there where its sound was heard.
êkwa ômisi itwêw wîsahkêcâhk: "blblblbl!" ||| And Wisahketchahk said, “Blblblbl!”
âhci piko êkota apiw, pisisik êkosi ê-itwêt, "blblblbl!" ||| Still he sat there, all the while saying, “Blblblbl!”
êkwa kôna kahkiyaw nama kêkway. ||| Then all the snow disappeared.
êkwa mistahi nipiy ôta pê-ayâyiw, ita ê-apit. ||| Then much water came and was where he sat.
piyisk ômayikohk iskopêw nipiy. ||| At last he was up to here in the water.
êkoyikohk pasikôw, pêyak askiy, "blblblbl!" ê-itwêt. ||| Only then he arose to his feet, having said, “Blblblbl!” for a whole year.
ômisi itwêw: "wâcistakâ nama kî-ayiwâkitonâmâw nisîm!" itwêw. ||| He said, “Incredible, how my little brother cannot be out-talked!”
êkosi êkoyikohk êwako. ||| That is the end of this.
kîtahtawê wîsahkêcâhk ê-pimohtêt, kâ-wâpahtahk mîkiwâhp. ||| Once upon a time, as Wisahketchahk was walking along, he saw a tipi.
ê-takohtêt, "ham ham!" itwêw. ||| When he reached it, he said, “Hum, hum!”
mâka mîna nôhtêhkatêw. ||| As usual, he was hungry.
"ahaw, tawâw!" itik. ||| “Yes, yes, come in!” someone called to him.
ê-pîhtokêt, pêyakoyiwa nâpêwa. ||| When he entered there was a lone man.
ê-nahapit, nanâtawâpahtam kêkway ka-mîcit. ||| When he sat down, he looked all round for something to eat.
kîtahtawê ômisi itwêyiwa: "yâ, nistês onôhtêhkatâh!" itwêyiwa. ||| Presently the other said, “Oh dear, but I am forgetting that my elder brother is hungry!” he said.
wêskwâhtêmihk êkotê kîkway êtokê ê-tahkopitêyik wâpahtam. ||| He saw that something or other was tied fast in the doorway.
êwako itinamiyiwa, ê-âpahamiyit: pôti ôma astotin, sihkosiwayân ohci astotin, mîna kicohcikanis. ||| The other took that thing and removed the covering: it turned out to be a headgear, a headgear of weasel-skin, and a little flute.
akwâsiwêpahamiyiwa iskotêw, ê-miyâhkasikêyit, miyâhkasamiyit astotin mîna kicohcikanis. ||| The man scattered some embers of the fire and burned incense for the headgear and the flute.
ka-kitâpamêw, ê-tôtamiyit. ||| He watched the man do it.
postastotinêyiwa, ê-yôhtênamiyit, êkwa wîpisisiyiw pêyak ê-otinamiyit. ||| The man put on the headgear, opened the door-flap, and took one of his arrows.
ê-kitohtâyit, kiyipa pâpayiyiwa mostoswa pêyak, ôta iskwâhtêmihk ê-pimipayiyit. ||| When he blew on the flute, quickly a buffalo came running, and ran right past the doorway.
pimêyiwa; nipahêyiwa. ||| The man shot it and killed it.
kâwi kêtastotinêyiwa, ê-asiwatâyit, ê-tahkwâskwêpitamiyit apasôhk. ||| He took off the headgear, put it back in its covering, and tied it fast to the wood of the tent-poles.

tâpwê otinam, ê-nitawi-manisahk otêyaniy. ||| So he took it, and went out and cut out the tongue.
"mâna êkâ nika-kîspohtân!" itêyihtam. ||| “It looks as if we should not get our fill!” he thought.
wayawîw, "mistahi nika-otinên wiyâs," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He went out of the tent, thinking, “I shall take a lot of the meat.”
nama kêkway mostoswa; sipwêhtêyiwa. ||| The buffalo was not there; it had gone away.
kâwi pîhtokêw, êkwa ê-mîcisocik. ||| He went back in, and they ate.
"nisîm, kâkikê cî ôma êkosi ê-isi-minahoyan?" itêw. ||| “Little brother, do you always kill game in this manner?” he asked him.
"êha." "nama wîhkâc, wâh-minahoyâni, nipapâmohtân." "êwako ôma nipostastotinân, wâh-minahoyâni, ê-kitohtâyân, ê-pêcimakik mostoswak," itwêyiwa. ||| “Yes. I never tramp about when I want to kill game. I put on this head-dress, when I want to kill game, and by blowing the flute, summon the buffalos,” said the man.
ômisi itêyihtam wîsahkêcâhk: "nika-kimotamawâw!" itêyihtam; "nika-âcimostawâw, ta-nôhtêhkwasit, êkâ ta-kiskêyihtahk, kimotamawaki," itêyihtam. ||| Wisahketchahk thought thus: “I shall steal it from him!” he thought; “I shall tell him stories to make him sleepy, so that he will not know when I steal it from him.” he thought.
êkwa ê-tipiskâyik, âcimostawêw, ê-wî-kakwê-nôhtêhkwastimât. ||| Then, when night came, he told him tales, so as to make him get sleepy.
ê-kiskêyimât, ê-nôhtêhkwasiyit, êkwa kawisimôwak. ||| When he knew that the other was sleepy, then they went to bed. He kept from going to sleep.
nama wî-nipâw. mayaw ê-nipâyit, otinam, ê-wayawîhtatât ôma astotin, ê-kimotit, ê-nayahtahk. ||| As soon as the other slept, he took the headgear, and went out of the tent with it, stealing it and carrying it over his shoulder.
pâh-pimipahtâw, konita ê-wâ-wâkohtêt, "êkâ ta-mitisit," ê-itêyimât. êkwa ê-wî-wâpaniyik, ita ê-wâyahcâyik, êkota kawisimôw. ||| He ran on and on, making all kinds of turns and twists, with the thought, “So that he may not track me.” Then, towards dawn in a hollow place he lay down.
"kîsikâki, pimohtêyâni, nika-wâpamik, pê-nawaswâsici," itêyihtam; "iyikohk tipiskâki, nika-tapasîn," ê-itêyihtahk, êkota kâ-kawisimot. ||| “If I walk on in daytime, he will see me, in case he comes here pursuing me,” he thought; “When night comes, I shall continue in my flight,” he thought, as he lay down.
mayaw ê-pimisihk, nipâw, mitoni ê-papêtikosihk, ê-nayôhtahk ôma astotin. ||| As soon as he lay down, he fell asleep, lying all doubled up, with the headgear still on his shoulders.
kîtahtawê, ê-mêkwâ-nipât, koskoskonik, "nistêsê, waniskâ! ||| Suddenly, in the midst of his sleep, someone shook him and roused him, saying to him, “Big brother, get up!
kikipiskawin." "niwî-kotawân," ê-itikot. ||| You are blocking my way. I want to build the fire.”
êsa ôma pîhcâyihk wîkiyihk, ita kâ-kotawêyit mâna êkota êsa ôma kâ-nipât. ||| There he was, inside the other's tipi; he had been sleeping right were the other always built the fire.
"yahô, nisîm, êkosi êsi-kîskwêhkwasiskiyân!" "awa êtokê ka-otinamân kiwîskwêpitâkan!" itêw, ê-kêtôwatêt, kâwi ê-tahkopitahk. ||| “Dear me, little brother, I am afflicted with sleep-walking like this! And here it seems I have taken your sacred bundle!” he told him, removing his burden and tying it back in its place.
"ohcitaw nika-kimotin," itêyihtam. ||| “All the more surely, I will steal it,” he thought.
âsay mîna ê-tipiskâyik, âcimostawêw, ê-wî-kakwê-nêstohkwastimât. ||| That night again he told him stories to make him sleepy.
