êkosi nahapiw, mistikohk ê-aspatisihk. ||| So he sat down, leaning against the tree.
ômisi isi kîskipitam oskotâkay, mistikwa ôhi ê-asitahpitisot. ||| Like this he tore his jacket and tied himself fast to the tree.
aspin piko ê-nipât, kîtahtawê kâ-koskoskonikot. ||| Hardly had he gone off to sleep, when suddenly the other shook him awake.
"nistêsê, waniskâ!" "kôtamihin; nitastotin!" "niwî-kakwê-minahoh!" itik. ||| “Big brother, get up! You are delaying me; my headgear! I want to try and kill some game!” the other was saying to him.
ê-tôhkâpit, awîna ôma, pîhcâyihk kî-apiw, apasôhk ê-asitahpisot. ||| When he opened his eyes, what was this? He was sitting inside the place, tied fast to a tent-pole.
ômisi itwêw: "yahô!" "êkosi ôma mâna ê-isi-kîskwêhkwasiskiyân, piko êtokê ê-otinamân kiwîskwêpitâkan, nisîm!" itêw, ê-pasikôt, kâwi ê-tahkopitahk. ||| He said, “Dear me! this is the way I am afflicted with the habit of walking in my sleep; and it seems that in some way I have taken up your sacred bundle, little brother!” he said to him, and rose to his feet, and tied the thing back where it belonged.
kiyipa otinamiyiwa, ê-kwayakonamiyit, ê-postastotinêyit. ||| The other at once took it, shook it out, and put on the headgear.
âsay mîna ê-kitohtâyit, pêcimêyiwa mostoswa. ||| Again when he blew the flute, he called a buffalo.
mîna êwakoni pimwêyiwa, ê-nipahâyit. ||| This one, too, he shot and killed.
"hâ, nisîm, tânêhki pêyak piko kâ-nipahat?" itêw. ||| “Now, little brother, why do you kill only one?” he asked him.
"hâ, êkoyikohk ka-kîsponânaw pêyak otêyaniy," itêw. ||| “Oh, one tongue is quite enough to give us our fill,” he told him.
êkosi tahkopitamiyiwa mîna ôma otastotiniyiw. ||| With this he again tied up that headgear of his.
êkwa wiya nitawi-otinam otêyaniy. ||| And Wisahketchahk went and took up the tongue.
êkosi ê-kî-mîcisocik, piyisk mîna tipiskâyiw. ||| When thus they had eaten, finally night came again.
iyikohk mîna ê-nipâyit, âsay mîna kimotiw, âsay mîna ê-tapasît. ||| Again, as soon as the other slept, he stole it, and again made off in flight.
mitoni êkwa wî-kakwê-mîhkawikiw. ||| He was bound to run fast, now, and far.
wâhyaw mîna ê-ayât, âsay mîna ê-wî-wâpaniyik, âsay mîna sêskisiw. ||| When again he had gone a great distance, and again dawn was near, again he went into the brush.
nîso mistikwa ê-nîswaskisoyit, êkota tastawâyihk nahapiw, ê-asitahpitisot, "namôya êkwa êkotê pîhcâyihk nika-nipân!" ê-itêyihtahk. ||| Where two trees stood side by side, there he sat down between them, and tied himself fast, thinking, “This time I shall not be sleeping inside there!” So he went to sleep.
êkosi isi nipâw. kîtahtawê ê-mêkwâ-nipât, kâ-koskoskonikot. ||| Suddenly, in the midst of his sleep, there was the other, shaking him awake.
"nistêsê, waniskâ!" "kikipiskawin." "niwî-pônên." ||| “Big brother, get up! You are blocking my way. I want to put wood on the fire.”
êsa ôma ita kâ-ôh-wayawîhk, iskwâhtêmihk êkota êsa ôma kâ-asitahpisot. ||| It appeared that in the place where one went out of the tent, right in the doorway it appeared that he was tied fast.
"yahô, nisîm, kikî-wîhtamâtin ê-kîskwêhkwasiskiyân." "nama cî awa kitastotin êwako, 'nika-ayâwik!' ê-itêyimit kitastotin?" itêw. ||| “Dear me, little brother, I told you I was given to walking in my sleep. Are you sure that this headgear of yours has not been thinking ‘Let him possess me!’ meaning me?” he asked him.
mîna ê-tipiskâyik, âsay mîna ê-nipâyit, otinam, ê-wîwahot, mîna ê-tapasît, ê-sôhki- ê-tapasît. ||| The next night, as soon as the other slept, again he took the thing slung the bundle across his shoulder, and again made off, fleeing with all his might.
iyikohk mîna ê-wî-wâpahk, âsay mîna wî-nipâw. ||| When dawn again was near, again he meant to sleep.
kîhcêkosîw ispimihk. ||| He climbed high up on a tree.
êkota êkwa nipâw, mîna ê-asitahpisot. ||| There he went to sleep, after again tying himself fast.
aspin ê-nipât, kîtahtawê mistik ohci kâ-koskoskoyahkahokot, "waniskâ, nistêsê! ||| He had gone off to sleep, when suddenly the other was prodding him awake with a stick, saying to him, “Get up, big brother!
niwî-pônên," ê-itikot, wîkiyihk ispimihk ê-akosît, ita kâ-ôh-wayawiyâpohtêyik êkota. ||| I am going to put wood on the fire,” and there he was, perched on top of the other's dwelling, right at the place where the smoke comes out of the tipi.
"yahô, nisîm, êkoyikohk êkosi ôma êsi-kîskwêhkwasiskiyân!" itêw, ê-pê-nîhtakosît, ê-pîhtokêt, ê-ta-tahkopitahk, ita kâ-kî-tahkopitêyik. ||| “Dear me, little brother, just see how terribly I am afflicted with sleep-walking!” he said to him, as he climbed down and came into the tent and tied the thing back into the place where it had been tied fast.
ômisi itik: "wîsahkêcâhk, namôya ka-kî-kimotamawin nitastotin." "êwako ôma nêpâyani ê-pê-kîwêhtahikoyan." "nawac ta-pônihtâyan!" itik. ||| The other answered him thus: “Wisahketchahk, you will not be able to steal my headgear from me. It was this headgear itself which brought you back here whenever you went to sleep. You might as well give it up!” the other told him.
êkosi ê-kî-mîcisot, sipwêhtêw. ||| At this, as soon as he had eaten, he went away.
êkoyikohk êskwâk âtayôhkêwin. ||| That is the end of the sacred story.
kîtahtawê pêyak ayîsiyiniw itahk ê-wa-wîkit, ê-pêyakot, nama wîhkâc wâpamêw ayîsiyiniwa, wiya piko êkota ê-ayât. ||| Once upon a time a man lived all alone and never saw any people, being all alone in that place.
kâ-nipâci kâ-tipiskâyik, wiyâpaniyiki mâcîw. ||| When he had slept at night, in the morning he went hunting.
wiyâpamâci mostoswa, nipahêw. ||| Whenever he saw buffalo, he killed them.
pêyak otêyaniy otinam, êkwa pêyak opêminak, ê-kîwêt, ê-takohtêt wîkihk, êkwa mâna ê-kîsitêpot, kâ-mîcisoci, êkwa ê-nikohtêt. ||| He would take a tongue and a thigh-bone and go home, and when he reached his dwelling, he would prepare his meal, and when he had eaten, he would gather firewood.
êkosi êkwa piyisk tipiskâyiw mâna. ||| So night would come upon him.
êkwa ê-ay-apit, piyisk kaskêyihtam ê-pêyakot. ||| As he stayed thus by himself, at last, he felt lonesome.
ê-wâpaniyik, mîna ê-mâcît, mîna pêyak nipahêw mostoswa. ||| When daylight came and he as usual went hunting, again he killed a buffalo.
kîwêw; apisîs otinam kâ-mîcit. ||| He went home; he took a little to eat.
cîki ê-ihtât wîkihk, kâ-wâpahtahk mistahi ê-astêyiki mihta wîkihk. ||| When he was near his dwelling-place, he saw a great pile of firewood by his tent.
ay-itêyihtam; "awiyak ê-kî-takohtêt," êkosi itêyihtam. ||| He wondered about it; “It must be that someone has come,” he thought. He was glad.
miywêyihtam. ê-pîhtokêt, nama awiya wâpamêw, êsa kâ-wêpâhtakahikêwihk. ||| When he entered, he saw nobody, though it was plain that someone had swept the place.
mihtâtam êkâ ê-wâpamât awiya. ||| He was sorry that he saw no one.
"tânêhki ôma êkâ kâ-ôh-apit awiyak?" itêyihtam. ||| “How is it that there is no one here?” he thought.
pôti ita kâ-apit maskisina miskam. ||| Lo, there where he sat, he found some moccasins.
mistahi miywêyihtam, "iskwêw mâskôc kâ-kî-takohtêt," ê-itêyihtahk; "kîkisêpâ nika-mâcîn;" "nika-kakwê-kêsiskawâw, mîna takohtêci," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He was very glad, thinking, “A woman perhaps is the one who came here. In the morning I shall hunt; I shall try to come upon her while she is here, if she comes again,” he thought.
ê-wâpaniyik, kiyipa sipwêhtêw, ê-mâcît. ||| At daybreak he quickly went off to hunt.
mîna nipahêw pêyak mostoswa. ||| Again he killed a buffalo.
otêyaniy otinam êkwa ospikêkana êkwa otihtikosiwa êkwa opêminak. ||| He took the tongue, the ribs, the kidneys, and a thigh bone.
êkosi isi kîwêw, "nika-kêsiskawâw," ê-itêyihtah. pâh-pimipahtâw. ||| Then he went home, thinking, “I shall come in time to find her there.” He kept running.
cîki ê-ihtât wîkihk, wâpahtam ê-pikihcêsiyik, mîna mistahi mistahi ê-astêyiki. ||| When he got near his dwelling, he saw a little smoke, and a great pile of firewood.
ê-pîhtokêt, iyâyaw nanâtawâpiw: nama awiya wâpamêw. ||| When he entered, eagerly he looked about: he saw no one.
mistahi mihtâtam êkâ ê-apiyit awiya. ||| He was very sorry that no one was there.
êkwa ê-paminawasot, kîtahtawê kâ-miskahk maskisina. ||| Then, as he went about his cooking, soon he found some moccasins.
otinam, ê-wâ-wâpahtahk, ê-miywâsiniyiki. ||| He picked them up and examined them; they were very pretty.
"mâskôc iskwêw kâ-tâh-takosihk," itêyihtam; "hâh, ohcitaw nika-kakwê-kêsiskawâw." "kîkisêpâ nika-sipwêhtân," êkosi itêyihtam. ||| “Probably it is a woman has been coming here,” he thought; “Now all the harder I shall try to find her here. Early in the morning I shall go,” he thought.
tâpwê ê-kî-mîcisot kawisimôw ê-nipât. ||| After eating he lay down to sleep.
kîkisêpâ waniskâw; namôya mîcisôw, ê-sipwêhtêt, ê-mâcît. ||| He got up early; without eating he went forth to hunt.
pôti kiyipa nipahêw mostoswa. êkwa ê-kî-wiyanihât, ospikêkana otihtikosiwa otinam, ê-ati-kîwêt. ||| In a short time he killed a buffalo, and when he had cut it up, took the ribs and the kidneys and went home.
cîki ê-ihtât wîkihk, kâ-wâpahtahk mistahi ê-pikihtêyik wîki. ||| When he saw close to his dwelling, he saw much smoke rising from his tent.
mistahi miywêyihtam, "mâskôc apiw," ê-itêyihtah. ||| He was very glad, thinking, “Perhaps she is there.”
ê-takohtêt, ê-pîhtokêt, awîna ôhi kî-apiyiwa mistahi ê-miyosiyit iskwêwa ohtapiwinihk. ||| When he got there and entered, lo and behold, there sat a very handsome woman on his settee.
êkota nahapiw, ê-wî-pâhpihikot, ê-kitâpamât. ||| He sat down there, and she smiled at him as he looked at her.
sâsay êsa kâ-paminawasoyit. ||| It appeared that she had already done the cooking.
sêmâk otinamiyiwa omaskisina, ê-kêtaskisinênikot, kotaka ê-wî-postaskisinahikot, êkwa ê-kâsîcihcênikot, ê-kâsîhkwênikot. ||| Without delay she took off his moccasins and put others on his feet, and she washed his hands and face.
êkosi êkwa asamik; êkwa mîcisowak. ||| Thereupon she gave him to eat, and they took their meal.
â, mistahi miywêyihtam. ||| Oh, he was very glad.
ômisi itêw awa iskwêw: "tânêhki apisîs kâ-pêtâyan wiyâs?" ||| Thus spoke that woman: “Why do you bring so little meat?”
"â," itwêw awa nâpêw, "nama awiyak nitihtatêyimâw;" "êwako ohci apisîs kâ-ôh-pêtâyân," êkosi itwêw awa nâpêw; "tânitê mâka ôma ê-ohtohtêyan?" itwêw awa nâpêw. ||| “Oh,” said the man, “I did not think anyone was here; that is why I brought only a little,” he said; “But whence do you come?” he asked.
"wâhyaw ôtê ê-wîkiyâhk," itwêw awa iskwêw; "kiyâm miyâcîyani mistahi pêtâ wiyâsa;" "nôhtêhkatêwak," itwêw awa iskwêw, "nôhtâwiy," itwêw. ||| “A long ways from here we dwell,” she answered. “Please, when you hunt, bring much meat; they are in want of food,” she said, “my father and his people.”
"êha," itwêw awa nâpêw. ||| “Very well,” said he.
êkota ohci tahto-kîsikâw mâcîw. ||| So he hunted every day.
piyisk mistahi nipahêw mostoswa. ||| In time he killed many buffalo.
awa iskwêw mistahi atoskêw, wiyâsa ê-osihtât. ||| The woman worked a great deal, preparing the food.
mistahi ê-ayâcik, "nawac itohtêyahk nôhtâwiy," itwêw awa iskwêw; "mistahi nôhtêhkatêwak." ||| When they had a large amount of it, “Suppose we go to my father's place,” said the woman; “They are very hungry.”
"êha," itwêw awa nâpêw. ||| “Very well,” said the man.
"wâpahki," itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Tomorrow,” she said.
"kêkway kê-âpacihtâyahk ta-pimiwitâyahk kêkway?" ||| “But what are we to use to carry things?”
"â, tita-ihtakon êtokê tânisi ta-isi-pihkohoyahk," itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Oh, there will be some way we can manage,” she answered.
tâpwê kîkisêpâ ê-mîcisocik, "nîkânohtêhkan," itêw owîkimâkana; "itâp mistikwa ka-cimatân, êkota ta-kapêsiyahk; êkota ohci ka-mâcîn," itêw awa iskwêw onâpêma. ||| Then, when they ate in the morning, “Go on ahead,” she told her husband; “Then you will set up some sticks at the place where we are to camp; from that place you will go hunting,” she said to her husband.
tâpwê ê-kîsi-mîcisocik sipwêhtêw awa nâpêw. ||| So, when they had eaten, the man set out.
êkwa awa iskwêw wawêyîw, ôhi ocayânisiwâwa onîmâwiniwâwa nâh-nâway ê-astât. ||| And the woman made ready, laying their belongings and their food supply in a row.
êkwa ê-kîsi-wawêyît awa iskwêw ati-tâh-têhci-tahkoskêw onîmâwiniwâwa; êkosi ê-ati-sipwêhtêt, nama kêkway ihtakoniyiwa ôho onîmâwiniwâwa. ||| Then, when she had got ready, she went along, stepping each time upon their bundles of food; and when in this wise she set out, not a trace was there of their supplies of food.
êkosi isi ê-pa-pimohtêt. ||| So then she walked on.
itê ê-otâkosiniyik kâ-miskahk mistikwa ê-cimatêyiki, êkota kapêsiw. ||| Toward nightfall she found the sticks that were set up in the ground; there she made camp.
êkwa ê-tahkiskâcikêt awa iskwêw, wîkiwâw êkota astêyiw. ||| When she kicked the ground, there lay their tent.
êkwa otinam, ê-mânokêt. ||| Then she took the tent and set it up.
ê-kîsi-mânokêt, pîhcâyihk âsay mîna tahkiskâcikêw; kahkiyaw êkotê pahkihtiniyiwa ocayânisiwâwa onîmâwiniwâwa. ||| When she had set it up, inside again she stamped the ground; on that spot fell all their belongings and their supplies of food.
êkosi êkwa pîhtokêw awa iskwêw, ê-paminawasot. ||| Then she went inside and cooked their meal.
pôti ê-ati-kîwêt awa nâpêw, kâ-wâpahtahk wîkiwâw, "tânisi tiyôtahk?" ê-itêyimât owîkimâkana. ||| There, when the man came back and saw their dwelling, “How did she do it?” he thought concerning his wife.
ê-pîhtokêt, kâ-wî-pâhpihikot owîkimâkana. ||| When he entered, there saw was, smiling at him.
ê-itâpit, kahkiyaw wâpahtam ocayânisiwâwa onîmâwiniwâwa. ||| He looked about and saw all their belongings and their supplies of food.
mistahi mâmaskâtam ê-tôtamiyit. ||| He wondered greatly at what she had done.
ômisi itwêw awa awa iskwêw: "wâpahki ka-takohtânânaw ita nôhtâwiy kâ-ayâcik." "mistahi nôhtêhkatêwak," itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| Thus spoke she: “Tomorrow we shall come to where my father's people stay. They are in great want of food,” she said.
tâpwê ê-wâpahk, kîkisêpâ waniskâwak. ||| So when day broke, early they arose.
ê-kî-mîcisocik, wawêyîwak. ||| When they had eaten, they made ready.
"wîcôhkamawin," itwêw awa iskwêw; "'tânisi ê-tôtahk?' kâ-itêyihtaman, ka-kiskêyihtên tânisi ê-tôtamân," itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Help me,” said the woman; “Since you have been thinking, ‘How does she do it?’ you shall now know how I do,” she said.
"ahaq," itwêw awa nâpêw. ||| “Yes,” answered the man.
tâpwê wawêyîwak, nâh-nâway ê-astâcik ocayânisiwâwa onîmâwiniwâwa. ||| Accordingly they made ready by laying in a row their possessions and their stored meats.
ê-kitâpamât owîkimâkana, ê-ati-sipwêhtêyit, ê-ta-têhci-tahkoskêyit onîmâwiniwâwa, nama kêkway wâpahtam awa nâpêw. ||| When he watched his wife, as she went forth and stepped on one after another of their bundles, he saw nothing at all there.
êkosi isi pimohtêcik, mistahi mâmaskâtêw owîkimâkana, ê-tôtamiyit. ||| So as they walked on, he marvelled greatly at what his wife had done.
êkosi isi ê-pa-pimohtêcik, kîtahtawê, ê-ati-otâkosiniyik, kâ-wâpahtahkik ê-pikihtêyik ita ê-pasahcâyik, ê-sakâyik; êkota ê-sâkêwêcik, kâ-pê-matâwisiyit osîmisa awa iskwêw. ||| Then, as they walked on, towards evening they saw smoke rising from a wooded ravine; when they came in sight of that place, the woman's younger sister came forth.
ômisi itwêyiwa: "âyêyi, misi-pêtâw nîmâwina nimis!" itwêyiwa. ||| She cried: “Splendid! My elder sister is bringing a great store of meat!”
êkosi ati-takohtêwak wîkiyihk. ||| So they went on and came to the house.
awa kisêyiniw, "hay hay hay!" matwê-itwêw. ||| The old man called out, “Splendid!”
ê-yôhtênahk awa iskwêw, ê-pîhtikwê-ta-tahkiskâcikêt, pîhcâyihk pahkihtiniyiwa onîmâwiniwâwa ocayânisiwâwa. ||| When the woman opened the door and, as she entered, stamped repeatedly, then into the lodge fell their stored meats and their belongings.
êkosi awa nôtokêsiw ê-ati-otinahk, mistahi miywêyihtam, "êkwa kê-mîcisoyân," ê-itêyihtah. nanâskomôw awa kisêyiniw. êkosi pîhtokêwak. ||| Then when the old woman went on to pick them up, she greatly rejoiced, thinking, “So now I shall eat.” The old man gave thanks: [no translation given]
ômisi itwêw awa kisêyiniw: "êkosi ê-kî-itêyihtamân, nitânis, 'itohtê!' kâ-kî-ititân, "ê-pa-pêyakot ninahâhkisîm,"" itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Thus I had it in mind, daughter, when ‘Go there,’ I said to you, ‘where my son-in-law dwells alone,’” said the old man.
pâti kinwêsk ê-kî-ayât êkota, êkwa ê-miyoskamiyik, kâ-kiskêyihtahk wâkayôsa kâ-wîwit ôhi iskwêwa kâ-itêyihtahk, ôhi mîna kisêyiniwa nôtokêsiwa wâkayôsa êsa ôhi. ||| When he had been there a long time, and spring had come, then he knew that she, the woman, as it seemed to him, whom he had to wife, was a bear, and that also the old man and the old woman were bears.
êkwa mihtâtam êkâ tahki ta-kî-wîcêwât. ||| And he was sorry that he could not always be with them.
êkosi êkoyikohk êwako âtayôhkêwin. ||| That is the end of this sacred story.
kîtahtawê pêyak nâpêw wiya piko ê-pêyakokamikisit pisisik mâna. ||| Once upon a time a certain man always dwelt off along with his family.
kîtahtawê namôya wîhkâc apiyiwa owîkimâkana, tahto-kîsikâw ê-sipwêhtêyit, kâ-wawêsîhoyici, ayôwinisa ê-miywâsiniyiki tahto-kîsikâw ê-postiskahk awa iskwêw. ||| After a while his wife never stayed at home, but went off every day, after putting on her fine clothes; every day that woman put on her good clothes.
kîspin piyê-kîwêci, mistahi mâna mâyâtaniyiwa, konita mâna misiwê ê-asiskîwiyiki. ||| When she came back home, they were always in a bad state, muddied all over.
"tânêhki êtokê" itêyihtam awa nâpêw: "mahti nika-kakwê-wâpamâw," itêyihtam. ||| “I wonder what this means?” thought the man; “Suppose I watch her,” he thought.
êkwa kîmôc pê-wâh-wîskawahtâw wîkiwâw, mahti ê-wî-kiskinawâpamât owîkimâkana, tânitê isi kita-sipwêhtêyit. ||| Then he gradually stole up to the lodge, to watch his wife and learn which way she would go.
kâ-wâpamât aspin ôta sakâhk ê-isi-sipwêhtêyit, kiskêyimêw itê ê-itohtêyit. kâ-wâpamât êkotê sakâhk wâkayôsa ê-wâh-owîcimosiyit, mistahi kisiwâsiw, ê-ohtêyimât ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| When he had seen her go off into the woods, he knew where she was going [no translation] [no translation: He saw her there in the bush, she had a bear for a lover, he was very angry and jealous of the bear.]
"wâpahki nika-nipahâw!" itêyihtam. ||| “Tomorrow I shall kill him!” he thought.
tâpwê ê-otâkosiniyik, ômisi itwêw awa: "anohc wâkayôs nimiskawâw ita ê-ôwâtit," itwêw awa nâpêw, ê-kîwêt. ||| So then in the evening he said, “Today I found a bear's den,” said the man, when he came home.
êkwa ômisi itwêw ana iskwêw; ômisi êsa kî-itik ôhi wîcimosa wâkayôsa: "kîspin nipahikawiyâni, otinâhkan nipahkêkin," kî-itik êsa; "êkosi itâp nitawêyihtamani piko ispîhk ayîsiyiniwak mihcêt kika-nipahâwak," kî-itik êsa awa iskwêw; êkosi ômisi itêw onâpêma: "êkâya misiwê pîkoswâhkan." "tâpiskôc atâwâkan kâ-isi-pahkoniht, êkosi isîhâhkan," kî-itêw êsa onâpêma. ||| Then the woman spoke thus; for thus she had been told by her lover, the bear: “If I am slain, do you then take my hide,” he must have told her; “In this way, later, should you so desire, you may at any time kill many people,” he must have told that woman; so now she said to her husband, “Do not cut him up. Just as one skins a fur-bearing animal for sale, do you so prepare him,” she told her husband.
"êha," itwêw awa nâpêw, ê-sîhkimikot wîwa. ||| “Very well,” said the man, in answer to his wife's request.
tâpwê wîhpi-pahkonêw ôhi, ispîhk ê-nitawi-nipahât ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| So he cut the creature out of its hide, when he went to kill that bear.
ômisi itwêw ana iskwêw: "namôya katâc ta-môwâyahk!" ||| The woman said, “We do not have to eat him, do we?”
"êkamâ mâka awiyak kê-kî-mowât ê-owîcimosiyit!" itêw owîkimâkana. ||| “[no translation]” replied the husband.
êkosi tâpwê kîsihêw ôhi wâkayôsiwayâna. ||| Then accordingly she prepared that bearskin.
êkwa ocawâsimisiw awa iskwêw. ||| Then that woman gave birth.
nîso nâpêsisak ayâwêw sêmâk, nîsôtêwa. ||| Even then and no later, she had two boys, twins.
êwakoni wâkayôsa êsa owîtôsêmâh. tâpwê âpihtaw wiyawiwâhk misiwê opîwâwak êsa ôki nâpêsisak. ||| [no translation] And those boys were covered with fur all over half of their bodies.
êkosi êyiwêhk kitimâkêyimêw awa nâpêw; êyiwêhk wî-kakwê-ohpikihêw, âta namôya wiya otawâsimisa. ||| Then that man to some extent took pity on them; he decided to bring them up as best he could, even though they were not his.
tâpwê ohpikiwak ôki awâsisak. ||| And so those children grew up.
êkwa ê-ati-misikiticik, kîtahtawê ômisi itêw: "êkâya wîhkâc tâpwêhtamok, nitawâsimisitik, âhki kiyawâw'wâkayôsak' itikawiyêko." "kiyawâw tâpwê êkotôwahk." "êkosi itikawiyêko kîspin, ka-kwêskimonâwâw." ||| Then, as they were growing up, at one time he told them, “Never give credence to it my children, if ever you are called ‘bears.’ Such, indeed, you are. If that is said to you, you will change your bodily form.”
êkosi tâpwê nama wîhkâc êsa tâpwêhtamwak ôki awâsisak, êkosi êtihtwâwi. ||| Accordingly, those boys never gave heed when they were called that way.
kîtahtawê awa osîmimâs, "kiyâm wâkayôsiwitân mahti!" itêw ôhi ostêsa. ||| Then at one time, “Let us turn into bears!” the younger one said to the elder.
tâpwê wâkayôsiwiwak. ||| So they turned into bears.
pê-nôcihêwak awâsisa, ê-pê-pâ-pâskatayêpitâcik. ||| They came pursuing the children, and when they reached them, tore them open at the belly.
êkwa kisiwâk wîkiwâhk kâ-pê-nipahihtwâwi ôki maskosisak, sêmâk awa iskwêw kisiwâsiw êsa. ||| Then when, close to the lodge those bear-cubs were killed, at once that woman grew angry.
onâpêma kîhkâmêw; wayawî-kwâskohtiw; nitawi-otinêw ôhi kâ-kî-osihât oskotâkaya, ôhi maskwayâna. ||| She upbraided her husband; she sprang out of the lodge; she went and took that mystic dress she had made, that bear-skin robe.
êkosi isi ati-isi-kwêskîmôw. ||| At once she thus changed her bodily form.
pîhtikwê-kwâskohtiw kêhciwâk wîkiwâhk; onâpêma ati-nipahêw. ||| She came bounding right into the lodge; she killed her husband.
êkota ohci mitoni kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwa mêscihêw. ||| Then she killed off all the people.
mitoni êsa ê-mihcêtihk, êwakoni kahkiyaw mitoni nipahêw. ||| Although there were many of then, she killed them all. Only her mother she spared.
okâwiya piko iskohêw. âta ê-pâ-pâskisoht, namôya êsa kî-sâkôcihâw; namôya kî-nipahâw, piyisk êkosi isi kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwa kâ-kîsi-mêscihât. ||| Although she was shot at again and again, she could not be overcome; it was impossible to kill her, so that at last she thus had exterminated those people.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw kîwôtêw, êwako awa omisa kâ-wâkayôsiwiyit. ||| Then that young man went visiting, whose elder sister was the woman who had turned into a bear.
êkwa awa iskwêw ôhtâwiya iskohêw. ôhcitaw ê-wî-kakwâtakihât. ||| And that woman had spared her father, only so as to torture him.
tâpwê pêyak mistahi kwâtakihêw okâwiya, mîna osîmisa pêyak, êwakoni piko ê-iskohât. ||| Truly, she tormented her mother and her little sister, having spared only them.
êkwa mâna piko itê ê-papâmâcihot, piyê-takohtêci piko nayêstaw ê-kîhkâmât, nanâtohk ê-isi-kwâtakihât, kiyikaw ê-saskahwât, misiwê êsa omikîwak ôki kêhtê-ayak mîna awa iskwêsis. mistahi êsa kitimahêw. ||| When she had been going about here and there, when she came back, she would do nothing but scold them, and torment them in various ways, burning them pell-mell, so that those old people and that little girl were all covered with scars.
kîtahtawê awa oskinîkiw kâ-takohtêt, "tânêhki ôma?" itêyihtam, ita ôma kâ-kî-mihcêtiyit ayîsiyiniwa kahkiyaw ê-mêscihimiht. ||| She kept them in a grievous state. Presently, when that young man arrived, “What can be the matter?” he thought, since all the many people there had been killed.
pêyak piko mîkiwâhp wâpahtam, ohpimê ê-cimatêyik. ||| He saw only one tipi, standing off to one side.
êkwa kîtahtawê osîmisa kâ-wâpamât, ê-nitawi-tâpakwêyit, wâposwa ê-wî-kakwê-nipahâyit. ||| Then presently he saw his little sister going out to snare rabbits.
"tânêhki ôma kâ-ôh-ispayik, nisîmis?" itêw. ||| “How has this happened, little sister?” he asked her.
ômisi itêw awa iskwêsis: "ê-kî-mêscihtât kimisinaw." "kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwa kî-mêscihêw." "nayêstaw piko kôhtâwiyinaw pimâtisiw," itwêw awa iskwêsis. ||| Said the girl, “Because our sister has killed all in the place. She has exterminated the people. “Only our father is alive,” said the girl.
mistahi pakwâtam awa nâpêw. ||| The man was deeply shocked.
"êkwa mistahi namôya ê-sâkôcihiht, âta ê-pâskisoht," itwêw awa iskwêsis. ||| “And she has not been overcome, even by shooting,” said the girl.
êkosi êkwa, "tânisi kê-kî-tôtamân?" itêyihtam awa nâpêw. ||| Then, “What shall I be able to do?” thought the man. “It seems that the only way is for you to ask her where is her mortal spot. Ask her. ‘Surely someone has put you up to this!’ she will say to you. ‘No! It is only that you are so greatly endowed with supernatural power, that you cannot be killed,’ you will say to her.”
tâpwê kîwêw awa iskwêsis. ||| Accordingly the girl went home.
nîso wâposwa nipahtamâk ôhi ostêsa. ||| Her brother killed two rabbits for her.
ômisi itwêw: "nôhtâ," itêw, "nistês niwâpamâw," itêw ôhtâwiya, "êwakoni ôhi ê-nipahtamawit." "'kakwêcimâhkêhk tânitowihk ê-ohci-nipit,' itwêw ana." ||| She spoke thus: “Father,” she said to her father, “I have seen my brother; he it was killed these for me. ‘Ask her in what spot a wound would cause her death,’ he says.”
â, tâpwê awa mayaw ôhi ê-takohtêyit, mitoni misiwê êsa ê-miswâkaniwit awa iskwêw. ||| Then truly, as soon as that other had arrived, that woman was wounded all over her body.
êkwa tâpwê kakwêcimêwak. ||| Then accordingly, they asked her.
"tânêhki kâ-ôh-nôhtê-kiskêyihtamêk?" "nama cî ahpô kikosisiwâw kâ-kî-kîwôtêt niwî-kakwê-nipahik?" itwêw êsa awa iskwêw. ||| “Why do you want to know? Is it not perhaps that your son who visited here wants to kill me?” said the woman.
"hâ, namôya, nitânis!" "'mâskôc mistahi manitôwiw,' ê-itêyimitân, kâ-ôh-nôhtê-kiskêyihtamân tânimatôwihk ta-onipiwiniyan." ||| “Oh, no, my daughter! Because I thought of you, ‘Doubtless she is greatly endowed with spirit power,’ is why I wish to know in what part you have your vital spot.”
"hâ, nôhtâ, âta nikiskêyihtên ê-wî-kakwê-nipahikawiyân, kâ-ôh-kakwêcimiyan!" itwêw awa iskwêw; "nisitihk tawâyihk." ||| “Ho, father, I do know that you are asking me because an attempt is to be made against my life!” said the woman; “It is in the middle of my foot.”
êkwa tâpwê mayaw ê-sipwêhtêyit awa, sêmâk itohtêw awa oskinîkiw, ôhtâwiya ê-nitawi-wâpamât mîna okâwiya. ||| Then, as soon as she had departed, the young man came to see his father and mother.
"hwâ, 'nitâwisitânihk nitonipiwinin; êwako ohci êkâ awiyak kâ-ôh-kî-nipahit,' itwêw êsa." ||| “Ha, ‘At the sole of my foot is my vital spot; that is why no one can kill me,’ she says.” Then the young man said, “Point the ends of some sticks. Then you will stick them upright in the ground everywhere. Then she will prick herself on them. That is the way we shall kill her,” said the young man.
mayaw ê-sipwêhtêyit, misiwê cimatâwak miscikosa. ||| As soon as she had gone away, they stuck the little slivers everywhere into the ground.
tâpwê ê-takohtêyit, "mahti asamik!" ê-itikocik, sêmâk mâci-kîhkâmêwak. ||| And so, when she came and told them, “Give me to eat!” at once they began to revile her.
"kêhcinâ awiyak êkosi ê-kî-itikoyêk, kâ-ôh-kâh-kîhkâmiyêk!" itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Surely someone has told you to do this, that you all insult me!” said the woman.
"êha; ôta kî-takohtêw nistês," itwêw awa iskwêsis. ||| “Yes; my brother has been here,” said the little girl.
iskotêw êsa ohci pakamahwêw ôhi omisa. ||| And then with a burning brand she struck the woman, her sister.
tâpwê piko êkosi isi wayawîyâmôwak. ||| Then at once, they fled out of the lodge.
êkosi êkwa awa iskwêw otihtinêw ôhi oskotâkaya, ôhi mâna kâ-otinât wâh-nipahtâkêci maskwayâna. ||| Then the woman seized her mystic dress, the bearskin robe which she always took when she was about to kill.
mayaw ê-ati-pimipayit awa iskwêw, mâka mîna ê-kwêskimot, sêmâk otâwisitânihk kisisin. ||| As soon as the woman dashed along, changing, as always, her bodily form, at once she ran a sliver into her sole.
êkota êsa kî-nipahâw êwako iskwêw, mihcêt ayîsiyiniwa ê-kî-nipahât. ||| And so there that woman was slain who had killed so many people.
kayâs êsa nêhiyawak, misâw ôtênaw; wîkiwâwa întaw-mîkiwâhpa. ||| Among the people of old there was a large town; their houses were ordinary lodges of skin.
mihcêtiwak awâsisak. ||| There were many children.
kîtahtawê ê-pipohk mihcêt awâsisak mâ-mêtawêwak mistikwa; sôsimêwak, mitâtaht nîsosâp. ||| At one time, in winter, many children were playing with sticks; they were throwing snow-darts, twelve of them.
êkwa sôsimâna êkoni mitihtêwak. ||| They followed the snow-darts.
awiyak itê poyoyici osôsimâna, êkotê ta-ôh-pê-kîwêcik. ||| From wherever anyone's snow-dart stopped in its course they would go home.
piyis nîso piko ayisiyiniwak. ||| At last only two were left.
piyisk nêwâw na-nipâwak; ê-otâkosihk êkwêyâk otihtêwak osôsimâna, êwako ê-apisîsisit osîmimâw, êwako nâpêsis osôsimâna. ||| Four nights they slept on the way; not till the next morning did they reach the snow-dart of the smallest one, the youngest brother, that boy's snow-dart.
êkosi êwako iskwêyâc otihtêwak nêwâw mwêhci ê-nipâcik. ||| This one they reached last, after four nights.
êkosi osîhtâwak mistikwa ohci wîkiwâw. ||| Thereupon they built a tent for themselves out of sticks.
mwêhci mitâtaht ê-tipiskâk, êkwa mistahi mâyi-kîsikâw. ||| On the tenth night came a great storm.
nêwo-tipiskâw êkoyikohk mispon. ||| For four nights it snowed.
êkosi nôhtêhkatêwak. ||| So they began to be hungry.
kîtahtawê osôsimâna otinêw; wayawîw; pakamisimêw: "mâcîk!" itêw. ||| Then at one time, he took his snow-darts; he went outside; he threw them on the ground: “Hunt!” he told them.
êkosi âsay ê-wâpahk, kayâhtê apiyiwa pîhcâyihk osôsimâna. ||| Thereupon, when daylight had come, there suddenly within the lodge lay his snow-darts.
êkwa wayawîw: wiyâs mistahi wayawîtimihk astêw. ||| Then he went outside: a great store of meat lay outside the lodge.
êkosi êkwa pîhtokatâw. ||| Accordingly he brought it in.
êkosi êkwa awâsisak mîcisôwak. ||| So the children ate.
tahtwâw ê-tipiskâk mispon. ||| Every night it snowed.
êkwa wanihâwak; wîkiwâhk wanihâwak. ||| They were lost; at home they were given up as lost.
kapê-pipon êkotê ayâwak. ||| All winter they stayed there.
kîtahtawê êkwa, "kîwêtân!" tâpwê sipwêhtêwak. ||| Then at one time, “Let us go home!” So they set out.
êkosi ê-tipiskâk takohtêwak. ||| At nightfall they arrived.
êkosi, "tânitê ê-kî-ayâyan?" ||| then, “Where have you been?”
"ê-kî-papâ-mêtawêyân." ||| “Playing about here and there.”
êkosi kitahamâk ôhtâwiya. ||| His father forbade him to do that.
"kâ-kî-wîcêwacik namôya cî awiyak kimisi-wanâcihâw?" ||| “You have not brought to grief any of those who went with you?”
"namôya awiyak; kahkiyaw nipêsiwâwak." ||| “Not one; I have brought them all home.”
"êkosi kiyâm kanawêyimik," itwêw pêyak kisêyiniw. ||| “Then you may as well take care of them,” said an old man.
êkosi nôhtêhkatêwân. ||| For his people there were starving.
êkosi wîhtamwak mîciwin wiyâs mistahi ê-ayâcik itê kâ-kî-itohtêcik. ||| So they told that they had much food over at the place where they had gone.
êkosi kotakihk têpwêw kisêyiniw, ta-nâtahkik ayîsiyiniwak mîciwin, itê kâ-kî-itohtêcik awâsisak. ||| Then the old man called out at the other lodges that the people were to fetch food from the place where the children had been.
tâpwê mistahi pêtâwak. ||| They really brought a great deal.
ê-takohtêcik, "tânita, tânisi êsi-kaskihtâyêk mîciwin mistahi kâ-ayâyêk?" ||| When they arrived, “But how did you manage to have so much food?”
"nisôsimân ê-mâh-minahot." ||| “Because my snow-dart killed game.”
"hâw, nitawâc kâ-osôsimânisit kika-isiyîhkâson." ||| “Very well, then your name shall be Little-Snow-Dart.”
kîtahtawê ê-nîsicik awâsisak mâka mîna sôsimêwak. ma-mitihtêwak. ||| Then again, at another time the two children threw snow-darts and followed them.
êkoni. nikotwâsik ê-nipâcik otihtêwak osôsimâniwâwa. ||| After six nights on the way they reached their snow-darts.
kotaka mîkiwâhpa êkotê kiyôtêwak. ||| There they visited some other lodges.
tâpwê pêhtâkwan ê-takohtêcik. ||| The report went round that they had come.
kisêyiniw pêyak: "takosin kâ-osôsimânisit." "mistahi manitôwiw;" "êkâ wiya mawinêhohk;" "nama wiya ka-kî-sâkôcihâwâw." ||| One old man said, “Little-Snow-Dart has come here. He has great spirit-power. Do not attack him; you will not be able to defeat him.”
êkosi ê-nîpiniyik, "êkwa ayîsiyiniw wî-ohpikihitôw." "nîkân ôtê kika-âpacihikowâw êwako ana kî-ohpikit." "êkosi kaskihtâw kî-ohpikit ana." "kika-âpacihikowâw êwako." "nama wiya miywâsin kita-môtoyêk." ||| Then, when summer had come, “Now mortal man is to come into the generations of his life. In the time ahead he will make use of you, that one who is now to come into life. In this way he will be able to live. He will make use of you. It is not good that any longer you should eat one another.”
âtiht wâkayôsak, âtiht mostoswak êwako ôtênaw mîkiwâhpa, kêhciwâk ê-nipahitocik. ||| Some were bears and some were buffalo who lived there in the same village of tents but killed each other.
"êkosi nanânisk sakâhk ki-otaskînâwâw," itêw wâkayôsa. ||| “And so in different places of the woods you shall have your place of abiding,” he said to the bears.
"êkwa kiyawâw paskwâhk kika-otaskînâwâw." "maskosiya ka-mîcinâwâw." "êkosi mâka niwî-kîwân." ||| And you others shall dwell on the prairie. You shall eat grass and herbs. And now I shall return to my home.”
takohtêwak wîkiwâhk. ||| They arrived at their camp.
"tânitê ê-kî-itohtêyan mâka mîna?" ||| “And where did you go this time?”
"â, ê-kî-papâ-mêtawêyân." ||| “Oh, I have been playing here and there.”
"â, pônihtâ; êkâya kîhtwâm papâ-mêtawê." "osâm ka-misi-wanâcihâw awâsis, konita kâ-papâmâcihoyan;" "nama wiya tahki ka-sâkôcihâw ayîsiyiniw." ||| “Now, stop it; never again go about to play. For you will bring the children to grief wandering about in this needless way; not always will you defeat people.”
"namôya." "kâkikê kahkiyaw êkwa nisâkôcihâwak, ê-mâ-mitonêyimakik aniki kâ-wî-ohpikicik." "osâm namôya ta-kî-miyo-ohpikiwak ayîsiyiniwak, tâpitawi maci-nôcihitoyêko." "êkosi kiyawâw ispimihk kika-otaskînâwâw." "êkwa niya asinîwacîhk nika-otaskîn." "kâkikê nika-pamihâw ayîsiyiniw ana kâ-ohpikit." "êkosi piko ta-isi-ohpikihitôw ayîsiyiniw." "osâm nikitimâkêyimâw, êkâ wîhkâc ê-nahi-papâmâcihot ayîsiyiniw, tahki ê-astâhâyêk ta-ma-misi-wanâcihâyêk." "êwako piko ê-wâpahtamân, ta-miyopayik ôma askiy." ||| “No. For all time now I have defeated them all, with the thought of those who are to come into life. For mortal men will not be able to live properly, if you continue like this in your evil pursuit of one another. Therefore, you shall have your abode up aloft. And I shall dwell in the Rocky mountains. For all time I shall take care of mortal man, that one who is to come into life. Only so will the generations of man be able to live. For I have taken pity on mortal man, who can never roam about since you afright him with the fear that you will bring him to destruction. Only in this way do I see a good future course for this earth.”
êkosi nanânisi-sipwêhtêwak. ||| Accordingly they departed in various directions.
wîsta sipwêhtêw; kiwâpamâw asinîwacîhk ê-cimasot; wîhkimâkosiwak; sîhtapihkwanak isiyîhkâsôwak. ||| He too departed; you can see him standing in the Rocky mountains; pleasant is their scent; fir-cones they are called.
êwako yâhki kahkiyaw kâ-kî-paskiyawât tahto kâ-macihtwâyit. ||| That is he who of yore overcame all the beings of evil power.
kîtahtawê wîkiwak ayîsiyiniwak, nîso okimâwak, pêyak macihkiwis ôhtâwiya. ||| Once upon a time some people dwelt in a place, and there were two chiefs, and one of them was Silly-Fellow's father.
kîtahtawê awâsisak mihcêt sôsimêwak. ||| Then at one time many of the children played at throwing snow-darts.
"mahti kakwêciyawêhitotâk ôma kâ-sôsimêyahk kahkiyaw, mahti awîna nêhtâ-sôsimêt, awîna wâhyaw kê-pahkisiniyit," itwêw pêyak awâsis ôhkoma ê-ohpikihikot. ||| “Let us all try to outdo each other throwing snow-darts, and see who is the best at it, whose snow-dart lands farthest away,” said one child, who was being brought up by his grandmother.
êkwa ati-otinêwak sôsimâna. ||| Then they went and picked up their snow-darts one after the other, as they came to them.
piyis pêyak osôsimâna ayîsisiniyiwa kônihk. ||| At last only one boy's snow-dart was left lying on the snow.
"êkâ wiya awiyak nôhtaw kita-kîwêw!" itwêw. ||| [no translation] At last they found it had gone into a wood. As they followed the track of that snow-dart, across a far stretch of prairie there, into the woods it had sped.
kîtahtawê ê-otâkosiniyik, awîna ôma, kî-mihtiskâyiw. ||| Presently, as evening came on, they were deep in the woods.
kêkâc pahkisimoyiw; kwayask ômisi isi cimasoyiwa osôsimâna. ||| It was near sunset; there, standing straight upright in the snow, like this, was the boy's snow-dart.
êkoyikohk yôtiniyiw; misponiyiw. ||| Just then the wind began to blow; it snowed.
"ôta ayâtâk." "ka-kawacinânaw." "mânokêtâk; mihtikowâhp osîhtâtâk." "âtiht maskosiya kita-otinamwak." "misîhtâk kîkinaw," itwêw. ||| “Let us stay here. We might freeze. Let us set up a shelter; let us build a hut of wood. Some of you are to gather grasses. Make our hut big,” he said.
piyisk ê-tipiskâyik, kîsihtâwak. ||| At last, when night came, they had finished it.
ê-wâpaniyik, kêyâpic mistahi mâyi-kîsikâyiw. ||| The next morning it was still very stormy weather.
"êkâya kîwêtâk." "ka-kawacinânaw," itwêw; "nikohtêk." "êkwa ôta iskwâhtêmihk câh-cahkâkonêhamok." "pêsîhkok kisôsimâniwâwak kahkiyaw," itwêw. ||| “Let us not go home. We should freeze,” he said; “Gather firewood. And here by the door, dig away the snow. All of you bring me your snow-darts,” he said.
kahkiyaw êkwa wêskwâhtêmihk cimahêw kahkiyaw sôsimâna. ||| Then he stuck all the snow-darts on end into the floor, opposite the doorway.
êkwa kîkisêpâ wayawîw, ê-otinât kahkiyaw sôsimâna. ||| Then, early in the morning, he went out, taking all the snow-darts.
mâcîk!" itwêw awa, sôsimâna kâ-kî-itisahomiht, kâ-kî-pimitisahomiht. ||| Hunt!” he sang whose snow-dart had been followed to that place, had been pursued across the land.
êkwa ê-otâkosiniyik, "kahkiyaw pîhtokêk." "ôta tawayâk iskwâhtêmihk mîna wêskwâhtêmihk," itwêw. ||| Then, in the evening, “All of you indoors. Form two lines from the doorway to the opposite wall,” he ordered.
piyis êkosi tôtamwak. ||| Soon they had done this.
kîtahtawê awa kâ-kî-mitihtimiht osôsimâna êwako kâ-pîhtokêkociniyit osôsimâna. ||| Then presently the snow-dart of him whose snow-dart had been tracked, came flying into the hut.
ê-kî-itaskôtoyit osôsimâniwâwa, êkosi isi itaskôtoyiwa. ||| in the order in which their snow-darts had gone, in that order they now came, one following the other.
kahkiyaw mihkôwiyiwa sôsimâna. ||| All the snow-darts were stained with blood.
"êkâya wayawîk!" itwêw. ||| “Do not go out of the house!” he said.
kêtahtawê kâ-pa-pitihkohtiniyik kîkwaya. ||| Presently some things were falling with a repeated thud.
ê-kî-isi-pitihkohtiniyik kêkway, "ê hâw, êkwa wayawîk!" itwêw awa kâ-kî-mitihtimiht osôsimâna. ||| When those things had fallen with a thud, “There, now go out!” said he whose snow-dart had been tracked.
awîna ôhi, nanâtohk pisiskiwa, okwâskwêpayihôsa, nanâtohk êhtasiyit pisiskiwa, ôki ê-minahocik sôsimânak, êwakonik ê-âpohtêcik, osâm ê-manitôwit awa osôsimâna kâ-mitihtimiht. ||| What was there, but all kinds of game-animals, jumping deer, all the game-animals there are? For these snow-darts had killed game, and it was they were supplying meat, so much of a manitou person was he whose snow-darts had been tracked.
ômisi itêyihtam: "ôki awâsisak ta-wani-kiskisiwak." "wîkiwâhk namôya ta-pîkiskâtamwak!" itêyihtam. ||| thus he thought: “Let these children forget. Let them not get homesick!” he thought.
"hâw, osîhtâk têsipicikana kiyâm mihcêt!" itwêw. ||| “Come, set up a great many drying frames!” he said.

êkosi tôtamiyiwa ôhi awâsisa. ||| The children did as he said.

wayacîwîw. tahki paswêmâkwaniyiw. ||| All the while he smelled the scent of fat meat.

"kâ-misâk nipiy êkotê niwî-ayân," itwêw. ||| “Now then, when the order of things is completed, as many of you as have cast it up, trees shall be your food, and grasses, of some. For, ‘Go lay down a law!’ I was told. You, my brother, when mortal men grow forth and flourish, ‘Lynx,’ they will call you; you will find your sustenance in the woods; and so you, my brother, have found your place. And you, my father, ‘Mink,’ mortal man will call you; by the water you will have your domain; but all kinds of things you will eat, the flesh of little snakes; from whatever creature has flesh you will get your life. êkoyikohk êskwâk âtayôhkêwin. ||| This is the end of the sacred story.
kêtahtawê ayîsiyiniwak ê-mihcêtokamikisicik, kihtimiw êkota pêyak oskinîkiw, kâkikê ê-pimisihk. ||| Once upon a time, where some people dwelt, a certain youth was so lazy that he was always lying down.

kêtahtawê ê-pa-pimisihk, kâ-pê-kitotiht. ||| Then at one time, as he lay there, someone came and called to him.

pâh-pôtâcikêw: misiwê ocêpihka misiwê itamoyiwa, aspin mâna itâmâskîhk, êkwa ê-mamâhcikwahpitikot ocêpihka ohci. ||| He blew forth his breath more than once: on all sides roots clung fast, roots from way down under the ground, until he was firmly tied down by the roots.
"nôsisê, ômisi kika-isiyîhkâson," itik; "watapîwiyin kika-isiyîhkâson." "êkâ wiya kitâpamâhkan awiyak," itik omosôma; "ôhi cikahkwâna kakwê-nawatina." Here to the stick of the doorflap I shall tie these things which I give you, and also your tobacco-pouch,” his grandfather told him; “Do not look at anyone that may come to you.”
"êha, nimosô," itêw. ||| “Yes, grandfather,” he told him.
tâpwê namôya kêkway wî-kitâpahtam iskwâhtêm. ||| Accordingly not at all would he look at the door.

"kêhcinâ miyosiwak!" itêyihtam awa oskinîkiw. ||| “Surely they must be beautiful!” thought the young man.

"tâpwê kipakwâtikonaw kîtimosinaw watapîwiyin!" itik; "niyâ, kîwêtân, nitayîm!" itwêyiwa. ||| “Truly, we are disdained by our sweetheart Pine-Root!” they said to him; “Come, let us go home, sister-wife!” they said.

â, pêhtam awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth heard that.

kîtahtawê ê-papâmohtêt awa wacôw-awâsis, apisîs sîpîsis kâ-wâpahtahk. ||| Presently as Clotkin went about, he came upon a little brook.
êkotê itohtêw akâmihk awa oskinîkiw kâ-miyosit. ||| The handsome youth crossed it and went somewhere on the other side.
ê-ati-kîwêt, kâ-wâpamât nôtokêsiwa, "nôsisê, nayômin; nama nikî-âsowahên," ê-itwêyit. ||| On his way back, he saw an old woman, who said, “Grandson, take me on your back; I cannot get across.”
"â nôhkô, âsokanis nika-osîhtân, ta-pimohtêyan." ||| “Grandmother, I shall make a little bridge so you can walk.”
"nôsisê, nika-pakastawêpayin," itwêw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| “Grandson, I should fall into the water,” said the old woman.
piyisk, "ahaq," itêw. ||| At last he consented.
nayômêw, ê-âsowahohât. ||| He took her on his back and carried her across.
"hâ, nôhkô, êkota êkwa," ê-itât, namôya wî-nîhtakosîw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| But when he said to her, “Now, grandmother, here you are!” that old woman would not get down.
ê-wî-kakwê-pahkwatinât ôhi nôtokêsiwa, nama kî-pihkohêw; tâpiskôc pîwâpisk ospitoniyiwa oskâtiyiwa mîna. ||| When he tried to pull the old woman off, he could not get her free; like iron were her arms and legs.
êkwa namôya wî-kîwêw, ê-nêpêwisit, nôtokêsiwa ê-nayômât. ||| So then he did not care to go home, [sic] for he ws ashamed to be carrying the old woman on his back.
piyisk ômisi ôta wî-kipihkitonênik. ||| But in time, here, like this, she had him almost strangled.
ê-wâpamât awa omisimâw, mistahi pâhpiw, "tânêhki okistêyimoh wacôw-awâsis, nôtokêsiwa kâ-pê-nayômât?" ê-itwêt. ||| When that elder sister saw him, she laughed much, saying, “What was he so proud about, this Clotkin who comes with an old woman riding on his back?”
awa oskinîkiskwêw ê-wâpamât onâpêma, mistahi pakwâtâw. ||| When the young woman saw her husband, she was greatly distressed.
ê-âta-pakamahwât, namôya kî-nipahêw. ||| Although she clubbed her, she could not kill her.
kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwak ê-âta-pakamahwâcik, namôya kî-nipahêwak ôhi nôtokêsiwa. ||| Though all the people clubbed her, they could not kill that old woman.
piyisk wî-nipiw awa wacôw-awâsis. ||| Finally Clotkin was near to death.
piyisk ômisi tôtam, ômisi, êkâ ê-kî-pîkiskwêt. ||| At last he did like this, like this, being unable to walk.
êkwa watôwa êwakoni ê-mâwacihimiht, êkota ê-kawipayihot. ||| Then, where the lumps of clotted blood had been laid in a heap, thither he flung himself.
awa nôtokêsiw ôhi watôwa êkoni piko miciminêw. ||| The old woman was holding fast to nothing but a clot of blood.
awa wiya wacôw-awâsis ohpimê ohci pasikôw. ||| But Clotkin rose from the ground off at one side.
awa nôtokêsiw ômisi itwêw: "nôsisê, kiyâm nika-pimâtisin?" itwêw. ||| The old woman said, “Grandson, please let me live!”
"êha," itwêw wacôw-awâsis. ||| “Yes,” said Clotkin.
êkosi otinêw ôhi nôtokêwa, ositiyihk ê-miciminât. ||| With that he took the old woman, holding her by the feet.
ômisi itwêw: "hâ, nôtokêsiw, cêskwa ôtê nîkân ayîsiyiniwak tita-ayâwak;" "ômisi tita-itwêwak,"- pakamisimêw; osit piko ôma nôkwaniyiw awa nôtokêsiw,- "'kôhkôhk-ôyaman' tita-itwêwak!" ||| Thus he spoke: “Now, old woman, off in the future there will be mortal men; this they will say;” - and he flung her down; only one foot could be seen of that old woman - “‘Pig-vermilion,’ they will say!”
"âstam!" itêw ôhi kâ-kî-pakwâtikot iskwêwa. ||| “Come here!” he said to the woman who had scorned him.
ê-âta-mâtoyit, otinêw; mistik ê-cimasoyit, êkota pakamisimêw. ||| Weep as she might, he took hold of her; where a tree stood, he flung her against it.
"êkota kiya ka-kikamon;" "'wâsaskwêtôw' kika-itikwak ayîsiyiniwak." "nama nânitaw kika-itâpatisin; osâm kikistêyimon-" "hâ, âstamitik kahkiyaw ayîsiyinîtik!" "hâw, nimanâcimâkan, kiya kitawâsimisak kiwîkimâkan, â, sipwêhtêk! ||| “This is where you will stay fast; ‘Glowing fungus,’ the people will call you. You will not be good for anything; you are too conceited. - Now, come hither, all you people!
niyâk!" "kiyawâw ôtê nîkân ayîsiyiniwak'wâkayôsak' ka-isiyihkâtikowâwak,-" "êkwa kiyawâw,"- kotaka,- "kiyawâw mahîhkanak, êkwa kotakak kiyawâw mahkêsîsak, êkwa kotakak kiyawâw pisiwak, kiyawâw kîhkwahâhkêsak!" ||| Now then, my father-in-law, you, your children, and your wife, now, depart! Be off! Off in the future mortal men will name you ‘Bears.’ - And you” to the others “you they will call wolves, and you others foxes, and you others lynxes, and you coyotes!”
êkosi kahkiyaw pisiskiwa êkwa osîhêw. ||| So in this wise he made all the animals.
êkwa sipwêhtêw; kîwêw; owîkimâkana mîna wîcêwêw. ||| Then he went from there; he went home; he took his wife with him.
nistwâw ê-nipâcik, otihtêw ôhtâwiya mistanaskwa. ||| When they had been two nights on the way, he came to his father, Badger.
miywêyihtam awa mistanask ê-otihtikot okosisa. ||| Badger was glad that his son had come to him.
êkosi pêyak tipiskâw êkota ê-ayât, ômisi itêw: "hâ, nôhtâ, osâm kikî-miyo-pimâtisin." "hâ, kiya ôtê nîkân ayîsiyiniwak'mistanask' kita-itwêwak êyakonik ayîsiyiniwak." "kika-môwikwak, osâm ê-kî-miyopimâtisiyan." "- êkwa kiya,"- okâwiya,- "'sikâk' kita-itwêwak;" "mistahi ka-miyo-pimâtisin; nama wîhkâc ka-tahkwamâwak ayîsiyiniwak." "hâ, niyâ! ||| Then when he had been there one night, he said to him, “Now, father, you have been too good a creature. So now, mortal men in the time to come will say of you, ‘Badger,’ these mortal men. They will eat you, because you have been a good creature.
'wînicoyêsîs' kika-itikwak ayîsiyiniwak; kika-môwikwak." ||| And you” to his mother “‘Skunk,’ they will say; a very good creature you will be; never will you bite people. There, go! ‘Polecat,’ mortal men will call you; they will eat you.”
"êkwa niya watôw; mihko ôma, watôw niya." "êkosi êkwa nama kêkway." ||| “As for me, a blood clot, blood am I. And, therefore, nothing at all.”
êkosi êkwa nama kêkway âcimowin. ||| And so there is nothing at all of my tale.
êkoyikohk ê-iskwâk âtayôhkêwin. ||| This is where the sacred story ends.
kîtahtawê pêyak awa nâpêw êkwa pêyak iskwêw, owîkimâkana, nîsiwak. ||| Once upon a time there were two people, a man and his wife.
kîtahtawê awâsisa ayâwêwak. ||| Presently they had a child.
êkotê êkwa ê-ay-ayâcik, pisisik mâcîw awa nâpêw. ||| There where they dwelt the man would always hunt.
piyisk wâpamêwak awâsisa, nâpêsis. ||| And so, in the course of time, they had a child, a boy.
êkwa êkota ay-ayâwak. ||| They stayed in that place.
piyisk misikitiw awa nâpêsis. ||| In time the boy grew big.
pôti miyosiw awa nâpêsis. ||| He turned out handsome.
miywêyimêwak; sâkihêwak okosisiwâwa. ||| They loved him; they were fond of their son.
namôya kêkway atoskêw awa nâpêsis. ||| They boy did not work at all.
tahki miywâsiniyiwa otayôwinisa, ê-kaskikwâtahk awa iskwêw okosisa otayiwinisiyiwa. ||| His clothes were always good, for the woman sewed her son's clothing.
êkosi piyisk oskinîkiw awa awâsis. ||| So in time the child became a young man.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw ômisi itwêw: "mahti kakwê-nipa ocêk," itêw ôhtâwiya. ||| Then that young man spoke as follows: “Pray, try to kill a fisher,” he said to his father.
miyâkîki awa nâpêw wî-kakwê-wâpamêw ocêka. ||| And so that man tried to get sight of a fisher.
kîtahtawê wâpamêw ocêka; nipahêw. ||| Presently he saw a fisher; he killed it.
êwakoni osîhêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth prepared it.
ê-kîsihât, otastotiniw. ||| When he had finished it, he wore it as a hat.
mîna acosisa ayâw, nikikwayâna ê-opîhtatwânit, êkota ê-asiwatêyiki wîpisisa awa oskinîkiw. ||| He had arrows, too, and used an otterskin for his quiver, to put his arrows in, that youth.
oskotâkay pahkêkin ê-pîmikitêyik; otâsa mîna ê-pîmikitêyiki. ||| His coat was a hide ornamented with quill-work; and his breeches, too, were worked with quills.
kîtahtawê ômisi itwêw: "nôhtâ, kiyânaw cî piko ê-ayîsiyinîwiyahk?" itêw. ||| Then at one time he spoke thus: “Father, are we the only human beings there are?” he asked him.
"namôya." "misiwê ayâwak ayîsiyiniwak." "mâka namôya ê-miywâtisicik, pisisik ê-mêtawêcik." "kîspin sâkôcihitocik, misi-wanâcihitowak; namôya miywâtisiwak." ||| “No. Everywhere are people. But they are not good, they always contend. When they defeat one another, they destroy each other; they are not good.”
"kah!" itwêw awa oskinîkiw; "mahti nika-kakwê-wâpamâwak kotakak ayîsiyiniwak," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “Just think of it!” said the yout; “I should like to try and see the other people,” said the youth.
mihtâtam awa kisêyiniw mîna awa iskwêw, okosisiwâwa ê-sâkihâcik. ||| The old man was sorry at this, and the old woman, for they cherished their son.
"mâskôc ta-misi-wanâcihôw," ê-itêyimât okosisiwâwa, mâtôw awa iskwêw. ||| “Surely he will go to his undoing,” thought the woman of their son, and wept.
êkosi namôya kî-kitahamawêwak ê-wî-sipwêhtêyit okosisiwâwa. ||| And so they were not able to keep their son from going forth.
"wâpahki nika-sipwêhtân," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “Tomorrow I shall go,” said the youth.
"hêhêhêy!" itwêw awa nâpêw; "nikosis, êkâ wiya âpihtâ-kîsikâhk isi itohtê!" itêw okosisa. ||| “Dear me!” said the man; “My son, do not go in the direction of noon!” he told his son.
"ahaq," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “Very well,” answered the youth.
tâpwê ê-wâpaniyik, sipwêhtêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| Accordingly, when day broke, the youth departed.
ômisi itwêw: "nôhtâ, nêkâ, nika-takosinin, êkâ misi-wanâtisiyâni." "têpiyâhk ê-wî-wâpamakik ayîsiyiniwak," itwêw awa oskinîkiw, ê-postastotinêt. ||| He said, “Father, mother, I shall come here, if I am not destroyed. It is only that I want to see the people,” said the youth, as he put on his hat.
"hâw, ocêkiwayâna kâ-otastotinit nitisiyîhkâson," itwêw, ê-ati-wayawît. ||| “Now then, Fisherskin-Hat is my name,” he said, as he stepped out of the house.
mâtoyiwa okâwiya, ê-atamiskâkot. ||| His mother wept as she said farewell to him.
êkosi sipwêhtêw, ê-pimohtêt. ||| So he set out and walked along.
kapê-kîsik pimohtêw, êkâ ê-pîsimôwiyik itêhkê isi ê-itohtêt. ||| All day he walked, walking in the direction where there is no sun.
kîtahtawê ê-pimohtêt, ê-otâkosiniyik, kâ-wâpamât pihyêwa. ||| Presently, as he walked along, in the evening, he saw a partridge.
pimwêw; nipahêw, "nika-môwâw, ita kapêsiyâni," ê-itêyihtah. êkosi ê-kî-otinât, ati-pa-paskopitêw. ||| He shot it and killed it, thinking, “I shall eat it when I camp for the night.” So he took it and plucked it.
ê-âyapâskwêyâyik ê-pimohtêt, kîtahtawê kâ-wâpahtahk wîstêpahkwayikamikos. ||| As he walked by a place where there were clumps of trees, presently he saw a little lodge of smoked-up leather.
êkota itohtêw, "mahti kêkway ôma ita ê-ayât?" ê-itêyihtah. ||| He went there, thinking, “I wonder what sort of person stays there.”
ê-takohtêt iskwâhtêmihk, "pîhtokê, nôsisimis!" kâ-itwêt nôtokêsiw. ||| When he reached the doorway, “Come in, grandchild!” said an old woman.
ê-pîhtokêt, pôti ôhi kî-pêyakoyiwa. ||| When he went in, there she was, all by herself.
"ta-tawâw!" itwêyiwa; "nêtê ohci-api," itik. ||| “Come in!” she said; “Sit over there!” she told him.
ôhi pihêwa kâ-tahkonât miyêw ôhkoma. ||| He gave his grandmother the partridge he was holding.
"kitatamihin, nôsisimis; êkotôwahk ninôhtê-môwâw!" itwêyiwa. ||| Thank you, my grandchild; this is exactly what I was wanting to eat!” she said.
êkosi êkwa ômisi itik: "nôsisimis, âyiman ôma itê kâ-itohtêyan." "nawac wâpahki kîwêyin." "âyimisiwak ôma ayîsiyiniwak," itik ôhkoma. ||| Then she told him thus: “Grandchild, it is a hard place to which you are going. It would be better if you went home tomorrow. Hard to deal with are the people there,” his grandmother told him.
"namôya, nôhkô; osâm âsay nipê-sipwêhtân," itêw. ||| “No, grandmother; for now I have already set out this way,” he answered her.
"kah!" itik; "awahê mâka, nôsisê!" itik. ||| “Dear me!” she said to him; “Then be careful, grandson!”
tâpwêw paminawasoyiwa, pêyak mînis ê-pakâhtâyit êkwa pêyak cîsâwânis. ||| And so she set about cooking a meal, putting in the pot a single berry and a single bit of chopped meat.
ê-kitâpamât, "kêhcinâ namôya nika-kîspon!" itêyihtam. ||| When he observed her, “Surely I shall not eat my fill!” he thought.
ômisi itwêw awa nôtokêsiw: "nôsisimis, kika-kîspon ôma," itêw. ||| Thus spoke his grandmother; “My grandchild, you will eat your fill of this,” she told him.
"yahê!" itêyihtam awa oskinîkiw, "namôya êcika awa kê-kî-mâ-mitonêyimak!" itêyihtam. ||| “Goodness me!” thought the youth, “Plainly, I shall not be able to think about her!” he thought.
katât cî ka-mâ-mitonêyimin?" itik. ||| Why should you have to think about me?” she said to him.
kiskêyihtamiyiwa ê-mâ-mitonêyimât. ||| She knew that he had taken her as his object of meditation.
êkosi êkwa asamik; êkosi isi pakitinamâk otaskihkoyiwa. ||| So then she gave him to eat; she gave him her cooking-pot, just as it was.
êkwa ê-mîcisot, kahkiyaw mâna ê-otinahk, ê-saskamot, êtâpici askihkosihk, kêyâpic nîso kî-astêyiwa. ||| As he ate, whenever he took up the whole contents and put it into his mouth, when he looked at the little pot, there lay the two morsels again.
piyisk âhkamêyimôw ê-mîcisot. ||| At last he ate all the faster.
piyisk kîspôw; namôya kî-kitâw ôhi kâ-asamikot ôhkoma. ||| At last he had enough; he was not able to eat up the things his grandmother had given him to eat.
"namôya nikî-kitân, nôhkô," itêw. ||| “I cannot finish it, grandmother,” he said to her.
"nah, nôsisimis tâpwê ê-yîkicikâwît ê-mîcisot, êkâ kâ-kî-kitât nimînisima, nikîsitêpôwina!" itik. ||| “Dear me, truly my grandchild merely pecks at his food, seeing that he cannot finish my little berries, my bits of cooked meat!” she said to him.
piyisk mistahi tipiskâyiw. ||| By now it was deep night.
"nôsisê, kinêstohtâh; kawisimo," itik. ||| “Grandson, you must be tired from walking; like down,” she told him.
kawisimôw; wîsta kawisimôw awa nôtokêsiw. ||| He lay down; the old woman, too, lay down.
êkosi ê-wâpaniyik, ê-waniskâcik, mîna mîcisôwak. ||| When dawn came, when they got up, they ate again.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, "â, nôsisê, êkây ôma ôta ê-ohci-sâkâstêk, êkây itohtê!" "âyimisiw êkota ê-ayât," itik; "ôtê isi nâtakâm isi itohtê," itik. ||| When they had eaten, “Now then, grandson, do not go in this direction whence comes the morning light! Hard to deal with is he who dwells there,” she told him; “Go this way, toward the north,” she told him.
"êha," itwêw, ê-sipwêhtêt, ê-pimohtêt. ||| “Very well,” said he, as he departed and continued his journey.
wâhyaw ê-ihtât, "mahti tânêhki ôma kâ-ôh-kitahamawit nôhkom?" itêyihtam. ||| When he had gone a long ways, “I wonder why my grandmother warned me away from this place?” he thought.
kîtahtawê, kêkâc ê-âpihtaw-kîsikâyik, kâ-wâpamât ayîsiyiniwa ispatinâhk ê-apiyit. ||| Presently, when it was almost noon, he saw someone sitting on a knoll.
ohpimê êkota wî-ati-itohtêw, ê-pasikôyit, êkotê kâ-isi-waskît. ||| He was going to walk on, leaving the place to one side, when the other arose, in the very direction toward which he had turned.
êkâ âta ê-wî-itohtêt, mâka êkotê isi ispayiw. ||| Although he tried not to go there, yet he landed in that direction.
piyisk âmaciwêw, ê-wâpamât. ||| At last he went up the hill where he saw the other.
pôti ôhi mistahi mâyâtisiyiwa ayîsiyiniwa, ê-mâskâwikanêyit, ê-apisîsisiyit, maskwayâna ê-kikasâkêyit, ê-pê-nâtikot, konita ê-pê-ostostotamiyit ômisi ê-itikot: "ocêkiwayâna kâ-otastotinit, mâna kipê-mêtawâh!" itik; "kayâs, 'wî-papâ-mêtawêw,' kikî-itikawih!" ||| There he saw that that man was very ugly, hunchbacked and small, and clad in a bearskin coat; this man came to meet him, and as he came, had a fit of coughing, and said to him: “Fisherskin-Hat, you always were coming here to play!” he told him; “Of old, ‘He will go about engaging in contests,’ was said of you, you know!”
"namôya ê-papâ-mêtawêyân," itêw. ||| “It is not going about to engage in contests I am,” he told him. “Oh, don't say that! Only do let us have a contest!” the other said to him.
"îh nêma kâ-sakâk kiwâpahtên cî kâ-pikihtêk?" ||| “Do you see that clump of trees right over there, where the smoke is rising?”
"mistahi aniki êkota ê-miyosicik oskinîkiskwêwak nîso ê-ayâcik." "êwakonik kika-astwâtonânaw," itik. ||| “Very beautiful are the two young women who live there. They will be the prize,” the other told him.
"â, kiyâm mâsihitotân!" itik. ||| “Oh, please do let us wrestle!” the other said to him.
êkwa astâw otakohp mîna wîpisisa; kahkiyaw otayiwinisa; otastotina piko namôya ahêw. ||| Then he put down his blanket-robe and his arrows, and all his clothes; only his hat he did not put down.
"hâ, kitastotin mîna ahi," itik. ||| “Ho, set down your hat, too,” the other told him.
êkosi isi mâsihitôwak. ||| So then they wrestled.
mwêhci ê-nayawapit, âcikêwêpahwêw; kawiwêpinêw. ||| At last, just as he was getting out of breath, he tripped the other and threw him; he got him down.
"â, ocêkiwayâna kâ-otastotinit, nipisohên kiskât, kâ-ôh-sâkohiyan." "pêyakwâw!" itik. ||| “Ho, Fisherskin-Hat, I stumbled over your leg, that is why you have got the better of me. Once more!” the other said to him.
âsay kisâkohitin," itêw. ||| I have beaten you now,” he answered the other.
ê-mêkwâ-mâsihitocik, kwâskwêwêpinêyiwa otastotina. ||| While they were at grips, the other knocked his his hat up into the air.
êkosi êkwa sâkohik; kaskâwikanênik, ê-sâposkâkot, ê-maskamikot omiyosiwin. ||| Thereupon the other overcame him; he broke his back and entered his body, taking away his good looks.
kâ-kî-wâpamât ê-isinâkosiyit, êkosi isinâkosiw awa oskinîkiw. ||| As he had seen the other to look, such was now the appearance of that youth.
êkwa ôhi kâ-mâyâtisiyit miyosiyiwa. ||| And that other, who had been ugly, was now handsome.
ê-kitâpamât, "mistahi piko ôma ê-miyosiyân, kâ-kîsinâcihit, ê-maskamit nimiyosiwin!" itêyihtam. ||| When he looked at him, “Greatly has he injured me as to my good looks, robbing me thus of my beauty!” thought he.
otayiwinisa otinamiyiwa, ê-postayôwinisêyit, otastotina mîna. ||| The other took his clothes and put them on, and his hat as well.
"êkoni anihi kitayiwinisa, maskwayânêtâs!" itik. ||| “These here are your clothes, Bearskin-Breeches!” the other told him.
otayiwinisiyiwa êkwa postayôwinisêw. ||| Then he put on the other's clothes.
wiyaskoc êkwa pisisik ostostotam. ||| And now he, instead of the other, was incessantly coughing.
ayisk namôya tâpwêhtam kâ-kî-itikot ôhkoma. ||| Well, he had not followed his grandmother's advice.
"hâw, maskwayânêtâs, nitawi-wîwitân!" itik. ||| “Well now, Bearskin-Breeches, let us go take our wives!” the other told him.
tâpwê sipwêhtêwak, ê-itohtêcik ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| So they set out to go to those young women.
cîki ê-ihtâcik, kâ-pê-wayawiyit ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| When they were near the place, out came the elder sister.

"êha, wâpahki ka-sipwêhtânânaw." "kitimâkisitokênik; mâka kayâs kâ-pê-nakatakik," itêw. ||| “Very well, tomorrow we shall depart. No doubt, they are in want; after all, it is a long time since I left them to come here,” he answered her.
tâpwê iyikohk ê-wâpaniyik, wawêyîwak, ê-wî-sipwêhtêt, tâpwê kahkiyaw awiya ayîsiyiniwa ê-atamiskâkocik. ||| Accordingly, when day broke, they made ready for his departure, and truly, all the people bade them farewell.
êkosi ê-sipwêhtêcik, nîswâw ê-kî-kapêsicik, êkoyikohk wâpahtamwak wîkiwâw ita kâ-itohtêcik. ||| So they departed, and when they had camped twice on the way, they came in sight of his people's home to which they were going.
"hâw, nika-nîkânipahtân;" "nika-wîhtamawâw nitawi nôhtâwiy ê-wî-takohtêyahk," itêw. ||| “Here, I shall run ahead; I shall go tell my father that we are about to arrive,” he said to her.
ê-takohtêt, pôti namwâc mamîhk kêkway wâpahtam, ta-mîciyit. ||| When he got there, behold, he saw nothing at all of things to eat.
ê-pîhtokêt, pôti ôhi ay-apiyiwa ôhtâwiya okâwiya, "hây hây! ||| When he entered the lodge, there sat his father and his mother; “Splendid!
nikosis takosin!" ê-itwêyit, ê-atamiskâkot, konita ê-mâtoyit okâwiya, iyikohk ê-miywêyihtamiyit ê-wâpamikot. ||| Our son has come!” they cried, as they greeted him, and his mother wept for no reason at all, except that she was so glad to see him.
êkosi nanâskomoyiwa. ||| And so they gave thanks.
"â, kisiwâk pê-ihtâw ê-pê-wîcêwak iskwêw, mîna kôsisimiwâw," itêw. ||| Now, close by on her way hither is a woman who has come here with me, and also your grandchild,” he told them.
nanâskomôw awa kisêyiniw. ||| The old man spoke his thanks.
"mahti!" itwêw awa nôtokêsiw, ê-wayawît, ê-nitawi-nakiskawât ostima êkwa ôsisima. ||| “Oh, I must!” exclaimed the old woman, and went out of the lodge, to go meet her daughter-in-law and her grandchild.
ita ê-nakiskawât, ocêmêw. ||| When she met her, she kissed her.
"nistim!" itêw; "pêsiw nôsisimis!" itêw. ||| “My daughter-in-law!” she said to her; “Give me my grandchild!” she said to her.
miyik, mîna êkoni ê-oy-ocêmât. ||| The other gave her the child, and him too she kissed many times.
êkosi ê-ati-sipwêhtêcik, ôsisima ê-nayômât. ||| Then they left that spot and went on, and she carried her grandchild.
ê-takohtêcik, ê-pîhtokahât, sêmâk awa kisêyiniw nitomêw ôsisima, ê-oy-ocêmât. ||| When they arrived, and she took him into the house, at once the old man called his grandson, and kissed him repeatedly.
êkosi êkota êkwa ê-ay-ayâcik, êkwa mîna ê-mâh-mâcît awa oskinîkiw, êkwa awa oskinîkiskwêw mistahi ê-atoskêt, ê-pamihât omanâcimâkana. ||| So then they stayed there; and the young man always hunted, and the young woman worked hard, taking care of her parents-in-law.
kitimâkêyimêw mitoni, iyikohk ê-miyo-pamihât osikosa osisa mîna. ||| She was very kind to them and took good care of her mother-in-law and of her father-in-law.
aspin êkoyikohk ê-iskwâk âcimowin âtayôhkêwin. ||| And this is the end of the story, of the sacred story.
pêyak ôtênaw ê-misâk, kayâs êsa ê-môtocik. ||| There was a certain large town, of old, when, as we are told, they ate each other.
êkosi awa iskwêw ê-okimâwit, piyêsiw-iskwêw, napatê ôtênaw ê-tipêyihtahk, êkwa napatê ôtênaw ê-tipêyihtahk êwako okimâw mahîhkan; nâpêw êwako. ||| And there a woman was chief, a Thunderbird-Woman, who ruled over one-half of the town; and over the other half there ruled as chief a Wolf; a man was this one.
otôskinîkîmiwâwa ê-astwâtocik, ê-mêtawêcik, ê-manitowi-mêtawêcik, pêyak siyâkôcihihci, êkosi owîcêwâkana ê-nipahimiht, ê-môwimiht, êkosi piko"ê-môtocik" isiyîhkâtêw. nanâtohk, ôki ayîsiyiniwak kâ-itwêhk, nanâtohk pisiskiwak êwakonik. ||| They used their followers as prizes of the contest, of their manitou contests, so that, whenever one was defeated, then his followers were killed and eaten; that is what is called “eating each other.” Various kinds, those who were called men, various kinds of beasts they were.
êkwa awa mahîhkan kâ-okimâwit, êkota ohci pêyak oskinîkiskwêw, osîmisa, nâpêsisa ê-apisîsisiyit, ê-kitimâkêyimât, ê-sâkihât, ôhtâwiya okâwiya kotaka wîcisâna kahkiyaw ê-nipahimiht, wiyawâw piko nîso ê-pimâtisicik osîmisa, ômisi itêyihtam: "nika-sipwêhtân;" "nisîmis awa mâskôc wî-pimâtisici," ê-itêyihtahk; "osâm kitimâkisiw, ê-apisîsisit," itêyihtam; "hâw, anohc kâ-tipiskâk, mistahi ta-mâyi-kîsikâw! ||| Then in the part where the Wolf was chief, a young woman from there, who had a small brother whom she cared for and loved, when her father and mother and all her other brothers and sisters had been killed, and only the two, she and her little brother were left alive, then thus she thought: “I shall go away; perhaps it will be possible for my little brother here to live,” she thought; “He is too pitiful, the little fellow,” she thought; “So then, tonight let there be very bad weather!
ta-mispon!" itwêw; "nika-sipwêhtân, êkâ ta-kiskêyimikawiyân itê kâ-wî-itohtêyân." êkosi itêyihtam. ||| Let it snow!” she said; “I shall go away and no one shall know whither I go.” So she thought.
tâpwê ê-tipiskâk, mistahi mâyi-kîsikâw, ê-mispohk. ||| Really, when night ell, there was very bad weather, and it snowed.
êkwa miywêyihtam awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| Then the young woman was glad.
mayaw mistahi ê-tipiskâk, wawêyîw, wîkiwâw ê-manisahk, ispimihk ita ê-mâyâtahk ê-wêpinahk. ||| As soon as it was very dark, she made ready; she cut down her lodge and threw it aloft into the storm.
êkwa otanâskâna, otakohpa, kahkiyaw ta-kî-âpacihtât kêkwaya otinam, ê-kîsi-wawêyît, mostoswayân êkota ê-wêwêkahpitahk ocayânisa. ||| And her sleeping-mats and her blanket-robes and all the things she would have occasion to use, she took, when she had made ready, and she wrapped all her possessions in a buffalo robe.
êkosi isi ê-sipwêhtêw, ê-otâpêt ôhi ocayânisa, tâpiskôc napakitâpânâsk, êkosi isi ê-otâpêt, êkwa osîmisa ê-nayômât. ||| In this way she set out, dragging her belongings, dragging them as if on a flat sled, and carrying her little brother.
isi mistahi mâyi-kîsikâyiw. ||| The storm kept on all night, while she walked on.
kapê-tipisk mâyi-kîsikâyiw, ê-pimohtêt. ||| At last day dawned; the bad weather did not abate.
piyisk wâpaniyiw; âhci piko mâyi-kîsikâyiw. ||| All that day it stormed.

ê-wâpaniyik, êkwa mâtoyiwa osîmisa, ê-nôhtêhkatêyit. ||| Then, when day broke, her little brother cried, because he was hungry.
êkosi nicawâc wawêyîw, ê-sipwêhtêt. ||| Yet she needs made ready to go on.

tâpwê miskam sakâhk ê-ihkatawâyik, ê-nipîwiyik, wâsakâm mistahi ê-sakâyik, êkota kapêsiw. ||| There she pitched camp.

êkwa mihta ê-otinahk, êkota kâ-otinahk mihta, tapasîyiwa êkota ohci wâposwa. ||| Then, as she gathered faggots, from the place where she gathered faggots, some rabbits scampered forth.

êkwa nisîmis kê-mîcisot!" itêyihtam. ||| Now my little brother shall eat!” she thought.
kîwêhtahêw; iyâyaw osîhêw, ê-wî-kîsiswât, ê-wî-asamât osîmisa. ||| She took it back with her; eagerly she prepared it to cook, that she might give her brother to eat.

mwêhci ê-pahkisimoyik, kâ-matwê-ma-mawimoyit wâposwa. ||| Just at sunset she heard a rabbit squeal.
itohtêw: pôti pêyak. ||| She went there: there was one.
"êkosi namôya ta-nôhtêhkatêw nisîmis," itêyihtam. ||| “So my little brother will not go hungry,” she thought.
êkwa ê-tipiskâyik, mâ-mitonêyihtam, "pitanê êkâ ohci awiyak miskawit!" ê-itêyihtahk; "kahkiyaw ayîsiyiniwak êkosi isi ayâwak êtokê?" ê-itêyihtahk; itê kâ-ôh-itohtêt ôhi ayîsiyiniwa kâ-itâtisiyit, kâ-nâh-nipahitoyit, ê-môtoyit, "êkosi êtokê kotakak mîna isi ayâwak?" ê-itêyihtahk, êwako ohci kâ-ôh-itwêt. ||| Then, in the night she meditated, thinking, “Would that no one might ever find me! Are all persons, I wonder, even so?” she thought; the way those people were in the place whence she had come, they who always killed and ate each other, because she thought, “Are others, I wonder, that way too?” was why she spoke thus.
tâpwê miywêyihtam ê-pêyakot, "êkosi mâskôc nika-ohpikihâw nisîmis," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| Truly, she was glad to be alone, for she thought, “In this way, perhaps I shall bring up my little brother.
êkota tahto-kîsikâw mihta ê-otinahk, mîna ê-tâpakwêt ê-mihcêtiyit wâposwa, tâpwê têpiskâyiki, kâ-nipâci, wiyâpahk ê-nâtât wâposwa, mitoni miywêyihtam mâh-mihcêt ê-nipahât. ||| There every day she gathered firewood and snared many rabbits; and truly, after each night, when she had slept and in the morning fetched the rabbits, she was very glad that she continued to kill many of them.

kîtahtawê êkwa, kinwêsk ita ê-ayât êkwa, osîmisa êkwa misikitiyiwa. ||| Then in time, when she had been there a long while, her brother grew larger.
êkwa osîhtâw acosisa, osîmisa ê-osîhtawât, ê-wî-kakwê-nihtâ-pimohtahkwêhât. ||| Then she made arrows for her brother, meaning to teach him to be a good marksman.
tâpwê piyisk nihtâ-pimohtahkwêyiwa; piyisk nakacihtâw kêkway ta-wî-kakwê-nipahât awa nâpêsis. ||| Really, in the end he was a good shot; in time the lad became skilled to the point where he wanted to try to kill something.
kîtahtawê sakâhk ê-papâmohtêt awa nâpêsis, wâpamêw wâposwa. ||| Presently, as he walked about in the wood, he saw a rabbit.
ê-wî-kakwê-nipahât, tâpwê nipahêw. ||| When he tried to kill it, really, he killed it.
ha, miywêyihtam, ê-pîhtokahât. ||| He was glad, and brought it into the lodge.

êkwa tâpwê kotaka osîhtâw acosisa, nawac ê-misâyiki, "kêkway cita-ôh-miyo-nipahtât," ê-itêyihtahk. piyisk ê-kîsihtât, êkwa êwakoni ê-âpacihtât awa nâpêsis, tâpwê mâh-mihcêt nipahêw wâposwa. ||| And so she made some more arrows, larger ones, thinking, “So that he can do well at killing things with them.” At last, when she had finished them, and the lad was using them, really he killed many and many rabbits.
êkwa awa iskwêw pîkonam apahkwâson, ê-osihtât osîma cita-otâsiyit, mîna ta-oskotâkâyit. ||| Then the woman tore pieces from the tent-covering and made something for her brother to wear as breeches and as a shirt.
êkwa kêkâc oskinîkiw awa nâpêsis. ||| By this time the lad was almost a young man.
mistahi miyosiw awa nâpêsis. ||| He was very handsome.
êkwa êkota ôma ê-ay-ayâcik, kîtahtawê wâposwa ê-wî-kakwê-wâpamât, ê-papâmohtêt, kâ-mâtâhât pêyak apisi-môsosa. ||| Then, as they dwelt there, presently, as he was walking about, trying to get sight of rabbits, he came upon the track of a dwarf moose.
"kîkway awa?" itêyihtam; "mahti nika-kakwê-wâpamâw," itêyihtam. ||| “What kind of creature is this?” he thought; “Suppose I try to get a look at him,” he thought.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpamât. ||| Presently he saw it.
"kêkway awa?" itêyihtam; "mahti kê-kî-nipahak," itêyihtam. ||| “What kind of creature is this?” he thought; “Let me see if I can kill him,” he thought.
tâpwê pimwêw; tâpwê nipahêw. ||| So he shot an arrow at it; really, he killed it.
ê-otihtât, namôya nisitawêyimêw kîkwaya ôhi. ||| When he went up to it, he did not know what manner of beast it was.

apisi-môsos awa," itik. ||| This is a dwarf moose,” she told him.

awa oskinîkiskwêw ê-wâpamât, "hây hây hây!" itwêw; "êkwa nisîmis êwakoni kî-otanâskânit." ||| When the young woman saw it, “Splendid! Splendid!” she exclaimed; “Now my brother can have this one for his sleeping mat.”
