ê-kiskêyimikot ê-kîsi-paminawasot, waniskâyiwa. ||| When he knew that she had finished cooking, he got up.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, êkoyikohk wayawîw awa oskinîkiw, ê-nitawi-kîskatahwât asâmâhtikwa, ê-wî-osîhât asâma, mîna ê-wanihikêt, nîso ê-osîhtât wanihikana. ||| When they had eaten, the youth went out of doors, to cut sticks for snowshoes which he intended to make, and to set traps, two traps which he had built.
iyikohk ê-takohtêt, ê-wâpahtahk awa iskwêw mistikwa ê-pîhtokatâyit, ê-kî-asamât, êkwa otinam ôhi mistikwa awa iskwêw, ê-tihkisahk. ||| When he came back when the woman saw that he was bringing sticks of wood, after giving him his meal, the woman took the sticks, and melted some fat.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot awa oskinîkiw, ê-môhkotahk, asâma ê-osihât, êkoyikohk kiskêyihtam awa iskwêw ê-osîhâyit asâma. ||| When the youth had eaten, and was whittling the sticks to make snowshoes, then the woman knew that he was making snowshoes.
êkwa osîhtâw ôma pahkêkin, ê-wî-wâskâsahk awa iskwêw. ||| Then she prepared that rawhide for cutting round the edge.
tâpwê ê-wâpahk, ê-nitawâpahtahk owanihikana, pêyak tasôhêw kihîwa, êkwa pêyak nikikwa. ||| Then, the next morning, when he went to look at his traps, he had trapped an eagle and an otter.
êwakoni mîkwana kahkiyaw otinêw. ||| He took all the feathers.
êkwa ôhi kihîwa pahkonêw awa iskwêw, ê-pâswât. ||| And the woman skinned the otter, and dried the skin.
"mâskôc ê-wî-otastotinit nisîm," itêyihtam. ||| “No doubt my brother wants a head-dress,” she thought.
piyisk êkwa osîhêyiwa asâma. ||| Then he made also his snowshoes.
ê-kîsi-osîhât, êkwa awa iskwêw otinêw, ê-askimâtât ôhi asâma, ê-pâswât. ||| When he had done making them, the woman took the snowshoes and threaded them with the thongs, and dried them.
êkosi ê-kîsi-pâsoyit, kîkisêpâ iyikohk mîna ê-waniskât, kayâhtê mâka mîna namôya nipâyiwa osîma, âsay ê-mâcîyit, ê-wî-ay-atoskêt wayawîtimihk, pahkêkinwa ê-ay-osîhtât, "ê-miywâsik nika-osîhtân nîkinân," ê-itêyihtahk. iyikohk ê-otâkosihk, wayawîtimihk ê-nîpawit, kîkway kâ-pêhtahk. ||| And so, when they had dried, when in the morning she got up, again her brother no longer slept, but had gone hunting; so she went about her work outside the lodge, tanning hides, thinking, “I shall improve our dwelling.” Towards evening, as she stood outside the door, she heard something.
ê-nitotahk, pôti kâ-pê-nikamoyit awiya; itêyihtam. ||| As she listened, it appeared that someone was singing as he came; so it seemed to her.
"nisîm êtokê," itêyihtam. ||| “I wonder if it is my brother,” she thought.
ê-pîhtokêt, kiyipa âsay kisiwâk kâ-pêtwêwitamiyit. ||| When she went inside, quickly from close by came the sound of that person.
kisiwâk ê-pê-ayâyit, kîskowêyiwa. ||| When he had come near, he broke off his song.
pôti osîma kâ-matwê-takosiniyit. ||| It was her brother, coming home with song.
mihta ita ê-astêyiki, êkota ê-têhciwêpinâyit otasâmiyiwa, kâ-kitoyit. ||| Where the faggots lay, on top there he threw his snowshoes, and as he did so, they gave a call.
"êwakonik êcika kâ-pê-nikamocik!" itêyihtam awa iskwêw. ||| “And so it is they who came a-singing!” thought the woman.
pôti ê-wayawît, pisisik askêkin kâ-pêtâyit. ||| When she went out, he was bringing nothing but fresh hides.
ê-otinât, ê-wâ-wâpahtahk, pôti êsa iyâpêyisa kâ-wâpamât, êskana ê-kikamoyit, êkwa waskasîyiwa. ||| When she took it, and looked at it, she saw that it was the skin of a young bull, with the horns and the hoofs.
êwakoni mâh-maniswêw, ohpimê ê-ahât. ||| These she cut off, and laid them aside.
askêkin mîna ôma mihtihk têhtastâw. ||| The hide she laid also on top of the firewood.
"ê-wî-otakohpit êtokê," itêyihtam. ||| “Doubtless he wants a blanket-robe,” she thought.
êskana ôhi mîna owaskasîyiwa pîhtokahêw, ê-ahât. ||| The horns and the hoofs she brought indoors and put them down.
êkwa ê-kîsi-mîcisot awa oskinîkiw, otinêw ôhi êskana, iskotêhk cîki êkota ê-ahât, ê-wî-kêcikwahahk anihi oskana. ||| Then, when the young man had eaten, he took the horns and placed them close to the fire, to take out the bone.
piyis kahkiyaw otinam anihi oskana. ||| At last he took all the bone.
ê-wâpahk pêyakwanohk apiw; namôya mâcîw, ê-osîhât êskana. ||| The next morning, he sat in one place; he did not hunt, but prepared the horns.
êkwa awa iskwêw ôhi mostoswayâna ê-osîhât, êkwa, "nôhtêhkatêtokê!" ê-itêyimât osîma, ohtapiwinihk kâ-ôh-pasikôyit osîma. ||| And the woman, preparing the buffalo robe, just as she thought of her brother, “He must be hungry!” even then her brother rose from his settee.
êkosi êkota, "tânêhki êtokê?" itêyihtam. ||| Then, “I wonder what is the matter!” she thought.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw ê-kî-wî-kimotamawât omisa mîkisisa. ||| But it was because that youth meant to steal his sister's wampum-beads.
êkosi, "kîkway êtokê?" itêyihtam awa iskwêw. ||| So, “What can it be?” thought the woman.
piyisk kîsihêw ôhi êskana awa oskinîkiw, mîna ôhi waskasiya. ||| At last the youth finished preparing the horns and the hoofs.
ê-tipiskâk kîsihêw awa iskwêw mostoswayâna. ||| By nightfall the woman finished the buffalo robe.
iyikohk ê-wâpahk, êkoyikohk kikamohêw awa oskinîkiw ôhi êskana, mîna ôhi waskasîyiwa, ê-wî-otakohpit awa oskinîkiw. ||| When the next day dawned, the youth attached to it the horns and the hoofs, to make him a blanket-robe.
ômisi itêw omisa: "nimisê, mîkisisak cî kitayâwâwak ê-wâpiskisicik, êkwa ê-askihtakosicik?" itêw. ||| He said to his sister, “Sister, have you wampum beads that are white, and some that are blue?” he asked her.
êkosi awa iskwêw otinêw, ê-itisinamawât. ||| Accordingly, she took them and handed them to him.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw ê-sîkahot, ê-kîsi-sîkahot, ôhi mîkisisa ê-pâh-pôtâtât, mâh-mihcêtiyiwa kâ-wâpiskisiyit ôhi mîkisisa ôta ostikwânihk, napatê wêscakâsa kahkiyaw ê-tâpiskawât mîkisisa, tâpiskôc ê-wâpistikwânêt napatê, êkwa napatê ôhi kâ-askîhtakosiyit mîkisisa ê-itamoyit ostikwânihk, ê-mîkisistikwânêt. ||| Then the youth combed his hair, and when he had combed it, breathed upon those beads, whereupon a great many of those white wampum-beads were on his head there; he had threaded all the hairs on one side of his head with the beads, just as though his hair were white, and on the other side the blue beads were strung on his head; he was a Wampum-Head.
êkwa tâpwê miyosiw awa oskinîkiw: oskotâkay ê-pîmikitêyik, sihkosiwayâna ê-kikamoyit, mîna otâsihk ê-kikamoyiki, ê-pîmikitêyiki, mîna êkota sihkosiwayâna ê-kikamoyit, êkwa ôhi nikikwayâna ê-otastotinit, otakohpa êskana ê-kikamoyit êkwa waskasîyiwa êkota ê-kikamoyit. ||| Then truly handsome was that young man; his coat was ornamented with quill-work and with tassels of weasel skins, and some were on his breeches, and they, too, had quill-work, and they had weasel-skins on them, and he had a headgear of that otterskin, and on his robe were horns, and hoofs were on it.
êkwa tâpwê miyosiw awa oskinîkiw, êkosi êkwa ê-kîsi-nânapâcihisot. ||| Then truly handsome was that youth, when in this guise he had decked himself.
êkota êkwa tahto-kîsikâw êkwa ê-mâcît, tahto-kîsikâw pêyak ê-nipahât mostoswa, piyis mistahi mîciwin ayâwak. ||| Then, as he hunted each day, and each day killed a buffalo, in time they had a plenty of food.
kîtahtawê kinwêsk êkwa ita ita ê-ayâcik, kîtahtawê nama wiya wî-mâcîw awa oskinîkiw, pêyakwanohk ê-apit. ||| Then at one time, when they had long dwelt there, then presently the youth did not care to hunt, but sat still in one place.
iyâta-asamâci osîma, namôya wî-mîcisôw awa oskinîkiw, tahki ê-kâmwâtapit. ||| Although she gave her brother food, the youth would not eat, but sat listlessly there.
ômisi itêyihtam awa iskwêw: "kêhcinâ wîsakêyihtam nisîm," itêyihtam. ||| The woman thought, “Surely my brother is in pain.”
piyisk nîso-kîsikâw namôya nânitaw itohtêw awa oskinîkiw, tahki ê-kâmwâtapit. ||| At last two days passed and the youth had not gone anywhere, but sat all the time inactive.
kîtahtawê ômisi itêw awa iskwêw: "â nisîmis, ê-wîsakêyihtaman cî?" "kikaskêyihtamihin, êkâ ê-mîcisoyan," itêw. ||| Then the woman asked him, “Brother, are you in pain? You make me sad, not eating,” she told him.
"namôya," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “No,” said the youth.
êkosi namôya wîhtamawêw kêkway. ||| Thus he did not tell her what it was.
ê-wâpahk, mîna ê-waniskâcik, ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, "hâw, nimisê, ôma kâ-isinâkosiyân, kâ-isîhoyân, êkosi cita-isinâkosiw oskinîkiw;" "mîna otasâma êkosi ta-isinâkosiyiwa." "ôma kâ-âpihtâwi-kîsikâk, êkotê tita-ohtohtêw oskinîkiw." "ôta iskwâhtêmihk êkota kita-ahêw otasâma." "'hâw, niwîkimâkan, ê-pê-nâtitân!' kika-itik." "êkosi itiski, êkâya kitotâhkan." "ê-wî-pê-mawinêhot êwako awa oskinîkiw," itêw omisa; "niwî-mâcîn ôtê isi êkâ ê-pîsimowik; êkotê kâkikê kâ-isi-mâcîyân, êkotê nika-ohtohtân," itêw omisa; "kîspin kitotaci, nika-sâkôcihik; mâka êkâ kitotaci, êkosi nika-sâkôcihâw," itêw omisa; "kwayask âpihtâ-kîsikâki, êkospî kâ-wî-takohtêt," itêw omisa. ||| The next morning, when they got up and had eaten, “Now then, my sister, even as I look, even as I am dressed, so a young man will look; even his snowshoes will look so. From the direction of noon that youth will come. Here by the door he will place his snowshoes. ‘Come, my wife, I have come to fetch you!’ he will say to you. When thus he speaks to you, do not address him. One who comes to challenge me is that youth,” he told his sister; “I shall hunt over here, in the direction where the sun never goes; from this direction, where always I do my hunting, from this direction I shall come,” he told his sister; “If you speak to him, he will defeat me; but if you do not speak to him, then I shall defeat him,” he told his sister. “Exactly at noon, that is when he will come,” he told his sister.
êkosi ê-wawêyît, ê-mâcît. ||| With that he went out of the lodge, on his hunt.
êkwa awa iskwêw ômisi itêyihtam: "mâskôc kinwêsk ê-nîsiyâhk nisîmis, mâskôc awa êkwa ê-akâwâsit," itêyimêw osîma; ê-môhcôwit awa iskwêw, kâ-itêyimât osîma. ||| Then the woman thought thus: “Perhaps because my brother and I so long have been alone together, perhaps now he has fallen in love with me,” she thought concerning her brother; because she was silly, she thought thus of her brother.
êkosi aspin kâ-mâcîyit osîma. ||| So her brother was off hunting.
êkwa ê-kiskêyihtahk ê-wî-âpihtâ-kîsikâyik, pîhtokêw, ê-paminawasot awa iskwêw. ||| When she knew that noon was at hand, she went indoors, and prepared her meal.
ê-wî-mîcisot, mwêhci ê-kîsi-paminawasot, kîtahtawê kêkway pêhtam; âpihtâ-kîsikâhk itêhkê isi kâ-pêhtahk ê-pê-nikamoyit awiya. ||| As she was about to eat, just as she had done cooking, she heard something; in the direction of noon she heard someone who came a-singing.
"êkosi mâna kâ-itihtâkosiyit nisîm otasâma," itêyihtam. ||| “Even so my brother's snowshoes always sound,” she thought.
kisiwâk ê-pê-ihtâyit, kîskowêyiwa. ||| When he had come near, he ceased from his song.
êkwa mosis êkwa pê-pimohtêyiwa. ||| And now he was in sight, walking hither.
ôtê iskwâhtêmihk ê-pê-takohtêyit, otasâmiyiwa êkota âsosimêyiwa. ||| When he came to the doorway, there he leaned upon his snowshoes.
ê-pê-pîhtokêyit, mitoni naspitawêyiwa osîma. ||| When he came inside, greatly he resembled her brother.
"yâhki ay-apiw awa niwîkimâkan!" "ê-pê-nâtitân ôma!" kâ-itikot. ||| “From of old my wife sits here! It is to fetch you I have come!” he told her.
osîma ôhi kâ-isinâkwaniyiki otayiwinisiyiwa, êkosi isinâkwaniyiwa otayiwinisiyiwa. ||| As looked those clothes of her brother's, so looked this person's clothes.
mîna ôma ostikwâniyiw êkosi isinâkwaniyiw. ||| His head, too, looked exactly so.
namôya kitotêw awa iskwêw. ||| The woman did not speak to him.
ê-pê-nâtitân ôma! ê-wî-wîkimitân!" kâ-itwêyit. ||| It is to fetch you I have come!” he said to her.
ômisi itwêw awa iskwêw: "namôya êkosi ê-itêyihtamân, kâ-wî-kakwê-ohpikihitân, nisîmis!" itwêw awa iskwêw. ||| Thus spoke the woman: “It was not with the like of this in mind that I did my best to bring you up, my brother!” she said.
êkosi kâ-ati-pasikôt awa nâpêw. ||| At that the man rose to his feet.
"hâw, kê-wâpahk âpihtâ-kîsikâki, nika-takosinin, ta-pê-mawinêhwak nîci-mîkisistikwân," kâ-itwêyit; "cikêmâ ani ita awiyak nama nikitotik," kâ-itwêyit, ê-ati-wayawiyit, ê-ati-otinâyit otasâmiyiwa, êkosi ê-ati-pa-postasâmêyit. ||| “Very well, tomorrow at noon I shall come to challenge my fellow Wampum-Head,” he said; “Seeing that everywhere else no one ever speaks to me,” he said, and went out of the lodge, taking his snowshoes as he went, and putting them on.
mayaw ê-ati-sipwêhtêyit, kâ-ati-nikamoyit asâma. ||| As soon as he started away, the snow-shoes began to sing.
mistahi mihtâtam awa iskwêw ôhi ê-kitotât nâpêwa, âta ê-kî-wîhtamâkot osîma. ||| Very sorry was the woman that she had spoken to this man in spite of her brother's instruction.
pôti âpihtaw ê-otâkosik kâ-pêhtawât nâtakâm ohci ê-pê-nikamoyit asâma. ||| Then, in the middle of the afternoon she heard snowshoes come singing from the north.
êkoni êkwa osîma, mâka mîna ê-âpohtêyit. ||| It was her brother, bringing, as always, a treat of game.
mâka mîna otasâmiyiwa ê-têhciwêpinâyit, kâ-kitoyit asâma. ||| When he threw his snowshoes, as always, on the wood, the snowshoes gave a call.
ê-pê-pîhtokêyit, mistahi mihtâtam ê-kî-kitotât ôhi nâpêwa. ||| As he came into the lodge, deeply she regretted that she had spoken to that man.
ê-kî-nahapiyit osîma, asamêw. ||| When her brother had sat down, she gave him his meal.
êkwa ê-mîcisoyit, wiya atoskâtam ôhi wiyâsa kâ-pêtâyit osîma, ê-âh-akotât wayawîtimihk. ||| While he ate, she worked at the meats which he had brought, hanging them out of doors.
iyikohk ê-kîsi-atoskêt, ê-pîhtokêt, êkwa nahastâw otoyâkaniyiwa, âsay ê-kîsi-mîcisoyit. ||| When she had finished her work, she went indoors and put away her brother's dishes, for he had done eating.
"nimisê, tâpwê kikitimahin, kâ-kitotat ana nâpêw," itwêyiwa; "namôya ana ê-wî-wîkimisk," itik; "hâw, takohtêci, wâpahki, pê-mawinêhoci, ôta nika-ôh-kotâwaskamikîn;" "wiya mîna êkosi ta-tôtam." "pîhtokêci, wî-mawinêhoci, 'kiya nîkân!' nika-itâw ani." "tâpwêhtawici, êkota ta-ôh-kotâwaskamikîw;" "ômê ôta kâ-apiyân, êkota cita-ôh-sâkiskwêw." "êkosi nika-kîskikwêwêpahwâw." "ostikwân ohpimê ta-pahkihtin." "otinamôhkan anima ostikwân." "êkosi ôma miyaw ôma nika-miciminên." "mâka, êkâ otinamani ôma mistikwân, kâwi ta-tâpiskopayiyiw ostikwân." "êkosi nika-sâkôcihik." "hâ, êkosi, nimisê!" ||| “Sister, truly, you have brought me to an evil pass by speaking to that man,” he said; “His purpose is not to marry you,” he told her; “Now then, when tomorrow he comes to challenge me, at this spot I shall sink into the ground; he, in turn, will do the same. When he comes into the lodge to challenge me, ‘You first!’ I shall say to him. If he complies, there he will sink into the ground; and right here where I sit he will stick out his head from the ground. At that I shall slash off his head. He head will fall to one side. Do you then take his head. I shall hold fast to the body. But, if you do not take the head, his head will fly back into place. In this way he will overcome me. There, that is the way of it, sister!”
â, sêkisiw awa iskwêw. ||| Oh, that woman was frightened.
"piyisk niya mîna êkosi nika-tôtên, ta-kotâwaskamikîyân." "nîsta êkosi nika-tôtâk." "êkosi sêmâk tita-otinam nistikwân, ta-ati-wayawîhtatât." "kîspin êkosi ispayiki, sâkôcihici, itê kâ-pahkisimohk, êkotê tita-ohtohtêw nâpêw." "kahkiyaw otayiwinisa ta-mihkwahikâtêyiwa." "êwako ana ê-wî-pê-nâtisk, ê-wî-wîkimisk." "tâpwêhtawâhkan êwako, ê-miywâtisit," itik osîma awa iskwêw; "hâh, êkosi, nimisê!" ||| “Then I, too, shall do the same, I shall sink into the ground. He will do the same thing to me. Then at once he will take my head with him out of the lodge. If this happens, if he defeats me, then from the direction of the setting sun will come a man. All his garments will be made of red. He will come to fetch you; he will marry you. Give credence to him, for he is good,” her brother told her; “there, that is the way of it, my sister!”
ê-wâpahk, ê-kî-waniskât, êkwa ê-kî-mîcisocik, mitoni nânapâcihôw awa oskinîkiw, ê-wawêsit. ||| In the morning, when he got up and when they had eaten, the youth made a careful toilet and put on his finery.
piyisk kêkâc âpihtâ-kîsikâyik, namôya kêkway atoskâtam awa iskwêw, ê-kaskêyihtahk; ôma osîma, "mâskôc nika-sâkôcihik," kâ-itwêyit, êwako tahki ê-mâ-mitonêyihtah. piyisk âpihtâ-kîsikâyiw, âsay kâ-pêtwêwitamiyit, ê-pê-nikamoyit asâma. ||| It was almost noon, but the woman did not work at anything, for she was unhappy; she brooded without cease on her brother's words, “Perhaps he will defeat me.” At last it was noon, and already that person came noising it, snowshoes a-singing.
"hêh," itêyihtam, "mitoni êcika ôma ê-kakêpâtisiyân,‘ nisîm êtokê,’ kâ-kî-itêyihtamân!" itêyihtam. ||| “Alas,” she thought, “It is plain that I was most stupid to think, ‘Perhaps it is my brother!’” she thought.
ôta ê-pê-takohtêyit oskinîkiw, ôta iskwâhtêmihk âsosimêyiwa otasâmiyiwa. ||| When the youth arrived there, he leaned up his snowshoes in the doorway.
ê-pê-pîhtokêyit, "yah, nîci-mîkisistikwân, ê-pê-mawinêhotân!" kâ-itwêyit. ||| When he came into the lodge, “Ha, my fellow Wampum-Head, I have come to challenge you!” he said.
"ahaq!" itwêyiwa osîma. ||| “Yes!” spoke her brother.
ê-kitâpamât, tâpiskôc pêyak ayîsiyiniw êkosi isinâkosiyiwa. ||| When she looked at them, they looked like one and the same person.
"hâ, kiya nîkân, nîci-mîkisistikwân!" itimâwa osîma. ||| “Ha, you first, my fellow Wampum-Head!” her brother was told.
kiya kipê-mêtawân," itwêyiwa osîma. ||| It is you have come to play,” said her brother.
ita ê-apiyit, êkota wêh-kotâwaskamikîyit, osîma itahk ê-ohtiskawapiyit, êkota wêh-sâkiskwêyit, osîma omôhkomâniyiw ohci kîskikwêwêpahwêyiwa. ||| There where he sat, there he sank into the earth, and there in front of her brother as he sat, there he came sticking out his head, and her brother with his knife slashed through the other's neck.
itê kâ-apit awa iskwêw, êkota pahkihtin ôma ostikwân. ||| Toward where the woman sat fell that head of his.
otami-tapasîw awa iskwêw; namôya otinam. ||| She was taken up with fright; she did not seize it.
ôma ostikwân kâwi êkota tâpiskopayiyiw. ||| That head of his went back into place.
pê-wayawiyiwa; kâwi êkotê nahapiyiwa. ||| He emerged from the earth; he sat down again in his place.
"hâw, kiyaskoc mâka!" kâ-itimiht osîma. ||| “There, but now it is your turn!” her brother was told.
wawêyîyiwa; ita kâ-apiyit osîma, êkota wêh-kotâwaskamikîyit osîma. ||| He made ready, from where her brother sat, he sank into the earth.
nêhi kâ-pê-mêtawêyit ita kâ-isi-ohtiskawapiyit, êkota kâ-sâkiskwêt osîma. ||| In front of where he sat who had come to play, there her brother stuck out his head from under the earth.
ê-kîskikwêwêpahomiht osîma, itê ê-pahkihtiniyik otinam awa oskinîkiw, ê-ati-wayawît. ||| When her brother's head had been slashed off, that youth took it from where it fell, and started out of the lodge.
"ita nâha awiyak kî-ôh-sâkôcihit!" itwêyiwa, ê-ati-sipwêhtêyit, ê-sipwêhtatâyit ôho mistikwân. ||| “There is the one who, of all anywhere, could defeat me!” he said, as he started to go away, taking with him that head.
êkwa ma-mawimôw, ê-mâtot, osîma ostikwâniyiw ê-sipwêhtatâwiht. ||| Then she lamented, weeping, because her brother's head was taken away.
otinam osîma wiyawiyiw, ê-astât ohtapiwiniyihk. ||| She took up her brother's body, and placed it upon his settee.
namôya nipiw, ê-âta-sipwêhtatâwiht ostikwân. ||| He did not die, even though his head had been taken away.
yêhyêyiwa, ê-pa-pimisiniyit ohtapiwiniyihk. ||| He breathed, as he lay there, on his couch.
êkwa tahki ê-mâtot awa iskwêw, piyisk kinwêsk êkota ayâw, tahki ê-yêhyêyit osîma; mâka nama kêkway ostikwân. ||| Then, weeping without respite, at last a long time that woman stayed there, her brother all the while breathing; but he had no head.
êkosi kîtahtawê kâ-takohtêyit nâpêw, pahkisimôtâhk ê-ohtohtêyit. ||| Then, at one time, there arrived a man who came from the region of the setting sun.
ê-pîhtokêyit, tâpwê piko ohtapiwinihk nahapiyiwa, "ê-pê-nâtitân; ê-wî-wîkimitân," ê-itikot. ||| When he came into the lodge, really, he sat down directly upon her couch, saying to her, “I have come to fetch you; I mean to marry you.”
sêmâk nisitawêyimêw êwakoni kâ-kî-itikot osîma. ||| At once she recognized him as the one of whom her brother had told her.
"êha," itêw; "pita ka-mîcisonânaw," itêw. ||| “Yes,” she said to him; “But first let us eat,” she said to him.
ê-kîsi-paminawasot, êkwa mîcisôwak. ||| When she had prepared her meal, they ate.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, "hâw, wawêyî êkwa," itik. ||| When they had eaten, “Come, make ready now,” he told her.
"cêskwa pita," itêw; "pita nika-pônên, êkâ tita-âhkwacit nisîm," itwêw awa iskwêw, ê-wayawît, nêwo ê-otinât yôskihtakwa, êwakoni ê-pônât. ||| “Wait a bit,” she said to him; “First I must put fuel on the fire, that my brother may not freeze,” said the woman, and went out of the lodge; she took four sticks of crumbling wood and put them on the fire.
"haw," itwêw, ê-pakitinât, "êkâya wîhkâc âstawî!- hâw, êkosi!" ||| “There,” she said, as she set them down, “Never go out! Well, I am ready!”

êkosi nêtê, kêkâc ê-tipiskâk, takosin wîkiwâhk awa nâpêw. ||| Accordingly, over yonder, at nightfall, that man arrived at their dwelling.

tâpwê miywêyihtam awa iskwêw ê-wîcêwât nâpêwa. ||| Truly, the woman was glad to be with the man.

"hâw, namôya nika-mâcîn," itwêw; "osâm mistahi kika-atoskân." "êkwa awâsis ê-wî-ayâwat, namôya ninitawêyihtên ta-atoskêyan." "mâskôc wî-ohpikici awa awâsis kâ-wî-ayâwâyahk," itêw. ||| “Very well, I shall not hunt,” he said, “You would be working too much. Now that you are going to have a child, I do not want you to work. Perhaps the child we are to have will grow up,” he told her.
"êha," itêw awa iskwêw. ||| “Yes,” the woman answered him.
tâpwê namôya mistahi ôh-atoskêw, êkâ ta-misiwanâcihât ôhi awâsisa. ||| Accordingly, from that time on she did not work much, so as not to injure that child.

kîtahtawê, "tâpiskôc kotak," itêyihtam. ||| Presently, “It seems as if there were another,” she thought.
"miyâmay mîna pêyak," itêw onâpêma. ||| “Surely there is one more,” she told her husband.
tâpwê mîna êwakoni wâpamêwak. ||| Really, they saw this one, too.
miywêyihtam awa nâpêw, mîna awa iskwêw. ||| The man was glad, and the woman too.

piyisk kinwês ita ê-ayâcik, piyisk misikitisiwak awâsisak ôki. ||| At last, when they had been there a long time, those children grew bigger.
êkwa ê-pimohtêcik awâsisak ôki, otôskwanisiwâhk môhkomâna sâkikiniyiwa ôki nâpêsisak. ||| Then, when those children had begun to walk, knives grew forth from the elbows of those boys.
mitoni mâmaskâtamwak otawâsimisiwâwa ê-môhkomânitôskwanêyit. ||| They wondered greatly at their children's having knife-elbows.
êkwa atoskêwak, awa nâpêw ê-mâh-mâcît. ||| Then they worked, as the man hunted.
awa mîna iskwêw atoskêw êkwa. ||| The woman, too, now worked.
êkwa ôki awâsisak pisisik ma-mêtawêwak, acosisa ê-ayâcik, ê-ohci-mêtawêcik. ||| And those children always played, having arrows with which to play.

kîtahtawê, "ka-wanisininâwâw!" itêw ocawâsimisa. ||| Presently, “You will get lost!” she told her children.
piyisk misikitiwak ôki nâpêsisak. ||| At last those boys grew to full size.
kîtahtawê mâka mîna ê-îkatêhtêyit, ê-âkawêwêyit, wî-kakwê-wâpamêw awa iskwêw okosisa. ||| Then at one time, when in their usual way they had walked off and out of sight, the woman decided to try to observe her sons.

iyikohk ê-wî-tipiskâyik, kâ-takohtêyit okosisa. ||| Not until nightfall did her sons come home.
"kêkway ôma mâna ê-nâtamêk, kâ-kapê-kîsik êkâ kâ-takosiniyêk?" ||| “What is it you always go after, when all day you do not come home?”

iyikohk ê-pôni-mâtot, ômisi itêw: "nicawâsimisitik, kisisiwâw ana; nisîmis ana;" "mistahi ana ê-kî-miyosit, ê-kî-mîkisiwiyik ostikwân, mâka ê-kî-mawinêhokot wîci-mîkisistikwâna, aspin ê-kî-sipwêhtatâyit ostikwân." "kêyâpic cî yêhyêw?" ||| When she stopped weeping, she said to them, “My children, he is your mother's brother; he is my younger brother; he was very handsome, and beaded was his head, but his fellow Wampum-Head challenged him to a contest and carried off his head. Is he still breathing!”
"êha; kêyâpic yêhyêw," itik okosisa. ||| “Yes; he still breathes,” her sons told her.
ômisi itwêw awa osîmimâs: "nistêsê, êwako êcika anima ôtê ôtênaw kâ-ayâk, ana pîhtêyask kâ-wîkit, êwako êcika anima ispimihk kâ-akotêk, ita kâhkâkiw kâ-akosît," itwêw awa osîmimâs: "hâ, kê-wâpahk mîna ka-nitawâpamânaw kisisinaw," itwêw awa osîmimâs. ||| The younger brother spoke as follows: “Elder brother, plainly it appears that it is none other than that which, in the town over there, hangs aloft over the dwelling of him who lives in the centre, there where the raven sits aloft,” said the younger brother; “Come, tomorrow let us again visit our uncle,” said the younger lad.
tâpwê ê-otâkosik, takosin awa nâpêw, ê-kî-mâcît. ||| At nightfall that man arrived from his hunt.
owîkimâkana ka-kâmwâtapiyiwa. ||| His wife was sitting and brooding.
"tânêhki, niwîkimâkan?" itêw. ||| What is the matter, my wife?” he asked her.

Then, when night came, and they had slept, then in the morning early, again their children went off. And now the woman did not care to stop her children.
ê-nitawâpamâcik ôki awâsisak osisiwâwa, êkotê ê-takohtêcik, ê-kî-pônahkik, ômisi itwêw awa ostêsimâs: "hâ, nisîmis, mahti niya nîkân nika-kakwê-nâtên kisisinaw ostikwân," itêw. ||| When those children went to see their uncle, and had come there and built up the fire, the elder boy said, “Now, younger brother, let me first try to get our uncle's head.”
"hâ, nisîmis, kîspin pêtâyâni, kakwê-waniskâpitâhkan kisisinaw," itêw. ||| “Well then, brother, if I come bringing it, try to pull our uncle to his feet,” he told him.
êkosi ê-ati-wayawît awa oscêsimâs, êkota iskwâhtêmihk ê-ayât, "hâw, oskac ê-kî-itêyihtamân tita-omîcaskosîsiwiyân!" ||| Then, as the elder brother was going out of the lodge, as he stood in the doorway, “Now, at the very first I did think that I should be a swallow!”
tâpwê ohpihâw, ê-pimihât êkotê kâ-kî-wâpahtahk osisa ostikwâniyiw. ||| Really, he rose into the air and flew to where he had seen his uncle'e head.
êkotê ê-takohtêt, cîki mwêhci ê-ihtât, kâ-kitoyit ôhi kâhkâkiwa. ||| When he got there, just as he was near, that raven croaked.
êkosi awa kâ-mîkisistikwânêt wayawîw, ê-têpwêt, "kiwî-maskamikawinânaw nikâhkwâskwahikan!" ê-itwêt. ||| At that the wampum-headed one came out of the lodge, and hallooed, crying, “Someone is trying to rob us of my lodge-emblem!”

â, mahti niya!" itwêw awa osîmimâs. ||| Now, let me try!” said the younger lad.
êkwa awa osîmimâs wayawîw. ||| Then the younger brother went out of the lodge.

tâpwê kêhkêhkôwiw; ohpihâw, ê-ispihât. ||| So he turned into a hawk; he rose into the air, flying high.
êkotê ê-takosihk, ispimihk ohci môskîstawêw ôhi kâhkâkiwa. ||| When he came to that place, from on high he attacked the raven.
kâhkâkiw awa ispî ê-wâpamât, namôya wî-kitôw, ê-kostât kêhkêhkwa. ||| When the raven saw him, it would not croak, for it feared the hawk.
ôma ostikwân manipitam awa kêhkêhk, êkosi ê-tapasît. ||| The hawk snatched that head and made off in flight.
iyikohk wâhyaw ê-ihtât, êkoyikohk kitoyiwa. ||| Not until he was far on his way did the raven croak.
iyâta-wayawîpahtât awa, âsay wâhyaw kî-atimihâyiwa. ||| Though that person came running forth from the lodge, by this time the other had flown far off on his course.
"êhêhê!" itwêw; "nawaswêk, nawaswêk! ||| “Alas!” he cried; “Go in pursuit!
kimaskamikawinânaw nôstikwânim!" itwêw. ||| We have been robbed of my head!” he cried.

sinikohkitonêpis!" itêw. ||| Rub his mouth!” he told him.
tâpwê tâpiskopayiw ôma ostikwân, êkwa awa ostêsimâs ê-sinikohkitonênât. ||| Truly, that head flew into place, and the elder lad rubbed his mouth.
kâ-nawaswêcik ôki kahkiyaw kîwêwak. ||| All those who had given chase went back.
miywêyihtamwak ôki nâpêsisak ê-pimâtisiyit osisiwâwa. ||| Those boys rejoiced that their uncle had come to life.

tâpwê pimi-nîsokâpawiwak wîpisisihk. ||| Truly they went along, two of them standing on his arrow.

"sôhki, misi-kinêpik! ||| “Courage, Great Serpent!

mitoni tâskiswêw ôhi misi-kinêpikwa. ||| He cut the Great Serpent all to strips.
awîna ôhi, ostêsa osisa ôhtâwiya êkota ohci pê-wayawiyiwa. ||| Whom did he see but his brother, his uncle and his father, coming out from there!
nipahêw ayisk ôhi; êkosi kîwêhtahêw. ||| For he had slain that creature; so now he brought them home.
kîwêwak; ê-tipiskâyik takosinwak wîkiwâhk. ||| They went home; at nightfall they arrived at their dwelling.
êkwa ê-wâpahk, ômisi itwêw osîmimâs awa: "hâw, osâm kimôhcôwin, nistêsê." "namôya êsa ani kimanitôwin; pisisik kisâkôcihikawin." "nicawâc ê-itêyihtamân niya kika-ititinâwâw." ||| Then, the next morning, thus spoke that younger lad: “Now then, you are too foolish, my elder brother. It seems that you have no manitou power; you are always being defeated. It will be better if I tell you what I have planned.”
"hâw, nôhtâ, kiyawâw nikâwiy: cêskwa ayîsiyiniwak tita-ihtâwak;" "nîkân ôtê wacîhk kika-ayânâwâw;" "ka-misikitinâwâw;" "okiniyak ka-isiyîhkâsonâwâw," itêw ôhtâwiya êkwa okâwiya, "osâm ê-miyo-pimâtisiyêk" "êkwa kiya, nisisê, ôtê ê-pahkisimohk, êkotê kika-otaskîn." "'ê-mîkisistikwânêt ayîsiyiniw nikitimâkêyimik,' tita-itwêw ayîsiyiniw;" "ê-nipât, kika-wâpamik, nisisê" "êkwa niyanân: ôta nîkânês isi tita-apisîsisiwak acâhkosak; câh-cîki tita-ayâwak;" "nika-êkotôwiwinân niyanân nistês," itêw; "hâh, êkosi, niyâk!" ||| “Well then, my father, as for you and my mother: soon there will be mortal men; in future time you will stay on the hills; you will be tall; thorn-trees you will be called,” he told his father and his mother, “because you are good beings. And you, my uncle, over here in the place of the setting sun, there you will have your habitation. ‘The man with the beaded head has taken pity on me,’ a man will say; in his sleep he will see you, my uncle. And as for us: here, a little ways ahead there will be small stars; they will be near to each other; such will we be, my elder brother and I,” he said to them; “There, that is the way of it; be off!”
êkosi ôki sipwêhtêwak. ||| Accordingly, those others went off.
waciy ê-otihtahkik awa owîkimâkana, kawipayihôwak; okinîwiwak. ||| When they came to a hill, he and his wife, they threw themselves upon the ground; they turned into thorn-trees.
êkwa ôki nâpêsisak ispimihk itohtêwak, ê-acâhkosiwicik. ||| And those boys went up aloft and turned into stars.
êkosi êkoyikohk ê-iskwâk âtayôhkêwin. ||| And so this is the end of the sacred story.
pêyak êsa ôma ôtênaw ê-misâk, ê-mâh-mêtawêcik, ê-môtocik. ||| The story goes that there was this big town where they always had contests and ate each other.
kîtahtawê pêyak awa iskwêw pakwâtam, ê-kitimâkêyimât osîmisa. ||| Then at one time a certain woman took a dislike to this, because she loved her little brother.
"nika-sipwêhtahâw; ta-kakwê-ohpikiw," itêyihtam. ||| “I shall take him away from here; I shall try to have him grow up,” she thought.
ê-tipiskâyik, sipwêhtêw, ê-tapasît. ||| In the night she went away, fleeing.
"mâskôc,- nôhtâwiy nikâwiy ê-nipahihcik, êkwa nipêyakon nisîmis,- asici mâskôc mêtawêhki, êkwa nika-nipahikawin," itêyihtam; êwako ohci kâ-ôh-sipwêhtêt. ||| “Perhaps since my father and my mother have been killed, I am now alone with my little brother perhaps, if there is another mass contest, I now shall be killed,” she thought; that is why she went away.
nistwâw ê-nipât, êkotê miywâsiniyiw askiy, misiwê ê-sakâyik. ||| After two nights journeying, she was at a place where the land was good, with woods everywhere.
"âh, mâskôc ôta nama awiyak nika-otihtik," itêyihtam; "êkosi tita-ohpikiw nisîmis," itêyihtam. ||| “Oh, perhaps here no one will come upon me,” she thought; “In this way my little brother will grow up,” she thought.
tâpwê êkota osîhtâw wîki. ||| So there she set up her dwelling.
kiyipa kîsihtâw wîki. ||| She quickly built her lodge.
êkwa osîhtâw astis ohci tâpakwâna, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahât wâposwa, "êkotôwahk piko nika-ôh-pimâtisinân nisîmis," ê-itêyihtah. ||| Then she made snares of sinew, meaning to try to kill rabbits, thinking, “Only from these shall my little brother and I be able to get our sustenance.” So she set her snares.
tâpwê tâpakwêw. êkwa mihta mistahi âwatâw. ||| Then she gathered a great amount of firewood.
êkwa ê-tipiskâyik, ê-kî-nipâcik, ê-wâpahk, nâtam otâpakwâna. ||| Then, when night had come and they had slept, in the morning she went to look at her snares.
nîso nipahêw wâposwa. ||| She had killed two rabbits.
êkwa nisîmis kê-mîcisot!" itwêw, ê-kîwêhtahât. ||| Now my little brother will eat!” she said, as she took them home.
tâpwê miywêyihtam awa nâpêsis, ê-pêsîmiht wâposwa. ||| The little boy was glad when the rabbits were brought.
êkwa kîsiswêw awa iskwêw, ê-asamât osîmisa. ||| Then the woman cooked them and gave her little brother to eat.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, kotaka mîna osîhtâw, âsay mîna ê-nitawi-tâpakwêt; êkoyikohk mâna kâ-kîwêci, ê-atoskâtahk mihta, ita ê-ay-ayât. ||| When she too had eaten, she made some more snares and went again to lay then; and then, whenever she went home, she tended to the firewood, and stayed there.
piyisk misikitiyiwa osîma, êkwa ê-osîhtât acosisa, ê-kiskinôhamawât ta-pimotahkwêyit osîmisa. ||| In time her brother grew big, and then she made arrows and taught him to shoot.
tâpwê kaskihtâw ê-pimotahkwêt awa nâpêsis. ||| So the boy learned to shoot.
"mâskôc kîkway wêh-nipahtâci oskinîkici," ê-itêyimât, kâ-ôh-kiskinôhamawât. ||| Perhaps he will kill something when he comes to adolescence,” was why she taught him.
wiya tahto-kîsikâw ê-nipahât wâposwa, êwako piko ê-atoskêt, êkwa awa nâpêsis pisisik ê-mêtawêt pîhcâyihk, âskaw wayawîtimihk, awa piko iskwêw ê-atoskêt, mitoni kitimâkêyimêw osîmisa, ita ê-wî-ohpikihât. ||| As she killed rabbits every day, she was the only one of them to work; as the boy was always playing in the lodge, or sometimes out of doors, and only the woman worked, she was very good to her little brother, there where she was trying to raise him.
kîtahtawê êkwa ê-misikitiyit osîma, osîhtâw otayiwinisiyiwa, wîki ê-pîkosahk, êwako ohci oskotâkayiyiw ê-osîhtât, mîna otâsiyiwa. ||| Then, presently, when her brother grew big, she made clothes for him, cutting pieces from the tent, from which she made him a coat and breeches.
êkwa wêskwâhtêmihk ohtapiw awa, ê-ati-oskinîkit; êkwa pêyakwanohk apiw awa, ê-ati-oskinîkit. ||| And he sat in the place opposite the door, as he came to the age approaching manhood; he stayed always right there, as he came to adolescence.
namôya êkwa papâmohtêw wayawîtimihk, nayêstaw ê-mîcisot, wâposwa piko ê-môwâcik omisa. ||| He did not go about now out of doors; he did little more than eat his meals, and rabbits were all they had to eat, he and his sister.
nama wîhkâc kitotitôwak. ||| They never spoke to each other.
kîtahtawê otinam omôhkomân, ê-nitawi-kîskikahahk misâskwatwa, êkwa ahcâpiya, ê-pîhtokatât, ê-wî-osîhtât, ê-môhkotahk, ôhi mîna ahcâpiya, acosisa ê-wî-osîhtât. ||| Then at one time he took his knife and went to cut some saskatoon sticks, and wood for a bow, and brought them inside the lodge to work at them, whittling them, and the bow as well, to make arrows.
êkwa namôya tâpwê kî-nipahêw awa iskwêw wâposwa. ||| And then the woman was no longer well able to kill rabbits.
pakwâtam awa iskwêw ê-nôhtêhkatêcik, osâm pêyakwanohk ê-apiyit osîma. ||| The woman was grieved that they should hunger because her brother always stayed right there.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw kâ-osîhtât ôhi misâskwatwa, otinam cîkahikan, ê-nitawi-wanihikêt mistikwa ohci, mistiko-wanihikan. ||| When the youth had prepared those saskatoon sticks, he took an ax and went to set a trap of boughs.
êkosi ê-kîwêt, pêyak piko nipahêyiwa omisa wâposwa. ||| Then when he came home, his sister had killed but one rabbit.
pôti ê-wâpahk, ê-nitawâpahtahk owanihikana, nipahêw kihîwa, êkwa ôhôwa; êkosi nîso. ||| In the morning, when he went to look at his traps, he had killed an eagle and an owl; one in each trap.
êwakoni mîkwana ohci osîhtâw wîpisisa. ||| He made his arrows with those feathers.
ê-kîsihtât, êkwa omisa astis miyik, ê-osihtât, ahcâpîhk ê-tahkopitahk. ||| When he had finished them, his sister gave him a sinew, which he prepared and fixed on his bow.
êkwa mîna ê-nitawâpahtahk owanihikana, tasôhêw nikikwa êkwa ocêka, êkwa ocêkiwayâna ê-wî-opîhtatwânit, nikikwa ê-wî-otastotinit, nikikwayâna. ||| The next time he went to look at his traps, he had trapped an otter and a fisher; and now he meant to make a quiver of the fisherskin, and of the otter a hat, of the otterskin.
êkwa ôhi kihîwa, oskan ôta ômatôwahk, otihcimanikanis otinam, kicohcikanis ê-osîhtât. ||| And from the eagle he took the bone here, like this, from the upper part of the wing, and made a flute.
ê-kîsi-osîhtât, otinamiyiwa omisa kâwiya, ê-wî-kikamohâyit kicohcikanisihk. ||| When he had made it, his sister took some porcupine-quills to attach to the little flute.
ê-kîsihtâyit, akotâw. ||| When she had finished it, he hung it up.
êkosi miywêyihtam awa iskwêw, "êkwa kêkway ta-nipahtâw nisîm!" ê-itêyihtahk. ||| Then the woman was glad, thinking, “Now my brother will kill something!”
pôti nama wiya wî-mâcîyiwa osîma, pêyakwanohk ê-apiyit. ||| But she found that her brother would not hunt, and did not stir from the spot.
âskaw nama kêkway nipahtâw wâposwa awa iskwêw. ||| Often enough the woman did not kill any rabbits.
êkosi nama kêkway mîciwak. ||| Then they had nothing to eat.
pakwâtam awa iskwêw êkâ ê-wî-mâciyit osîma; êkâ kêkway ê-asamât osîma, êwako ohci kâ-ôh-pakwâtahk. ||| She was grieved that her brother did not care to hunt; because she had nothing to give her brother to eat, was why she disliked it.
mîna ê-wâpahk, ê-nâtahk otâpakwâna, nama kêkway nipahtâw. ||| The next morning, when she went to her snares, she had not killed anything.
ê-takohtêt wîkiwâhk, omaskisina ê-pahpawahahk, ê-kôniwiyiki, "hê ê êy!" itwêw awa iskwêw; "tâpwê nimihtâtên êkâ kêkway ê-asamak nisîm!" itwêw; "êkwa ê-oskinîkit, wiyaskoc êtokê kêkway ta-nipahtâw, ta-mîciyâhk, nitêyihtêh, êkâ kâ-ispayik," itwêw awa iskwêw, ê-otinahk mihta, ê-wî-pônahk. ||| Then she came to their dwelling and was shaking out her moccasins, for they were full of snow, she cried, “Oh dear, oh dear! Really I am sorry I have nothing to give my brother to eat!” she said; “Now that he is a young man, he in his turn ought to kill something for us to eat; so I thought, at least, but it has not turned out that way,” said the woman, as she took up some faggots to put on the fire.
"nika-pêhtâk nisîm," ê-itêyihtahk, ôma kâ-ôh-itwêt. ||| “My brother will hear me,” was her idea in speaking so.
ê-pa-pimisihk awa oskinîkiw, waniskâw, ê-otinahk kicohcikanis mîna wîpisisa. ||| The youth arose from where he lay, and took the flute and his arrows.
êkwa maskosiya otinam, iskotêw ê-akwâsiwêpahahk. ||| Also he took some dried incense-grass and pushed back the fire.
êkota astâw maskosiya, ê-kaskâpahtêyik, kicohcikanis ôma êkota ê-itisinahk, ê-miyâhkasahk. ||| There he placed the grass, and when it began to make smoke, he held the little flute over it, perfuming the incense.
êkosi ômisi itwêw: "hê êy, nimisê, ê-kitimâkinâtân, êkâ kêkway kâ-ôh-wî-nipahtâyân, osâm mistahi ta-atoskêyan, ê-itêyimitân," itêw omisa; "yôhtêwêpina!" ||| At the same time he spoke as follows: “Dear me, sister, it is because I feel sorry for you that I have not been killing anything, because I thought you would have too much work,” he told his sister; “Throw open the door-flap!”
yôhtênam awa iskwêw, êkwa awa oskinîkiw ê-kitohcikêt. ||| The woman opened the doorway, and the youth played on his flute.
ê-kîsi-kitohtât, akotâw. ||| When he had done playing music, he hung it up.
kiyipa kâ-pâpayiyit apisi-môsosa, ê-mihcêtiyit, êkota iskwâhtêmihk ê-pimipayiyit, êwakoni ê-pâh-pimwât. ||| At once there came running dwarf-moose in great number, and as they ran past the doorway, he kept shooting them.
iyikohk ê-mêstinahk wîpisisa, êkoyikohk pôyôw. ||| He stopped only when he had used up his arrows.
âhci piko mihcêt mistahi nipahêw. ||| He killed a great many of them.
"ê, nimisê, nitawi-otina nîpisisa." "mihkôwikwâwi, kâsîhamôhkan." ||| “There, sister, go get my arrows. If they are bloody, wipe them off.”
tâpwê wayawîw awa iskwêw. ||| Accordingly, the woman went outside.
ê-itâpit, mihcêt apisi-môsosa nipahêyiwa. ||| When she looked to see, he had killed many dwarf-moose.
êkwa kê-mîcisot nisîmis!" itwêw, acosisa ôhi ê-wâh-wîhkwatinahk, ê-ati-kâsîhahk. ||| Now my brother will eat!” she said, as she kept pulling out the arrows and wiping them.
ê-pîhtokatât, pôti kî-mosêskatêyiwa osîma, ê-wêwêkinamiyit otakohpiyihk. ||| When she brought them indoors, there was her brother undresseed, wrapped up in his blanket-robe.
ê-kî-otinamiyit acosisa, ôhi otayôwinisiyiwa, "nimisê, wayawîwêpina!" ||| When he had taken back his arrows, then, of his clothes, he said, “Sister, throw them out of the lodge!”
ê-wayawîwêpinahk, êkwa omôhkomân otinam, ê-wayawît. ||| When she had thrown them out, she took her knife and went out.
ê-nanâtawâpahtahk ôhi kâ-wayawîwêpinahk, namôya wâpahtam. ||| When she looked about to see the things she had thrown out, she did not see them.
êkosi êkwa ê-wiyanihtâkêt. ||| Then she set about skinning and cutting up the game.
ôhi apisi-môsosa ê-kîsi-wiyanihât, iyâyaw paminawasôw. ||| When she had cleaned those dwarf-moose, she set eagerly about her cooking.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, êkwa awa apisi-môsoswayâna nêwo otinêw, ê-wî-pâswât. ||| When she had eaten, sbe took four of the skins of the dwarf-moose to dry.
êkosi owiyâsima pîhtokêyâwatâw. ||| Then she brought in her meat.
êkwa âtiht wayawîtimihk astêyiwa, osâm mihcêt kâ-nipahâyit. ||| But some was left outside, for he had killed too many.
ê-kîsi-nahastât, êkwa pîhtokêw, pêskis mîna ê-paminawasot, âskaw ê-atoskâtât ôhi apisi-môsoswayâna. ||| When she had arranged it all, she came in, and again attended to her cooking, even while working the hides of the dwarf-moose.
ê-otâkosiniyik, âsay kîsihêw, êkwa ê-kaskikwâtahk osîma ê-otayôwinisiyit. ||| Towards evening, she had finished tanning them and began sewing clothes for her brother.
kêkâc ta-kawisimocik, ê-ispayiyik, kîsihtâw. ||| When it was almost time for them to go to bed, she had finished them.
postayôwinisêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| The youth put on the clothes.
âsay mîna kotaka pâswêw. ||| Then she dried some more.
êkosi ê-kawisimot awa oskinîkiw, awa wiya iskwêw atoskâtêw apisi-môsoswayâna. ||| Then, when the youth went to bed, the woman kept on working the moose-hides.
piyis ê-nôhtêhkwasit, kawisimôw. ||| At last, when she grew sleepy, she went to bed.
kîkisêpâ ê-pêkopayit, âsay osîma simatapiyiwa. ||| Early in the morning, when she awoke, her brother was already sitting up.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, âsay mîna awa oskinîkiw iskotêw otinam, mîna ê-miyâhkasahk okitohcikanis. ||| When they had eaten, the youth again took some fire and burned incense to his little flute.
"yôhtêwêpina, nimisê!" itêw. ||| “Open the door-flap, sister!” he said to her.
ê-kî-yôhtênahk, kitohtâw. ||| When she had opened it, he blew on his flute.
êkwa wâwâskêsiwa êwako pêcimêw, êwakoni êkwa ê-nôcihât. ||| This time he brought deer to his call, and gave chase to them.
iyikohk mîna ê-mêstinahk wîpisisa, êkoyikohk mîna tapasîyiwa. ||| Again, only when he had used up his arrows, did they flee.
"â, nimisê, otina nîpisisa!" ||| “There, sister, take up my arrows!”
ê-wayawît awa iskwêw, â, mihcêt êkwa wâwâskêsiw. ||| When the woman went out, there were many deer.
mahti êkwa êkâ ê-nôhtêhkatêyân!" itwêw awa iskwêw, ôhi ê-wâh-wîhkwatinahk acosisa. ||| Now, surely, I shall not go hungry!” she said, as she went about pulling free the arrows.
ê-pîhtokatât, âsay mîna kî-mosêskatêpiyiwa osîma. ||| When she brought them in, again her brother sat without his clothes.
"hâ, nimisê, êwakoni anihi wayawîwêpina!" itêw. ||| “There, sister, throw these things out!” he said to her.
êkwa omôhkomân otinam awa iskwêw, ê-wî-wiyanihtâkêt. ||| Then she took her knife, to clean the game.
nama kêkway wâpahtam osîma otayiwinisiyiwa, ayis ê-wêpinamiyit. ||| Not a thing did she see of her brother's clothes; he had cast them off.
êkosi êkwa mîna wiyanihtâkêw. ||| Then, accordingly, she again cleaned game.
ê-kîsi-wiyanihtâkêt, êkoyikohk êkwa kîsitêpôw, ê-wî-mîcisocik. ||| When she had finished cleaning game, she cooked, that they might eat.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, iyâyaw êkwa osîhêw apisi-môsoswayâna, êkwa pêyak wâwâskêsiwa, wâwâskêsiwayâna. ||| When she had eaten, she eagerly went about preparing dwarf-moose skins and one deer-skin.
iyikohk ê-otâkosik, kahkiyaw kîsihtâw, êkwa pita ê-paminawasot. ||| By evening she had finished it all, and then she stopped to cook.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, êkwa kaskikwâsôw. ||| When they had eaten, she sewed.
êkwa kîsihtâw otayiwinisiyiwa osîma. ||| Then she finished her brother's clothes.
iyâyaw êkwa pâsam pahkêkinwa. ||| Then, with zeal she went about drying hides.
piyis mistahi tipiskâyiki, iyikohk kawisimôw. ||| At last, when it was quite dark, she went to bed.
iyikohk ê-pêkopayit, êkoyikohk sâsay waniskâyiwa osîma. ||| When she awoke, her brother had already got up.
kakwêyâhôw ê-paminawasot. ||| She worked quickly, cooking the meal.
mayaw ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, âsay mîna miyâhkasamiyiwa okicohcikanisiyiw. ||| When they had eaten, he again burned incense under his flute.
ê-yôhtêwêpinahk, kitohtâw. ||| When she had opened it, he played.
âsay mîna pêcimêw môswa, êkwa êwakoni mîna ê-nôcihât. ||| As before, he made moose come by the sound, for these he now sought.
iyikohk mîna ê-mêstinahk wîpisisa, pôyôw. ||| Again, when he had exhausted his arrows, he ceased.
"â, nimisê, nitawi-otina nîpisisa!" ||| “Now, sister, go take up my arrows!”
ê-wayawît, mihcêt êkwa môswa. ||| When she went out, there were many moose.
êkwa êkâ mayaw kê-nôhtêhkatêyâhk!" itwêw awa iskwêw, ê-ati-otinahk acosisa. ||| Now we shall not for a long time go hungry!” said the woman, as she set about taking the arrows.
ê-pîhtokêt, âsay mîna mosêskatêpiyiwa. ||| When she went indoors, again he sat undressed.
"â, nimisê, êkoni anihi wayawîwêpina!" itêw omisa. ||| “Now, sister, throw those things out!” he told his sister. She threw them outside; then she took her knife and went out and began to clean the carcasses. She skinned them and cut them up. When she had finished cleaning them she set about her cooking. When they had eaten, then she again prepared skins of dwarf-moose, and a deer-hide, with the thought, “that he may have it for a blanket-robe,” and just as darkness was coming on, she had them dome, and stopped to cook again, to feed her brother. So, when they had eaten, she sewed and made clothes. Before her brother went to bed she had them done, and already was drying other skins of dwarf-moose and of moose. When she got sleepy, she ceased work and went to bed. The next morning, when she arose, her brother was already sitting up. So then she cooked, that they might eat. As soon as they had eaten, he again burned incense to his flute. The woman threw open the door-flap, and her brother played the flute. Then buffalo came running, and he made a killing of these too. Again, only when he had used up his arrows did he cease killing them.
otina nîpisisa!" itêw. ||| Take up my arrows!” he told her.
ê-wayawît awa iskwêw, âsay mîna miywêyihtam. ||| When the woman went out, again she was glad.
êkosi êcika ôma êkâ wîhkâc kê-kôta-mîciyân!" itwêw awa iskwêw, ê-âh-otinahk acosisa. ||| So now, it appears, I shall never be at a loss for something to eat!” she said, as she went on taking the arrows.
ê-pîhtokêt, âsay mîna kî-mosêskatêpiyiwa osîma. ||| When she went in, again her brother sat without his clothes.
"â, nimisê, êwakoni wayawîwêpina!" itik; "ê-manâ-mistahi-atoskahitân, êkâ kâ-ôh-ma-mâcîyân," itêw. ||| “Now, sister, throw these out of the lodge!” he told her; “It was because I hesitated to give you too much work, that I never used to hunt,” he told her. So the woman threw them out of the lodge, and took her knife, and went out and cleaned the game. She eagerly set about skinning a young bull-calf.
"êwakoni êkwa ta-otakohpiw nisîm," itêyihtam. ||| “Now my brother shall have a blanket-robe of this one,” she thought.
ê-kîsi-wiyanihât, pita êwakoni pîhtokahêw, ita ta-pâsoyit ê-kikamohât. ||| When she had skinned it, she first brought it inside and fastened it to dry.
êkoyikohk êkwa ê-nitawi-wiyanihtâkêt. ||| Then she went again to cut up game.

"namôya ê-papâ-mêtawêyân," itêw. ||| “I do not happen to be going about in search of contests,” he told him.

"wâpahki mâskôc ka-mawinêhokwak," itâw. ||| “Doubtless they will challenge you none the less. They challenge at once any new arrival,” he was told; “But it is evening now. Tomorrow probably they will challenge you,” he was told.
êwako kîkisêpâ, ê-kî-mîcisocik, sâsay kâ-têpwêwiht. ||| Then, the next morning, when they had eaten, already he heard the announcing call.
wawêyîk!" "pê-nitawâpahkêk!" "wî-mêtawâniwiw!" "ê-papâ-mêtawêt, ê-itwêhk, kâ-takohtêt otâkosihk pîsimôwâsis, wî-mêtawêw pîwâpisko-maskwa!" "pê-wayawîk!" ||| there will be a contest! Last night arrived Sun-Child, who, it is said, is going about seeking contests; he is to contend with the Iron Bear! Come forth!”
"hâw, pîsimôwâsis, kiwî-wawêyîn, pîwâpisko-maskwa ê-wî-mawinêhosk." ||| “Come, Sun-Child, you are to come forth, as the Iron Bear is to challenge you.”
êkosi, "hâw, êyiwêhk wawêyî." "misawâc âta êkâ tâpwêhtamani, ohcitaw ka-kakwê-misi-wanâcihik," itik ôhi wîkiyihk kâ-pîhtokêt, ôma ita kâ-apit. ||| Then, “at any rate, go forth. In any case, even if you pay no heed, none the less he will seek to destroy you,” he was told by him into whose lodge he had come, where now he stayed.
"êha." "namôya nôh-papâ-mêtawân," itwêw; "êyiwêhk mâka," itwêw. ||| “Very well. It is not true that I am going about seeking contests,” he said; “but never mind,” he said.
sâsay ita ê-tahtakwahcâsiyik, êkota ê-itohtêyit. ||| Already, where there was a stretch of level land, thither the other had gone.
"hâ, kiyipa pê-wayawî!" itâw. ||| “Ho, quickly, come forth!” he was told.
êkosi wayawîw, ê-itohtêt. ||| Accordingly, he went out and proceeded to the place.
sâsay wîhkwêkâpawiyiwa. ||| They were already standing about in a circle.
ê-takohtêt, "haw, pîsimôwâsis, kipapâ-mêtawân, kititikawin." "kiya mâka nîkân ka-pimotên." ||| When he arrived, “Now then, Sun-Child, you are going about engaging in contests, it is said concerning you. You shall have the first shot.” “No! You first! Seeing it is not of my own will I am contending.”
"êêg," itwêw awa wâkayôs. ||| “Very well,” said that bear.
âsay ômisi itêyihtam: "hâw, nôhtâ, kisiwâk ohci kanawêyimin!" itwêw, ômisi ê-itêyihtah: "mâskôc kisâstêki, ta-nayawapit," ê-itêyimât ôhi wâkayôsa. ||| Already he thought as follows: “Now, O my father, watch me from close by!” he said, thinking this: “Perhaps, if the weather is hot, he will tire,” thinking this of the bear.
tâpwê ati-kisitêyiw, ê-ati-kisâstêyik. ||| Really, it grew hotter and hotter, as the bright glow of the sun increased.
"haw, nêtê nika-pê-ohtohtân." "nêwâw ka-wâyonîstâtin; mwêhci nêwâw êkota nika-pimakocinin," ê-wî-otihtinikot, ê-wî-kakwê-nipahikot. ||| “Now then, from yon place I shall come. Four times I shall start for you; and on the fourth time I shall spring,” meaning that he would seize him, that he would try to kill him.
mistahi ati-sipwêhtêw awa wâkayôs, êkotê ê-ohci-pê-sipwêhtêt, ê-pê-nâtât pîsimôwâsisa. ||| The bear went off a long ways, starting from a good distance to come running at Sun-Child.
tâpiskôc ê-yôskahcâyik, ê-pê-pimohtêyit, iyikohk ê-kotâwahcinamiyit. ||| Just as if the ground were soft swamp, when he came, he sank deep into it.
kisiwâk ê-ihtâyit, wâyonîyiwa. ||| When he was near he turned back.
mîna êkotê ohci pê-sipwêhtêyiwa. ||| Again he started from the same place.
ayiwâkês êkwa iskoskiwêyiwa. ||| This time he sank even farther into the ground.
mîna kisiwâk ê-ihtâyit, wâyonîyiwa. ||| Again, when he had come near, he turned back.
âsay mîna pê-sipwêhtêyiwa, tahki ayiwâk ê-iskoskiwêyit. ||| Again he started hither, always sinking deeper into the earth.
kêyâpic wâyonîyiwa êkwa, êkota êkwa ka-kakwê-nipahikot. ||| Now he turned back once more, and now was when he would try to kill him.
mâka sâsay mistahi nayawapiyiwa. ||| But by this time he was very tired.
ispî kisiwâk êkwa ê-ayâyit, pisisik pîwâpisk isinâkosiyiwa. ||| When he was near, he looked as though all of iron.
konita ê-sâkôwêwiht, "êkwa miyâmay wî-pê-kwâskwêpayihôw!" ê-itêyihtahk, ôhi owîcêwâkana ita kâ-kî-pîhtokêt êwakoni, "âhkamêyimo!" tahki ê-itikot, êkwa ê-pê-kwâskwêpayihoyit, kawipayihôw. ||| Those on his side were yelling wildly. “Now surely he will come leaping!” he thought. His comrade at whose house he was staying kept telling him to take heart.
iyâta-isi-kwâskwêpayihoyit, ita kâ-kî-nîpawit, âsay itê kâ-ohtohtêyit, êkotê âsay nîpawiw awa wâkayôs, ê-kwêskipayihot. ||| The other did not see him. In vain the other tried to hurl himself to the spot whence he had stood; already he stood there when the other had come, throwing himself from place to place.
êkosi ê-môskîstawât. ||| At once he attacked him.
wâh-otihtâci, ê-kawipayihoyit, namôya wâpamêw, konita mâna kâ-sâkôwêwiht owîcêwâkana pîsimôwâsis, ê-miywêyihtamiyit ôhi ê-mêtawâkâtât. ||| When the other, as soon as he was upon him, flung himself down, he could not see him; wildly all this time his companions were whooping for Sun-Child, happy that he was giving that other a fight.
piyisk wî-nipahatâhtamiyiwa. ||| At last the other was helpless from want of breath.
ôki mîna ayisiyiniwak mâkôhkasôwak, osâm kisiwâk ê-ayâyit pîsimwa. ||| Those men, too, were oppressed by the heat, for the Sun was too near.
piyisk pêyakwanohk nîpawiw awa wâkayôs, ê-wî-nipahatâhtahk. ||| At last he stood still in one place, that bear, almost dead from want of breath.
piyisk êkwa otinam wîpisisa, nêhi nôtokêsiwa kâ-kî-ohpikihikot êwakoni ê-kî-osîhtâkot. ||| So then he took his arrows, which that little old woman who had raised him had made for him.
ê-tâwatiyit awa wâkayôs, ê-wî-nipahatâhtahk, êwakoni kâ-pimwât otôniyihk; ayisk êkota piko namôya pîwâpiskôwiyiwa. ||| Where that bear stood with open mouth, helplessly panting, he shot him in the mouth; for only there was the other not of iron.
aspin ê-pîhtokêhâyit kêhkêhkwa, ê-sâpowêyawihâyit, otêhiyiw ê-ati-tahkonamiyit, ka-sâkôwêwiht owîcêwâkana pîsimôwâsis. ||| In flew a hawk, flying clear through the creature's body, seizing his heart, while Sun-Child's companions cheered him.
"hâw, pîsimôwâsis, ôtê âpihtâ-kîsikâhk isi kwâhkonin." "êkotê, 'ê-pîwâpiskôwit wâkayôs nikitimâkêyimik,' itwêci ayisiyiniw cêskwa kâ-wî-ohpikit, ta-tâpwêw," itwêw. ||| “Very well, Sun-Child, throw me in the direction of noon. There, when mortal man, who in time is to grow forth, says, ‘The Iron Bear has taken pity on me,’ he will speak true,” said he.
"hêy, isi-kawipayiho!" itêw. ||| “Ho, throw yourself to the ground facing so!” he told him.
êkosi isi-kawipayihoyiwa. ||| So the other threw himself to the ground, facing that way.
ômisi itwêw: "niwîcêwâkanitik, êkâ wiya nipahihkok kâ-astwâkawiyêk," itêw; "tahki êkosi tôtamêko, namôya ta-kî-ohpikiw ayisiyiniw," itêw; "êkosi ka-pônihtânâwâw kâ-mêtawêyêk," itêw. ||| Thus he spoke: “My comrades, do not kill those who have been given as stakes by your opponents,” he told them; “If you always do thus, mortal man will not be able to grow forth,” he told them; “In this wise you are to cease from your contests,”
"êkosi tâpwê!" itwêyiwa owîcêwâkana. ||| “Truly, that is right!” said his companions.
otiyinîmiwâwa êsa ôki mâna ê-kî-astwâtocik, mâka ê-sâkôcihât, kâ-ôh-kitahamawât, tâpwêhtâk. ||| For in fact these people were accustomed to stake their followers; but now that he had overcome them and prohibited it, they obeyed him.
êkwa kostik; namôya awiya êkwa ta-kî-mawinêhokot, êkoni piko ê-manitôwiyit kâ-sâkôcihât. ||| For they feared him; there was no one now who could challenge him, since he had defeated the one among them who had most spirit power.
êkosi wêtinahk êkwa ê-ayâcik ôki ayisiyiniwak. ||| So now these people lived in peace.
kîtahtawê ê-sipwêhtêt, ispatinâhk ê-nahapit, wani-kiskisiw asiniya mâna ê-anâskasot. ||| Then at one time, as he went forth and sat down on a hilltop, he forgot to follow his custom of using the stone as a seat.
kîtahtawê kâ-môsihât ê-kwayasitêyit ôtê, ita kâ-ôh-mîsît, kinêpikwa sîsîkwêwa, nêhi kâ-kî-mêscihimât otawâsimisiyiwa nôtokêsiwa, êwakoni ê-tôtâkot. ||| Presently he felt something crawl in here, [no translation] a rattlesnake; it was yon old woman whose children he had wiped out, was doing this to him.
ayis, "êkâya wîhkâc mostâhtak api!" kî-itik. ||| For, “Never sit on the bare ground!” she had told him.
êkwa ê-âta-kakwê-pihkohât, nama kî-pihkohêw. ||| Then, try as he might to get the creature out, he could not get it out.
piyisk owîcêwâkana otihtik. ||| At last his comrades came to where he was.
ôma ê-mâkohikot, ê-wî-nipahikot, piyisk mihcêtiwân ita ôma kâ-ayât, tahki ê-sîhkimikot ta-kakwê-nipahât ôhi sîsîkwêwa, osâm ê-miywêyimikot ôhi ayisiyiniwa. ||| As thus he was tormented by that creature which was trying to kill him, at last many came to where he was, urging him to try to kill that rattlesnake, for dearly those people loved him.
tahki ispimihk ati-itohtêyiwa; ôtê piyisk ostikwânihk asiwasoyiwa. ||| The creature kept going higher and higher; at last it got into his head here.
êkwa ôtê êkwa wî-kâh-kîskwêw, ê-wî-nipahikot. ||| And when it was here, he began to be delirious, as it was killing him.
kêkway omôhkomân nitotam. ||| He asked for something to use in the way of a knife.
êkwa ê-manisahk ôta, ê-wî-kakwê-pakonêhahk ostikwân, piyisk pakonêham. ||| Then he cut a piece away from here, trying to make a hole in his head, and at last succeeded.
"hâw, nôhtâ, nimâkohik; niwî-nipahik sîsîkwêw! ||| “Here, father, the rattlesnake is tormenting me and means to kill me!
kisiwâk pimohtê!" itêw ôhtâwiya. ||| Come near to me!” he said to his father.
tâpwê kisiwâk ayâyiwa. ||| Really, the latter came near.
ôki ayisiyiniwak pinasiwêwak, osâm mistahi ê-kisisocik. ||| Those people went down from the hill-top, because they were too hot.
kîtahtawê kâ-wayawiyâhtawêyit, ê-nipahîhkasoyit. ||| Presently it came climbing out, forced to extremity by the heat.
êkwa ôma ostikwân ômisi isi sinikonahk, iyiniwîw. ||| Then, when he rubbed his head like this, it healed.
êkoyikohk ôhtâwiya êkota kâ-nîpawiyit, "êhêhêhê haha!" ê-itikot; "ayisk kî-kakêpâtisiw kikâwiy, kâ-kî-sipwêhtahisk, êkâ awiyak kâ-ôh-kakêskimisk, kâ-papâ-misi-wanâtahkamikisiyan, kâ-ôh-kakêpâtisiyan." "tahki ayiwâkês kika-ati-misi-wanâtahkamikisin, nikosis." "nicawâc ka-kîwêhtahitin." "osâm kikakêpâtisin." "tahki êkosi papâ-tôtamani, namôya ta-miywâsin." "namôya êkosi nitisi-nôcihtân," itik. ||| Then, there stood his father, saying to him, “Alas and alas! No wonder, seeing how foolish was your mother who took you away with her, so that there was no one to instruct you, no wonder that you went about making a ruin of things at large, and that you are a fool. You will continue to make a greater and greater mess of things, my son. It will be better if I take you home with me. You are too much of a fool. If you continue to go about as you have, no good will come of it. I do not wish such things to be,” his father told him.
êkosi ê-kîwêcik, ispimihk wîkiyihk ê-itohtahikot, aspin omosôma ê-wîkimât. ||| So they went home, his father taking him aloft to where he dwelt; and from that time on he stayed with his grandfather.
êkoyikohk êskwâk âtayôhkêwin. ||| That is the end of the sacred story.
kîtahtawê nistiwak ayîsiyiniwak, nîso nâpêwak. ||| Once upon a time there were three people, two men and one woman, two men.
ôhi nâpêwa osîmiw awa iskwêw. ||| The men were the younger brothers of the woman.
êkwa pêyak namôya atoskêw osîmimâw. ||| The youngest one did not work.
misâskwat otinam; ayâw, ê-saskahohtêt ohci. ||| He took a stick of saskatoon willow; he kept it, walking with it as a cane.
êkwa ostêsa mâcîyiwa, mîciwin ê-tôtamâkocik. ||| His elder brother hunted, providing them with food.
kîtahtawê awa nâpêw ostêsimâw, mistahi ê-ayâcik mîciwin, "hâ, nisîm, mahti nika-nitonawâw awiyak kita-owîstâwiyahk, kimisinaw kita-onâpêmit." "êwako owîstâwiyahko, namôya kika-nêpêwisinânaw, nâpêw ôta ayâci." ||| Then at one time, when they had a big supply of food, the elder man said, “Well now, brother, suppose I look for someone to be our brother-in-law, so that our sister may have a husband. If we have him for brother-in-law, we shall not be embarrassed, when a man is here.”
kîtahtawê sipwêhtêw, ê-pa-pmohtêt. ||| Presently he set out and tramped along.
pêyakwâw ê-kî-nipât, wâpahtam mîkiwâhp. ||| After one night on the way, he saw a tipi.
âpihtâ-kîsikâhk itiskwâstawêstêyiw. ||| It stood with the door facing the direction of noon.
êkosi pôti kâ-wâpamât kâhkâkiwa ê-okâhkwâskwahikaniyit. ||| Then as he looked, he beheld a crow holding together the tips of the tent-poles.
pôti ê-otihtahk, kâ-kitoyit ôhi kâ-akociniyit mîkiwâhpihk. ||| When he came there, that creature at the top of the tent gave a call.
kî-pêyakoyiwa nâpêwa. ||| There was a man all alone.
pôti ê-kîsi-mîcisot, nâpêwa kâ-takosiniyit, kotaka oskinîkiwa. ||| When he had eaten, a man arrived, another youth.
êkwa ômisi itwêw: "kêkway ê-papâ-nâtaman, kâ-papâmohtêyan?" itik. ||| He said, “What are you seeking, that you wander about?” he asked him.
"â," itwêw, "ômisi ê-itêyihtamân kâ-ôh-papâmohtêyân: 'mahti nika-owîstâwih,' ê-itêyihtamân;" "'nika-miyâw nimisa,' ê-itêyimitân, ê-nayêhtâwîyân, êkâ wîhkâc ê-pîkiskwêt nimis, kâ-ôh-pê-miyitân." ||| “Why,” he said, “my idea in wandering about is this: ‘Suppose I get a brother-in-law’ is my thought; ‘I shall give him my elder sister,’ is my thought, concerning you, for I am inconvenienced by my sister's never speaking; that is why I have come to give her to you.” “Yes,” the other answered him; “as for me, I do not care about it; but perhaps my younger brother right here will like the idea,” he told him.
"hâ, osâm nama iskwa ninihtâ-nipahtân kêkway, ta-kî-wîwiyân wâwîs niya; ahpô kiya kêkway kinihtâ-nipahtân, êkâ tiyêpêyimoyin." ||| “Oh, as yet I am not good enough at killing things, to be able to marry, I above all, seeing that even you, who are good at killing things, do not like the idea.”
"ahahêy!" itwêw awa ostêsimâw; "ôta kisiwâk wîkiwak nisîmak ê-nisticik, pêyak nistês, ê-nêwicik êwakonik, nisto osîma ê-pamihikot." "osâm nihtâ-nipahtâwak kêkway êyakonik," itik; "êkosi êkotê ki-ka-itohtân," itik; "êyakonik ka-nitawâpamâwak." "mâskôc pêyak kitatêpêyimôw," itik. ||| “Dear me!” said the elder; “Near by here live three of my younger brothers and one elder brother, four of them; his three younger brothers take care of him. They are very good at killing game,” he told him; “So you had better go there,” he told him; “You had better go see them. Perhaps one of them will take to the idea,” he told him.
pôti ê-sâkêwêt ôma ispatinâyik, wâpahtam mîkiwâhp. ||| As he came over the crest of the hill, there he saw a tipi.
pôti kâhkwâskwahikana wâpamêw, ôhôwa, âsay kâ-kitoyit. ||| He saw what held the tips of the tent poles together, an owl, which already was giving its call.
mayaw ê-otihtahk, "tawâw, wêskinîkiyan!" itâw. ||| Just as he reached the place, “Come in, young man!” he was told.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, ist oskinîkiwa pîhtokêyiwa. ||| When he had eaten, look you, a young man came into the tent.
pîhtatwâna âh-akotêyiwa. ||| He hung up some quivers.
"hâw, tânisi êtiskâyan, ôma kâ-pê-itohtêyan ôta?" itwêw awa ostêsimâw. ||| “Hello, what is your errand, that you come here like this?” asked the eldest of his brothers.
ômisi itêw: "âh, nimis ê-pê-miyitakok pêyak." ||| He told him, “Oh, it is that I have come to give one of you my sister, elder than I.”
"niya wiya têpiyâhk ê-asamicik nisîmak." "nama kêkway ninihtâ-nipahtân." "namôya ta-kî-wîcêwak iskwêw," itwêw; êkwa, "hâw, nisîmitik, nikotwâw pêyak itohtêk kiyawâw!" ||| “As for me, I am only give food by my younger brothers. I am no good at killing any kind of game. I could not have a wife,” he told him; and then, “Now, brothers, some one of you go there!”
itik: "hâh, iyika mâ cêskwa kêkway nihtâ-nipahtâyâhk!" "namôya niya nika-kê-itohtân," itwêwak kahkiyaw. ||| They answered him, “Ho, as if we were any good as yet at killing game! I shall not be able to go there,” said all of them.
"ahêy, wêskinîkiyan! ||| “Dear me, young man!
ôma kâ-osêhcâk awasâyihk êkota wîkiw nôhtâwiy." "mâwaci ê-ostêsimâwiyit okosisa nêwo wîkimêw, êkâ cêskwa ê-wîwicik êwakonik nisîminânak, êkwa nîso oskinîkiskwêwak nisîminânak," itêw; "êkotê itohtê." "mâskôc nôhtâwiy wî-miyikoyêko otawâsimisa nisto, nîso iskwêwa êkwa pêyak nâpêw, wî-miyisk nôhtâwiy," itêw. ||| At the other side of the hill lives my father. He lives with his four eldest sons, and these our elder brothers are not yet married; nor are the two young women, our younger sisters,” he told him; “Go there. Perhaps my father will give you three of his children, two women and one man, if my father wishes to give them to you,” he told him.
êkosi tâpwê wayawîw. ||| Accordingly, he left the tent.
iyâyaw êkotê itohtêw kâ-kiskinôhamâht itê. ||| Eagerly he went to the place that had been indicated to him.
êkwa ê-ati-sâkêwêt, pôti tâpwê mîkiwâhp wâpahtam âpihtâ-kîsikâhk ê-itiskwâstawêstêyik. ||| And as on his way he came over the crest of a hill, there really he saw a tipi that stood with its doorway toward noon.
êkwa mayaw ê-wâpahtahk, wâpamik kâhkwâskwahikana, kihiwa. ||| As soon as he saw it, he was seen by the creature which held together the tips of the tent-poles, an eagle.
sêmâk kitôw awa kihiw. ||| At once the eagle gave its cry.
takohtêw mîkiwâhpihk. ||| He reached the tipi.
awîna ôhi, kisêyiniwa, nôtokêsiwa, namwâc awiya wâpamêw, nayêstaw ita ê-ohtapiyit ômatôwahk, ôma nôhtapiwin êkotôwahk ayihtahk, "hâw, tawâw!" kâ-itiht. ||| Whom did he see but an old man and an old woman, and no one else he saw but them, sitting alone on a thing like this blanket, like this on which I am sitting now; and, “Come in!” he was told.
ê-kî-pîhtokêt, "hâw, nôtokêsiw, asam! ||| When he had come in, “Now, old woman, give him food!
ha, kêtahtawê asamâw. ||| In due time he was given food.
ê-kîsi-mîcisot, kâ-pê-tatwêwitamiyit, pê-pâ-pîkiskwêyit iskwêwa. ||| When he had eaten, suddenly there came some people with loud noise, two women, talking both at once.
piyê-pîhtokêyit, awîna ôhi, oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| When they had come in, he saw that they were young girls.
ê-kîsi-nahapicik, kotakak mîna piyê-pîhtokêcik nêwo nâpêwak. ||| When they had taken their seats, some more people came in, four men.
êkwa ômisi itik: "hâw, wêskinîkiyan, tânisi ôma kâ-ôh-pê-ay-itohtêyan?" itwêw awa kisêyiniw; "ôta cî ôki nitawâsimisak kikî-pê-âh-otihtâwak?" ||| Then the other said to him, “Now then, young man, how is it you have come tramping all the way here?” asked the old man; “Have you come to be with my children here?”
"kêkway mâka kâ-ohci-papâmohtêyan?" ||| “But what is the aim of your wandering about?”
