êkosi wiya êwako pêyak mîna nikîsihtân âtayôhkêwin. ||| and so now I have finished this story too.
iskwêwak êwako: mitâtaht iskwêwak, piyêsiwak, iskwêwak, êkwa ôhtâwiyiwâwa mîna okâwiyiwâwa ôki iskwêwak, ê-okimâwiyit ôhtâwiyiwâwa. ||| This is about some women: ten women, Thunderer-Woman, and their father and mother; and their father was a chief.
êkwa ôta, askîhk ôta, êkota oskinîkiwak mîna mitâtaht, mîna êyakonik owîtisânihtocik, mâka nama awiya okâwiyiwâwa; ôhtâwiyiwâwa mîna nama awiya. ||| And here on earth were also ten youths, who, in the same way, were brothers, but these had no mother; and they had no father.
êkosi pêyak piko mîkiwâhp; nama awiya kotaka ayîsiyiniwa ayâyiwa kisiwâk. ||| So they had only one tent; no other people dwelt near there.
êkwa ôki ispimihk iskwêwak, itê kâ-ayâcik, misâw ôtênaw êwako. ||| And up above, where those women dwelt, that was a large town.
êwakonik ôki iskwêwak, pêyak omisimâw macihkihkwêwis isiyîhkâsôw. ||| Among those women, the oldest of the sisters was called Silly Maiden.
êkosi awa osîmimâw, awa oskinîkiskwêw miyosiw. ||| And the youngest was a pretty maid.
êkosi êkwa kotakak ôki oskinîkiwak mitâtaht kâ-ihtasicik, êwako ostêsimâw macihkiwis; kêyâpic awa osîmimâw, awa oskinîkiw miyosiw. ||| And likewise, among those others, those ten young men, the oldest was Matchihkiwis; and, again, the youngest brother was a handsome youth.
êkosi oskinîkiwak ôki namôya kiskêyimêwak iskwêwa nânitaw kita-ayâyit, mîna kotaka ayîsiyiniwa. ||| Now, those young men did not know that there were anywhere any women, or any other people at all.
pêyakwanohk ê-ayâcik ôki oskinîkiwak, pisisik mâcîwak kahkiyaw ôki oskinîkiwak. ||| Those youths stayed always in that one place, and all of them did nothing but hunt.
kîtahtawê ôma ê-mâcîcik mâna, êkâ awiya ê-apiyit, awa oskinîkiw osîmimâw êwako mâna nîkân takosin. ||| Then, as time went on, and they hunted, and none of them stayed at home, then that youngest brother was always the first to get home.
êkosi kahkiyaw nâh-nâway takosinwak. ||| After him they would all come, one after the other.
kîtahtawê ê-takohtêt awa oskinîkiw, kâ-wâpahtahk mistahi ê-astêyiki mihta. ||| Once upon a time, when that youth came home, he saw a great amount of firewood lying there.
tâpiskôc awiya ê-kî-takohtêyit, itêyihtam, ê-takohtêt. ||| Exactly as if someone had come there it seemed to him, as he approached.
mistahi miywêyihtam, "mâskôc awiyak pîhcâyihk tita-apiw," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He was very glad, thinking, “Perhaps there will be someone within.”
ê-pîhtokêt, nama awiya wâpamêw. ||| When he went inside, he saw no one.
êkosi wayawîw, ta-papâmohtêt, ka-wâpahtahk ita êsa ê-kî-pimohtêyit iskwêwa. ||| So he went out and walked round the place, and there he saw that a woman must have gone by.
êkwa mitihtêw itê ê-kî-nikohtêyit; nama awiya wâpamêw. ||| Then he followed her tracks to where she had gathered wood; he saw no one.
kâwi kîwêw; pîhtokêw, êkwa ê-kotawêt, ê-wî-paminawasot. ||| He went back again; he went indoors and built his fire, to cook the meal.
ê-kîsi-kotawêt, ohtapiwinihk ê-apit, kîtahtawê kêkway kâ-kiskêyihtahk itâmihk ê-astêyiki otanâskânihk. ||| When he had made his fire and was sitting on his couch, soon he knew that there were some things under his mat.
êkosi ê-pâskinahk, kâ-wâpahtahk maskisina. ||| When he uncovered them, he behold some moccasins.
otinam, ê-wâ-wâpahtahk; mistahi miywâsiniyiwa. ||| He took them and looked at them; they were very pretty.
miywêyihtam; nahastâw. ||| He was glad; he put them carefully away.
ômisi itwêw: "iskwêw êcika ani kâ-kî-takohtêt!" itêyihtam; "namôya ta-wâpahtamwak nistêsak," itêyihtam. ||| He said, “And so a woman has come here!” he thought; “My brothers had better not see them,” he thought.
ê-koci-postiskahk, pôti miyoskam. ||| When he tried them on, why, they fitted him well.
êkosi êkwa kotaka ostêsa kâ-ta-takohtêyit, piyisk kahkiyaw takohtêyiwa ostêsa; mâka namôya wî-wîhtamawêw. ||| And then his brothers began to arrive, one after the other, until all of them had come; but he did not care to tell them about it.
êkosi mîna ê-kî-nipâcik, ê-wâpahk, kîkisêpâ sipwêhtêw awa oskinîkiw, ê-mâcît. ||| Then, when they had slept, on the next day, early in the morning that youth went out to hunt.
kotakak mîna âsk-âskaw sipwêhtêwak, namôya mâna ê-wîcêhtocik ôki oskinîkiwak kâ-mâcîcik, kahkiyaw ê-pâ-pêyakocik, miyâcîtwâwi. ||| The others, too, one after the other at intervals, set out, for those young men did not keep each other company when they hunted, but did their hunting each by himself.
êkosi êkwa awa oskinîkiw, "mâskôc ê-wî-wîkimit awa iskwêw kâ-kî-takosihk," itêyihtam. ||| Then that youth thought, “Perhaps it is because she wants to marry me that this woman has come here.”
itê ê-nipahât mostoswa, êkwa otêyaniy, êkwa ita ê-miywâsiniyik wiyâs, êkwa pêyak opêminak, êwako otinam, êkwa omâw, ê-kîwêt. ||| Where he killed a buffalo, he took the tongue, and the best parts of the flesh, and one thigh-bone, and the smallest stomach, and went home.
"mâskôc takohtêci ana iskwêw, ta-mîciw ôma omâw;" "mîna ta-pâstaham ôma opêminak, ta-mîcit," ê-itêyihtahk, kîwêw. ||| “Perhaps, if that woman comes, she will eat this stomach; and she will split this thigh-bone and eat it,” he thought as he went home.
êkwa kisiskâhtêw, ê-wî-kakwê-kêsiskawât oskinîkiskwêwa, ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He walked fast, thinking to come upon the young woman while she was there.
pôti ê-otâkosiniyik, ê-takohtêt, âsay mîna mihta wâpahtam mihcêt ê-astêyiki. ||| Then, towards evening, when he arrived, again he saw a great amount of firewood lying there.
wâpahtam ê-pikihtêyik wîkiwâw. ||| He saw smoke rusing from their tipi.
"mâskôc apiw," itêyihtam. ||| “Perhaps she is there,” he thought.
ê-pîhtokêt, nama awiya wâpamêw, êsa kâ-wêpâhtakahikêyit. ||| When he entered, he saw no one, but it was plain that someone had swept.
êkwa pônam, ê-wî-paminawasot. ||| Then he fed his fire, to cook their meal.
êkwa ê-apit, ê-paminawasot, âsay mîna kêkway itêyihtam ita kâ-kî-astêyiki maskisina. ||| Then, as he sat there while cooking, it seemed to him that again there was something where the moccasins had been.
ê-otinahk, mîna êwakoni maskisina. ||| When he took it out, this too was a pair of moccasins.
âsay mîna miywêyihtam, ê-wâ-wâpahtahk. ||| Again he was glad, as he looked at them.
mistahi miywâsiniyiwa, ê-pîmikitêyiki. ||| They were very pretty, embroidered with quill-work.
êkosi astâw, "namôya ta-wâpahtamwak nistêsak," ê-itêyihtahk. êkwa ôki oskinîkiwak ê-tâh-takohtêcik, wâpahtamwak mihta mihcêt. ||| He put them away, thinking “My brothers had better not see them.” Then, when those young men arrived, one after the other, they saw a great amount of firewood.
miywêyihtamwak, "tâpwê kiyipa mistahi nikohtêw," ê-itêyimâcik osîmiwâwa. ||| They were glad to think of their younger brother, “Truly, in a short time he gathers a great deal of wood.”
awa ostêsimâw, êwako macihkiwis, ômisi itwêw: "tâpwê nimiywêyihtên mihta mistahi ê-astêki," itwêw. ||| The oldest one, Matchihkiwis, said, “Truly I am glad that there is so much firewood.”
"êha," itwêwak oskinîkiwak. ||| “Yes, indeed,” said the young man.
êkosi namôya wî-wîhtam awa oskinîkiw. ||| Then that youth did not care to tell what had happened.
êkosi êkwa tipiskâyiw mîna. ||| Then it grew dark again.
ê-kî-mîcisocik, ê-ay-apicik, konita ê-âh-âcimocik, piyisk kawisimowak. ||| When they had eaten, and had sat a while, telling all kinds of stories, they went to bed.
"hâw, kiyipa nika-waniskân," itêyihtam awa oskinîkiw; "nika-sipwêhtân kiyipa," ê-itêyihtahk. ||| “Now then, I shall get up early,” thought the youth; “I shall set out early,” was his thought.
tâpwê kiyipa waniskâw, ê-wî-mâcît. ||| So he got up early, to go hunting.
tâpwê ê-kî-mîcisot, wawêyîw, ê-mâcît. ||| When he had eaten, he made ready to go hunting.
"mâskôc ê-wî-wîkimit awa iskwêw kâ-takosihk," itêyihtam. ||| “Perhaps it is because she wants to marry me that this woman has come here,” he thought.
êkosi itê ê-nipahât mostoswa, êkwa otinam ita ê-miywâsiniyik wiyâs. ||| So then, where he killed a buffalo, he took the best parts of the meat.
êkwa ê-kîwêt, pâh-pimipahtâw, "mâskôc nika-wâpamâw," ê-itêyihtahk. cîki ê-ihtât wîkiwâhk, kâ-wâpahtahk mistahi ê-pikihtêyik wîkiwâw. ||| When he went home, he kept running, for he thought, “Perhaps I shall see her.” When he had got close to their tipi, he saw that much smoke was rising from it.
ê-takohtêt, mistahi wâpahtam mihta ê-astêyik. ||| When he arrived, he saw that much firewood lay there.
ê-pîhtokêt, nama awiya wâpamêw, êsa mitoni kâ-wêpâhtakahikêyit, mîna otanâskâniwâwa êsa ê-pahpawahamiyit; mîna êsa kâ-paminawasoyit astêyiwa. ||| When he entered, he saw no one, though it was plain that someone had swept the place clean, and had brushed out their mats; and there was a meal which she must have cooked.
âsay mîna kâ-wâpahtahk kêkway ê-astêyiki. ê-otinahk, âsay mîna maskisina. ||| When again he saw somethings lying there, and took them up, again it was moccasins.
"hâw, namôya nika-wîhtamawâwak nistêsak," itêyihtam. ||| “Now, I shall not tell my brothers about it,” he thought.
pôti ê-otâkosihk, kâ-tâh-takohtêyit ostêsa. ||| Toward evening his brothers arrived, one after the other.
êkwa ômisi itwêw awa ostêsimâw: "tâpwê kikiyipîn, mihta ê-otinaman," itêw osîma. ||| Then the oldest brother said, “Really, you are very quick about getting faggots,” he said to his brother.
"êha, ayisk kiyipa nikî-takosinin," itêw. ||| “Yes, for, you see, I got home early,” he told him.
êkosi kotakak mîna ôki ê-kî-mîcisocik, êkosi ati-tipiskâyiw. ||| Then, by the time the others had eaten their meal, it was getting dark.
êkwa ay-apiwak, ê-âcimocik, ôma kâ-kî-mâcîcik êwako ê-âcimocik, ê-pâ-pâhpicik. ||| Then they sat there a while, telling stories, telling about the hunting they had done, and laughing.
"êkosi mîna wîpac nika-sipwêhtân," itêyihtam awa oskinîkiw. ||| “This time, too, I shall set out early,” he told him.
êkosi kahkiyaw kawisimôwak, ê-nipâcik. ||| Then they all went to bed and slept.
pôti kiyipa waniskâw awa oskinîkiw, ê-paminawasot. ||| That youth got up early, and cooked his food.
êkosi kahkiyaw waniskâwak, êkwa ê-mîcisocik. ||| Then they all arose and ate.
mayaw ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, wawêyîw, ê-mâcît awa oskinîkiw. ||| As soon as they had eaten, that youth made ready to go hunting.
ê-kî-sipwêhtêt, êkoyikohk kahkiyaw sipwêhtêwak, ê-mâcîcik. ||| When he had departed, then they all went out to hunt.
itê ê-minahot awa osîmimâw, mistahi wiyâs kîwêhtatâw, kiyipa ê-wî-kakwê-takohtêt wîkiwâhk. ||| From where he killed his game, the youngest brother took home a great deal of meat, and he meant to try to get home quickly.
tâpwê cîki ê-ihtât, wâpahtam mistahi ê-pikihtêyik wîkiwâw; êkwa tâpwê mistahi wâpahtam mihta. ||| And truly, when he got near, he saw much smoke rising from their tipi; and truly, he saw much firewood.
ê-ati-takohtêt wîkiwâhk, kâ-matwê-kitowêhtâyit pîhcâyihk awiya. ||| When he went on and approached the tent, there was someone noisily carrying on within.
ê-pîhtokêt, ê-nanâtawâpit, kâ-wâpamât iskwêwa. ||| When he entered, as he looked about, there he saw a woman.
pôti mitoni miywâsiniyiwa otanâskâniyiwa ê-pêtâyit. ||| Lo, very beautiful were her mats which she had brought.
miywêyihtam ê-nahapîstawât. ||| He was happy to go and sit by her.
sêmâk omaskisina kâh-kêtikonamiyiwa, kotaka ê-postaskisinahikot, ê-itikot, "tâpwê mitoni yâhki kikaskêyihtên, ê-wî-wâpamiyan, ê-kiskêyihtaman ôta ê-kî-nakatamân ta-kikaskisinêyan," ê-itikot. ||| At once she took off his moccasins and put others on his feet, and said to him, “Truly, you were very sad, of late, with longing to see me, when you knew that I had left those moccasins here for you to wear.” [no translation] [no translation]
"êha," itwêw awa oskinîkiw; ômisi itwêw: "ayisk namôya kiyipa kitakohtân, kayâs ê-takohtêyan ta-kî-kisâtaman sêmâk," itêw; "konita kikî-kâh-kîwân," itêw. ||| “Yes,” said the youth; “For indeed, not promptly have you come, seeing that you might have stayed at once, when long ago you arrived,” he told her; “Needlessly you have been going back and forth,” he told her.
"ayisk, 'pita nitawi-âh-atoskê,' ê-isit nôhtâwiy," êkosi itwêw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| “It was because my father told me, ‘First go there several times to work’,” said that young woman.
êkosi êkwa mîcisôwak. ||| Then they ate their meal.
ê-kîsi-mîcisocik, kâ-takohtêcik ôki kotakak oskinîkiwak, piyîhtokêtwâwi, wiyâpamâtwâwi ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| When they had eaten, then, when those other young men arrived, as they entered and saw that young woman, they were very glad.
mistahi miywêyihtamwak. nanâskomôwak ê-owîtimocik. ||| They gave thanks that they had a sister-in-law.
awa ostêsimâw macihkiwis nâway takosin. ||| That oldest brother, Matchihkiwis, came last.
ê-pîhtokêt, ê-wâpamât ôhi iskwêwa, mistahi nanâskomôw. ||| When he entered and saw the woman, he was delighted.
"hay hay!" itwêw; "êkwa, êkâ êkwa kê-kaskikwâtisoyahk!" itwêw. ||| “Splendid!” he said; “So now we won't have to sew for ourselves!” he said.
êkotê tahto-kîsikâw mâcîwak. ||| Then every day they went hunting.
ômisi itwêw awa iskwêw: "hâw, nîtimotik, kâ-nipahâyêkok mostoswak, mistahi pêtâk wiyâs." "mîna askêkinwa êkâ wiya wêpinamok; êkwa nama kêkway kika-omaskisininâwâw," itêw awa iskwêw. ||| Thus spoke that woman; “Now, my brothers-in-law, when you kill buffalo, bring home much meat. And do not throw away the hides; otherwise you will have nothing for moccasins,” she told them.
"ahaq," itwêwak ôki oskinîkiwak. ||| “Very well,” said the young men.
miyâcîtwâwi, âh-iyawis pêsiwêwak, ôma wiyâs. ||| When they hunted, they always brought the animals entire, for meat.
miywêyihtam awa oskinîkiskwêw ê-atoskêt, pahkêkinwa ê-osîhtât, mîna kâhkêwakwa ê-nîmâwinihkêt, piyisk kahkiyaw ôhi nâpêwa omaskisiniyiwa ê-osihtât, piyis mîna otayiwinisiyiwa ê-osihtât pahkêkinwa ohci, mâka mîkisa ê-kikamohât otâsiyihk mîna oskotâkayihk. ||| The young woman was happy at her work, preparing leather, and making stores of dried meat, and in time making moccasins for all those men, and clothes out of the hides, and, what was more, putting beadwork on their leggings and their coats. Those young men were very glad to have their sister-in-law take such good care of them.
mistahi miywêyihtamwak ôki oskinîkiwak, iyikohk ê-pamihikocik wîtimowâwa. ||| They were very fond of the woman. She worked very hard.
mistahi kitimâkêyimêwak ôhi iskwêwa. mistahi atoskêw awa iskwêw. ||| [no translation] [no translation] Time passed; she had been there a long while.
êkwa kahkiyaw ê-mâcîcik, macihkiwis awa kâ-têtipêwêt ita mâna ê-nikohtêyit wîtimwa, ômisi ê-itêyihtahk: "nika-owîcimosin nîtim," ê-itêyihtah, êkota ê-kâsôhtawât. ||| Then, when all were hunting, Matchihkiwis went circling about the place where his sister-in-law was wont to gather firewood, and this was his thought: [no translation] he thought, as he hid from her there.

[no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] that was why she went away. Then, as for those young men, when he came home whose wife she was, lo, their tent was without a fire. He did not see his wife. “I wonder why she is not here?” he thought.
ê-nitonawât, namôya miskawêw. ||| When he looked for her, he could not find her.
piyisk itohtêw itê mâna kâ-nikohtêyit. ||| At last he went to where she used to gather faggots.
wâpahtam êsa nâpêwa ê-kî-takohtêyit, êsa ê-mâsihitoyit, kâ-wâpahtahk ostêsa wîpisisiyiw ê-astêyik ê-mihkôwiyik, kâ-wâpahtahk ita êsa ê-ati-pimohtêyit owîkimâkana, ê-sipwêhtêyit. ||| [no translation] and then he saw his brother's arrow lying there, covered with blood, and he saw where his wife had walked, as she went away.

oskinîkiwak namôya wâpamêwak ôhi wîtimowâwa. ||| The young men did not see their brother's wife.

"namôya nikiskêyimâw," itwêw awa oskinîkiw; "kayâhtê ê-takohtêyân, namôya apiw;" "êkwa ê-nitonawak, namôya nimiskawâw." Then I went to where she is in the habit of gathering wood; there I saw that our oldest brother had come [no translation] At last I saw an arrow of our brother's lying there. It was covered with blood. Then, it appeared, your sister-in-law had gone away. I trailed her; there was blood every little ways, where she had walked, but at last I came home,” said that youth.
"hêhêhêy!" itwêwak ôki oskinîkiwak; "mâka mîna êcika ani êkâ katawa tiyôtahk kistêsinaw!" itwêwak. ||| “Heavens and earth!” said those young men; “And so again our eldest brother has been guilty of unseemly conduct!” they said.

mistahi ê-tipiskâyik, êkoyikohk kâ-takohtêt awa macihkiwis. ||| When it was entirely dark, then Matchihkiwis arrived.
ê-pîhtokêt, wâpamêw ê-kâmwâtapiyit kahkiyaw osîma. ||| When he came in, he saw that all his brothers were sitting in dejection.
"nisîm, tânêhki êkâ kâ-ôh-apit nîtim?" itwêw. ||| “Brother, why is my sister-in-law not here?” he asked.
mâskôc nânitaw ê-itohtêt," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| Perhaps she has gone somewhere or other,” said that youth.
"êhêhêy hêhe!" itwêw macihkiwis; wîsta mihtâtam, tâpiskôc êkâ nânitaw ê-kî-tôtahk; ayisk môhcôwiw awa macihkiwis. ||| “Heavens and earth!” cried Matchihkiwis; he was too sorry, just as though he had had nothing to do with it; for this Matchihkiwis was a crazy sort of person.
piyisk namôya nipâwak, ê-mihtâtâcik ôhi iskwêwa. ||| When the time came, they did not sleep, what with their grief for that woman.
wawêyîw awa oskinîkiw. ||| That youth made himself ready.
"âh hâw, nistêsitik, niwî-nitonawâw kîtimowâw," itwêw. ||| “So now, brothers, I am going to look for your sister-in-law,” he said.
"êha," itwêwak oskinîkiwak. ||| “Yes,” said the young men.
êkosi êkwa sipwêhtêw awa oskinîkiw, ê-mitihtât owîkimâkana, ê-pimohtêt. ||| So then that youth set out to track his wife, and walked on.
êkwa ôki oskinîkiwak pêyakwanohk apiwak; namôya wî-mâcîwak, ê-pakwâtahkik ê-sipwêhtêyit ôhi iskwêwa, ê-mihtâtâcik. ||| And the other young men stayed where they were; they did not care to hunt, for they were grieved that that woman had gone away and were sad at her absence.
êkwa awa oskinîkiw kâ-ma-mitihtât owîkimâkana, piyisk namôya wâpahtam ita ê-pimohtêyit êsa; tâpiskôc ê-ohpihâyit itêyihtam. ||| But that youth who was tracking his wife, at last came to a point where he could not see the signs of where she had walked; it seemed to him just as if she had risen from the ground and taken wing.
pôti êkota nîpawiw, ê-nanâtawâpit. ||| He stood there and looked about him.
tânita ta-kî-itohtêyit owîkimâkana namôya kiskêyihtam. ||| He did not know where his wife had gone.
nitawâc otinam omistanipîwayân, ê-pôtâtahk. ||| Knowing no other way, he took a hair of fur and blew upon it.
"hâw, tânitê niwîkimâkan ê-itohtêt, êkotê nika-itâsin!" "nika-omistanipîwayâniwin!" itwêw. ||| “Now, whithersoever my wife is bound, thither shall I be wafted! I shall be a hair of fur!” he said.
tâpwê ispimihk itâsiw. ||| And truly, he was borne aloft by the wind.
kîtahtawê kâ-wâpahtahk ê-asinîwacîwiyik. ||| Presently he saw where there was a rocky cliff.
êkotê tahkohcâyihk kâ-pônâsit. ||| There, at the summit, he was put down by the breeze.
êkosi êkota ê-pasikôt, kâ-wâpahtahk ita êsa ê-kî-pimohtêyit owîkimâkana. ||| Thereupon, when he rose to his feet, he saw again where his wife had walked.
êkwa ê-mitihtât, ê-ispatinâyik ê-ati-takohtêyit, ê-sâkêwêt, kâ-wâpahtahk ê-misâyik ôtênaw. ||| Then, when he trailed her, and came to a rise in the land, as he came round to the other side, there he behld a large town.
piyisk kinwês êkota apiw, ê-ka-kitâpahtahk ôhi mîkiwâhpa. ||| He sat there for a long time, looking at all the tipis.
kîtahtawê kâ-pêcâstamohtêyit iskwêwa. ||| Presently a woman came walking his way.
kisiwâk ê-pê-ihtâyit, kâ-nisitawêyimât owîkimâkana. ||| When she had come nearer, he recognized his wife.

sêmâk ocêmik, "tâpwê nimiywêyihtên ê-takohtêyan," ê-itikot; "ayisk kakêpâtisiw kistês, kâ-ôh-pê-sipwêhtêyân," itik. ||| At once she kissed him, and, “Truly, I am glad that you have come,” she said to him; “You must know it is because your eldest brother is senseless that I went away and have come here,” she told him.
"tânisi ê-tôtâsk nistês?" itwêw. ||| “What did my eldest brother do to you?” he asked.
"anima kâ-mâciyêk, ê-nitawi-nikohtêyân, êkota kâ-pê-takohtêt kistês, ômisi ê-isit: 'ê-miywêyimitân,' ê-isit." "'nîsta kimiywêyimitin,' nititâw;" "'mâka kâ-itêyihtaman namôya wiya êwako ta-kî-êkosi-ispayiw,' nititâw." "'pêyakwâw têpiyâhk ka-wîcêtin,' nititik;" "'itâp namôya ta-kiskêyihtam nisîm,' itwêw." "'nisâkwêyimon,' ê-itak, kâ-pê-otihtinit, ê-mâsihit." "mâka namôya nikî-sâkohik." "piyisk êkâ ê-kî-sâkohit, kâ-pimot ôta nipwâmihk." "êkosi aspin ê-sipwêhtêt." [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] Then, off he went. So then I drew out that arrow; I laid it there, as I went away. ‘I love my husband,’ was my thought, ‘but his brother has put me to shame,’ and so I needs came back here,” she said.
"hâw, ê-pê-nâtitân," itik. ||| “And now, I have come to get you,” she told him.
ê-takohtêcik mîkiwâhpihk, miywêyihtamiyiwa ôhi ayisiyiniwa. ||| When they reached the tipi, those people were glad.
pôti pîhtêyask ê-cimatêyik ê-misâyik mîkiwâhp, êkota kâ-takohtêcik, ê-pîhtokêcik, kâ-wâpamât oskinîkiskwêwa ê-mihcêtiyit. ||| It was a large tipi which stood in the centre of all, to which they came, and, when they entered, there he saw a great many young women.
"ê ê iy!" itwêyiwa; "kîtimonaw takosin!" kâ-itwêyit, ê-nahapit. ||| “Why!” they cried; “Our brother-in-law has come!” they cried, as he took his seat.

There stayed that youth. Then, in time, he would go away and sit on a hilltop and look at all the tipis. After a while his wife would come to him there on the hilltop. At last he grew sad, because he did not see his brothers, having been there so long.
kîtahtawê konita ê-sa-sipwêhtêt, kîtahtawê kâ-wâpahtahk, ita ê-pasahcâyik, ê-sakâyik, êkota kâ-wâpahtahk môhkiciwanipêk, ê-miywâsiniyik asiskiy, tâpiskôc oyaman kâ-isinâkwaniyik. ||| Then at one time, when he went off at random, he came to a wooded ravine and there saw a spring, and some good clay which looked exactly like vermilion.
otinam, ê-miywêyihtahk, oskotâkâhk ê-âh-ayîsihtitât, êkwa ostikwânihk, tâpiskôc ê-tômihkwêt ê-itêyihtahk. ||| He took some, because he liked it, and placed it here and there on his coat, and on his head, thinking to himself that it was just as though he were painting his face.
ê-takohtêt wîkiwâhk, ê-pîhtokêt, ê-kitâpamikot ôhi iskwêwa wîtimwa, sêmâk kâ-pâhpiyit, "manâ!" ê-itikot, "mâmaskâc awa iyikohk wî-mihkôwiw, ê-piyâsi-minahot!" kâ-itikot. ||| When he reached their dwelling, when he entered, and those women, his wife's sisters, looked at him, “A strange sight, the way he gets himself full of blood, when he has killed all the game he likes!” they said to him.
"hay hay hay!" itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Splendid! Splendid!” exclaimed the old man.
ômisi itwêw awa oskinîkiw: "namôya kêkway ninipahâw," itwêw. ||| The youth said, “I have not killed any kind of creature.”
"nâh, ê-minahoyan, ôma mistahi kâ-mihkôwiyan!" itik wîwa. ||| “Why, surely it was in killing some game that you got yourself all full of blood like this!” his wife told him.
êkosi otinamiyiwa nipiy, ê-kisîpêkinamiyit ôma oskotâkay mîna ostikwân. ||| Then she took some water and washed his coat for him and his head.
"mâmaskâc awa iyikohk ê-wî-mihkowit!" itwêyiwa. ||| “A strange sight, the way he gets himself covered with blood!” she said.
êkosi kâ-ati-wayawît awa kisêyiniw. ||| Then the old man went out of the tipi.
"hâw, hâw, nitôskinîkîmitik, wawêyîk!" "nikwatisotân!" "ninahâhkisîm nipahêw onîcâniwa ê-wîcêwâyit ocawâsimisiyiwa!" itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Come, come, my followers, make yourselves ready! Let us fetch meat from the killing! My son-in-law has killed a dam with her young!” cried the old man.
"hâw, nitânis, ta-kiskinôhtahiwêw ninahâhkisîm," itwêw. ||| “Come, daughter, let my son-in-law show the way,” he said.
êkosi awa oskinîkiw ômisi itwêw: "namôya kêkway ninipahâw," itâw owîkimâkana. ||| Then that youth said, “I have not killed any kind of creature,” he told his wife.
"ôma," itik, "tânita ê-ohtinaman, ôma‘ asiskiy’ kâ-itwêyan, êkota kâ-itohtêyan?" itik owîkimâkana; "ayîsiyiniwak cî ôma ê-itêyimiyâhk?" kâ-itikot owîkimâkana. ||| “But this,” she said to him, “where did you get it, this, which you call ‘clay,’ at the place to which you went?” his wife asked him; “And do you think we are human beings here?” she asked him.
"êha," itwêw awa oskinîkiw. ||| “Yes,” said that youth.
"namôya," itik owîkimâkana; "kiyawâw ôtê nîhcâyihk kâ-ayâ-yêk ômisi: 'piyêsiwak,' kâ-itwêyêk, niyanân êkotôwa," itik; "awa kâ-nipahat kâ-itikawiyan, 'misi-kinêpik,' kâ-itwêyêk, êkotôwa." "ita ê-ayât ôma asiskiy kâ-pêtâyan, omihko niyanân nititwânân," itik owîkimâkana. ||| “No,” his wife told him; “When you who dwell there below, say ‘Thunderers,’ even such are we,” she told him; “That creature which they tell you you have slain, when you say ‘Great Serpent,’ such it is. That clay which you have brought from where it is, we call it that creature's blood,” his wife told him.
êkosi êkwa sipwêhtêwak, êkotê ê-itohtahât ôhi ayîsiyiniwa. ||| So then they set out, that mortal man leading them thither.
kahkiyaw wîcêwêw wîtimwa. ||| All his wife's sisters went with him.
ê-takohtêcik êkotê, ômisi itwêyiwa osisa: "hâw, nitân, ninahâhkisîm kanawêyim, êkâ ta-sêkihikot ôhi kâ-wî-otinâyit ominahôwina," itwêyiwa. ||| When they got there, his father-in-law said, “Now, daughter, take care of my son-in-law, that he be not frightened by those who are about to take up the game he has killed,” said he.
êkosi owîkimâkana otinik, tâpiskôc ê-apisîsisit, êkosi ê-tôtâkot, otihkôkaniyihk êkota ê-ahikot. ||| Thereupon his wife picked him up; as if he were but a small creature she handled him, and placed him under her arm.
êkoyikohk, "êkwa namôya ayisiyiniwak!" itêyihtam, kahkiyaw ê-papâmihâyit; "êkwa piyêsiwak!" owîkimâkana mîna, ê-misi-kimiwaniyik, mistahi ê-kitoyit piyêsiwa, tâpiskôc kêkway ê-pâskisamiyit, mistahi ê-na-namipayiyik askiy, ê-itêyihtahk. ||| At that, “No, they are not mortals!” he thought, as they all began to fly about; “And so they are Thunderers!” as his wife joined them, and there came a great rain, and the Thunderers roared loud, as if they were shooting some object, and the earth trembled much, as it seemed to him.
ê-pôni-pêhtâkosiyit, êkwa ê-otinikot owîkimâkana, kâ-wâpamât ê-misikitiyit kinêpikwa êkwa pêyak ê-apisîsisiyit. ||| When they had ceased their noise, and his wife took him forth, there he saw a Great Serpent and a small one.
mâmaskâtam ita ê-ohtinâyit môhkiciwanipêkohk, ê-kî-wâpamât. ||| It seemed strange to him that they had got those creatures from the spring, when he saw them.
"nitânis, kîwêhta ninahâhkisîm," itwêw awa kisêyiniw; "ka-pakwâtam, kinwêsk kitâpamâci ôhi kinêpikwa," ê-itêyihtahk awa kisêyiniw. ||| “Daughter, take my son-in-law home,” said the old man; “It will not agree with him to look too long at these serpents,” was the old man's thought.
êkosi kîwêhtahêw owîkimâkana awa iskwêw, aspin ê-wiyanihtâkêyit. ||| So that woman took her husband home, as the others began to cut up the kill.
êkosi wiyawâw wîkiwâhk takohtêwak. ||| So they arrived at their dwelling.
mînisa mîcisôwak owîkimâkana. ||| He and his wife ate berries.
kîtahtawê kâ-takohtêyit, êkwa ê-pêtâyit wiyâs, itêyihtam. ||| Presently the others arrived, bringing meat, as it seemed to him.
"hâ, nitânis, ispatinâhk nitawi-ay-apik," itwêw awa kisêyiniw, ômisi ê-itêyihtahk"kîsitêpowihki, wî-mîcisowihci, ta-pakwâtam ninahâhkisîm," ê-itêyihtahk; ayisk ôhi misi-kinêpikwa ê-wî-môwâcik, êwako ohci kâ-ôh-itât onahâhkisîma. ||| “Now, daughter, go you two, and stay on the hilltop,” said the old man, thinking, “When the cooking is being done, and when we eat our meal, it will be painful for my son-in-law,” for they were going to eat that Great Serpent; that was why he said this of his son-in-law.
piyisk kinwêsk êkotê ayâw awa oskinîkiw, piyêsiwa ê-wîcêwât. ||| For a long time, finally, that youth stayed there, with the Thunderers.
êkwa ômisi itwêw awa kisêyiniw: "nitânis, êkwa kîwêk." "ninahâhkisîm mistahi kitimâkisiyiwa ostêsa, ê-kaskêyihtamiyit, êkâ ê-wâpamikot." "osâm kinwês ôtê ayâw." "kikî-itikonaw kâ-tipêyimikoyahk, êkâ îni-ayîsiyiniwa ta-wîcêwâyahk ôtê ispimihk," itwêw awa kisêyiniw. ||| Then thus spoke that old man: “Daughter, now go home. My son-in-law's brothers are very unhappy with grieving because they cannot see him. He is staying here too long. He told us who is our Master, that we are not to have mortal men for our companions here above,” said the old man.
"hâh, wâpahki ka-kîwânânaw." ||| “There, tomorrow we shall go home.” [no translation] [no translation] [no translation] The Silly Maiden was very glad that she was to go take to husband that Matchihkiwis; she kept laughing a foolish laugh, and she thought, that Silly Maiden, “I wish tomorrow would hurry up!” for she was eager to have a husband. So then when night came, when they had slept, in the morning, after they had eaten, they set out. Very fine was Silly Maiden's coat, jingling with bells all over, for she had put on much finery. Those things into which they put their clothes and their moccasins, they carried in their hands, as they set out. In time they came to the place from which that youth had walked. He could not see the earth, when he looked down below. There they stood.
"hâw, niwîkimâkan," itik, "âstam!" ||| “Now then, my husband,” she said to him, “come here!”
ê-nahikâpawistawât, otinik, tâpiskôc ê-apisîsisit ê-tôtâkot, otihkôkaniyihk êkota ê-ahikot, kâ-pêhtawât ê-kâ-kitoyit piyêsiwa. ||| When he came and stood close to her, she took him up, handling him as though he were but a small creature, and placed him under her arm, and then he heard the Thunderers' repeated call.

piyisk nîhcâyihk takosinwak. ||| Soon they arrived below.

I shall go and tell my brothers,” he said to those women; “I shall come back and tell you,” he said to them.

awa macihkihkwêwis mistahi wawêsîw. ||| That Silly Maiden decked herself out splendidly.
awa oskinîkiw ê-takohtêt wîkiwâhk, pôti nama awiya itêyihtam. ||| When the youth reached their dwelling, at first he thought there was no one there.
ê-pîhtokêt, kahkiyaw ostêsa kâ-pimisiniyit. ||| When he entered, thee were all his brothers lying on their beds.

ê-ohpiskwêyit awa macihkiwis, kâ-wâpamât osîma ê-apiyit. ||| When Matchihkiwis raised his head, there he saw his brother.
"waniskâk, nisîmitik;" "kisîminaw takosin!" itwêw. ||| “Get up, brothers; our brother has come!” he cried.

ê-nahapîstâkot macihkiwis, mistahi miywêyihtam. ||| When she sat down by Matchihkiwis' side, he was delighted.
kahkiyaw êkwa ayâwêwak iskwêwa, konita ê-pâ-pîkiskwêcik, ê-âcimocik, ê-pâhpicik. ||| So now all of them had wives, and they talked and talked and jabbered, and told stories, and laughed.
kîtahtawê ômisi kâ-itwêt macihkiwis: "yâw, nisîmitik, tâni ôma êtapiyêk?" "kinahâhkapihtânaw!" itwêw. ||| Presently Matchihkiwis said, “Why, brothers, why do you sit here like this? Do not forget we are newly married!” he said.
otinam kaskaskisiw, ê-sikwatahahk, ê-tômihkwêt, êkwa ê-kaskitêwikanakâpit ôta oskîsikohk. ||| He took some charcoal, ground it up, and painted himself, blackening his face round the eyes.
otinam opakamâkan, ê-ati-wayawît, ôta kisiwâk ê-piskwahcâyik, êkota ê-pa-pakamahikêt; konita kâ-matwê-ma-mawimoyit wâkayôsa, nipahêw. ||| He took his club and went out of the tipi, and where, close by, there was a small knoll in the land, he knocked with his club; then he heard the growling of a bear; he killed it.
kîwêhtahêw; pîhtokahêw. ||| He took it back to the lodge with him; he brought it inside.
"hâw, êwako ana, niwîkimâkan!" "ômisi êtokê kiwî-ay-itahcikân êtokê, ê-itêyihtaman, kâ-oh-pê-wîkimiyan," itwêw macihkiwis. ||| “Here, this is for you, my wife! I daresay you were looking forward to this kind of food when you decided to come here and marry me,” said Matchihkiwis.
tâpwê nimiywêyihtên wâkayôs ê-wî-môwak," itwêw macihkihkwêwis. ||| Truly, I am glad that I am to eat bear's meat,” said the Silly Maiden.
êkosi ê-wiyanihtâkêt êkwa ê-pakâsimât wâkayôsa, kahkiyaw êyakonik ê-môwâcik. ||| So then she cut up the bear and put it in the kettle, and they all ate of it.
êkwa ê-kî-mîcisocik, êkoyikohk tipiskâyiw, ê-kî-nipâcik. ||| When they had eaten, it was dark, and so they went to bed.
êkwa tahto-kîsikâw mâcîwak, ê-pêtâcik wiyâs. ||| Then they hunted every day and brought home the meat.
mistahi ka-kâyawisiwak ôki iskwêwak. ||| Very industrious were those women.
mistahi ê-atoskêcik, kiyipa wîkiwâwa kîsihtâwak; kahkiyaw êkwa pâh-pêyakokêwak. ||| They worked hard and soon had made their tipis; so then they lived each in a separate tent.
ayisk mitâtasiwak iskwêwak; mitâtaht osîhtâwak wîkiwâwa. ||| For there were ten women; they made ten tipis.
êkosi aspin ê-wâ-wîkicik. ||| And so they lived there from that time on.
êkoyikohk ê-iskwâk âtayôhkêwin. ||| This is where the sacred story ends.
kîtahtawê yâhki mâh-mêscihtâsôw wîhtikôw. ||| Once upon a time, long ago, a Windigo carried on his work of extermination.
tapasîwak êsa mitâtaht oskinîkiwak. ||| Ten youths took flight.
âyîtaw ê-ohkwâkanit awa wîhtikôw, mihcêt âta mîkiwâhpa ê-ihtakohki, êsa mâna ê-mâh-mêscihtât. ||| That Windigo, with a face on either side of his head, no matter how many tents there were, always killed off all the people.
mitâtaht êsa ê-ihtasicik ôki oskinîkiwak, "tapasîtân!" itwêwak êsa; "kiyânaw piko kika-iskwâhikonaw," itwêwak êsa. ||| Then those youths, who were ten, said, “Let us flee! We alone shall not be killed,” they said.
tâpwê wawêyîwak; mîkiwâhp wâhyaw wacîhk nitawi-osîhtâwak. ||| So they made ready; far off on a mountain they went to build their tipi.
êkwa kîtahtawê kîwêwak; nâtêwak osîmisiwâwa. ||| Then, after a time, they went back; they fetched their little brother.
êkotê nikwatis owîkiwak. ||| They had their tent off there alone.
êkotê kîtahtawê ê-wa-wîkicik, kîtahtawê nâpêsis mâna ê-kanawâpokêt, kîtahtawê êsa ê-pônahk, kâ-kisisihk. ||| Then, at one time, as they continued to dwell off there, and the little boy always stayed to keep the house, then presently, as he was feeding the fire, he ran a splinter into himself.
miscikos wîhkwacipitam. ||| He pulled out the sliver of wood.
ôma miscikos ositihk kâ-kisisihk iskwâhtêmihk ê-wêpinahk, kâ-pê-pîhtokêtâcimoyit iskwêsisa. ||| When he threw out of the door that sliver of wood which he had run into his foot, there came crawling in a little girl.
otinêw êsa, "misawâc namôya nika-kî-ohpikihâw," ê-itêyihtahk êsa. ||| He lifted her up, thinking, “It is no use, I should not be able to bring her up.”
êkwa kâ-pê-pîhtokêyit, âsay mîna ê-kî-wayawîwêpinât, âsay mîna kîhtwâm wayawîwêpinêw. ||| When she came into the tent, after he had twice thrown her out, again he threw her out.
êkwa kîhtwâm ê-pê-pîhtokêyit, "nistêsê!" kâ-itikot êsa. ||| Then, when again she came in, she called to him, “Big brother!”
ahpô êtokê kita-oskinîkiskwêwiw, kîhtwâm wayawîwêpinaki!" itêyihtam êsa. ||| I should not be surprised if she were to turn into a young woman, if I threw her out again!” he thought.
êkwa ômisi itwêw: "kita-wî-oskinîkiskwêwiw, ahpô êtokê ê-wîcihikowisiyân!" itwêw êsa. ||| Then he spoke thus: “Let her be a young woman, since it seems that I am being aided by the Powers!” he said.
êkwa kâ-pê-pîhtokêyit oskinîkiskwêwa, "ay-api, nimisê!" itwêw êsa awa nâpêsis. ||| Then, when there entered a young woman, “Be seated, my big sister!” said the boy.
pîhkahtêwâhtik isiyîhkâtêw êsa ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| “Burnt-Stick” it seems that he called the young woman.
êkosi êkwa miywêyihtam ê-omisit; mîna ê-mihcêtiyit ostêsa, miywêyihtam kita-pamihikocik ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| And now he was glad to have a big sister; and he was glad that all his elder brothers would have this young woman to do their household work for them.
êkota êsa mâka mîna wîkihkêmôw wîsahkêcâhk ôhi oskinîkiwa; êwako ohci, kâ-ôh-kiskêyihtamiyit kita-isi-tapasiyit ôhi wîhtikôwa. ||| And now it appears that in his usual way Wisahketchahk was staying with these young men; it was because they knew in which direction that Windigo would take flight.
ayisk kî-mâhpinêw wîsahkêcâhk; êwako ohci kâ-wîsâmât ôhi oskinîkiwa. ||| For Wisahketchahk was badly frightened; that was why he had asked hospitality of these young men.
"mâcika, nisîmis!" itwêw êsa. ||| “You will see, little brother!” he must have said.
nîkân êsa mâna pîhtokêw awa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| Wisahketchahk was always the first to come into the tipi.
"tânisi ka-itêyihtên," itwêw awa nâpêsis, "oskinîkiskwêw kita-ayâwâyahk?" itwêw êsa. ||| “What would you think,” asked the boy, “of our having a young woman?”
êkwa wiya wîsahkêcâhk, "kika-osîminânaw!" itwêw; kahkiyaw kêkway kî-osîmiw ayisk êsa wîsahkêcâhk. ||| And Wisahketchahk, for his part, said, “We shall have her as our younger sister!” for it seems that Wisahketchahk had every manner of creature for his younger brother and sister.
kîtahtawê êkwa mistahi kâ-kâyawisiyiwa ôhi osîmiwâwa, ê-kaskikwâtikocik, mîna ê-paminawasoyit. ||| Then this younger sister of theirs was very diligent, sewing for them, and doing their household work.
mitoni êsa kwayask pamihikwak, êkwa mistahi wîstawâw êsa ê-kitimâkêyimâcik. ||| It seems that she kept them very well, so that they, in turn, became very fond of her.
êkwa ê-mâh-mâcîcik, sêmâk wîpac êsa mâna ê-ati-kîsihtâyit pahkêkinwa, êkwa mâna otayiwinisiwâwa ê-osîhtâyit, mitoni kwayask êsa ê-pamihikocik. ||| When they did their hunting, without delay, it seems, she always tanned the hides and made clothes for them, taking in every way excellent care of them.
kîtahtawê ômisi itwêw êsa wîsahkêcâhk: "âh, âsay kiskêyihtam ôta ê-ayâyahk âyîtaw kâ-ohkwâkanit wîhtikôw," itwêw êsa; "piko nika-kîwôtânân," itêw; "êkwa mîna kêkway pêhtamani, êkâya wîhkâc nâkatôhkê, nêkohtêyani," itêw êsa ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa, pîhkahtêwâhtik kâ-isiyîhkâsoyit; êkwa êsa, "êkâya wîhkâc, wâpahtamani kêkway, otin," itêw êsa, "otina." "êkota ohci êkwa mîna nika-kîwôtânân." "kêkway mîna pêhtamani, êkâ apiyâhko, mistahi manitôwiw kâ-âyîtawihkwâkanêt wîhtikôw." "êkosi niya wiya wîsahkêcâhk nikostâw," itwêw êsa wîsahkêcâhk; "êkwa mîna tâpiskôc niyanân kika-itihtawinân," itwêw êsa; "tâpwê nêwo-tipiskâw nika-kîwôtânân." "mitoni ani kita-kisinâw." "êkwa ka-pêhtawinân;" "êkâ yôhtênamôhkan," itêw êsa ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| Presently Wisahketchahk spoke as follows “Oh, by this time the Windigo with a face on either side of his head knows that we are here,” he said; “But we shall go visiting,” he told her; “And then, if you hear anything, never listen to it, when you are gathering wood,” he must have told the young woman who was called Burnt-Stick; and “Never, when you see anything, take it up,” he told her; Never take it up. Then we shall be off visiting again. If then again you hear anything, when we are not at home, great manitou power has that two-faced Windigo. So great that even I, Wisahketchahk, fear him,” Wisahketchahk must have said; “Then, again, you will hear exactly, as it will seem, the sound of our voices,” he said; “Really, for four nights we shall be off visiting. And it will be very cold weather. Then you will hear our voices; do not open the door,” he must have told the young woman.
tâpwê ê-kî-kakêskimiht awa oskinîkiskwêw, êkwa mâci-nikohtêw, mayaw kahkiyaw ê-sipwêhtêyit ôhi ostêsa. ||| Accordingly, when the young woman had been instructed, she started to gather firewood, as soon as all her brothers had gone away.
êkwa kahkiyaw mîna kîsâc nâh-nâtwâham; mîna êsa kîsâc kahkiyaw pîhtokatâw; êkwa êsa mîna kotak kîskatahwêw ê-misikitiyit mîtosa. ||| And she split all the wood, so that it should be quite ready for use; and she brought it all indoors ready for use; and she cut a big poplar tree besides.
êkwa sôhki mitoni kipaham wîkiwâw. ||| Then she closed up their tipi solidly.
mistahi êsa kisinâw. ||| It was very cold weather.
êkwa kîtahtawê kâ-matwê-itwêwiht: "nisîmis, nitakosininân!" kâ-matwê-itwêwiht êsa. ||| Presently she heard someone call, “Little sister, here we are!” seemed to be spoken for her to hear.
êkwa ayisk kî-kakêskimâw; namôya êsa wî-waskawîw. ||| But, after all, she had been warned; she did not stir from the spot.
piyisk wâsakâm êkota wîkihk matwê-nipahaciyiwa. ||| At last all round the lodge there was the sound of them dying of cold.
waniskâw kîkisêpâ; ê-âta-wayawît, namwâc ahpô awiya kita-mâtâhât. ||| In the morning she arose; when she went outside, she found not even a footprint.
"tâpwê êcika ani!" itêyihtam awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| “So it really is thus!” thought the young woman.
nêwo-tipiskâw ê-kî-ispayik, takohtêwak ôki oskinîkiwak. ||| When four nights had passed, the young men arrived.
êkwa mâna ka-kapê-kîsik ê-nikohtêt piko awa oskinîkiskwêw, nama wîhkâc kêkway otinam, âta nanâtohk kêkway wiyâpahtahki. ||| Then, when the young woman always gathered wood all day, she never picked up anything, although she saw all manner of things.
kîtahtawê êsa mistahi ê-miyosiyit mîkwana wâpamêw êsa. ||| But then at one time she saw a most beautiful feather.
êkwa otinêw, "mêtokêta êkâ kika-wayêsihitih!" kâ-itikot, kayâhtê ôta ê-ohci-pasikôyit ôhi wîhtikôwa âyîtaw kâ-ohkwâkaniyit. ||| She picked it up, when, “Of course I could not get the better of you!” said the two-faced Windigo, suddenly rising from the feather.
ômisi êsa itwêw awa wîhtikôw: "tâpwê niwî-miyo-mîcison, pîhkahtêwâhtik ê-wî-mowak!" "hâw, pîhkahtêwâhtik, pita ka-kîwêhtahitin; kika-wiyinohitin." ||| Thus spoke the Windigo: “Truly, I shall have good eating, when I eat Burnt-Stick! Now, Burnt-Stick, first I shall take you home with me; I shall make you fat.”
êkosi awa wîhtikôw nayômêw êsa ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa. ||| With that the Windigo took the young woman on his back and carried her.
kîwêhtahêw, mistahi êsa ê-kakwâtakihât nôtokêsiwa ê-ayâwât, tahto-kîsikâw ê-kwayâci-pakâhtamâkot, ê-kwayâci-kîsisamâkot, tahto-kîsikâw êsa mâna nîso ayîsiyiniwa ohci ê-mowât, êkwa mâna ayîsiyiniw otakisiya, têkohtêci, pita nîkân êwakoni êsa mâna ê-mîcit. ||| He took her home with him, to where he had an old woman whom he led a dreadful life; every day this old woman had his stew ready for him, cooking it done before he got home, for every day he ate two men, his habit being, as soon as he got home, first to eat their entrails.
êkwa, "nôhkô," itwêw êsa; "kikî-kwayâci-pakâhtân cî otakisiya ta-mîciyân?" "mistahi êkwa miyosiw oskinîkiskwêw kâ-pêsiwak, ta-mowak." "âhkamêyimo ê-kakwê-wiyinohat," itwêw êsa. ||| So now, “Grandmother,” he said; “have you boiled the entrails ready for me to eat? Now very pretty is the young woman I have brought home to eat. Do not spare your pains to fatten her,” he said.
tâpwê, "êha," itwêw êsa awa nôtokêsiw. ||| Then, “Very well,” said the old woman.
mistahi miywêyimêw ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa awa nôtokêsiw, pîhkahtêwâhtik kâ-isiyîhkâsoyit. ||| The old woman became very fond of the maid, Burnt-Stick.
êkwa êsa, "nôsisê, tâpwê mistahi iyâkwâma ta-nipahitân nipakwâtên," itwêw êsa; "mahti kiyâm kakwê-cîsi;" "niya nipahin," itwêw êsa awa nôtokwêw; "êkwa êkosi kika-pakâsimin," itwêw êsa awa nôtokwêw. ||| Then, it seems, “Grandchild, surely I hate the very thought of killing you,” she said; “Do try to deceive him; do you, instead, kill me,” the old woman said; “And then you will set me to boil,” said the old woman.
tâpwê awa oskinîkiskwêw miywêyihtam ê-itikot ôhi nôtokêsiwa. ||| Truly, the maid was pleased at what the old woman told her.
"tânisi mâka kê-tôtamân ta-nipahitân?" itwêw êsa awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| “But how must I do to kill you?” asked the young woman.
"ômisi," itwêw awa nôtokwêw; "cîkahikan kika-otinên;" "nistikwânihk ka-pakamahên," itwêw awa nôtokwêw; "ôtê êkâ ê-pîsimôwik nêwo osêtinawa, ôma ôta nistam osêhcâw kika-âmaciwân." "êkota ohci mîna kotak ispatinâw ka-têpâpahtên." "nêwo ispatinâwa miyâskamani, êkotê kakwê-takwâmôhkan pîwâpisko-wâskahikan." "êwakoni êkotê ê-sâkôcihikot." "kîspin êkotê takwâmoyani, êkosi kika-pimâtisin," itik êsa; "takwâmoyani êkotê, ômisi itwêhkan: 'nistêsê, niwî-nipahik âyîtawihkwâkan wîhtikôw!' kika-itwân." "itâp ana kika-yôhtênamâkwak." ||| Thus spoke the old woman: “You will take an ax; you will strike a blow on my head,” said the old woman; “Yonder, in the direction where there is no sun, are four hills, the first and nearest of which you will climb. From there you will see the second hill. When you have crossed four hills, there try to reach in your flight an iron house. The one who dwells there will overcome him. If you manage to get there in your flight, then you will live,” she told her; “When you reach the place in your flight, speak thus: “Big brother, the both-side-faced Windigo wants to kill me!' you will say. Then they will open the door for you.”
tâpwê ê-kî-kakêskimikot awa pîhkahtêwâhtik ôhi nôtokêsiwa, pakamahwêw ostikwâniyihk. ||| Accordingly, even as the old woman had directed Burnt-Stick, she struck her on the head.
êkwa êkosi isi wiyanihêw, ê-kî-nipahât. ||| Then she skinned her and cut her up, whom she had slain.
ê-kî-kîsiswât, êkosi isi sôhki tapasîw. ||| When she had cooked her done, she ran away as fast as she could.
pimipahtâw mitoni sôhki. ||| She ran with all her might.
kîtahtawê ispatinâw nitawâpahtahk, ê-ati-kapê-tipisk ê-pimipahtât. ||| Presently she saw a hill, and all night long she ran.
âsay mîna kotak ispatinâw wâpahtam; âsay mîna êwako miyâskam. ||| Then she saw another hill; she crossed it, too.
mîna kotak ispatinâw wâpahtam; êwako mîna miyâskam. ||| She saw another hill; this, too, she crossed.
kotak ispatinâw ê-âmaciwêt, âsay êkwa kâ-matwê-têpwâtikot ôhi wîhtikôwa. ||| When she climbed the next hill, already she heard the Windigo shouting to her.
"namôya misawâc kita-pîhcâw askiy kita-itâmoyan!" kâ-matwê-isi-têpwâtikot. ||| “It is no use! The earth will not be large enough to give you refuge!” he shouted to her.
mistahi êsa kisiwâsiw awa wîhtikôw, ôhkoma ê-mowât. ||| It appears that the Windigo was very angry at having eaten his grandmother.
êkwa ta-pinasiwêw; kotak ê-osêhcâyik ê-âmaciwêt, ôta nîhcâyihk kî-astêyiw pîwâpisko-wâskahikan. ||| Now she was running down-hill; as she climbed the rise, there down below was the iron house.
nâway ê-itâpit, kî-pêtisâpamêw êsa wîhtikôwa; sôhki êsa êkwa tâpwê tapasîw. ||| When she looked behind her, already she saw the Windigo coming; then really she fled with all her might.
ê-otihtahk, wani-kiskisiw tânisi kâ-kî-isi-kakêskimikot ôhi nôtokêsiwa ka-kî-nipahât. ||| When she reached it, she forgot the instruction she had been given by the old woman whom she had killed.
"tawinamawin!" "âyîtawiskîsik niwî-nipahik, nistêsê!" itwêw êsa. ||| “Open the door for me! Both-Side-Eyes wants to kill me, big brother!” she cried.
piko isi âta ê-itwêt, mwêhci êkwa ê-wî-pê-sakinikot, kâ-kiskisopayit anihi nôtokêsiwa kâ-kî-isi-kakêskimikot. ||| Although she called in all manner of ways, he was even about to seize her, when she remembered what the old woman had told her.
"nistêsê," itwêw êsa mîna kîhtwâm, "tawinamawin!" itwêw êsa; "âyîtawihkwâkan niwî-nipahik!" itwêw êsa. ||| “Big brother,” she cried again, “open the door for me!” she cried; “Both-Side-Face wants to kill me!” she cried.
yôhtêpayiyiw ôma pîwâpisko-wâskahikan. ||| The door of the iron house swung open.
wâpamêw êkota pîhcâyihk ê-owîkiyit oskinîkiskwêwa mîna oskinîkiwa. ||| She saw those who had their dwelling inside there, a young woman and a young man.
ômisi êsa itik ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa: "nicâhkos, ay-api!" itik êsa. ||| Then the young woman said to her, “sister-in-law, sit down!”
kîtahtawê wayawîtimihk ôta kâ-matwê-takohtêyit ôhi wîhtikôwa. ||| Soon with noise the Windigo arrived outside.
"tawinamawin, pîwâpisko-wâskahikan kâ-owîkit!" itwêyiwa êsa. ||| “Open for me, Iron-House-Dweller!” he cried.
êkosi êsa yôhtênam awa oskinîkiw, ê-ati-kîskikwêtahwât ôhi wîhtikôwa. ||| Then the young man opened the door and chopped off the Windigo's head.
êkwa awa oskinîkiskwêw êkota ay-ayâw. ||| Then the young woman stayed there.
ayisk mistahi kitimâkêyimik ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa mîna ôhi nâpêwa. ||| For that young woman and that man were very good to her.
kîtahtawê kâ-pîmoyohikot kêkway ohci kita-manitôwit. ||| Then in time, they gave her something to keep in the bosom-fold of her garment, to give her manitou power.
tâpwê mistahi sôhkisiwin ayâw; mistahi êkwa mîna êwako manitôwiw êsa. ||| And really, she had great strength; she too had now manitou power.
êkwa osîhtâyiwa nâpêw-ayiwinisa, êkotôwa êkwa ê-postiskahk, mîna onâpêwin ê-osîhtâyit. tâpwê papâmâcîw. ||| Then they made men's clothes, which she put on, [no translation] Then really, she went about hunting.
kîtahtawê ômisi itik ôhi: "mistahi kistêsak kipîkiskâtikwak." "mistahi kakwâtakihtâwak, nawac kakwê-wâpamacik," itik; "ih, tâpwê wiya ôta namôya wâhyaw ispatinâw kika-otihtên." "êkota mîkiwâhp ka-wâpahtên, mitoni ê-misâk, êkota ayîsiyiniwak ohcitaw ê-kakwâtakihât, ê-wacistwanihkêt, êkwa mâna ayîsiyiniwa ê-tâh-têhci-kwâskohtit," "êkota mitoni ê-sâkaskinêcik ayîsiyiniwak, nanâtohk ê-isi-kakwâtakihtâcik, piko itôwihk ê-ati-pa-pîkoskawât ana êkota kâ-ayâ-t maci-ayîsiyiniw," itik êsa; "êwako piko ê-âyimahk, mâka piko oskinîkiskwêwa êkoni piko kâ-itinât wiya; nâpêwa namôya pisiskêyimêw." "mayaw pimâpamiski, ômisi kika-itik: 'mahti sikitân, awîna wâhyaw kê-pahkihtiniyik'," itik êsa; "êkosi kika-itik." ||| Then at one time they said to her, “Your brothers miss you very much. They are suffering greatly; you ought to try to see them,” they told her; “Now, not far from here you will come to a hill. There you will see a very large tipi. He who lives there is intent on tormenting people; he builds a nest from which he jumps on people. That place is full of people who suffer from all kinds of injuries, since that evil person who lives there breaks different parts of their bodies as he comes down on them,” they told her; “This is the only difficulty, but, after all, he takes only young women; he pays no attention to men. “As soon as he sees you, he will say to you, “[no translation]” they told her; “That is what he will say to you.”

êkwa kîkisêpâ awa nâpêw kâ-wîwit ôhi oskinîkiskwêwa kâ-môhcôwiyit, osîmisiyiwa kâ-nipahâyit, ômisi itêw: "nitawi-asamik ôki âpakosîsi-nôtokêwak," itêw êsa. ||| Then, in the morning, that man who had to wife the young woman who was so mad and had slain her brother, spoke thus to her: “Go feed those Old Mouse Women,” he told her.
êkwa tâpwê nitawi-asamêw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| Then accordingly, the young woman went to give them food.
ê-pîhtokêt, kâ-wâpamât ôhi ka-kî-nipahât nâpêsisa. ||| When she entered, there she saw the boy she had killed.
"âsay êcika ôki mîna ê-kî-pimâcihâcik maci-nôtokêsiwak!" itwêw êsa. ||| “So it seems that these evil old women have brought him back to life!” she said.
êkwa ômisi itwêw awa nâpêw: "kiyâm êkâya, niwîkimâkan." "kêyiwêhk ana nika-wîcêwâw miyâcîyâni," itêw. ||| Then the man said, “Never mind, do not kill him, my wife. After all, I can take him with me when I hunt,” he told her.
êkosi pônihêw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| So the young woman left him alone.
êkwa tâpwê ôki nôtokêwak wawêyîhêwak ôsisimiwâwa, ta-mâciyit. ||| Then, accordingly, the old women made their grandchild ready, that he might hunt.
tâpwê awa nâpêw ê-wî-mâcît, "âstam, wêskinîkiyin!" "iskêkâni nahâhkapiyani," itâw awa awâsis. ||| So, when that man was ready to go hunting, “Come here, young fellow! It would seem you are staying with people,” the child was told.
êkwa tâpwê wawêyîw awa awâsis, êkwa ê-sipwêhtêcik, ôhi ê-wîcêwât ôhi nâpêwa, ê-mâcîyit. ||| Then the child made himself ready, and they set out, as he accompanied that man on his hunt.
iyâta-mâtâhâtwâwi, "namôya êwako," itik mâna; "osâm apisîsisiw," itik mâna. ||| Although they would come upon some creature's trail, “Not this one,” the other would say to him; “He is too small,” the other would say to him.
êkwa tâpwê kotaka mitoni ê-mâh-mahkiskamiyit, êwakoni êti-pimitisahwâyit misi-iyâpêwi-wâwâskêsiwa, wîpac êti-nipahâyit. ||| Then really, when they saw the trail of another whose tracks were of enormous size, then the man went off pursuing this giant stag, and soon off there slew him.
nâway ê-takohtêt, âsay kêkâc kîsi-wiyanihêyiwa. ||| When the boy later arrived, the other had almost finished preparing the carcass.
êkwa ômisi itik: "nawacî ôma otakisiy," itik. ||| Then the man told him, “Roast this tripe,” he told him.
êkwa ê-kîsisahk, ômisi itêw: "âyîtaw ohci kika-mîcinânaw," itêw. ||| When he had cooked it done, he said to the man, “Let us eat it from either end.”
êkwa, "tânêhki kâ-ôh-itwêyan?" itwêw awa nâpêw; "kiya ôma kitawâsisîwin, mistahi kâ-nitawêyihtaman kita-mîciyan," itêw êsa. ||| Then, “What makes you say that?” said the man; “You, you are but a child, to be wanting to eat so much,” he told him.
"mâka ayisk namôya nikaskihtamâson kêkway," itwêw awa nâpêsis. ||| “But since I have no power of any kind!” said the boy.
tâpwê ê-kîsisahk ôma mayaw otakisiy, tâpwê âyîtaw ohci miciminamwak, ê-mîcicik. ||| Accordingly, as soon as he had cooked done that tripe, they each took hold of an end, and ate it.
êkwa kêkâc ê-kitâcik, maskamêw. ||| Then, when they had almost eaten it up, he snatched it away from the man.
"hâw, ôma mîci, piyêsiw!" itwêw êsa. ||| “Come, eat this, Thunderer!” he said.
"ô, kêkway ita kê-kitimâkêyimikoyan?" itik êsa ôhi nâpêwa; "kakwêyâho!" itik êsa; "ati-pasikô!" itik êsa. ||| “Ho, what sort of thing will give its aid to you?” the man said to him; “Get to work!” he told him; “Up with you!” he told him.
ita kisiwâk ostikwân ohpimê ê-astêyik, otinamiyiwa itê isi kâ-isi-kâsitêskanêyit; nayahtahik. ||| Close by there, off to one side, where lay the stag's head, the man took it up by the beast's pointed horns; he put it on the boy's back, for him to carry.
"kakwêyâho!" itik; "pasikô!" itik: "mâ ani âta ê-manitowakêyimoyan, ita wiya ati-atimitâni, kika-nipahitin;" "kika-ati-patakwâtimâtitin." ||| “Look lively!” he told him; “Get up!” he told him; “Believe it or not, though you think yourself of manitou kind, if I overtake you on the way, I will kill you; I will stamp you under my snowshoes.”
tâpwê ati-sipwêhtêw awa nâpêsis. ||| So the boy started off.
cîki wîkiwâhk ê-ati-ayât, âsay kisiwâk kâ-pêcâstamohtêyit, ê-atimikot. ||| When he had got close to their lodge, the other had already come near, and now overtook him.
êkosi isi sâ-sâkwâkimâtik. ||| At once he crushed him under his snowshoes.
êkwa êsa nipahik; êskana kâ-kîhcitâskamâk. ||| He killed him; he jabbed the horns into him.
êkwa mistahi miywêyihtam awa oskinîkiskwêw, nôhtaw ê-pê-nipahimiht. ||| Then the young woman was very glad that he had been killed before reaching the place.
êkwa âsay mîna ôki nôtokêsiwak kâ-kî-pimâtisihâcik mîna itwêwak, "pêyakwâw ta-kakwê-pimâcihâcik!" ||| Then again those old women who had restored him to life said, “Let them try once more to bring him to life!”
tâpwê awa kâ-misikitit nôtokwêw âpakosîsi-nôtokêw awatêw êwako. ||| Then, accordingly, that big old woman, that Old Mouse Woman took him off with her.
tâpwê âsay mîna pimâcihêwak. ||| they succeeded in bringing him again to life.
êsa mâna wâh-pimâcihâtwâwi, matotisiwak. ||| It seems that they took a steam-bath whenever they were about to bring him to life.
êkwa âsay mîna kîkisêpâ, "nitawi-asam kôhkominawak," itwêw êsa awa nâpêw. ||| Then again, in the morning, “Go feed our grandmothers,” said the man.
tâpwê ê-itohtêt awa oskinîkiskwêw, kî-pimâtisiyiwa ôhi nâpêsisa. ||| When, accordingly, the young woman went there, the boy was alive.
"âsay êcika ôki mîna kîhtwâm!" "nikî-miywêyihtamwâh ê-nipahimiht!" itwêw êsa. ||| “And so they have done it again! I was glad he had been killed!” she exclaimed.
"kiyâm êkosi ana pêyakwâw mîna nika-wîcêwâw," itwêw awa nâpêw. ||| “Never mind, I shall simply take him with me again,” said the man.
tâpwê pônihêw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| Then the young woman left him alone.
êkwa wawêyîw awa nâpêsis. ||| Then the boy made ready.
pê-wîsâmik ôhi nâpêwa. ||| The man came to take him along.
âsay mîna sipwêhtêwak; âsay mîna mâtâhêwak wâwâskêsiwa. ||| Again they set out; again they came upon the trail of a stag.
"awa cî?" ê-ati-itât, "namôya! ||| “Is this the one?” he asked him, but, “No!
osâm apisîsisiw," itik. ||| He is too small,” the other answered.
mitoni nâspic ê-mâh-mahkiskamiyit, êwakoni pêmitisahwâyit, "itâp kika-pê-atimin," itik. ||| When one had left hoofprints of enormous size, this one the man pursued; “You will catch up to me later,” he told him.
tâpwê mwêstas êkotê ê-takohtêt, âsay kêkâc kîsi-wiyanihêyiwa. ||| Truly, later, when the boy got there, he had already nearly finished cleaning the carcass.
âsay mîna, "hâw, awâsis, ôma nawacî;" "mîcîhkahk ôma otakisiy," itik êsa. ||| Again, “Come, child, roast this; let us later eat this tripe,” he told him.
tâpwê, "âyîtaw ohci mîna kika-mîcinânaw," itêw êsa. ||| Then, “Let us eat it again from either end,” he told the man.
tâpwê, "nîswâw êkwa êkosi kititwân," itik êsa. ||| Then, “Now for the second time you say thus,” the other answered him.
"ayisk niya nikitimâkisin," itwêw êsa awa nâpêsis. ||| “After all, as for me, I am but a poor creature,” said the boy.
"êha," itwêw êsa awa nâpêw. ||| “Yes, very well,” said the man. Then, “Let me have the big end, let me eat from the big end,” said the boy.
piyisk mîna sâkôcimêw. ||| At last he talked the man into it.
êkwa tâpwê âyîtaw ohci miciminamwak ê-mîcicik. ||| So then they took hold of it at either end and ate it.
apisîs ê-iskwahtahkik, ispimihk isiwêpinam awa nâpêsis. ||| When they had but a little uneaten, the boy flung it aloft.
"haw, ôma mîci," itwêw êsa, "piyêsiw!" itwêw êsa. ||| “Come, eat this,” he said, “O Thunderer!”
êkwa âsay mîna ohpimê astêyiw ôma ostikwân, âsay mîna êwako kâ-otinamiyit, ê-nayahtahikot. ||| Now again, off to one side lay the head, and again the man took it and put it on the boy's back.
âsay mîna pasikôtisahok, "kakwêyâho!" ê-itikot. êkwa ati-sipwêhtêw. ||| Again he drove him to his feet, telling him, “Look lively!” He started out.
"kîspin ita atimitâni, kika-ati-mâtakoskâtin nitasâmak ohci!" itik êsa. ||| “If anywhere I catch you, I will stamp you flat with my snowshoes!” he called to him.
kisiwâk êkwa wîkiwâhk ê-ati-ayât, kâ-pê-atimikot. ||| When he had got near the lodge, the other overtook him.
ômisi itwêw êsa ê-wî-pê-nipahikot: "piyêsiw, êwako ana nipahtamawin! ||| As the other was about to come upon him and kill him, he cried, “Thunderer, kill this one for me!
niwî-nipahik!" itwêw awa nâpêsis. ||| He wants to kill me!” said the boy.
êkwa tâpwê piyêsiwak sôhki pêhtâkosiwak. ||| Then truly the Thunderers made themselves loudly heard.
nipahêwak ôhi nâpêwa, awâsisa kâ-wî-nipahâyit. ||| They killed that man who was going to kill the child.
êkosi pê-wayawî-kwâskohtiw awa oskinîkiskwêw. ||| Then the young woman came leaping out of her dwelling.
